Philippine News Agency (2019). Sports tourism boosts tourist arrivals in Dumaguete. https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1088794 hosting the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup created an economic impact of Php 17.8 billion.3 Projections for hosting a single future event like the Volleyball World Championship estimate a total economic impact of over USD 40 million and an alignment with a destination tourism market valued at USD 5.4 billion.4 Yet, despite our proven capability to host world-class events and earning praise for our people’s renowned hospitality, we fail to consistently translate this potential into lasting national success. For too many Filipinos, sports remains a dream rather than a viable and honored profession. It is a calling we deny to our own people because we lack the right systems, support, and structures. This systemic weakness is most evident in the Olympics. The long wait between the 1996 boxing silver medal by Mansueto Velasco and Hidilyn Diaz's historic gold in weightlifting in 2020 highlights the challenges faced by Filipino athletes in reaching their full potential on the world’s biggest sporting stage. The Philippine Sports Commission (PSC), established in 1990 through Republic Act No. 6847, is mandated to, among others, “provide the leadership, formulate the policies and set the priorities and direction of all national amateur sports promotion and development, particularly giving emphasis on grassroots participation.” However, its focus on grassroots participation may not fully address the needs of elite athletes to compete at the highest levels of sports competitions. In 2001, Republic Act No. 9155 or the “Governance of Basic Education Act of 2001” abolished the Bureau of Physical Education and School Sports (BPESS) and transferred “[a]ll functions, programs and activities of the Department of Education related to sports competition” to the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC). While physical education remains in the curriculum, this shift has weakened overall sports development. This measure will address the perennial challenges that hinder the growth of Philippine sports. This bill proposes the creation of a Department of Sports, a cabinet-level agency that will provide focused leadership for national sports promotion and development, and address the needs of athletes, coaches, trainers, and sports officials across all levels. With a dedicated department, we can find comprehensive solutions to the problems besetting Philippine sports, particularly the lack of a coherent national sports program, the need to enhance the partnership with various sectors involved in sports, obsolete training methods, lack of modern and high-quality training facilities, equipment, and sports venues. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE As the agency responsible for training and capacitating the country's workers, the Technical Education and Skills Education (TESDA) was established to encourage the full participation of and for the mobilization of the industry, labor, local government units and technical-vocational institutions in the skills development of the country's human resources. The COVID-19 pandemic brought the world to an unprecedented level of societal disruption. Many industries were immediately impacted by this: with the loss of markets came the loss of jobs. Prior to the pandemic, Asia Pacific had some of the highest economic growth rates in the world; but still afflicted with high levels of worker hardship, with 300 million workers living with their families in poverty and some 58 million in extreme poverty in 2019.1 Through the Employment Recovery Agenda of the National Employment Recovery Strategy (NERS) 2021-2022 Task Force, TESDA took part and facilitated trainings and introduced approaches to restart economic activities, restore business 1 https://www. iio.org/wcmsp5/groups/public/—dgrcports/—dcomm/— publ/documents/publication/wcms_795453.pdf and consumer confidence, upgrade and retool the workforce, and facilitate labor market access. It has assisted 2.08 million individuals and benefitted 129,000 establishments, with 780,119 jobs generated.2 In order to comply with the growing demand of labor resources, TESDA is developing strategies on Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) for global competitiveness and social equity. However, these strategies may not be attained if TESDA's organizational structure, its own manpower and ability to produce higher quality of learning and training materials are still among the primary hindrances that prevent the progress of TESDA. This bill seeks to create a Department of Technical Education Training and Certification, which will take the place and absorb the current TESDA. It is high time to empo wer TESDA and enable the agency to fulfill its mandate as the leading partner in the development of the Filipino workforce. ■ In lieu of the foregoing, immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought NLEGARDA ■■ t-t. i. title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7796, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TESDA ACT OF 1994 AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The creation of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) paved the way in providing millions of Filipnos with relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education and skills development in support of the development of high quality Filipino middle-level manpower responsive to the country’s development goals and priorities. In 2018 alone, there are more than 2 million who benefitted in the agency’s various Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) program. For twenty-five (25) years, after the passage of Republic Act No. 7796 or the TESDA Act which was enacted on August 25, 1994, continues to be in the forefront in ensuring that Filipinos have access to technical education and skills development (TESD) that is not only relevant and efficient, but also accessible and of high quality. Despite much progress and lives changed, the agency is facing various and enormous challenges in order to adapt to the ever- changing local and global environment that the organization needs to focus on. In order to meet world standards, TESDA must address the need for modern facilities and equipment to level with the requirements in addressing the challenges created by the 4IR (Fourth Industrial Revolution) and other advancements that may happen in the future. It must also be bestowed with the police powers to impose sanctions and penalties to erring TESD implementers. These are among the limitations to what TESDA can do which can be ultimately addressed if the agency will be elevated into a line Department of the government. This proposed Bill seeks to repeal R.A. 7796 or the TESDA Act of 1994 and to reinforce the powers and organizational function of TESDA by turning it into a Department. The proposed Department shall become the primary policy formulation, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulating and administrative entity of the government for technical education and training and certification policies, plans and programs. It shall be headed by a Secretary, four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries. Page | 1 With the proposed legislative measure, TESDA will be strengthened as an implementing and regulatory institution of the Technical and Vocational Sector of the country’s trifocal education system. This measure is made in the interest of the Filipinos who wants to regain new skills and improve their well-being, and will be achieved in greater capacity vision as the transformational leader in the technical education and skills development of the Filipino workforce. The immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. TESDA's mandate is relevant since skills and training are essential to the workforce. To properly support such relevant activities, there is a need to revamp the system. By elevating the authority into a department, adequate budgetary support, personnel, and resources will be provided to fUrther develop the projects and programs of TESDA.

explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 7796 or the TESDA Act of 1994 was approved on August 25, 1994 which paved the way for the creation of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA). Sec. 2 of the law specifically mandated TESDA to carry out the government efforts in providing relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education and skills development in support of the development of high quality Filipino middle-level manpower responsive to the country’s development goals and priorities. By virtue of this law, the former National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), the Bureau of Technical Vocational Education of the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports (BTVE-DECS) and the Apprenticeship program of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) were integrated into TESDA. The merger of these entities was based on the recommendation of the Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM) that had undergone a nationwide review of the state of the Philippine education and training system in 1991. Twenty-five (25) years hence, TESDA has been the leading authority in ensuring that technical education and skills development (TESD) is relevant, efficient, accessible, and of high quality. However, the agency has been facing enormous challenges due to changes in the local and global environment that the organization needs to focus on. There are limitations to what TESDA can do which can be addressed if it will be elevated into a line Department of the government. TESDA must address the need for modern facilities and equipment in order to be at par with the requirements of the challenge posed by the Fourth Industrial Revolution and other advancements that may happen in the future. The bill seeks to repeal R.A. 7796 or the TESDA Act of 1994 and to strengthen the powers and the organizational function of TESDA by elevating it into a Department. The proposed Department shall be the primary policy formulation, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulating and administrative entity of the government for technical education and training and certification policies, plans and programs. It shall be headed by a Secretary, four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries. Carrying out the functions of the new Department shall be done by the various bureaus, service offices and Regional/ Provincial/ District Offices. Implementation of direct training programs will be done by the technology institutions. With the proposed legislative measure, TESDA will be strengthened as an implementing and regulatory institution of the Technical and Vocational Sector of the country’s trifocal education system. The agency will have a better capacity to fulfill its vision as the transformational leader in the technical education and skills development of the Filipino workforce. The immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MARK O. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) was established through the enactment of Republic Act No. 7796 otherwise known as the "Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994" with the aim to encourage the full participation of and mobilize the industry, labor, local government units and technical vocational institutions in the skills development of the country's human resources. The said Act integrated the functions of the former National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), the Bureau of Technical-Vocational Education of the Department of Education, Culture and Sports (BTVE-DECS) and the Office of Apprenticeship of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) as a result of a national review of the state of Philippine education and manpower development which was undertaken by the Congressional Commission on Education back in 1991. TESDA has been the leading authority managing technical skills education in the Philippines. Its major thrust is the formulation of a comprehensive development plan for middle-level manpower based on the National Technical Education and Skills Development Plan that includes apprenticeship, dual training system and other similar schemes. TESDA is also improving its language course offerings in partnership with foreign embassies and international organizations consistent with the strategy to reposition technical vocational education and training (TVET) for global competitiveness. The language-related courses —Arabic, Mandarin, Korean, Italian and French —will be added to the existing courses under its National Skills Language Center (NLSC). President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said in his inaugural address on June 30 that “sharpening the language skills” of Filipino workers, including Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs), is important to give them the advantage to survive and thrive in foreign countries. title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION TRAINING AND CERTIFICATION, PROVIDING FOR ITS POWERS, STRUCTURE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 7796 or the Technical Education and Skills Education Act (TESDA) was passed into law in 1994. It was created to provide relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education and skills development of the country’s human resources. Over the years, TESDA has established itself as the nation's leading source of labor in highly technical disciplines. The agency’s purpose was all the more highlighted during the pandemic when TESDA launched its TESDA Online Program (TOP) and “TESDA Abot Lahat ang OFWs” program which aims to upskill and retool workers in order to recoup job losses.1 Nonetheless, the current system leaves much to be desired and it is evident that changes must be had in order to make technical and vocational education in our country more efficient. Thus, this bill seeks to create a Department of Technical Education Training and Certification, which will take the place and absorb the current TESDA with the end goal of providing more quality and accessible technical and vocational education for all. In line with the policy adopted by its original proponent Senator Loren Legarda, this bill therefore likewise serves as a counter-part House Bill. It is for the reasons stated above that the passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ANTONIO B. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The creation of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) on August 25, 1994, through the merger of the former National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), the Bureau of Technical Vocational Education of the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports (BTVE-DECS) and the Apprenticeship program of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), was an offshoot of the trifocalization of education recommended by the 1991 Congresssional Education Commission or EDCOM. By virtue of Republic Act No. 7796 (TESDA Act of 1994), the TESDA is mandated to ensure the delivery of relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education and skills development and to develop high quality middle-level manpower responsive to the country’s development goals and priorities. However, after more than two decades of delivering relevant, accessible, and efficient technical education and skills development thoughout ther country, TESDA has been encountering many challenges and limitations that affect the performance of its functions, delivery of technical-vocational education and training (TVET) programs, and fulfillment of its vision. One of these is the need to sstrengthen its organizational structure and functions to keep pace with the advent of technology and the demands of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR). The frequent transfer of the TESDA from one office to another has also affected its functions, programs and projects, and delivery of educational services. From an attached agency of the Department of Labor and Employment, TESDA was transferred to the Office of the President and now, to the Department of Trade and Industry through executive order signed by President Duterte. Moreover, under the TESDA Charter, the TESDA Director-General shall enjoy the benefits, privileges ad emoluments equivalent to the rank of Undersecretary. However, the current and past two Presidents of the Philippines appointed the TESDA Director General with a Cabinet rank position or equivalent to a Secretary. By elevating the TESDA into a department, it shall be headed by a Secretary, four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries and attain self-determination to ensure permanence and continuity of mandated programs. This will also strengthen the implementing, regulatory, and policy-making functions of the agency, as well as make it more responsive and agile in the era of the 4IR and digital economy. The proposed Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) will not only improve the resource/budget allocation for TVET programs, but will also ably represent the TVET sector as a whole, changing its “second class” perception. More importantly, the proposed DTESD will have a better capacity to fulfill its vision as the transformational leader in TVET in the country. The immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF THCHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSH REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7796, OTHERVISE KNOWN AS THE TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS I)EVELOPMENT AUTHORITY OR TESDA ACT OF 1994, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution of the Philippines Article XII, Section 14 provides that "The sustained development of a reservoir of national talents consisting of Filipino scientists, entrepreneurs, professionals, managers, high-level technical manpower and skilled workers and craftsmen in all fields shall be promoted by the State." The Constitution likewise asserts in Article XIV, Section 1 that "The State shall protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and shall take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all." Also, Article XIV, Section 2 emphasizes the govemment's duty to ensure a complete and suitable education system that meets the needs of the people in an ever-changing environment. It also calls for support for students through scholarships and other aid, especially for those from underprivileged backgrounds. Additionally, it promotes alternative leaming approaches, including informal and community-based programs. Critical to the promotion of sustained development of a highly skilled work force, the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) was established through Republic Act No. 7796 (TESDA Act of 1994) on August 25,1994. Through the merging of National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), Bureau of Technical and Vocational Education (BTVE), and the Apprenticeship Program of the Bureau of Local Employment a3LE), TESDA is mandated to oversee skills development, set standards, accredit institutions, fund projects, and support trainer programs for the development of a top-quality middle-level manpower capable of adapting towards emerging issues and necessities of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. TESDA has aimed to set the direction, promulgate relevant standards, and implement programs geared towards a quality-assured and inclusive technical education and skills development and certification system for the country's technical-vocational education and training (TVET) system. The frequent transfer between various administrative entities has been driven by different factors, including changes in government priorities, administrative restructuring, and attempts to enhance coordination between TESDA and other government agencies. However, these transfers have often resulted in disruptions to TESDA's operations, delays in the implementation of programs, and challenges in maintaining continuity and coherence in policy and programmatic efforts. Recognizing the need for stability, coherence, and focused leadership in the promotion of technical education and skills development, this bill proposes the establishment of the Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) as a permanent and dedicated government agency. By elevating TESDA into a department, the bill aims to provide TESDA with the necessary institutional franiework, authority, and resources to effectively cany out its mandate in a sustained and coherent manner. The creation of the DTESD is envisioned to address the ever-changing labor landscape and its frequent transfers between different government offices. By consolidating efforts in TVET development under a single department, the bill seeks to streamline governance, enhance coordination, and ensure the continuity and effectiveness of policies and programs aimed at developing a skilled and globally competitive workforce in the Philippines. Approval of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution provides that: the State shall promote a just and dynamic social order that will ensure the prosperity and independence of the nation and free the people from poverty through policies that provide adequate social services, promote full employment, a rising standard of living, and improved quality of life for all (Sec. 9, Art. II); the State shall promote social justice in all phases of national development (Sec. 10, Art. II); the State shall give priority to education, science and technology, arts, culture, and sports to foster patriotism and nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development (Sec. 17, Art. II); the Congress shall give highest priority to the enactment of measures that reduce social, economic, and political inequalities (Sec.1, Art. XIII); the State shall encourage non-formal, informal, and indigenous learning systems, as well as self- learning, independent, and out-of-school study programs particularly those that respond to community needs (Sec 2[4], Art. XIV); and Science and technology are essential for national development and progress. The State shall give priority to research and development, invention, innovation, and their utilization; and to science and technology education, training, and services. It shall support indigenous, appropriate, and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, and their application to the country’s productive systems and national life (Sec. 10, Art. XIV). In this regard, the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) which was created by virtue of Republic Act 7796, otherwise known as the “Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994” is the government agency tasked to manage and supervise technical education and skills development in the Philippines. TESDA’s vision is a transformational leader in the technical education and skills development of the Filipino workforce, with a mission of setting directions, promulgating relevant standards, and implementing programs geared towards a quality-assured and inclusive technical education and skills development and certification system. Under the bill, the proposed Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) shall be the primary policy formulation, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulatory, and administrative entity of the government for technical education and training programs. With its gargantuan task, it is believed that by converting Page 1 of 15 it into a Department, TESDA will be strengthened as an implementing and regulatory institution of the technical and vocational sector. It will make this Agency in a better position to fulfill its vision and mission, believing in demonstrated competence, institutional integrity, personal commitment, culture of innovativeness, and a deep sense of nationalism. The early passage of this Bill, therefore, is earnestly requested. BIENVENIDO M. ABANTE, JR. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) was established on August 25, 1994, by virtue of Republic Act No. 7796, otherwise known as the “Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994.” Since its creation, TESDA has remained an essential contributor to the National Government’s mission of providing Filipinos with quality-assured technical education and skills development programs, and mobilizing technical-vocational institutions across the country. Over three decades after its establishment, TESDA continues to serve as the leading government agency responsible for setting the direction of, and ensuring the efficient delivery of, technical education and skills development programs across various sectors nationwide. However, TESDA has also faced challenges and limitations, particularly in today’s ever-changing local and global environment. To address pressing concerns such as strengthening TESDA’s organizational structure and modernizing skills training facilities, the overall system of the Authority must be enhanced through an increased budget, as well as sufficient personnel and resources. Hence, this proposed measure seeks to repeal Republic Act No. 7796, or the “Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994,” and strengthen the powers and organizational functions of TESDA by transforming it into a full-fledged Department. The Department shall serve as the primary policy- making, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulating, and administrative entity of the government for technical education, training, and certification programs. It shall be headed by a Secretary, supported by four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries. Such a reform is necessary to address challenges and implement policies consistent with the demands of the Fourth Industrial Revolution and other global advancements. Through this proposed legislative measure, TESDA will be further strengthened as the implementing and regulatory institution for the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector within the country’s trifocal education system. Most importantly, this measure is being filed to promote the interests and meet the needs of the hardworking and highly skilled Filipino workforce. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. JONATHA) T. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The creation of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) on August 25, 1994, through the merger of the former National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), the Bureau of Technical Vocational Education of the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports (BTVE-DECS) and the Apprenticeship program of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), was an offshoot of the trifocalization of education recommended by the 1991 Congresssional Education Commission or EDCOM. By virtue of Republic Act No. 7796 (TESDA Act of 1994), the TESDA is mandated to ensure the delivery of relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education and skills development and to develop high quality middle-level manpower responsive to the country’s development goals and priorities. However, after more than two decades of delivering relevant, accessible, and efficient technical education and skills development thoughout ther country, TESDA has been encountering many challenges and limitations that affect the performance of its functions, delivery of technical-vocational education and training (TVET) programs, and fulfillment of its vision. One of these is the need to sstrengthen its organizational structure and functions to keep pace with the advent of technology and the demands of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR). The frequent transfer of the TESDA from one office to another has also affected its functions, programs and projects, and delivery of educational services. From an attached agency of the Department of Labor and Employment, TESDA was transferred to the Office of the President and now, to the Department of Trade and Industry through executive order signed by President Duterte. Moreover, under the TESDA Charter, the TESDA Director-General shall enjoy the benefits, privileges ad emoluments equivalent to the rank of Undersecretary. However, the current and past two Presidents of the Philippines appointed the TESDA Director General with a Cabinet rank position or equivalent to a Secretary. By elevating the TESDA into a department, it shall be headed by a Secretary, four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries and attain self-determination to ensure permanence and continuity of mandated programs. This will also strengthen the implementing, regulatory, and policy-making functions of the agency, as well as make it more responsive and agile in the era of the 4IR and digital economy. The proposed Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) will not only improve the resource/budget allocation for TVET programs, but will also ably represent the TVET sector as a whole, changing its “second class” perception. More importantly, the proposed DTESD will have a better capacity to fulfill its vision as the transformational leader in TVET in the country. The immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION, TRAINING AND CERTIFICATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7796, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “TESDA ACT OF 1994”, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines, with its growing economy, faces a significant challenge in bridging the skills gap in its workforce. Technical-vocational education and training (TVET) play a crucial role in developing a skilled labor force capable of meeting the demands of modern industries. However, the country has long faced inefficiencies in the management and delivery of TVET programs. These challenges stem from fragmented governance, outdated curricula, underfunding, and mismatched industry needs, among others. The Philippine technical education system is divided among various government agencies, which results in inconsistent policies, misallocation of resources, and lack of coordination. TESDA oversees skills development, while DepEd handles secondary-level vocational programs. Higher education institutions (HEIs) also offer technical courses under the Commission on Higher Education (CHED). This fragmented structure complicates the implementation of nationwide reforms and makes it difficult to monitor and evaluate the quality of training programs. Likewise, the skills taught in many TVET programs do not always meet the evolving demands of industries. While TESDA has attempted to bridge this gap, there is still a lag in updating curricula and aligning programs with technological advancements and market needs. Many TVET institutions lack modern equipment, and instructors often receive inadequate training. These deficiencies hinder the development of a skilled workforce capable of competing in global markets. There are geographic and socioeconomic barriers that limit access to quality technical education. Many regions, particularly in rural areas, lack sufficient training centers and resources to support the growing demand for skilled workers. The establishment of a Department of Technical Education and Training (DTET) will centralize the management of technical education and training across various levels. This new department will be tasked with the integration of TVET programs under one cohesive strategy, improving coordination among government agencies, educational institutions, and industries. The DTET will streamline decision-making processes, ensuring that policies and programs are coordinated and aligned with national economic priorities. This unified governance will help resolve issues of duplication and inefficiency, leading to a more coherent and effective TVET system. The DTET will be empowered to work closely with industries and employers to identify current and future skill requirements. By fostering partnerships with private sector organizations, the DTET can ensure that TVET curricula are continuously updated to meet the demands of emerging industries such as digital technologies, renewable energy, and healthcare. Studies, such as those by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), have stressed the need for curricula reforms that align education with labor market needs to reduce the skills mismatch. The creation of a dedicated department will allow for better prioritization and allocation of resources toward upgrading infrastructure, purchasing modern equipment, and improving the professional development of trainers and instructors. This will ensure that TVET institutions are equipped to deliver high-quality education. Additionally, the DTET can advocate for more sustainable and long-term funding for technical education programs, ensuring their continuity and expansion. With a single department overseeing all aspects of TVET, the DTET will be able to implement nationwide strategies to expand access to training, especially in underserved regions. Through initiatives like mobile training units, partnerships with local government units (LGUs), and the expansion of online and blended learning, the DTET can ensure that technical education opportunities are available to all Filipinos, regardless of their geographic or socioeconomic background. The creation of the Department of Technical Education and Training in the Philippines is a vital step toward improving the country’s technical education system. By centralizing governance, aligning curricula with industry needs, improving resource allocation, and expanding access, the DTET will help produce a highly skilled and employable workforce capable of driving economic growth and meeting the demands of an evolving labor market. Through this proposed legislation, the Philippines can build a robust technical education system that supports both individual and national development. In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this bill is earnestly sought. DALE B. title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7796, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TESDA ACT OF 1994 AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In an increasingly competitive and rapidly evolving global economy, the country must ensure that its workforce possesses relevant, high-quality, and industry-responsive skills. While existing systems under the Republic Act No. 7796 created the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), there is a growing need to elevate and strengthen this mandate into a full-fledged department to better address persistent issues such as job mismatch, unemployment, underemployment, and unequal access to skills training. Thus, this bill measure seeks to establish the Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) as the primary government body responsible for the formulation, coordination, implementation, and regulation of policies and programs on technical education and skills development (TESD) in the Philippines. 1 The DTESD will be mandated to formulate a National Technical Education and Skills Development Plan (NTESDP) to guide the country’s manpower development strategy and ensure alignment with national development goals. Further, it will prioritize access to technical education for marginalized and disadvantaged sectors, including beneficiaries of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) under Republic Act No. 11310, to support poverty reduction and inclusive growth. By transforming TESDA into a full department, we can expect improvement in the quality and global competitiveness of Filipino workers, reduction in job-skills mismatch, expansion of employment and livelihood opportunities, strengthening of industry participation in workforce development and enhancement of social mobility. Finally, we recognize Rep. Mark O. Go of the Lone District of Baguio for filing a similar bill in the Nineteenth Congresses. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The culture and the arts are not just mere forms of expression and entertainment, more importantly, they are essential tools for nation-building. Arts and Culture are integral to a nation’s struggle for national identity as they can evoke dialogue, induce reflection, and charter new relationships and ideas—all of which are essential to a healthy society. This is exemplified through the works of renowned Filipino artists during the Spanish and American Colonial Period, which have helped shape a sense of national identity among Filipinos. It is the policy of the State under Section 17, Article II of the Constitution to give priority to arts and culture so as to “foster patriotism nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development.” However, with the transfer of the administration of cultural agencies to the National Commission on Culture Arts from the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports, effective promotion of the culture and arts took the sidelines due to the limited powers and resources of the NCCA and attached agencies. To this end, this proposed measure seeks to reorganize the National Commission on Culture and Arts into an independent Department of Culture or Kagawaran ng Kultura which shall be the primary policy- formulating, planning, coordinating, implementing, and administrative entity of the executive branch of the National Government that will develop, manage and implement the pertinent provisions of the Constitution regarding culture and arts. With more powers and better resources, the creation of the Department of Culture would be better equipped for the enormous task of preservation of the Filipino heritage and the promotion and advancement of cultural education among Filipinos. On behalf of the people of Parañaque City’s Second District, and for the common good of the Filipino people, the approval of the said measure is earnestly sought. REP. GUSTAVO S. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipino culture is rich and diverse. It is a reflection of the people's faith and a culmination of their stories and values. At its core, the concepts of "pakikipagkapzm tao/' the celebration of life, and oneness with nature have shaped our way of life for centuries. Deeply rooted in history and tradition, the State recognizes culture to have a significant role in our society as it defines our identity and unifies all Filipinos. Thus, the Constitution mandates the State to prioritize arts and culture, and to foster the preservation, enrichment, and dynamic evolution of Filipino culture to promote nationalism and human development and boost social and economic progress. Despite the positive impact of culture on our country and its people, culture is often ignored as a central factor in socio-economic progress and in enhancing the quality of life. For one, it is an empowering tool for local and indigenous groups and provides people with opportunities to come together. It is also environmentally conscientious to preserve older structures, which in turn attracts tourism, brings investments to communities, and many more. The importance and prioritization given to it over the past decades are not commensurate with its extent and value. Now, more than ever, the protection and management of our culture are necessary to ensure that its values and functions are maximized for the benefit of all generations - past, present, and future. Recognizing the role played by the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA) in implementing the cultural programs of the government and the importance of the culture and the arts in the enricliment of the Filipino identity despite the limited resources, such importance must be echoed in appropriate and improved government structures and increased funding. Therefore, this bill seeks to reorganize the existing NCCA into the Department of Culture, safeguarding its place in the priorities of the government and ensuring that the finest elements of our culture will be passed on for generations to come. label: SB 817
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Culture is a key driver of inclusive development, soft power, innovation, and national identity. Deeply rooted in history and tradition, it shapes who we are as a people and unites Filipinos across regions and generations. The 1987 Constitution affirms this by mandating the State to prioritize arts and culture to foster patriotism and nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development. Culture empowers local and Indigenous communities, fosters participation and solidarity, and contributes to human development, community cohesion, and socio­ economic transformation. It also offers sustainable pathways for development through the conservation of heritage structures, the promotion of cultural tourism, and the revitalization of local economies. Yet despite this vast potential, the Philippines has yet to establish a dedicated Department of Culture, unlike many of its neighbors in Southeast and East Asia. This institutional gap has led to fragmented policy direction, chronic underinvestment, and missed opportunities to fully harness our rich cultural assets. While the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA) serves as the primary coordinating and policy-making body, it is not a line agency and lacks direct authority over many of the cultural institutions responsible for implementation. As a result, the cultural sector remains underprioritized in national development planning and falls short of its potential as a strategic pillar of growth and national unity. According to UNESCO, cultural and creative industries generate nearly US$2.3 trillion in annual global revenues, equivalent to 3.1 percent of the world's gross domestic product (GDP). Their contribution to national value added varies among G20 economies, ranging from 0.7 percent in Mexico to 3 percent in the United States. These industries also provide employment for approximately 6.2 percent of the global workforce.1 In the Asia-Pacific region, countries like Japan and South Korea have successfully institutionalized cultural governance, generating massive returns. In 2023, Japan's anime industry (including television and film productions, streaming distribution, merchandising, music, events, and overseas licensing), supported by Agency for Cultural Affairs (Bunkachd) under the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), reached an all-time high of ¥3.3465 trillion (approximately US$22.3 billion). Of the total revenue, ¥1.6243 trillion (around US$10.8 billion) came from domestic sources, while ¥1.7222 trillion (about US$11.5 billion) was generated from international markets.2 South Korea's cultural content industry (Korean Wave or Hallyu), supported by its Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, has steadily grown into a high value-added sector marked by robust domestic sales and expanding exports. South Korea's cultural content industry grew steadily from 2021 to 2023, with total sales rising from W137.5 trillion (US$105.8 billion)3 to W154.2 trillion (US$110.5 billion),4 and exports increasing from US$12.45 billion to US$13.3 billion during the same period. 1 UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD). Retrieved August 1,2025, from https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10468573 In contrast, the Philippines' creative economy reached PhPl.94 trillion (USD 34,64 billion) in 2024. This marked an 8.7 percent increase from the PhPl.78 trillion (USD 31.95 billion) recorded in 2023, reflecting continued expansion across key creative sectors such as digital media, advertising, symbolic content, and traditional cultural expressions,5 These data points underscore a vital truth: countries that invest in strong cultural governance and infrastructure reap significant returns, not only in terms of economic growth, employment, and exports, but also in global influence, innovation, and national unity. In contrast, the Philippines continues to operate without a dedicated Department of Culture, limiting its ability to fully harness the value of its diverse cultural assets. With the Philippines'creative economy already contributing 7.3 percent to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and growing, the absence of a dedicated department risks leaving our rich cultural capital under-leveraged and fragmented. This bill seeks to address that institutional gap. By establishing the Department of Culture, it provides the policy leadership, operational mandate, and organizational structure necessary to protect, develop, and promote Philippine culture, both as a heritage to be preserved and as a resource to be activated for inclusive growth. label: HB 8939
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10586, INTRODUCING AMENDMENTS TO THE ANTI-DRUNK AND DRUGGED DRIVING ACT OF 2013, AND ESTABLISHING A VISION ZERO PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The implementation of Republic Act No. 10586, known as the "Anti-Drunk and Drugged Driving Act of 2013," was intended to curb road fatalities, yet over a decade of data reveals that transport-related deaths and injuries remain a persistent public health crisis in the Philippines. National statistics show a staggering increase in fatalities shortly after the law’s adoption, rising from 89 deaths in 2013 to a peak of 560 in 2019—a nearly 530% increase. While a temporary decline occurred during pandemic lockdowns, fatalities began surging again by 2024, indicating that the underlying risks of reckless driving and driving under the influence (DUI) have not been effectively mitigated. In the City of Cebu, a significant number of accidents were recorded to have occurred late at night, or at dawn, involving intoxicated drivers.1 High-traffic zones like the South Road Properties (SRP) are experiencing a troubling increase in incidents.2 Notable incidents include a pedestrian fatality on Valentine's Day 2026 that tragically claimed the lives of two senior citizens3 and several collisions involving sedans and SUVs during the New Year's celebrations of 2025-2026.4 Moreover, residential areas bustling with nightlife, such as Paseo Saturnino in Barangay Banilad, have also seen tragic events, most recently the harrowing Kingston Cheng case, where, in the early morning of February 8, 2026, a hit-and-run incident claimed the life of a young entrepreneur along Paseo Saturnino.5 This incident and the circumstances following the tragic death of Kingson 1 C. The danger of DUI is magnified by the unsafe physical infrastructure of Philippine roads. Unlike jurisdictions with highly developed “Vision Zero” infrastructure, such as Sweden or the Netherlands, Philippine roads lack consistent sidewalks, pedestrian overpasses, and dedicated bike lanes. Because pedestrians are often forced to walk on the shoulder or the literal edge of the driving lane, they are in constant proximity to moving vehicles. In a “forgiving” road system, a driver’s error might result in hitting a guardrail; on Philippine roads, the same error results in hitting a pedestrian. Therefore, the law must be stricter to compensate for the lack of structural safety. Under the current law, applicants for driver’s license must undergo alcohol education, officers can conduct sobriety/chemical tests on suspected intoxication, and penalties are imposed upon erring drivers. Yet recent incidents have exposed gaps in the implementation of the RA 10586, and the failure of the law to act as deterrence against further DUI incidents. label: HB 8947
title: AN ACT MAKING THE APPOINTMENT OF AN AGRICULTURIST MANDATORY IN MUNICIPALITIES WHERE AGRICULTURE IS A SIGNIFICANT INDUSTRY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE AND 482 (A) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to mandate the appointment of a city or municipal agriculturist in local government units where agriculture is a significant industry or the primary source of livelihood. It amends Section 482(a) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the “Local Government Code of 1991”. It aims to strengthen local agricultural governance by ensuring that qualified professionals lead the planning, implementation, and monitoring of agricultural programs at the local level. Agriculture remains a cornerstone of the Philippine economy, particularly in rural areas where it serves as the main source of income and employment. However, many cities and municipalities with strong agricultural sectors do not have designated agriculturists to provide technical guidance, coordinate programs, and support farmers. This gap weakens the delivery of essential services such as extension support, technology transfer, crop management assistance, and disaster response, ultimately affecting productivity and farmers’ incomes. This measure addresses this concern by requiring local government units with significant agricultural activity to appoint a qualified agriculturist. Institutionalizing this position will ensure that local policies and programs are science-based, responsive to farmers’ needs, and aligned with national agricultural priorities. It also enhances coordination between local governments and national agencies such as the Department of Agriculture DA, thereby improving the efficiency and impact of agricultural interventions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8948
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE NATIONAL FOOD AUTHORITY TO ESTABLISH RICE DRYING FACILITIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to mandate the National Food Authority (NFA) to establish, operate, and maintain rice drying facilities nationwide to support Filipino rice farmers, reduce post-harvest losses, and strengthen the country’s rice supply chain. Ensuring accessible and adequate drying infrastructure will enable the farmers to preserve the quality of their harvest and directly sell their produce to the government at fair and competitive prices. Rice farmers across the Philippines continue to face significant post-harvest challenges, particularly in drying palay during peak harvest seasons and adverse weather conditions. Without access to reliable drying facilities, farmers often incur losses due to spoilage, reduced grain quality, and lower market value. These constraints force many farmers to sell their produce immediately at lower prices to private traders who possess drying capabilities, thereby limiting farmers’ income and bargaining power. This proposed measure addresses these gaps by directing the NFA to procure, construct, install, and manage sufficient rice drying facilities that are strategically located and easily accessible to farming communities. It also allows farmers to use these facilities at no cost, provided that the dried palay is intended for direct sale to the NFA. This system strengthens the NFA’s capacity to procure high-quality rice while empowering farmers to secure better returns for their harvest. Furthermore, this measure promotes inclusive agricultural development, enhances food security, and supports the livelihood of Filipino rice farmers by improving post-harvest systems and reinforcing government support mechanisms. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8949
title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE MANDATORY INCLUSION OF BASIC FARMING AND AGRICULTURAL AWARENESS IN THE CURRICULA OF ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to mandate the inclusion of Basic Farming and Agricultural Awareness in the curricula of all public and private elementary schools throughout the Philippines in order to instill in the youth a deep appreciation of agriculture and its vital role in national development. It aims to equip learners at an early age with fundamental knowledge and practical skills in farming, thereby strengthening food security, promoting sustainable practices, and nurturing a generation that values and supports the agricultural sector. The Philippine agriculture sector continues to face persistent challenges such as declining interest among the youth, an aging farmer population, food supply vulnerabilities, and increasing dependence on imported agricultural products. Despite being an agricultural country, many young Filipinos grow up with limited understanding of where food comes from and how it is produced. This disconnect contributes to the declining number of individuals entering the agricultural workforce, threatening the long-term sustainability of the sector. This measure responds to these concerns by integrating basic farming concepts and agricultural awareness into elementary education. It empowers learners with essential knowledge on crop production, environmental stewardship, and the socio-economic importance of agriculture. Embedding these principles in early education will promote a culture of self-sufficiency, responsibility, and innovation among the youth. The bill further directs the Department of Education (DepEd), in coordination with the Department of Agriculture (DA), the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), and the Agricultural Training Institute (ATI), to develop age-appropriate, science-based, and practical learning modules. It also ensures that teachers receive adequate training and resources to effectively deliver the subject matter. Moreover, this proposed measure promotes holistic education while addressing long-term national priorities. It strengthens rural development, supports food security initiatives, and inspires future generations to actively participate in building a resilient and progressive agricultural sector. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8950
title: AN ACT PROVIDING POST-HARVEST FACILITIES FOR PALAY AND RICE FARMERS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide comprehensive post-harvest facilities for palay and rice farmers by mandating the construction of warehouses and rice mills, and the provision of essential equipment and machinery. This reduces post-harvest losses, improves product quality, and increases farmers’ incomes. It also aims to strengthen the agricultural value chain by ensuring that farmers have access to adequate infrastructure necessary to process, store, and market their produce efficiently. Despite the vital role of rice farmers in ensuring national food security, many continue to suffer from inadequate post-harvest support. The lack of accessible and modern facilities such as warehouses and rice mills results in significant losses due to spoilage, inefficient processing, and poor storage conditions. These challenges force farmers to sell their produce at lower prices immediately after harvest, often to middlemen, thereby reducing their potential earnings and limiting their participation in value-added activities. This proposed measure directly addresses these concerns by directing the Department of Agriculture (DA) and the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR), in coordination with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), to construct post-harvest facilities in rice-producing areas across the country. It ensures that every legislative district with rice-producing municipalities will have access to at least one warehouse and one rice mill, particularly during the initial phase of implementation. Furthermore, the bill mandates the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), in coordination with relevant agencies and farmer cooperatives, to provide the necessary equipment, machinery, and transport facilities to support the efficient operation of these infrastructures. It also empowers farmers’ cooperatives by allowing them to acquire these facilities through an affordable, long-term, and interest-free amortization scheme, thereby promoting ownership, sustainability, and inclusive growth within the agricultural sector. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8951
title: AN ACT GRANTING TAX DEDUCTIONS TO QUALIFIED PARENTS AND LEGAL GUARDIANS OF CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL NEEDS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to grant a fifty thousand pesos (P50,000.00) tax deduction from the taxable income of parents and legal guardians of children with disabilities. It provides them financial relief and support from the daily responsibility of caring for children with disabilities. Raising a child with special needs extends beyond ordinary household expenses. Families often face an invisible “disability tax” where a portion of their household income goes toward non-negotiable expenses like speech therapy, specialized tutoring, and transportation to medical facilities. These financial pressures often result in delayed interventions, interrupted schooling, or foregone treatment, which adversely affect the long-term development and integration of these children into society. This proposed measure empowers parents to sustain the long-term requirements of their children’s conditions without compromising the family’s basic economic stability. It also establishes clear eligibility criteria to ensure that the benefit reaches those who provide substantial financial support and actual caregiving to qualified children with disabilities. The bill reduces financial barriers faced by families, and enables children with disabilities to access the services they need to reach their full potential. It strengthens the State’s commitment to equity by recognizing that equal opportunity sometimes requires specialized support for those with greater needs. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8952
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE USE OF CROP CLIMATE CALENDARS AND LOCALIZED WEATHER INFORMATION, ENHANCING FARMER RESILIENCY AND CLIMATE-SENSITIVE DECISION-MAKING IN RESPONSE TO ADVERSE WEATHER AND CLIMATE EVENTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to enhance the resiliency and adaptability of Filipino farmers to adverse weather and climate events by institutionalizing the use of crop climate calendars, strengthening climate-sensitive decision-making, and ensuring access to localized weather and climate information. It aims to equip farmers with timely, science-based tools and knowledge that will enable them to anticipate risks, optimize planting and harvesting schedules, and minimize losses caused by increasingly unpredictable climate conditions. The Philippine agricultural sector remains highly vulnerable to typhoons, droughts, floods, and shifting weather patterns brought about by climate change. These hazards continue to disrupt farming activities, reduce yields, and threaten food security and rural livelihoods. Many farmers still rely on traditional practices and generalized weather forecasts, which are often insufficient to guide critical farm decisions at the local level. This measure directly addresses these challenges by mandating the Department of Agriculture (DA) to develop and promote crop climate calendars that are customized to specific localities. These calendars provide farmers with clear, visual guidance on cropping cycles, weather patterns, and climate-related risks, enabling them to plan more effectively and reduce uncertainties in farm operations. The bill further strengthens farmers’ capacity by directing the Agricultural Training Institute (ATI) to deliver continuous training on climate-sensitive decision-making. Through simplified and accessible learning materials, farmers will gain practical skills in interpreting climate data and adjusting their strategies based on evolving weather conditions. In addition, the measure requires the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) to provide regular, localized, and easily understandable weather and climate information directly to farmers and local government units. Ensuring that information reaches the grassroots level in appropriate languages and formats, the bill will bridge the gap between scientific data and on-the-ground application. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8953
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DISTRIBUTION OF IMPORTED RICE AT KADIWA STORES, CENTERS, AND OUTLETS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8178, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “AGRICULTURAL TARIFFICATION ACT”, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to ensure the affordable and accessible distribution of imported rice to Filipino consumers by mandating its sale through Kadiwa stores, centers, and outlets at actual importation cost, while amending Republic Act (RA) No. 8178, otherwise known as the “Agricultural Tariffication Act”, as amended by RA No. 11203. It aims to stabilize rice prices, protect vulnerable sectors, and strengthen government intervention in the rice market through transparent and targeted distribution mechanisms. Despite the liberalization of rice importation under existing laws, many Filipino households, particularly those belonging to low-income and vulnerable sectors, continue to experience high and unstable rice prices. Market-driven importation, while increasing supply, does not always translate to affordable retail prices due to layers of distribution costs, mark-ups, and market inefficiencies. As a result, access to affordable rice remains a pressing concern, especially during periods of inflation and supply disruptions. This measure addresses these challenges by authorizing the Department of Agriculture (DA), through the National Food Authority (NFA) and other appropriate agencies, to undertake government-to-government rice importation and ensure its direct distribution through licensed Kadiwa outlets. Selling rice at actual import cost will eliminate excessive intermediaries and profit margins, thereby making rice more affordable and accessible to the public. The bill further directs that priority be given to low-income households and vulnerable sectors in the distribution of imported rice. It also mandates the use of available government resources to support procurement and distribution, while ensuring transparency, accountability, and efficiency in program implementation. At the same time, it provides safeguards to protect local farmers by ensuring that domestic production remains supported and prioritized in national and local markets. This proposed measure balances the need for immediate consumer relief with the long-term goal of sustaining local agricultural development. It reinforces the State’s commitment to food security, price stability, and inclusive economic growth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8954
title: AN ACT GRANTING LIFETIME VALIDITY OF PHILIPPINE PASSPORTS ISSUED TO SENIOR CITIZENS, FURTHER AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 10 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8239, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PHILIPPINE PASSPORT ACT OF 1996”, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to grant lifetime validity to Philippine passports issued to senior citizens, thereby easing the burden of repeated passport renewals and recognizing the needs and contributions of the elderly sector. Under existing law, Philippine passports are issued with limited validity, requiring periodic renewal regardless of age. While this system ensures updated identification records, it also imposes logistical, financial, and physical burdens on senior citizens, many of whom face mobility constraints, health challenges, and limited access to passport processing facilities. The process of securing appointments, traveling to consular offices, and complying with documentary requirements can be particularly taxing for elderly individuals. This measure addresses these concerns by allowing passports issued or renewed upon reaching sixty (60) years of age to have lifetime validity. At the same time, the measure retains safeguards by allowing the government to limit passport validity when necessary in the interest of national security, economic stability, or other compelling considerations. It also provides for the issuance of new passports when required, ensuring that the integrity of the passport system is maintained. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8955
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A UNIFIED NATIONAL EMERGENCY HOTLINE “911” AS THE NATIONWIDE EMERGENCY TELEPHONE NUMBER FOR PUBLIC SAFETY AND SECURITY, PROVIDING ITS FRAMEWORK AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to strengthen the protection of agricultural workers and their families from the health and environmental hazards arising from pesticide use in agricultural sites. The duty of the State to protect the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology, extends to the millions of Filipinos whose livelihoods depend on agriculture. As one of the country’s largest employment sectors, agriculture sustains a significant portion of the population, making the safety and welfare of farm workers a matter of national concern. Despite existing government programs that support farmers through equipment, training, and research, protection in actual farm working conditions remain inadequate, particularly in areas where pesticides are heavily used. International and local studies have long documented the prevalence of unintentional pesticide poisoning worldwide, resulting in serious illness and thousands of deaths annually. Many farmers and farm workers also lack sufficient knowledge on the proper use, handling, and disposal of pesticides. These conditions endanger not only workers but also their families through secondary exposure in homes and communities. This measure therefore establishes concrete obligations for farm owners and operators to adopt safety standards that reduce pesticide-related risks, ensure early detection of exposure, and promote awareness and accountability. By prioritizing the health and dignity of agricultural workers and their families, the bill places their welfare at the forefront of public service and recognizes their indispensable role in sustaining the nation’s food security. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8956
title: AN ACT PROMOTING ACCESS TO QUALITY LEGAL EDUCATION BY PROVIDING FOR FREE TUITION AND OTHER SCHOOL FEES IN STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to promote access to quality legal education by providing free tuition and other school fees to qualified Filipino students enrolled in law programs in State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), thereby removing financial barriers that hinder deserving individuals from pursuing a career in the legal profession. Despite the critical role that lawyers play in upholding the rule of law, protecting human rights, and ensuring access to justice, legal education in the Philippines remains largely inaccessible to many due to its high cost. This has resulted in a limited and uneven distribution of legal practitioners, particularly in underserved and remote areas where legal services are most needed. By institutionalizing a Free Legal Education Program, the State affirms its commitment to democratizing access to the legal profession and addressing the persistent shortage of lawyers in public service. The measure not only covers tuition but also other essential school fees, including bar examination and licensure expenses to provide comprehensive financial support to law students. At the same time, the bill also integrates a mandatory return service component, requiring beneficiaries to serve in government agencies or the Public Attorney’s Office, thereby directly contributing to the delivery of legal services to marginalized and indigent sectors. The proposed measure aligns with existing frameworks such as the Unified Financial Assistance System for Tertiary Education (UniFAST) and strengthens clinical legal education by encouraging student participation in legal aid programs. By investing in legal education, the State invests in a more equitable justice system and empowers future legal professionals In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 8957
title: AN ACT DEFINING THE CLASSIFICATION, REGISTRATION, AND OPERATION OF ALL TYPES OF ELECTRIC MOTOR VEHICLES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to define and institutionalize the classification, registration, and operation of all types of electric motor vehicles (EMVs) in the Philippines in order to establish a clear, comprehensive, and responsive regulatory framework that promotes innovation, ensures road safety, and supports sustainable transportation. The rapid emergence of electric vehicles—including e-bikes, e-tricycles, e-scooters, and other electric mobility devices—has transformed the country’s transport landscape. However, the absence of a unified legal and regulatory framework has resulted in inconsistent policies, confusion among users and regulators, and gaps in enforcement. This measure addresses these issues by standardizing vehicle classifications, prescribing appropriate operational guidelines, and streamlining registration processes under the Land Transportation Office (LTO). The proposed measure establishes corresponding rules on where these vehicles may operate, the requirements for driver licensing and registration, and safety standards such as the mandatory use of protective helmets. By doing so, the bill ensures that electric vehicles are properly integrated into the existing transport system while safeguarding all road users. By encouraging the adoption of electric mobility, this measure contributes to lowering transportation costs, enhancing energy security, and mitigating environmental impacts. This bill advances the State’s commitment to a modern, efficient, and sustainable transportation system that is adaptive to technological developments while remaining anchored on safety, accountability, and public welfare. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8958
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE SCHOLARSHIP OF CHILDREN AND DEPENDENTS OF FARMERS AND FISHERFOLKS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide full educational scholarship to the children and dependents of farmers and fisherfolks, ensuring their access to quality education from basic education up to the completion of tertiary level, while establishing a dedicated fund to support this program and promote inclusive and equitable development in the agricultural sector. Farmers and fisherfolks remain among the most economically vulnerable sectors in the country, despite their indispensable role in ensuring food security and sustaining the national economy. Limited access to education continues to hinder opportunities for their families, perpetuating cycles of poverty and limiting social mobility. This measure grants comprehensive scholarship benefits covering tuition and other school fees, as well as essential support such as board and lodging, transportation, allowances for books, clothing, and food. It ensures that financial constraints will not prevent qualified beneficiaries from pursuing and completing their education, whether in public or private institutions. To guarantee the sustainability of the program, the bill establishes the “Educational Benefits for Farmers and Fisherfolks Fund,” with an initial allocation of Fifty Million Pesos (₱50,000,000.00), to be used exclusively for the implementation of the scholarship program. The measure designates the UniFAST Governing Board, in coordination with the Department of Agriculture and representatives from the sector, to administer and manage the fund, as well as to formulate the necessary guidelines to ensure efficient and transparent implementation. This proposed legislation strengthens the State’s policy of promoting social justice, improving access to education, and uplifting the living conditions of farmers and fisherfolks. It recognizes that education is a powerful tool in breaking the cycle of poverty and in building a more resilient and productive agricultural sector. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8959
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE FINANCING SYSTEM FOR AGRICULTURE AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT IN THE PHILIPPINES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10000 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE AGRI-AGRA REFORM CREDIT ACT OF 2009”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to strengthen the financing system for agriculture and rural development in the Philippines by establishing a more inclusive, responsive, and accessible credit framework, while repealing Republic Act No. 10000 or the “Agri-Agra Reform Credit Act of 2009”. It introduces a “Plant Now, Pay Later” approach that provides zero-interest financing, expands credit access, and aligns financial services with the realities of agricultural production cycles to improve productivity, increase farmers’ incomes, and promote rural economic growth. Despite existing mandates on agricultural credit, many farmers, fisherfolk, and rural enterprises continue to face limited access to affordable financing. The current system has often resulted in compliance-driven lending rather than meaningful financial inclusion, with banks opting for alternative modes of compliance instead of directly extending credit to agricultural stakeholders. As a result, small farmers and rural communities remain underserved, constraining their ability to invest in modern technologies, expand production, and withstand economic and climate-related shocks. This measure addresses these gaps by mandating all banking institutions to allocate at least twenty-five percent (25%) of their loanable funds for agriculture and rural development financing, while ensuring that such financing directly benefits rural stakeholders. It requires banks to design appropriate financial products tailored to agricultural cash flows and production cycles, including the provision of zero-interest loans without additional charges, thereby easing the financial burden on borrowers and encouraging greater participation in formal financial systems. The bill also broadens the scope of eligible financing activities to cover the entire agricultural value chain, including production, processing, logistics, infrastructure, agri-tourism, and sustainable or green projects. It promotes innovative financing mechanisms such as agricultural value chain financing and supports investments in rural infrastructure and digital banking solutions to reach underserved and remote communities. Furthermore, the measure strengthens institutional support through the creation and utilization of a Special Fund sourced from penalties for non-compliance, which will be used to finance agrarian reform initiatives, provide credit facilities, and support capacity-building programs for farmers and rural enterprises. It also enhances regulatory oversight and accountability through reporting requirements and the involvement of key agencies such as the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the Department of Agriculture (DA), and the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR). Transforming the agricultural credit system into one that is farmer-centered and development-oriented, the bill will support long-term food security and national economic resilience. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8960
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR GOVERNMENT FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS UNIFIED INITIATIVES TO DISTRESSED ENTERPRISES FOR ECONOMIC RECOVERY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide a comprehensive and coordinated financial assistance framework through government financial institutions (GFIs) to support distressed enterprises, particularly micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and strategically important companies, in order to accelerate economic recovery and preserve employment in the aftermath of economic disruptions. The economic impact of large-scale disruptions, such as public health emergencies and mobility restrictions, has significantly affected business operations across various sectors, leading to liquidity constraints, reduced revenues, and heightened risk of closure. MSMEs, which comprise a substantial portion of the country’s economic backbone and workforce, are particularly vulnerable to such shocks. Without timely intervention, these challenges may result in widespread job losses and prolonged economic stagnation. This measure strengthens the capacity of key government financial institutions, including the Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP) and the Land Bank of the Philippines (LandBank), to expand lending, rediscounting, and other credit support programs for affected enterprises. The bill further provides fiscal incentives, including tax exemptions and reduced transaction costs, to encourage participation and facilitate the efficient implementation of financial assistance programs. By enhancing access to financing, preserving business continuity, and safeguarding employment, this measure contributes to restoring economic stability, strengthening resilience against future disruptions, and fostering sustainable growth across key industries. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G.
