label: HB 8961
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING JOB PLACEMENT OFFICES IN PUBLIC HIGH SCHOOLS TO PROVIDE CAREER SERVICES TO THE YOUTH, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish Job Placement Offices or “Trabaho Centers,” in all public high schools to provide accessible, structured, and responsive career services to Filipino students as they transition from education to employment. Despite ongoing reforms in the education sector, many senior high school graduates continue to face uncertainty in choosing career paths and securing employment opportunities. The absence of institutionalized career support mechanisms at the secondary level often results in job mismatch, underemployment, and limited awareness of labor market demands. This measure addresses these gaps by embedding career guidance, job matching, and employment facilitation directly within public high schools. The proposed Trabaho Centers shall serve as hubs for career advocacy, assessment, and job placement services. They will provide students with up-to-date labor market information, access to job vacancies, and linkages with employers through coordination with Public Employment Service Offices (PESOs), local government units (LGUs), and relevant stakeholders. Through trained Career Advocates, the Centers will also administer career assessments, organize training and seminars, and guide students in aligning their skills, interests, and competencies with available opportunities in the labor market. By institutionalizing career development programs at the high school level, this bill empowers the youth with the necessary knowledge, skills, and opportunities to make informed career choices, enhances their employability, and promotes inclusive economic growth. It also ensures that education is more responsive to the evolving needs of the labor market. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8963
title: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 7432, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “AN ACT TO MAXIMIZE THE CONTRIBUTION OF SENIOR CITIZENS TO NATION BUILDING, GRANT BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”, TO EXPAND EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR SENIOR CITIZENS AND PROVIDE RELATED SUPPORT SERVICES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In the Philippines, resident citizens who are aged sixty (60) or older are considered senior citizens. They are entitled to certain privileges such as twenty (20%) discount and VAT exemption on essential goods and services, medicines, transportation, restaurants, and medical services, among others. The downside, however, of being a senior citizen for some is that they have a slimmer chance for employment after retirement. Republic Act No. 7641 or the Retirement Law provides that compulsory retirement for private sector employees in the Philippines is at age sixty-five (65), while optional retirement at age sixty (60) is allowed provided that they have served at least five (5) years. The same is generally true for government employees. While some may enjoy their retirement and can well afford health services and other essential goods and amenities, many senior citizens face the burden of financial limitations after leaving the service. They either have to rely on their meager monthly pensions and/or insurance benefits, or on their families’ financial aid for their daily needs. As of 2025, Filipinos aged sixty (60) and above comprise 9.6 percent of the country's 113.7 million population, just short of the ten percent (10%) threshold used by international agencies such as the World Bank to define an aging society.1 Philippine Statistics Authority data show that about 1.8 million senior citizens are employed in agriculture, wholesale and retail trade, transportation and other service sectors.2 For now, it is safe to say that we have a young society in the Philippines, but it is also necessary that the government provides opportunities for our senior citizens who are still able and willing to find a gainful employment. Republic Act 7432, as amended by Republic Act No. 9257 and Republic Act No. 9994, provides assistance for gainful employment of senior citizens. It recognizes that senior citizens who have the capacity and desire to work shall be provided information and matching services, and a tax incentive for private entities employing qualified senior citizens, subject to conditions. Hence, this proposed measure seeks to mandate the Department of Labor and Employment, through the Public Employment Service Offices nationwide, to assist senior citizens who are willing to be employed or re-employed through job matching and employment facilitation. This bill likewise intends to encourage the private sector to provide employment opportunities for senior citizens by increasing the allowable additional deduction from gross income to twenty-five (25%) of the total amount paid as salaries and wages, and by expressly including documented job-related training costs actually incurred for senior citizens, subject to the rules on deductions under the National Internal Revenue Code, as amended. This incentive may be availed by private entities, provided that the statutory conditions for employment incentive continue to be observed. This bill further provides that the enhanced deduction shall be available only to employers that maintain senior citizens at not less than twenty-five percent (25%) of their total workforce. This requirement is intended to ensure that the increased incentive is granted to employers that meaningfully and consistently invest in senior citizen employment. It also complements the existing statutory safeguards that employment must continue for at least six (6) months and that the annual income of the senior citizen must not exceed the latest poverty threshold published by the Philippine Statistics Authority for that year. ____________________ 1 Nat’l discussion on aging timely as senior population hits 11M. Available at https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1268289 2 Ibid. Lastly, this proposed bill shall grant free annual check-ups for every registered senior citizen in the country. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. LAZATIN, JR. label: HB 8964
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1340, ENTITLED “AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR AND FIVE OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN HUNDRED THIRTY-ONE PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE NATIONAL CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE PURPOSE,” RENAMING THE NATIONAL CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL AS THE NATIONAL CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL AND MEDICAL CENTER AND INCREASING ITS AUTHORIZED BED CAPACITY TO FOUR HUNDRED (400) 23 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 26 27 SECTION 1. Amendment of Section 1 of Republic Act No. 1340. Section 1 of Republic Act No. 1340 is hereby amended to read as follows: 30 “SECTION 1. THERE IS HEREBY ESTABLISHED UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH THE NATIONAL CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL AND MEDICAL CENTER, HEREINAFTER REFERRED TO AS THE NCHMC, WHICH SHALL BE A TERTIARY PEDIATRIC SPECIALTY REFERRAL HOSPITAL AND MEDICAL CENTER UNDER THE MANAGEMENT AND SUPERVISION OF A CHIEF OF HOSPITAL OR MEDICAL CENTER DIRECTOR, AS THE CASE MAY BE, POSSESSING THE QUALIFICATIONS PRESCRIBED BY THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH UNDER EXISTING LAWS, RULES, AND REGULATIONS. 41 THE NCHMC SHALL HAVE ALL THE POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF A GOVERNMENT MEDICAL CENTER AND SHALL SERVE AS A NATIONAL REFERRAL CENTER FOR PEDIATRIC CARE, TRAINING, AND RESEARCH.” 46 47
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 14 Republic Act No. 1340, enacted in 1955, governs the establishment and statutory framework of the National Children’s Hospital. While the institution has since evolved in function, patient load, and clinical complexity, its enabling law has not kept pace with present-day pediatric health demands, referral patterns, and service standards. 20 Over the decades, the National Children’s Hospital has effectively operated beyond the scope of a basic specialty hospital and now functions in substance as a tertiary pediatric referral institution handling complex, multidisciplinary, and subspecialty cases. Patient congestion, long waiting times, and high bed occupancy rates indicate a persistent capacity gap relative to national pediatric healthcare needs. 26 This measure amends Republic Act No. 1340 to formally rename the institution as the National Children’s Hospital and Medical Center, thereby aligning its statutory identity with its actual and intended role as a tertiary pediatric specialty and training center. The designation “Medical Center” reflects expanded mandates in advanced clinical care, residency and fellowship training, research, and nationwide pediatric referral support. 33 The bill further increases the authorized bed capacity to four hundred (400) in order to address sustained patient demand, reduce overcrowding, and enable the phased expansion of intensive care, neonatal, oncology, surgical, and other high- dependency pediatric services. The capacity increase is paired with authority for phased implementation to ensure fiscal and operational prudence. 39 The proposed amendments preserve the original public service mandate of the hospital while modernizing its legal framework, institutional classification, and service scale. Strengthening pediatric referral infrastructure is a direct investment in child health outcomes, equity in access to specialized care, and long-term human capital development. 1 In view of the foregoing, approval of this measure is earnestly sought. 2 3 4 5 6 REP. label: HB 8965
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A COMPREHENSIVE NATIONAL CARE PLAN TO ENCOURAGE COOPERATION, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND RESEARCH FOR THE EDUCATION AND SUPPORT OF PERSONS WITH AUTISM AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a comprehensive national policy that will ensure early detection, inclusive education, continuous support services, and full societal participation for persons with autism (PWAs). It aims to institutionalize a coordinated and rights-based framework that will eliminate discrimination and guarantee access to essential programs and opportunities. Autism is a lifelong developmental condition that affects communication, behavior, and social interaction. While awareness has increased in recent years, significant gaps remain in the Philippine setting, particularly in diagnosis, service accessibility, and inclusive systems. Estimates indicate that around one (1) in every one hundred (100) Filipinos may be on the autism spectrum, equivalent to approximately 1.2 million individuals nationwide. Despite this, support services are limited and unevenly distributed, with most resources concentrated in urban centers. Available data further show that only a small number of schools are equipped to address special education needs, and even fewer provide appropriate therapeutic interventions, underscoring the inadequacy of current infrastructure. The proposed measure addresses these gaps by promoting inclusion and safeguarding PWAs from discrimination in schools, workplaces, and public institutions. It provides for a unified and long-term national strategy that harmonizes efforts across sectors to improve service delivery, accessibility, and overall quality of life. Ultimately, this bill seeks to uphold the dignity, rights, and potential of every Filipino with autism by fostering an inclusive and supportive society where PWAs are empowered to thrive, contribute, and live independently. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 8966
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL POPULATION AND DEVELOPMENT POLICY TO ENHANCE THE COUNTRY’S DEMOGRAPHIC RESILIENCE, REPEALING FOR THIS PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 79, SERIES OF 1972, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In December 1967, the United Nations Declaration on Population was signed by 18 heads of states, where it was stated that: “The population problem must be recognized as a principal element in long-range planning if governments are to achieve their economic goals and fulfill the aspirations of their people.” The Commission on Population or POPCOM, was originally created in 1969 by virtue of Executive Order (EO) 171 which established a 22-member Commission on Population. Subseguently, Republic Act (RA) 6365, or the Population Act of the Philippines, was enacted into law on August 16, 1971, which established the “National Population Policy”. Under Presidential Decree No. 79, signed on December 8, 1972, the "Revised Population Act of the Philippines," reorganized the Commission on Population (POPCOM) as the central planning and coordinating body for national population policies, including serving as the monitoring agency for the Philippine Population Management Program (PPMP). It amended R.A. 6365 to strengthen population control, integrating it with social and economic development. In 1970 the Ad Hoc Commission on Population, created the year prior, recommended the launch of the National Population Program through EO 233. Toward the next decade, POPCOM was listed as an attached agency to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) by virtue of EO 123 in 1986. In 1990, EO 48, placed POPCOM under the Office of the President in order to “facilitate coordination of policies and programs relative to population.” The following year, EO 476, made POPCOM an attached agency of the NEDA. However, in managing the national population program, POPCOM was limited to family planning, health and welfare for decades – more focused on simple population control and family planning, rather than actually informing development strategies. It is high time that the national population and development policy is strengthened so as to manage population growth as a strategy for economic progress and improved living standard, and enhance demographic resilience. 1 In view thereof, immediate approval of this bill is requested. label: HB 8967
title: AN ACT DECLARING THE MUNICIPALITY OF SANTA MARIA, BULACAN AS THE CHICHARON CAPITAL OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Santa Maria, Bulacan, has long been recognized as the Chicharon Capital of the Philippines. Its thriving chicharon industry dates back to the early 1900s (around the 1920s), when it began as a backyard industry using leftover portions from butchered hogs, particularly native black pigs. Over decades, this local craft evolved into a major economic driver, with dozens of chicharon makers producing the town's signature thick, crispy pork rind—often featuring a generous layer of fat—that has become a beloved Bulacan brand and a popular pasalubong nationwide. The municipality's chicharon industry supports numerous livelihoods, contributes significantly to local revenue, and has transformed Santa Maria into a food tourism destination. Every February, Santa Maria holds the Chicharon Festival as part of its town fiesta honoring its patron La Purisima Concepcion, which features street dancing, cultural performances, and chicharon variety cooking contest centered on this iconic snack. This event draws visitors from Metro Manila and beyond, boosting the local economy and promoting Filipino culinary heritage. Formally declaring Santa Maria as the Chicharon Capital of the Philippines will officially recognize the town's historical and cultural contribution to Philippine cuisine. It will strengthen its identity as a premier food tourism spot and encourage investment in the chicharon industry, related agri-processing, and tourism infrastructure. This will also promote the preservation of traditional chicharon-making techniques and highlight the role of local industries in national economic and cultural development. This measure aligns with the State's policy to promote cultural heritage, support micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and foster tourism under the Philippine Development Plan and relevant laws on local government and cultural preservation. No substantial additional funding is required, as implementation can be integrated into existing municipal and provincial tourism and economic programs. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this bill is earnestly requested. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 8971
title: AN ACT GIVING TAX CREDIT TO REGISTERED PHYSICIANS PROVIDING PRO BONO MEDICAL SERVICES TO INDIGENT PATIENTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to incentivize registered physicians who provide free medical services to indigent patients. It grants them tax credits to be deducted from their annual income tax due, subject to the limitations and conditions provided under Republic Act no. 8424, otherwise known as the “National Internal Revenue Code of 1997”, as amended. The COVID-19 pandemic taught us the indispensable role of the medical profession in maintaining national stability. However, the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II) reported that as of early 2026, the Philippines only records 21.2 healthcare workers for every ten thousand (10,000) people1. This is less than half the World Health Organization’s recommended doctor-to-population ratio of ten (10) doctors per ten thousand (10,000) patients. Physicians who dedicate their time and resources to treat patients who fall below the official poverty threshold often absorb the operational costs of consultations and procedures themselves. However, despite their critical contribution, limited incentives exist to provide them economic relief, and to recognize their voluntary services. This proposed measure grants a tax credit of up to ten percent (10%) of the registered physician’s annual income tax due to further encourage their charitable reach. It also mandates a rigorous verification process to ensure fiscal integrity and transparency. It ensures that the tax credits granted are commensurate with the actual medical services rendered, and the requirement of strict documentation is required to prevent fraudulent claims. 1 EDCOM 2 Communications. 15 February 2026. EDCOM 2 Workforce Development Plan highlights large shortages in healthcare workers nationwide. https://edcom2.gov.ph/edcom-2-workforce-development-plan-highlights-large-shortages-in-healthc are-workers-nationwide/ This vital piece of legislation acknowledges that while the spirit of volunteerism is priceless, the State must provide the necessary fiscal environment to sustain it. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8972
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A NATIONAL TELEMEDICINE SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to formally establish a National Telemedicine Council and institutionalize the use of telemedicine as an avenue to deliver essential healthcare services across the Philippines. It ensures that Filipinos, especially those in remote communities, have access to clinical specialists in their region and to that of the public hospitals nationwide, within the safety and comfort of their own homes. Teleconsultation services have become increasingly accessible through mobile applications, hotlines, and official platforms of the Department of Health (DOH), as well as private providers. However, there is a disconnect between existing policy frameworks and actual ground experience. While Joint Administrative Order No. 2021-0001, through the DOH, Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), and the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth), provides the guidelines on the implementation of telemedicine in the delivery of individual-based health services1, its intended benefits remain unevenly realized in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas due to lagging digital infrastructure. This measure strengthens the delivery of essential healthcare services in remote areas and enables the strategic use of information and communication technology (ICT) during emergencies, disasters and states of calamity. It further mandates the education and training of health personnel to ensure competence in telemedicine systems and establishes the necessary regulatory oversight to ensure compliance with Republic Act No. 10173, otherwise known as the “Data Privacy Act of 2012”. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. YAP 1 DOH-DILG-PHILHEALTH JAO 2021-0001. label: HB 8973
title: AN ACT MAKING THE APPOINTMENT OF AN ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES OFFICER MANDATORY IN ALL PROVINCES, CITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES, FURTHER AMENDING SECTION 484 (A) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991”, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to mandate the appointment of an Environment and Natural Resources Officer (ENRO) in every province, city, and municipality across the country. It further amends Section 484 (a) of Republic Act No. 7160, or the “Local Government Code of 1991”, as amended. Currently, the appointment of ENROs in local government units (LGUs) remains optional. This has resulted in several LGUs encountering problems with the coordination and implementation of programs on environmental protection, natural resource management, solid waste management, and climate change adaptation and mitigation. This proposed measure recognizes that LGUs serve as the frontliners in addressing environmental degradation and biodiversity loss. It ensures that each LGU establishes a competent focal person to develop policies, enforce environmental laws, coordinate with national government agencies, and implement science-based and community-responsive interventions. The mandatory appointment of an ENRO strengthens local environmental governance and enhances accountability in the stewardship of the environment and the country’s natural resources. It also aligns with the government’s efforts to ensure environmental protection and disaster resilience. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8974
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP AND RETURN SERVICE PROGRAM FOR DESERVING STUDENTS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide a legal scholarship to deserving and aspiring students who wish to pursue further legal education. It also mandates a two (2-) year return service program for the intended beneficiaries of said scholarship. The Philippine Statistics Authority, in its 2024 Census of Population (POPCEN), indicates that the Philippines has a total population of one hundred twelve million, seven hundred twenty-nine, and four hundred eighty-four (112,729,484)1. As of January 2024, the Roll of Attorneys listed ninety two thousand two hundred and fifty-nine (92,259) lawyers2 since 1901. While five thousand five hundred and seventy two (5,572) new lawyers3 joined the ranks following the September 2025 Bar examinations, the current lawyer-to-client ratio remains approximately one (1) lawyer for every two thousand five hundred (2,500) Filipinos. This restricts the access of ordinary citizens to essential legal services. The 2025 Bar examinations saw the highest applicant turnout in Philippine history, and highlights the earnest interest of many students in pursuing a legal profession. However, tuition fees in post graduate studies remain hefty, with tuition fees starting at One thousand five hundred pesos (P1,500.00) per unit in state universities and colleges, excluding living and review costs. 1 Philippine Statistics Authority. 2024 Census of Population (POPCEN) Population Counts Declared Official by the President. https://psa.gov.ph/content/2024-census-population-popcen-population-counts-declared-official-president 2 Supreme Court Lawyers’s List (https://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/lawyers-list-2/) 3 Supreme Court of the Philippines. 7 February 2026. 5,572 New Lawyers Take Their Oath, Sign Roll of Attorneys. https://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/20260207-PR-Events-Bar-Oath-taking-Final-resize.pd f This proposed measure incentivizes the entry of aspiring and idealistic youth into the legal field, ensuring the sustainability of the public legal sector. In exchange, the mandatory return service program directs these new lawyers toward government service, reinforcing the ranks of the Public Attorney’s Office and the National Prosecution Service, among others. This vital piece of legislation fosters a sense of patriotism, promotes social justice for the marginalized, and ensures that the investment in legal education translates directly into public service. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE ELECTRONIC HEALTH OR HEALTH SYSTEM AND SERVICES IN SUPPORT OF UNIVERSAL HEALTH CARE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to expand quality healthcare access to medically unserved and underserved geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDAs) via information and communications technology (ICT), referred to as the National eHealth System (NeHS). It mandates secure health information sharing across providers, and regulates telehealth services to ensure the protection of personal health data and the delivery of safe and efficient healthcare. Building on lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, this proposed measure addresses gaps in the country’s healthcare delivery system while making use of the transformative potential of digital technologies to ensure continuity of care to all citizens, especially during public health emergencies. Despite ongoing reforms, many Filipinos, particularly those in remote communities, continue to experience inadequate medical services because of distance, cost, and the limited availability of healthcare professionals. This bill strengthens the country’s digital infrastructure and integrates it with existing healthcare systems. Its passage will enable patients to consult healthcare providers without the burden of travel. It will likewise allow healthcare providers to deliver more informed and coordinated health service delivery. This bill further aligns with and strengthens the implementation of Republic Act No. 11223, otherwise known as the “Universal Health Care Act”, by enhancing service delivery networks and promoting equitable access to health through digital innovation. This vital piece of legislation affirms the State’s commitment to the fundamental right to health. It ensures that no Filipino is deprived of care because of distance or circumstance, and that every patient is given a fair and equal opportunity to receive timely and quality healthcare. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 8976
title: AN ACT PROMOTING ACTIVE TRANSPORT BY ESTABLISHING A SAFE PATHWAYS NETWORK OF BICYCLE LANES, WALKWAYS AND SLOW STREETS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize active transport by establishing a safe, inclusive, and interconnected network of bicycle lanes, walkways, and slow streets in communities nationwide, to promote sustainable mobility, improve public health, and enhance the overall quality of life of Filipinos. Rapid urbanization and increasing reliance on motorized transport have contributed to worsening traffic congestion, rising carbon emissions, and declining air quality in many parts of the country. At the same time, recent volatility in global oil prices, which has significantly affected fuel costs in the Philippines, further underscores the country’s vulnerability to external shocks and its heavy dependence on imported petroleum. These developments highlight the urgent need to diversify transportation options and reduce reliance on oil-based mobility systems. The proposed measure mandates local government units (LGUs), in coordination with relevant national agencies, to establish and maintain dedicated bicycle lanes, pedestrian walkways, and slow streets that regulate motor vehicle access and prioritize non-motorized transport. It also promotes the integration of end-of-trip facilities such as bicycle parking, repair stations, and changing areas, thereby supporting the practical needs of active transport users. By embedding active transport into local development planning and national infrastructure strategies, this measure advances the State’s commitment to environmental sustainability, climate action, and public health, while also addressing economic vulnerabilities linked to oil dependency. It aligns with the broader goal of creating walkable and bikeable communities that are resilient, inclusive, and responsive to the needs of present and future generations. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. It also ensures the continuous and effective delivery of education through blended and distance learning modalities. Despite their critical role in sustaining the education system and honing the minds of the future of the nation, teachers continue to bear out-of-pocket expenses for internet connectivity and communication services to perform their duties. label: HB 8978
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL STRATEGIC PETROLEUM RESERVE PROGRAM, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 334, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The recent escalation of the US-Iran conflict has brought on a global oil crisis, exposing the Philippines’ serious vulnerability to external supply shocks. With international shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz facing continuous disruptions and global crude prices reaching critical levels, this volatility undermines national economic stability and increases the cost of living for every Filipino. Currently, the Philippines relies almost exclusively on the Minimum Inventory Requirement (MIR) of private oil companies1, a framework that is increasingly insufficient for navigating long-term geopolitical emergencies. This measure seeks to strengthen our energy security by establishing a National Strategic Petroleum Reserve (NSPR), providing a state-controlled buffer that ensures the uninterrupted flow of fuel and shields the domestic economy from the impact of international conflict. The experiences of neighboring Asian nations demonstrate the necessity of establishing a reserve program to insulate domestic economies. Drawing from the recommendation of the International Energy Agency (IEA), an international organization founded to ensure security of oil supply among its member-countries, Japan and South Korea as IEA members maintain 1 Executive Order No. 134, Series of 2002 entitled, “Requiring Oil Companies and Bulk Suppliers to Maintain a Sufficient Minimum Inventory of Petroleum, for Purposes of Ensuring Continuity, Adequacy, and Stability of Crude and Fuel Supply." massive stockpiles. As of 2021, Japan held 219 days of imports, while South Korea held 183 days. China and India, as non-IEA members, have also built their own state-owned reserves. China operates nine major stockpiles with a 37.7 million-ton capacity, while India manages three sites through a dedicated government-owned entity.2 A key feature of this proposed measure is the amendment of Presidential Decree No. 334 to explicitly mandate the Philippine National Oil Company (PNOC) to establish, manage, and administer the National Strategic Petroleum Reserve program of the Philippines. The bill likewise mandates a physical reserve equivalent to 120% of the 90-day oil requirements specifically for Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. The measure also seeks to establish a Special Trust Fund sourced from 25% of the previous year’s total annual excise tax collections and provides an exemption from the National Government Procurement Act (RA 12009), allowing for more responsive and competitive acquisition strategies. Likewise, the President is granted the authority to suspend the program during periods of prolonged market stability, which ensures that public funds remain fluid and available for other priority national projects, while maintaining a standby mechanism for immediate reinstatement the moment national security demands it. By establishing a sufficient buffer, the Philippines shifts from a reactive position to a proactive energy security framework, protecting Filipino consumers and the national economy from the unpredictable shocks of the global energy market. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. SERGIO C. DAGOOC REP. PRESLEY C. DE JESUS APEC Party-List PhilRECA Party-List 2 Navarro, A. M. May 2022. label: HB 8979
title: AN ACT REPEALING BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 36, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “AN ACT IMPOSING AN ENERGY TAX ON ELECTRIC POWER CONSUMPTION”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Batas Pambansa Blg. 36, enacted on September 7, 1979, imposes an energy tax on the monthly electric power consumption of every residential customer of electric utilities. The tax is structured based on consumption levels: Consumption Bracket Tax imposed Not over 650kWh Exempt 650kWh to 1,000kWh P0.10 per kWh in excess of 650kWh 1,000kWh to 1,500kWh P35.00 plus P0.20 per kWh in excess of 1,000kWh Over 1,500kWh P135.00 plus P0.35 per kWh in excess of 1,500kWh The primary objective of BP 36 was energy conservation and promoting the efficient utilization of electric power. At the time of its enactment in 1979, the Philippines was grappling with the global oil crisis, necessitating fiscal measures to curb excessive energy consumption, particularly among high- volume residential users. The law acted as a progressive "penalty" for higher consumption to discourage waste. Almost fifty years had passed since the enactment of this law, and the energy landscape has shifted to a complex, restructured market. The imposition of a "conservation tax" on top of billing components is incompatible in an era where the state aims to lower electricity costs for global competitiveness. Today, end-users already bear the weight of a 12% Value-Added Tax (VAT) on all components of the electric bill, system loss charges, universal charges, among others. Furthermore, the thresholds set in 1979, where 650 kWh was considered the "luxury" ceiling, do not reflect modern consumption patterns, where increased reliance on appliances and technology has made such levels common. Repealing Batas Pambansa Blg. 36 is a necessary step to streamline the Philippine electric power sector's tax structure, provide immediate relief to consumers, and eliminate a token levy that no longer serves its original purpose in a fully unbundled and competitive power market. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. SERGIO C. DAGOOC REP. PRESLEY C. label: HB 8980
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL ENERGY POLICY AND FRAMEWORK FOR A CLEAN AND JUST ENERGY TRANSITION IN THE COUNTRY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines stands at a critical moment in its pursuit of sustainable economic growth and resilience. While the country has historically relied on fossil-based energy sources to drive development, the escalating threats of climate change warrant a substantial change in our national energy policy. This bill seeks to institutionalize a clean and just energy transition framework that balances the urgent need for decarbonization with the essential requirements of energy security and economic equity. Current global energy trends and international commitments under the Paris Agreement demand a concrete move toward renewable and clean energy systems. By setting a moratorium on new fossil fuel power plants and establishing a clear roadmap for the phase-out of existing systems, this measure ensures that the Philippines remains competitive in a global market that is rapidly prioritizing "green" investments. Furthermore, the inclusion of a Carbon Tax mechanism creates a necessary fiscal deterrent against high- emissions activities, while the prohibition on passing these costs to end- consumers ensures that the burden of transition remains with the industrial emitters rather than the Filipino households. An important anchor of this legislation is the principle of a "Just Transition." Recognizing that a shift away from fossil fuels could disrupt the livelihoods of thousands of workers in the coal and transport sectors, the bill mandates comprehensive labor protection and retraining programs. By involving agencies such as DOLE and TESDA, the state guarantees that the workforce is equipped with the skills necessary to thrive in the emerging energy industry. Finally, this bill provides the necessary institutional mechanisms by empowering the Climate Change Commission to lead a multi-sectoral technical working group. This "whole-of-government" approach harmonizes existing law, including the Renewable Energy Act and the Electric Vehicle Industry Development Act, into a single, cohesive Energy Transition Plan. By providing clear national targets and a stable regulatory environment, this Act will attract sustainable investments, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and secure a cleaner, more resilient future for all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. SERGIO C. DAGOOC REP. PRESLEY C. label: HB 8984
title: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 183 OF ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS "THE REVISED PENAL CODE", AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11594, PROVIDING FOR AN INCREASED PENALTY FOR PERJURY COMMITTED THROUGH FABRICATED CRIMINAL COMPLAINT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE “A false witness will not go unpunished, and he who breathes out lies will perish.” — Proverbs 19:9 Truthfulness in sworn statements and judicial proceedings is a fundamental pillar of the justice system. The integrity of affidavits, testimonies, and criminal complaints is essential to the fair administration of justice, the protection of individual rights, and the preservation of public trust in legal institutions. When individuals deliberately make false statements under oath, particularly through fabricated criminal complaints, they do not merely commit perjury—they weaponize the legal system against innocent persons. Under existing law, perjury is penalized; however, the current penalties may not sufficiently address the gravity of cases where false statements are used to maliciously impute serious crimes upon another person. Fabricated criminal complaints can lead to wrongful arrests, prolonged detention, reputational damage, financial loss, and severe emotional and psychological harm to the accused. In some instances, individuals may suffer consequences equivalent to those of actual offenders, despite being entirely innocent. This proposed measure seeks to strengthen accountability by imposing a penalty commensurate to the seriousness of the false accusation. Where perjury is committed through the execution of a fabricated criminal complaint, affidavit, or sworn statement falsely imputing the commission of a crime, and where the penalty for such falsely imputed offense is higher than the existing penalty for perjury, the law shall impose a penalty equivalent to that prescribed for the offense falsely alleged. By aligning the penalty with the gravity of the harm caused, the measure aims to deter the misuse of legal processes, uphold the sanctity of sworn declarations, and protect individuals from malicious and baseless accusations. It reinforces the principle that the justice system must not be exploited as a tool for harassment, coercion, or personal vendetta. 1 Ultimately, this bill affirms the State’s commitment to truth, accountability, and fairness in the administration of justice. Strengthening penalties for perjury committed through fabricated criminal complaints serves not only as a deterrent but also as a safeguard against the erosion of public confidence in the legal system. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8985
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE FULL DISCLOSURE OF GOVERNMENT TRANSACTIONS THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A DIGITAL BUDGET PORTAL TO ENHANCE TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN THE PHILIPPINE BUDGET PROCESS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Citizen Access and Disclosure of Expenditures for National Accountability (CADENA) Act seeks to institutionalize a modern, tamper-resistant, and publicly accessible digital system for the disclosure of all national government budget documents and fiscal transactions. For years, the fight against corruption has been undermined by fragmented disclosure practices, opaque procurement systems, inconsistent data formats, and delayed publication of crucial budget information. Numerous scandals involving anomalous fund releases, questionable procurement awards, and undisclosed project modifications have revealed how gaps in transparency allow irregularities to flourish. These scandals have eroded public trust and demonstrated the urgent need for structural reform, not just case-by-case investigation. This measure addresses that need by establishing CADENA, a unified digital budget portal where all national government departments, agencies, and government- owned and controlled corporations are mandated to record and publish their budget preparation documents, fund releases, procurement records, audit findings, and other fiscal data in structured, machine-readable, verifiable, and tamper-resistant formats. The system is anchored on data integrity, security, interoperability, and traceability, ensuring the public can follow every peso from authorization to disbursement and final use. The Act creates a multi-stakeholder National Budget Transparency and Accountability Council (NBTAC) composed of key government oversight bodies and citizen-sector representatives to govern standards, enforce compliance, and ensure independent monitoring. A phased implementation timeline ensures readiness while preventing indefinite delays. Administrative and criminal penalties are included to deter non-disclosure, falsification, concealment, or destruction of mandated records. By enabling real-time public access to linked budget-cycle datasets, CADENA strengthens oversight by Congress, COA, civil society, the media, and the general public. It helps close systemic loopholes exploited in past corruption cases and shifts 1 transparency from a discretionary promise into a mandatory, enforceable, and technologically safeguarded public right. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8986
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE ADOPTION OF DIGITAL PAYMENTS FOR FINANCIAL TRANSACTIONS OF THE GOVERNMENT AND ALL MERCHANTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The rapid advancement of digital technology has transformed the way economies function, particularly in the movement of money and financial services. Digital payment systems have become essential tools for improving financial efficiency, reducing transaction costs, strengthening transparency, and expanding financial inclusion. For governments, the adoption of digital payments also enhances accountability in the handling of public funds and minimizes leakages associated with manual and cash- based transactions. In the Philippines, while significant progress has been made in promoting digital financial services, the adoption of digital payments across government institutions and among merchants remains uneven. Many government collections and disbursements are still conducted through traditional processes that are time-consuming, costly, and vulnerable to inefficiencies. Likewise, many micro, small, and medium enterprises, particularly in the informal sector, still lack access to safe and affordable digital payment systems that would allow them to participate fully in the modern digital economy. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize the adoption of digital payments in government transactions and promote their wider use among merchants and enterprises. By mandating the use of secure and interoperable digital payment systems for government disbursements and collections, the measure aims to improve efficiency, transparency, and service delivery across public institutions. At the same time, it encourages the development of a competitive and inclusive digital payments ecosystem that enables merchants of all sizes, including micro and small enterprises, to adopt digital payment capabilities without undue burden. The bill also emphasizes consumer protection, data privacy, and cybersecurity safeguards to ensure that digital payment systems operate in a manner that protects users while maintaining public trust. Furthermore, it supports interoperability among payment platforms and promotes financial literacy and capacity-building initiatives to assist both government entities and private merchants in transitioning toward digital payment solutions. 1 By advancing the use of digital payments nationwide, this measure supports the country’s broader goal of building a more transparent, efficient, and inclusive financial system, while accelerating the transition toward a resilient and cash-lite digital economy. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8987
title: AN ACT PROTECTING THE RIGHT TO TRAVEL OF FILIPINO CITIZENS BY INSTITUTING RIGHTS-BASED SAFEGUARDS IN OUTBOUND IMMIGRATION PROCEDURES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The right to travel is a fundamental liberty afforded to every Filipino citizen under Section 6, Article III of the 1987 Constitution. It is an essential component of personal freedom, economic participation, and global engagement. However, in recent years, concerns have been raised regarding the inconsistent, opaque, and at times arbitrary implementation of outbound immigration procedures, particularly in cases involving the denial of departure or so-called “offloading” of Filipino travelers. While the State has a legitimate interest in preventing human trafficking, enforcing immigration laws, and safeguarding national security, these objectives must be pursued within the bounds of due process, transparency, and respect for individual rights. Reports of travelers being denied departure based on unclear standards, discretionary profiling, or undocumented suspicions highlight the urgent need to establish clear legal parameters and institutional safeguards governing such actions. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize a rights-based and rule-bound framework for outbound immigration control. It clearly defines the lawful grounds upon which a Filipino citizen may be denied departure, limiting such authority to verifiable and documented bases, including court-issued orders, active warrants of arrest, and formally endorsed investigations related to trafficking or national security concerns. The bill further mandates the adoption of intelligence-driven, risk-based screening protocols that move away from subjective profiling and toward data- informed and inter-agency coordinated approaches. By aligning immigration practices with international best practices, the measure ensures that the presumption of good faith remains the default, and that heightened scrutiny is grounded in legitimate and defensible indicators. To strengthen accountability, the measure requires the written documentation of all denial-of-departure decisions and guarantees affected individuals the right to administrative review. It also mandates public transparency in travel requirements and 1 provides for regular training of immigration officers on human rights and anti-trafficking standards. Ultimately, this bill seeks to restore public confidence in immigration processes by ensuring that the power to restrict travel is exercised lawfully, consistently, and with full respect for the rights and dignity of every Filipino. Lastly, it affirms that the protection of the national security on one hand, and that of individual liberties on the other hand, are not mutually exclusive but must be pursued together within a framework of accountability and justice. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8988
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING SUPPORT FOR PUBLIC BASIC EDUCATION SCHOOLS IN GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED AND DISADVANTAGED AREAS (GIDA) AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Education remains one of the most powerful tools for breaking the cycle of poverty and empowering communities. Yet for many Filipino children living in Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDA)—including remote upland communities, island barangays, and conflict-affected regions—access to quality basic education remains a persistent challenge. Long travel distances, lack of transportation, difficult terrain, inadequate school infrastructure, limited electricity and connectivity, and shortages of teachers often prevent learners from fully exercising their constitutional right to education. Despite the efforts of the Department of Education (DepEd) and local government units, existing education planning frameworks do not sufficiently address the unique geographic and socio-economic realities of GIDA communities. Many schools operate with inadequate facilities, multigrade classrooms, and minimal teaching personnel, while some communities remain without reasonable access to a school within a safe and practical distance. This proposed “GIDA Schools Act” seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive and targeted framework for improving access to basic education in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas. The measure formally recognizes GIDA Schools within the public education system and establishes clear indicators for their identification based on conditions such as remoteness, limited infrastructure, small student populations, multigrade classes, and the presence of Indigenous Peoples communities. The bill further mandates the development of a National GIDA Schools Mapping System to guide evidence-based education planning and resource allocation. Through this system, the government can more effectively identify underserved areas, prioritize infrastructure investments, and ensure that learners have reasonable geographic access to basic education facilities. Recognizing that education access challenges extend beyond school buildings alone, the measure promotes inter-agency collaboration involving key institutions such as the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) for access roads, the 1 Department of Energy (DOE) and National Electrification Administration (NEA) for electrification, and the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) for connectivity. Such coordinated efforts are essential to addressing the broader structural barriers faced by learners in remote communities. The bill also provides targeted support for teachers and non-teaching personnel assigned to GIDA Schools, including hardship allowances, mobility support, housing assistance, professional development opportunities, and localized recruitment strategies that prioritize community-based educators and Indigenous Knowledge holders. Importantly, the measure affirms the rights of Indigenous Cultural Communities and Indigenous Peoples, ensuring that educational initiatives within ancestral domains comply with the Indigenous Peoples’ Rights Act (IPRA) and incorporate Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Practices (IKSP) into the learning process where appropriate. By institutionalizing sustained government support for GIDA Schools, this measure seeks to ensure that no child is deprived of the opportunity to learn simply because of where they were born or where their community is located. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8989
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING PUBLIC BASIC EDUCATION SCHOOLS IN GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED AND DISADVANTAGED AND CONFLICT-AFFECTED AREAS, PROVIDING ACCESS ROADS LEADING TO LAST MILE SCHOOLS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The “Last Mile Schools Act” seeks to address the systemic educational gaps in the country’s most vulnerable and underserved areas by reinforcing the State policy to protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education. It specifically targets geographically isolated, disadvantaged, and conflict-affected areas (GIDCA) where access to basic education remains severely limited. To ensure the effectiveness and sustainability of education interventions, the bill provides for inter-agency collaboration to deliver complementary basic services, including: a) access roads through the Department of Public Works and Highways, to enable safe and efficient travel to and from schools; b) electrification through the Department of Energy and the National Electrification Administration, to power modern learning facilities; and c) ICT infrastructure through the Department of Information and Communications Technology, to bridge the digital divide. The bill explicitly protects the rights of indigenous cultural communities and ensures that the establishment and operations of Last Mile Schools respect their cultural traditions and comply with the Indigenous Peoples’ Rights Act of 1997 (Republic Act No. 8371). For this purpose, one of the criteria for the identification of Last Mile Schools is that at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the student population that is 75 shall be composed of indigenous peoples. The bill further mandates that Department of Education to design and implement context-specific programs for Last Mile Schools, including specialized training for teachers and school heads, appropriate staffing standards, and a distinct formula for maintenance and other operating expenses (MOOE) that reflects the higher cost of delivering education in remote and hard-to-reach areas. DepEd is also mandated to ensure that the learning outcomes are not obscured by national averages and that specific gaps are systematically identified and addressed. Recognizing the urgency of providing adequate, accessible, and culturally responsive education to learners in these areas, the bill provides for a time-bound five 1 (5)-year implementation period within which to construct, upgrade, and equip the necessary school facilities and support systems. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8990
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING MANDATORY PRE-AUDIT AND GEO-MAPPING REQUIREMENTS FOR GOVERNMENT-FUNDED PROJECTS, STRENGTHENING PREVENTIVE AUDIT MECHANISMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The effective management of public funds is a cornerstone of good governance. Ensuring that government expenditures are properly accounted for, transparently implemented, and verifiably delivered is essential to maintaining public trust and achieving national development objectives. However, despite existing audit mechanisms, instances of inefficiencies, irregularities, and misuse of public funds continue to arise, often due to gaps in preventive oversight and real-time verification systems. At present, audit processes are largely post-facto in nature, allowing irregularities to be identified only after funds have already been disbursed. This reactive approach limits the government’s ability to prevent anomalies before they occur and increases the difficulty of recovering misused public resources. Strengthening preventive audit mechanisms is therefore necessary to ensure that public funds are safeguarded at the earliest stages of project implementation. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize a system of mandatory pre-audit for all government-funded projects, requiring clearance from the Commission on Audit (COA) prior to the release of funds or processing of payments. By introducing a proactive layer of financial oversight, the measure aims to minimize the risk of irregular, unnecessary, or excessive expenditures and to reinforce fiscal discipline across government agencies. Complementing this, the bill introduces mandatory geo-mapping and geo-tagging requirements for government-funded projects, particularly infrastructure and capital outlays. By requiring location-based documentation at various stages of project implementation, the measure enables real-time verification of project existence, progress, and completion. This ensures that publicly funded projects are not only properly documented on paper but are physically present and deliverable on the ground. The integration of geo-mapping data into the pre-audit process strengthens accountability by providing objective, verifiable evidence to support disbursements. It 1 also enhances transparency, facilitates monitoring, and supports data-driven decision- making in public expenditure management. Ultimately, this measure seeks to shift the government’s audit approach from reactive enforcement to proactive prevention, ensuring that public funds are used efficiently, responsibly, and in accordance with their intended purposes. By combining strengthened pre-audit mechanisms with modern digital verification tools, the bill advances a more transparent, accountable, and trustworthy system of governance. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8991
title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE INSTALLATION OF STANDARDIZED PASSENGER SAFETY ACCESSORIES ON MOTORCYCLES USED FOR TRANSPORT NETWORK VEHICLES SERVICES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Motorcycle taxis have become an integral part of the country’s urban transportation landscape, providing commuters with a flexible and efficient alternative in congested cities. As their use continues to expand, so too does the State’s responsibility to ensure that public convenience does not compromise passenger safety. While existing laws and regulations address general road safety and vehicle registration, there remains no clear statutory requirement mandating standardized passenger safety accessories for motorcycles used in passenger-for-hire operations. As a result, safety practices vary widely among operators and platforms, leaving passengers exposed to unnecessary risks related to balance, stability, and sudden movement during travel. This bill seeks to address this gap by requiring all motorcycles used for motorcycle taxi services to be equipped with basic, standardized passenger safety accessories. These include secure rear handholds or safety rails and back-support devices such as top boxes with integrated backrests or equivalent attachments approved by the Land Transportation Office (LTO). These measures are intended to enhance passenger stability, reduce the likelihood of falls or loss of balance, and improve overall riding confidence. The measure recognizes the operational realities of motorcycle taxis by tasking the Department of Transportation (DOTr), through the LTO and in coordination with the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) and other relevant stakeholders and agencies, to develop technical standards that ensure safety accessories do not compromise vehicle balance, maneuverability, or compliance with existing road safety regulations. The bill further assigns responsibility to digital platform operators to ensure compliance among their partner riders, reflecting the role of platforms in regulating access to motorcycle taxi services. This shared accountability framework promotes consistent enforcement while avoiding undue regulatory burden on individual riders. 1 A reasonable compliance period is provided to allow existing operators to install the required accessories, while ensuring that newly accredited units meet safety standards prior to operation. Lastly, the measure mandates the government to provide such passenger safety accessories, without prejudice to operators shouldering it, to ensure that this requirement will not be a burden anymore to the working class of motorcycle taxi owners or drivers. By institutionalizing minimum passenger safety requirements for motorcycle taxis, this bill promotes safer urban mobility, protects the riding public, improves confidence of the passengers and ensures that innovation in transportation services is matched by clear and enforceable safety standards. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8992
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A NATIONAL PLAN OF ACTION FOR THE CARE, SUPPORT AND INCLUSION OF PERSONS WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition that affects social communication, behavior, and sensory processing. Individuals on the autism spectrum possess diverse abilities, talents, and potentials, yet many continue to face barriers to early diagnosis, healthcare, education, employment, and full participation in society. Families and caregivers likewise carry significant responsibilities in ensuring the well-being and development of persons with ASD, often without adequate institutional support. In the Philippines, services related to autism remain unevenly distributed and frequently inaccessible, particularly in underserved communities. Long waiting periods for assessment, limited numbers of trained specialists, insufficient intervention services, and gaps in inclusive education and employment support create substantial obstacles for individuals with ASD and their families. While existing laws such as the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability and the Universal Health Care Act provide general protections, a comprehensive and coordinated national framework specifically addressing Autism Spectrum Disorder remains necessary. This proposed measure seeks to establish a National Plan of Action for Autism Spectrum Disorder, ensuring coordinated policies, programs, and services across government agencies and sectors. The bill aims to strengthen systems for early detection, screening, and diagnosis; expand access to evidence-based health and intervention services; promote inclusive education and skills development; support employment opportunities; and enhance social protection and community-based support for persons with ASD and their families. The measure likewise emphasizes multi-sectoral collaboration among national government agencies, local government units, academic institutions, civil society organizations, and autism self-advocates to ensure evidence-based policymaking and effective service delivery. It also underscores the importance of public awareness and advocacy in reducing stigma and fostering a society that values neurodiversity and inclusion. 1 Ultimately, this bill recognizes that persons with Autism Spectrum Disorder are integral members of our society whose dignity, rights, and potential must be protected and nurtured. By strengthening institutional support and promoting inclusive environments, the State affirms its commitment to ensuring that persons with ASD are empowered to live meaningful, productive, and fulfilling lives. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8993
title: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL INTERAGENCY COUNCIL FOR FLOOD MITIGATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Flooding remains one of the most persistent and costly hazards in the Philippines, causing loss of lives, damage to property and infrastructure, disruption of economic activity, and long-term environmental degradation. Despite billions of pesos allocated annually for flood control projects, the country continues to experience widespread flooding. The problem is further exacerbated by the brazen system of corruption that drains public funds in flood control projects. The recent exposes and investigations on the flood control corruption issue reveal that the more fundamental problem is the lack of clear, comprehensive, integrated, science-based and cost-effective National Flood Mitigation Master Plan. Current efforts are fragmented across various agencies, resulting in uncoordinated budgets, overlapping projects, and, at times, conflicting priorities. The absence of a single, science-based and integrated strategy undermines the efficiency and effectiveness of flood control measures, wasting valuable resources and missing opportunities to implement sustainable and innovative solutions. A comprehensive Flood Mitigation Master Plan is crucial in addressing corruption in flood control sector because it will prevent the insertion of questionable flood control projects since priority projects are already identified and aligned with the national strategy. This framework will strengthen accountability and transparency in the allocation and implementation of flood control initiatives. Oversight will likewise be streamlined, as concerns about possible anomalies can be addressed directly through a Council established under this Act, rather than through fragmented district-level inquiries. This bill seeks to address this gap by introducing a multi-agency approach to solving the problem of flooding. This contrasts with the current framework where only a single agency – the Department of Public Works and Highways – dominantly carries the task of addressing the flood control problem. The bill creates the National Interagency Council for Flood Mitigation Master Plan, a high-level policymaking and coordinating body tasked with formulating, implementing, and regularly updating a comprehensive master plan. The Council aims to bring in all necessary expertise, Page 1 of 5 paradigm and people in one forum, harmonize programs and budgets concerning flood control, integrate scientific research and climate change adaptation strategies, and ensure stakeholder participation, including local government units, the private sector, and civil society organizations representing vulnerable sectors such as farmers, fisherfolk, and indigenous peoples. Through a coordinated, multi-agency and evidence-based approach, the Council will ensure that flood control efforts are not only cost-effective but also technically sound, socially inclusive, regionally representative, and environmentally sustainable. The creation of this body will help maximize the impact of public investments, prevent duplication of efforts, and ensure that the billions spent on flood control translate into real and lasting protection for communities nationwide. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8994
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE REIMBURSEMENT OF TRAVEL EXPENSES INCURRED BY FILIPINO PASSENGERS WHOSE INTERNATIONAL DEPARTURE IS DEFERRED OR DENIED BY THE BUREAU OF IMMIGRATION, SUBJECT TO ANTI- TRAFFICKING SAFEGUARDS, AND PRESCRIBING THE CONDITIONS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The right to travel is a fundamental liberty afforded to every Filipino citizen under Section 6, Article III of the 1987 Constitution. While the State has a duty to enforce immigration laws and combat human trafficking, such authority must be exercised in a manner that is fair, transparent, and respectful of other individual rights. In practice, however, numerous Filipino passengers have experienced deferred or denied departures due to extended immigration inspections, often resulting in missed flights and financial losses, even in cases where no violation of law is ultimately established. Concerns have been raised regarding the inconsistent, opaque, and at times arbitrary implementation of outbound immigration procedures, particularly in cases involving the denial of departure or so-called “offloading” of Filipino travelers. At present, there exists no clear statutory mechanism to provide relief to passengers who incur financial harm as a result of such deferred departures. This gap places an undue burden on law-abiding travelers, effectively penalizing them despite the absence of any wrongdoing. The lack of accountability mechanisms also risks undermining public confidence in immigration processes. This proposed measure seeks to address this gap by establishing a reimbursement mechanism for Filipino passengers whose international departure is deferred or denied by the Bureau of Immigration, in cases where such denial is not based on lawful or clearly established grounds. By limiting reimbursement to the cost of the outbound travel ticket and imposing reasonable eligibility conditions, the bill ensures that relief is targeted, fair, and fiscally responsible. At the same time, the measure carefully preserves the State’s authority to prevent human trafficking, illegal recruitment, and other transnational crimes. It explicitly excludes cases involving fraudulent documents, misrepresentation, trafficking indicators, or failure to comply with established legal requirements. In doing so, the bill strikes a necessary balance between protecting individual rights and maintaining effective border control. 1 The measure further introduces clear procedures for filing, evaluating, and resolving reimbursement claims, thereby promoting administrative efficiency, transparency, and accountability. It also mandates reportorial requirements to ensure oversight and proper use of public funds. Ultimately, this bill affirms that while the State may regulate the movement of persons for legitimate purposes, it must also take responsibility when such regulation results in unwarranted financial harm to its citizens. By institutionalizing a system of redress, the measure strengthens both the integrity of immigration enforcement and the protection of Filipino travelers. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8995
title: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL MOVIES, VIDEOS, LIVE PERFORMANCES, MUSEUMS, TOURIST SPOTS AND THEME PARKS, EDUCATIONAL VIDEOS AND MULTIMEDIA PROJECTS TO HAVE AUDIO DESCRIPTION OPTION
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to culture, education, information, and public life is a fundamental component of human dignity. Yet for millions of Filipinos who are blind, low vision, deafblind, or living with other sensory impairments, visual media and public spaces remain partially or entirely inaccessible. While Republic Act No. 7277 (Magna Carta for Persons with Disabilities), the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), the Marrakesh Treaty, and related accessibility laws affirm the right to equal participation in cultural and educational life, the Philippines has yet to institutionalize a comprehensive requirement for audio description in visual media and public entertainment venues. Audio description is not an alteration of artistic content. It is a parallel narrative layer that describes essential visual elements—actions, settings, facial expressions, scene changes, and on-screen text—during natural pauses in dialogue. It allows persons with visual impairments to understand and enjoy films, television programs, theater productions, museums, tourist attractions, theme parks, and educational multimedia on equal footing with sighted audiences. At present, access to audio description in the Philippines is inconsistent and largely voluntary. Some producers and institutions have adopted accessibility features, but there is no uniform legal standard requiring such inclusion. As a result, accessibility depends on goodwill rather than enforceable rights. This bill seeks to establish audio description as a national accessibility standard across movies, television programs, live performances, museums, tourist sites, theme parks, educational videos, and advertising materials. It aligns the Philippines with evolving global best practices in universal design and inclusive media production. The measure adopts a reasonable accommodation framework, recognizing that accessibility must be integrated into production and distribution processes. It further provides for technical standards to be formulated by appropriate government agencies 1 in accordance with international guidelines, including Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), and ensures coordination among cultural, communications, and disability affairs institutions. Importantly, this bill recognizes that accessibility benefits extend beyond persons with blindness or low vision. Audio description assists senior citizens, individuals within the autism spectrum, persons with learning difficulties, and language learners. Universal design strengthens inclusivity not just for a specific group, but for society at large. The proposed law also provides reasonable exemptions in cases where compliance would be economically burdensome, ensuring proportional implementation while upholding the principle of accessibility as the norm rather than the exception. In a nation that values family, culture, and shared public experiences, exclusion from media and public spaces is not a minor inconvenience—it is a barrier to full enjoyment of the benefits of citizenship. Accessibility must not be treated as charity. It is a right. By institutionalizing audio description as a standard feature in public and cultural content, this measure affirms the State’s commitment to inclusion, equality, and human dignity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 8996
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE INSTALLATION OF PLATFORM SAFETY BARRIERS IN ALL URBAN COMMUTER RAIL SYSTEMS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Railway systems are critical components of the country’s public transportation network, carrying hundreds of thousands and even millions of commuters daily. To illustrate, in year 2024 alone, the Metro Rail Transit-Line 3 (MRT-3) alone served 135,885,336 passengers which translates to an average of more than 372,000 passengers per day.1 With this sheer passenger volume, ensuring the safety of railway operations and station environments has become an urgent public concern. Incidents involving accidental falls, unauthorized track access, crowd surges, and deliberate self-harm attempts at train platforms highlight persistent safety vulnerabilities in the absence of adequate physical barriers.2 3 4 Platform safety barriers, including platform screen doors and safety rails, are considered effective measures in preventing accidents, injuries, and fatalities in railway stations. Such systems have been widely adopted in countries with dense urban rail networks, resulting in significant reductions in platform-related incidents while also improving crowd control, operational efficiency, and passenger confidence. In the Philippines, however, the installation of platform safety barriers has been uneven, limited to select stations, or omitted altogether, often due to the absence of a clear statutory mandate. This fragmented approach places commuters at continued risk and results in inconsistent safety standards across railway systems. This bill seeks to institutionalize railway platform safety by mandating the installation of platform safety barriers in all existing and future train stations nationwide. 1 January 9, 2025. label: HB 8997
title: AN ACT PENALIZING THE ABUSE OF DISCRETION BY REVENUE OFFICERS IN THE ISSUANCE OF UNREASONABLE TAX ASSESSMENTS, MANDATING JUSTIFICATION OF COMPROMISE PAYMENTS SIGNIFICANTLY LOWER THAN STATED DEFICIENCIES, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR GROSS NEGLIGENCE AND PROFESSIONAL MISCONDUCT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The power of taxation is a fundamental pillar of governance, providing the State with the resources necessary to fulfill its constitutional duties. However, this power must be exercised with utmost fairness, accountability, and integrity. In recent years, concerns have grown over the abuse of discretion by some revenue officers in the issuance of excessive, arbitrary, or unjustified tax assessments. These practices not only harm taxpayers—particularly small businesses and individuals with limited means—but also erode public trust in the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) and the tax system as a whole. The "Revenue Assessment Integrity and Accountability Act" seeks to address this systemic issue by instituting critical safeguards and mechanisms that promote transparency, professional diligence, and institutional accountability in the audit and assessment process of internal revenue taxes. The bill mandates the submission of sworn justification reports in cases where the final tax collected is significantly lower than the original deficiency assessment. It establishes a presumption of abuse or negligence in cases where such discrepancies are not properly explained, or when court rulings drastically reduce the BIR's assessments. These presumptions carry strong administrative sanctions, including dismissal from service, forfeiture of benefits, and civil liability to reimburse taxpayers for litigation costs incurred due to excessive or abusive assessments. Recognizing the collaborative nature of BIR audit and assessment procedures, the bill imposes solidary liability on all officials whose names appear in the routing and approval of flawed assessments—unless they can demonstrate that they objected or were misled. To promote internal reform and protect integrity whistleblowers, the bill introduces whistleblower protections and reward mechanisms for BIR employees and taxpayer representatives who expose systemic abuse. Furthermore, to ensure impartiality in oversight, it establishes an Independent Revenue Assessment Review Page 1 of 5 Panel under the Civil Service Commission—not the BIR—to evaluate justification reports and recommend sanctions. This proposed measure does not aim to hinder the government’s revenue collection mandate, but to professionalize and rationalize it. By holding accountable those who weaponize tax assessments for harassment, coercion, or personal gain, the State affirms its commitment to a fair, credible, and corruption-free tax system. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C.
