label: HB 9148
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE KALINGA PROGRAM TO SHIELD FILIPINO HOUSEHOLDS, WORKERS, FARMERS, FISHERFOLK, TRANSPORT OPERATORS, AND MICRO, SMALL, AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES (MSMEs) FROM FUEL-DRIVEN INFLATION, ENERGY SUPPLY DISRUPTIONS, AND ESSENTIAL GOODS PRICE SHOCKS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Fuel price volatility remains one of the most immediate drivers of increases in the cost of living of Filipino households, affecting transport costs, food prices, power generation, logistics, and the survival of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The need for an immediate and coordinated government response is underscored by the sharp acceleration of inflation in April 2026, when the country’s headline inflation rose to 7.2%, from 4.1% in March 2026 and 1.4% in April 2025. The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) identified the leading contributors to overall inflation are food and non-alcoholic beverages, contributing 31.9% or 2.3 percentage points, transportation costs contributing 27.0% or 1.9 percentage points, and housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels, contributing 23.2% or 1.7 percentage points. Food inflation likewise accelerated to 6.1% in April 2026 from 2.7% in the previous month, driven mainly by the increase in rice inflation to 13.7%, from 3.5% in March 2026. These figures demonstrate that inflation is no longer confined to fuel prices alone, but has already spread to food, transportation, utilities, and other basic necessities, thereby justifying the establishment of a coordinated, targeted, and time- bound national response framework.1 Consequently, the Department of Energy reported that as of 28 April 2026, domestic oil price movements resulted in year-to-date net increases of ₱44.23 per liter for gasoline, ₱48.96 per liter for diesel, and ₱57.99 per liter for kerosene, amid elevated global crude prices, geopolitical tensions, and foreign exchange pressures.2 The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas also warned in its 2025 Monetary Policy Report that 1 Philippine Statistics Authority. (n.d.). Consumer price index and inflation rate. https://psa.gov.ph/price-indices/cpi-ir 2 Department of Energy. (2026, April 28). Oil monitor: As of 28 April 2026 [PDF]. https://prod-cms.doe.gov.ph/documents/d/guest/oil- monitor_28-april-2026_male_reviewed_msdc_ayp-copy-pdf 1 domestic inflation could breach the government’s 2%–4% target range if Dubai crude oil prices average US$80 per barrel in 2026, even before considering second-round effects.3 This bill therefore provides a necessary, targeted, and fiscally responsible mechanism for government response. Instead of relying on fragmented or purely reactive subsidies, this measure, anchored on House Bill No. 8834 earlier filed, seeks to establish the KALINGA Program or the Komprehensibong Alalay sa Livelihood, Inflation, Negosyo and Goods Assistance Program, as a national emergency response framework to mitigate fuel-driven inflation, secure energy and essential goods supply, and provide targeted, time-bound assistance to vulnerable sectors. To further strengthen the responsiveness, integrity, and accountability of the measure, the bill introduces additional safeguards and implementation mechanisms, including a beneficiary identification to ensure accurate targeting and avoid duplication of aid, anti-hoarding, anti-profiteering, and price manipulation safeguards to prevent abuse during periods of supply and price instability, data privacy and cybersecurity protection to secure beneficiary information and payment disbursement, fuel and essential goods priority allocation to protect critical sectors and public services during supply disruptions, penalties for fraudulent claims to deter misuse of public funds and false availment of benefits and a mandatory public dashboard to promote transparency, public monitoring, and accountability in the release and utilization of government assistance. In view of the continuing threat of fuel-driven inflation and its direct impact on Filipino families, workers, farmers, fisherfolk, transport operators, MSMEs, and consumers, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. label: HB 9149
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE OPEN FINANCE FRAMEWORK, ENSURING CONSUMER FINANCIAL DATA PORTABILITY, ENHANCING COMPETITION AND INNOVATION IN THE FINANCIAL SECTOR, STRENGTHENING DATA PRIVACY AND SECURITY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The continued digital transformation of the Philippine economy has reshaped how Filipinos save, borrow, pay, invest, remit, and access financial services. Financial data has become a key economic asset. Yet, for many consumers, this data remains locked within individual financial institutions, limiting their ability to use their own information to obtain better, cheaper, faster, and more inclusive financial products. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas has already laid the regulatory groundwork through BSP Circular No. 1122, which established the Open Finance Framework in 2021. This framework recognizes open finance as a mechanism for secure, permission-based data sharing among financial institutions and accredited third-party providers. The proposed measure builds on this existing regulatory initiative by providing a clear statutory basis for consumer-directed financial data portability, interoperable data sharing, consumer protection, and regulatory oversight. The bill expressly seeks to establish a Philippine Open Finance Framework, ensure consumer financial data portability, enhance competition and innovation in the financial sector, and strengthen data privacy and security. The need for this measure is urgent. While financial inclusion has improved, significant gaps remain. Based on the BSP’s 2021 Financial Inclusion Survey, the share of Filipino adults with formal accounts rose from 29% in 2019 to 56% in 2021, equivalent to around 22 million additional Filipinos opening an account during that period. However, this also means that roughly 44% of Filipino adults remained without a formal financial account.1 Digital finance is also expanding rapidly. The BSP reported that in 2024, digital retail payments accounted for 57.4% of total retail payment transaction volume, surpassing the Philippine Development Plan target of 52% to 54%. This demonstrates that Filipinos are increasingly relying on digital channels for everyday financial transactions. 2 However, greater digital adoption must be matched by stronger consumer rights, clearer consent rules, secure data-sharing infrastructure, and accountability among financial service providers. Open finance can help close persistent financial inclusion gaps. By allowing consumers to securely share their financial data with accredited providers, Filipinos may gain access to alternative credit scoring, lower-cost loans, better savings and insurance products, improved digital onboarding, and 1 2021 Financial Inclusion Survey Report – Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas 2 2024 Status of Digital Payments in the Philippines – Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas 2 more personalized financial management tools. This is especially relevant for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), overseas Filipinos, workers in the informal economy, farmers, fisherfolk, and rural communities that often lack traditional credit histories. The measure is also critical for MSME development. MSMEs remain the backbone of the Philippine economy. In 2023, government MSME statistics showed that the Philippines had more than one million business establishments, with MSMEs comprising the overwhelming majority of enterprises. 3 Many of these businesses face difficulty accessing formal credit because they cannot present sufficient collateral, audited financial statements, or traditional banking records. Open finance can help bridge this gap by allowing lenders and fintech providers to assess creditworthiness using verified transaction histories, payment behavior, cash flow data, and other consented financial information. At the same time, open finance must be implemented with strong safeguards. Consumer trust is central to any digital financial ecosystem. The right to financial data portability must not become a license for unauthorized profiling, predatory lending, discriminatory pricing, intrusive surveillance, or the misuse of personal and sensitive personal information. The bill therefore anchors open finance on explicit and informed consent, data minimization, cybersecurity standards, accreditation of data recipients, consumer protection, and coordination among regulators, including the BSP, the National Privacy Commission, the Philippine Competition Commission, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Department of Information and Communications Technology, and the Insurance Commission. 3 MSME Statistics – Department of Trade and Industry 3 This proposed Act also strengthens competition. At present, established financial institutions often have structural advantages because they exclusively hold consumer financial data. By empowering consumers to direct the secure sharing of their own data, open finance allows responsible fintech innovators, digital banks, insurers, investment platforms, and other accredited providers to compete on the basis of better products, lower costs, and improved service. This promotes a more dynamic, inclusive, and consumer-centered financial sector. Global experience shows that open finance is becoming an essential component of modern financial regulation. Jurisdictions such as the United Kingdom, the European Union, and the United States have moved toward frameworks that recognize consumer data rights, secure data access, and standardized financial data sharing. The Philippines must not fall behind. A statutory open finance framework will help ensure that the country’s financial sector remains competitive, innovative, and aligned with international developments while remaining firmly grounded in Filipino consumer protection and data privacy principles. Ultimately, this measure recognizes a simple but powerful principle: Filipinos should have meaningful control over their own financial data. When properly protected and responsibly shared, such data can become a tool for inclusion, competition, innovation, and economic empowerment. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 4 FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YE

label: HB 9156
title: AN ACT REDUCING THE VALUE-ADDED TAX (VAT) FROM 12% TO 10%, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 106 (A), 107 (A), AND 108 (A) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to face mounting economic pressures brought about by rising prices of fuel, transportation, electricity, food, and other essential goods and services. These increases have been aggravated by ongoing global economic uncertainties, geopolitical tensions, disruptions in international supply chains, and volatility in global oil markets, all of which have directly affected the cost of living for ordinary Filipino families. Recent reports likewise indicate that inflationary pressures have intensified anew due to rising global fuel prices linked to instability in the Middle East.1 As an oil import-dependent country, the Philippines remains particularly vulnerable to fluctuations in global energy prices and external economic shocks. The Philippine Statistics Authority reported that headline 1 The Philippine Star, “Inflation seen to breach 4% as oil prices surge,” March 22, 2026, https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2026/03/22/2516087/inflation-seen-breach-4-oil-prices-surge 1 inflation accelerated to 7.2% in April 2026 from 4.2% in March 2026 and 1.4% in April 2025, driven largely by increases in fuel and transportation costs. This is the highest inflation rate within a three-year period.2 The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas has also warned that higher global oil prices may create “spillover effects” that could further increase the prices of goods and services across the economy.3 Notably, because the value-added tax (VAT) is imposed ad valorem on the retail prices of goods and services, including the excise tax component, government VAT collections rise mechanically as prices rise. The current crisis has therefore produced a fiscal windfall: The national government is collecting additional VAT revenue as a direct consequence of the price increases that are burdening Filipino households. At a time when Filipino households are struggling with the rising cost of basic necessities, the government must adopt responsive and people- centered measures that can immediately ease the burden on consumers. A reduction in the VAT rate, which is the single broadest consumption tax in the country, would directly address this burden by lowering the tax component embedded in the price of almost every good and service. The VAT system, by its nature, is a consumption tax that disproportionately affects low- and middle-income households, as a larger portion of their income is spent on daily necessities. While existing VAT exemptions on raw food and other basic necessities provide partial relief, the bulk of household consumption such as fuel, electricity, transport, processed food, and household goods all remain subject to VAT. Reducing the VAT rate from twelve percent (12%) to ten percent (10%) will provide 2 Philstar.com, Inflation Jumps to 7.2%, Highest Since March 2023, Philstar.com (May 5, 2026), https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2026/05/05/2525813/inflation-jumps-72-highest-march-2023 3 Mikhail Flores & Nestor Corrales, Philippine Central Bank Warns of Oil Spike “Spillover Effects” as Inflation Breaches Target, Reuters (Apr. 7, 2026, 9:18 AM UTC), https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/fuel-price-surge-pushes-philippine-inflation-above- central-bank-target-2026-04-07/ 2 immediate and broad-based relief by lowering the tax component of prices across the entire consumption basket. This measure is expected to help temper inflationary pressures, increase household purchasing power, stimulate consumer spending, and support economic activity during a period of global uncertainty. Moreover, a lower VAT rate can provide relief not only to consumers but also to small businesses and enterprises that continue to recover from economic disruptions and weakened consumer demand. By easing the overall tax burden on transactions, the proposed measure seeks to promote a more equitable and sustainable economic recovery. Unlike a suspension of fuel excise taxes, a VAT reduction reaches every household through every taxable transaction, is verifiable by consumers on every receipt, and can be offset through progressive revenue measures to mitigate or neutralize the fiscal loss. This bill therefore seeks to amend Sections 106 (A), 107 (A), and 108 (A) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, by reducing the VAT rate from twelve percent (12%) to ten percent (10%) on the sale of goods and properties, importation of goods, and services, including digital services and the use or lease of properties. label: HB 9158
title: AN ACT MANDATING A 14TH MONTH PAY FOR EMPLOYEES IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution places the dignity and welfare of workers at the center of national development. Article II, Section 18 expressly declares that the State affirms labor as a primary social and economic force and shall protect workers' rights and promote their welfare. This guarantee is reinforced by Article II, Section 10, which directs the State to promote social justice in all phases of national development, and by Article II, Section 9, which commands the State to build a just and dynamic social order that shall free the people from poverty through policies that promote full employment, a rising standard of living, and an improved quality of life for all. Complementing these principles, Article XII, Section 1 mandates a more equitable distribution of opportunities, income, and wealth, while Article XIII, Section 3(2) specifically requires the State to afford full protection to labor and guarantee the rights of all workers to humane conditions of work and a living wage. Taken together, these provisions establish a clear constitutional duty: economic progress must be shared with the workers whose labor makes such progress possible. For decades, the Filipino worker has carried the weight of economic growth while receiving an increasingly diminished share of its rewards. Although Presidential Decree No. 851 institutionalized the 13th-month pay in 1975 as a vital form of income support, the economic realities confronting workers today are far different from those that existed when the decree was issued. The cost of food, transportation, housing, utilities, education, healthcare, and other household necessities has steadily risen, while wages for many workers remain stretched across growing family obligations. As Page 1 of 6 inflation erodes purchasing power and everyday expenses continue to climb, many employees find that their regular earnings and existing statutory benefits are no longer sufficient to provide genuine financial security. This burden is felt most sharply by ordinary wage earners who live from paycheck to paycheck. For millions of workers, a single salary is expected to cover rent, school expenses, medicine, debt payments, transportation costs, and daily subsistence. Any unexpected expense can immediately destabilize household finances. In such conditions, labor is performed honestly and continuously, yet economic vulnerability remains constant. No worker who contributes productively to society should remain trapped in perpetual precarity despite full and faithful work. The existing 13th-month pay remains an important protection, but standing alone, it no longer fully answers present realities. A policy that was adequate decades ago must evolve when social and economic conditions have fundamentally changed. Just as the law once recognized the need for an additional mandatory benefit to preserve the real value of wages, the present moment calls for renewed legislative action responsive to contemporary burdens faced by workers and their families. This measure therefore mandates a 14th-month pay for employees in the private sector who are already entitled to receive the 13th-month pay under existing law. To ensure coherence and administrative efficiency, the bill adopts, as far as practicable, the existing legal framework governing the 13th-month pay, including its standards, mechanisms, and implementing principles. In doing so, the measure avoids unnecessary duplication while providing a clear and workable extension of an already familiar labor standard. The proposed reform is not merely an additional monetary grant but a recognition that the value created by labor must be more fairly shared with those whose work sustains enterprises and drives the national economy. Additional income in the hands of workers is also income that returns to local markets through spending on food, education, transportation, housing, and other essential goods and services. When workers gain greater financial breathing room, families become more resilient, communities become more stable, and the broader economy becomes stronger. More importantly, this bill affirms a basic principle of justice: those who work with dignity deserve compensation that allows them to live with dignity. In advancing this measure, the State gives fuller meaning to its constitutional promise that labor shall be protected, welfare shall be promoted, and prosperity shall not be reserved for a few but shared by all. Page 2 of 6 In solidarity with the working class, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ELIJAH R. label: HB 9159
title: AN ACT PROVIDING EXCEPTIONS TO THE CONFIDENTIALITY OF BANK DEPOSITS FOR PUBLIC OFFICIALS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1405, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “SECRECY OF BANK DEPOSITS LAW,” REQUIRING THE DISCLOSURE AND VERIFICATION OF CERTAIN BANK DEPOSITS AND INVESTMENTS OF SUCH OFFICIALS, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution firmly declares that public office is a public trust. Article XI, Section 1 provides that public officers and employees must, at all times, be accountable to the people, serve them with utmost responsibility, integrity, loyalty, and efficiency, act with patriotism and justice, and lead modest lives. Complementing this mandate, Article II, Section 27 directs the State to maintain honesty and integrity in the public service and to take positive and effective measures against graft and corruption. These constitutional commands are clear: government authority must always be exercised in the open, and those entrusted with public power must remain answerable to the Filipino people. Yet despite these principles, corruption continues to erode public institutions, weaken democratic trust, and divert resources meant for social services, infrastructure, healthcare, education, and decent livelihoods. Public funds that should uplift workers, farmers, students, and marginalized communities are too often lost through illicit enrichment, hidden assets, and abuse of office. When corruption is allowed to persist, it is ordinary Filipinos who bear the heaviest burden through poor services, lost opportunities, and deepening inequality. One enduring obstacle to meaningful accountability is the misuse of financial secrecy laws as a shield against legitimate scrutiny. Republic Act No. 1405, otherwise known as the Secrecy of Bank Deposits Law, was enacted to encourage confidence in the banking system and protect lawful privacy. However, a law designed for financial Page 1 of 5 stability must never be distorted into a refuge for dishonesty in public office. Confidentiality in private banking transactions serves a valid purpose, but secrecy cannot be absolute where public accountability is at stake. Those who exercise the powers of the State must be held to a higher standard than private citizens because they manage authority and resources that belong to the people. This measure, therefore, seeks to harmonize the legitimate interest in financial privacy with the superior constitutional demand for transparency and integrity in government. It provides carefully defined exceptions to bank confidentiality rules for elected and appointed public officials, allowing lawful examination of deposits, accounts, investments, and related financial records by competent authorities acting within their constitutional or statutory powers. It further strengthens existing accountability mechanisms by requiring the truthful disclosure of relevant financial interests and by authorizing verification consistent with law. In doing so, the bill supports lifestyle checks, anti-corruption investigations, asset recovery efforts, and the prosecution of offenses involving public funds and public office. These safeguards recognize a simple principle: those who honestly serve the public have nothing to fear from lawful accountability, while those who exploit public office should not be allowed to hide behind technical barriers and outdated protections. A government that asks sacrifice from workers and taxpayers must itself be transparent. A nation that seeks inclusive development must ensure that public resources reach the people for whom they are intended. By closing avenues for concealment and strengthening mechanisms of accountability, this measure advances clean governance, protects the public treasury, and affirms that no office is above scrutiny. More importantly, it gives life to the constitutional promise that power is held in trust for the people and never for private gain. In solidarity with the working class, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ELIJAH R. label: HB 9160
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL GROUNDWATER PRESERVATION AND MANAGEMENT PROGRAM, PROVIDING FOR THE SUSTAINABLE USE, PROTECTION, AND RESTORATION OF GROUNDWATER RESOURCES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is increasingly confronted with the twin challenges of groundwater depletion and groundwater contamination brought about by rapid urbanization, population growth, unsustainable extraction practices, and the worsening impacts of climate change. Groundwater remains a critical source of potable water, agricultural irrigation, industrial use, and ecological stability, particularly in areas vulnerable to drought, saltwater intrusion, and seasonal water shortages. Consistent with the State policy to protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology, there is a need to institutionalize a comprehensive and science-based approach to groundwater preservation and management. Despite its importance, the country has yet to adopt a comprehensive national framework specifically focused on the preservation, sustainable management, and restoration of groundwater resources. Excessive groundwater withdrawal has already resulted in declining water tables, land subsidence, saltwater intrusion in coastal communities, and the degradation of aquifers in several parts of the country. These threats endanger water security, food production, public health, environmental sustainability, and long-term economic resilience. This proposed measure seeks to establish a National Groundwater Preservation and Management Program that institutionalizes groundwater monitoring, recharge enhancement, aquifer protection, sustainable extraction practices, and inter-agency coordination among national government agencies and local government units. It further integrates groundwater preservation into climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction strategies while promoting water-efficient technologies and responsible resource management. The bill likewise strengthens local participation by encouraging the integration of groundwater preservation measures into local land use and climate action planning, while providing incentives for industries, farmers, cooperatives, and communities adopting sustainable water conservation and recharge practices. By harmonizing national and local efforts toward the protection of the country’s groundwater resources, this measure aims to secure a sustainable and resilient water future for present and succeeding generations. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9161
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL CENTER FOR COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT IN THE POLYTECHNIC UNIVERSITY OF THE PHILIPPINES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Cooperatives are recognized under Republic Act No. 9520 as vital instruments for promoting social justice, economic development, and people empowerment. The law affirms the State’s policy to foster the creation and growth of cooperatives as practical vehicles for self-reliance and grassroots development, particularly among marginalized and underserved sectors. Complementing this mandate, Republic Act No. 11364 strengthened the institutional framework for cooperative regulation and development through the reorganization of the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA). The CDA is tasked with registration, regulation, and capacity-building initiatives; however, persistent sectoral gaps remain in higher-level education, advanced research, and professionalization of cooperative management. Furthermore, Republic Act No. 7722 mandates the State to promote quality higher education and research, while Republic Act No. 10931 expands access to tertiary education for Filipino students. These laws collectively underscore the State’s obligation to invest in human capital formation, particularly in specialized fields that support national development. Despite this robust legal framework, many cooperatives continue to face structural constraints, including weak governance systems, limited managerial expertise, inadequate research support, and insufficient access to continuing education. These challenges hinder their ability to fully realize the developmental objectives envisioned under RA 9520 and related laws. The Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP), with its long- established leadership in cooperative education, is strategically positioned to address these gaps. Its historical role as a training center for non-agricultural cooperatives and pioneer of the Bachelor in Cooperatives program provides a strong institutional foundation for expanded national engagement. This measure therefore proposes the establishment of the National Center for Cooperative Development (NCCD) within PUP. The Center shall serve as a specialized national institution dedicated to advancing cooperative education, research, and extension services in support of the policy objectives enshrined in RA 9520 and other related laws. Specifically, the NCCD shall: a) Provide degree and non-degree programs aligned with the competency standards and development priorities identified under the Cooperative Development Authority framework; b) Deliver continuing education and certification programs to enhance the capabilities of cooperative officers, in line with the governance and training requirements under RA 9520; c) Conduct applied research to support policy development, legislative initiatives, and evidence-based interventions for the cooperative sector; d) Extend technical assistance and consultancy services, particularly for micro and small cooperatives, to strengthen compliance, sustainability, and growth; Promote linkages among academic institutions, government agencies, and cooperative organizations to ensure coordinated sectoral development. The establishment of the NCCD likewise complements national development strategies, including the Philippine Development Plan, Ambisyon Natin 2040, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), by strengthening inclusive economic institutions and promoting equitable access to opportunities. By institutionalizing a dedicated national center for cooperative development within a state university, this measure operationalizes the State’s commitments under RA 9520, RA 11364, and related laws—bridging the gap between policy, education, and practice. It ensures that cooperatives are supported not only through regulation, but through sustained investments in knowledge, innovation, and leadership development. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9162
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AFFORDABLE FUNERAL SERVICES FOR INDIGENT FAMILIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Death is inevitable. Yet, for many Filipino families, the burden of laying a loved one to rest is compounded by financial constraints. In moments of grief, families are often compelled to make urgent decisions on funeral arrangements despite limited resources. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) reported that approximately ₱1.7 billion in burial assistance was provided to 165,907 beneficiaries under the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) program from January to September 2024, highlighting the number of Filipino families who face difficulty in meeting funeral and burial costs. Funeral services including caskets, embalming, transportation of remains, and related arrangements remain costly and often beyond the means of indigent households. While existing mechanisms such as the DSWD’s AICS program and local government unit (LGU) assistance provide relief, these are often limited, discretionary, and insufficient to address prevailing market costs. Consistent with the State’s policy to promote consumer protection and ensure access to essential services, this measure strengthens the regulatory role of the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) in monitoring funeral service pricing and mandates all funeral establishments to offer affordable service packages. It likewise reinforces the role of LGUs and the DSWD in identifying qualified beneficiaries and facilitating access to available assistance, consistent with existing social protection frameworks. This measure seeks to ensure the availability of affordable funeral services for indigent and underprivileged families by regulating costs and promoting accessible service packages. While not entirely free, it aims to prevent grieving families from incurring undue financial burden or debt. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this measure is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9163
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE PHILIPPINE ONLINE LIBRARY AND THE DIGITIZATION OF ALL PRESCRIBED REFERENCES FOR PUBLIC EDUCATION, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XIV, Sections 1 and 2 of the 1987 Constitution mandate the State to protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and to take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all. The Constitution likewise directs the State to establish, maintain, and support a complete, adequate, and integrated system of education responsive to the needs of the people and society. In the modern digital era, access to educational materials and learning resources has increasingly become dependent on technology and internet connectivity. However, many Filipino learners, particularly those enrolled in public schools and those residing in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, continue to face difficulties in accessing updated textbooks, reference materials, and other educational resources due to financial limitations, insufficient library facilities, and unequal access to digital infrastructure. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize the Philippine Online Library as a centralized and accessible digital repository of textbooks, instructional materials, and other educational resources for elementary and secondary learners. Through the digitization of prescribed learning materials and the utilization of information and communications technology, the measure aims to expand educational access, promote digital inclusion, and strengthen the delivery of public education throughout the country. The bill likewise encourages inter-agency coordination among the Department of Education (DepEd), Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), and the National Library of the Philippines (NLP) to ensure the proper development, management, and maintenance of the digital platform and educational repository, while remaining consistent with existing laws on intellectual property, cybersecurity, and data privacy. By leveraging technology to improve access to quality educational resources, this measure seeks to help bridge the digital divide, support learners and educators, and advance a more inclusive, modern, and resilient educational system for present and future generations. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9164
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR NATURAL FLOOD MANAGEMENT AND EROSION CONTROL MECHANISMS, STRENGTHENING ECOSYSTEM-BASED APPROACHES TO DISASTER REDUCTION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Flooding and soil erosion remain among the most persistent environmental and disaster risks in the Philippines, resulting in loss of lives, damage to infrastructure, and disruption of livelihoods. These risks are further intensified by deforestation, land degradation, and the increasing impacts of climate change. While existing laws such as Republic Act No. 10121 and Republic Act No. 9729 provide comprehensive frameworks for disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation, there remains a need to strengthen the integration of ecosystem-based and nature-based solutions within these systems. Current approaches to flood control have largely relied on structural or “gray” infrastructure, which, while necessary, may be complemented by more sustainable and cost-effective natural interventions. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize Natural Flood Management (NFM) and erosion control strategies as complementary approaches to existing flood control systems. It promotes the restoration and protection of watersheds, wetlands, mangroves, and river systems to naturally regulate water flow, reduce flood risks, and prevent soil erosion. The bill establishes a National Program on Natural Flood Management and Erosion Control as a convergence mechanism among key government agencies, without creating new bureaucratic structures. It ensures alignment with existing national policies and reinforces the role of local government units, consistent with Republic Act No. 7160, in integrating these strategies into local development and disaster risk reduction plans. By strengthening ecosystem-based approaches, this measure aims to enhance community resilience, promote environmental sustainability, and provide long-term, cost-efficient solutions to flooding and land degradation. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9165
title: AN ACT EXEMPTING THE SYSTEM LOSS CHARGE COMPONENT IN THE SALE OF ELECTRICITY BY DISTRIBUTION COMPANIES AND ELECTRIC COOPERATIVES FROM THE COVERAGE OF THE VALUE-ADDED TAX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 109 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This Bill seeks to amend the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended by Republic Act Nos. 9377 and 10378, by exempting the system loss charge component in the electricity bills from the coverage of the value-added tax (VAT). VAT is a form of sales tax—a tax on consumption levied on the sale, barter, exchange or lease of goods or properties and services in the Philippines, as well as on the importation of goods into the country. As an indirect tax, it is shifted or passed on to the buyer, transferee, or lessee of goods, properties, or services. Being a pass-on tax, the burden of paying the VAT thus ultimately falls upon the final consumers—the consuming public. The system loss charge, on the other hand, is the component of an electric bill representing the cost of electricity lost during transmission, as well as losses due to pilferage and technical and administrative inefficiencies. Notably, consumers are made to shoulder the cost of even pilfered electricity and the power consumed by distribution companies such as Meralco and by electric cooperatives. As a result, consumers pay for more electricity than they actually use. Compounding this inequity, the system loss charge is further subjected to VAT, which drives electricity bills even higher. The table below illustrates the impact of the system loss charge and the corresponding VAT on non-lifeline residential customers of Meralco: System Loss VAT on System System Loss Consumption Total Bill Charge Loss Charge plus VAT 50 kWh 735.56 38.76 4.279104 43.039104 100 kWh 1,446.98 77.52 8.558208 86.078208 200 kWh 2,869.92 155.04 17.116416 172.156416 In pesos According to Meralco, the system loss charge comprises approximately five percent (5%) of the total electricity bill. As of April 2026, the system loss charge for residential consumers stands at ₱0.7752 per kilowatt-hour, subject to 11.04% VAT. By exempting the system loss charge from VAT, residential Meralco customers consuming between 50 to 200 kWh can save between ₱4.28 to ₱17.12 per month. Being a tax on consumption, VAT should, by definition, be imposed only upon goods and services that people actually purchase and consume. The imposition of VAT on the system loss charge is therefore not only illogical but legally indefensible— consumers are being taxed for electricity they never actually received or consumed. According to data from Global Petrol Prices,1 as of September 2025, the average residential electricity price in the Philippines is ₱12.383 per kWh ($0.203 USD), while the average rate for businesses stands at ₱9.618 per kWh ($0.157 USD). In terms of residential costs, the Philippines ranks 48th out of 145 countries globally and holds the fourth-highest rate in Asia, following Cyprus, Singapore and Japan. Notably, Philippine electricity costs are double those of Thailand and Indonesia. In another study conducted by the International Energy Consultants (IEC), a Perth-based consultancy firm commissioned by Meralco to conduct the study, the rates in Luzon are placed at ninth highest electricity tariffs of the 44 countries surveyed. 1 “Electricity prices.” Global Petrol Prices, 2026. Retrieved from https://www.globalpetrolprices.com/electricity_prices/ Per the IEC study, the primary reason for such higher power rates as compared to other countries is the absence of government subsidies for electricity, unlike countries like Indonesia, Thailand, and Malaysia, where electricity rates are subsidized by the government. These subsidies comprise a large part of their public budget. In Indonesia, for example, energy subsidies account for 24.0 percent of their 2013 public expenditure plan. Against this backdrop—and amid the persistent rise in the prices of basic commodities, fuel, education, and healthcare, worsening inflation, and the continuing erosion of the purchasing power of the peso—it is imperative that Congress take concrete and immediate steps to ease the financial burden on ordinary Filipinos, particularly those from the lower-income brackets. This Bill was first filed as House Bill 5543 in the 16th Congress by Bayan Muna Partylist Representatives Neri Colmenares and Carlos Isagani Zarate. It was refiled as HB 1616 in the 17th Congress and was passed by the House of Representatives on third reading. It was refiled again as HB 245 and HB 5994 during the 18 th and 19th Congresses, respectively. Passage of this Bill is thus earnestly sought. REP. ANTONIO L. TINIO ACT Teachers Party-list REP. label: HB 9166
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A FERTILIZER SUBSIDY PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipino farmers are struggling with skyrocketing fertilizer costs, a crisis exacerbated by volatile global markets, currency depreciation, and rising domestic logistics overheads. Because fertilizer is a cornerstone expense for cultivating vital staples like rice and corn, these inflated prices trap smallholder farmers who represent the backbone of the industry in a cycle of hardship. To survive, many are forced to reduce soil nutrients, incur heavy debt, or suffer complete financial collapse. The impact of these high production costs extends well beyond the farm, triggering a damaging socio-economic chain reaction. Lower fertilizer use leads to stunted productivity, resulting in meager harvests and inferior crop quality. This scarcity destabilizes the market, as the shrinking supply of rice and corn drives up retail prices Current legislation is unfortunately insufficient to protect the sector from these vulnerabilities. While the Rice Tariffication Law (RA 11203) and RA 11598 offers some financial relief, their scope is too limited and they lack a permanent, nationwide framework to manage price fluctuations across all crop types. Additionally, while RA 11321 regulates fertilizer quality, it does nothing to address the core problem of affordability. To solve these systemic failures, this bill proposes a transparent, targeted, and institutionalized Fertilizer Subsidy Program. By providing structured support to smallholder farmers during price surges, the measure aims to stabilize agricultural output, protect rural incomes, and mitigate inflationary pressure on food. Ultimately, this program fulfils the State’s mandate to foster sustainable agriculture and ensure national food security. Given these urgent circumstances, the immediate passage of this Bill is earnestly sought. REP. ELISA T. KHO, M.D., FPCCP REP. ANTONIO T. label: HB 9170
title: AN ACT GRANTING BENEFITS TO FILIPINO SEPTUAGENARIANS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11982, WHICH AMENDED REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10868, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “CENTENARIANS ACT OF 2016,” AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XIII, Section 11, and Article XV, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution declare the State’s duty to care for its elderly citizens by providing for and prioritizing their needs in health and social security programs. Republic Act No. 10868, otherwise known as the “Centenarians Act of 2016,” was enacted on June 23, 2016, to provide all Filipinos who reach the age of 100 years old a letter of felicitation from the President and a gift in the amount of P100,000.00 in honor of the centenarian’s longevity. On February 26, 2024, the “Centenarians Act of 2016” was amended by Republic Act No. 11982 to grant benefits, in the form of cash gifts of P10,000.00, to all Filipinos upon reaching the ages of 80, 85, 90, and 95. The amendatory bill was proposed and enacted in consideration of the reality that most Filipinos do not reach the age of 100 years old, and that the number of Filipinos who reach the ages of 80, 85, 90, and 95 decreases as their ages progress. According to a report by the Philippine Institute of Development Studies (PIDS) published in February 2021,1 Filipinos have a life expectancy of 71 years, while recent World Bank data puts the average Filipino life expectancy at 70 years, as of 2024.2 1 Ulep, V.G., Uy, J., Siy Van, V.T., & Bagas, J. Retrieved from https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SP.DYN.LE00.IN?locations=PH. 1 However, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), the average Filipino life expectancy as of 2021 is 66.4 years old in total, with 69.9 years old for females and 63.4 for males.3 This means that while Republic Act Nos. 10868 and 11982 rightfully seek to honor the Filipino elderly who reach the milestone ages of 80, 85, 90, 95, and 100 by providing them with cash benefits, most Filipinos do not live long enough to receive these benefits. Even when they do, they are often no longer able to enjoy the benefits themselves. As such, this bill seeks to further expand the coverage of the aforementioned laws honoring octogenarians, nonagenarians, and centenarians by including septuagenarians, or Filipinos aged 70 and 75, as recipients of cash benefits. This bill also increases the amount of benefits received by Filipinos upon reaching the ages of 80 and 90, creating a gradual progression in the amount starting from age 70 to age 100. By doing so, this bill seeks not only to honor the Filipino elderly by providing cash incentives for reaching milestone years, but also to provide them with the financial support they increasingly need as their capacity for work decreases and health complications increase with age. In the 20th Congress, similar bills were filed by Representatives Loreto Amante and JC Abalos. This bill proposes a unique set of benefits for Filipino Septuagenarians, Octogenarians, and Nonagenarians. Early approval of this measure is earnestly sought. LEILA M. label: HB 9171
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SELLING AND/OR BUYING OF ADMISSION TICKETS THROUGH UNAUTHORIZED SALES CHANNELS, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Ticket scalping refers to the practice of purchasing admission tickets to entertainment events and reselling them at prices far exceeding their original face value, often exploiting high demand for concerts, sports matches, and festivals. In recent years, the rise of online resale platforms and the use of automated purchasing tools or “bots” have made this practice more prevalent, allowing certain individuals or groups to hoard large quantities of tickets and artificially limit supply. While some argue that scalping reflects free market principles, it is widely regarded as an abusive and unfair practice that inflates prices, restricts access for ordinary consumers, and undermines the integrity of the ticketing system.1 This issue has been underscored by recent events in the Philippines. During the concert of a Filipino American singer, tickets originally priced at ₱1,500.00 were resold online for as much as ₱15,000.00, sparking widespread public outrage.2 Similarly, in a concert of the K-pop girl group in the country, numerous complaints were raised by fans regarding excessive resale prices. VIP tickets with an original price of ₱19,500.00 were reportedly resold by scalpers for up to ₱60,000.00 each.3 These 1 Abramova, A. (14 March 2025). Ticket Scalping – Profit for Some, a Problem for Others: How Platforms Can Stay Protected (2025). Retrieved from: https://sumsub.com/blog/ticket-scalping/ 2 Lauengco, G. (18 September 2024). Ticket scalping. Retrieved from: https://www.pna.gov.ph/opinion/pieces/940-ticket-scalping 3 Hicap, J. (5 December 2025). Many factors affect concert ticket prices in PH. Retrieved from: https://mb.com.ph/2025/12/05/many-factors-affect-concert-ticket-prices-in-ph 1 incidents highlight how unregulated resale practices enable profiteering at the expense of genuine fans and demonstrate the need for stronger regulatory measures. This bill is therefore a necessary response to protect consumers and ensure fair access to entertainment events. It seeks to curb exploitative practices by prohibiting the unauthorized buying and selling of tickets, particularly those resold at prices exceeding 10% above face value without proper authorization. It also imposes penalties on related acts such as ticket hoarding, selling through unauthorized channels, and failure to disclose accurate pricing information. Furthermore, the measure requires event organizers and ticketing entities to adopt clear anti-scalping policies and provide public advisories, thereby promoting transparency, accountability, and a more equitable ticketing system. Ultimately, the bill aims to restore public trust and ensure that access to live events is determined by fairness rather than the ability of intermediaries to exploit demand for profit. In the 20th Congress, similar bills were filed by Senator Francis N. Pangilinan, Mark A. Villar, Erwin T. Tulfo, Joel Villanueva, and Representative Karen Hope F. Garcia. This bill fully adopts the Senate Substitute Bill No. 1989. Early approval of this measure is requested. LEILA M. label: HB 9172
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE INCOME TAX EXEMPTION CEILING FOR INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS TO FOUR HUNDRED EIGHTY THOUSAND PESOS (P480,000.00) ANNUALLY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 24(A)(2)(a) and (b) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Tax Reform for Acceleration and Inclusion (TRAIN) law introduced a significant change to the Philippine income tax system by exempting individuals earning up to ₱250,000.00 annually from personal income tax. This reform was designed to ease the tax burden on low- and lower-middle-income earners, allowing them to retain a larger portion of their income. However, once annual earnings exceed this threshold, a progressive tax structure applies, with rates starting at 15 percent and rising to 35 percent for top earners. As a result, even modest increases in income can lead to disproportionately higher tax liabilities. For example, a worker earning ₱300,000.00 annually pays around ₱625.00 monthly in income tax, while at ₱360,000.00, this more than doubles to approximately ₱1,375.00.1 Notwithstanding the exemption threshold, employees continue to face mandatory contributions to government social protection programs, including 4.5 percent for the Social Security System (SSS), 2.25 percent for PhilHealth, and 1 percent for Pag-IBIG. These contributions, totaling nearly 8 percent of monthly income, are deducted alongside income taxes, significantly reducing the take-home pay. Combined, taxes and contributions can amount to ₱2,500.00 to ₱3,700.00 per month, or ₱30,000.00 to ₱44,000.00 annually, even before individuals allocate income for essential living expenses such as housing, food, and transportation.2 1 Mago, J. (21 July 2025). 2025 tax burden deepens for Pinoys. Retrieved from: https://tribune.net.ph/2025/07/20/2025-tax-burden-deepens-for-pinoys 2 Id. 1 Taxes remain the lifeblood of the government, enabling the provision of public funds for critical public services such as education, healthcare, and public safety. However, tax policy must be responsive to evolving economic conditions.3 In particular, inflation plays a crucial role in shaping the real impact of taxation. As prices rise, wages and nominal incomes tend to increase correspondingly, but without adjustments to tax brackets, taxpayers may be pushed into higher tax rates despite no real gain in purchasing power4, a phenomenon commonly known as “bracket creep.” The interaction between a progressive tax system and persistent inflation can lead to increased government revenues while unfortunately shifting the tax burden across income groups at the same time. Individuals who were previously exempt may become taxable, and those already paying taxes may face higher effective rates. If left unaddressed, this dynamic could result in a growing number of taxpayers being subjected to higher marginal tax rates, potentially affecting income distribution, economic behavior, and the overall effectiveness of taxation as a fiscal policy tool.5 Ultimately, while the TRAIN law aimed to increase disposable income for lower earners and stimulate economic activity through higher consumer spending, there is an equally important need for periodic review and adjustment of our tax policies.6 Ensuring that tax systems remain equitable, efficient, and responsive to inflation is essential to balancing revenue generation with the protection of taxpayers’ real income and purchasing power. In the 20th Congress, similar bills were filed by Senator Paolo Benigno “Bam” Aquino IV, Representatives Tobias M. Tiangco, Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez, Yedda Marie K. Romualdez, Andrew Julian K. Romualdez, Jude A. Acidre, and Iris Marie Demesa Montes. This bill fully adopts Senator Bam Aquino’s SBN 267. Early approval of this measure is requested. LEILA M. DE LIMA 3 Moral, M. label: HB 9173
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING CONTINUING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT (CPD) SUPPORT FOR NURSES, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The nursing profession is the backbone of the healthcare system. Our nurses are the primary providers of patient care, often working under high-pressure conditions that require constant adaptation to new medical technologies, protocols, and global health standards. Under current laws, Continuing Professional Development (CPD) is a mandatory requirement for the renewal of professional licenses. While the intent of CPD—to ensure lifelong learning and professional competence—is noble, the burden of fulfillment has fallen almost exclusively on the shoulders of the individual nurse. In many cases, nurses are forced to pay for expensive seminars out-of-pocket and utilize their limited rest days to attend training sessions. This financial and logistical strain contributes to professional burnout and encourages the migration of our skilled healthcare workers to countries that offer better institutional support for professional growth. This bill seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive support system for the CPD of nurses. It proposes that: 1. Public and private employers provide paid study leaves and subsidies for mandatory CPD units. 2. The Government establishes a scholarship and grant system for specialized nursing certifications. 3. Tax incentives should be granted to private healthcare institutions that invest in the professional development of their nursing staff. By investing in the continuous education of our nurses, we are not just supporting a profession; we are ensuring a higher standard of care for every patient in the country. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 9174
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY-BASED FIRE PREVENTION AND RESPONSE MECHANISMS THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF BARANGAY FIRE BRIGADES, FIRE SAFETY TRAINING, AND COMMUNITY FIRE RESILIENCE PROGRAMS IN ALL BARANGAYS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: SECTION 1. Short Title. - This Act shall be known as the "Barangay Fire Resilience Act." SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. - It is the policy of the State to prioritize the safety of its citizens and protect their property from the destructive effects of fire. Recognizing that the barangay is the primary political unit of the government, the State shall strengthen local capabilities to prevent, respond to, and recover from fire incidents through organized community participation. SEC. 3. Establishment of Barangay Fire Brigades. Every barangay is hereby mandated to establish a Barangay Fire Brigade (BFB). The BFB shall be composed of volunteer residents who are physically fit and have undergone the required training. • Composition: The BFB shall be headed by a Barangay Fire Marshal (appointed by the Punong Barangay) and shall consist of at least ten (10) members for every 2,000 residents. • Functions: The BFB shall serve as the initial response unit, conduct regular neighborhood fire patrols, and assist the BFP during large-scale operations.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Fire is a hazard that does not discriminate, but its impact is felt most acutely at the grassroots level. In the Philippines, the density of our communities— particularly in urban areas—often means that by the time a fire truck maneuvers through narrow alleys and traffic, a small kitchen fire has already become a neighborhood-wide conflagration. While the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) remains our primary line of defense, the "Golden Hour" of fire suppression belongs to the people on the ground. Statistics consistently show that the first few minutes of a fire are the most critical. Currently, many barangays lack the formal organization, equipment, and training to handle these initial moments effectively. This bill seeks to institutionalize Community-Based Fire Prevention and Response by mandating the creation of Barangay Fire Brigades in every barangay, ensuring that a disciplined, trained team of volunteers is ready to act before the professional engines arrive. By empowering the barangay, we are not just adding "more firefighters"; we are building a culture of vigilance. We are transforming our citizens from potential victims into active first responders. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 9175
title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE TO REGULATE FARM GATE PRICES FOR AGRICULTURAL AND FISHERIES PRODUCTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes the right of farmers to receive a just share of the fruits of their labor. It is unfortunate that in this day and age of trade globalization, the welfare of the people who grow or raise our food has been neglected. We talk about raising production, consumer protection, importing shortfalls, raising or lowering tariffs, mechanization and the use of technology in farming, livestock growing or aquaculture but never about the plight of the simple farmer, grower, raiser who are the backbone of our food producing sector. Our rice farmers have been plagued by losses brought about allegedly by the Rice Tariffication Law. Whatever the reason may be, the prevailing market price for their rice produce simply was not enough to cover the time, effort and expenses to raise their crops. SRPs have been imposed on meat and vegetable products to protect consumers. But who protects the supply side of the equation? It is also a fact that our economy has suffered a severe downturn brought about by the COVID 19 pandemic. Industries will take time to retool and rebuild but while we wait for our industries to catch up or resume normal production, economic experts point at the agricultural or food producing sectors as one of the sectors that could help bring our economy back up. It is however hard to entice farmers and food producers to work the land if it does not prove to be income generating. This proposed measure of authorizing the Department of Agriculture to regulate FARM GATE PRICES of agricultural produce, livestock, fisheries and aquaculture products will ensure that our farmers, growers, fisherfolk, all the people responsible for raising, catching or growing our food are assured of their just return for the time, effort and expense they have incurred. The approval of this measure is earnestly requested. BEVERLEY ROSE A. title: AN ACT IMPROVING AND SUSTAINING GENOMICS AND FORENSIC SCIENCE FACILITIES, AND ESTABLISHING SEPARATE DATABASES FOR GENOMICS AND FORENSIC DNA IN THE COUNTRY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE DNA or deoxyribonucleic acid is one of science and technology’s most important discoveries and has greatly contributed in the formation and development of society. DNA is a molecule that contains the instructions an organism needs to develop, live and reproduce. It has not only been used to determine an individual’s identity and parentage but also diagnose genetic disorders through DNA sequencing and testing—an indispensable tool for basic and applied research in health and medicine, agriculture, biodiversity, ethnicity, industry, environment, and forensic science. Considering how essential DNA is, the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) supported the formation of the Genomics Research and Development Program and the establishment of DNA Sequencing Core Facility and Bioinformatics Core Facility of the Philippine Genome Center. However, increasing demand for DNA sequencing and analysis for research and development require further upgrading of Genomics facilities and infrastructure. This holds true even in the field of forensic science. While, the Philippine National Police (PNP) has acquired the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS) used for routine casework analysis, the current facilities and infrastructures require upgrading to improve criminal investigation and crime laboratory capabilities for higher crime solution efficiency. The establishment of databases for each field—genomics and forensic science—are deemed necessary to further boost the country’s DNA capabilities in the areas of in health and medicine, agriculture, biodiversity, ethnicity, industry, environment, and forensic science. These improvements would not only lead to more breakthroughs in research and development, but most importantly in practical applications. Science and technology are undeniably important in nation building. The 1987 Constitution says that science and technology are essential for national development and progress. It further states that the State shall give priority to research and development, invention, innovation, and their utilization. It is high time the State lives up to this mandate. In view of the foregoing, the early passage of this bill is earnestly requested. BEVERLEY ROSE A. label: HB 9177
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FULL COVERAGE MEDICAL ASSISTANCE TO ANY OFFICER OR UNIFORMED PERSONNEL OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES, THE BUREAU OF FIRE PROTECTION, THE BUREAU OF JAIL MANAGEMENT AND PENOLOGY, THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD, AND THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, FOR INJURIES SUSTAINED DURING THE PERFORMANCE OF OFFICIAL DUTIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Late 2025, this Representation was approached by members of the Philippine National Police – Batangas City Police Office who were seeking medical assistance for their three comrades-in-arms wounded during a shootout and were confined in a private hospital in Batangas City. The hospital bill for each policeman ranged from half a million to almost a million pesos. The combined amount was so large that their co-workers were “passing the hat” in order to raise the funds needed. It took the donations from private individuals as well as numerous DOH Guarantee Letters to finally settle the bill. This incident made this Representation realize that our Military and Uniformed Personnel (MUP), the very people charged with securing the peace and order of our country and protecting our sovereignty lack the State’s support when their bodies are injured in the course of doing their duty as they lay their very lives on the line for our country. This incident should not be repeated ever again. It is for this reason that this measure seeking to provide members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), the Philippine National Police (PNP), the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), and the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) with full coverage medical assistance for injuries incurred in the line of duty is being filed. In view of the foregoing, the expeditious passage of this bill is earnestly sought. BEVERLEY ROSE A. label: HB 9178
title: AN ACT SIMPLIFYING PROCEDURES AND REDUCING DOCUMENTARY REQUIREMENTS FOR ACCESSING GOVERNMENT AID OR ASSISTANCE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The public demands fast and efficient service not only from the private sector, but most importantly from government. In fact, people have higher expectations from government with regard to providing services. It is for this reason that Republic Act No. 11032 or the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018 was enacted into law. Clearly, streamlining government processes is a priority of any administration. With the developments in the field of information technology, government processes can now easily be improved with appropriate legislation, strict implementation, and proper technology on information sharing. However, Filipinos in need of government aid still encounter delays in receiving assistance due to redundant or excessive documentary requirements, tedious procedures, long processing times and even the lack of availability of funds. To further remove administrative roadblocks from our countrymen in need of aid, this bill seeks to streamline the process / procedures and reduce the excessive requirements needed to avail of all applicable government aid or assistance. Moreover, this bill seeks to utilize digital systems to facilitate requests and processes for government aid or assistance. By adopting simplified and standardized procedures and requirements, the process of securing government aid need not be stressful. Hence, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 9180
title: AN ACT DEVELOPING AND EXPANDING THE PHILIPPINE SHIPBUILDING AND SHIP REPAIR, BOATBUILDING AND SHIP RECYCLING INDUSTRIES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS Section 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “SBSR DEVELOPMENT ACT OF 2026.” Section 2. Declaration of Policy. - The state recognizes the role of the shipbuilding and ship repair industry as one of the vital components of the maritime sector and that it plays a key role in the economic growth of the country. As such, it is important that the Philippine maritime industry develops and enhances the quality of its capacity and capability in the construction and repair of ships for water transportation as well as for its maritime and naval forces. The Philippines needs to continue modernization and expansion of its domestic shipping fleet to provide comfortable, accessible, affordable, safe and sustainable water transport in the country and to cope up with the latest trends and development in the maritime industry. To attain these objectives, it is hereby declared the policy of the State to: (a) encourage the development of a viable shipbuilding and ship repair, boatbuilding and ship recycling industries to support the Philippine Ship Registry and its strict adherence to safety standards which will ensure the seaworthiness of all ships; (b) attract capital and increase investment in the shipbuilding and ship repair, boatbuilding and ship recycling industries by creating a healthy and competitive and sustainable business environment for SBSR operations; (c) provide adequate capital incentives for the continued growth of the Philippine shipbuilding and ship repair, boatbuilding and ship recycling industries;
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines has historically been a significant maritime nation, with a sizable output and a globally prominent seafarer workforce. However, a substantial portion of the country’s 400-plus shipyards require rehabilitation, and the majority are limited to basic repair and maintenance operations rather than high-value construction and export activities. This Bill seeks to address these systemic limitations by establishing a nationwide policy of sustainable industrial growth, competitive investments, workforce upskilling, and technology adoption. It aims to transform the Philippines’ maritime industrial base by institutionalizing a comprehensive policy framework to modernize, expand, and globally position the domestic shipbuilding, ship repair, boatbuilding, and ship recycling sectors. In addition, it is grounded in the holistic vision articulated in the Maritime Industry Development Plan (MIDP) 2028, the national maritime strategy adopted under Executive Order No. 55, which envisions an integrated and globally competitive maritime industry through modernization, capacity expansion, research and development, eco-industrial parks, and incentives for shipbuilding growth. In view of the foregoing, approval of this Bill is earnestly sought. MAXIMO JR. Y. label: HB 9182
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COMPOSITION OF THE PHILIPPINE CREATIVE INDUSTRIES DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 4 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11904, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PHILIPPINE CREATIVE INDUSTRIES DEVELOPMENT ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine creative industries have emerged as a significant driver of economic growth, cultural development, and innovation. Recognizing its strategic importance, the State enacted Republic Act No. 11904 to establish a comprehensive framework for the promotion and development of the country’s creative sectors through the creation of the Philippine Creative Industries Development Council (PCIDC). As the creative economy continues to evolve, there is a growing need to ensure that the composition of the Council remains responsive, representative, and aligned with the realities of the industry. While the existing law already provides representation from several creative domains, certain sectors and institutional stakeholders that play critical roles in the development, promotion, and global competitiveness of Philippine creative industries remain underrepresented. This proposed measure seeks to strengthen the Philippine Creative Industries Development Council by expanding its composition to include the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) and the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) as ex officio members, as well as a dedicated private sector representative from the music industry. These additions recognize the increasingly global and skills- driven nature of the creative economy. The inclusion of the DFA acknowledges the growing importance of cultural diplomacy, international market access, and global promotion of Filipino creative content and talent. As Philippine creative works increasingly reach international audiences, stronger coordination with the country’s foreign service institutions becomes essential in supporting exports, international collaborations, and cultural exchange initiatives. Likewise, the inclusion of TESDA strengthens the linkage between creative industries and technical-vocational education, particularly as demand grows for specialized creative and digital skills across sectors such as design, animation, audiovisual production, live events, and digital media. Expanding skills development pathways is crucial to ensuring that the country’s creative workforce remains competitive and responsive to industry needs. The addition of a dedicated music industry representative also addresses a significant gap in sectoral representation. The music industry is a major component of the Philippine creative economy, contributing not only to cultural expression but also to employment, tourism, live entertainment, and digital content generation. Ensuring its direct representation in the Council enables more responsive and inclusive policymaking. By broadening representation within the PCIDC, this measure promotes more comprehensive coordination among government agencies and industry stakeholders, resulting in policies that are more reflective of the diverse and evolving needs of the Philippine creative sector. It strengthens the institutional capacity of the Council to fulfill its mandate under Republic Act No. 11904 and reinforces the State’s commitment to the sustainable growth and global competitiveness of Filipino creativity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. JAVIER MIGUEL L. label: HB 9186
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A DISTRICT OFFICE OF THE TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (TESDA) IN CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State recognizes the vital role of technical education and skills development in fostering inclusive economic growth, reducing unemployment, and enhancing the global competitiveness of Filipino workers. The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) has consistently provided accessible technical-vocational education and training (TVET) programs that respond to the evolving demands of industry. This bill seeks the establishment of a district office of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) in the City of Cagayan de Oro Cagayan de Oro City serves as the regional growth center of Northern Mindanao, with thriving sectors in logistics, trade, agro-industry, and services. Its strategic location, supported by key infrastructure such as the Port of Cagayan de Oro, makes it a hub for economic activity in the region. The population of Cagayan de Oro City has been steadily growing over the years, thanks to its booming economy and strategic location. As the city continues to develop, it is highly possible that the city will remain to attract more migrants and tourists, further contributing to its population growth. Given the city's population dynamics and more investments coming in, it is likely that requirement for the skilled workers will be needed for it to be able to respond to infrastructure development, job creation, and social services provision. The growth in population and the labor force requirements in Cagayan de Oro and the Misamis Oriental province continued to increase owing to the growing investments in the City and the entire province. Despite this progress, gaps remain in access to technical education and certification services, particularly among the urban poor, out-of-school youth, and displaced workers. Existing TESDA facilities in the province of Misamis Oriental are often overstretched, limiting their capacity to fully address the increasing demand for skills training and assessment. The TESDA Provincial Offices in the region was created by virtue of RA 7796 or TESDA Act in 1994 which provided the channel for access to TESDA programs and services. At present, TESDA Misamis Oriental Provincial Office caters to 23 municipalities and 2 component cities and 1 chartered city (CdO) for Technical vocational provision in various training delivery modes. There are 108 TVET providers in the province of which 49% are in Cagayan de Oro City. The establishment of a TESDA District Office in Cagayan de Oro City will decentralize service delivery, improve coordination with local government units, industry stakeholders, and educational institutions, and ensure more efficient implementation of skills development programs. It will also strengthen workforce readiness and contribute to sustained regional development. Therefore it is incumbent to propose for the separation of the TESDA District Office from the existing TESDA Provincial Office to ascertain requirements in the city for TVET is catered where its manpower can concentrate in its coordination, supervision and monitoring of the TVET development in the city. In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this measure is earnestly requested. RUFUS B. RODRIGUEZ MAXIMO B. RODRIGUEZ, JR. Importantly, the bill upholds breastfeeding as the primary and preferred method of infant feeding, positioning donor human milk strictly as a medically indicated alternative when a mother's own milk is unavailable or insufficient. It emphasizes that all human milk donation must remain voluntary, altruistic, and non-commercial, with safeguards against financial inducement and undue influence, consistent with the Philippine Milk Code. To ensure safety and quality, the measure provides for standardized donor screening, milk processing, storage, and distribution systems aligned with Department of Health regulations and internationally recognized practices. It also introduces innovations such as an Online Live Milk Map and Reserve System to improve real-time coordination, equitable allocation, and emergency response. By strengthening breastfeeding support systems and establishing a safe, ethical, and accessible human milk banking network, this measure aims to reduce infant morbidity and mortality, improve neonatal outcomes, and uphold the fundamental rights of every child to optimal nutrition and every mother to adequate breastfeeding support. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. AUDREY KAY T. ZUBIRI
