label: HB 9205
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND PRESERVATION OF PHILIPPINE CULINARY HERITAGE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Food is one of the most enduring expressions of a nation’s culture. In the Philippines, cuisine reflects centuries of interaction among indigenous knowledge systems, agricultural biodiversity, colonial histories, and contemporary innovation. Filipino foodways—recipes, ingredients, techniques, and rituals—form part of the nation’s intangible cultural heritage, yet remain largely under-documented, under-protected, and underutilized as a tool for education, rural development, and nation branding. The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) affirms that food traditions are central to community identity and continuity and has actively promoted culinary heritage as part of sustainable cultural tourism, particularly in Southeast Asia1. In the Philippines, government and industry data indicate that approximately 17% of tourist spending is allocated to food and beverage, translating to an estimated PHP 694 billion in gastronomy‑related tourism revenue in 20252. Market projections show the Philippine culinary tourism sector growing at double‑digit rates over the next decade, underscoring the need for a coherent policy framework to safeguard authenticity while supporting growth. Moreover, the preservation of culinary heritage is inseparable from the protection of agricultural biodiversity. The Philippines is internationally recognized as a center of agrobiodiversity, home to thousands of heirloom rice varieties and indigenous crops maintained by small farmers and indigenous peoples. label: HB 9210
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A CREATIVE INDUSTRY PROCESSING LANE UNDER THE EXISTING SPECIAL WORK PERMIT FRAMEWORK OF THE BUREAU OF IMMIGRATION FOR FOREIGN NATIONALS ENGAGED IN SHORT-TERM PROJECT-BASED CREATIVE WORK, PROVIDING SAFEGUARDS FOR FILIPINO CREATIVE WORKERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine creative industry is increasingly connected to the global market. Film, television, advertising, fashion, live performance, animation, game development, digital media, and other creative sectors now regularly involve cross-border collaboration among Filipino and foreign artists, performers, models, directors, technical specialists, production professionals, and other creative workers. Republic Act No. 11904, otherwise known as the Philippine Creative Industries Development Act, recognizes the importance of creative industries as drivers of economic growth, cultural identity, innovation, job generation, and global competitiveness. If the Philippines is to become a stronger creative production hub, its regulatory environment must allow legitimate international creative collaboration while protecting Filipino workers and ensuring compliance with Philippine law. At present, foreign nationals who participate in short-term creative work may be required to navigate separate immigration, labor, and tax processes. The Bureau of Immigration already issues Special Work Permits for certain foreign artists, athletes, entertainers, performers, and related temporary engagements under its existing authority. However, these processes are not always sufficiently integrated, digital, sector-specific, or responsive to the realities of project-based creative work, where engagements may last only a few days, weeks, or months and may involve productions operating under strict timelines. 1 This measure does not seek to create a competing or duplicate permit outside the existing Bureau of Immigration framework. Rather, it institutionalizes a creative industry processing lane within the existing Special Work Permit system, with clearer statutory rules on inter-agency coordination, accredited sponsorship, tax compliance, labor safeguards, digital processing, and protection of Filipino creative workers. The bill ensures that the Bureau of Immigration remains the primary issuing authority for the permit, while the Department of Labor and Employment retains its authority to determine whether Alien Employment Permit requirements, certificates of exclusion or exemption, or other labor-related safeguards apply. The Bureau of Internal Revenue is tasked to prescribe simplified tax compliance and withholding mechanisms, while the Department of Trade and Industry and relevant creative industry agencies assist in policy coordination and project validation. The National Privacy Commission is likewise included to ensure that digital processing and inter-agency data sharing comply with the Data Privacy Act of 2012. The proposed framework is designed to prevent abuse. It prohibits the use of the processing lane to evade Alien Employment Permit requirements, avoid tax obligations, displace Filipino creative workers, simulate projects, or facilitate unauthorized work. It also requires accredited sponsors to assume responsibility for the foreign creative workers they endorse and to report completion, cancellation, extension, or material changes in the approved engagement. By establishing a clear, streamlined, and safeguarded process for short-term project-based creative work, this bill supports the growth of the Philippine creative economy while upholding immigration control, labor protection, tax compliance, data privacy, and public accountability. It will help make the Philippines more attractive for legitimate international productions without weakening the rights, opportunities, and professional development of Filipino creative workers. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9211
title: AN ACT RECOGNIZING THE RIGHT OF PATIENTS TO DESIGNATE A HEALTHCARE AGENT THROUGH A HEALTHCARE PROXY, PROMOTING ADVANCE CARE PLANNING, AND PROVIDING FOR SUPPORTED HEALTHCARE DECISION-MAKING IN THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The delivery of healthcare is not only a matter of medical treatment, but also of respecting the dignity, autonomy, and wishes of every individual. Yet in the Philippines, many patients who become incapacitated due to illness, injury, disability, or old age are left without a clear legal mechanism for determining who may speak or decide on their behalf regarding healthcare decisions. This often results in confusion among family members, delays in treatment, conflict in healthcare settings, and uncertainty among healthcare providers. At present, Philippine law does not comprehensively recognize healthcare proxies or healthcare agents as a formal mechanism for advance care planning. In practice, healthcare providers are frequently compelled to rely on informal family arrangements or uncertain consent processes during critical medical situations. This gap becomes especially significant in emergency care, end-of-life situations, mental healthcare, and cases involving persons who may temporarily or permanently lose decision-making capacity. Globally, healthcare proxy systems and supported healthcare decision-making frameworks have long been recognized as essential tools in protecting patient rights and ensuring patient-centered care. These mechanisms empower individuals to designate trusted persons to make healthcare decisions consistent with their values, preferences, and best interests in the event they are no longer capable of communicating informed consent. Such frameworks are likewise consistent with the principles embodied in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), which recognizes the equal right of persons with disabilities to exercise legal capacity with appropriate support. 1 This proposed “Right to Care Act” seeks to institutionalize the right of every person to designate a Healthcare Agent through a Healthcare Proxy. It establishes a clear and accessible legal framework for advance care planning while promoting supported healthcare decision-making within the Philippine healthcare system. The bill provides safeguards to ensure that healthcare proxies are voluntarily executed, free from fraud or coercion, and always subject to revocation by the principal. It clarifies the rights, duties, and limitations of Healthcare Agents and Healthcare Providers, while also protecting healthcare providers who act in good faith reliance on healthcare decisions made pursuant to the Act. Importantly, the measure promotes a rights-based, person-centered, and non-discriminatory approach to healthcare decision-making. It recognizes that individuals must remain at the center of decisions affecting their own health and well-being, even during periods of incapacity. It likewise complements existing healthcare reforms under the Universal Health Care Act by strengthening patient participation, autonomy, and continuity of care. This measure also seeks to reduce unnecessary disputes among relatives and healthcare institutions by establishing a clear hierarchy and legal recognition of authorized healthcare decision-makers. At the same time, it preserves existing rights under law and does not authorize any act contrary to law or public policy. Ultimately, this bill affirms that healthcare is not solely about treatment, but about respecting human dignity, protecting individual choice, and ensuring compassionate care during some of the most vulnerable moments in a person’s life. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9212
title: AN ACT PROVIDING EQUITABLE CAREER PATHWAYS FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS AND LEADERS BY ESTABLISHING A SUPERVISION CAREER LINE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This proposed measure seeks to professionalize the public basic education sector by institutionalizing a dedicated Supervision Career Line within the Department of Education's (DepEd) expanded career progression system. Republic Act No. 12288, otherwise known as the “Career Progression System for Public School Teachers and School Leaders Act” was a landmark legislation that marked a significant milestone for teacher welfare. The law was enacted in 2025 in order to establish classroom teaching and school administration career lines with a ladder for professional advancement. However, this still leaves a policy gap that needs to be filled as more technical and pedagogical leadership is still required to sustain such career growth in the teaching profession. This piece of legislation shall serve as the critical pillar in transforming the teaching profession into a career that is growth-driven. It recognizes that instructional leadership, in the form of mentoring teachers and managing curriculum, is a distinct professional skill set that goes beyond classroom instruction and facility management. While the existing law successfully allowed teachers to reach higher salary grades, such as Master Teacher V and VI, without being forced to leave the classroom, without this proposed measure, these teachers often lack the specialized career scaffolding needed to meet increasingly complex professional standards. This bill ensures that Master Teachers who possess a genius for pedagogical leadership can transition into the Supervision Line as Education Supervisors or Senior Education Program Specialists. Under this expanded framework, the Supervision Career Line offers distinct tracks that cater to the evolving needs of the education system. Educators may advance through the Senior Education Program Specialist track (SG 19) or progress through the Education Supervisor I to IV levels (SG 20 to SG 23), culminating in the Chief Education Supervisor position (SG 24). These tracks are designed to ensure that technical assistance and pedagogical guidance are available at every level of governance, from the individual school to the regional office. The Supervision Career Line Act ensures that our educators are not just promoted, but are actively supported by a professionalized supervisory system. We are also hereby ensuring that the ladder provided by RA 12288 is held steady by a competent supervision line. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 9213
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE PROVISION OF AUDIO DESCRIPTION IN AUDIOVISUAL MEDIA AND PUBLIC CONTENTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE According to estimates of the World Health Organization (WHO), at least 2.2 billion people worldwide experience near or distance vision impairment. Despite significant advances in digital technology, a substantial portion of web-based and audiovisual content remains inaccessible to individuals who are blind, have low vision, color blindness, or other visual impairments. In view of this, there is a compelling need to adopt measures that ensure digital and audiovisual content is accessible to persons with visual disabilities. This objective is consistent with the principles embodied in the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the international standards established under the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), which promote equal access to information and communication technologies. Audio description is a recognized accessibility feature designed to narrate key visual elements of media content. It enables persons who are blind or visually impaired to fully understand and enjoy audiovisual materials on an equal footing with sighted audiences. Beyond its benefits for individuals with visual impairments, audio description also serves as an effective support for persons with cognitive disabilities who may experience difficulty interpreting visual cues or who prefer auditory learning modalities. It further provides practical benefits to users who engage with content in eyes-free environments, as well as to individuals learning a foreign language, for whom audio description can enhance comprehension and contextual understanding. Moreover, audio description contributes positively to language development, particularly among children and individuals with autism spectrum disorder. By explicitly describing actions, emotions, and facial expressions, audio description aids in the development of vocabulary, language skills, and the comprehension of social and emotional cues that may otherwise be challenging to interpret. Finally, audio description offers flexibility in content consumption by allowing users to engage with audiovisual materials without continuous visual attention. This has led to emerging usage patterns wherein audio-described media is consumed similarly to audiobooks, enabling individuals to listen while performing other activities such as driving, cooking, or household tasks. As listening plays a critical role in language acquisition and cognitive development, audio description may also serve as a valuable pedagogical tool that reinforces learning, introduces new vocabulary, and promotes active engagement among learners. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Ryan S. label: HB 9215
title: AN ACT POSTPONING THE NOVEMBER 2026 BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 12232, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution guarantees the right of suffrage, a fundamental pillar of democracy. However, the effective exercise of this right requires conditions that allow voters to participate freely, safely, and without undue economic or logistical constraints. The Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections scheduled on November 2, 2026, are expected to be held under extraordinary circumstances that may materially affect voter participation and election administration. The on-going US-Israel-Iran war, which broke out on February 28, 2026 has exacted socio-economic pressures, particularly the drastic increase in fuel prices, which would directly impact mobility, logistics, and access to polling places. As of the beginning of May 2026, fuel prices in the Philippines are estimated to range from approximately ₱74 to ₱107 per liter for gasoline and diesel ₱80 to ₱102 per liter for diesel. These prices represent a jump of 35–65% for gasoline and 55–85% versus pre-war fuel prices. This fuel crisis has contributed to higher transportation costs, which would disproportionately affect voters in remote and geographically dispersed areas, as well as the deployment of election personnel and materials nationwide. Given these realities, holding elections as scheduled would constrain the practical exercise of suffrage, particularly for sectors most affected by rising costs and limited mobility. Ensuring meaningful electoral participation necessarily requires the conditions that allow voters to access and engage in the electoral process without an unreasonable burden. While suffrage is protected, the timing of elections may be adjusted when justified by compelling and extraordinary circumstances, provided such measures are not arbitrary and are aimed at preserving the integrity of the electoral process. This measure therefore seeks to postpone the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections and provide for a transitional arrangement to ensure continuity of local governance, while safeguarding the meaningful exercise of the right of suffrage under prevailing conditions. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. RICHARD I. label: HB 9217
title: AN ACT GRANTING EMPLOYEES IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR THE RIGHT TO DESIGNATE THE FINANCIAL OR ELECTRONIC MONEY ACCOUNT TO WHICH THEIR WAGES OR COMPENSATION SHALL BE DEPOSITED, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 102 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution expressly requires the State to safeguard workers' rights, promote their overall welfare, and strictly prohibit combinations in restraint of trade alongside unfair market competition. At present, private sector employers hold the exclusive authority to dictate the specific banking institution where employee salaries are deposited. This entrenched practice creates unintended negative consequences on worker convenience and broader economic competition. Certain banks achieve an unfair competitive advantage, securing a captive market simply because a singular corporate entity handpicked them, rather than earning those clients through superior service. All employees must be granted the absolute freedom to select which traditional bank or Electronic Money Issuer they will trust for their wage deposits. In choosing an ideal depository institution, individuals consider vital factors like attractive financial products, higher interest rates, digital service availability, and geographical accessibility. If financial institutions were compelled to actively compete for individual payroll deposits, they would be strongly incentivized to provide superior goods and minimize account fees The financial landscape has evolved dramatically. Today, real-time inter-bank transfer networks and advanced digital wallets make cross-institution payroll disbursements completely seamless and technically effortless. This updated measure aims to grant private sector employees the undisputed right to designate their preferred bank or digital wallet for wage deposits, firmly promoting true market competition and financial autonomy. Crucially, the bill mandates that electronic transfer fees incurred during disbursement must be fully borne by the employer, guaranteeing that workers' salaries remain intact. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ANTONINO B. label: HB 9224
title: AN ACT AMENDING R.A.11697, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE ELECTRIC VEHICLE INDUSTRY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 11697, otherwise known as the Electric Vehicle Industry Development Act, was enacted to promote the development and adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) in the Philippines. Since its passage, the global shift towards electric mobility has accelerated as countries worldwide strengthened policies and incentives to reduce carbon emissions, improve air quality, and lessen dependence on fossil fuels. The Philippines continues to face rising fuel costs, heavy dependence on imported oil, and increasing transportation-related pollution. These challenges highlight the importance of expanding and extending the incentives and support mechanisms for electric vehicles and charging infrastructure in the country. This bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 11697 by increasing the required EV share in government and private fleets, expanding EV parking and charging infrastructure, and extending fiscal and non-fiscal incentives for EVs and charging stations until 2035. The measure also enhances discounts on vehicle registration and user charges for battery electric and hybrid electric vehicles to encourage wider adoption. Strengthening the country’s EV policy will help reduce fuel dependency, lower greenhouse gas emissions, improve public health through cleaner air, attract investments in green industries, and create new economic opportunities and jobs for Filipinos. Moreover, it will support the government’s commitment to sustainable transportation and long-term energy security. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is respectfully sought. FRANZ S. label: HB 9225
title: AN ACT DECLARING SEPTEMBER 12 OF EVERY YEAR AS A NATIONAL DAY OF PRAYER AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In II Chronicles 7:14, it is written: “If my people who are called by My name humble themselves, and pray and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and will forgive their sin and heal their land.” (New King James Version) Throughout the history of the Philippines, the Filipino people have relied on faith, prayer, and spiritual solidarity as sources of strength and hope, especially during times of difficulty and uncertainty. The 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution was a response of the millions of Filipinos, heeding the appeal of then Manila archbishop Jaime Cardinel Sin, “to pray because it is only through prayer that we may solve this problem” (Dela Peña, 2026). Fourteen months after the devastation of super typhoon Yolanda, Pope Francis visited Tacloban, Leyte. Though the Pope admitted he is at a lost for words, the pontiff enjoined those who gathered to pray in silence (Fernandez and Chiu, 2015). During the COVID-19 Pandemic, President Rodrigo Duterte, in an Interfaith Prayer Meeting, sought divine guidance, urging the Filipino to fervently pray for the Lord to heal the land (Parrocha, 2021). Today, the Filipino people continue to confront serious national challenges, including poverty, corruption, criminality, illegal drugs, social division, mental health struggles, economic instability, destructive effects of natural disasters, and moral decline. These challenges not only weaken institutions and strain communities, but erode moral and family values, the foundation of the nation. The proposed measure builds upon prior executive issuances recognizing September 12 a day of prayer and reflection, including Proclamation Nos. 910 (s. 2005), 1095 (s. 2006), 1362 (s. 2007), 1555 (s. 2008), and 1869 (s. 2009) issued by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, and Proclamation Nos. 25 (s. 2010) and 249 (s. 2011) issued by President Benigno S. Aquino III, all designating September 12 as National Day of Prayer. These issuances are reflection of a long-standing State policy of promoting voluntary, non-sectarian expression of faith as part of promoting peace, moral reflection, and fostering national solidarity. This bill seeks to institutionalize the observance of September 12 of every year as a “National Day of Prayer” to provide an inclusive, voluntary, and non- sectarian opportunity for Filipinos of all faiths, religious traditions, and beliefs to gather in prayer, reflection, and acts of goodwill for the nation and its people. The measure aims to promote peace, compassion, mutual respect, interfaith dialogue, cross-cultural understanding, civic responsibility, stronger Filipino families, and national harmony in a manner consistent with the constitutional principles of religious freedom and the separation of Church and State. This measure neither establishes a state religion nor compels participation in any religious activity. Rather, it recognizes the enduring role of prayer, reflection, and solidarity continue to play in fostering hope, moral renewal, family unity, social responsibility, and genuine national progress for the Filipino people. As the letter of Paul to Romans 10:13 reminds us: “For ‘whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.’” (New King James Version) In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 9230
title: AN ACT AFFIRMING THE AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITY OF THE SCHOOLS, THEIR ADMINISTRATORS AND TEACHERS TO DISCIPLINE CHILDREN UNDER THEIR SUPERVISION, INSTRUCTION, OR CUSTODY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Back in the days when the Philippines was a predominantly patriarchal society and the goods were more affordable, the mothers were the ones responsible for rearing and disciplining their children. Mothers spend more time with their children and can easily notice and correct undesirable manners and conduct. These responsibilities were only exercised by the schools, administrators, and teachers when children go to their schools. Fast forward to today, when the prices of basic necessities eat away a large chunk of an average Filipino’s family budget, both parents are compelled to work to better provide for their families or simply… survive. Because of this, children spend less time with their parents. Thus, the schools today have a larger role in the holistic development of our youth, including molding the character of children through the appropriate and commensurate methods of discipline. Under Article 220 par. (7) of the Executive Order No. 209, otherwise known as the “Family Code of the Philippines”, the parents and those exercising parental authority shall have, with respect to their unemancipated children or wards, the right and duty to impose discipline on them as may be required under the circumstances. Article 218 of the Family Code expressly stated that the school, its administrators and teachers, or the individual, entity or institution engaged in child shall have special parental authority and responsibility over the minor child while under their supervision, instruction or custody. With the enactment of Republic Act No. 7610, otherwise known as the “Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act”, traditional methods of imposing discipline against children now bordered a thin line with committing the offense of child abuse. At present, the determination of whether a certain action on discipline will constitute a violation of RA 7610 depends on the severity, nature, and intention of the action. Thus, light spanking might be tolerated, but beating with objects, or repeated beatings may be considered abusive. Physical punishment aimed at correction are acceptable but those done to vent frustration or humiliate the child are violative. However, no matter how brilliant or how academically competitive our students may be, without discipline, the schools’ mission and our teachers’ dedicated services are rendered meaningless because discipline is the tool that shapes academic brilliance into tangible success. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. DALE B. title: AN ACT REDISTRIBUTING THE SHARE OF THE METROPOLITAN MANILA DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY IN THE NATIONAL TAX ALLOTMENT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 10 (B) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7924, ENTITLED “AN ACT CREATING THE METROPOLITAN MANILA DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 284 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, otherwise known as the “Local Government Code of 1991”, provides that local government units (LGUs) shall receive 40% share from the national taxes based on the collection of the third fiscal year preceding the current year. Subsequently, Republic Act No. 7924 was enacted, creating the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) and providing among others that it shall continue to receive the Internal Revenue Allotment (now National Tax Allotment [NTA]) allocated to the now defunct Metro Manila Authority. In the present allocation of the NTA, the MMDA is considered as a province. Apart from its allocation from the NTA, MMDA also receives: (1) annual appropriations from the General Appropriations Act; (2) income from fines, fees and charges that it is authorized to impose and collect; and more importantly, (3) Five percent (5%) of the total annual gross revenue of the preceding year, net of NTA, of each LGU in the Metropolitan Manila. Hence, as the annual gross revenues of all the cities and municipality in the Metropolitan Manila exponentially increase due to dynamic economic activities, the respective shares of the MMDA proportionately increase with them. In fact, the total shares received by MMDA from constituent cities and municipality stood at P4.533-billion in 2025, which is substantially larger than its share from the NTA amounting to P0.817-billion in the same year or 18.02%. label: HB 9233
title: AN ACT DECLARING THE MUNICIPALITY OF DONSOL, PROVINCE OF SORSOGON, AS THE CAPITAL FOR BUTANDING INTERACTION AND CONSERVATION IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Certain natural wonders inspire awe as profoundly as the butanding, the largest fish in the world, yet among the gentlest of marine giants. Known for its immense size, calm presence, and striking white-and-gray spotted patterns, the butanding is one of the most majestic and recognizable species in the ocean, prized not only for its beauty and rarity, but also for its ecological importance.1 The Municipality of Donsol, Province of Sorsogon, has long been identified with the butanding and has earned national and international recognition as the country’s foremost destination for whale shark interaction. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), in its case study on Philippine best practices in sustainable tourism, described Donsol’s whale shark interaction program as the Philippines’ most successful ecotourism product. Its distinction has likewise been affirmed by major recognitions, including TIME Magazine’s “Best Place for an Animal Encounter” in 2004 and the 11th Kalakbay Award in 2003 for the eco-tourism product category.2 This measure is necessary because Donsol is not merely a place where tourists occasionally encounter butanding, but a locality that has built, over time, a model of ethical and conservation-based wildlife tourism. That commitment is reflected in Donsol’s Municipal Ordinance No. 12, series of 1998, which protected the butanding, declared Donsol’s municipal waters a sanctuary for the species, and vested upon the local government the authority to operate, control, and manage the community-based ecotourism program. This legal and policy foundation is further borne out by data reported by WWF-Philippines in 2024, showing that Donsol accounted for 40% of the 1 National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. (2024, June 16). What is the biggest fish in the ocean? National Ocean Service. https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/bigfish.html 2 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation. (2006, July). Best practices in sustainable tourism management initiatives for APEC economies (Chapter 6, Philippines). https://www.apec.org/docs/default-source/Publications/2006/7/Best-Practices-in-Sustainable-Tourism-Management-Initiatives-for- APEC-Economies-July-2006/TOC/Chapter-6-The-Philippines.pdf 1 2,024 whale shark sightings recorded in the Philippines since 2007, underscoring its central role in the country’s marine conservation efforts.3 Declaring Donsol as the Capital for Butanding Interaction and Conservation in the Philippines is to accord formal legislative recognition to its established role as a leading center of ethical, responsible, and sustainable ecotourism. The term “interaction” is particularly apt, as butanding are migratory species whose seasonal presence in Donsol reflects their natural movement consistent with the municipality’s non-intrusive ecotourism program. Thus, the bill does more than confer a title but provides a clear policy signal that can strengthen destination identity, enhance visitor confidence, and encourage greater public and private investment in tourism facilities, conservation initiatives, and local enterprise. The measure is likewise justified by its economic and social impact. Data from the Donsol Tourism Office, as cited by the Philippine News Agency, showed that the pre-pandemic 2019 butanding season generated ₱448 million in gross revenues and around 13,000 tourist arrivals, with substantial benefits flowing to the local community and the local government. These figures demonstrate that responsible tourism, when properly managed, can protect wildlife while creating dignified livelihoods, drawing investment, and expanding opportunities for local residents.4 Ultimately, this bill affirms a recognized model of development that our country may well uphold with pride, one in which tourism safeguards wildlife, sustains livelihoods, attracts investment, and empowers communities to become faithful stewards of nature. Having earned various distinction through years of conservation, responsible tourism, and community-driven progress, it is both just and timely for Congress to accord formal and lasting recognition to the Municipality of Donsol, Province of Sorsogon, by declaring it the Capital for Butanding Interaction and Conservation in the Philippines. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. ESCUDERO Representative 1st District, Sorsogon 3 Recebido, B. (2024, January 25). label: HB 9234
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING MENTAL HEALTH UNITS IN ALL GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS IN THE COUNTRY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of 1987 Constitution provides that the State shall protect the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. Also, the State shall adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development which shall endeavor to make essential goods, health, and other social services available to all the people at affordable cost. There shall be priority for the needs of the underprivileged sick, elderly, disabled, women, and children.1 Recent studies have highlighted a significant gap in mental health services within the Philippines. According to the World Health Organization, mental health disorders affect one in four people globally, yet access to mental health professionals remains limited, particularly in public healthcare settings. Research by the Department of Health indicates that the shortage of psychiatrists and mental health professionals contributes to inadequate mental health support, exacerbating conditions and leading to poorer health outcomes for those affected. 2 This bill proposes to establish mental health units in all government hospitals across the country and deploy psychiatrists and mental health practitioners in these units. By ensuring that each government hospital has three (3) dedicated psychiatric professionals, the bill aims to enhance the quality and accessibility of mental health services, providing timely and effective care to individuals in need. The presence of psychiatrists in these facilities will facilitate comprehensive mental health assessments, diagnosis, and treatment, thereby addressing mental health issues with the same urgency and importance as physical health conditions. Improved mental health 1 Article II, Section 15, 1987 Philippine Constitution 2 Mental health issues. (n.d.). Socioeconomic Research Portal for the Philippines. https://serp-p.pids.gov.ph/feature/public/index- view?slug=Mental-Health-Issues. 1 services will help lessen the financial burden on individuals, families, and people who find it difficult to pay for the costs of therapy. The need for this bill stems from the growing recognition of mental health as a critical aspect of public health. Institutionalizing psychiatrists in government hospitals will not only bridge the existing gaps in mental health services in the country but also promote a more integrated approach to healthcare that considers mental and physical health as interlinked. For people and communities, improved mental health services can lead to a higher economic productivity. By improving access to psychiatric care, this bill seeks to advance the nation's overall health standards, reduce the stigma associated with mental health issues, and ensure that every individual has the opportunity to receive the care they need HON. label: HB 9235
title: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM TAXES ALL INCENTIVES, REWARDS, BONUSES, EMOLUMENTS, DONATIONS, GIFTS, ENDOWMENTS AND CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED BY NATIONAL ATHLETES AND COACHES WHO WIN IN INTERNATIONAL SPORTS COMPETITIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10699, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "NATIONAL ATHLETES AND COACHES BENEFITS AND INCENTIVES ACT"
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Sports has always been more than a game. For many young Filipinos, especially those in the provinces, sports is discipline, education, confidence, community, and hope. As an advocate of both education and sports, this representation believes that every young person who is given a court, a coach, a uniform, and a chance to compete is also given a stronger chance to dream beyond poverty, distance, and circumstance. This assertion is supported by both international and local policy. The World Health Organization recognizes that regular physical activity provides significant physical and mental health benefits, while UNESCO emphasizes that physical education and sport are key to youth development. UNICEF likewise recognizes sport and play as instruments for education, protection, social inclusion, and empowerment, especially for vulnerable children.1 In the Philippines, the Department of Education has institutionalized School Sports Clubs in public schools to promote learners’ holistic development, physical fitness, well-being, and more accessible sports participation. The Philippine Sports Commission also recognizes grassroots and “Sports for All” development as a national mandate for inclusive sports growth nationwide.2 Filipino athletes and coaches have brought pride and honor to the country. The Philippines emerged as overall champion of the 2019 Southeast Asian Games. Hidilyn Diaz won the country’s first Olympic gold medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games, and Carlos Yulo won two Olympic gold medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics. These 1 World Health Organization. (2024, June 26). Physical activity. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/physical-activity 2 Department of Education. (2025, August 7). Policy guidelines on the institutionalization of the school sports club in public schools (DepEd Order No. 022, s. 2025) [PDF]. https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/DO_s2025_022r.pdf 1 victories prove that Filipino athletes, when supported, can stand among the best in the world. Yet behind every medal is a long and costly road: years of training, sacrifice, family support, coaching, nutrition, equipment, travel, and recovery. While Republic Act No. 10699 already grants benefits and incentives to national athletes and coaches, and while the Bureau of Internal Revenue has recognized the income tax exemption of prizes, awards, rewards, gifts, and donations received by athletes such as Carlos Yulo, gaps remain in the tax treatment of private support. In particular, private gifts and rewards may still create donor-side tax and deductibility concerns, which can discourage individuals and corporations from giving more generously and consistently to athletes and coaches. This measure therefore seeks to exempt from applicable taxes and fees the winnings, prizes, awards, bonuses, donations, gifts, endowments, and other forms of support received by national athletes and coaches in connection with international sports competitions. It also seeks to encourage greater private sector participation by making such support more meaningful, direct, and unburdened by unnecessary tax friction. Various state policies strongly encourage sports programs, league competitions, and training for international competitions to foster self-discipline, teamwork, and excellence for a healthy and alert citizenry. This bill gives life to that mandate. It honors not only the athlete on the podium, but also the coach, the family, the school, the community, and the local sports programs that helped make that victory possible. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 9236
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF THE RIGHTS OF AIRLINE PASSENGERS, IMPOSING OBLIGATIONS ON AIR CARRIERS, AND PENALIZING ACTS IN VIOLATION THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This Bill seeks to refile past versions of the proposal originally filed by Bayan Muna Party-List Representatives Neri Javier Colmenares and Carlos Isagani T. Zarate during the 16th Congress. Their House Bill 5361 was one of the mother bills made as main reference for the Consolidated House Bill 6191, entitled An Act Providing for the Protection of the Rights of Airline Passengers and Penalizing Acts in Violation Thereof that was approved on Third Reading, likewise during the 16th Congress. Air travel has become an indispensable mode of conveying passengers and goods in the Philippines. As a common carrier, an airline company assumes the express obligation to transport passengers to their destination safely and to observe extraordinary diligence in the conduct of their business. Providing safe, efficient, and convenient service to its customers is therefore a strictly construed obligation of an airline company. However, despite increasing profits from the air industry business, airline companies have wantonly disregarded passengers’ rights, confident that passengers do not generally demand for remedies against abuse due to the expensive and tedious legal processes that usually favor the rich and the powerful. Among other problems, long queues in check-in counters, delayed flights, overbooking, diversion of flights, passenger bumping, and sudden cancellations of flights, to name a few, continue to be prevalent in all airports in the country, plaguing airline passengers for decades. The government issued DOTC-DTI Joint Administrative Order 01-2012, providing for the Bill of Rights of Air Passengers and Airline Obligations, supposedly 1 to address these problems. However, such problems persist, becoming worse during peak seasons such as the holidays. The JAO, therefore, has failed to protect the rights of airline passengers and is bereft of sufficient penalties to sanction airline companies. Legal recourse for passengers against airline companies have proved difficult and costly, practically rendering ineffective their rights under the Warsaw Convention, the Montreal Convention, and other international law norms that provide for remedies for violation of air passengers’ rights. Airline companies are emboldened to disregard passengers’ rights in their drive for mega profits, while the government remains toothless against airline abuse. Republic Act 776, Presidential Decree 1462, Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) regulations, and other laws do not suffice to protect air passengers’ rights. Any legislation providing for piecemeal response will not lay down lasting solutions. A more comprehensive legislation on passengers’ rights has become an imperative. It is high time to impose obligations on airline companies to ensure safe, convenient and affordable travel for the people, to guarantee to victims speedy legal remedies, and to discourage airline companies from disregarding their passengers’ rights. Airline passengers who receive compensation and benefits under this proposed law may still avail of additional compensation or benefits under international law through the regular courts. But the purpose of this special law is to provide for a cheaper and faster remedy to victims, and at the same time deter airline companies from violating passengers’ rights. For the foregoing reasons, approval of this Bill is earnestly sought. REP. ANTONIO L. TINIO ACT Teachers Party-List REP. SARAH JANE I. ELAGO REP. RENEE LOUISE M. title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A MINIMUM AGE FOR SOCIAL MEDIA USE, REGULATING CHILDREN’S ACCESS TO SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS, PRESCRIBING OBLIGATIONS FOR SOCIAL MEDIA PROVIDERS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The rise of social media has transformed the way young people learn, communicate, and engage with the world. While digital platforms provide unprecedented opportunities for education, creativity, and civic participation, they have also exposed children to increasing risks such as cyberbullying, online exploitation, compulsive digital behavior, harmful content, and algorithm-driven engagement systems designed to maximize screen time rather than protect well-being. The Philippines, where internet and social media usage among the youth remains among the highest globally, faces the urgent challenge of protecting children in digital spaces. Existing regulatory frameworks address unlawful online conduct but remain insufficient to respond to the evolving architecture of modern social media platforms and the behavioral design systems that influence the habits, mental health, and development of minors. Globally, governments have begun adopting stronger regulatory measures in response to these concerns. Australia recently enacted landmark legislation imposing minimum age restrictions for social media access and strengthening platform accountability mechanisms to protect minors from harmful online exposure. France passed legislation restricting social media access for children below fifteen (15) years of age without verified parental consent. The United Kingdom, through its Online Safety Act and Age-Appropriate Design Code, now requires digital platforms to implement child-centered safety and privacy standards by default. Likewise in Southeast Asia, Indonesia has intensified its regulation of digital platforms through stronger child protection, electronic systems regulation, and content moderation rules aimed at addressing online exploitation, harmful content, and platform accountability. These developments reflect a growing international consensus that protecting children online is no longer solely a matter of parental supervision, but also a legitimate and necessary area of public policy and platform regulation. This proposed “Social Media Safety for Children Act” adopts a measured approach in addressing these emerging risks. Rather than imposing broad or punitive restrictions on children and families, the bill establishes clear and proportionate obligations on social media platforms to create safer digital environments for minors. Considering that modern online harms are often embedded not merely in content itself but in platform design choices that encourage compulsive engagement and excessive use, the measure requires platforms to implement safeguards against addictive features such as autoplay systems, manipulative notifications, and algorithmic recommendations directed at minors. Ultimately, this measure seeks to protect Filipino children from the harmful effects of unregulated social media usage. In recognizing that child protection in the digital age requires utmost responsibility, we must therefore enact strong public policies that ensure that the systems, algorithms, and engagement models of digital platforms shaping online behavior must prioritize the safety and protection of Filipino children. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 9238
title: AN ACT DECLARING THE LUMAMPAO VIEW DECK IN BARANGAY DON JUAN, MUNICIPALITY OF CUENCA, PROVINCE OF BATANGAS AS AN ECOTOURISM SITE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Municipality of Cuenca in the Province of Batangas is home to several natural attractions that contribute to the province’s growing eco-tourism industry. Among these is the Lumampao View Deck located in Barangay Don Juan, a scenic destination known for its panoramic landscapes in magnificent view of the Taal lake and Mt. Maculot, cool mountain atmosphere, and peaceful environment that provide opportunities for recreation, relaxation, and outdoor activities for both residents and visitors. As tourism continues to play a vital role in local economic development, there is a need to strengthen and institutionalize government support for emerging eco-tourism destinations such as the Lumampao View Deck. Declaring the area as an official tourism site will encourage sustainable development, improve accessibility and infrastructure, generate employment and livelihood opportunities for local communities, and promote Cuenca as a family-friendly and environmentally responsible destination in Batangas. This measure seeks to declare the Lumampao View Deck as a tourism site. This bill ensures that tourism development in the area shall be undertaken in a manner that preserves its natural beauty and ecological integrity through coordinated planning among the Department of Tourism (DOT), the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA), and the local government unit of Cuenca, Batangas. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 9239
title: AN ACT DECLARING THE SABANG RIVER IN BARANGAY WAWA, CITY OF TANAUAN, PROVINCE OF BATANGAS AS AN ECOTOURISM SITE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Province of Batangas is endowed with abundant natural resources and ecologically significant areas that possess immense potential for sustainable tourism development. Among these is the Sabang River located in Barangay Wawa, City of Tanauan, a scenic and environmentally important river system that serves as a source of livelihood, recreation, and ecological balance for the surrounding communities. The Sabang River is characterized by its natural beauty, rich biodiversity, and tranquil environment, making it an ideal destination for eco-tourism activities such as river trekking, nature appreciation, educational tours, and other environmentally sustainable recreational activities. Its preservation and responsible development can contribute significantly to environmental awareness while generating economic opportunities for local residents. Recognizing the growing importance of eco-tourism as a driver of inclusive local economic growth, it is imperative for the government to promote and develop environmentally sustainable tourism destinations that balance conservation with community development. Declaring the Sabang River as an eco-tourism site will encourage the establishment of appropriate infrastructure and tourism facilities while ensuring the protection and preservation of its ecological integrity. By enacting this measure, tourism in Tanauan will be showcased, thereby ensuring the environmental conservation of our natural heritage, and generating livelihood and employment opportunities for our local communities in Batangas. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 9244
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE BED CAPACITY OF THE CAGAYAN VALLEY MEDICAL CENTER (CVMC) IN TUGUEGARAO CITY, PROVINCE OF CAGAYAN, FROM ONE THOUSAND (1,000) TO ONE THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED (1,500) BEDS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to increase the authorized bed capacity of the Cagayan Valley Medical Center (CVMC) from one thousand (1,000) to one thousand five hundred (1,500) beds. As a premier tertiary government hospital in Northern Luzon, the Cagayan Valley Medical Center (CVMC) continues to experience a steady rise in patient admissions brought about by population growth, expanded healthcare coverage, and its vital role as a referral center for neighboring provinces. Although Republic Act No. 11498 previously increased the hospital’s authorized bed capacity to one thousand (1,000) beds, the current capacity remains insufficient to adequately address the growing healthcare demands of the population it serves. The persistent influx of patients has resulted in overcrowded hospital wards, hallway admissions, long queues for laboratory and diagnostic services, and increased strain on hospital resources, personnel, and infrastructure. This situation compromises the quality of care, patient safety, and overall operational efficiency of the hospital. In response thereto, this measure proposes to further increase the authorized bed capacity of the CVMC to one thousand five hundred (1,500) beds. The proposed expansion aims to decongest overcrowded wards, improve patient accommodation, and enhance the delivery of timely and quality healthcare services. It will also strengthen the hospital’s capacity to respond to emergencies, epidemics, and disasters, support the Universal Health Care program by expanding access to inpatient services, and promote better working conditions for healthcare personnel. The proposed increase shall be accompanied by the necessary augmentation in staffing, medical equipment, and facility improvements, subject to appropriate planning, budgeting, and approval by the relevant government agencies. This measure is necessary to ensure that CVMC remains capable of fulfilling its mandate as a leading government healthcare institution in the region and to address the growing healthcare needs of the population it serves. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOSEPH “JOJO” L. label: HB 9245
title: AN ACT DECLARING THE MUNICIPALITY OF PEÑABLANCA IN THE PROVINCE OF CAGAYAN AS A TOURISM DEVELOPMENT AREA, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Municipality of Peñablanca in the Province of Cagayan is endowed with exceptional natural, cultural, and ecological resources that make it a prime destination for sustainable tourism development. It is home to the renowned Peñablanca Protected Landscape and Seascape, which includes the Callao Cave, diverse limestone formations, underground rivers, and rich biodiversity. Peñablanca also holds significant historical and archaeological importance, being the site of some of the earliest evidence of human habitation in Northern Luzon. Its unique blend of eco-tourism attractions, cultural heritage, and adventure tourism opportunities positions it as a vital contributor to the region’s tourism industry. Despite its vast potential, the municipality remains underdeveloped in terms of tourism infrastructure, investment, and promotion. Declaring Peñablanca as a Tourism Development Area will enable the national and local governments to prioritize its development, attract investments, improve infrastructure, and ensure the sustainable management of its natural and cultural resources. This measure aims to promote inclusive economic growth, generate employment opportunities for local communities, and preserve the ecological integrity and cultural heritage of the area. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOSEPH “JOJO” L. label: HB 9251
title: AN ACT QUALIFYING ALL PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS TO RECEIVE THE TEACHING ALLOWANCE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT 11997 OR THE KABALIKAT SA PAGTUTURO ACT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act 11997 or An Act Institutionalizing the Grant of a Teaching Allowance for Public School Teachers and Appropriating Funds Therefor was enacted on March 13, 2024. Principally authored by ACT Teachers Party-List Rep. Antonio L. Tinio and Rep. France L. Castro, this law was borne out of a longstanding campaign for adequate support for the purchase of chalks, bond papers, cartolina, and countless other materials that they use in the delivery of education. Otherwise known as the Kabalikat sa Pagtuturo Act, the law not only institutionalized what was previously called the “chalk allowance” but increased it to ₱10,000. But under current regulations implementing this law, only classroom teachers or those with teaching loads are qualified to receive the allowance. Section 4 of the IRR reiterates the coverage of the law—which has a broad language that should be interpreted appropriately. However, per Section 8, only “qualified public school teachers assigned with teaching load” are the ones entitled to the allowance. For instance, Principals, those assigned as Assistant School Head Designates or Department Head Designates, and 1 others whose plantilla positions who do not as a general rule have teaching loads, are required to present proof of actual teaching hours that they rendered, and they will be given only pro-rated teaching allowance. If they had not been assigned teaching loads within the school year, they do not qualify for it at all. There have been reports from the field of teachers getting zero teaching allowance because they have been assigned only non-teaching functions. DepEd’s interpretation closes its eyes to the intent of the law, that is, to provide assistance to public school teachers by covering the expenses necessary for the delivery of quality education, thus, “for the purchase of tangible or intangible teaching supplies and materials, the payment of incidental expenses, and the implementation or conduct of various learning delivery modalities.” (Sections 2 and 4) By doing so, the DepEd excludes from the benefit many public school teachers who spend out of their own pockets for supplies, materials, and other expenses incidental to the delivery of education services. To cure this situation, this Bill seeks to amend Republic Act 11997 by clarifying the legislative intent that all public school teachers are entitled to the grant of the teaching allowance. Republic Act 4670 or the Magna Carta for Public School Teachers, defines public school teachers as “all persons engaged in classroom teaching, in any level of instruction, on full-time basis, including x x x all other persons performing supervisory and/or administrative functions in all schools x x x operated by the Government or its political subdivisions; but shall not include school nurses, school physicians, school dentists, and other school employees.” This means that even Principals or School Heads and Head Teachers, as well as those holding minimal classroom teaching loads such as Master Teachers, are public school teachers. In the course of their duties as such, they buy tangible and intangible teaching supplies, pay incidental expenses, and in general, implement the various learning delivery modalities—all of which must be paid for by the government through the teaching allowance per Sections 2 and 4 of Republic Act 11997. For these reasons, immediate approval of this Bill is sought. ______________________________ REP. ANTONIO L. label: HB 9252
title: AN ACT POSTPONING THE OCTOBER 2026 BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9164, AS AMENDED, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution, recognizes the value of local governments. The Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) play a vital role in ensuring grassroots democracy and local governance. However, numerous challenges have arisen that affect the effective conduct of these elections. These include the need for continuity in local programs, the efficient allocation of public funds, and the prioritization of national recovery efforts in light of economic pressures. Furthermore, the current global climate, marked by ongoing armed conflicts and geopolitical tensions, has underscored the urgent need for governments to exercise prudence in fiscal management. The Philippines must ensure the proper allocation of its fiscal resources to safeguard national interests, mitigate the economic impact of war-related disruptions, and strengthen resilience against external shocks. This election will also place a significant financial burden on the government, diverting resources that could otherwise be used for essential public services and development programs. This proposed measure seeks to postpone the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections originally scheduled for 2026 to 2029. The extension of the term of incumbent barangay and SK officials will allow for the uninterrupted implementation of ongoing projects, programs, and reforms at the community level. Moreover, it aims to afford the government ample time to introduce and implement necessary electoral reforms that will strengthen the integrity, transparency, and efficiency of future barangay elections. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ARTURO B. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 Chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a significant public health concern in the Philippines, with thousands of patients requiring regular dialysis to survive. However, access to dialysis services remains limited, particularly in public hospitals outside major urban centers, and the high cost of treatment continues to impose a heavy financial burden on patients and their families¹. 27 This bill seeks to require all national, regional, and provincial government hospitals to establish and maintain dialysis wards or units, ensuring that life-saving treatment becomes more accessible across the country. label: HB 9261
title: AN ACT GRANTING PHILIPPINE CITIZENSHIP TO SHIR SHAH AYOBI
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Shir Shah Ayobi, the current Country Director of the American Red Cross in the Philippines, has devoted more than thirty (30) years of his professional life to humanitarian service through the International Committee of the Red Cross and the American Red Cross. A civil engineer by training and an Afghan national of legal age, Mr. Ayobi has served in Asia, Africa, the Caribbean, and the Middle East in response to major disasters, including the Indian Ocean Tsunami, the Haiti Earthquake, and Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda). Mr. Ayobi has been residing and working in the Philippines since March 2018, with prior periods of residence from 2014 to 2016. In his capacity as Country Director, Mr. Ayobi has led and managed humanitarian programs focused on disaster recovery, disaster risk reduction, and community resilience. He oversaw the Typhoon Yolanda recovery and post-recovery programs in the Province of Leyte and supported long-term Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) initiatives in the provinces of Catanduanes, Albay, and Camarines Sur. As a civil engineer, he has likewise contributed to the construction of shelter facilities and the improvement of access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene for vulnerable Filipino communities. Mr. Ayobi has built deep and lasting relationships with local communities, government authorities, and members of civil society throughout the country. He has also developed a profound appreciation for the Filipino way of life, values, social bonds, and culture, and he has chosen the Philippines as the country where he wishes to permanently establish his home, as a personal and long-term commitment. His 1 family has likewise established roots in the Philippines, with his children having studied or currently studying at the International School of Manila. He is a person of good moral character, has demonstrated financial capacity, and has abided by Philippine laws and regulations throughout his residence in the country. In recognition of Mr. Ayobi's exceptional humanitarian contributions to the Filipino people, his demonstrated commitment to the Philippines as his permanent home, and his qualifications under existing law, the grant of Philippine citizenship by legislative act is earnestly sought. 10 11 12 MARIA RACHEL J. label: HB 9262
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FRESH GRADUATES OF PHILIPPINE TERTIARY EDUCATION, UNIVERSITIES, COLLEGES AND TRAINING INSTITUTIONS, OF A ONE-TIME CASH GRANT OF FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (PHP5,000)
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 13, Article II of the 1987 Constitution provides that, “the State recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building and shall promote and protect their physical and social well-being.” Further, the State is mandated to provide adequate social services, to promote full employment, a rising standard of living, and an improved quality of life for all. Republic Act No. 11261 was enacted to expand accessibility to government services and to provide incentives to improve a first time jobseeker’s access to employment. New graduates experience financial challenges directly related to seeking employment. Aside from fees and charges in obtaining proofs of identification, clearances, certificates or other documents, they incur expenses for other application requirements, transportation for interviews, and relocation. New graduates, who typically have little to no savings, find it difficult to navigate and address the mounting costs for seeking employment. Aware of this reality, it becomes imperative for the State to provide assistance to new graduates as a means to alleviate the financial challenges that new graduates face. This bill serves as a counterpart measure in the House of Representatives to the bill principally authored and filed by Senator JV Ejercito in the Senate. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. TOBIAS “TOBY” M. label: HB 9264
title: AN ACT MANDATING LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO GRANT HAZARD PAY TO ALL LOCAL GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES WHOSE WORK ENTAILS INHERENT RISK OR DANGER TO THEIR HEALTH AND SAFETY REGARDLESS OF EMPLOYMENT STATUS, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes the vital role of public servants and mandates the State to promote their welfare and ensure humane working conditions. Local government employees who perform duties involving exposure to physical, biological, chemical, environmental, and safety hazards play a crucial role in the delivery of essential public services. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many local government personnel— including health workers, traffic enforcers, street sweepers, cemetery workers, social welfare personnel, and other frontline employees—continued to perform their duties despite serious risks to their health and safety. However, many of these workers did not receive adequate hazard compensation despite the dangerous nature of their assignments. While existing laws provide hazard pay for specific sectors such as public health workers, there remains no comprehensive policy mandating all Local Government Units (LGUs) to grant hazard pay to local government personnel whose work inherently exposes them to danger, regardless of employment status. This bill seeks to institutionalize the grant of hazard pay to qualified local government employees, including those under temporary, casual, contractual, job order, and contract of service arrangements, in recognition of the risks attendant to their work and their indispensable contribution to public service. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9265
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE UPGRADE OF THE SALARY GRADES OF DENTISTS IN THE PUBLIC SECTOR, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Dentists in the public sector play a vital role in promoting oral health, preventing dental diseases, and delivering essential healthcare services to Filipinos, especially in underserved and vulnerable communities. They serve in government hospitals, rural health units, public schools, state universities and colleges, and other public health institutions where access to dental care is often limited. Despite the importance of their profession and the increasing demands of public healthcare service, government dentists continue to receive compensation that is not commensurate with their duties, responsibilities, qualifications, and professional expertise. The current salary structure has contributed to low morale, difficulty in retaining qualified personnel in government service, and the migration of dental professionals to the private sector or overseas employment opportunities. Republic Act No. 7305, otherwise known as the “Magna Carta of Public Health Workers,” recognizes the State policy of promoting and improving the social and economic well-being of health workers and encouraging competent professionals to remain in government service. In line with this policy, there is a pressing need to upgrade the salary grades of dentists in the public sector to ensure fair compensation, strengthen the delivery of oral healthcare services, and enhance the government’s capacity to attract and retain competent dental professionals. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9266
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ANNUAL GRANT OF THE WORLD TEACHERS’ DAY INCENTIVE BENEFIT FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS AND INCREASING THE AMOUNT OF THE INCENTIVE TO THREE THOUSAND PESOS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Teachers play a vital role in shaping the minds of the youth and in promoting national development through quality education. Their dedication, commitment, and sacrifices deserve meaningful recognition and continued support from the State. In recognition of the invaluable contribution of teachers, Congress enacted Republic Act No. 10743, declaring October 5 of every year as National Teachers’ Day, in line with the observance of World Teachers’ Day established by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Since 2019, public school teachers have been granted a World Teachers’ Day Incentive Benefit (WTDIB) through the annual General Appropriations Act in the amount of One Thousand Pesos (₱1,000). However, the grant remains dependent on yearly appropriations and has not been adjusted despite increasing economic challenges and the rising cost of living. This bill seeks to institutionalize the annual grant of the World Teachers’ Day Incentive Benefit and increase the amount to Three Thousand Pesos (₱3,000) for every public school teacher. The measure aims to ensure the continuous and consistent release of the incentive while providing greater recognition and support to teachers for their indispensable service to the nation. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9267
title: AN ACT CREATING THE THIRD COMMISSION ON EDUCATION (EDCOM III) AS AN INTER-AGENCY AND LEGISLATIVE EDUCATION POLICY ADVISORY COMMISSION, PROVIDING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XIV, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution mandates the State to protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and to take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all. Education remains a vital pillar of national development, human capital formation, economic competitiveness, and social equity. Despite significant reforms and investments in the education sector, the Philippines continues to face persistent and interconnected challenges, including learning poverty, high dropout and attrition rates, inadequate school infrastructure, shortage of qualified teachers, digital inequality, skills mismatch, and the evolving demands of emerging industries and technologies. Recent global assessments and national studies likewise underscore the urgent need for a more cohesive, future-oriented, and evidence-based education reform agenda. The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II) has played a crucial role in assessing the state of Philippine education and recommending reforms across the basic, higher, and technical-vocational education sectors. However, the rapidly evolving educational landscape, driven by digital transformation, artificial intelligence, labor market shifts, and increasing global competitiveness, necessitates the institutionalization of a stronger and continuing mechanism for policy coordination, monitoring, evaluation, and long-term strategic planning. This measure seeks to create the Third Commission on Education (EDCOM III) as a congressional-executive consultative and advisory commission tasked to review, assess, monitor, and recommend policies, programs, and institutional reforms necessary to improve the quality, accessibility, relevance, and responsiveness of the Philippine education system. It likewise seeks to strengthen coordination among the Department of Education (DepEd), the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), and other key government agencies involved in innovation, labor development, budgeting, statistics, and national development planning. The proposed measure further recognizes the importance of multi-sectoral participation by engaging experts from the academe, business sector, civil society organizations, parents’ associations, local government units, and development partners in shaping a comprehensive, inclusive, and future-responsive national education agenda. Through EDCOM III, Congress seeks to ensure sustained policy continuity, stronger inter-agency collaboration, data driven and evidence-based education governance, and a responsive education framework capable of preparing Filipino learners for the demands of the future while addressing longstanding structural gaps in the education system. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9268
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A TREE PARK IN EVERY MUNICIPALITY IN THE PHILIPPINES AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 16, Article II of the 1987 Constitution declares that the State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature. In the face of rapid urbanization, climate change, deforestation, and environmental degradation, there is a growing need to expand and preserve green spaces within local communities. Trees and urban green spaces play a vital role in improving air quality, reducing heat, mitigating flooding, conserving biodiversity, and promoting the physical and mental well-being of the public. However, many municipalities across the country continue to experience limited access to sustainable and protected public green areas. This bill seeks to establish at least one (1) Tree Park in every municipality in the Philippines to serve as a living repository of native flora, a center for environmental awareness and education, and a public space for recreation and ecological conservation. The proposed measure likewise aims to strengthen local climate resilience and support national reforestation and environmental sustainability efforts through active participation of local government units and communities. By institutionalizing municipal tree parks nationwide, this measure promotes environmental stewardship, biodiversity protection, and sustainable local development for the benefit of present and future generations. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L.
