explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State recognizes that road networks that connect provincial boundaries to key urban corridors are essential to regional integration, mobility, and economic activity. Such roads facilitate the continuous movement of goods and people across jurisdictions and strengthen linkages between neighboring provinces and cities. The Misamis Oriental–Maria Cristina Boundary Road to Iligan City Diversion Road serves as a vital connector between the boundary of Misamis Oriental and the urban road network of Iligan City. Extending from the vicinity of El Centro along Quezon Avenue in Barangay Poblacion to Pala-o Bridge, the road provides a direct linkage to a major diversion route, supporting both local traffic and inter-provincial movement. The road has been previously validated for conversion into a national road, recognizing its functional importance within the transport network. However, it remains under local jurisdiction, limiting its integration into the broader national system and constraining sustained development and maintenance. Given its role in linking provincial and city road networks and supporting traffic flow toward a major diversion corridor, the conversion of this road into a national road is necessary. This will enable the Department of Public Works and Highways to ensure its continued improvement, maintenance, and compliance with national standards. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. This will ensure that the road meets national standards and continues to support the efficient movement of goods, services, and people, particularly in relation to port operations. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 9367
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PHILIPPINE STRATEGIC PETROLEUM RESERVE SYSTEM TO ENSURE ENERGY SECURITY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Despite its heavy reliance on imported petroleum products, the Philippines lacks a comprehensive legal framework establishing a government-owned and controlled strategic petroleum reserve. In contrast, many countries maintain strategic petroleum reserves as a core component of their energy security policies. Based on reports, Japan holds one of the largest petroleum reserves in Asia, with supplies estimated to last over 200 days.1 South Korea and China have likewise substantial reserves, reflecting strong commitment to energy security planning among major Asian economies. A research published in Energy Policy notes that a strategic petroleum reserve is a practical tool for stabilizing supply and demand, moderating price fluctuations, handling emergencies, and safeguarding the national economy.2 In the recent disruptions affecting the Strait of Hormuz, nations with established strategic petroleum reserves were able to release oil stocks to stabilize domestic supply and cushion economic impact. In comparison, the Philippines had no comparable reserve to draw from and remained largely exposed to market volatility, relying instead on existing commercial inventories and external supply conditions. This vulnerability contributed to cumulative oil price hikes exceeding 100 percent, which could push an additional 1.34 million Filipinos to poverty, according to the policy brief of the Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS).3 This highlights the urgent need for the Philippines to establish its own strategic petroleum reserve as a safeguard against future supply shocks and economic disruption. The proposed measure seeks to establish a Philippine Strategic Petroleum Reserve to function as a vital buffer against severe oil supply disruptions. It provides for the creation of a government-managed reserve composed of crude oil and refined petroleum products, the development of storage facilities, management and maintenance of the reserves, clear guidelines for the release of reserves, and implementation timelines based on technical, financial, infrastructure, and logistical considerations. (SOCOTECO I) TO CONSTRUCT, INSTALL, ESTABLISH, OPERATE, OWN, MANAGE AND MAINTAIN DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM FOR THE CONVEYANCE OF ELECTRIC POWER TO END-USERS IN THE CITY OF KORONADAL AND IN THE MUNICIPALITIES OF TAMPAKAN, TANTANGAN, BANGA, SURALLAH AND NORALA IN THE PROVINCE OF SOUTH COTABATO
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates that the goals of the national economy must be "a more equitable distribution of opportunities, income, and wealth," ensuring that "all regions of the country shall be given optimum opportunity to develop". In the pursuit of these constitutional objectives, access to reliable and affordable electricity serves as a fundamental enabling component for socio-economic growth. For over five decades, the South Cotabato I Electric Cooperative, Inc. (SOCOTECO-I) has functioned as a critical partner of the national government in achieving these goals within its service area. This bill seeks to grant SOCOTECO-I a formal legislative franchise, ensuring the continued delivery of electric power to the City of Koronadal and five neighboring municipalities. This measure aligns with the modern legislative framework for power distribution utilities, mirroring the standards of accountability and transparency found in Republic Act No. 12306 (2025) and other contemporary franchises. By formalizing this franchise, Congress ensures that SOCOTECO-I remains subject to the rigorous regulatory oversight of the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) and the National Electrification Administration (NEA), thereby protecting the public interest. The importance of this franchise extension to the progress and prosperity of Filipino families cannot be overstated. As a member-owned cooperative, SOCOTECO-I operates on a non-profit basis, prioritizing service reliability and local development over investor profit. The cooperative has achieved 100% electrification of all 172 barangays in its area, directly bridging the rural-urban divide for approximately 139,676 billed consumers. This access translates into tangible benefits for stakeholders: Page | 1 • For Families: Reliable lighting for education, safe food storage, and easier access to information and health services. • For Marginalized Users: The bill explicitly mandates the implementation of a “lifeline rate,” providing subsidized power to low-income households as required by Republic Act No. 9136. • For Local Businesses: Stable power supports agricultural processing, small-scale entrepreneurship, and the growth of industries, enabling them to compete effectively. • For Regional Governance: As the City of Koronadal serves as the seat of government for Region XII, SOCOTECO-I provides the essential energy infrastructure for regional administrative operations. Strategically, SOCOTECO-I has demonstrated its commitment to regional energy security by maintaining a "Mega Large" classification and proactively modernizing its infrastructure, such as the energization of the 30 MVA substation in San Isidro. These investments are critical for managing the average annual energy demand growth of 6.36% recorded over the last decade. Consistent with the State policy to promote self-reliance and social justice through cooperatives, this measure secures a vital utility service for South Cotabato. In view of its essential role in fueling regional progress and ensuring that no community is left in the dark, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND L. label: HB 9376
title: AN ACT GRANTING THE LEYTE V ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE INC. (LEYECO V) A FRANCHISE TO CONSTRUCT, INSTALL, ESTABLISH, OPERATE, OWN, MANAGE AND MAINTAIN DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS FOR THE CONVEYANCE OF ELECTRIC POWER TO THE END-USERS IN THE CITY OF ORMOC AND MUNICIPALITIES OF ALBUERA, KANANGA, MATAG-OB, VILLABA, PALOMPON, TABANGO, SAN ISIDRO, CALUBIAN, LEYTE, MERIDA, AND ISABEL, PROVINCE OF LEYTE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Reliable electricity service is a basic requirement for local development, public service delivery, livelihood, education, health, disaster response, and the daily comfort and security of Filipino households. In the Province of Leyte, the Leyte V Electric Cooperative, Inc. (LEYECO V) has been performing this essential public service for decades, supplying electricity to communities, institutions, and industries within its coverage area. This measure seeks to grant LEYECO V a legislative franchise to construct, install, establish, operate, own, manage, and maintain distribution systems for the conveyance of electric power to end-users in the City of Ormoc and in the municipalities of Albuera, Kananga, Matag-Ob, Villaba, Palompon, Tabango, San Isidro, Calubian, Leyte, Merida, and Isabel, all in the Province of Leyte. LEYECO V traces its institutional foundation to its incorporation with the National Electrification Administration on December 21, 1977. On August 1, 1979, it assumed the operations of the former Ormoc Electric and Lights Company, then serving fewer than 3,000 consumers concentrated mainly in Ormoc City. Since then, the cooperative has expanded its reach and capability, now serving the electricity requirements of one city and eleven municipalities in the 3rd and 4th Districts of Leyte. At present, LEYECO V has energized three hundred ninety-one (391) barangays and provides electric service to households, schools, public facilities, commercial establishments, industries, and other registered member-consumers within its franchise area. To meet the increasing needs of its member-consumer-owners, LEYECO V maintains multiple substations with significant installed capacity and sources its power from several suppliers and the electricity market. It has also undertaken system improvement initiatives, including the uprating of substations and the deployment of technologies intended to strengthen reliability, system monitoring, and operational efficiency. LEYECO V has likewise moved toward a more modern and consumer- responsive distribution utility. Its operations now include online and electronic payment options, SMS advisories, digital complaint mechanisms, automated systems, Android-based meter reading with GPS, website and social media information platforms, radio-based public updates, and other innovations intended to make service more accessible to its member- consumer-owners. The cooperative’s modernization efforts are also aligned with the need to build a more resilient and efficient electric distribution system. Through its smart distribution utility initiatives, including SCADA deployment, GIS-based asset management, advanced metering initiatives, and fiber optics planning, LEYECO V is preparing its network to respond to the changing demands of consumers, technology, and the electric power industry. The grant of a franchise to LEYECO V will ensure the continuity of electric distribution service in its coverage area and will provide the legal basis for the cooperative to continue improving its facilities, expanding its services, and protecting the welfare of its member-consumer-owners. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SERGIO C. DAGOOC PRESLEY C. label: HB 9378
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE GOVTECH PHILIPPINES CORPORATION AS A GOVERNMENT-OWNED OR CONTROLLED CORPORATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AS THE CENTRAL DIGITAL ENGINEERING, PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, AND SERVICE DELIVERY AUTHORITY OF THE GOVERNMENT, ENHANCING THE PHILIPPINE E-GOVERNANCE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The government has a fundamental responsibility to deliver efficient, accessible, secure, and citizen-centric public services. In our increasingly digital society, it is essential for the government to design, build, operate, and continuously improve digital products, applications, and platforms that meet citizens' needs and improve the delivery of government services. Digital transformation is no longer a peripheral function of governance but a core mechanism for delivering public service, ensuring transparency, enhancing economic competitiveness, and strengthening public trust. In an increasingly data-driven and technology- enabled world, governments must adapt institutional structures that are agile, innovative, and capable of responding to rapidly evolving technological demands. Global experience shows that effective digital governments rely on empowered, agile institutions. The Government Technology Agency of Singapore exemplifies this with its flexible structure, technical independence, and product-focused strategy for managing government digital platforms. Digital initiatives across government agencies are currently fragmented, inconsistent, and redundant. Each agency develops and procures its own systems independently, leading to duplication of efforts, inconsistent standards, cybersecurity risks, vendor dependence, and ineffective use of public funds. Observations indicate that there is no single entity designated as the central authority for digital engineering and product development within the government. The government cannot rely on private companies indefinitely for the development, maintenance, operation, and evolution of essential platforms and infrastructure. Government digital systems carry out sovereign functions, process sensitive personal and state data, and support the ongoing delivery of critical public services. Relying on private vendors for these core functions exposes the government to several risks, including vendor lock-in, rising long- term costs, loss of institutional knowledge, continuity failures, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and reduced accountability. Without an internal, permanent digital engineering and product development capability, the government struggles to effectively manage, secure, and enhance its own digital assets. The Philippines is currently falling behind its regional and global peers in digital government performance. According to the United Nations E-Government Development Index (EGDI), the Philippines ranks 73rd globally, significantly trailing behind leading countries such as Estonia (2nd), Singapore (3rd), and South Korea (4th). This disparity highlights a structural weakness in the country’s digital governance framework, particularly in the execution and integration of digital government services. International experience shows that successful digital states maintain a clear separation between ICT policy and regulation, on one hand, and the delivery of digital government services, on the other. Although the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) effectively manages ICT infrastructure, cybersecurity standards, and sector regulation under Republic Act No. 10844, the rapidly evolving digital landscape poses challenges. The DICT was not specifically designed to serve as a comprehensive digital service delivery agency for the entire government and as a sectoral department for ICT policy and planning, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and industry regulation and not as a tool for restructuring public administration. E-government is not primarily a technology or infrastructure issue but rather a governance and administrative reform challenge that requires redesigning processes, integrating agencies, harmonizing legal mandates, and improving service delivery across the entire bureaucracy. These functions fall outside the DICT’s core statutory design. Moreover, DICT operates as a line department with a vertical structure, while effective e-government requires horizontal, whole-of-government authority. DICT cannot compel peer departments, constitutional bodies, or local government units to reengineer workflows or integrate systems without risking institutional overreach. While the recent passage of the E-Governance Act established a national framework for electronic governance and designated the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) as the lead policy agency, this law did not create a permanent institution responsible for the actual creation, development, operation, and maintenance of government digital products, platforms, and shared infrastructure. Under the current framework, the Department of Information and Communication Technology is tasked simultaneously with policy formulation, regulation, and, through the E- Government Unified Project Management (Egov-UPMO), the implementation of digital systems. The E-Government Unified Project Management Office (Egov-UPMO), established under the E-Governance Act, remains project-based and transitional, leading to fragmented portals, duplicated systems, and weak platform ownership. Its role is best understood as a coordination and transition mechanism and not as a permanent digital government institution. Hence the need to abolish and elevate it to a Government-owned or Controlled Corporation to ensure strategic independence, enhance specialization and fiscal stability. A critical feature of this proposed bill is the institutional separation of policy-making and regulatory functions from operation and technical execution. The digital governance model of Singapore clearly delineates these functions: the Ministry of Communications and its successor policy structures is responsible for policy direction and regulatory oversight, while the Government Technology Agency of Singapore serves as the dedicated implementation and engineering arm, focused exclusively on building, operating, and continuously improving government digital platforms.

label: HB 9379
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes the vital role of education in national development and explicitly guarantees the academic freedom of institutions of higher learning. Over the years, however, the regulatory environment governing higher education has become increasingly complex, resulting in tensions between academic freedom and the State’s supervisory powers, as well as inconsistencies in the treatment of public and private higher education institutions (HEIs). This proposed measure, entitled the “Strengthened Higher Education Institutions Act,” seeks to clarify, strengthen, and harmonize the legal framework governing higher education in the Philippines. It affirms institutional academic freedom as a foundational principle while clearly defining the scope and limits of reasonable State supervision and regulation, primarily through the Commission on Higher Education (CHED). The bill reiterates the four essential freedoms of higher education institutions—namely, the freedom to determine who may teach, what may be taught, how it shall be taught, and who may be admitted to study—while recognizing the authority of the State to impose minimum standards to protect public welfare and ensure quality education. In doing so, it provides HEIs with wider discretion over admissions, curricula, faculty appointments, and financial allocations, consistent with their academic mission and institutional autonomy. This measure also strengthens the mandate of the CHED by vesting it with ample authority to set mandatory minimum institutional and course requirements, oversee external governance of HEIs, and regulate the establishment, conversion, recognition, and closure of academic programs. At the same time, it respects the internal governance structures of HEIs by leaving internal management decisions to their respective governing boards and administrative officials. To promote a balanced and integrated higher education system, the bill adopts the principle of competitive neutrality in the recognition of programs offered by public HEIs, particularly state universities and colleges (SUCs) and local universities and colleges (LUCs). It recognizes the complementary roles of public and private institutions and seeks to prevent unnecessary duplication, inefficiency, and monopolization of academic offerings, while ensuring that programs essential to national, regional, and local development are supported. The measure further advances quality assurance through outcomes-based education, industry and stakeholder participation in curriculum development, and incentives for HEIs that consistently demonstrate standards of excellence through voluntary accreditation. It institutionalizes incentives such as Centers of Excellence, Centers of Development, and autonomous and deregulated status, thereby encouraging innovation, research, and global competitiveness. 2 In recognition of the increasing globalization of higher education, the bill promotes the internationalization of academic programs by removing unnecessary administrative barriers to foreign student admission and aligning Philippine higher education standards with international norms, consistent with existing laws on transnational education. Additionally, the bill provides tax exemptions for government subsidies granted to private HEIs, ensuring that public funds intended to support education are fully utilized for academic and institutional development. It also includes transitory provisions to allow existing institutions, particularly local colleges and universities, sufficient time to comply with updated regulatory requirements. Ultimately, this measure seeks to strengthen the Philippine higher education system by striking a principled balance between academic freedom and responsible State regulation, fostering quality, accessibility, competitiveness, and sustainability in higher education. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9383
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE BASE EXEMPTION FOR PERSONAL INCOME TAX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 24 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, AND INSTITUTING AUTOMATIC INDEXATION BASED ON THE CONSUMER PRICE INDEX
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates the State to evolve a progressive system of taxation. In 2018, Republic Act No. 10963, or the Tax Reform for Acceleration and Inclusion (TRAIN) Law, took a monumental step towards this goal by restructuring the personal income tax brackets and establishing a PHP 250,000 annual tax exemption threshold. This effectively shielded minimum wage earners and the lower-middle class from the burden of income taxation. However, since the passage of the TRAIN Law, the Philippine economy has experienced compounding inflation, significantly eroding the purchasing power of the peso. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) has consistently risen, meaning that the PHP 250,000 threshold established eight years ago no longer holds the same real- world value today. We are once again facing the threat of "bracket creep"—a phenomenon where workers receive nominal wage increases simply to keep up with the cost of living, only to be pushed into higher tax brackets without any real increase in their wealth or purchasing power. This bill seeks to immediately correct this injustice by increasing the base personal income tax exemption from PHP 250,000 to PHP 350,000, mathematically adjusting for the cumulative inflation from 2018 to 2026. This adjustment will instantly restore the intended financial relief for Filipino workers, giving them greater take-home pay to afford basic necessities. Furthermore, to prevent the recurrence of "bracket creep" and to avoid the need for Congress to pass continuous remedial tax legislation, this bill institutionalizes an automatic indexation mechanism. By mandating the Department of Finance to adjust the income tax brackets every three (3) years based on the prevailing Consumer Price Index, we ensure that our tax system remains permanently fair, equitable, and economically sound. In view of the foregoing, immediate passage of the bills is earnestly sought for. ANTONINO B. UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8134, ENTITLED "AN ACT GRANTING THE PRIMAX BROADCASTING NETWORK, INC., A FRANCHISE TO CONSTRUCT, INSTALL, OPERATE AND MAINTAIN RADIO AND TELEVISION BROADCASTING STATIONS IN THE PHILIPPINES"
front_matter: May 25, 2026 8:00 am Republic of the Philippines House of Representatives Quezon City TWENTIETH CONGRESS First Regular Session House Bill No. 9385 Introduced by HON. MONIQUE YAZMIN MARIA Q. LAGDAMEO Explanatory Note This legislative measure seeks to renew the legislative franchise of the PRIMAX BROADCASTING NETWORK, INC. to construct, install, establish, operate and maintain radio and television broadcasting stations throughout the Philippines. The Primax Broadcasting Network, Inc. (Primax, for brevity) was incorporated and registered at the Securities and Exchange Commission with a primary purpose of establishing radio and television broadcasting stations in the Philippines for a commercial purpose and in the public interest and to the extent that it may be authorized by law. It is guided by the tenet that broadcasting is a public trust and the network is mindful of its duty to share in the task of nation-building. With its twenty-five years of existence, it strives to serve more audiences in more areas possible. The Primax will be embarking to set the pace by establishing stations in areas that are underserved, if not served at all, by free-to-air broadcasting. Hence, there is an urgent need to seek a legislative authorization for its continued operations. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9386
title: AN ACT RECONSTITUTING THE PHILIPPINE RACING COMMISSION INTO THE PHILIPPINE RACING CORPORATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine Racing Commission was created under Presidential Decree No. 420 in 1974 to supervise and regulate horse racing in the Philippines. After several decades, however, the legal framework governing the racing industry needs to be updated to respond to present regulatory, developmental, fiscal, and social protection concerns. This bill seeks to reconstitute the Philippine Racing Commission into the Philippine Racing Corporation, a government-owned or controlled corporation with original charter. The proposed reconstitution will allow the agency to exercise its regulatory mandate with greater institutional capacity, corporate flexibility, and financial accountability. As a GOCC, the Corporation will be better equipped to manage revenues, administer industry development programs, support the growth and modernization of the racing industry, and professionalize its governance subject to the oversight mechanisms applicable to GOCCs. A stronger and more competitive racing industry may also expand economic activity, generate employment, and increase potential government revenues from racing-related operations. The bill strengthens the Corporation as the primary regulatory and developmental authority for horse racing and other authorized animal racing in the Philippines. It rationalizes its powers and functions, expands its jurisdiction to other forms of animal racing, and provides a clearer framework for licensing, regulation, enforcement, and revenue monitoring. The measure also enhances the welfare of jockeys and horse trainers by institutionalizing and strengthening the Jockeys and Horse Trainers Injury, Disability and Death Compensation Fund. This recognizes the occupational risks faced by racing personnel and provides a mechanism for injury, disability, death, medical, and other welfare benefits. The bill likewise places the National Stud Farm under the supervision and control of the Philippine Racing Corporation to better align horse breeding, genetic improvement, racehorse development, and animal health programs with the broader modernization of the racing industry. Finally, the bill provides for the transfer of assets, personnel, records, pending matters, licenses, permits, and issuances from the existing Commission to the new Corporation to ensure continuity of operations. It repeals Presidential Decree No. 420, as amended, and amends or repeals Republic Act No. 6115 insofar as inconsistent with the proposed Act. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PRESLEY C. label: HB 9389
title: AN ACT STANDARDIZING THE DOCUMENTARY STAMP TAX ON HORSE RACING TICKETS, AMENDING SECTION 190 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, SECTION 6 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7978, AND SECTION 10(a)(1) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11649, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine horse racing industry has long formed part of the country’s regulated gaming and sports sector. Beyond its entertainment value, the industry supports employment, breeding, training, jockeying, racing operations, and allied economic activities. It also contributes to government revenues through taxes, fees, and regulatory charges imposed on racing operations and betting transactions. At present, documentary stamp tax is imposed on horse race tickets under existing tax laws and the legislative franchises governing racing clubs. However, the current rate places an additional cost on every ticket transaction, which may affect bettor participation, reduce betting volume, and limit the capacity of the industry to remain competitive. A more balanced tax structure is therefore necessary to encourage wider participation in horse racing while preserving the government’s revenue interests. This bill seeks to amend Section 190 of Republic Act No. 8424, otherwise known as the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended; Section 6 of Republic Act No. 7978; and Section 10(a)(1) of Republic Act No. 11649, by lowering the documentary stamp tax imposed on horse racing tickets to Five centavos (P0.05) for every One peso (P1.00), or fractional part thereof, of the cost of each ticket. The proposed measure also standardizes the applicable documentary stamp tax rate on horse racing tickets across the relevant laws governing the industry. By harmonizing the tax treatment of horse race tickets, the bill promotes clarity, consistency, and ease of implementation for regulators, operators, and stakeholders. While the proposed rate is lower, the measure is intended to stimulate greater transaction volume, encourage increased bettor participation, and support the continued viability of the horse racing industry. A more competitive payout structure may attract renewed public interest in horse racing and encourage reinvestment in the sector, including in horse breeding, training, race operations, and the organization of additional events. At the same time, the bill recognizes the need to protect government revenues. By encouraging higher participation and increasing the volume of taxable transactions, the proposed adjustment seeks to maintain, and potentially improve, revenue collection while giving the industry a more sustainable fiscal environment. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PRESLEY C. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Barangay officials, barangay tanods, and members of the Lupong Tagapamayapa serve as the frontline providers of government services and play a crucial role in maintaining peace and order, implementing community programs, and responding to the immediate needs of the people at the grassroots level. Despite their vital contribution to local governance and nation-building, many continue to receive inadequate compensation, limited benefits, and insufficient social protection. This measure seeks to recognize their dedication, sacrifices, and years of public service by enhancing their benefits and providing additional forms of assistance and protection. The bill likewise grants retirement gratuity pay and other non-monetary benefits aimed at promoting their welfare, morale, and economic security. Recognizing the fiscal implications of the proposed measure, the bill mandates coordination among the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), the Department of Finance (DOF), and other concerned agencies to ensure fiscal sustainability and effective implementation. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9393
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A NATIONAL COMPREHENSIVE PROGRAM ON AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition that affects communication, social interaction, behavior, sensory processing, and adaptive functioning, with varying levels of support needs. Across the country, many persons with ASD and their families continue to face challenges in accessing early diagnosis, intervention services, inclusive education, healthcare, employment opportunities, and social support systems. These difficulties are further aggravated by the lack of comprehensive and coordinated government programs specifically designed to address their unique needs. While existing laws such as Magna Carta for Disabled Persons and Inclusive Education Act recognize the rights of persons with disabilities and learners with disabilities, there remains a need for a more focused, integrated, and nationwide approach that specifically addresses ASD across all stages of life. This proposed measure seeks to establish a National Comprehensive Program on Autism Spectrum Disorder through a whole-of-government and multi-sectoral framework that promotes early identification and intervention, public awareness, inclusive education, healthcare access, skills development, employment opportunities, community participation, and protection against discrimination. This bill proposes the creation of an Inter-Agency ASD Coordinating Committee (IACC) tasked with formulating and implementing policies and programs relating to ASD. It likewise mandates epidemiological surveillance and research initiatives to generate reliable data necessary for evidence-based policymaking and service delivery. Recognizing the importance of accessibility and inclusion, the measure also strengthens support mechanisms for families and caregivers, promotes reasonable accommodation in schools and workplaces, expands training for government personnel and service providers, and encourages the development of community-based and telehealth intervention systems, particularly in underserved areas. Further, this bill seeks to uphold the dignity, rights, and full participation of persons with ASD in accordance with the principles embodied in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and other relevant laws and policies. By institutionalizing a comprehensive national program for persons with ASD, this measure aims to foster a more inclusive, accessible, compassionate, and responsive society where persons with ASD are empowered to reach their fullest potential and meaningfully contribute to nation-building. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9394
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT AND WELL-BEING OF CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL NEEDS, PROVIDING FOR COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT SYSTEMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State recognizes the vital role of children in nation-building and affirms its duty to protect and promote the rights and welfare of every child, especially those who require specialized care, intervention, and support. Children with special needs (CSN) often face barriers in accessing quality healthcare, therapy, education, and social services, while their families bear significant financial, emotional, and social burdens. Despite existing laws protecting persons with disabilities and promoting inclusive education, many Filipino children with special needs continue to experience inadequate access to early intervention programs, therapeutic services, assistive devices, and inclusive learning opportunities, particularly in underserved communities. Families likewise encounter high costs of treatment and limited institutional support. This measure seeks to establish a comprehensive and inclusive framework that will ensure accessible therapy and education, strengthen support systems for families and caregivers, expand financial assistance and health coverage, promote public awareness and acceptance, and reinforce inter-agency coordination for the welfare of children with special needs. The bill likewise strengthens the participation of Local Government Units (LGUs) in implementing community-based intervention programs and establishes a national registry and data collection system, subject to the provisions of the Data Privacy Act of 2012, to support evidence-based policymaking and effective service delivery. Furthermore, this proposed measure is aligned with the principles and policies embodied in existing laws such as the Magna Carta for Disabled Persons, the Inclusive Education Act, and the Universal Health Care Act, ensuring a harmonized and rights-based approach to inclusive development. Through this proposed legislation, the State endeavors to uphold the dignity, inclusion, and full development of children with special needs and empower their families toward a more compassionate, equitable, and inclusive society. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9395
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND DIGITAL LITERACY TO COMBAT DISINFORMATION, MISINFORMATION, MALINFORMATION, AND COORDINATED INAUTHENTIC BEHAVIOR ONLINE, RECOGNIZING AN INDEPENDENT MULTI-SECTORAL ETHICAL BODY, WITHOUT INFRINGING ON FREEDOM OF SPEECH AND THE PRESS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The rapid expansion of digital platforms and social media has transformed the way people communicate, access information, and participate in public discourse. While these technologies have strengthened democratic engagement and expanded access to information, they have also enabled the widespread dissemination of disinformation, misinformation, malinformation, and coordinated inauthentic behavior that undermine public trust, distort democratic processes, threaten public safety, and erode institutional credibility. In recent years, online disinformation campaigns, troll farms, fake accounts, bot networks, and deceptive digital practices have increasingly been used to manipulate public opinion, spread fraudulent content, interfere in civic discourse, and exploit the vulnerabilities of digital communication systems. The absence of sufficient transparency and accountability mechanisms among digital platforms has further aggravated these harms. At the same time, any effort to address harmful online conduct must remain firmly consistent with the constitutional guarantees of freedom of speech, freedom of the press, and the free flow of information. Regulation must therefore focus not on suppressing legitimate expression, criticism, dissent, journalism, or political advocacy, but on promoting transparency, accountability, ethical standards, and informed digital participation. This proposed measure seeks to establish a balanced and rights-based framework for digital platform accountability by requiring transparency in online advertising, coordinated inauthentic behavior takedowns, recommender systems, and platform moderation practices. It also provides safeguards for users through notice-and-action mechanisms, statements of reasons for moderation decisions, and accessible dispute resolution systems. This bill further recognizes the role of a multi-sectoral and independent Digital Media Standards Coalition (DMSC) that shall promote ethical standards, support fact-checking initiatives, and encourage responsible digital conduct without exercising censorship powers or infringing upon editorial independence. In addition, this measure promotes media and digital literacy through educational institutions and strengthens government transparency through open and verifiable public information systems. Ultimately, this bill seeks to protect democratic discourse and strengthen public trust in digital communications while upholding the fundamental freedoms guaranteed under the Constitution. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9396
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SATELLITE CAMPUS OF THE VISAYAS STATE UNIVERSITY IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF JAVIER, PROVINCE OF LEYTE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 1, Article XIV of the 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates that “The State shall protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and shall take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all.” In accordance with this constitutional mandate, this bill seeks to establish a Visayas State University satellite campus in the Municipality of Javier, Province of Leyte. Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), a British company specializing in evaluating higher education institutions worldwide, assigned Visayas State University (VSU) a 3-star rating. VSU was awarded the QS certification on May 8, 2020. A 3-star rating indicates that VSU is "nationally well-known and may have even begun to attract international recognition." This institution conducts credible research, and its graduates are attractive to potential employers. The Javier Satellite Campus is intended to serve students who are unable to travel far for college due to family obligations, financial constraints, or other factors, and to provide quality education in response to global needs. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARL NICOLAS C. label: HB 9398
title: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRODUCTION, IMPORTATION, SALE, DISTRIBUTION, PROVISION, USE, RECOVERY, COLLECTION, RECYCLING, AND DISPOSAL OF SINGLE-USE PLASTIC PRODUCTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to face an escalating environmental crisis brought about by the unchecked production, distribution, and disposal of single-use plastics. Plastic waste pollutes our rivers, coastlines, oceans, and communities, threatens marine biodiversity, clogs drainage systems that worsen flooding, and endangers public health and food security. Despite growing awareness and local initiatives, the volume of plastic waste generated daily remains alarming. Single-use plastics, by their very nature, are designed for convenience but impose long-term environmental costs that burden present and future generations. Sachets, plastic bags, straws, disposable utensils, and other non-recyclable plastic products persist in the environment for decades, fragmenting into microplastics that contaminate water systems, fisheries, and even the human food chain. At this critical juncture, the nation must remain steadfast in its commitment to environmental preservation and sustainable development. Protecting the environment is no longer merely an advocacy, it is an obligation rooted in our duty to safeguard the welfare, health, and future of the Filipino people. This proposed measure seeks to regulate the production, importation, sale, distribution, provision, use, recovery, collection, recycling, and disposal of single-use plastic products by adopting a comprehensive and science-based approach toward waste reduction and circular economy practices. It encourages the transition toward reusable, recyclable, and environmentally sustainable alternatives while promoting producer responsibility, consumer awareness, and institutional accountability. The measure likewise strengthens the role of government agencies, local government units, private enterprises, and communities in addressing plastic pollution through coordinated recovery systems, recycling programs, public education campaigns, and incentives for innovation and sustainable packaging alternatives. By reducing dependence on disposable plastics, this bill aims to preserve ecological balance, protect marine and terrestrial ecosystems, prolong the lifespan of sanitary landfills, reduce flooding caused by clogged waterways, and cultivate a culture of environmental responsibility among Filipinos. Environmental protection requires consistency, courage, and collective action. We must remain resolute in advancing policies that prioritize sustainability over convenience and long-term national welfare over short-term consumption habits. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 9400
title: AN ACT PROVIDING PRIORITY EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR BARANGAY OFFICIALS WHO HAVE COMPLETED THEIR TERMS OF OFFICE IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, SUBJECT TO CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: SECTION 1. Short Title. - This Act shall be known as the "Barangay Officials’ Career Transition Act." SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy - It is the policy of the State to recognize the roles of barangay officials as frontliners of government service and to provide them with opportunities for career advancement and economic stability after their tenure, consistent with the principle of merit and fitness in the civil service.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Barangay is the primary planning and implementing unit of government policies, programs, projects, and activities in the community. As the grassroots level of our democratic institution, Barangay Officials—including the Punong Barangay, Sangguniang Barangay members, the Sangguniang Kabataan Chairperson, the Barangay Secretary, and the Barangay Treasurer—serve as the frontliners of public service. These individuals are often on call 24/7, mediating disputes, maintaining peace and order, and implementing national health and social programs. However, upon completion of their terms of office, many of these dedicated public servants find themselves without stable employment or a clear career path, despite years of invaluable experience in public administration, community leadership, and crisis management. This bill seeks to recognize the service of former Barangay Officials by providing them with preferential consideration for employment in Local Government Units (LGUs) and National Government Agencies (NGAs). To maintain the integrity of the bureaucracy and ensure the quality of public service, this preference is strictly subject to the requirements of the Civil Service Commission (CSC) and the specific qualifications of the positions. By facilitating their entry into the professional civil service, the state not only rewards faithful community service but also retains experienced individuals within the government workforce who have a proven track record of dealing with the needs of the Filipino people. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 9401
title: AN ACT PROVIDING COMPREHENSIVE GOVERNMENT SUPPORT AND BENEFITS FOR CHILDREN WITH CRITICAL ILLNESSES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: SECTION 1. Short Title. - This Act shall be known as the "Pediatric Critical Illness Support Act." SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy - The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people, particularly children who are the most vulnerable. It is hereby declared the policy of the State to provide comprehensive medical, financial, and psychosocial support to children diagnosed with life-threatening or critical illnesses.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE A diagnosis of a critical illness in a child—be it cancer, rare genetic disorders, or end-stage organ failure—is a devastating blow that ripples through an entire family. In the Philippines, the "catastrophic" cost of medical care often pushes families into deep poverty. While programs like PhilHealth and the Malasakit Centers provide a safety net, they are often insufficient to cover the specialized, long-term, and multi- disciplinary care these children require. Beyond the hospital bill, families face "hidden" costs: the loss of income as parents become full-time caregivers, the travel expenses from rural provinces to specialized centers in Manila, and the psychological toll on the child and their siblings. This bill, the "Pediatric Critical Illness Support Act," seeks to bridge these gaps. It provides for a dedicated National Pediatric Fund, mandates the establishment of regional specialized care wings, grants "Caregiver Leave" for parents, and ensures that a child’s education is not abandoned during treatment. No parent should be forced to choose between their child’s survival and their family’s financial existence. It is the duty of the State to ensure that every child, regardless of their economic background, has a fighting chance. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 9406
title: AN ACT IMPOSING WINDFALL PROFITS TAX ON PETROLEUM COMPANIES AND AGGREGATE RETAILERS DURING NATIONAL ENERGY EMERGENCY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In times of crisis, there is no greater injustice than the enrichment of the few at the expense of the suffering public. Those who control the capital often take the situation as an opportunity to increase profit. Instead of sharing the burden, they pass it on to the consumers while raking in more gains. A windfall profits tax is a temporary or time-bound levy imposed upon a petroleum company or an aggregate retailer during a declared national energy emergency. Unlike the Value-Added Tax, which is directly passed on to consumers as a consumption tax, this tax is imposed on the excess net profit of entities engaged in refining, importation, distribution, or sale of petroleum products. This may be akin to an excise tax, which the manufacturer, importer or seller must technically bear. However, in reality, an excise tax is embedded in product prices, thereby passing it on to the consumers. This measure establishes a price manipulation detection mechanism to frustrate such a scheme. This measure imposes a 50% windfall profits tax on the excess net profits of petroleum companies and aggregate retailers engaged in refining, importation, distribution, or sale of petroleum products. Excess net profit, or windfall profit, shall be determined by taking the sum of the baseline profit and a 20% margin, and subtracting it from the current net profit. The average monthly net profit over the past 2 years shall determine the baseline net profit. The 20% margin is an internationally recognized policy-calibrated margin used to allow normal business fluctuations, avoid penalizing legitimate performance, and isolate excessive gains caused by crisis, price spikes, or supply disruptions. The windfall profits tax revenue shall be earmarked for fuel subsidies and cash assistance to vulnerable sectors affected by the energy crisis. Given the foregoing, we urge the immediate passage of this bill. LORDAN G. label: HB 9409
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A NATIONAL COACHES AND TRAINERS REGISTRY AND CERTIFICATION PROGRAM UNDER THE PHILIPPINE SPORTS COMMISSION AND THE TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (TESDA), PROVIDING STANDARDS FOR BASIC SAFETY AND SPORTS COMPETENCY CERTIFICATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Sports coaches, trainers, and athletic instructors play a critical role in the physical development, safety, and well-being of Filipino athletes across all levels—from grassroots and school sports to amateur and professional competition. However, the Philippines currently lacks a unified national registry and standardized competency framework governing individuals who provide sports coaching and training services. Incidents involving preventable sports injuries, undiagnosed medical conditions, improper physical conditioning, and inadequate emergency response demonstrate the urgent need for minimum competency standards among coaches and trainers. Many coaches operate without formal education in athlete safety, basic life support, kinesiology, mobility assessment, injury prevention, or emergency response procedures. This measure seeks to institutionalize a National Coaches and Trainers Registry under the Philippine Sports Commission, in coordination with the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, to ensure that all registered sports coaches and trainers possess fundamental competencies necessary to protect athletes and improve sports development nationwide. The bill establishes mandatory baseline certifications in: ● Basic Life Support (BLS) and emergency response; ● Early detection of physical impairments and life-threatening conditions; ● Basic mobility, movement screening, and kinetics; ● Athlete safeguarding and injury prevention; and ● Other competencies to be prescribed by the PSC and TESDA. The proposed measure also creates a tiered certification system, continuing education requirements, and a centralized database of accredited coaches and trainers accessible to schools, sports organizations, local government units, and the public. By professionalizing sports coaching standards and promoting athlete safety, this measure aims to strengthen grassroots sports development, reduce preventable injuries and deaths, and improve the overall quality of sports instruction in the country. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly sought. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 The rapid growth of social media and digital platforms has accelerated the spread of fake news and online disinformation in the Philippines. According to a 2025 survey by Publicus Asia, 68% of Filipinos rely on internet search engines for political and current affairs information, while 66% rely on Facebook, making online platforms among the primary sources of information for the public.¹ At the same time, the survey noted that the prevalence of fake news and disinformation has significantly eroded public trust in media and information sources.² 29 Recent reports likewise show the increasing scale of online misinformation in the country. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 The steady inflow of remittances from Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) remains a key pillar of the Philippine economy, supporting household consumption and national economic stability. According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), OFW remittances consistently reach billions of dollars annually, highlighting their significant contribution to the country’s foreign exchange earnings. Despite this, many OFWs and their families remain financially vulnerable due to limited access to structured financial literacy programs and exposure to scams, high-interest lending, and fraudulent investment schemes. 30 Government agencies such as the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) have repeatedly issued warnings and initiatives addressing the financial risks faced by OFWs, particularly in relation to investment fraud and improper money management. However, financial education efforts remain fragmented and not uniformly accessible to all migrant workers and their dependents. 37 With the increasing complexity of financial products and the rise of digital financial transactions, there is a clear need to institutionalize a comprehensive and accessible financial education program for OFWs and their families. This bill seeks to integrate mandatory financial literacy into pre-departure and post-arrival training programs, and to extend access to families through online platforms, with the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) leading implementation in coordination with relevant agencies. 44 By strengthening financial literacy among OFWs and their families, this measure aims to promote responsible financial management, protect earnings from exploitation, and enhance long-term economic well-being. 48 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 1 2 3 REP. title: AN ACT DECLARING THE UNIVERSITY OF EASTERN PHILIPPINES AS THE NATIONAL UNIVERSITY FOR SUSTAINABILITY STUDIES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFORE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates the State to protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education and to advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature. In furtherance of this constitutional policy, Republic Act No. 9512, otherwise known as the National Environmental Awareness and Education Act of 2008, recognizes the vital role of educational institutions in promoting environmental awareness, sustainability education, ecological protection, and responsible stewardship of natural resources. The law likewise encourages the integration of environmental education in academic instruction and institutional programs. The University of Eastern Philippines, being the first state university in the Visayas region, has consistently demonstrated its commitment to accessible and quality tertiary education while addressing the socio-economic and environmental needs of Eastern Visayas and the nation. Guided by its vision of becoming “a globally competitive green entrepreneurship university,” UEP has institutionalized sustainability-oriented instruction, research, extension, governance, and community engagement programs. The university has also established several sustainability and innovation-centered research facilities and programs, including the Center for Environmental Studies and Advocacy (CESA), the Research Center for Climate Change and Resiliency, the Affiliated Renewable Energy Center, the University Technology Innovation Center, and other research and extension initiatives dedicated to environmental protection, sustainable development, and green innovation. This proposed measure seeks to formally declare the University of Eastern Philippines as the National University for Sustainability Studies in recognition of its institutional leadership in sustainability education, environmental stewardship, green entrepreneurship, climate resiliency, and community empowerment. Moreover, this bill aims to strengthen the university’s capacity to advance sustainability-centered higher education, expand research and innovation initiatives, promote environmentally responsible development practices, foster global academic linkages, and produce graduates equipped to address contemporary environmental and developmental challenges. The enactment of this measure shall further reinforce the State’s commitment to sustainable development, ecological protection, and inclusive national progress through transformative and future-oriented higher education. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. JUDE A. label: HB 9416
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF BUGALLON, PROVINCE OF PANGASINAN, A LEVEL II GENERAL HOSPITAL WITH A CAPACITY OF AT LEAST ONE HUNDRED (100) BEDS, TO BE KNOWN AS THE BUGALLON MEDICAL CENTER AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This proposed legislative measure seeks to establish a Level II, Department of Health (DOH)- retained General Hospital with a minimum 100-bed capacity to be strategically located in Barangay Poblacion, Bugallon, Pangasinan. This initiative directly addresses the critical healthcare facility gap in the Second District of Pangasinan, driven by an expanding population and a severe shortage of public tertiary healthcare institutions in the area. The proposed location in Bugallon is central and highly accessible, situated along the Romulo Highway. This ensures rapid transit and reduced travel times from any point within the Second District. Crucially, the primary catchment area of this facility extends across the entirety of the First and Second Districts, with a maximum potential catchment capable of serving the First, Second, Third, and Fourth Districts of Pangasinan. By significantly reducing travel time to a fully equipped hospital, this measure directly mitigates the risks of preventable mortality and morbidity caused by delayed medical intervention. As the first public Level II hospital in the Second District, this facility will provide vital diagnostic, therapeutic, and emergency medical services. Its establishment will significantly decongest the over-extended bed capacities of surrounding Level I facilities, specifically the Lingayen District Hospital (LDH) and the Mangatarem District Hospital (MDH). Furthermore, it will optimize the distribution of the patient load of the Pangasinan Provincial Hospital (PPH) in Barangay Bolingit, San Carlos City, thereby alleviating the severe burden currently carried by the region’s primary Level III facility, the Region I Medical Center. The Second District of Pangasinan is home to approximately 518,738 residents, representing roughly 16% of the province’s total population. Applying a conservative, standard bed- capacity-to-population ratio of 1:1,000 residents, the district’s existing public healthcare infrastructure can only adequately accommodate around 130,000 people. A rigorous bed capacity gap analysis reveals a critical deficit of at least 389 beds within the district. By establishing a Level II general hospital with a 100-bed capacity, this legislation will effectively close the district's public bed capacity gap by 25.71%. The urgency of this measure is further underscored by alarming healthcare data: the bed occupancy rate at the Lingayen District Hospital currently stands at an overwhelming 182%, while the Mangatarem District Hospital operates at an unsustainable 212.73%. These figures drastically exceed the internationally and nationally accepted optimum bed occupancy rate of 60% to 85%. Presently, the only two existing Level II general hospitals in the district are privately owned, leaving the Second District without a single DOH-managed general hospital to serve its underprivileged constituents. Finally, this bill directly complements Republic Act No. 11223, otherwise known as the Universal Health Care (UHC) Act, fulfilling its mandate to provide equitable access to quality and comprehensive healthcare services for all Filipinos. The law explicitly dictates that all government hospitals must allocate no less than ninety percent (90%) of their bed capacity to basic or ward accommodations, ensuring that the poor and marginalized are prioritized. In view of the pressing need to safeguard the health, well-being, and lives of the people of Pangasinan, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. MARK O. title: AN ACT RECOGNIZING AND REGULATING THE USE OF MOTORCYCLES AS PUBLIC UTILITY VEHICLES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Traffic congestion in Metro Manila causes the country an estimated Php3.5 billion in economic losses daily.1 According to the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), as traffic congestion continues to worsen, without an effective intervention, the associated costs are likely to increase to Php6 billion by 2030. 2 Among the primary drivers of traffic congestion is the country’s poor public transport system, which remains fragmented, unreliable, and underfunded.3 As such, many Filipino commuters have explored an alternative mode of transportation known as motorcycle taxis, similar to habal-habal in rural areas. Compared to traditional modes of public transportation, such as jeepneys, buses, and trains, which either require passengers to wait in long lines, sit through the traffic congestion, or both, motorcycles are more efficient, convenient, and cost-effective.4 As more Filipino commuters rely on motorcycle taxis for their daily transportation, and more bikers depend on this mode of transportation for their daily income, the government has to step in and provide a more responsive and robust 1 Padilla, T.B. This bill seeks to recognize motorcycles as legitimate public utility vehicles (PUVs). Motorcycles-for-hire shall be placed under the regulatory authority of the Land Transportation Office (LTO), the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB), and concerned local government units (LGUs). This will ensure the motorcycle’s roadworthiness, promote the safety and protection of passengers and other road users, and guarantee the biker’s compliance with the necessary training and licensing standards, with due regard to fair pricing schemes and reasonable operating rules. Upon the recommendation of the sectors concerned, this bill fully adopts Senator Ejercito’s Senate Bill No. 10. Early approval of this measure is earnestly sought. LEILA M. label: HB 9418
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE DISABILITY AND SURVIVORSHIP BENEFITS OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT OF 1990”, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8551
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to strengthen the disability and survivorship benefits granted to members of the Philippine National Police who suffer permanent and total disability in the line of duty. It amends Section 73 of Republic Act (RA) No. 6975, otherwise known as the “Department of the Interior and Local Government Act of 1990”, as amended by RA No. 8551. It also provides for an updated computation of disability pensions to reflect prevailing salary adjustments of active-duty police personnel and removes the existing limitation on survivorship pension benefits granted to qualified dependents. Police officers continue to face life-threatening risks in the performance of their duties. In a July 2024 report, the Philippine National Police disclosed that sixteen (16) police officers died and forty (40) others were injured in the line of duty from January to July 2024 alone. This highlights the dangerous realities faced daily by law enforcers1. In another incident reported in January 2024, three (3) police officers were killed while four (4) others were wounded during a gun battle with an armed criminal group in Samar while serving warrants of arrest2. Meanwhile, permanently disabled retirees and their families continue to struggle against rising living costs. The Philippine Statistics Authority reported that headline inflation rose to 7.2% in April 2026, driven largely by increases in food, transportation, and utility costs3. Despite these economic realities, existing law does not provide automatic adjustments in disability pensions corresponding to salary increases granted to active police personnel, causing many disability pensioners to receive benefits that gradually lose value over time. 1 Caliwan, C.L. (2024, July 14). PNP chief: Emulate love, dedication of cops killed in line of duty. Philippine News Agency. Accessed from: https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1228936. Accessed on: May 6, 2026. 2 Amazona, R. and Meniano, S. (2024, January 31). 3 cops killed, 4 others wounded in clash with Samar gang. Accessed from: https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217932. Accessed on: May 6, 2026. 3 Philippine Statistics Authority. (2026, May 5). Summary Inflation Report Consumer Price Index (2018=100): April 2026. Accessed from: https://psa.gov.ph/price-indices/cpi-ir. Accessed on: May 6, 2026. This proposed measure provides for automatic pension adjustments based on the prevailing scale of base pay of active police personnel. It likewise removes the restrictive five-year survivorship limitation and ensures the continued receipt of pensions by surviving spouses and dependent legitimate children after the death of a permanently disabled retiree. The bill strengthens the social protection framework for police personnel who sustain permanent disabilities in the line of duty and guarantees that benefits remain responsive to prevailing economic conditions and the long-term needs of affected families. This measure responds to a profound obligation owed to those who place their lives at risk in service to the nation. Police officers who become permanently disabled often carry the physical, emotional, and financial consequences of duty long after operations end. Behind every injured officer is a family forced to confront uncertainty, rising expenses, and the painful reality that sacrifice sometimes comes with lifelong hardship. The nation cannot allow those who protected communities and preserved peace and order to face abandonment once disability prevents them from continuing service. This bill recognizes that genuine public service deserves enduring protection, meaningful support, and a system that upholds the dignity of those who sacrificed health and livelihood in defense of the Filipino people. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 9419
title: AN ACT GRANTING A TEN-DAY BEREAVEMENT LEAVE WITH FULL PAY TO ALL EMPLOYEES IN THE PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTORS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize a mandatory bereavement leave benefit of ten (10) days with full pay for employees in both the public and private sectors in recognition of the emotional, psychological, and familial burden caused by the death of an immediate family member. The measure aims to provide workers sufficient time to grieve, attend a funeral, and support their families during periods of loss without fear of losing income, employment, or workplace security. The loss of a loved one often creates profound emotional and mental distress that directly affects an employee’s well-being and capacity to work. Despite this reality, the Philippines still has no national law guaranteeing bereavement leave benefits for all workers. Many employees rely solely on the discretion of employers or are forced to consume vacation and sick leave credits during periods of mourning. According to the Mayo Clinic1, grief can trigger emotional, physical, and mental health effects, including anxiety, fatigue, depression, difficulty concentrating, and sleep problems that may significantly impair daily functioning and work performance. Meanwhile, the Cleveland Clinic2 explained that unresolved grief may negatively affect emotional stability, productivity, and overall health, emphasizing the importance of allowing individuals sufficient time and support during bereavement. In the Philippines, employees who suddenly lose family members often exhaust vacation leaves, incur debt to finance funeral expenses, or return to work immediately despite emotional distress due to fear of salary deductions and job insecurity. These realities reveal significant gaps in labor protection and employee welfare policies. This proposed measure addresses these policy gaps through the 1 Mayo Clinic. (2022, December 13). Complicated Grief. Accessed from: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/complicated-grief/symptoms-causes/syc-2036037 4. Accessed on: May 7, 2026. 2 Cleveland Clinic. (2023, February 22). Grief. Accessed from: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/24787-grief. Accessed on: May 7, 2026. establishment of a uniform bereavement leave benefit applicable to both public and private sector employees. It guarantees ten (10) days of leave with full pay upon the death of an immediate family member and prohibits employers from using the availment of such leave as grounds for dismissal, demotion, or adverse employment action. The bill also directs the Department of Labor and Employment and the Civil Service Commission to formulate implementing rules that ensure consistent and fair application across all sectors. Through these safeguards, the measure recognizes bereavement not merely as a personal matter but as a legitimate labor and social welfare concern deserving of statutory protection. This measure responds to a deeply human reality that every Filipino family may eventually face. No worker should have to choose between mourning a loved one and preserving financial stability. During moments of grief, employees need time to comfort their families, process loss, and fulfill cultural and familial obligations without the additional burden of workplace insecurity. A compassionate labor policy reflects not only economic priorities but also the values of solidarity, dignity, and humanity that define Filipino society. This bill recognizes that behind every worker is a family, and behind every family facing loss is a need for understanding, protection, and time to heal. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 9420
title: AN ACT RENAMING BADEO BARRIO SCHOOL IN BARANGAY BADEO, MUNICIPALITY OF KIBUNGAN, PROVINCE OF BENGUET, TO NGOPOS ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to rename the Badeo Barrio School located in Barangay Badeo, Municipality of Kibungan, Province of Benguet, into “Ngopos Elementary School” in recognition of the invaluable contribution of the late spouses Obay Tiglin, also known as “Ngopos,” and Odani Ngopos, whose generosity made possible the establishment of the school and the continued access of children in the community to basic education. The proposed measure is consistent with Section 13(e), Chapter II, Book I of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the “Local Government Code of 1991”, and complies with Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 29, s. 2011 governing the naming and renaming of public schools. Historical records and local accounts show that the late spouses Obay Tiglin, most commonly known as Ngopos and Odani Ngopos, donated the parcel of land in Badeo, Kibungan, Benguet. This later became the site for Badeo Barrio School established sometime in 1960. On October 27, 2003, their surviving heirs, namely Esnad Ngopos, Gegeya Ngopos Guapo, and Leilani Ngopos Laguitao, executed an affidavit confirming said donation. Despite the enduring contribution of local donors in sustaining public education in geographically isolated and disadvantaged communities, many schools across the country continue to bear names disconnected from the individuals whose sacrifices laid their foundations. In recognition of this reality, DepEd issued DepEd Order No. 29, s. 2011, encouraging proper institutional processes in preserving local history and honoring individuals who contributed significantly to educational development. The measure carries the endorsement of the Parents-Teachers Association (PTA) through School Resolution No. 1, Series of 2025, the support of the descendants of the donors, the Sangguniang Barangay of Badeo through Barangay Resolution No. 7, s. 2025, the Municipal School Board of Kibungan through Resolution No. 6, Series of 2025, and the Sangguniang Bayan of Kibungan through Resolution No. 60-2025. Through this measure, the State strengthens the preservation of local heritage and recognizes the role of ordinary citizens in nation-building through education. More than a renaming initiative, this measure serves as a lasting tribute to the quiet generosity of the family of Ngopos who chose to invest their land and legacy in the future of their community. Every learner who enters the school stands on ground once freely offered so that children of Badeo may have a chance to be educated and have a better life. At a time when communities continue to struggle for accessible education in remote areas, preserving the memory of those who sacrificed for the welfare of future generations becomes both a moral responsibility and a source of inspiration. Naming the school after the Ngopos family ensures that their legacy of compassion to education will continue to guide and inspire generations of learners in Kibungan, Benguet. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 9421
title: AN ACT RENAMING LANIPEW BARRIO SCHOOL IN BARANGAY TACADANG, MUNICIPALITY OF KIBUNGAN, PROVINCE OF BENGUET, TO DIONISIO ALIGANG ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to rename the Lanipew Barrio School located in Barangay Tacadang, Municipality of Kibungan, Province of Benguet, into “Dionisio Aligang Elementary School”. This aims to recognize the invaluable contribution of the late Dionisio Aligang to the establishment of the school and the advancement of education in the community. The measure operationalizes the authority granted under Section 13(e), Chapter II, Book I of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the “Local Government Code of 1991”, and complies with the Revised Guidelines on the Naming and Renaming of Schools under Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 29, s. 2011, as further reinforced under DepEd Order No. 40, s. 2014. Across many rural and geographically isolated communities in the country, public schools continue to exist because of the sacrifices and generosity of ordinary citizens who voluntarily donated land and resources for the education of future generations. In Barangay Tacadang, Kibungan, Benguet, the late Dionisio Aligang donated a ten-thousand-square-meter (10,000 sqm) school site through a notarized Affidavit of Quitclaim and Waiver of Rights dated July 23, 1993. This has paved the way for the establishment and continued operation of Lanipew Barrio School. Despite such contributions, many local benefactors remain historically unrecognized in official public institutions which results in the gradual loss of community memory and local heritage. Recognizing this, the DepEd reiterated through DepEd Order No. 29, s. 2011 that naming and renaming public schools must undergo a formal and lawful process involving the Local School Board and local legislative bodies to preserve historical and cultural significance in educational institutions. The bill gives due recognition to an individual whose contribution directly benefited generations of learners while complying with the standards prescribed by the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) and the Department of Education. It also strengthens community participation in educational governance, considering that the proposal already carries the endorsement of the Parents-Teachers and Community Association (PTCA), the Sangguniang Barangay of Tacadang, the Municipal School Board of Kibungan, and the Sangguniang Bayan through Resolution No. 20-2025. This proposed measure preserves the story of a man whose generosity opened the doors of education to countless children in a remote community in Benguet. Every classroom standing on the land he donated stands as a silent testimony to sacrifice, public spirit, and belief in the power of education. Allowing his name to fade into obscurity would diminish the very values communities strive to teach their children: service, compassion, and love for future generations. At a time when many young Filipinos search for examples of genuine heroism, this bill ensures that the legacy of Dionisio Aligang remains alive not only in memory, but in the very institution that his selflessness helped build. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G.
