label: HB 9468
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE OPEN LAW SYSTEM, PROVIDING FOR A FREE, CONSOLIDATED, UPDATED, AND ACCESSIBLE PUBLIC DATABASE OF PHILIPPINE LAWS, RULES, REGULATIONS, AND JURISPRUDENCE, INSTITUTIONALIZING SAFEGUARDS FOR AI-ASSISTED LEGAL INFORMATION SERVICES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The law binds every Filipino. Under the Civil Code, ignorance of the law excuses no one from compliance therewith.1 This rule is indispensable to public order, for no legal system can function if citizens may evade compliance simply by claiming unfamiliarity with the law. But the same rule carries an equally important obligation on the part of the State: if the people are bound by law, the law must be reasonably accessible, knowable, and understandable to them. The Supreme Court has long recognized that publication is essential to the binding force of laws. In Tañada v. Tuvera, the Court held that publication is indispensable because the people must be informed of the rules that govern them.2 The 1987 Constitution likewise recognizes the right of the people to information on matters of public concern and guarantees access to official records, documents, papers pertaining to official acts, transactions, or decisions, and government research data used as a basis for policy development, subject only to limitations provided by law.3 These principles reflect a deeper democratic premise: the law is not the private property of lawyers, publishers, institutions, or government offices. It belongs to the people because it governs the people. At present, however, public access to Philippine law remains fragmented. Official legal texts may be available online, but they are often scattered across different repositories, presented as originally enacted or promulgated, and not always 1 Republic Act No. 386, art. 3 (1949) (Phil.) 2 Tañada v. Tuvera, G.R. No. L-63915, 146 SCRA 446, 453–54 (Dec. 29, 1986) (Phil.). 3 CONST. (1987), art. III, § 7 (Phil.). consolidated with later amendments, repeals, implementing rules, or related jurisprudence. A citizen attempting to understand a law amended several times may have to locate the original statute, track each amendatory law, determine which provisions remain in force, consult implementing rules, and search for relevant jurisprudence. For lawyers and institutions with paid legal databases, this may be a routine. For workers, farmers, fisherfolk, students, microentrepreneurs, barangay officials, and ordinary citizens, this can be practically impossible. This difficulty is not merely technical. It is an access-to-justice problem. The Philippines continues to face serious gaps in legal assistance, rule-of-law performance, and digital inclusion. The World Justice Project has reported that the Philippines ranked 97th out of 143 countries in the 2025 Rule of Law Index, and 13th out of 15 in the East Asia and Pacific region.4 Earlier legal-needs data also showed that many Filipinos experiencing legal problems do not obtain formal legal help.5 At the same time, the Philippine Statistics Authority reported that only 48.8% of households had internet connection in 2024, confirming that digital public services must be designed for low-bandwidth, mobile-first, and offline or assisted-access conditions.6 This bill, therefore, seeks to establish the “Philippine Open Law System,” a free, consolidated, continuously updated, searchable, accessible, and publicly available legal information platform for Philippine laws, rules, regulations, jurisprudence, and other legal issuances. This creates the public infrastructure necessary to help Filipinos locate and understand the law they are already required to obey. This measure should be understood as part of the same transparency agenda advanced by the proposed Senate Bill No. 1432, or the People’s Freedom of Information Act. Freedom of information strengthens the citizen’s right to request and obtain government records. This bill strengthens the State’s corresponding duty to proactively supply the most basic public information in a democracy: the law itself. It ensures that statutes, rules, regulations, jurisprudence, and other public legal materials are not merely published in scattered form, but made available through an authenticated, searchable, reusable, and accessible public system. In this sense, the proposed Philippine Open Law System is the supply-side infrastructure that gives practical force to the demand-side right protected by freedom of information. 4 WORLD JUSTICE PROJECT, The Philippines Ranks 97 out of 143 in the WJP Rule of Law Index 1 (2025). https://worldjusticeproject.org/sites/default/files/documents/Philippines_3.pdf 5 WORLD JUSTICE PROJECT, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019: Philippines (2019); see also United Nations Dep’t of Econ. & Soc. Affs., Access to Justice Project. 6 Philippine Statistics Authority, Percentage of Households with Internet Connection Increased to 48.8 Percent in 2024; Two in Every Three Individuals Aged 10 Years and Over Used the Internet (July 21, 2025). The proposed system shall preserve official source texts, provide consolidated versions of laws and issuances, maintain amendment histories and prior versions, support open and machine-readable formats, and progressively integrate local ordinances and agency issuances. It shall also include accessibility measures for persons with disabilities, low-connectivity communities, and citizens who rely on public terminals, barangay facilities, libraries, schools, or local government offices for access to digital services. The bill also anticipates the responsible use of artificial intelligence in public legal information. Legal AI tools may assist citizens in searching, summarizing, translating, or navigating legal texts, but they must not be allowed to replace lawyers, courts, or competent legal authorities. Empirical studies have shown that even specialized legal AI tools may produce inaccurate or fabricated legal outputs, making safeguards indispensable.7 For this reason, the bill requires source citation, accuracy testing, human oversight, hallucination-risk monitoring, public feedback mechanisms, data privacy compliance, cybersecurity protection, and clear disclaimers stating that AI-generated outputs are not lega

title: AN ACT EXPANDING PATERNITY LEAVE BENEFITS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8187 OR THE PATERNITY LEAVE ACT OF 1996
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In recent years, the traditional roles and responsibilities of fathers and mothers around the world have shifted. Fathers are no longer seen solely as providers and breadwinners of the families, but as vital partners in child-rearing, while mothers have increased their participation in the workforce. In the Philippines, this shift has been seen in households where fathers have assumed the primary parenting roles while mothers migrate for work.1 Despite these changing dynamics and shifts in traditional gender roles, our legal framework has not yet fully adopted. This can be seen in Republic Act No. 8187 or the Paternity Leave Act of 1996, enacted 30 years ago, containing provisions that no longer reflect modern situations. Under this law, married male employees are granted seven days of paternity leave for the first four deliveries of the legitimate spouse with whom he is cohabiting. This excludes fathers who are not married, but wish to support their partners who have given birth, particularly those in common-law relationships or long-term cohabitation. The law also limits paternity leaves to the first four deliveries, unduly limiting support for larger families. Further, the current number of days of paternity leave does not provide sufficient time to meaningfully support the mother and newborn during the critical first month. label: HB 9470
title: AN ACT EXEMPTING INCENTIVES, REWARDS, BONUSES AND OTHER FORMS OF EMOLUMENTS RECEIVED BY NATIONAL ATHLETES AND COACHES FROM TAXES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10699, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “NATIONAL ATHLETES AND COACHES BENEFITS AND INCENTIVES ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In recent years, more and more Filipinos have been gaining international recognition for their accomplishments in various sports events. Their wins are no longer isolated victories but a testament to Filipinos’ hope, dedication, and perseverance. Notably, Carlos Yulo, Aira Villegas, and Nesthy Petecio took home Olympic medals in the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris. In the 2025 SEA Games, the Philippines won a total of 277 medals,1 with medalists including Alex Eala, EJ Obiena, and Kayla Sanchez. Watching these athletes compete to the best of their abilities and gain recognition for their country has brought Filipinos together. Ordinary Filipinos and even various private corporations have rallied behind these athletes who continue to bring pride to the country.2 In recognition of their contribution to national unity, Republic Act No. 10699 or the National Athletes and Coaches Benefits and Incentives Act was enacted. This law grants benefits and privileges to registered national athletes and coaches, such as discounts for transportation services, hotels, and restaurants, grants free medical and 1 https://www.olympics.com/en/news/sea-games-2025-all-philippines-medal-winners-full-list 2 https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/970266/filipinos-rally-to-support-filipino-athletes- beyond-wins-with-galing-ay-ilabas-galing-ng-pilipinas-chan/story/; https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/aug/05/paris-olympics-2024-carlos-yulo-artistic- gymnastics-floor-vault-philippines-gifts-gold 1 dental consultations in government hospitals,3 and provides cash incentives to athletes who win gold, silver, and bronze medals, and to their coaches. Meanwhile, the National Internal Revenue Code exempts from income tax “all prizes and awards granted to athletes in local and international sports competitions and tournaments whether held in the Philippines or abroad and sanctioned by their national sports associations.”4 These laws show the State’s intent to enable athletes to enjoy the benefits of their hard work, and to incentivize sports in the country, consistent with the constitutional mandate to give priority to sports to foster patriotism and nationalism.5 However, there remain gaps in our laws. The income tax exemption does not cover prizes and awards received by coaches of the athletes. Donations granted to said coaches are also subject to donor’s tax. Additionally, the tax exemptions for athletes only apply to prizes and awards and are thus contingent upon winning. This overlooks the effort and sacrifice of athletes who compete but do not secure a podium finish, and fails to encourage support for athletes during their training stages. This bill therefore seeks to expand the exemptions provided by current law. It seeks to exempt from national or local taxes any and all incentives, rewards, bonuses, donations, gifts, endowments, and contributions received by either competing or winning athletes and their coaches, whether from public or private persons. This measure also incentivizes contributing to the athlete’s training, as it provides that donations made prior to the competition and exclusively used to fund training and competition-related expenses will be considered as allowable deductions from the gross income of the donor. In every competition or tournament, they carry with them their own dreams and their nation’s hope and pride. In turn, we provide them with the unwavering support they need as we encourage the next generation of Filipino athletes and coaches to continue on. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this measure is earnestly sought. BRIAN RAYMUND S. label: HB 9471
title: AN ACT ENCOURAGING CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY AND PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution declares that the State recognizes the indispensable role of the private sector and encourages private enterprise.1 This policy reveals that national development is not the sole responsibility of the government, but a shared responsibility between the public and private sectors. In practice, many corporations in the Philippines have already taken on this role through their own Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives. Various companies have programs for disaster relief, livelihood opportunities, and educational scholarships. These efforts show that more than operating for profit, businesses are able to make lasting social impact on Filipino lives. This measure seeks to further these programs and private initiatives by providing companies with incentives to expand their CSR programs and make it an integral part of their business models. Thus, this measure encourages all business organizations to observe CSR in their operations. CSR-related activities include charitable programs, scientific research, youth and sports development, services to senior citizens, environmental sustainability, and social welfare, among others. As an incentive, this measure amends the Revised Corporation Code to allow corporations to retain surplus profits in excess of 100% of their paid-in capital stock for definite CSR projects. Additionally, the DTI shall recognize and reward all business 1 CONST. Article II, Section 20. 1 organizations for outstanding, innovative and world-class CSR-related services. Let us work hand in hand to ensure inclusive growth and a better future for all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this measure is earnestly sought. BRIAN RAYMUND S. label: HB 9472
title: AN ACT PROMOTING ENTREPRENEURSHIP BY ESTABLISHING A SUSTAINABLE FINANCING PROGRAM FOR MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES THROUGH THE PONDO SA PAGBABAGO AT PAG-ASENSO PROGRAM, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of our country’s economy.1 They generate employment opportunities, encourage local growth and development, and contribute to poverty reduction and the country’s gross domestic product. However, MSMEs remain vulnerable to economic and environmental circumstances, and may sometimes require additional capital to keep afloat or to grow as a business. Access to finance together with costs of utilities and labor continue to be key challenges for MSMEs.2 As such, some MSMEs resort to informal lenders with predatory interest rates and schemes that trap them into a cycle of debt and strip away any profit that they generate. These small business owners often find it difficult to obtain financing from formal banking institutions due to the more stringent requirements and required collateral. Recognizing this critical gap, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), through its lending arm, the Small Business Corporation (SBCorp.), provides a simple financing program for MSMEs, called the Pondo sa Pagbabago at Pag-asenso (P3) Program. 1 MSMEs: Pillars of Inclusive Growth and Resilience in the Philippine Economy. Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Research Academy. Available at https://www.bsp.gov.ph/Inclusive%20Finance/EFLP/EFLP_MSMEs_01a.pdf. 2 Id. 1 Under the P3 Program, businesses can get collateral-free loans with minimal requirements. In the implementation of our livelihood programs in the 2nd District of Parañaque, such as the Dagdag Puhunan program, I saw how a small amount can spell the difference between a business that closes its doors and one that thrives and expands. This is why the P3 Program is a landmark initiative that deserves yearly funding and prioritization, and should not be bound to annual budgetary whims and shifting administrative priorities. This bill seeks to institutionalize the P3 Program to ensure a stable and accessible source of financing for our country’s entrepreneurs. Under this measure, a P3 Fund will be created and lent out to qualified micro and small enterprises (MSEs). SBCorp is tasked to prioritize lending to underserved and unserved areas and MSE segments of the country, but with the goal of reaching all provinces and barangays of the country. To encourage accessible financing, the interest rates to be imposed on the loans will not exceed 1% per month for direct lending with SBCorp. or 2.5% per month for lending through accredited partner financial institutions. These interest earnings will accrue to the P3 Fund. Additionally, there shall be no collateral requirement from the P3 Fund loan beneficiaries. With this measure, our goal is not only to further promote entrepreneurship in the country, but to establish trust in our formal financing institutions. Ultimately, livelihood is about transforming the daily struggle for survival into an opportunity for upward mobility. By institutionalizing the P3 Program, we give our entrepreneurs hope and a fighting chance for a better future for themselves and their families. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this measure is earnestly sought. BRIAN RAYMUND S. label: HB 9473
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE NATIONAL URBAN AND PERI-URBAN AGRICULTURE PROGRAM TO ADDRESS FOOD SECURITY CONCERNS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE PURPOSE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Food security remains to be one of the significant challenges faced by our country today.1 In 2023, 31.4% of households suffered from moderate to severe food insecurity.2 Recent global difficulties, including the conflict in the Middle East and the resulting rise in fuel prices, have further highlighted our country’s vulnerability to external economic shocks and disruptions in the food supply chain. These circumstances emphasize the need to strengthen our domestic food production systems, and to build more resilience and localized sources of food. The country’s increasing reliance on imported agricultural products further highlights this vulnerability. In 2025, the country’s total agricultural imports was valued at $20.37 billion, representing a 15.2% share of the country’s total imports. This is an increase of 4.7% from the agricultural imports in 2024.3 In fact, imports have consistently outpaced exports by more than double, resulting in agricultural trade deficits since 2018.4 1 Seminano, Go, Javier, Ferrer. (2025). Socioeconomic Determinants of Food Insecurity in the Philippines: Evidence from the 2018–2019 and 2021 Expanded National Nutrition Surveys. Philippine Journal of Development Volume 49, No. 2. https://doi.org/10.62986/pjd2025.49.2b. Available at https://pidswebs.pids.gov.ph/CDN/document/pidspjd49-2025-2b.pdf 2 Id. 3 https://psa.gov.ph/statistics/agricultural-export-import/annual 4 State of Food Security and Nutrition in Southeast Asia. Facts in Figures. Congressional Policy and Budget Research Department, House of Representatives. January 2026 (No. 3). Available at https://cpbrd.congress.gov.ph/ff2026-03-state-of-food-security-and-nutrition-in-south-east-asia-2025/ 1 In this context, urban and peri-urban agriculture has emerged as a possible approach to increasing reliable food sources in cities, thereby strengthening food security and resilience. Urban farming is the growing, raising, processing, and distribution of food and non-food products within or on the fringe of a town or city.5 This provides not only food but also livelihood opportunities for people in the city. It can increase access to fresh produce, empower communities, and reduce transportation costs.6 Seeing the importance and potential of urban and peri-urban agriculture, the Department of Agriculture created the National Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture Program. A banner program established in 2022, this was initiated partly due to unstable food supplies during the COVID-19 pandemic. This Program focuses on the distribution of agricultural inputs to program beneficiaries, establishment of community urban farms, start-up of corporate urban farms for commercial scale, and establishment of urban agriculture training and technology centers.7 While this is a laudable effort from the Department of Agriculture, its implementation remains uneven across regions and dependent on yearly budgeting constraints. As such, this measure aims to institutionalize the National Urban And Peri-Urban Agriculture Program, including activities to establish urban, outdoor, rooftop, or indoor farms and greenhouses, and hydroponic, aeroponic, and aquaponic farm facilities. Other urban and peri-urban agriculture modules may also be adopted as new technologies develop. This bill also mandates the DOST and other pertinent agencies to prioritize the research, development, and transfer of technologies necessary in promoting integrated agriculture technologies. Moreover, idle and abandoned government lots and buildings owned by either national and local governments or available land resources in state universities and colleges will be considered for growing crops, raising livestock, and producing food using urban agricultural methods. Finally, this measure creates an Urban and Peri-urban Agriculture Fund to be used for the implementation of the proposed program. Ultimately, our goal is to ensure that every Filipino has greater access to affordable and nutritious food, while promoting innovation and sustainability in local food production systems. 5 Alumasa & Magnaye. label: HB 9474
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AN EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES SYSTEM (EMSS), CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL EMSS COUNCIL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XIII, Section 11 of the 1987 Constitution mandates the State to "adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development which shall endeavor to make essential goods, health and other social services available to all the people…” Further to this, Article II, Section 15 expressly mandates the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. The policy is further reflected in landmark health legislation such as the Universal Health Care Act, which recognizes that access to timely and quality healthcare is not limited to treatment inside hospitals, but also includes responsive and accessible emergency care systems. International experience shows that institutionalized and coordinated emergency medical systems are vital for better clinical results. Our neighboring countries in Southeast Asia, such as Singapore, have established centralized emergency hotlines and standardized EMS protocols, allowing for faster emergency response and better patient outcomes.1 Further, research on health systems in low- income and middle-income countries highlight the importance of interoperability, 1 Lateef, F. (2006). The emergency medical services in Singapore. Resuscitation, 68(3), 323-328. 1 standardization, and coordinated emergency response systems in improving overall healthcare delivery.2 However, at present, emergency medical response in the Philippines remains fragmented. Different local government units (LGU) operate under varying standards for ambulance services, ambulance dispatch systems, emergency personnel training, and patient transport protocols. In many areas in the country, ambulances are still inadequately equipped, emergency hotlines are either unavailable or poorly coordinated, and response capability still depends on the financial capacity of the LGU. This measure seeks to address these realities by institutionalizing a comprehensive and integrated Emergency Medical Services System nationwide. Simply, the bill aims to ensure that when a Filipino calls for help during a medical emergency, there is a functioning system ready to respond. Further, it institutionalizes the long-overdue use of a unified emergency hotline (911) which would simplify access to emergency assistance. The bill also establishes clear national standards for ambulances, emergency personnel, dispatch operations, and emergency treatment protocols, and strengthens coordination among national government agencies, LGUs, hospitals, and first responders, so that emergency response becomes more organized and more dependable. Equally important, it mandates the training and professionalization of emergency medical personnel, in recognition of the fact that emergency response requires specialized skills that must be properly regulated and continuously developed. In many life-threatening situations, survival is determined not by the sophistication of the hospital equipment, but by how quickly help arrives. Essential as it is for our government to invest in better hospitals, medicines, and medical technology, even more critical is ensuring a system is in place to connect people to these services when they need them most. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this measure is earnestly sought. BRIAN RAYMUND S. YAMSUAN Representative 2nd District, Parañaque City 2 Jayathissa, P., & Hewapathirana, R. (2023). label: HB 9475
title: AN ACT PROVIDING AN INCREASE AND AN AUTOMATIC ADJUSTMENT MECHANISM IN THE PERSONNEL ECONOMIC RELIEF ALLOWANCE (PERA) GRANTED TO GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Personnel Economic Relief Allowance (PERA) was introduced more than thirty (30) years ago through Budget Circular No. 4 (1991), which granted a ₱500.00 allowance to government employees to help cushion the adverse effects of inflation and economic instability in the country. In 2009, an additional ₱1,500.00 was authorized through Joint Resolution No. 4, s. 2009, in recognition of the rising cost of living. However, the PERA has remained fixed at ₱2,000.00 per month for the past sixteen (16) years. During this period, the Philippines experienced multiple economic crises, public emergencies, global supply disruptions, and sustained increases in the prices of basic commodities, transportation, fuel, electricity, healthcare, and housing. While essential commodities continued to rise, the value of the PERA steadily declined. To restore its purpose as a genuine economic relief measure, this bill seeks to increase the PERA to ₱5,000.00. It also mandates a periodic review to ensure that future adjustments remain reasonable and aligned with the government’s financial capacity. The urgency of this measure has become even more apparent in recent years. Despite rising daily expenses, public sector workers continue to deliver essential 1 services during disasters and public emergencies. Teachers continue educating despite increasing classroom and transportation costs. Health workers, emergency responders, and maintenance personnel remain on duty even as inflation steadily diminishes the real value of their salaries and allowances. By providing a more realistic economic relief allowance, this measure helps ensure that government employees can continue serving the public while still being able to provide a dignified living for themselves and their families. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this measure is earnestly sought. BRIAN RAYMUND S. label: HB 9476
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING MOBILE LEGAL CLINICS AND BARANGAY LEGAL AID DESKS TO PROVIDE ACCESSIBLE AND FREE LEGAL SERVICES TO UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, STRENGTHENING ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution expressly recognizes the right of all persons to free access to adequate legal assistance. Yet, for millions of Filipinos, this promise of accessible justice remains a distant ideal. In reality, ordinary citizens are effectively locked out of our justice system because legal services are time-consuming, physically inaccessible, and expensive. This is especially true in densely populated urban centers, which are often burdened by a critical shortage of Public Attorney’s Office (PAO) lawyers and severely clogged court dockets. In these communities, everyday disputes involving unpaid debts, property boundaries, family disagreements, small financial claims, and neighborhood conflicts frequently escalate simply because residents lack immediate, accessible legal guidance. This measure seeks to address this and make good the Constitutional promise of adequate legal assistance. It establishes a mechanism for free legal advice, basic legal assistance, and mediation at the community level through the creation and operation of Mobile Legal Clinics (MLC) and Barangay Legal Aid Desks (BLAD). The MLCs, operated by the Department of Justice (DOJ) and PAO, will bring legal aid “on-wheels” directly to far-flung communities, and will be fully-equipped to provide legal consultation, mediation and conciliation services, simple legal document assistance, and legal education sessions. Strengthening the MLCs’ initiatives are the BLADs in every barangay, which shall likewise be staffed by trained paralegals, volunteer lawyers, and legal interns. 1 In many cases, people do not immediately need a courtroom battle to assert their right; they simply need guidance and a fair opportunity to be heard. By placing capable legal volunteers within communities, this bill would enable residents to receive immediate assistance without the burden of engaging a private counsel or spending time and money travelling to city centers or courts for free legal assistance. More importantly, it would strengthen our system of mediation and amicable settlement, which has long been part of the Filipino tradition of resolving conflicts within the community. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this measure is earnestly sought. BRIAN RAYMUND S. title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING AND PROTECTING THE LAND OWNERSHIP OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION SCHOOL SITES AND MANDATING THE EXPEDITED ISSUANCE OF TITLES FOR REAL PROPERTIES USED AS PUBLIC SCHOOL SITES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

However, despite the thrust towards increased education spending, our government continues to face an infrastructure crisis in public basic education. The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II) estimates that the national classroom backlog has already exceeded 165,000 classrooms, with Metro Manila among the regions most severely affected.2 In the NCR alone, the shortage is estimated at more than 24,000 classrooms.3 As a result, many schools have been forced to implement double or even triple shifts, reducing actual instructional time for students and placing additional strain on teachers.4 The problem extends beyond the lack of new classrooms, as we are likewise confronted by a growing crisis of deteriorating school buildings. label: HB 9488
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING LOCAL FISCAL AUTONOMY BY PROVIDING AN ADDITIONAL SHARE IN NATIONAL TAXES FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE More than three (3) decades after the enactment of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the “Local Government Code of 1991,” local government units (LGUs) continue to bear primary responsibility for delivering essential public services and implementing local development programs. The Mandanas-Garcia ruling affirmed that LGUs are entitled to their just share in all national taxes, thereby increasing the overall National Tax Allotment (NTA). However, it did not fully address the structural inequities embedded in the distribution of national transfers. Municipalities remain particularly disadvantaged. Despite serving around sixty percent (60%) of the country’s population and delivering critical services such as health care, agriculture, local infrastructure, disaster response, social welfare, environmental protection, and community development, municipalities receive only thirty-four percent (34%) of the NTA. In 2023, cities generated and spent approximately Ten Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty- Six Pesos (P10,966.00) per capita on average, compared to only Three Thousand One Hundred Eighty-Six Pesos (P3,186.00) per capita for municipalities, reflecting a substantial disparity in fiscal capacity. Fiscal inequality likewise exists within LGU categories. Among cities, the proportion with Annual Regular Income per capita below the national average increased from forty-five and sixty-five hundredths percent (45.65%) in 2015 to fifty-nine and seventy-three hundredths percent (59.73%) in 2024, indicating that revenue growth has become increasingly concentrated among a smaller number of fiscally stronger cities. Similar disparities are evident among provinces and other LGUs. This bill seeks to strengthen local fiscal autonomy by granting LGUs an additional five percent (5%) share in all national taxes, to be phased in at one percentage point (1%) annually. Recognizing the fiscal constraints faced by municipalities, seventy percent (70%) of the additional allocation shall be distributed to municipalities, while ten percent (10%) each shall accrue to provinces, cities, and barangays. The preference for municipalities is based on substantial distinctions. Municipalities generally have narrower revenue bases, fewer opportunities to capture economic growth, more limited administrative capacity, and significant responsibility for frontline services, especially in geographically dispersed and less urbanized communities. The measure therefore uses the additional share, not the existing NTA, to correct fiscal imbalance without reducing the current shares of provinces, cities, municipalities, or barangays. The bill further introduces an Income Classification Equalization Factor to provide greater support to lower-income LGUs. For provinces, cities, and municipalities, this factor shall be based on the income classification system under Republic Act No. 11964, otherwise known as the “Automatic Income Classification of Local Government Units Act.” For barangays, the equalization factor shall be based on the income classification of the city or municipality where the barangay is located, unless a separate official barangay income classification system is subsequently provided by law. The bill also addresses practical implementation concerns by providing clear rules on computation, automatic release, official data sources, treatment of newly created or converted LGUs, correction of data errors, transparency reporting, and fiscal impact monitoring. These safeguards are intended to make the measure technically sound, politically supportable, and administratively implementable. By enhancing local fiscal space, especially for municipalities and fiscally weaker LGUs, this measure is expected to improve local development outcomes, strengthen decentralization, reduce overreliance on congressional insertions and discretionary national assistance for basic infrastructure and services, and enable LGUs to better fulfill their devolved functions under the Local Government Code and the Mandanas-Garcia framework. Immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ANTONINO B. label: HB 9489
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A LIVELIHOOD AND ENTERPRISE SUPPORT PROGRAM FOR BENEFICIARIES OF THE BALIK PROBINSYA, BAGONG PAG-ASA PROGRAM, PROVIDING FOR LIVELIHOOD STARTUP KITS, SKILLS TRAINING, AND POST-RELOCATION SUPPORT, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to experience significant regional disparities in economic development, employment opportunities, and access to sustainable livelihoods. This imbalance has contributed to persistent rural underdevelopment and the overconcentration of population and economic activity in major urban centers, resulting in congestion, informal settlements, unemployment, and increased socioeconomic vulnerability. In response to these long-standing structural challenges, the government launched the Balik Probinsya, Bagong Pag-asa (BP2) Program, which encourages voluntary relocation of families from urban areas to their home provinces. While the program addresses spatial redistribution, there remains a critical need to ensure that returning families are not only relocated but are also empowered with sustainable and dignified sources of livelihood in their communities. 1 Thus, this bill seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive, coordinated, and sustainable livelihood support system for BP2 beneficiaries. It recognizes that successful reintegration requires more than relocation assistance; it demands long- term economic empowerment anchored on skills development, enterprise creation, and local economic integration. Central to the bill is the establishment of an Enterprise Matching System, which aligns livelihood assistance with local economic conditions, available resources, and the skills of beneficiary households. This ensures that support provided is not arbitrary but strategically designed to foster viable and sustainable microenterprises in the provinces. The bill likewise institutionalizes safeguards for transparency, accountability, and non-politicization in the selection of beneficiaries and distribution of assistance. A centralized database and monitoring system will be established to prevent duplication, improve program efficiency, and ensure that assistance reaches intended beneficiaries based on objective criteria. Ultimately, this proposed Act aims to transform the BP2 Program from a relocation initiative into a comprehensive rural development and livelihood empowerment strategy. It seeks to promote inclusive growth, reduce regional inequality, and build resilient provincial economies where Filipino families can thrive with dignity and self-sufficiency. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9490
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE BARANGAY EMPLOYMENT REGISTRY SYSTEM IN ALL BARANGAYS, PROVIDING FOR ITS ADMINISTRATION AND UTILIZATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to face persistent challenges in unemployment, underemployment, and informal employment, particularly at the community level where many workers remain outside formal labor market systems. Despite existing employment and livelihood programs, the absence of a standardized and updated barangay-level employment database limits the government’s ability to efficiently identify jobseekers, match workers with opportunities, and deliver targeted interventions. Barangays, as the government units closest to the people, are in the best position to gather accurate and timely information on the employment status, skills, and livelihood needs of residents. Establishing a Barangay Employment Registry (BER) will strengthen grassroots labor market information systems and improve coordination among local government units (LGUs), Public Employment Service Offices (PESOs), and national government agencies. This bill seeks to institutionalize a standardized Barangay Employment Registry nationwide to facilitate employment matching, skills training, livelihood support, and evidence-based labor planning. It likewise promotes inter-agency coordination, digital integration with existing employment systems, and compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 to ensure responsible handling of personal information. By creating a reliable community-based employment registry system, this measure aims to expand access to jobs and economic opportunities while strengthening inclusive and responsive local employment governance. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9491
title: AN ACT GRANTING DISTINCTIVE HONORS AND PRIVILEGES TO NATIONAL ATHLETES, CREATING A NATIONAL ENDOWMENT FUND FOR SPORTS HEROES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Sports has long served as a powerful platform for national pride, unity, discipline, and excellence. Filipino athletes, through perseverance and sacrifice, have consistently elevated the country’s honor in the international arena despite limited resources and immense challenges. Their achievements inspire generations of Filipinos and embody the values of patriotism, resilience, sportsmanship, and service to the nation. The historic victories of Filipino athletes in international competitions, most notably in the Olympic Games and other world-class sporting events, have demonstrated the need for a more institutionalized and enduring system of recognition, support, and protection for the country’s sports heroes. While existing laws provide incentives for medal-winning athletes, there remains no comprehensive framework that formally recognizes their lifelong contributions to Philippine sports and nation-building. 1 This proposed “Bayaning Atletang Pilipino Act” seeks to fill this gap by establishing the Order of National Athletes (Orden ng mga Pambansang Atleta) as the highest state recognition for Filipino sports heroes who have brought immense honor and prestige to the country. The measure likewise institutionalizes additional honors such as the National Medal of Excellence in Sports, the Balangay Medal for Sportsmanship, and the Coaching Excellence Medal to recognize exemplary achievements, heroism, and mentorship in sports. Furthermore, the bill creates the Hidilyn Diaz Endowment Fund for Sports Heroes to ensure sustainable support for deserving athletes through pensions, medical assistance, insurance coverage, scholarships, and continued international training opportunities. By naming the endowment fund after Olympic gold medalist Hidilyn Diaz, the measure honors her groundbreaking achievement and symbolizes the aspirations of future generations of Filipino athletes. Through this Act, the State affirms its commitment to honoring their sacrifices, securing their welfare, and promoting a culture of excellence in Philippine sports. Finally, we recognize Rep. Gus Tambunting of the 2nd District of Parañaque for filing a similar bill in the Nineteenth Congresses. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. label: HB 9492
title: AN ACT ENSURING THE WELFARE AND PROTECTION OF BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING (BPO) WORKERS IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) industry has emerged as a major driver of economic growth in the Philippines and is widely recognized as one of the primary pillars of the national economy. Over the past two decades, the sector has positioned the country as a global hub for customer service, information technology services, finance and accounting support, healthcare information management, and other knowledge-based services. The continued expansion of the BPO sector has generated substantial foreign exchange earnings, stimulated regional development, and created employment opportunities for a young and highly skilled workforce. However, the nature of BPO operations—largely servicing multinational corporations across different time zones—requires round-the-clock operations and shifting work schedules. Consequently, a significant portion of the workforce is assigned to night-shift work and extended irregular hours, exposing employees to heightened health risks, workplace stress, safety concerns, and long-term physiological effects associated with shift work. Given the scale of employment in the sector and the unique occupational conditions faced by its workforce, there is a compelling need to institutionalize additional protections tailored specifically to BPO workers. While existing labor laws provide general safeguards, the distinct circumstances of night-shift and shifting work arrangements necessitate enhanced standards to ensure their health, safety, security, and overall welfare. This proposed measure seeks to protect and promote the welfare of workers in the BPO industry through the establishment of sector-specific employment standards and occupational health and safety policies. Among its salient features are the mandated regularization of BPO workers upon completion of six (6) months of employment, including those engaged as trainees or under probationary training; the prohibition of discrimination; the institutionalization of workplace health programs; and the provision of full health insurance coverage for employees. By strengthening employment security, promoting occupational health, and ensuring equitable workplace protections, this bill affirms the State’s commitment to safeguarding the rights and well-being of BPO workers who play a vital role in sustaining the country’s economic stability and global competitiveness. Finally, we recognize Rep. Gus Tambunting of the 2nd District of Parañaque for filing a similar bill in the Nineteenth Congresses. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9493
title: AN ACT RECOGNIZING UNPAID CARE AND DOMESTIC WORK AS AN ECONOMIC CONTRIBUTION TO NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT, INTEGRATING IT INTO NATIONAL STATISTICS AND POLICYMAKING, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Despite the significant contribution of unpaid care and domestic work to the well-being of Filipino families, communities, and the national economy, such labor remains largely invisible, undervalued, and unsupported in public policy and economic planning. Across the Philippines, women and girls continue to bear the disproportionate burden of caregiving and household responsibilities, often at the expense of their education, employment opportunities, economic participation, health, and personal development. Unpaid care work includes essential activities such as childcare, eldercare, caring for persons with disabilities and sick household members, cooking, cleaning, laundry, household management, and other domestic responsibilities necessary for daily life and social reproduction. While indispensable to the functioning of society and the economy, these contributions are not adequately measured in conventional economic systems and are frequently excluded from national statistics, development planning, and public investment priorities. 1 Thus, this proposed measure seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive national framework for recognizing, reducing, redistributing, and supporting unpaid care and domestic work through the establishment of a coherent care economy policy system. The bill mandates the integration of unpaid care work into national statistics through regular time-use surveys and the development of a Satellite Account for Unpaid Work. It also strengthens evidence-based policymaking by ensuring that care-related data are incorporated into development planning, budgeting, labor policies, and social protection programs. The measure further establishes the Care Economy Policy and Planning Office (CEPPO) under the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) to serve as the central coordinating body for care economy policies and programs. It likewise promotes whole-of-government and whole-of-society approaches through inter-agency coordination, local government participation, public awareness campaigns, capacity-building initiatives, and partnerships with civil society, labor groups, academia, and the private sector. By recognizing care work as essential social and economic labor, this measure aims to promote gender equality, strengthen family and community resilience, expand women’s economic participation, improve human development outcomes, and build a more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable economy. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9494
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING COMPREHENSIVE REFORMS TO MODERNIZE THE DELIVERY OF CITIZEN SERVICES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The growing demand for transparent, responsive, and technology-driven governance has underscored the urgent need to modernize government systems and eliminate outdated bureaucratic processes that burden citizens and businesses alike. Despite the enactment of reforms on ease of doing business and anti-red tape measures, many government transactions remain slow, repetitive, costly, and dependent on obsolete documentary requirements. These inefficiencies not only inconvenience the public but also create opportunities for corruption, discourage investments, and undermine public trust in institutions. In an era where digital transformation has become indispensable, there is a compelling necessity to establish a more integrated, accessible, and citizen-centered system of governance. The measure aims to simplify government procedures, reduce redundant requirements, promote digitalization, and streamline citizen and business transactions. Among its salient features are the removal of obsolete documentary requirements such as the community tax certificate or cedula, the establishment of interoperable and fully digital government systems, the promotion of online applications and electronic payments, and the integration of government databases and social service records. The bill likewise strengthens accountability and transparency in public service by encouraging process reengineering, reducing opportunities for graft and corruption, and improving the accessibility and inclusiveness of government services, particularly for ordinary citizens, small businesses, and beneficiaries of social welfare programs. Moreover, the proposed measure complements existing national initiatives on ease of doing business, electronic governance, and public sector modernization. By institutionalizing reforms that prioritize efficiency, transparency, and service delivery, the State can foster greater public confidence in government institutions while enhancing national competitiveness and economic productivity. Finally, we would like to recognize Rep. Joey Sarte Salceda of the 2nd District of Albay for filing a similar measure during the 19 th Congress. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9495
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE COFFEE AND CACAO INDUSTRIES, ESTABLISHING SUPPORT MECHANISMS FOR PRODUCTION, PROCESSING, MARKETING, AND EXPORT DEVELOPMENT, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine coffee and cacao industries possess significant potential to contribute to rural development, employment generation, value-added agriculture, and export growth. Many upland and highland areas in the country are well-suited for coffee and cacao production, yet farmers continue to face challenges such as limited access to quality planting materials, inadequate post- harvest facilities, weak market linkages, and insufficient technical support. Despite increasing global demand for premium coffee and cacao products, many local farmers and small enterprises are unable to maximize economic opportunities due to low productivity and limited access to processing and marketing support. Strengthening these industries will not only improve farmer incomes but also promote sustainable agricultural development and countryside enterprise growth. This bill seeks to institutionalize government support for the coffee and cacao sectors through the establishment of regional nurseries for quality seedlings, provision of marketing grants and processing support, strengthening of buyer linkages, and expanded technical and capacity-building assistance for farmers, cooperatives, and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). By enhancing productivity, processing, and market access, this measure aims to develop globally competitive Philippine coffee and cacao industries while creating sustainable livelihood opportunities in rural communities. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9496
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE RURAL EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE PROGRAM, PROVIDING FOR RURAL PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT, LIVELIHOOD SECURITY, CLIMATE-RESILIENT COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Many rural communities in the Philippines continue to face persistent poverty, seasonal unemployment, underemployment, and economic vulnerability, particularly during agricultural lean seasons, natural disasters, and climate-related disruptions. Limited access to stable income opportunities often leaves rural households highly susceptible to hunger, indebtedness, and economic insecurity. Despite existing government programs, there remains a need for a more comprehensive and institutionalized employment guarantee mechanism that can provide immediate income support while creating productive community assets and strengthening local resilience. This bill seeks to establish a Comprehensive Rural Employment Guarantee Program that will provide up to one hundred (100) days of paid public employment annually to eligible rural households willing to engage in labor- intensive community work. The measure aims to generate rural employment while supporting infrastructure development, environmental restoration, disaster resilience, food security, and climate adaptation initiatives. The bill further promotes community-based implementation through local government units, ensures transparency and accountability in program management, and integrates skills development, financial inclusion, and social protection mechanisms to help beneficiaries transition toward sustainable livelihoods and long-term economic opportunities. By creating a rights-based and inclusive rural employment framework, this measure seeks to reduce rural poverty, strengthen local economies, and promote more equitable and resilient development across the country. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9497
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL DIGITAL MARKETPLACE AND E- COMMERCE SUPPORT PROGRAM FOR LOCAL PRODUCERS, PROVIDING DIGITAL, LOGISTICAL, FINANCIAL, AND CAPACITY- BUILDING ASSISTANCE TO MICRO, SMALL, AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES (MSMEs), FARMERS, FISHERFOLK, ARTISANS, AND COOPERATIVES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), farmers, fisherfolk, artisans, cooperatives, and community-based producers remain among the most important drivers of the Philippine economy. They generate employment, sustain local industries, strengthen food security, and contribute significantly to rural development and national economic growth. Despite their economic contribution, many local producers continue to face limited access to wider markets, insufficient digital infrastructure, logistical barriers, financial exclusion, and unequal participation in the rapidly growing digital economy. The rise of e-commerce and digital marketplaces has transformed how goods and services are bought, sold, and distributed both locally and globally. However, a significant number of Filipino producers—particularly those in rural, geographically isolated, and underserved communities—remain unable to fully benefit from these 1 opportunities due to inadequate digital literacy, high logistics costs, limited online visibility, fragmented support systems, and barriers to onboarding in existing commercial platforms. Thus, this bill seeks to establish a National Digital Marketplace and E- Commerce Support Program that will strengthen market access, digital inclusion, financial literacy, logistics support, and technological capability for Filipino local producers. The measure adopts a comprehensive approach that combines government support, public-private partnerships, digital infrastructure development, consumer protection mechanisms, and capacity-building initiatives. The bill likewise promotes interoperability among digital payment systems, logistics providers, and accredited digital commerce platforms while ensuring compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 and applicable cybersecurity standards. It also provides mechanisms for consumer protection, dispute resolution, anti-fraud safeguards, and transparency in digital transactions. Furthermore, it seeks to empower underserved sectors—including women-led enterprises, indigenous peoples, youth entrepreneurs, cooperatives, and rural producers—through targeted training, onboarding assistance, and market linkage opportunities. Digital commerce is no longer merely an option but an essential component of inclusive economic participation in the modern economy. By providing local producers with the tools, infrastructure, and institutional support needed to compete in the digital marketplace, the State can help create a more resilient, innovative, and inclusive economy for all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9498
title: AN ACT EXPANDING HEALTH BENEFITS AND WELLNESS PROGRAMS FOR SENIOR CITIZENS, FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9994, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZENS ACT OF 2010,” AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution (Article XV, Section 4) explicitly mandates the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people and to afford full protection to the elderly. While the Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010 (R.A. No. 9994) and the Universal Health Care Act (R.A. No. 11223) have laid crucial foundations for elderly welfare, systematic gaps persist in delivering holistic, preventive, and wellness-oriented care tailored to the needs of senior citizens. Despite existing benefits such as free hospitalization and discounted medicines, many senior citizens continue to face preventable health deterioration, unmet mental health needs, and limited access to rehabilitative and wellness programs. The lack of structured preventive care contributes to avoidable hospitalizations, reduced quality of life, and unnecessary financial burdens on families and the healthcare system. The Expanded Senior Citizens Health and Wellness Act addresses these gaps by institutionalizing a comprehensive and proactive approach to senior health and wellness. The measure provides for mandatory annual preventive check-ups, the establishment of age-friendly wellness centers nationwide with rehabilitative and mental health services, mobile and telehealth programs for homebound and rural seniors, and strengthened inter-agency coordination among the DOH, DSWD, LGUs, and PhilHealth. It also includes digital literacy and inclusion programs to empower senior citizens in navigating online health services and combating misinformation, with dedicated funding mechanisms to ensure sustainability. With the Filipino population rapidly aging and projected to reach fourteen percent by 2030, this legislation is urgent. By emphasizing preventive care, wellness, and digital inclusion, it seeks to uphold the dignity and welfare of senior citizens, reduce long-term healthcare costs, and foster a healthier, more resilient, and digitally empowered society. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9499
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT-MANAGED FARM-TO- TABLE FOOD HUBS IN ALL 5TH AND 6TH CLASS MUNICIPALITIES TO CONNECT FARMERS AND FISHERFOLK WITH INSTITUTIONAL BUYERS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Food security, rural poverty reduction, and agricultural modernization remain among the most pressing development priorities of the Philippines. While the country is endowed with rich agricultural and fishery resources, many small farmers and fisherfolk continue to face structural challenges such as limited market access, weak bargaining power, high post-harvest losses, and dependence on layers of intermediaries that significantly reduce farmgate incomes. The “Farm-to-Table Food Hubs Act” seeks to address these long-standing inefficiencies by establishing an integrated, localized, and institutionalized system of agricultural aggregation, processing, distribution, and market linkage through the creation of Farm-to-Table Food Hubs (FTFHs) in 5th and 6th class municipalities. These hubs are envisioned as strategic facilities that directly connect local producers with institutional buyers such as government feeding programs, schools, hospitals, 1 and private sector markets, thereby shortening the supply chain and improving both producer income and consumer access to affordable food. The bill adopts a whole-of-government and multi-sectoral approach by designating the Department of Agriculture as the lead implementing agency, in coordination with key government institutions such as the Department of the Interior and Local Government, Department of Trade and Industry, Department of Education, Department of Health, Department of Social Welfare and Development, and the Cooperative Development Authority, among others. It likewise recognizes the critical role of Local Government Units, cooperatives, associations, civil society organizations, and private sector partners in ensuring the effective implementation and sustainability of the program. The bill further strengthens market access for local producers by encouraging institutional procurement through accredited food hubs, consistent with existing procurement laws and regulations. It also supports the development of value-adding activities, logistics systems, and post-harvest infrastructure to reduce losses and improve competitiveness in agricultural and fishery sectors. By modernizing agricultural market systems and institutionalizing farm-to- market integration at the local level, the State affirms its commitment to food security, poverty reduction, and sustainable rural development. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9500
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A MODERN HOSPITAL NETWORK LICENSING SYSTEM, REGULATING INTEGRATED HEALTHCARE DELIVERY NETWORKS, MODERNIZING HOSPITAL LICENSING, REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4226, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 4226, otherwise known as the “Hospital Licensure Act,” was enacted in 1965 to regulate the establishment, operation, and maintenance of hospitals and clinics in the Philippines. While progressive during its time, the law was crafted for a healthcare system composed primarily of standalone facilities and predates the emergence of integrated hospital systems, digital health technologies, telemedicine, electronic medical records, healthcare interoperability, and modern healthcare quality assurance frameworks. The Philippine healthcare system has significantly evolved through the enactment of the Universal Health Care Act, the expansion of PhilHealth coverage, regionalized healthcare delivery, public-private healthcare partnerships, and the growing use of information technology and artificial intelligence in healthcare operations. 1 Despite these developments, the country’s hospital regulatory framework remains largely facility-centric and fragmented. Existing laws insufficiently address integrated healthcare delivery networks, coordinated emergency response systems, interoperable health information systems, patient continuity of care, and modern healthcare governance standards. This proposed measure seeks to establish a modern hospital network licensing framework that: 1. shifts regulation from isolated facilities to integrated healthcare delivery systems; 2. institutionalizes quality-based healthcare regulation; 3. strengthens emergency preparedness and referral coordination; 4. mandates health information interoperability and cybersecurity standards; 5. modernizes enforcement and accountability mechanisms; and 6. aligns hospital regulation with the Universal Health Care framework. The measure further repeals Republic Act No. 4226 and replaces it with a comprehensive, technology-responsive, patient-centered, and systems-oriented regulatory regime. By modernizing the country’s hospital regulatory framework and transitioning toward an integrated, technology-responsive, and patient-centered healthcare system, this measure seeks to strengthen the capacity of the State to respond to present and future healthcare challenges. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9501
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DEVELOPMENT, PROTECTION, AND PROMOTION OF INDIGENOUS CULTURAL ENTERPRISES IN ANCESTRAL COMMUNITIES, ESTABLISHING MECHANISMS FOR COMMUNITY-LED LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine Constitution recognizes and protects the rights of Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) to preserve and develop their cultures, traditions, institutions, and ancestral domains. Likewise, Republic Act No. 8371, or the Indigenous Peoples’ Rights Act of 1997, affirms the State’s obligation to uphold indigenous self-determination, cultural integrity, and sustainable development. Despite these guarantees, many indigenous communities continue to face economic marginalization, cultural erosion, displacement, and the unauthorized commercialization of their traditional knowledge and cultural expressions. Traditional crafts, practices, and indigenous livelihoods that once sustained communities are increasingly threatened by poverty, globalization, imitation products, and the lack of institutional support and market access. 1 Thus, this bill seeks to establish a framework for the development and protection of Protected Cultural Enterprises in ancestral communities. The bill promotes community-led livelihood initiatives grounded in customary decision- making processes and Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC). It likewise ensures that indigenous enterprises receive institutional, technical, financial, marketing, and legal support from relevant government agencies. Furthermore, the measure strengthens safeguards for traditional knowledge and indigenous cultural expressions by providing mechanisms against unauthorized commercialization, fraudulent representation, and misuse of indigenous identity and heritage. It also encourages coordination among the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP), local government units, national agencies, and indigenous communities to ensure culturally appropriate and sustainable implementation. By empowering ICCs/IPs to preserve and strengthen their cultural heritage through sustainable livelihood opportunities, this measure contributes to inclusive economic development, cultural resilience, local tourism promotion, and intergenerational transfer of indigenous knowledge. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. Due to the geographical location of the Philippines, many areas are prone to natural disasters ranging from typhoons, earthquakes, and volcanic eruptions. This, alongside the rising poverty rate, raises the importance of providing affordable shelters in accessible locations. label: HB 9503
title: AN ACT PROMOTING AND SUPPORTING LOCAL HANDICRAFTS, WEAVING COMMUNITIES, AND HERITAGE INDUSTRIES THROUGH CAPACITY BUILDING, MARKET DEVELOPMENT, AND FISCAL INCENTIVES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines possesses a rich and diverse cultural heritage reflected in its traditional crafts, artisanal industries, indigenous knowledge systems, and community-based cultural practices. Across the country, generations of Filipino artisans have preserved unique traditions in weaving, pottery, embroidery, woodcarving, metalwork, basketry, and other heritage crafts that embody the identity, history, and creativity of local communities. Despite their cultural and economic significance, many artisans and heritage industries continue to face serious challenges, including declining transmission of traditional skills, limited market access, lack of financing and technological support, imitation and unauthorized commercial use of cultural designs, and the gradual loss of indigenous and community-based knowledge systems. Globalization, changing consumer trends, and the aging population of master artisans further threaten the continuity and sustainability of Philippine heritage industries. 1 Thus, this bill seeks to establish a comprehensive national framework for the preservation, development, promotion, and modernization of Philippine handicrafts and heritage-based industries. The measure recognizes that cultural heritage is not only a matter of historical preservation, but also a vital driver of inclusive economic growth, rural livelihood generation, tourism development, creative industry expansion, and national cultural identity. The bill institutionalizes a Local Handicrafts and Heritage Promotion Program under the leadership of the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), in coordination with the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA), the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), the Department of Tourism (DOT), the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPOPHL), Local Government Units (LGUs), and other stakeholders. The measure likewise strengthens the protection of traditional knowledge, cultural expressions, and indigenous designs against unauthorized exploitation and cultural misappropriation. It establishes a system of certification and cultural authenticity labeling to promote genuine Philippine heritage products, enhance consumer confidence, strengthen export competitiveness, and safeguard the integrity of culturally significant crafts and traditions. By supporting both cultural preservation and sustainable enterprise development, the State affirms its commitment to protecting the country’s heritage while creating meaningful economic opportunities for present and future generations. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9504
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING LOCAL HEALTH SYSTEMS THROUGH NATIONAL STANDARDS, PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKING, CAPACITY- BUILDING, AND SUSTAINED SUPPORT FOR DEVOLVED HEALTH SERVICES, ESTABLISHING A HEALTH SYSTEMS STRENGTHENING FUND, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution declares that the State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. While devolution has enabled LGUs to directly manage and deliver healthcare services tailored to local needs, disparities in healthcare capacity, infrastructure, funding, workforce availability, and administrative capability continue to persist across provinces, cities, and municipalities. These inequalities are particularly pronounced in low-income LGUs and geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDAs), where access to quality healthcare remains limited. Many LGU-managed hospitals, rural health units (RHUs), and barangay health stations (BHSs) continue to face challenges such as inadequate medical equipment, insufficient health personnel, fragmented health information systems, uneven service quality, weak emergency preparedness, and limited fiscal capacity. 1 Thus, this bill seeks to address these challenges by establishing a comprehensive national framework to strengthen devolved healthcare systems while respecting local autonomy. The measure provides for national standards and performance benchmarks for healthcare delivery, sustained technical and financial assistance to LGUs, institutional and human resource development programs, digital health integration, and mechanisms for transparency, accountability, and evidence- based monitoring. The bill likewise establishes the Health Systems Strengthening Fund (HSSF) to support infrastructure upgrading, procurement of medical equipment, healthcare workforce development, emergency preparedness, and other critical health system investments, with priority given to underserved communities and disadvantaged LGUs. By strengthening local health systems, improving governance and accountability, and ensuring equitable support for all LGUs, this measure seeks to build a more resilient, responsive, and inclusive healthcare system capable of meeting the present and future health needs of the Filipino people. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9505
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE COMPETITIVENESS OF PHILIPPINE EXPORTS THROUGH THE MODERNIZATION OF EXPORT LOGISTICS, TRADE FACILITATION, DIGITAL INTEROPERABILITY, AND SUPPLY CHAIN INFRASTRUCTURE, CREATING THE NATIONAL EXPORT LOGISTICS COMPETITIVENESS COUNCIL, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Efficient logistics systems and modern trade facilitation mechanisms are critical drivers of economic growth, industrialization, investment promotion, and export competitiveness. In an increasingly interconnected and technology-driven global economy, the ability of a country to move goods efficiently across borders significantly influences its attractiveness to investors, its participation in global value chains, and the competitiveness of its domestic industries. Despite the strategic importance of exports to national development, the Philippines continues to face persistent logistics and supply chain inefficiencies that increase the cost of doing business and weaken the competitiveness of Philippine goods in international markets. Exporters continue to encounter fragmented regulatory processes, duplicative documentary requirements, port congestion, prolonged cargo dwell times, inconsistent border procedures, and insufficient digital 1 interoperability among government agencies. These inefficiencies disproportionately affect micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), agricultural exporters, and emerging industries seeking access to global markets. This proposed measure seeks to establish a comprehensive national policy framework for export logistics competitiveness by institutionalizing coordinated trade facilitation reforms, digital interoperability among government agencies, modern customs and border processing systems, performance-based logistics standards, and infrastructure alignment for export development. The bill likewise establishes a National Export Logistics Competitiveness Council (NELCC) to ensure whole-of-government coordination and measurable implementation of export logistics reforms. The measure further promotes the establishment of a Single Electronic Export Window to enable end-to-end paperless export processing, reduce administrative burdens, improve transparency, and streamline interactions between exporters and government agencies. It likewise institutionalizes risk-based inspections, trusted exporter programs, logistics performance monitoring systems, and public transparency mechanisms to improve efficiency and accountability in export processing. By establishing a modern, integrated, transparent, and technology-driven export logistics system, the State affirms its commitment to building a more resilient, innovation-oriented, and globally competitive Philippine economy capable of adapting to the evolving demands of international trade and supply chain development. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9506
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE MSME FINANCING CORPORATION, PROVIDING FOR A MODERN DEVELOPMENTAL FINANCING FRAMEWORK FOR MICRO, SMALL, AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES, PROMOTING FINANCIAL INCLUSION, DIGITAL ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT, AND INCLUSIVE ECONOMIC GROWTH, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are widely recognized as the backbone of the Philippine economy, comprising the vast majority of business establishments in the country and generating substantial employment across sectors and regions. They play a critical role in fostering inclusive economic growth, stimulating local production, supporting innovation, and advancing regional development. Despite their importance, MSMEs continue to face persistent structural challenges that constrain their growth and sustainability, particularly in accessing adequate and affordable financing. Existing government financial institutions and programs have provided various forms of support to MSMEs; however, these initiatives remain fragmented across multiple agencies and often lack a unified developmental framework that integrates financing with enterprise capability-building, digital transformation, and 1 innovation-driven growth. There is therefore a need to establish a specialized institution that is explicitly mandated to address these gaps through a coherent, inclusive, and development-oriented approach. This proposed measure seeks to establish the Philippine MSME Financing Corporation (PMFC) as a dedicated government-owned and controlled corporation tasked with providing accessible, affordable, and sustainable financing programs for MSMEs. The Corporation shall serve as a specialized developmental financing institution designed not only to extend credit but also to promote enterprise modernization, strengthen financial capability, and support innovation, digitalization, and climate-resilient enterprise development. The bill institutionalizes a comprehensive framework that integrates financing with enterprise development services, financial literacy programs, and digital finance systems. It further introduces credit guarantee and risk-sharing mechanisms to expand access to credit while maintaining financial sustainability and responsible lending practices. The Corporation is likewise mandated to adopt risk-based and data-driven approaches, ensuring that lending decisions are guided by transparency, objectivity, and sound financial principles. To promote efficiency and accountability, the measure establishes a governance structure that includes key economic and financial agencies, private sector representatives, and MSME stakeholders, while instituting safeguards against political interference in lending decisions. It also mandates the implementation of digital finance systems, alternative credit scoring mechanisms, and interoperable platforms to modernize MSME financing and improve accessibility, especially for underserved sectors. By establishing a dedicated and modernized MSME financing institution, the State affirms its commitment to reducing inequality, expanding economic opportunities, and fostering sustainable and broad-based economic growth. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ 2 ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A.
