label: HB 9507
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RATIONALIZATION OF WAGE LEVELS ON A NATIONAL AND INDUSTRIAL BASIS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill proposes to amend Presidential Decree No. 442, known as the Labor Code of the Philippines and institute the rationalization of wage levels on a per industry basis, instead of the current regional minimum wage structure. For this purpose, it seeks to abolish the existing Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Boards (RTWPBs) and instead empower the National Wages and Productivity Commission to determine and fix the national minimum wage rates according to industries and address regional wage distortions. The current regional minimum wage set-up, introduced by Republic Act No. 6727, otherwise known as the Wage Rationalization Act, allows each region in the Philippines has a unique minimum wage set by the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Boards (RTWPBs) based on the poverty threshold, employment rate, and cost of living specific to the region. As a result, however, despite its original intent to encourage industries to disperse to areas outside Manila, Cebu and Davao and other urban areas, wage distortions have emerged in different regions. The 1 RTWPBs have failed to ensure decent standard of living for the Filipino workers, especially in the regional countryside, especially since there is a significant disparity in wages across regions while the difference in the cost of living is minimal. The rationalization of wage levels on a per industry basis will result in equitable pay between workers in the different regions and in the process, decongest the country’s overpopulated capital, which is often the top choice of workers due to higher wages. Most businesses still concentrate in these urban centers where the bulk of their markets or customers are, intensifying the internal migration to urban centers. Replacing the regional with an industrial-based minimum wage set-up will ensure that the national minimum wage remains responsive to certain peculiarities unique to each industry. With an equitable pay structure between urban and rural workers, industries will now be encouraged to invest in regions where operating and production costs are significantly lower than in the urban centers. This will result in higher income productivity and ensure a more inclusive economic growth that will benefit ordinary Filipino workers and their families. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 9513
title: AN ACT MAINSTREAMING THE USE OF BAMBOO AS A SUSTAINABLE MATERIAL FOR THE BUILT ENVIRONMENT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The increasing demand for sustainable, climate-resilient, and resource- efficient construction materials calls for innovative approaches in the country’s built environment. As the Philippines continues to confront the impacts of climate change, rapid urbanization, and infrastructure expansion, there is an urgent need to promote building materials that are environmentally sustainable, locally available, and structurally reliable. Bamboo presents a viable and strategic solution. As a rapidly renewable material with high strength-to-weight ratio and significant carbon sequestration capacity, bamboo has long been utilized in traditional construction and has gained global recognition as a sustainable alternative to conventional building materials. However, despite its potential, the absence of comprehensive and unified technical standards has limited its broader and systematic integration into mainstream architectural and structural practice. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize bamboo as a recognized and regulated construction material within the Philippine built environment. The bill mandates the development of a Bamboo Architectural Code (BAC) and a Bamboo Structural Code (BSC), to be adopted into the Architectural Code of the Philippines and the Structural Code of the Philippines, respectively. It further requires that all construction projects utilizing bamboo as a primary load-bearing material comply with the provisions of both Codes to ensure safety, structural integrity, and quality standards. The measure likewise promotes bamboo as a sustainable building material and integrates the practical education of bamboo utilization into the curricula of architecture, engineering, and related disciplines, thereby equipping future professionals with the technical competence to apply bamboo responsibly and innovatively. Additionally, it provides that bamboo products, by-products, and derivatives intended for construction must comply with Philippine National Standards, the National Building Code of the Philippines, and other applicable referral codes. By establishing clear standards, strengthening professional education, and promoting sustainable practices, this legislation advances environmental stewardship, supports local industries, enhances disaster-resilient construction, and contributes to a more sustainable and climate-responsive built environment. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. (ESAMELCO) A FRANCHISE TO CONSTRUCT, INSTALL, ESTABLISH, OPERATE, OWN, MANAGE AND MAINTAIN DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS FOR THE CONVEYANCE OF ELECTRIC POWER TO THE END-USERS IN THE CITY OF BORONGAN, AND MUNICIPALITIES OF MAYDOLONG, BALANGKAYAN, LLORENTE, SAN JULIAN, SULAT, GUIUAN, MERCEDES, SALCEDO, LAWAAN, BALANGIGA, GIPORLOS, QUINAPONDAN, GENERAL MACARTHUR, HERNANI, TAFT, CAN-AVID, DOLORES, ORAS, MASLOG, JIPAPAD, SAN POLICARPO, AND ARTECHE, ALL IN THE PROVINCE OF EASTERN SAMAR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to grant a congressional franchise to Eastern Samar Electric Cooperative, Inc. (ESAMELCO) to continuously provide an electric power distribution system to the people of City of Borongan, and Municipalities of Maydolong, Balangkayan, Llorente, San Julian, Sulat, Guiuan, Mercedes, Salcedo, Lawaan, Balangiga, Giporlos, Quinapondan, General MacArthur, Hernani, Taft, Can-avid, Dolores, Oras, Maslog, Jipapad, San Policarpo, and Arteche, all in the Province of Eastern Samar including any other municipality that may hereafter be created, reconstituted, or otherwise added to the Province. Furthermore, it lays down the standards and conditions that the franchise grantee must attain and fulfill in order to implement an effective partnership between the government and the distribution utility as its implementing partner for total electrification. ESAMELCO has been in operation from 1981 up to the present as a service-oriented, non-stock, and non-profit cooperative. Pursuant to the provisions of Presidential Decree No. 269, ESAMELCO was registered on December 9, 1977. On September 9, 1981, the National Electrification Administration (NEA) issued Certificate of Franchise No. 081 to ESAMELCO, granting it a 50-year franchise to operate. The franchise is set to expire on September 9, 2031. As the sole franchise holder for electric distribution in the coverage area, ESAMELCO has been providing excellent service to the 22 municipalities and 1 city of the province, achieving 95.85% electrification level, based on the potential household connections as of September 30, 2025. Over the years, the cooperative has demonstrated its technical, financial, and institutional capability to carry out its mandate, evidenced by its efforts in reducing system loss, minimizing power outages, and maintaining high collection efficiency. It is worth noting that the cooperative has garnered NEA’s performance rating of AAA, from 2016 to 2022, A for 2023, and AA for 2024. For the year 2025, ESAMELCO regained an AAA rating from NEA due to its continuous efforts to improve services for its member consumer-owners. Granting this franchise will ensure the continuous supply of electricity to the people of Eastern Samar. It will also allow ESAMELCO to sustain its mission of playing a vital role in the socio-economic development of its coverage area by providing an affordable, dependable, efficient and reliable electric service to its member-consumer-owners. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. SERGIO C. DAGOOC REP. PRESLEY C. label: HB 9522
title: AN ACT GRANTING THE NEGROS ORIENTAL II ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE (NORECO II) A FRANCHISE TO CONSTRUCT, INSTALL, ESTABLISH, OPERATE, OWN, MANAGE, AND MAINTAIN DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS FOR THE CONVEYANCE OF ELECTRIC POWER TO THE END-USERS IN THE CITIES OF DUMAGUETE, TANJAY AND BAYAWAN AND THE MUNICIPALITIES OF PAMPLONA, AMLAN, SAN JOSE, SIBULAN, VALENCIA, BACONG, DAUIN, ZAMBOANGUITA, SIATON, STA. CATALINA AND BASAY, PROVINCE OF NEGROS ORIENTAL
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Negros Oriental II Electric Cooperative (NORECO II) has long served as a vital distribution utility in the province. Incorporated with the National Electrification Administration on April 2, 1977, and registered with the Cooperative Development Authority on February 27, 1996, NORECO II has been engaged in the retail distribution of electricity within its franchise area for decades. Its existing franchise, which began on February 9, 1983 for a period of fifty (50) years, has enabled the cooperative to construct, operate, and maintain the distribution systems necessary to bring electricity to its member-consumer-owners. NORECO II’s service area covers the Cities of Dumaguete, Tanjay, and Bayawan, and the Municipalities of Pamplona, Amlan, San Jose, Sibulan, Valencia, Bacong, Dauin, Zamboanguita, Siaton, Santa Catalina, and Basay, all in the Province of Negros Oriental. Across this coverage area, the cooperative has energized 272 out of 272 barangays, reflecting the full reach of its electrification efforts and its important role in sustaining access to electricity for households, institutions, and enterprises. As of December 2025, NORECO II serves a total membership of 183,456, composed of 180,635 regular members and 2,821 associate members. It operates with 339 employees and maintains several sub-offices, collection centers, and substations strategically located across its franchise area. These facilities allow the cooperative to respond to consumer concerns, manage distribution operations, collect payments, and maintain service reliability throughout its coverage area. The scale of NORECO II’s operations further demonstrates its importance to the local economy. It recorded total energy purchases of 470,767,434 kilowatt-hours, an average peak demand of 91.08 megawatts, total revenue of ₱4,702,134,648.00, and total assets amounting to ₱3,475,000,219.00. These figures show not only the magnitude of the cooperative’s responsibility, but also the continuing growth in electricity demand within its franchise area. The renewal and grant of legislative franchise to NORECO II is therefore necessary to ensure the uninterrupted distribution of electricity in its service areas. Without a valid franchise, the cooperative’s authority to construct, install, establish, operate, own, manage, and maintain distribution systems may be placed in uncertainty, to the prejudice of its member-consumer- owners and the communities dependent on its services. This bill seeks to grant NORECO II a franchise to continue providing electric distribution service to the Cities of Dumaguete, Tanjay, and Bayawan, and the Municipalities of Pamplona, Amlan, San Jose, Sibulan, Valencia, Bacong, Dauin, Zamboanguita, Siaton, Santa Catalina, and Basay, Province of Negros Oriental. It recognizes the cooperative’s established infrastructure, institutional capacity, and continuing public-service mandate in advancing rural electrification and supporting local development. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SERGIO C. DAGOOC PRESLEY C. label: HB 9555
title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE LAND TRANSPORTATION (LTO) DISTRICT OFFICE IN THE CITY OF CALAMBA, PROVINCE OF LAGUNA, FROM CLASS “C” TO CLASS “A”, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Calamba District Office of the Land Transportation Office (LTO) in Calamba City, Laguna, serves as a vital frontline government office catering not only to the residents of Calamba City but also to motorists, transport operators, and vehicle owners from neighboring cities and municipalities in Laguna and nearby provinces. With the rapid urbanization, industrial expansion, and sustained economic growth of the area, the demand for LTO services has significantly increased over the years. Pursuant to LTO Memorandum Circular No. VDM-2024-2693, the classification of LTO District Offices is determined primarily by their average revenue collections for the last three fiscal years, among other operational indicators. The Memorandum Circular provides that District Offices with average revenue collections exceeding One Hundred Million Pesos (₱100,000,000.00) qualify for classification as a Class “A” District Office. Records show that the Calamba District Office generated revenues amounting to One Hundred Seventy-Seven Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Two Thousand Three Hundred Forty- Three Pesos and Sixty-Five Centavos (₱177,872,343.65) in 2023, One Hundred Ninety-Two Million One Hundred Seventy-Eight Thousand Four Hundred Seventy-Four Pesos and Sixty- Five Centavos (₱192,178,474.65) in 2024, and One Hundred Ninety-Five Million Nine Hundred Forty-Six Thousand Two Hundred Fifty-Six Pesos and Fifty-One Centavos (₱195,946,256.51) in 2025. These collections yield a three-year average revenue of approximately One Hundred Eighty-Eight Million Six Hundred Sixty-Five Thousand Six Hundred Ninety-One Pesos and Sixty Cents (₱188,665,691.60), substantially exceeding the minimum threshold prescribed for a Class “A” District Office. Moreover, the Calamba District Office has consistently recorded a high volume of transactions, averaging approximately Three Hundred Fifty-Seven Thousand Two Hundred Fifty (357,250) transactions annually over the last three years. This volume reflects the growing demand for vehicle registration, driver's licensing, permit issuance, enforcement-related services, and other LTO transactions within its area of jurisdiction. Despite its current classification as a Class “C” District Office, the office already performs functions and handles workloads comparable to those of higher-classified district offices. The existing classification no longer adequately reflects the operational realities, revenue-generating capacity, and service demands faced by the Calamba District Office. The proposed upgrading of the Calamba District Office from Class “C” to Class “A” will enable the expansion of its organizational structure, augmentation of personnel complement, enhancement of facilities, and improvement of service delivery. Ultimately, this measure will strengthen the government's capacity to provide efficient, accessible, and responsive transportation and regulatory services to the motoring public in Calamba City and surrounding areas. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. CHARISSE ANNE C. label: HB 9556
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FREE FINANCIAL LITERACY EDUCATION FOR OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS AND THEIR FAMILIES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) continue to play a vital role in the Philippine economy through their remittances, which reached a record-high USD 35.63 billion in 2025. These remittances provide financial support to millions of Filipino families and contribute significantly to national economic growth. Despite the steady inflow of remittances, studies show that many OFW families remain vulnerable to financial instability due to limited knowledge of budgeting, savings, investments, and long-term financial planning. Research further indicates that while OFW households generally demonstrate financial skills, there remains a need to strengthen responsible financial behavior and financial decision-making among both OFWs and their families. It is therefore imperative for the State to promote financial literacy as a tool for economic empowerment, helping OFWs and their families maximize the benefits of their hard- earned income, avoid excessive debt, build savings, and invest in sustainable sources of livelihood. This bill seeks to provide free financial literacy education for Overseas Filipino Workers and their families to enhance their financial capability, promote responsible management of remittances, and secure their long-term economic well-being. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this measure is earnestly sought. CHARISSE ANNE C. label: HB 9557
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL ACADEMIC CONTENT REPOSITORY AND PROVIDING DIGITAL LEARNING RESOURCES AND FREE INTERNET ACCESS IN STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes education as a fundamental right and mandates the State to make quality education accessible to all. Access to educational resources is essential to ensuring quality and inclusive higher education. However, many students in State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), particularly those in underserved and remote areas, continue to face difficulties in obtaining learning materials and reliable internet connectivity necessary for academic study and research. This measure seeks to establish a National Academic Content Repository (NACR) that will provide SUC students and faculty with free access to digital textbooks, open educational resources, lecture materials, and other academic content. It likewise aims to expand campus-wide internet connectivity through the provision of free Wi-Fi services in SUCs, thereby supporting digital learning, research, and innovation. By harnessing information and communications technology to improve access to knowledge and educational opportunities, this bill promotes academic excellence, digital inclusion, and equitable access to higher education for all Filipino students. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9558
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING REGIONAL YOUTH LEADERSHIP AND NATION- BUILDING TRAINING CENTERS FOR STUDENT LEADERS IN ALL REGIONS OF THE COUNTRY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The youth are among the nation's most valuable assets and they play a vital role in shaping the country's future. Developing competent, ethical, and service-oriented young leaders is essential to strengthening democratic institutions, promoting civic engagement, and fostering responsible citizenship. Despite the presence of student governments and youth organizations across the country, opportunities for structured leadership development remain uneven and often inaccessible, particularly in underserved regions. There is a need to institutionalize a comprehensive leadership and nation-building program that equips young Filipinos with the knowledge, skills, values, and commitment necessary for public service and community development. This bill seeks to establish Regional Youth Leadership and Nation-Building Training Centers in all regions of the country to provide accessible and sustained leadership education, civic training, governance awareness, and community engagement opportunities for student leaders and young Filipinos. Through partnerships among government agencies, educational institutions, civil society organizations, and the private sector, the program aims to cultivate a new generation of responsible leaders dedicated to nation-building and inclusive development. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9559
title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE NATIONAL FEEDING PROGRAM TO UNDERNOURISHED CHILDREN IN SECONDARY SCHOOLS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11037, ENTITLED, “AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A NATIONAL FEEDING PROGRAM FOR UNDERNOURISHED CHILDREN IN PUBLIC DAY CARE, KINDERGARTEN, AND ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS TO COMBAT HUNGER AND UNDERNUTRITION AMONG FILIPINO CHILDREN AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 13 of the 1987 Constitution recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building and mandates the State to promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual, and social well-being. Likewise, Article XIV, Section 1 provides that the State shall protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and shall take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all. Republic Act No. 11037, otherwise known as the “Masustansyang Pagkain Para sa Batang Pilipino Act,” institutionalized a national feeding program for undernourished children in public day care, kindergarten, and elementary schools. While the law has significantly contributed to addressing hunger and malnutrition among younger learners, many students in secondary schools continue to experience food insecurity and undernutrition, adversely affecting their health, school attendance, academic performance, and overall development. Adolescent learners, particularly those from low-income and vulnerable households, face increasing nutritional demands necessary for their physical growth, cognitive development, and educational participation. Hunger and malnutrition among secondary school students remain major barriers to effective learning and productivity, especially in economically disadvantaged communities. This bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 11037 by extending the coverage of the National Feeding Program to undernourished learners in public secondary schools from Grades 7 to 12. The measure further strengthens the implementation of the program by providing mechanisms for nutrition education, parental participation, local government support, and collaboration with community-based organizations, micro, small, and medium enterprises, and other stakeholders. By expanding the National Feeding Program to include secondary school learners, the State affirms its commitment to combating hunger and malnutrition, improving educational outcomes, and safeguarding the welfare and future of Filipino youth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9560
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution mandates the State to adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development and to give priority to the needs of the elderly through programs on social security and social assistance. Republic Act No. 7432, as amended by Republic Act No. 9994 or the “Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010,” recognizes the invaluable contribution of senior citizens to nation-building by granting them various benefits and privileges aimed at promoting their welfare and improving their quality of life. Despite these measures, many elderly Filipinos continue to face economic hardship brought about by rising costs of living, inflation, and limited sources of income. In several local government units, birthday cash incentives are already being granted to senior citizens as a form of recognition and support. However, the amount and availability of these benefits vary widely across the country, resulting in unequal treatment among senior citizens. This bill seeks to institutionalize a minimum birthday cash benefit of Five Hundred Pesos (P500.00) for all qualified senior citizens nationwide. The proposed measure likewise ensures that such benefit shall be released in a timely and accessible manner, free from transaction or service charges, and without prejudice to other benefits already granted under existing laws. While several local government units already provide birthday incentives to senior citizens through local ordinances, there is presently no national law institutionalizing a uniform minimum birthday cash benefit for senior citizens nationwide. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9561
title: AN ACT STANDARDIZING THE RETIREMENT BENEFITS OF JUSTICES, JUDGES, AND JUDICIARY OFFICIALS CONFERRED WITH JUDICIAL RANK, SALARY AND PRIVILEGES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 910, AS AMENDED”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes the vital role of the Judiciary as an independent and co- equal branch of government tasked with safeguarding the rule of law and ensuring the fair and impartial administration of justice. To preserve judicial independence and maintain the dignity of judicial office, it is imperative that members of the Judiciary, including Judiciary officials granted judicial rank, salary, and privileges, are afforded adequate retirement protection and benefits commensurate to the nature and importance of their public service. Republic Act No. 910, as amended, grants retirement and survivorship benefits to members of the Judiciary. Over the years, however, several Judiciary officials who were granted judicial rank, salary, and privileges by law have remained outside the full and uniform coverage of the said retirement law despite performing functions that are closely related and indispensable to the administration of justice. Moreover, disparities continue to exist in the retirement treatment and survivorship benefits received by certain Judiciary officials similarly situated with incumbent Justices and Judges. This bill seeks to standardize the retirement benefits of Justices, Judges, and Judiciary officials with judicial rank, salary, and privileges by expressly including them within the coverage of Republic Act No. 910, as amended. The measure likewise seeks to ensure parity and equity in the grant of retirement gratuities, survivorship benefits, disability retirement benefits, and pension adjustments, including the automatic adjustment of pensions whenever there is an increase in the salaries and allowances of corresponding positions in the Judiciary. The measure further recognizes the invaluable contribution of members of the Judiciary by extending educational benefits to their qualified children and by strengthening survivorship protections for their legitimate surviving spouses. These mechanisms serve not only as social protection measures but also as means of promoting morale, institutional stability, and continued dedication to public service within the Judiciary. This proposed legislation substantially reenacts a measure that was approved on Third Reading by the House of Representatives during the Nineteenth Congress, thereby reflecting the continuing recognition by Congress of the necessity of strengthening and standardizing the retirement benefits of members and officials of the Judiciary. Ultimately, this bill affirms the State’s commitment to uphold judicial independence by ensuring that those entrusted with the administration of justice are provided with adequate security and protection during retirement and after long years of faithful and honorable public service. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 9566
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL POLICY IN PREVENTING ADOLESCENT PREGNANCIES, INSTITUTIONALIZING SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR ADOLESCENT PARENTS, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Adolescent pregnancy remains a persistent and urgent public health and social development challenge in the Philippines. Despite efforts by the government and civil society, the country continues to record thousands of births among girls aged 10 to 19 each year, underscoring the need for stronger, coordinated, and evidence-based policy interventions. Data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) and the National Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) show that in 2018 alone, 183,967 adolescents aged 10 to 19 gave birth, followed by 180,916 in 2019, 136,302 in 2021, and 150,138 in 2022. These figures illustrate that adolescent pregnancy remains a persistent national concern that demands sustained policy attention. More alarming is the rising number of pregnancies among very young adolescents aged 10 to 14 years old. Recorded births in this age group increased from 2,411 in 2019, 2,113 in 2020, and 2,320 in 2021, to 3,135 in 2022, 3,343 in 2023, and 3,612 in 2024.1 According to the Commission on Population and Development (CPD), an average of twenty-four (24) babies are born to teenage mothers every hour in the Philippines, highlighting the magnitude of the issue2. Even more concerning, 95.1 percent of babies born to adolescent mothers below fifteen years old are born out of wedlock, exposing 1 Casucian, J. A. C. (2026, February 14). CPD, PSA flag rise in pregnancies among girls aged 10–14. GMA News Online. 2 Rita, J. (2019, October 23). Law addressing adolescent pregnancy sought as rate keeps rising. GMA News Online. these young mothers and their children to increased social stigma, poverty, and limited access to opportunities3. Adolescent pregnancy carries profound and long-term consequences. Young mothers face higher risks of maternal complications, while their infants are more likely to experience poor health outcomes. According to Save the Children Philippines, educational disruption is also a significant consequence with 71.4 percent of teenage pregnancies involving adolescents who have no formal education or who are out of school. Early pregnancy often forces young girls to abandon their education, limiting their employment opportunities and perpetuating intergenerational cycles of poverty and inequality. Beyond the social impact, adolescent pregnancy imposes an estimated P33 billion economic burden annually. Addressing adolescent pregnancy is therefore not only a public health priority but also a critical investment in the country’s human capital and sustainable development. This proposed measure is firmly grounded in the 1987 Constitution, which mandates the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people (Art. XIII, Sec. 11), recognize the vital role of the youth in nation-building (Art. II, Sec. 13), ensure the fundamental equality of women and men (Art. II, Sec. 14), and strengthen the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation (Art. XV). At the same time, the bill supports the country’s commitments under the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 3, SDG 4, and SDG 5, while advancing the long-term national vision of Ambisyon Natin 2040 and the priorities of the Philippine Development Plan in strengthening human capital and youth development. No child should be forced to become a parent before they are ready. Addressing adolescent pregnancy requires decisive and sustained national action. This measure provides a comprehensive and forward-looking framework that empowers adolescents, strengthens families, and supports communities in safeguarding the future of the nation’s youth. For these reasons, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. ESCUDERO Representative 1st District, Sorsogon 3 Alhambra, A. M. V. (2021, December). label: HB 9567
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL INTEGRATED PSORIASIS MANAGEMENT AND TREATMENT PROGRAM, PROMOTING ACCESSIBLE AND CONTINUING CARE FOR PERSONS WITH PSORIASIS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE According to The Lancet, a peer-reviewed general medical journal and one of the world's oldest and best-known medical publications, psoriasis is a common, lifelong inflammatory skin disease that can appear at any age and poses significant personal and societal burdens. It is associated with serious comorbidities such as depression, psoriatic arthritis, and cardiometabolic disorders. Although psoriasis cannot yet be cured, optimal management requires early intervention, prevention of comorbidities, lifestyle modifications, and individualized therapy to lessen both its physical and psychological impact. In 2014, Member States of the World Health Organization (WHO) recognized psoriasis as a serious noncommunicable disease (NCD) through a World Health Assembly resolution. The resolution emphasized that many people around the world suffer needlessly from psoriasis due to incorrect or delayed diagnosis, inadequate treatment options, insufficient access to care, and social stigmatization. Likewise, a 2025 global study shows a significant rise in psoriasis cases, with the number of people affected increasing by 86%-from 23.06 million in 1990 to 42.98 million in 2021. The total number of psoriasis-related disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), which represent the overall disease burden, increased from 2 million in 1990 to 3.7 million in 2021. In the Philippines, the estimated number of individuals with psoriasis is about 2 million, although some organizations believe the actual figure may be higher due to undiagnosed cases. In this light, and consistent with the recommendations of the Global Report on Psoriasis to: 1 a) Ensure that people with psoriasis have access to professional medical care and comprehensive, individualized treatment; b) Provide patients with medicines listed in the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines, including systemic therapies; c) Cover the cost of psoriasis treatments through universal health coverage schemes; d) Make optimal treatment for psoriasis and its comorbidities available; e) Ensure that health services for psoriasis are responsive to patient preferences and delivered in a manner that is safe, effective, timely, efficient, and of acceptable quality; f) Urge governments and nongovernmental organizations to support education on common chronic skin conditions for health-care professionals, including in undergraduate medical and nursing curricula and in-service primary care training; and g) Encourage governments to support psoriasis research and to reduce stigma and discrimination. This bill seeks to address the unmet needs of Filipinos living with psoriatic disease by establishing a national integrated program for the prevention and treatment of psoriasis as a public health concern. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 9571
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE TESDA WOMEN’S TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT CENTER IN THE PROVINCE OF TARLAC, PROVIDING FOR ITS FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines recognizes the indispensable role of women in nation-building and mandates the State to ensure substantive equality between women and men. In furtherance of this constitutional policy, the government continues to strengthen programs that empower women through education, livelihood, and employment opportunities. Despite existing laws promoting gender equality and women’s welfare, many women in the Province of Tarlac—particularly those from rural communities, low- income households, solo-parent families, indigenous groups, and displaced workers—continue to face limited access to technical-vocational training and sustainable sources of livelihood. Economic barriers, lack of accessible training facilities, and insufficient industry-linked programs hinder many Tarlaqueñas from fully participating in the local economy. Tarlac is strategically positioned as a growing center for agriculture, commerce, logistics, tourism, and emerging industries in Central Luzon. However, there remains a need for a dedicated institution that will equip women with specialized technical skills responsive to the present and future demands of industry and entrepreneurship within the province. This proposed measure seeks to establish a TESDA Women’s Center in the Province of Tarlac to serve as a specialized training and development hub focused on women empowerment, skills enhancement, and economic inclusion. The Center shall provide accessible and gender-responsive technical-vocational education and training programs designed to improve employability, encourage entrepreneurship, and expand livelihood opportunities for women across the province. The proposed TESDA Women’s Center shall prioritize programs in areas such as digital technology, food processing, agri-based enterprises, tourism services, creative industries, renewable energy, dressmaking, wellness services, and other in- demand sectors identified by local labor market studies. It shall likewise provide entrepreneurship training, financial literacy seminars, career counseling, and employment facilitation services in coordination with local government units, educational institutions, and private sector partners. Moreover, the Center shall create a safe and inclusive learning environment for women by integrating support mechanisms, including gender-sensitive policies, psychosocial support, and community-based outreach programs, particularly for disadvantaged groups. By investing in the skills and capabilities of women in Tarlac, this measure aims to strengthen local economic development, reduce unemployment and underemployment, and promote greater participation of women in productive and leadership roles within their communities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MARIA CRISTINA C. label: HB 9572
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AND MAINSTREAMING SCIENCE DIPLOMACY IN PHILIPPINE GOVERNANCE AND FOREIGN POLICY, CREATING THE PHILIPPINE SCIENCE DIPLOMACY OFFICE UNDER THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution commands the State to give priority to science and technology and to recognize them as essential for national development and progress (Article II, Section 17; Article XIV, Section 10). In an interdependent world, the great challenges confronting the Philippines — climate change, disasters, pandemics, food and water security, energy transition, and the governance of emerging technologies — are transboundary in character and cannot be addressed by any nation acting alone. They demand that scientific evidence and international scientific cooperation be placed at the center of how the country conducts its foreign relations and plans its development. The discipline now widely known as “science diplomacy” was articulated in its modern form by the American Association for the Advancement of Science and the Royal Society in their 2010 report, New Frontiers in Science Diplomacy, which set out three mutually reinforcing dimensions: science in diplomacy, diplomacy for science, and science for diplomacy. Since then, numerous States have adopted national strategies that harness science as an instrument of cooperation and soft power. The Philippines has engaged in this practice through the Department of Science and Technology, the Department of Foreign Affairs, the academic community, and its active participation in ASEAN scientific cooperation. Filipino scientists and practitioners have helped advance the field in the regional context; among them, Science Diplomat Glenn Banaguas, through Climate Smart Philippines and his work with the ASEAN science diplomacy community, has contributed to popularizing the practice and to building a network of science diplomats across Southeast 1 Asia. These efforts, however, remain fragmented and have not been organized under a single, coherent legal framework. This bill addresses that gap. It institutionalizes science diplomacy as a whole-of-government policy and mainstreams it across foreign policy, development planning, disaster risk reduction, public health, education, and environmental governance. It creates the Philippine Science Diplomacy Office under the Office of the President to coordinate, mainstream, and monitor the implementation of this policy — expressly in coordination with, and without supplanting, the mandates of the Department of Foreign Affairs over the conduct of foreign relations and of the Department of Science and Technology over science and technology. By embedding scientific evidence into the conduct of its foreign affairs, the Philippines will strengthen its capacity to respond to shared regional and global challenges, deepen its cooperation within ASEAN, and assert a constructive, evidence-based voice in international affairs. The measure will help ensure that the country’s development is informed by the best available knowledge and that its diplomacy advances the welfare and resilience of the Filipino people. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly requested. HON. label: HB 9573
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL COORDINATING COUNCIL FOR EDUCATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In the Philippines, the education sector is currently governed and managed by multiple agencies with differing functions and mandates, including the Department of Education (DepEd), the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), and local government units (LGUs). Unfortunately, this arrangement comes with overlapping responsibilities, fragmented policy implementation, and uneven responses to issues related to education. A coordinated national mechanism is needed to ensure coherent policy direction across basic, higher, and technical-vocational education; to integrate health, social protection, and local government inputs; and to align education planning with labor market needs and national development goals. This fragmentation is at odds with the State’s constitutional and statutory obligations to protect and promote accessible quality education. To guarantee permanence, stability, and institutional continuity, the bill seeks to establish the National Coordinating Council for Education (NCCE), an interagency and multistakeholder body responsible for strategic coordination across all levels of the education system. The NCCE will harmonize policy formulation and implementation, consolidate and standardize education data and research, coordinate resource allocation and emergency responses, and strengthen engagement with non-government stakeholders to improve outcomes and accountability. label: HB 9574
title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE VALIDITY OF MOTOR VEHICLE REGISTRATION TO FIVE (5) YEARS, ESTABLISHING A MODERNIZED MOTOR VEHICLE REGISTRATION SYSTEM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "LAND TRANSPORTATION AND TRAFFIC CODE," AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The registration of motor vehicles serves as a fundamental mechanism through which the State regulates the operation of vehicles on public roads, promotes road safety, ensures accountability among vehicle owners, and facilitates the collection of lawful government revenues. However, the current system requiring frequent registration renewals imposes recurring financial and administrative burdens upon motorists and contributes to congestion in Land Transportation Office (LTO) offices nationwide. With the continuous advancement of digital governance, automated monitoring systems, centralized databases, and electronic payment platforms, there is an opportunity to streamline vehicle registration procedures without compromising public safety and regulatory oversight. Many vehicle owners spend considerable time and resources complying with annual registration requirements despite maintaining valid insurance coverage, roadworthy vehicles, and updated ownership records. This measure seeks to extend the validity of motor vehicle registration to five (5) years while preserving the government's authority to conduct periodic inspections, enforce roadworthiness standards, verify insurance compliance, monitor environmental requirements, and ensure the accuracy of ownership records. The bill likewise establishes a modernized registration management framework that utilizes digital technologies to improve efficiency, reduce administrative costs, curb opportunities for corruption, and enhance public service delivery. By reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens while strengthening compliance mechanisms, this measure promotes a more efficient, citizen-centered, and technologically advanced transportation system that benefits both motorists and the government. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9575
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING LAWS ON RECKLESS IMPRUDENCE, PROMOTING RESPONSIBLE AND DEFENSIVE DRIVING, PROVIDING DRIVER PROTECTION, ESTABLISHING FAIR PRESUMPTIONS OF LIABILITY, DEFINING THE AUTHORITY OF LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS, AND IMPOSING APPROPRIATE PENALTIES AND LIABILITIES FOR ROAD SAFETY INCIDENTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Road traffic accidents are one of the leading causes of injury and death in the Philippines, with a significant portion attributed to reckless and negligent driving. Existing laws, while penalizing offenders, often fail to distinguish between truly negligent drivers and those who have exercised due diligence and defensive driving. This has led to situations where innocent drivers are unjustly detained despite clear evidence of compliance with traffic laws. This proposed measure seeks to address this imbalance by promoting responsible and defensive driving while ensuring fairness in the determination of liability. It introduces clear standards on aggravating and mitigating circumstances, establishes presumptions of liability, and strengthens the authority of law enforcement officers in handling road safety incidents. Moreover, the bill recognizes the importance of modern evidence such as dashboard cameras and CCTV footage in protecting innocent drivers. By allowing the presentation of such evidence, it ensures that individuals who exercise due care are not unjustly penalized. Ultimately, this measure aims to create a balanced legal framework that upholds accountability, protects the rights of drivers, and enhances road safety for all. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9576
title: AN ACT FURTHER STRENGTHENING THE RIGHTS, PRIVILEGES, BENEFITS, AND IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7277, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MAGNA CARTA FOR DISABLED PERSONS,” AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State recognizes its constitutional duty to protect and promote the rights and welfare of persons with disabilities (PWDs) and to ensure their full participation in society. Republic Act No. 7277, otherwise known as the “Magna Carta for Persons with Disability,” as amended, has long served as the principal law safeguarding the rights, privileges, and welfare of PWDs in the Philippines. Despite existing legal protections, many PWDs continue to face barriers in accessing government services, employment opportunities, mobility assistance, social protection, and essential support systems. One recurring concern raised by persons with disabilities, particularly those with permanent disabilities and elderly PWDs, is the burdensome process of repeatedly renewing identification cards despite the permanent nature of their conditions. Many are compelled to endure travel difficulties, inaccessible government facilities, long queues, and repetitive documentary requirements merely to maintain access to benefits already guaranteed by law. This situation imposes unnecessary hardship on a sector that the State is duty-bound to protect. This measure seeks to strengthen and modernize the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability by institutionalizing reforms that improve accessibility, promote inclusion, and prevent abuse of the privileges granted to PWDs. It establishes standardized validity periods for PWD identification cards, including lifetime validity for persons with permanent disabilities and elderly PWDs, while ensuring safeguards against fraudulent use. It further enhances accountability through stronger penalties against the falsification, misuse, or illegal issuance of PWD identification cards. The bill likewise expands support mechanisms for PWDs by recognizing assistive devices and assistive technology services as essential tools for independent living and social participation. It provides free assistive devices and services for marginalized PWDs, grants additional social protection measures such as monthly stipends for indigent persons with severe disabilities, mandates express lanes in establishments, and exempts qualified PWDs from certain travel-related government fees and charges. In addition, the measure strengthens employment incentives for private entities hiring PWDs and promotes more meaningful compliance with employment opportunities reserved for them. It also mandates inter-agency coordination in establishing a unified and reliable database of persons with disabilities to improve policy implementation and service delivery nationwide. Through these reforms, the bill seeks to uphold the dignity of persons with disabilities, eliminate unnecessary barriers to their participation in society, and ensure that government policies are truly inclusive, responsive, and accessible. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9577
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL PETROLEUM RESERVE SYSTEM TO ENSURE ENERGY SECURITY, MAINTAIN EMERGENCY PETROLEUM STOCKPILES, PROVIDE MECHANISMS FOR SUPPLY STABILIZATION DURING CRITICAL DISRUPTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to rely heavily on imported petroleum products to meet its energy requirements. As an archipelagic nation with a growing economy and an energy-intensive transportation and industrial sector, the country remains highly exposed to fluctuations in global oil prices, geopolitical instability, supply chain disruptions, and external market shocks. Recent international developments, including armed conflicts in major oil- producing regions, disruptions in critical maritime trade routes such as the Strait of Hormuz, and heightened volatility in global energy markets, have underscored the urgent need for the Philippines to strengthen its energy security framework. These events have demonstrated how disruptions occurring beyond Philippine territory can immediately affect domestic fuel prices, transportation costs, inflation, food supply chains, and overall economic stability. At present, the country largely depends on commercial inventories maintained by private oil industry participants under existing regulations. While such inventories provide a degree of short-term supply stability, they are insufficient to address prolonged or severe disruptions in global petroleum supply. The absence of a permanent, government-controlled strategic petroleum reserve leaves the nation vulnerable during periods of international crisis, natural disasters, or extraordinary supply interruptions. This proposed measure seeks to establish a Philippine Strategic Petroleum Reserve System that will serve as a national emergency buffer against critical petroleum supply disruptions. The measure provides for the creation and maintenance of government-managed reserves of crude oil and refined petroleum products, the establishment of strategically located storage facilities across the country, the implementation of stock rotation and quality management mechanisms, and the creation of a dedicated reserve fund to ensure sustainable financing. The bill likewise seeks to ensure that emergency petroleum reserves are utilized solely for genuine supply emergencies and national energy security purposes, while preserving the principles of a deregulated downstream oil industry. It further promotes transparency, accountability, and coordination among relevant government agencies and private sector stakeholders in safeguarding the country’s long-term energy resilience. In light of increasing geopolitical uncertainty, recurring global energy shocks, and the country’s continuing dependence on imported petroleum, the establishment of a strategic petroleum reserve has become both timely and necessary to protect the Filipino people and ensure the uninterrupted functioning of essential national services and economic activities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9578
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA OF THE OUT-OF-SCHOOL YOUTH, STRENGTHENING GOVERNMENT SUPPORT MECHANISMS FOR THEIR EDUCATION, EMPLOYMENT, SOCIAL PROTECTION, AND REINTEGRATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building and mandates the State to promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual, and social well-being. Despite this constitutional guarantee, millions of Filipino children and youth remain out of school due to poverty, unemployment, family problems, early pregnancy, lack of access to educational opportunities, and other socio-economic barriers. Recent data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) and various government studies continue to show that a significant number of Filipino youth remain outside the formal education system. Many are forced to work at an early age to help their families survive, while others discontinue schooling because of financial hardship, displacement, mental health concerns, conflict, abuse, or lack of support systems. As a result, many out-of-school youth become vulnerable to exploitation, discrimination, criminality, trafficking, substance abuse, and long-term poverty. The problem of out-of-school youth is not merely an educational concern. It is a social justice issue, an economic issue, and a national development issue. Every Filipino youth who is denied the opportunity to study, develop skills, or secure decent employment represents lost human potential and a setback to national progress. This measure seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive Magna Carta for the Out-of-School Youth that will recognize, protect, and promote their rights and welfare. It aims to strengthen the role of the government in ensuring accessible education, technical-vocational training, employment opportunities, social protection, mental health support, and reintegration programs for out-of-school youth across the country. The bill likewise adopts a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach by directing national government agencies, local government units, educational institutions, the private sector, and civil society organizations to coordinate and implement programs specifically designed for the needs of out-of-school youth. It further recognizes the need for stronger interventions for youth in especially difficult circumstances, including victims of abuse, trafficking, exploitation, armed conflict, teenage pregnancy, and extreme poverty. Ultimately, this proposed measure seeks to empower out-of-school youth to become productive, self-sufficient, and active participants in nation-building by giving them genuine opportunities to complete their education, acquire skills, obtain decent work, and improve their quality of life. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9579
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING GAME-FIXING, POINT-SHAVING, AND OTHER FORMS OF SPORTS MANIPULATION, PROMOTING FAIR, EQUAL, AND RESPONSIBLE COMPETITION, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 19, Article XIV of the 1987 Constitution mandates the State to promote physical education and encourage sports programs and competitions that foster self- discipline, teamwork, excellence, and the development of a healthy and alert citizenry. Sports play a vital role in shaping character and instilling values such as integrity, respect, discipline, responsibility, and perseverance. They provide an avenue where individuals, regardless of social status, background, or circumstance, can compete on equal footing and demonstrate their talents through honest effort and dedication. At its core, sports is founded on the principles of fairness, equality of opportunity, and respect for rules. The essence of competition lies in the uncertainty of its outcome. Athletes, teams, coaches, officials, and spectators place their trust in the belief that sporting events are conducted fairly and that success is determined solely by skill, preparation, teamwork, and sportsmanship. When this trust is violated through game-fixing, point- shaving, or other manipulative practices, the integrity of sports is undermined and public confidence in athletic competitions is diminished. Dishonest schemes that predetermine results, influence performances, or manipulate outcomes are contrary to the values that sports seek to promote. These acts deprive athletes of a fair opportunity to compete, distort the spirit of competition, and send the wrong message to the youth regarding accountability, responsibility, and ethical conduct. This bill seeks to declare unlawful and impose appropriate penalties upon any person who engages in game-fixing, point-shaving, game machinations, and similar fraudulent acts in sports competitions. By deterring such practices, this measure aims to uphold the principles of fair play, equal opportunity, transparency, and responsible participation in sports while promoting genuine sportsmanship among athletes and sports stakeholders. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9580
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING AND EXPANDING THE APPLICATION OF RELEASE ON RECOGNIZANCE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10389, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “RECOGNIZANCE ACT OF 2012”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The right to bail is a constitutional guarantee anchored on the presumption of innocence. Thousands of detainees remain in congested jails, not because they pose a danger to society, but because they are too poor to post bail. Republic Act No. 10389, otherwise known as the “Recognizance Act of 2012,” was enacted to address this inequity by allowing the release of indigent accused persons on recognizance. While the law provides a framework for such release, it does not establish a clear and standardized mechanism for determining indigency or assessing whether posting bail would result in undue hardship. The absence of uniform standards has resulted in inconsistent applications across jurisdictions. Recent policy discussions have highlighted the urgency of reform. During the Jail Decongestion Summit convened by the Justice Sector Coordinating Council (JSCC) composed of the Supreme Court, the Department of Justice, and the Department of the Interior and Local Government, stakeholders underscored that jail congestion remains a systemic concern largely driven by prolonged pretrial detention and the inability of low-income accused persons to post bail. The Summit emphasized the need for evidence-based release mechanisms, improved bail reform policies, and structured risk assessment tools to ensure that detention prior to conviction is used only when necessary to secure court appearance or protect public safety. The Summit further recognized that a significant proportion of persons deprived of liberty are charged with non-violent offenses and remain incarcerated solely due to poverty. It recommended stronger coordination among courts, prosecutors, public attorneys, and local government units to standardize procedures for indigency determination and pretrial release. This bill responds directly to those policy recommendations by strengthening and operationalizing the Recognizance Act through the institutionalization of a Financial Capacity Assessment prior to the grant of recognizance. By introducing financial-based standards, this measure promotes fairness, uniformity, and transparency in the administration of pretrial release. It strengthens judicial discretion through structured guidelines while safeguarding the constitutional rights of the accused. More importantly, the bill contributes to the urgent national effort to decongest detention facilities. Rational and evidence-based release mechanisms will help alleviate overcrowding, reduce detention costs, improve case flow management, and uphold the dignity of persons awaiting trial. This proposed amendment affirms a simple but fundamental principle: liberty before conviction should not depend on wealth, but on justice and risk. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9581
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL INTEROPERABLE ELECTRONIC HEALTH INFORMATION SYSTEM, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE A NATIONAL HEALTH INFORMATION GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK, MANDATING THE ADOPTION OF ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS IN ALL HEALTH FACILITIES, PROVIDING SAFEGUARDS FOR DATA PRIVACY AND CYBERSECURITY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Constitution recognizes the duty of the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people and to instill health consciousness among Filipinos. In support of this constitutional mandate, Republic Act No. 11223, or the “Universal Health Care Act,” emphasizes the need for an integrated and efficient health information system that will strengthen the delivery of accessible, responsive, and patient-centered healthcare services throughout the country. While efforts toward healthcare digitalization continue to progress, the country’s health information systems remain largely fragmented and disconnected. The absence of a unified and interoperable electronic health record infrastructure has resulted in delays in patient care, duplication of medical procedures, inefficiencies in health service delivery, and limitations in public health monitoring and planning. These challenges are especially evident in underserved and geographically isolated communities where access to healthcare information and digital infrastructure remains limited. This proposed measure seeks to establish a National Interoperable Electronic Health Information System (NIEHIS) that will integrate public and accredited private healthcare institutions into a secure, reliable, and patient-centered digital health network. Through the institutionalization of a National Electronic Health Record (EHR) System, the bill aims to ensure interoperability among healthcare providers, strengthen data privacy and cybersecurity protections, improve continuity and quality of care, and support evidence-based health governance and disease surveillance. It likewise provides mechanisms for offline accessibility in rural and remote areas and establishes a clear governance and implementation framework for the modernization of the country’s healthcare information systems. Moreover, the measure upholds the rights of patients over their personal health information by ensuring informed consent, data protection, and secure access to medical records, while enabling authorized healthcare professionals’ timely access to accurate patient information necessary for efficient healthcare delivery. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9582
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE RESPONSIBLE DEVELOPMENT, DEPLOYMENT, UTILIZATION, AND REGULATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE PHILIPPINES, CREATING THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (AIDA), AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping economies, industries, public institutions, and everyday life at an unprecedented pace. Across the world, governments are adopting national policies and regulatory mechanisms to harness the benefits of AI while safeguarding the public against its potential risks. From healthcare and education to transportation, finance, agriculture, and public governance, AI technologies are increasingly influencing how societies function and how decisions are made. The Philippines stands at a crucial point in its digital transformation journey. While AI presents immense opportunities to improve public services, strengthen national competitiveness, generate employment, and accelerate innovation, it likewise raises serious concerns relating to privacy, cybersecurity, labor displacement, misinformation, algorithmic discrimination, and the misuse of automated systems. The absence of a comprehensive legal and institutional framework governing AI may expose the country to technological vulnerabilities and leave Filipino citizens inadequately protected from harmful and unethical applications of emerging technologies. This proposed measure seeks to establish a balanced, adaptive, and rights- based framework for the development and regulation of Artificial Intelligence in the Philippines. It aims to encourage innovation and investment in AI while ensuring that the deployment and use of such technologies remain transparent, accountable, fair, secure, and aligned with constitutional rights and national interests. The bill provides guiding principles for ethical AI governance, promotes research and development, strengthens workforce preparedness, protects human rights and data privacy, and establishes mechanisms for transparency and public accountability in AI systems. It likewise adopts a risk-based approach to AI regulation, ensuring that high-risk AI systems are subject to stricter oversight and compliance standards. Central to this proposed legislation is the creation of the Artificial Intelligence Development Authority (AIDA), which shall serve as the lead government body responsible for formulating national AI policies, coordinating inter-agency initiatives, developing regulatory standards, and ensuring compliance with ethical and legal safeguards in the use of AI technologies. Ultimately, this measure seeks to position the Philippines as a responsible and globally competitive participant in the evolving AI ecosystem while ensuring that technological advancement remains people-centered, inclusive, and beneficial to all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 9583
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6981, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE WITNESS PROTECTION, SECURITY AND BENEFIT ACT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 6981, otherwise known as the Witness Protection, Security and Benefit Act, was enacted on April 24, 1991 to ensure that individuals who possess material knowledge of crimes are afforded protection, security, and support in exchange for their testimony. It is designed to encourage individuals with knowledge of criminal activities to come forward and testify. To achieve this, the Department of Justice (DOJ) is responsible for developing and implementing the Witness Protection, Security and Benefit Program. Three decades on, the law has fallen behind the evolving nature of crime and the heightened risks faced by those who dare to testify. The structural and operational gaps have undermined the State’s power to secure convictions in serious cases. Without immediate reform, these gaps will continue to weaken prosecutions, discourage cooperation, and entrench impunity in our justice system. First, the current law does not provide a mechanism for the perpetuation and preservation of the testimony of witnesses who are elderly, seriously ill, under threat, or otherwise unable to testify during trial. In high-risk cases, justice can be derailed by delay. When a witness dies, becomes incapacitated, or is silenced before trial, critical evidence is permanently lost. Without a clear statutory authority for timely perpetuation of testimony, prosecutions of grave crimes may collapse—not for lack of truth, but for lack of preserved evidence. Second, Section 3 (d) excludes members of the Philippine National Police, the Armed Forces of the Philippines, and other law enforcement agencies from joining the program.1 This blanket exclusion weakens the fight against corruption and syndicated crimes, particularly those involving state actors. Honest officers who are willing to testify against wrongdoing within their own ranks are left vulnerable and unprotected. This exclusion not only discourages whistleblowing but also undermines the constitutional guarantee of equal protection by denying protection solely on the basis of institutional affiliation.2 Finally, and equally urgent, the provision on financial assistance under Section 8 (b) of the law is inadequate. The current text merely provides that the DOJ shall, “whenever practicable,” assist the witness in obtaining a means of livelihood and that financial assistance shall be granted “in such amount and for such duration as the Department shall determine.” This language provides no minimum guarantee, no clear standard, and no mechanism for periodic adjustment. In practice, this may result in inconsistent support, prolonged uncertainty, and financial insecurity for witnesses and their families. Witnesses who are relocated often lose employment, housing, and community support. Without sufficient and predictable financial assistance, they may face economic hardship that discourages cooperation or exposes them to renewed risk. Protection must be meaningful and sustainable; otherwise, the very objectives of the Program are undermined. Hence, this bill which seeks to: (1) expressly authorize the perpetuation of testimony of witnesses admitted into the Program by allowing the filing of petitions before the Regional Trial Court; (2) extend the coverage of the 1 Rep. Act No. 6981, Sec. 3(d). 2 Section 1, Article III, 1987 Constitution. Witness Protection, Security and Benefit Program to allow the participation of law enforcement personnel who may serve as material witnesses against their own agencies; (3) comprehensively establish and strengthen the rights and privileges of witnesses before, during, and after the giving of testimony; (4) grant witnesses the right to receive livelihood and skills training, including appropriate technical and vocational training from the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA); (5) provide a guaranteed minimum monthly allocation of One Hundred Thousand Pesos (P100,000) as financial assistance with a provision for periodic review and adjustment indexed to inflation; and (6) strengthen safeguards against intimidation and retaliation by increasing the penalty for harassment of witnesses to a fine of not more than Two Hundred Thousand Pesos (P200,000.00), without prejudice to imprisonment and perpetual disqualification from public office in the case of public officers. These reforms are not merely procedural improvements; they are necessary safeguards to ensure that justice is neither delayed nor denied. By institutionalizing testimony preservation, expanding eligibility, and securing reliable funding, this measure fortifies the Witness Protection, Security and Benefit Program against present realities and emerging threats. title: AN ACT GRANTING DISTINCTIVE HONORS AND PRIVILEGES TO NATIONAL ATHLETES, CREATING A NATIONAL ENDOWMENT FUND FOR SPORTS HEROES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Education remains one of the most powerful instruments for national development, social mobility, technological advancement, and economic transformation. As the country confronts the challenges of industrial modernization, digital transformation, and global competitiveness, there is an urgent need to strengthen institutions that specialize in technical, vocational, applied scientific, and professional education. The Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP), as one of the largest state universities in the country and a leading institution in providing affordable and accessible higher education, is uniquely positioned to fulfill this national role. Since its establishment, PUP has consistently produced graduates who contribute significantly to the nation's workforce, public service, industry, entrepreneurship, research, and innovation. However, the increasing complexity of economic and technological demands requires a stronger institutional framework that will enable the University to exercise greater academic leadership, expand its research and extension functions, strengthen industry linkages, and serve as a model for polytechnic education throughout the country. This measure seeks to formally strengthen the Polytechnic University of the Philippines as the country's First National Polytechnic University. The bill affirms PUP's leadership role in advancing polytechnic education and mandates it to provide guidance and support to other polytechnic state universities and colleges in developing professional, technical, and applied academic programs responsive to national development priorities. The proposed legislation further enhances the University's institutional and fiscal autonomy, strengthens its governance structure, expands its academic and administrative capacities, protects and maximizes the productive use of its assets and landholdings, and grants fiscal incentives necessary to support its educational mission. It likewise provides safeguards to ensure transparency, accountability, and 1 responsible stewardship of university resources while preserving the institution's academic independence and public character. By elevating and strengthening PUP as the National Polytechnic University, the State invests in a strategic institution capable of producing highly skilled professionals, advancing applied research, promoting technological innovation, supporting industrial development, and expanding educational opportunities for millions of Filipinos. This measure is expected to contribute significantly to nation-building by cultivating a globally competitive workforce equipped to meet the demands of the twenty-first century economy. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES OFFICE IN ALL PROVINCES, CITIES, AND MUNICIPALITIES, PROVIDING FOR PERMANENT PLANTILLA POSITIONS, ENVIRONMENTAL ENFORCEMENT UNITS, ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE AUDITS, AND DEDICATED LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUNDS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution declares that the State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature. In pursuit of this constitutional mandate, Congress enacted various environmental laws, including Republic Act No. 9003 or the “Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000,” Republic Act No. 8749 or the “Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999,” Republic Act No. 9275 or the “Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004,” and Republic Act No. 9729 or the “Climate Change Act of 2009.” In the landmark case of Oposa v. Factoran, the Supreme Court eloquently affirmed the doctrine of intergenerational responsibility, recognizing the duty of the present generation to protect the environment for “generations yet unborn.” The Court declared that the right to a balanced and healthful ecology is so basic that it “need not even be written in the Constitution for they are assumed to exist from the inception of humankind.” This principle underscores the urgent need to institutionalize effective and accountable environmental governance mechanisms at the local level to ensure that natural resources are preserved, protected, and sustainably managed for present and future Filipinos. Despite the existence of these landmark environmental laws, implementation at the local government level remains weak and inconsistent. Many provinces, cities, and municipalities still lack permanent and properly staffed environment offices capable of effectively enforcing environmental laws, managing solid waste, protecting watersheds and coastal resources, regulating extractive activities, and implementing climate adaptation and disaster resilience programs. 1 In many local government units (LGUs), environmental functions are merely assigned as additional duties to existing offices or personnel without specialized expertise, technical support, or institutional continuity. As a result, environmental governance suffers from fragmented implementation, poor enforcement, inadequate planning, and limited accountability. The increasing threats posed by climate change, improper waste disposal, flooding, deforestation, water pollution, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation underscore the urgent need to institutionalize permanent Local Environment and Natural Resources Offices in all provinces, cities, and municipalities nationwide. This measure seeks to establish and institutionalize permanent Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Offices (PENROs) and Municipal/City Environment and Natural Resources Offices (MENROs/CENROs) in the entire country, provide for plantilla positions with minimum qualification standards, create dedicated environmental enforcement units, mandate annual environmental performance audits, and establish dedicated local environmental funds to ensure sustained implementation of environmental programs and policies. By strengthening local environmental governance and institutional capacity, this proposed measure aims to empower LGUs to become more proactive, accountable, and effective stewards of the environment and natural resources for present and future generations. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JAMES “JOJO” ANG JR.
