label: HB 9601
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming economies, institutions, and daily life across the globe. From automated customer service systems to advanced data analytics, AI influences sectors such as healthcare, education, finance, agriculture, defense, governance, and creative industries. As this technology continues to evolve, it presents both significant opportunities and serious challenges that require thoughtful consideration. This proposed measure, entitled “An Act Promoting the Development and Regulation of Artificial Intelligence in the Philippines,” establishes a comprehensive national framework to guide the growth, governance, and responsible use of AI. It seeks to encourage innovation and technological advancement, while proactively addressing emerging risks and challenges. The bill ensures that AI development and deployment are conducted in a manner that is ethical, accountable, and consistent with the values, welfare, and long-term interests of the Filipino people. While there are clear advantages of AI in certain sectors of industry such as healthcare, science, SME and MNC businesses, we must not outweigh the advantages against the disadvantages of AI. Job displacement is a growing concern with the proliferation of AI usage in private and public sectors. Privacy and Data protection concerns loom as AI systems require heavily on large datasets, often containing sensitive personal information on real people. Weak safeguards on these datasets may result in misuse, breaches or surveillance risks. AI can be used to create sophisticated cyberattacks, deepfakes, and automated misinformation campaigns, potentially undermining and interfering with democratic institutions and public trust. Artificial Intelligence is neither inherently beneficial nor inherently harmful, its impact depends largely on governance, and regulation. Philippine policy must strike a balance between fostering innovation and protecting citizens from harm. A clear regulatory framework, anchored in transparency, accountability, data protection, and human oversight can help ensure that AI serves the public well while mitigating its risks. The proposed measure creates the Artificial Intelligence Development Authority (AIDA), a dedicated body mandated to lead the formulation and execution of a comprehensive National Artificial Intelligence Strategy. This strategy will advance research and innovation, strengthen AI-driven industries, and equip the Filipino workforce with the necessary skills to compete in an increasingly technology-driven economy. In addition to its developmental mandate, AIDA shall exercise regulatory oversight over the creation and deployment of AI systems within the country, ensuring that such technologies adhere to standards of transparency, accountability, safety, and responsible use. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this measure is earnestly sought. label: HB 9602
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE LASTING POWER OF ATTORNEY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 1919 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 386, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING FOR ITS REGISTRATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution, under Article XV, Section 1, recognizes the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation and mandates the State to strengthen its solidarity and actively promote its total development. Furthermore, Article XIII, Section 11 requires the State to adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development. However, our current civil laws fail to protect families during one of their most vulnerable moments: the mental incapacitation of a family member due to advanced age, dementia, Alzheimer’s disease, coma, severe stroke and the like. While a Power of Attorney (POA) is commonly used to authorize another person to act on one’s behalf, under the New Civil Code of the Philippines, a contract of agency (such as a Power of Attorney) is strictly and automatically extinguished upon the insanity or incapacity of the principal. In effect, families who need continuing POA after a family member’s incapacity often have no option but to resort to special proceedings. One such proceeding is a judicial guardianship under Rule 93 of Rules of Court, which involves court processes, time, expense, and documentary requirements that can be difficult and time consuming during emergencies. This creates a harsh legal paradox: at the moment a person becomes incapacitated and desperately needs their trusted agent to manage their medical bills, bank accounts, and properties, the law strips the agent of all authority. Meanwhile in countries such as Singapore, continuing legal authority over a family member’s finances after incapacity are still honored. In Singapore, this legal tool is referred to as a “Lasting Power of Attorney” or LPA. This tool does not give the trustee full control over the principal’s finances, but rather, allows the principal to give specific directions and financial access during incapacity for the principal’s medical care and financial family obligations. The LPA will only enforce the directives explicitly listed by the principal so as to avoid abuse and exploitation during incapacity. This tool allows the family more financial security and decision-making power in times of crisis, especially in cases where the incapacitated individual is the patriarch, matriarch, spouse or breadwinner of the family. The Philippines has no equivalent national framework that is specifically designed to keep authority legally effective upon incapacity, while also ensuring safeguards against abuse towards the principal. This bill seeks to introduce the "Lasting Power of Attorney" (LPA) into Philippine jurisprudence. Patterned after the successful legal frameworks in Singapore and the United Kingdom, this measure will allow any person of legal age and sound mind to proactively appoint a trusted person (an Agent) to make decisions on their behalf concerning their Personal Welfare and/or Property and Affairs, should they lose mental capacity in the future. By amending Article 1919 of the Civil Code and creating a secure National LPA Registry under the Department of Justice, this bill empowers Filipinos to plan for their future, protects incapacitated individuals from exploitation, and spares their families from unnecessary emotional and financial distress. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 9604
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE "EMERGENCY FILIPINO SIGN LANGUAGE" (EFSL), AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11106 OR THE "FILIPINO SIGN LANGUAGE ACT", PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Ponggay Sambajon, was a 24-year old pregnant and hearing-impaired young Filipina, who was studying at La Salle - St. Benilde, an institution which features the School of Deaf Education and Applied Studies (SDEAS) and the Benilde Deaf School (BDS). In April 2025, then seven (7) months pregnant, she found herself prematurely bleeding while attending an end-of- semester gathering held in the campus. She was initially taken by her colleagues to the campus clinic, but the clinic personnel recommended that she be brought to a hospital. So, emergency responders were contacted and an ambulance arrived. However, what would have been a standard procedure for a medical emergency response team ended up being a complicated procedure due to the lack of medical personnel with training in Filipino Sign Language. The arduous and long-drawn emergency medical response experience resulted in Ponggay's placement in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), but not without the help of her relatives who intervened as interpreters between the patient and the medical crew. Without reliable interpreters of FSL, the medical staff would not have been able to properly address the emergency. In 2018, Republic Act No. 11106 or "The Filipino Sign Language Act" was enacted to establish the Filipino Sign Language or FSL as the official sign language for the government in all transactions involving Filipinos who are hearing- and speech-impaired. Section 8 of the Act mandates that "State hospitals and all health facilities shall take steps to ensure access of the Filipino deaf to health services, including the free provision of FSL interpreters and accessible materials upon request of deaf patients, or individuals who have family members who are deaf." Ponggay's medical emergency, exposes a gap in RA No. 11106 that needs to be addressed in order for emergency responders of health, security, fire or disaster emergencies, to be able to communicate with hearing and speech impaired Filipinos, especially at the most critical moments. The existing law does not accommodate highly stressful situations when there is no time to request for an FSL interpreter and life or death hangs in the balance. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), the estimated number of Filipinos with hearing difficulty stood at 1,784,690 in 2020. R.A. 11106 aligned our national laws with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, which aimed to promote, protect, and ensure the full and equal enjoyment of all human rights and fundamental freedoms of persons with disabilities. Studies and reports from the World Health Organization (WHO) further show that persons with disabilities are disproportionately affected during emergencies due to barriers in communication, mobility, and access to services. This bill introduces amendments to RA No. 11106 to include the following: (1) the formulation and formalization of a standard "Emergency FSL" that addresses the key emergencies, namely, medical, security, disaster, fire and security, (2) the institutionalization of "text message" in the 911 emergency response protocol, and (3) the requirement of all emergency responders to undergo a certified training for "Emergency FSL" prior to becoming an emergency responder. It must be noted that we are not requiring a full range of FSL communication skills but a targeted range of FSL skills to address specific questions and answers expected during emergency situations and rescue operations. By removing FSL communication barriers, this measure promotes equal protection, inclusivity, and dignity, ensuring that no Filipino is left behind in times of crisis. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. RICHARD I. label: HB 9620
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE POLYTECHNIC UNIVERSITY OF THE PHILIPPINES AS THE NATIONAL POLYTECHNIC UNIVERSITY, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1341, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The right of every Filipino to quality education is not merely a political aspiration but a solemn constitutional obligation. Section 1, Article XIV of the Constitution declares that “the State shall protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and shall take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all.” Section 5(2) of the same Article guarantees academic freedom in all institutions of higher learning, while Section 5(5) affirms that the State shall assign the highest budgetary priority to education. These provisions are not decorative clauses but are enforceable obligations binding upon every branch and instrumentality of government. When the State fails to equip its public universities with the governance structures, the resources, and the institutional autonomy they need to fulfill their mission, it does not merely fall short of a policy goal but violates a constitutional duty owed to every Filipino child who cannot afford to go anywhere else. It is in the light of this constitutional imperative that the modernization of the Charter of the Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP) becomes not only warranted but urgent. The PUP traces its origins to the Manila Business School, established in 1904, and has since grown into one of the largest and most consequential public universities in the nation, with campuses spanning the National Capital Region and multiple provinces serving students from the most underserved communities in the country. Its current foundational charter, Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1341 enacted on April 1, 1978, has, for nearly five decades, served as the legal foundation of an institution that has produced principled, competent, and socially committed graduates Page 1 of 24 who now serve in every government agency, in every vital industry, and in countless communities across the archipelago and beyond. Surveys on the most preferred graduates by employers in the Philippines consistently place PUP alumni at the very top of the list, a testament not to privilege or resources but to the resilience and excellence of a university that has done more with less than almost any comparable institution in the country. Yet a decree conceived in 1978 cannot govern a university that must compete in the 21st century and beyond. PD 1341 was crafted in an era that could not have anticipated the global dominance of artificial intelligence, the imperative of computational literacy across all sectors of the economy, the depth of digital transformation reshaping labor markets, or the scale of demand for inclusive, flexible, and technology-enabled higher education. The result is an institutional framework that, however admirable at its inception, has become structurally inadequate. PUP's branches and campuses operate under chronic underfunding, with a documented funding gap of over ₱9 billion in 2026 alone. Several campuses face the very real threat of closure due to the absence of sustained national government support. Faculty positions remain unfilled. Infrastructure remains incomplete. Research capacity remains constrained. These are not administrative inconveniences but are failures of the State to honor its constitutional promise to the working families whose children fill PUP's classrooms. Legislative efforts to correct this injustice have spanned successive Congresses. In 2019, President Rodrigo Duterte vetoed a bill that sought to designate PUP as the National Polytechnic University. In 2025, President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. vetoed a similar measure, once again deferring what had become an overdue legislative commitment. These repeated vetoes have not extinguished the imperative for reform, but rather sharpened it. Every day that PUP operates as an underfunded institution under its old charter is another day its students learn in deteriorating facilities, its faculty serve without adequate support, and its campuses in the provinces remain vulnerable to the political vagaries of annual appropriations. The passage of this bill is, therefore, not a matter of institutional prestige but a matter of constitutional fidelity and social justice. The State must not allow yet another generation of Filipinos to bear the cost of inaction. This measure seeks to repeal Presidential Decree No. 1341 and enact the Revised Polytechnic University of the Philippines Charter, thereby strengthening PUP as the National Polytechnic University and providing it with the governance architecture, institutional autonomy, fiscal security, and expanded mandate that its students, its faculty, and the nation's working class have long deserved. The reforms introduced by Page 2 of 24 this bill are substantive, structural, and long overdue. They address, in a direct and concrete manner, the deficiencies that decades of delay have allowed to accumulate. Before describing those reforms, however, it is necessary to address the misinformation that has too often distorted public discourse on measures of this kind, and that has been weaponized, whether through ignorance or bad faith, to obstruct progress for the University. To begin with, this bill does not rename the PUP, since the designation of National Polytechnic University confers an elevated mandate and nothing more, functioning in precisely the same manner as the national university status of the University of the Philippines and the national engineering university designation of Batangas State University. PUP will remain PUP. Equally without basis is the claim that this bill abolishes social science programs, humanities, or any existing academic offering, given that the proposed charter's enumeration of disciplines is deliberately broader than the one it replaces, contains no enrollment ratio requirements, and imposes no prohibition on non-technical programs. label: HB 9639
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FREE CASKET AND DISCOUNTS ON FUNERAL SERVICES FOR INDIGENT AND EXTREMELY POOR FAMILIES, TO BE IMPLEMENTED BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipinos are known for their nurturing nature and are admired globally for their respect and compassion especially for the sick family members. Even when family members pass away, their relatives still see to it that the deceased is given a decent funeral and the customary wake. However, many extremely poor and indigent families had to make difficult choices during their time of loss due to the exorbitant costs of caskets and funeral services. At some point, the bereaved families who are facing financial constraints had to make do with the confined spaces of their homes, available spaces in barangay halls or even the sidewalks in the barangays. To aid the indigent and extremely poor families, the State shall mandate the local government units to provide free caskets and discounts on funeral services to ensure that those who are financially challenged would still be able to provide dignified burial for their loved ones. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. LAZATIN, JR. label: HB 9640
title: AN ACT GRANTING FREE GLAUCOMA SCREENING FOR SENIOR CITIZENS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Glaucoma is one of the leading causes of blindness in the Philippines and has affected an estimated number of over one (1) million Filipinos. 1 Unfortunately, only about half of these cases are diagnosed and many patients seek treatment only when the disease is already in advanced stages. This may be attributed to limited awareness about glaucoma symptoms, lack of access to eye care services, and the expensive cost of diagnostic tests and treatment.2 It may also be due to the belief that poor vision and other eye-related problems are part of aging. With the proposed bill, the State seeks to establish a program for free glaucoma screening for senior citizens to curb the increasing number of blind individuals, especially the indigent who could not afford costly eye treatment, and to afford our elderly citizens a chance to enjoy the beauty of their environment and explore freely without the need for assistance of a relative or caregiver. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. label: HB 9641
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PUBLIC CREMATORIUMS AND PROVIDING FREE BURIAL AND CREMATION SERVICES FOR SENIOR CITIZENS AND PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipinos are known for our close- knit family ties, which is why the death of our relatives often bring profound grief. However, during these crucial times, it is rather difficult for most Filipinos to properly mourn the passing of a family member especially for those whose resources were already depleted due to medical expenses and could no longer afford to cover funeral and burial services for the deceased. In an effort to ease the burden of the surviving family, many local government units are already offering free caskets and those maintaining public cemeteries/ mortuaries are giving discounts on burial and crematory services. Further, Republic Act No. 9994, otherwise known as the Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010, and Republic Act No. 10754, which expanded the benefits and privileges of PWDs, recognize funeral and burial services among the covered entitlements. In Republic v. Pryce Corporation, Inc., the Supreme Court further clarified that “funeral and burial services” should be construed liberally in favor of senior citizens, and that interment services form part of the covered services. These measures reflect the State’s policy to support vulnerable sectors and promote social justice. However, discounts by themselves do not ensure actual access. In many localities, families still face high out-of-pocket expenses and the absence of a public crematorium option. This proposed measure seeks to address this concern and mandates the establishment of public crematoriums and the provision of free burial and cremation services for senior citizens and persons with disabilities. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. LAZATIN, JR. title: AN ACT GRANTING THE BUKIDNON II ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC. (BUSECO) A FRANCHISE TO CONSTRUCT, INSTALL, ESTABLISH, OPERATE, OWN, MANAGE AND MAINTAIN DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS FOR THE CONVEYANCE OF ELECTRIC POWER TO THE END-USERS IN THE MUNICIPALITIES OF MANOLO FORTICH, LIBONA, SUMILAO, MALITBOG, BAUNGON, IMPASUG-ONG, MALAYBALAY, TALAKAG, LANTAPAN, AND CABANGLASAN IN THE PROVINCE OF BUKIDNON
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to reliable, affordable, and sustainable electricity is indispensable to economic growth, social development, and the improvement of the quality of life of Filipinos. Electric cooperatives play a critical role in advancing rural electrification and ensuring that communities, including those in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, have access to dependable electric power services. The Bukidnon II Electric Cooperative, Inc. (BUSECO) has been at the forefront of providing electric distribution services to a substantial portion of the Province of Bukidnon. BUSECO’s franchise area presently covers the municipalities of Manolo Fortich, Libona, Sumilao, Malitbog, Baungon, Impasug-ong, Talakag, Lantapan, and Cabanglasan, as well as Malaybalay City. Through the years, BUSECO has significantly contributed to the province’s socio-economic development by energizing households, educational institutions, health facilities, agricultural enterprises, commercial establishments, and industries. This proposed measure grants BUSECO a franchise for a period of twenty-five (25) years to construct, install, establish, operate, own, manage, and maintain distribution systems for the conveyance of electric power to end-users within its service area. It likewise ensures that the cooperative remains subject to the regulatory oversight of the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC), the National Electrification Administration (NEA), and other relevant government agencies. The bill further mandates compliance with applicable laws and regulations, promotes consumer welfare, encourages employment generation, and safeguards the interests of the government and the public. The enactment of this measure will help ensure the uninterrupted delivery of electric power services to the people of Bukidnon, strengthen rural development, attract investments, generate employment opportunities, and contribute to the continued economic progress of the province and the nation. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Jose Manuel F. label: HB 9644
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA OF BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to quality healthcare at the grassroots level is a fundamental component of public health, safety, and overall community well-being. Yet, the barangay health workers (BHWs) who serve at the forefront of this delivery often lack the necessary support and protection of their own welfare. This disparity is not merely a service gap; it reflects a systemic issue in our health infrastructure that underutilizes these critical partners in development. Medical and social demands on the community require BHWs to serve as advocates, educators, and healthcare providers. Meanwhile, existing policies often fail to account for their voluntary status and the hazards they face. The result is an imbalance where those providing essential services are burdened with high responsibility but limited security. Therefore, this bill seeks to address this inequity by adopting a rational standard for those rendering primary healthcare. This approach would professionalize their services, provide mandatory honoraria and allowances, and healthcare coverages. By ensuring that BHWs are empowered and their potential is effectively harnessed, the State can better provide fair, dignified, and efficient healthcare access for all. Moreover, through the approval of this bill, we promote fairness and inclusivity towards Barangay Health Workers, taking a significant step towards ensuring that our healthcare system is responsive to the needs of all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 9645
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10121, AND TRANSFERRING THE POWER TO DECLARE A STATE OF CALAMITY IN A LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT TO THE LOCAL CHIEF EXECUTIVE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines remains highly vulnerable to typhoons, earthquakes, floods, volcanic eruptions, and other natural and human-induced disasters that place communities at risk and disrupt the delivery of essential government services. In times of calamity, the swift declaration of a state of calamity is crucial in order to immediately mobilize government resources, facilitate rescue and relief operations, and ensure the timely delivery of assistance to affected communities. Under existing law, the declaration of a state of calamity in local government units requires action by the local Sanggunian upon recommendation of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC). However, in actual emergency situations, convening the Sanggunian and securing the necessary quorum and approval may cause delays at a time when immediate government response is urgently needed. Therefore, this bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 10121 by authorizing the local chief executive to declare a state of calamity within the local government unit upon recommendation of the LDRRMC. By streamlining the declaration process, government agencies and local officials will be able to respond more rapidly and efficiently during emergencies and disaster situations. In effect, this measure should strengthen disaster response mechanisms, improve the delivery of emergency assistance, and protect the welfare and safety of communities affected by calamities and disasters. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 9646
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AN EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES SYSTEM (EMSS), CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL EMSS COUNCIL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to timely and effective emergency medical care remains a critical concern in many parts of the country, particularly in rural communities, geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, and densely populated urban centers. During accidents, disasters, sudden illnesses, and other life-threatening emergencies, delays in medical response often mean the difference between life and death. At present, emergency medical services in the Philippines are delivered through a combination of local government units, hospitals, private ambulance providers, volunteer organizations, and non-government institutions. While these entities provide invaluable service, the absence of a unified and standardized national framework has resulted in inconsistent protocols, inadequate coordination, varying levels of training among responders, and unequal access to emergency medical care across localities. Therefore, this bill seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive Emergency Medical Services System (EMSS) that will strengthen and standardize emergency response mechanisms nationwide. The proposed system aims to establish national standards for emergency medical personnel, ambulance services, dispatch centers, training programs, and emergency treatment protocols to ensure efficient, coordinated, and professional emergency response services. Ultimately, this measure aims to improve survival rates, reduce preventable deaths and disabilities, and ensure equitable access to life-saving emergency medical services for all Filipinos through a responsive, integrated, and well-coordinated national emergency medical services system. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 9647
title: AN ACT GRANTING AN ANNUAL COMPASSIONATE PAID LEAVE OF FIVE (5) DAYS TO OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES IN THE PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTORS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Workers inevitably face moments of bereavement, family crises, serious illness, and caregiving responsibilities that require time, compassion, and emotional recovery. However, many employees are often compelled to choose between attending to urgent family matters and preserving their income or employment benefits. In the absence of a dedicated compassionate leave policy, workers experiencing personal or family emergencies may suffer additional emotional and financial strain during already difficult circumstances. Compassion and humanity in the workplace are essential to the dignity of labor and the overall well-being of employees. A humane and supportive work environment allows workers to attend to critical family needs, provide care and support during times of illness or loss, and recover from emotional distress without fear of losing their livelihood. Therefore, this bill seeks to grant an annual compassionate paid leave of five (5) working days to officials and employees in both the public and private sectors. The proposed leave shall cover urgent family or personal matters of a serious or sensitive nature, including death, serious illness, medical emergencies, caregiving responsibilities, and other analogous circumstances as may be determined by appropriate government agencies. Ultimately, this bill recognizes the importance of institutionalizing compassion in the workplace as a matter of right rather than discretion. By providing clear standards and protections against discrimination or reprisal, this measure seeks to promote fairness, empathy, and mental well- being among workers across all sectors. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 9648
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROFESSIONAL REGULATION COMMISSION (PRC) SERVICE CENTER IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF IROSIN, PROVINCE OF SORSOGON, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipino professionals play a vital role in nation-building by providing essential services that contribute to the growth, safety, welfare, and development of communities. The Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), through its mandate to regulate and supervise the practice of professions in the country, ensures that Filipino professionals remain competent, qualified, and globally competitive. However, many professionals and aspiring examinees in provincial areas continue to face difficulties in accessing PRC services due to the limited number of service centers and the considerable distance they must travel to process applications, secure certifications, renew licenses, and avail themselves of other regulatory services. These challenges result in additional transportation costs, lost work opportunities, and delays in transactions. The growing number of graduates and licensed professionals further underscores the need to expand the accessibility of PRC services across the country. Establishing an additional PRC Service Center will help decongest existing offices, improve efficiency in the processing of transactions, and bring government services closer to the people, particularly those residing in underserved and geographically distant areas. Therefore, this bill seeks to establish a Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) Service Center in the Municipality of Irosin, Province of Sorsogon, in order to provide more accessible, efficient, and responsive services to professionals, board examinees, and the general public within the province and nearby localities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 9651
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE GROUNDS FOR DECLARATION OF NULLITY OF MARRIAGE, WHILE PRESERVING THE SANCTITY AND INDISSOLUBILITY OF MARRIAGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, SERIES OF 1987, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES", AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution lays the foundational principles for marriage and family by declaring the sanctity of family life and the indissolubility of marriage, and recognizing marriage as the cornerstone of the family and the family as the bedrock of the nation. The Constitution has, thus, imposed upon the State the duty to protect and preserve marriage and family. The Family Code of the Philippines builds on these principles, defining marriage as a special contract of permanent union between a man and a woman and providing the legal framework for its regulation. Contemporary realities, including irreparably broken unions and domestic abuse, have prompted calls for reform to current laws. This proposed Bill seeks to address these issues, while remaining faithful and aligned to the constitutional values of permanence, inviolability, indissolubility, and sacredness of marriage. Marriage is, at its core, a covenant based on free, mutual, and fully-informed consent. And marital consent must rest upon a full understanding of and the readiness to embrace the nature, responsibilities, and consequences of the marital bond. It is this kind of consent that breathes juridical life into the union; without it, there is no marriage to speak of. Many failed marriages can be traced to a defect in such consent which already existed prior to or at the time of celebration of marriage (ab initio). Often, one party entered into the union without full knowledge or understanding of the nature and significance of the act entered into, or with incomplete or lack of vital, material and correct information necessary to make the lifelong commitment. A defect in marital consent may arise from the unique personal makeup of one or both parties, or from influences in their physical or social environment, as well as a multitude of life circumstances and events that shape their identities and decisions—in particular, their decision to marry. When someone enters marriage under such conditions, their consent cannot truly be considered free, mutual, or fully informed. Often, the consequences of this deficiency only become apparent later, manifesting as ongoing breakdowns in the relationship or an inability to fulfill the essential duties and responsibilities of marriage. Under existing laws, the grounds for declaration of nullity of marriage remain restrictive, offering limited remedy for marriages that can be considered void from inception. In fact, what may appear as a mere “defect” in consent is, in substance, a total absence of such consent. This defect does not merely make the marriage voidable, but void ab initio because consent is completely absent from the start. It is precisely this kind of consent that defines the situations addressed by the proposed amendments. This bill seeks to broaden the legal grounds for declaring certain marriages null and void from the outset, while remaining anchored on the constitutional commitment to protect the sanctity and indissolubility of marriage and the principle that family is the very cornerstone of our nation. In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this measure is earnestly requested. RUFUS B. RODRIGUEZ MAXIMO B. RODRIGUEZ, JR. label: HB 9652
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A COMPREHENSIVE AND REGULATED CHILD-MINDING FACILITY NETWORK IN EVERY CITY AND MUNICIPALITY NATIONWIDE, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The contemporary Philippine socioeconomic landscape presents a profound structural paradox for families. While the nation frequently ranks as a leading performer in global gender equality indexes, macroeconomic pressures, severe regional climate and energy disruptions, and unprecedented inflationary dynamics have fundamentally reshaped household stability. Data indicates that Filipino families face an average annual living expenditure that demands both parents participate actively in the labor force just to cross baseline poverty thresholds. Despite this dual-income necessity, the structural support system for childcare remains severely fragmented, imposing what economists define as a heavy and persistent motherhood penalty. According to empirical assessments compiled by the International Labor Organization (ILO) and localized labor indicators, married women in the Philippines are roughly 40% less likely to successfully transition into or remain within the formal labor force compared to single women. This disparity is directly driven by the lopsided distribution of caregiving. Data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) shows that women across the archipelago spend nearly double the hours on unpaid care and domestic workloads as men, which remains as a burden that has intensified due to recent localized utilities and economic bottlenecks. The existing Barangay Day Care Center system, governed by Republic Act No. 6972 and Republic Act No. 10410, shall be distinguished from the proposed Child-Minding Facilities (CMFs). While Day Care Centers are vital community assets, they were never legally or operationally designed to support full-time working parents. Traditional day care centers focus strictly on early childhood education and pre-kindergarten preparation for children aged 3 to 5 years old. Consequently, they operate on a highly abbreviated schedule of only two to four hours per session, typically requiring parents to pick up their children by midday. Furthermore, their physical layouts resemble standard classrooms with small desks and blackboards, and a single worker is frequently left to manage a massive cohort of 25 to 30 children simultaneously. The Child-Minding Facilities (CMFs) institutionalized under this measure are built as an explicit response to the dual-income care crisis, operating not as a brief educational school day, but as a full-day labor support system. The said facilities bridge the unaddressed developmental gap by expanding eligibility down to vulnerable infants and toddlers aged 6 months up to 4 years old. Operationally, CMFs are mandated to remain open for a minimum of eleven consecutive hours daily to fully mirror full-time work shifts and commuting realities. Structurally and medically, they swap out traditional classrooms for sterile infant environments equipped with dedicated, safe zones for crawling, napping, and hygienic milk preparation. Additionally, they enforce strict, 1 medically backed child-to-caregiver ratios, which ranges from 1:3 for infants up to 1:6 for older toddlers, all supervised by early-care professionals certified by TESDA. Recent structural audits by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II) in 2023 highlight severe gaps in our early childhood systems, revealing that approximately 14% of lower-income municipalities lack any functional daycare infrastructure whatsoever. Left with no viable public alternatives, low-income and informal sector working mothers are forced to rely on highly unstable, informal localized care networks, which often leaves toddlers under the supervision of older school-aged siblings or elderly relatives. This dynamic creates a damaging ripple effect, it stalls the educational progression of older children who miss school to watch younger siblings, keeps mothers trapped in low-paying, highly volatile informal or part-time jobs, and leaves infants exposed to high rates of chronic undernutrition and home hazards during their most critical windows of brain development. The proposed Bill aims to mitigate said intersectional crises by institutionalizing structured, full-shift, safe, and heavily subsidized Child-Minding Facilities (CMFs) at the municipal and city level. Transforming childcare from an isolated domestic burden into a regulated public utility directly unlocks the economic potential of millions of Filipino women, protects vulnerable single-parent households, and ensures that the lowest-income children receive institutional health, safety, and nutritional scaffolding during their foundational years. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. OMAR VINCENT S. DUTERTE HON. PAOLO Z. label: HB 9657
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING BICYCLE-FRIENDLY COMMUNITY LANES IN BARANGAY KALIGAYAHAN, QUEZON CITY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Metro Manila has long been recognized as one of the world’s megacities, with severe traffic congestion and consistently ranking among the most congested urban areas globally. Recent data from the TomTom Traffic Index (2024) continues to place Metro Manila among the slowest-moving cities in Asia, with average travel times significantly exceeding pre-pandemic levels. While temporary relief was observed during the height of COVID-19 lockdowns, congestion has since rebounded sharply with the economy's full reopening. The Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) estimates that traffic congestion in Metro Manila costs the Philippine economy approximately Php 3.5 billion daily, and, without substantial intervention, this figure is projected to increase to Php 5.4 billion per day by 2035 (JICA, “Roadmap for Transport Infrastructure Development for Metro Manila and Its Surrounding Areas,” 2014). More recent assessments suggest that actual losses may already be higher due to inflation and prolonged commute times, underscoring the need for practical and sustainable interventions. As a measure to help ease traffic congestion in Metro Manila— particularly in the Fifth District of Quezon City—this bill proposes the establishment of bicycle-friendly community lanes in Barangay Kaligayahan, Quezon City. The measure aims to promote cycling as a safe, viable, and sustainable alternative mode of transportation, while improving road safety and accessibility at the barangay level. Among the various modes of transport, cycling is widely recognized as environmentally sustainable, producing zero emissions and minimal noise. It also provides health benefits, serving as a form of regular physical activity that helps reduce stress and improve overall well-being (World Health Organization, 2020). Thus, promoting bike-friendly communities not only addresses economic losses from traffic congestion but also contributes to environmental protection and public health. With the implementation of this measure, the barangay is positioned to move toward a safer, cost-efficient, and sustainable transport system for its residents. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is urgently sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 9669
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING BICYCLE-FRIENDLY COMMUNITY LANES IN BARANGAY CAPRI, QUEZON CITY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Metro Manila has long been recognized as one of the world’s megacities, with severe traffic congestion and consistently ranking among the most congested urban areas globally. Recent data from the TomTom Traffic Index (2024) continues to place Metro Manila among the slowest-moving cities in Asia, with average travel times significantly exceeding pre-pandemic levels. While temporary relief was observed during the height of COVID-19 lockdowns, congestion has since rebounded sharply with the economy's full reopening. The Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) estimates that traffic congestion in Metro Manila costs the Philippine economy approximately Php 3.5 billion daily, and, without substantial intervention, this figure is projected to increase to Php 5.4 billion per day by 2035 (JICA, “Roadmap for Transport Infrastructure Development for Metro Manila and Its Surrounding Areas,” 2014). More recent assessments suggest that actual losses may already be higher due to inflation and prolonged commute times, underscoring the need for practical and sustainable interventions. As a measure to help ease traffic congestion in Metro Manila— particularly in the Fifth District of Quezon City—this bill proposes the establishment of bicycle-friendly community lanes in Barangay Capri, Quezon City. The measure aims to promote cycling as a safe, viable, and sustainable alternative mode of transportation, while improving road safety and accessibility at the barangay level. Among the various modes of transport, cycling is widely recognized as environmentally sustainable, producing zero emissions and minimal noise. It also provides health benefits, serving as a form of regular physical activity that helps reduce stress and improve overall well-being (World Health Organization, 2020). Thus, promoting bike-friendly communities not only addresses economic losses from traffic congestion but also contributes to environmental protection and public health. With the implementation of this measure, the barangay is positioned to move toward a safer, cost-efficient, and sustainable transport system for its residents. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is urgently sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 9674
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A RECOVERY MECHANISM FOR ERRONEOUS ELECTRONIC FUND TRANSFERS, PROVIDING REMEDIES AGAINST UNJUST ENRICHMENT, DEFINING THE RESPONSIBILITIES OF FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS AND PAYMENT SERVICE PROVIDERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In the age of instant digital payments, a single wrong digit can mean the loss of hard-earned money. While the law already rejects unjust enrichment, ordinary consumers who mistakenly transfer funds to the wrong account or mobile number are often left without a clear, prompt, and effective means of recovery. This premise is connected to the rapid growth of digital payments, mobile wallets, online banking, and instant fund transfers has made financial transactions more convenient for millions of Filipinos. With a few taps on a mobile phone, money may now be sent instantly to another person through a bank account, e-wallet, mobile number, QR code, or other digital payment channel. In many cases, the online sender discovers the mistake only after the transfer has already been completed. The sender is then left to rely on customer service escalation, which at times is very tedious, and the cooperation of the unintended recipient, or costly and time-consuming legal remedies. Under existing principles of civil law, no person should unjustly enrich himself or herself at the expense of another. Where a person receives money without legal right and by reason of mistake, the obligation to return arises. Yet, while the substantive right to recover exists, there remains no clear, fast, uniform, and accessible statutory mechanism for ordinary consumers to recover funds erroneously transferred through digital payment systems. This gap disproportionately affects workers, small entrepreneurs, farmers, fisherfolk, students, overseas Filipino families, public transport workers, and ordinary consumers who rely heavily on digital wallets and electronic fund transfers for daily transactions. Even a modest amount sent to the wrong account may be significant to a Filipino household. 1 This bill seeks to establish a fair and practical recovery and redress mechanism for erroneous electronic fund transfers. It requires covered financial institutions and payment service providers to adopt preventive safeguards, including clear transaction confirmation prompts. It also provides for a timely reporting mechanism, provisional holding of disputed funds when still available, notice to the unintended recipient, consent-based return, and a structured process for contested claims. The measure carefully balances the rights of both the sender and the recipient. It does not authorize arbitrary or automatic reversal of transactions. Instead, it provides a clear mechanism to verify the claim, protect the funds where appropriate, and return the money when the mistake is admitted, uncontested, or duly established. It also protects good-faith recipients while imposing liability on persons who knowingly retain, conceal, withdraw, transfer, or spend money that they received by mistake and without lawful right. By establishing a practical legal framework for erroneous fund transfers, this measure strengthens consumer protection, promotes trust in digital financial services, prevents unjust enrichment, and ensures that the benefits of financial technology are not undermined by the absence of accessible remedies. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 9675
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL STRATEGIC FUEL RESERVE AND THE TARGETED FUEL RELIEF PROGRAM, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines remains highly vulnerable to external shocks in the global oil market. As a net importer of crude oil and refined petroleum products, the country is directly exposed to geopolitical conflicts, disruptions in major shipping routes, supply chain instability, and sudden increases in international fuel prices. These shocks are immediately felt by Filipino households through higher fuel pump prices and, subsequently, through rising transportation, electricity, food, and basic commodity costs. Recent tensions in the Middle East and disruptions affecting key maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, underscore the urgent need for the country to strengthen its energy security. Fuel is not an ordinary commodity. It is essential to transportation, agriculture, fisheries, food logistics, power generation, emergency response, and the daily movement of goods and people. Any prolonged fuel supply disruption can therefore trigger serious economic and social consequences. This bill, which serves as the counterpart measure of Senate Bill No. 1993 filed in the Senate, seeks to establish a National Strategic Fuel Reserve to provide the country with a reliable emergency buffer against severe petroleum supply disruptions and extraordinary oil price shocks. The Reserve shall be equivalent to not less than ninety (90) days’ supply and not more than one hundred eighty (180) days’ supply, subject to the standards and mechanisms provided under the measure. The Reserve shall be released or utilized only under clearly defined circumstances, including severe supply disruptions, sharp increases in international fuel prices, a declared State of Calamity or State of Emergency, or for stock rotation, quality management, and other measures necessary to ensure the usability and readiness of the Reserve. This ensures that the Reserve will not be used as a routine market intervention tool, but as a strategic national safeguard during periods of genuine need. The bill likewise establishes a Targeted Fuel Relief Program to provide direct cash assistance or fuel vouchers, as may be appropriate, to sectors most affected by fuel supply disruptions and sharp increases in petroleum prices. These include small farmers and fisherfolk, 1 public transport and delivery drivers, micro and small enterprises engaged in fuel- dependent activities, and other vulnerable sectors to be identified in coordination with relevant government agencies. By creating a strategic fuel reserve and a targeted relief mechanism, this measure seeks to protect Filipino consumers, safeguard essential sectors, strengthen disaster and crisis preparedness, and promote greater stability in the national economy. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 9676
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD SYSTEM TO ENSURE CONTINUITY OF CARE, IMPROVE MEDICAL EFFICIENCY, AND PROMOTE UNIVERSAL HEALTH ACCESS FOR ALL FILIPINOS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Electronic health records (EHR) are essentially a consolidation of a patient’s entire health history and information, including inpatient hospitalization records, outpatient clinic visits, laboratory results, imaging reports, and records of medication prescribed and dispensed. The EHR system makes it possible to provide better overall care for the patient and improved quality of documentation and administrative efficiency. A national HER system can allow full interoperability and a seamless transmission of patients’ health information across different healthcare settings, including enhanced clinical decision-making abilities and cost- effectiveness. A National Electronic Health Record System can be another cornerstone of our Universal Health Care law. Creating it within the Philhealth system will not only help Philhealth keep track of each patient’s medical journey, but also ensure that medical insurance claims under the UHC law is not abused. It is high time that the Philippines follow this global practice which will serve to boost our medical system and will ultimately redound to the benefit of our citizenry. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. BEVERLEY ROSE A. label: HB 9677
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ANNUAL GRANT OF THE WORLD TEACHERS' DAY INCENTIVE BENEFIT FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS AND INCREASING THE AMOUNT OF THE INCENTIVE TO THREE THOUSAND PESOS Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: SECTION 1. Short Title. - This Act shall be known as the "Institutionalizing the World Teachers' Day Incentive Benefit Act" SECTION 2. Declaration of Principles. - It is the policy of the State to promote the welfare of public school teachers and improve their work incentives. SECTION 3. Annual World Teachers· Day Incentive Benefit. - There is hereby established an Annual World Teachers' Day Incentive Benefit, in the amount of Three Thousand Pesos (P3,000), which shall be given to each public school teacher not earlier than October 5 of every year, subject to guidelines to be issued by the Department of Education. SECTION 4. Appropriations. - The amount necessary to implement this Act shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act. SECTION 5. Effectivity. - This Act shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In order to give our full appreciation and recognition for our teachers, this Representation filed a House Bill proposing that October 5 of every year be declared a national working holiday in honor of our teachers. However, this proposed measure does not seem to be enough. This Representation has learned that Congress, in its wisdom, has supported the inclusion of the World Teachers Day Incentive Benefit by including it as a fund item under the Department of Education’s budget in the annual General Appropriations Act. It is therefore humbly proposed by this Representation to institutionalize the granting of the WTDIB and increasing it from Php 1,000.00 to P 3,000.00. Not only will this improve the welfare of our teachers but also reward them for their invaluable work and dedication. Thus, the approval of this bill is earnestly requested. BEVERLEY ROSE A. label: HB 9678
title: AN ACT DECLARING APRIL 25 OF EVERY YEAR AS NUEVA ECIJA FOUNDING DAY, A SPECIAL NON-WORKING HOLIDAY IN THE PROVINCE OF NUEVA ECIJA, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Known for its vast rice fields and various contribution to the field of agriculture, The Province of Nueva Ecija has long since earned its title as the “Rice Granary of the Philippines”. Now, it positions itself as a major contributor towards rice production and food security nationwide. However, its history is far from peaceful being deeply rooted in the courage, industry, and the enduring spitir of its people. Historically, the province was established by virtue of a superior decree issued under Governor-General Rafael María de Aguilar on April 25, 1801. It was originally a corregimiento or a military district named after the Spanish City of Écija being composed of Upper Pampanga and certain settlements of Tayabas. Various records has also shown its active participation in the fight for the country’s independence and freedom from the Spanish reign. During 1896, thousands of Novo Ecijanos took up arms and joined the revolution for the country’s freedom and independence. This was later known as the “The First Cry of Nueva Ecija” or “Ang Unang Sigaw ng Nueva Ecija”. This act of defiance against our oppressors became the Province’ legacy. Being regarded as one of the first eight provinces to rise against the Spanish reign, the Province is immortalized as one of the eight rays of the sun in the Philippine National Flag. Despite its valuable contributions then and now as well as its rich culture and history, the province has yet to formally commemorate its true founding date. Realizing the need to establish the true birth of the Province with both certainty and finality, a historical research initiative was conducted from 2013 under the leadership of Governor Aurelio “Oyie” Matias Umali. After three years of arduous investigation, examination, and verification, from various historical records, it has been confirmed that Nueva Ecija was indeed founded on April 25, 1801. Subsequently, this finding was then confirmed by the National Historical Commission on October 24, 2025 through its Chairperson, Regalado Trota Jose, Jr. Later on, the Office of the President, by virtue of Proclamation No. 1211, s. Republic of the Philippines House of Representatives Quezon City, Metro Manila 2026, April 25, 2026 was declared a special non-working day in the Province of Nueva Ecija to celebrate its Founding Anniversary. To pay homage to the Province’ rich culture, valuable contribution to history, and its continued support towards food security, the bill aims to declare April 25 of every year as Nueva Ecija Founding Day. Additionally, it aims to designate the said day as a special non-working holiday in the Province of Nueva Ecija allowing Novo Ecijanos to commemorate its founding, participate in civic and cultural activities, honor the sacrifice of those who fought for freedom, and to strengthen the community’s shared identity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MARIO O. label: HB 9679
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING PROJECT CHERISH OF THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution of the Philippines provides an unequivocal mandate: that the State shall promote social justice and give priority to the needs of the underprivileged, the sick, the elderly, the disabled, and the marginalized. The same living document affirms the dignity of every human and guarantees full respect for human rights, mandating Congress to give highest priority to enacting measures that protect our people by equitably distributing wealth and public resources for the common good. Children with disabilities represent among the most vulnerable members of Philippine society. Yet for too long, they and their families have navigated their daily realities without adequate government support, denied not by lack of law or rights but by absence of appropriate and accessible public programs. Recognizing the opportunity to help the families of children with disabilities, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) took the life-saving initiative by launching the Community-based Holistic Early Response and Intervention for Children with Disabilities, also known as Project CHERISH. Project CHERISH provides financial assistance, therapy access, and rehabilitation support for children with disabilities and their families. Each participating family-beneficiary receives a monthly disability support package of up to Ten Thousand Pesos (P10,000), covering basic needs, healthcare, therapy, and caregiver training. The program also provides a graduated monthly disability allowance ranging from Two Thousand Pesos (P2,000) to Ten Thousand Pesos (P10,000) based on assessed need, to defray costs related to healthcare, therapy, education, and transportation. Social justice is neither a slogan nor an abstraction but a concrete and operative directive requiring affirmative State action in favor of those who are disadvantaged. The institutionalization of Project CHERISH as a permanent national program is one such affirmative act aiming to transform a commendable program into an enduring public commitment, ensuring that benefits and beneficiaries are not contingent on budget cycles or administrative discretion but guaranteed by law. A society that neglects its children with disabilities and the families who sacrifice daily to care for them falls short of its own highest ideals. The institutionalization of DSWD’s Project CHERISH will ensure that the promise of an inclusive society is not merely dictated in law, but ultimately realized in homes, barangays, and communities across the nation. label: HB 9680
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SALE, DISTRIBUTION, AND PROMOTION OF FLAVORED VAPOR PRODUCTS TO MINORS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The increasing prevalence of vaping among children and adolescents has become a growing public health concern in the Philippines. While vapor products were originally introduced as alternatives for adult smokers, the proliferation of flavored variants, such as fruit, candy, dessert, and beverage flavors, has made these products especially appealing to minors, leading to early nicotine addiction and long-term health risks. Numerous studies and health authorities, including the Department of Health, have warned that nicotine exposure during adolescence can impair brain development, increase susceptibility to addiction, and serve as a gateway to conventional smoking. Despite existing laws regulating tobacco and vapor products, the availability and aggressive marketing of flavored vape products continue to undermine efforts to protect minors from harmful substances. This proposed measure seeks to address this gap by specifically prohibiting the sale, distribution, and promotion of flavored vapor products to minors. By focusing on flavors that are designed to attract younger consumers, the bill reinforces the State’s duty to safeguard the health and welfare of children without unduly restricting adult access to regulated products. The measure also strengthens accountability among retailers and online sellers by requiring strict age verification and imposing graduated penalties for violations. In doing so, it complements existing laws such as Republic Act No. 9211, Republic Act No. 11467, and Republic Act No. 11900, and ensures that the protection of minors remains paramount in the regulation of vapor products. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 9681
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA OF BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Barangay Health Workers (BHWs) are the backbone of the Philippine health care system. They are the first point of contact between government healthcare providers and ordinary Filipinos, especially the poor, the elderly, pregnant women, children, and those living in remote and underserved communities. In times of public health emergencies, disasters, outbreaks, and daily health concerns, BHWs are our frontliners and first responders, conducting house-to-house visits, monitoring illnesses, assisting in maternal and child care, disseminating life-saving health information, and facilitating immediate access to health services. However, despite the critical nature of their work, BHWs remain among the most under-recognized, under-protected, and under-compensated health workers in the country. This bill seeks to establish the Magna Carta of Barangay Health Workers to fully recognize their indispensable role in safeguarding the health, safety, and welfare of our communities. It declares as a policy of the State the promotion of the welfare and well-being of BHWs as essential partners in development and as vital actors in achieving universal health care and national health goals. The measure provides clear definitions, registration, and accreditation mechanisms to professionalize BHW services while maintaining their community-based and volunteer-driven character. It establishes a national registry to ensure proper identification, validation, and coordination of BHWs across all levels of government. It also mandates a reasonable ratio of BHWs to households, ensuring that every barangay has sufficient first responders who can immediately address health concerns at the grassroots level. Recognizing the risks BHWs face in the performance of their duties, exposure to disease, emergencies, and hazardous conditions, this bill seeks substantial increases in their grant of incentives and benefits. These include honoraria, hazard pay, subsistence and transportation allowances, health and insurance benefits, leave privileges, retirement incentives, legal assistance, and access to education and career advancement. These provisions are not mere privileges but are necessary forms of protection and compensation for frontliners who routinely place themselves at risk in service of our kababayans. The Magna Carta for BHWs is a declaration that all Filipinos' health, safety and well-being are of paramount importance. Let us give our BHWs their well-deserved recognition and empower them as medical professionals, respected leaders of our communities, and ultimately, lifesavers. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 9688
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY, PEOPLE’S PARTICIPATION, COMMUNITY MONITORING, AND LOCAL REVENUE SHARING IN THE FREEPORT AREA OF BATAAN, ENHANCING PARTICIPATORY GOVERNANCE AND COMMUNITY SAFEGUARDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9728, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11453, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “FREEPORT AREA OF BATAAN (FAB) ACT OF 2009”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution unequivocally recognizes the vital role of the people in governance and mandates the State to uphold transparency, accountability, social justice, environmental protection, and the participation of citizens in matters affecting their lives and welfare. Article II, Section 23 declares that the State shall “encourage non-governmental, community-based, or sectoral organizations that promote the welfare of the nation,” while Article XIII, Section 16 further provides that the “right of the people and their organizations to effective and reasonable participation at all levels of social, political, and economic decision-making shall not be abridged.” Complementing these constitutional guarantees are the State policies under Article II promoting full public accountability, the protection of labor, and the preservation of a balanced and healthful ecology for present and future generations. These constitutional principles are especially significant in the governance and administration of the Freeport Area of Bataan (FAB), which has emerged as one of the country’s major industrial, logistics, and investment hubs under Republic Act No. 9728, otherwise known as the “Freeport Area of Bataan (FAB) Act of 2009,” as amended by Republic Act No. 11453. Through these laws, the Authority of the Freeport Area of Bataan (AFAB) has been vested with broad regulatory, administrative, developmental, and quasi-governmental powers intended to accelerate economic growth, attract investments, and strengthen industrial development in the Province of Bataan. Page 1 of 13 While these expanded powers are intended to advance national development, they likewise heighten the need for stronger democratic safeguards, meaningful community participation, and institutional accountability. Large-scale industrial and infrastructure projects within economic zones often generate profound social, environmental, and economic consequences for workers, local communities, fisherfolk, informal settlers, and Indigenous Peoples. In the absence of effective transparency and participatory mechanisms, development projects may lead to displacement, labor exploitation, environmental degradation, social conflict, and erosion of public trust. Worse, communities directly affected by such projects are frequently excluded from decision-making processes despite bearing the long-term consequences of these developments. At present, there remains no comprehensive statutory mechanism within the FAB governance framework that institutionalizes the participation of civil society organizations, affected communities, labor groups, and other stakeholders in project review, monitoring, and grievance redress. Existing laws primarily focus on expanding the administrative and regulatory powers of the AFAB without establishing corresponding participatory structures capable of ensuring that development remains equitable, transparent, and socially accountable. Consequently, consultations are often discretionary, monitoring mechanisms are fragmented, and grievance systems remain inaccessible or inadequate for ordinary citizens and workers. This measure seeks to address these longstanding gaps by institutionalizing participatory governance, transparency mechanisms, and community accountability systems within the FAB. Central to this reform is the recognition that people’s participation is not merely symbolic consultation but an essential component of democratic governance and sustainable economic development. When communities are given meaningful opportunities to participate in decisions affecting their livelihoods, land, environment, and welfare, development becomes more stable, inclusive, and legitimate. Ultimately, this measure recognizes that genuine development cannot be measured solely by investment inflows or infrastructure expansion. Economic growth that excludes workers, disregards community welfare, weakens environmental protections, or silences public participation cannot be considered sustainable or just. Development must be people-centered, transparent, and accountable to those whose lives are directly affected by it. By institutionalizing participatory governance mechanisms within the FAB, this bill seeks to balance economic development with social justice, environmental Page 2 of 13 stewardship, labor protection, and democratic accountability. It affirms the constitutional principle that governance must remain accountable to the people and that those most affected by development must never be excluded from decisions shaping their future. In solidarity with the working class, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ELIJAH R. label: HB 9691
title: AN ACT MANDATING FULL DISCLOSURE OF GOVERNMENT EXPENDITURES THROUGH AN OPEN, SECURE, AND TECHNOLOGY-NEUTRAL DIGITAL PLATFORM WITH MECHANISMS FOR REAL-TIME PUBLIC ACCESS, DATA INTEGRITY, AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN THE USE OF PUBLIC FUNDS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to modernize fiscal transparency through a unified digital portal known as the Citizen Access and Disclosure of Expenditures for National Accountability (CADENA). It is carried with the intention to provide the public with real-time access to the entire lifecycle of public funds. While existing laws and policies, including Republic Act No. 12254, otherwise known as the “E-Governance Act”, have advanced the digitalization of government processes, inconsistent reporting and publication practices across government agencies continue to weaken citizen oversight. This also limits public participation in governance and hinders the public’s ability to fully trace how public funds are allocated and utilized. This measure creates an integrated and accessible transparency framework that standardizes fiscal reporting across all national government agencies, government-owned and controlled corporations, and local government units. Through a centralized platform, the public shall be empowered to monitor government revenues, expenditures, procurement activities, contracts, and audit findings in a clear, accurate, and verifiable manner. The CADENA Act likewise mandates the proactive disclosure of public financial information to strengthen accountability, deter corruption, and promote informed public scrutiny. To ensure effective implementation and independent oversight, the measure establishes a National Budget Transparency and Accountability Council composed of representatives from relevant government agencies, civil society organizations, academe, media, and other stakeholders. A public office is a public trust. It is this trust that government institutions must uphold to remain effective, credible, and responsive to the people they serve. In this light, government must facilitate, and even encourage, meaningful citizen participation in the national budget process and ensure that every peso collected is properly accounted for. As public funds represent the Filipinos’ hard-earned contributions, they must be safeguarded with the highest degree of integrity and openness. It is transparency, accountability, and good governance that makes a public office worthy of the Filipino people’s trust. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9692
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE ADOPTION OF DIGITAL PAYMENTS FOR FINANCIAL TRANSACTIONS OF THE GOVERNMENT AND ALL MERCHANTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize secure, efficient, interoperable, and inclusive digital payment systems across the country. It further promotes the widespread adoption of digital payments in government and private sector transactions. As digital technology continues to transform commerce, banking, and public service delivery, the use of digital payments has become increasingly important and critical in improving financial inclusion, transparency, efficiency, and ease of doing business. However, despite significant advancements in financial technology, many government transactions and merchant activities in the Philippines remain heavily cash-dependent, resulting in delays, inefficiencies, higher transaction costs, and greater exposure to fraud, leakage, and corruption. Many Filipinos, particularly those in underserved and rural communities, still face limited access to safe and affordable digital financial services. Small businesses and informal sector players likewise encounter barriers in adopting digital payment systems due to inadequate infrastructure, limited digital literacy, and concerns over costs and security. At the same time, the absence of fully interoperable and standardized payment systems continues to hinder seamless financial transactions across platforms and institutions. This bill mandates the adoption of digital payment options for government collections and disbursements. It also encourages merchants to adopt digital payment capabilities, strengthens interoperability among payment systems, and promotes consumer protection, cybersecurity, and data privacy safeguards. The measure likewise supports financial inclusion initiatives to ensure that digital payment systems remain accessible, secure, and beneficial to all sectors of society, particularly micro and small enterprises that form the backbone of our economy. This transition toward a digital payments ecosystem is essential in building a more transparent, efficient, and resilient economy. This bill is created to improve government service delivery, advance economic growth in the digital age, and strengthen public trust. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9693
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE AND SUSTAINABLE REINTEGRATION PROGRAM FOR OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive and full-cycle reintegration program for Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) and returnee-OFWs. It provides for employment facilitation, skills and qualification recognition, entrepreneurship development, financial literacy, social protection, psychosocial support, and other interventions necessary to help returning OFWs successfully reintegrate into Philippine society and the local economy. Overseas Filipino Workers continue to make immense contributions to the country through their hard work, skills, and remittances. Yet many OFWs who return home after years of working abroad encounter difficulties in finding suitable employment and establishing sustainable livelihoods that are necessary for a successful transition back to their families and communities in the country. Existing reintegration initiatives, while valuable, remain fragmented and often insufficient to address the diverse needs of returning migrant workers. This measure institutionalizes a coordinated national reintegration framework by providing access to employment opportunities, entrepreneurship and financing programs, business capacity-building, financial literacy training, psychosocial counseling, social assistance, and skills recognition mechanisms. It likewise establishes a Returnee-OFWs Management Information System designed to ensure that reintegration services are accessible, responsive, and tailored to the needs of OFWs and their families. The nation owes a lasting debt of gratitude to the millions of OFWs whose hard work and sacrifices have helped sustain countless Filipino families and contributed significantly to national development. It is therefore imperative that the State provide meaningful opportunities and comprehensive support to ensure their successful return, reintegration, and continued participation in the country's growth and progress. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON.
