label: HB 9938
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9344 ALSO KNOWN AS THE "JUVENILE JUSTICE AND WELFARE ACT OF 2006," AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10630, REDUCING THE MINIMUM AGE OF CRIMINAL LIABILITY TO TEN (10) YEARS OLD AND IMPOSING OTHER PENALTIES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE At 9:20 in the morning of June 22, 2026, gunshots reverberated across San Jose National High School, a campus of over 1,600 students and 110 teachers in Tacloban City, Province of Leyte. The shooting rampage left three (3) students, two (2) female and one (1) male, dead and 20 others injured from direct gunshot wounds. This incident unfolded to be one of the deadliest school-related attacks in the history of the Philippines. What was most alarming was that the two (2) suspect shooters were minors aged fourteen (14) and fifteen (15). One of the shooters was armed with a Glock 9-millimeter pistol with two magazines of ammunition, while the other shooter brought a 38-caliber revolver, with five (5) live bullets still in the firearm. One of the shooters reportedly used the firearm of a relative who was a member of the police force. Further aggravating the public's concerns were reports that the shooters had allegedly meticulously planned the attack. Eastern Visayas Police Chief Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy revealed that the suspects began plotting as early as April or May. Furthermore, investigators noted that the 14-year old suspect was heavily exposed to GoreBox, a graphically violent mobile sandbox game. Moreover, the suspects were also aware that the existing law exempts them from criminal liability because of their age. When Republic Act No. 9344 was enacted in 2006, and even under its amending law, Republic Act No. 10630 in 2013, the world that our youth was exposed to was very different. The internet then was largely accessible only to corporate, industrial or government activities. Now it is ubiquitous across ages, themes, activities, social, economic and demographic groups. This 1 evolving landscape has altered the youth's awareness when it comes violence, its legal consequences, as well as the tactical and technical mechanics in the use of firearms. While the motive allegedly arose from cases of bullying, which is also seriously concerning, our laws have to draw the line on what constitutes a crime, especially when it involves murder, and identify who would be considered a person with sufficient criminal discernment and autonomy. Accordingly, this bill seeks to lower the age of criminal liability to ten (10) years old. Moreover, with the reduction in the minimum of age of criminal liability, this bill proposes to impose liability and penalties to parents, guardians or other influential adults who through neglect or active influence, have facilitated, motivated, or aggravated the child's criminal actions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. RICHARD I. label: HB 9939
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE MANUFACTURE, IMPORTATION, SALE, DISTRIBUTION, AND USE OF VAPORIZED NICOTINE AND NON-NICOTINE PRODUCTS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES, THEREBY REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11900
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The rapid proliferation of vaporized nicotine and non-nicotine products, commonly known as electronic cigarettes or vapes, poses a significant public health concern, particularly among the youth. Marketed as safer alternatives to conventional tobacco products, these devices in reality expose users to more harmful substances, including toxic irritants, heavy metals, and carcinogenic compounds. Such exposures are associated to cardiovascular disease, neurological impairments, nicotine dependence, and respiratory injury, including E-cigarette or Vaping Use-associated Lung Injury (EVALI), an emerging condition not observed in conventional tobacco use, which recorded its first Filipino fatality in 2024. Considering the associated major health risks, youth uptake remains particularly alarming. Flavored products, “toy-like” devices, and the expansion of online sales have lowered the barrier to youth access, facilitating early nicotine initiation and increase the risk of long-term addiction. Thus, the Department of Health (DOH) is strongly pushing for a ban on vapes and e-cigarettes, citing severe health risks like EVALI, nicotine addiction, and increased usage among youth. The DOH argues these products pose safety hazards and urges lawmakers to restrict access, treating them as dangerous, not as safer alternatives to smoking. Incidents of devices exploding, such as one involving a 17-year-old boy, have increased urgency for a ban. The DOH advises parents and guardians to be vigilant against youth accessing these products, noting that 20% of users are in the 15-20 age group, says a Facebook post by CTFK Global. Despite the enactment of Republic Act No. 11900, otherwise known as the “Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act,” enforcement challenges persist. Regulatory safeguards have been undermined by market availability to minors and persistence of illicit trade. As a result, the current framework has failed to curb youth access, prevent unregulated distribution, or mitigate growing public health burden associated with vaping. This measure is anchored on Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Constitution, which mandates the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. In furtherance of this mandate, the State is empowered to exercise its police power to enact measures necessary to safeguard public health, subject to the requirements of reasonableness and public safety. Likewise, this proposed bill is consistent with the country’s obligations under the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (WHO-FCTC), which calls State Parties to adopt effective measures to reduce tobacco use, including nicotine dependence. Given the demonstrated harms associated with vapor products, supported by the recognition that no regulatory framework will be sufficient to prevent youth access, curb illicit trade, and mitigate health risks and address the demonstrated harms of exposure to vapor products, the adoption of a comprehensive prohibition constitutes a proportionate and necessary response to protect public health. Toward this end, this measure seeks to prohibit the manufacture, importation, sale, distribution, and use of vaporized nicotine and non-nicotine products and repeal RA No. 11900 to replace this regulatory regime with a prohibition model. In light of the growing scientific evidence on the harms of vapor products and the demonstrated limitations of the existing regulatory framework, the shift toward prohibition is justified, compelling, and necessary. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this bill is earnestly sought. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Psoriasis is widely misunderstood as a mere skin condition. This perception is consequentially wrong. In truth, psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune disorder caused by a dysregulation of T-cell activity, which accelerates skin cell turnover and generates the visible plaques on the body.1 These skin lesions also silently damage the cardiovascular system, joints, and mental health of the patient.2 It is associated with serious comorbidities including psoriatic arthritis, depression, and cardiometabolic disease.3 The skin, in this sense, is not the disease. It is merely where the disease is noticed. It is estimated that between one and two million Filipinos are presently living with the disease; a possible undercount given the many undiagnosed cases outside of urban centers.4 The disease is not limited to the elderly. Studies on Filipino patients show a mean age of onset of 25.9 years old, with patients typically seeking 1 Michelle A. Lowes, Mayte Suarez-Fariñas, & James G. Krueger, Immunology of psoriasis, Annu. Globally, the number of people affected by psoriasis rose by 86% from 1990 to 2021, with psoriasis-related disability-adjusted life-years increasing from 2 million to 3.7 million over the same period.6 Left untreated, psoriasis has severe consequences. Studies found that psoriasis is associated with a 50% higher relative risk of cardiovascular disease.7 Severe cases are linked to increased rates of myocardial infarction and stroke even after adjusting for traditional risk factors.8 Psoriatic arthritis, which develops in approximately one- third of untreated patients, causes irreversible joint destruction.9 Depression is also a well-documented comorbidity and has itself been shown to further increase cardiovascular mortality in patients.10 A Philippine study at Rizal Medical Center found that 57.4% of patients already had moderate to severe psoriasis, and 63.9% reported an extremely large effect on their quality of life.11 Treatment is both lifelong and prohibitively expensive for most Filipinos. label: HB 9941
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FIVE (5) DAY SPECIAL EMERGENCY LEAVE FOR ALL WORKERS IN THE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR DIRECTLY AFFECTED BY NATURAL CALAMITIES OR DISASTER
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The vulnerability of the Philippines to natural disasters is a recurring and destructive hazard to all of us. Based on the World Risk Index 2025, the Philippines topped the list as the most disaster-prone country out of the 193 countries assessed. In the first half of 2026, our country experienced severe weather, such as the massive flooding and landslides caused by shear line in Caraga region,1 as well as series of earthquakes in various areas, such as the recent 7.8 magnitude earthquake that struck the province of Sarangani and nearby provinces.2 These natural disasters cause about millions worth of damages to infrastructure and livelihoods of our countrymen. Filipinos resiliency can only do so much. Article XIII, Section 3, 1987 Constitution guarantees the right to humane conditions of work. This mandates the protection and promotion of the welfare of the workers. Moreover, the support of the State must continue to evolve beyond reactive post-disaster response and institutionalize legal protection for the workforce. 1 https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2184753/shear-line-triggers-<loods-landslides-across-caraga-region. 2 Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology, "Primer on the 08 June 2026 Magnitude (Mw) 7.8 Offshore Sarangani Earthquake," June 8, 2026, https://www.phivolcs.dost.gov.ph/primer-on-the-08-june- 2026-magnitude-mw-7-8-offshore-sarangani-earthquake/. As such, this bill seeks to institutionalize the grant employees, whether from government sector or from private sector, a five (5) - day special emergency leave with pay. The special emergency leave may be used by the employee for several valid purposes, such as urgent repair and clean-up of damaged house; recovery from disease or illness incurred by and/or aggravated by natural disaster or calamity; being stranded in affected areas, where there are no means of transportation to ensure safe transit to and from workplace, or caring for immediate family members affected by natural disaster or calamity. Whether it is a string of six consecutive typhoons, a crushing 7.8 magnitude earthquake, or a toxic ash cloud from an active volcano, the Filipino worker is constantly on the frontlines of natural disasters. When weather disruptions or other natural disasters occur back-to-back, employees are forced to exhaust their standard yearly vacation or sick leave on initial events, leaving them completely defenseless against subsequent disasters. With the institutionalization of a 5 days special emergency leave, we are giving the Filipino workforce a humane shield to protect their homes, their health and their families first. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. CHEENO MIGUEL D. label: HB 9942
title: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 5(g) AND 11(2)(a)(4), AND INSERTING A NEW SECTION 5-A IN REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9514, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “FIRE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES OF 2008,” ESTABLISHING A RISK-BASED APPROACH AND POST-RENEWAL FIRE SAFETY COMPLIANCE MECHANISM FOR BUSINESS PERMITS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 9514, otherwise known as the “Fire Code of the Philippines of 2008,” requires the issuance of a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) as a prerequisite to the issuance of occupancy permits, business permits, and permits to operate. While this requirement serves the important objective of ensuring compliance with fire safety standards, its uniform application to all business permit applications and renewals, regardless of the degree of fire risk involved, has contributed to delays in business registration and permit processing, particularly among micro, small, and medium enterprises. This bill seeks to harmonize fire safety regulation with the principles of efficient government service delivery, ease of doing business, and risk-based regulation. Consistent with Republic Act No. 11032, or the “Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018,” the measure adopts a differentiated approach that aligns regulatory requirements with the level of fire risk presented by a business activity. Under the proposed measure, establishments classified as Medium Degree of Fire Hazard and High Degree of Fire Hazard shall continue to be required to secure an FSIC prior to the issuance of a new business permit. Establishments classified as Low Degree of Fire Hazard, however, may be issued a business permit subject to the submission of the required FSIC within forty-five (45) calendar days from permit issuance. For renewals of business permits, regardless of hazard classification, the FSIC shall no longer be a prerequisite to renewal. Establishments that do not possess a valid and subsisting FSIC at the time of renewal shall be required to secure the corresponding FSIC within forty-five (45) calendar days from the issuance of the renewed permit. Occupancy permits shall remain subject to the existing requirement of prior issuance of an FSIC. The measure further authorizes the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), in consultation with relevant government agencies and stakeholders, to establish, maintain, and periodically review a classification system for business activities based on their degree of fire hazard. Such classification shall take into account the nature of the business, the materials used or stored, occupancy characteristics, operational processes, technological developments, and other relevant risk factors, thereby ensuring that regulatory requirements remain responsive to evolving fire safety conditions. Failure to secure the required FSIC within the prescribed period shall constitute sufficient ground for the denial of the subsequent renewal of the business permit and may warrant the inclusion of the establishment in the Negative List maintained pursuant to Republic Act No. 11032 and its implementing rules and regulations, without prejudice to the imposition of penalties and other enforcement measures authorized under the Fire Code and other applicable laws. By adopting a risk-based and post-compliance framework, this measure preserves the State’s commitment to public safety while reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens, streamlining business permit processing, and fostering a more efficient and business-friendly regulatory environment. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ROLANDO M. label: HB 9948
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF REGIONAL K-9 ADOPTION SHELTERS FOR RETIRED POLICE DOGS, PROVIDING FOR ADOPTION, VETERINARY CARE, AND POST-ADOPTION MONITORING, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In June 2026, nine (9) retired Narcotic Detection Dogs (NDDs) from the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) that have served for years in the anti-illegal drug operations across the Philippines were put up for adoption. These dogs have an average age of 12 years and have retired from the service. While in the service, these dogs played key roles in anti-drug operations, including inspections in jail facilities, search-and-seizure operations, interdiction activities, and checkpoints operations in airports, seaports, and transport terminals nationwide.1 In 2022, three (3) retired canines in Cordillera were also put up for adoption. These dogs assisted in locating a missing Korean National who was hiking in Barlig, Mountain Province in 2017. They also aided in the search and rescue /retrieval operations after a landslide in Sitio Sakrang, Barangay Banawel, Natonin, Mountain Province in 2018.2 The Philippine National Police (PNP) Explosive Ordnance Disposal and Canine Group manages hundreds of trained dogs nationwide, while PDEA operates a specialized K-9 facility for narcotics detections dogs. These service canines are reliable partners of law enforcement agencies. Upon retirement, however, many are either retained by handlers or placed for adoption without a uniform, dedicated shelter-and-adoption framework that ensures standardized veterinary care, adopter screening and post-adoption monitoring. ___________________________ 1 ”PDEA puts 9 retired drug detection dogs up for adoption”. Available at https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1277521 2 ”3 retired canine cops in Cordillera up for adoption”. https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1182614 This proposed measure seeks to honor retired police dogs by institutionalizing Regional K- 9 Adoption Shelters that provide temporary housing, humane care, and a structured adoption system that prevents abuse, neglect, and exploitation, consistent with our existing laws, rules and regulations. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. LAZATIN, JR. label: HB 9949
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, TO EXCLUDE FROM GROSS INCOME CERTAIN OVERTIME PAY, NIGHT SHIFT DIFFERENTIAL PAY, AND HAZARD PAY RECEIVED BY COMPENSATION EARNERS, SUBJECT TO LIMITATIONS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Many Filipinos render services beyond the regular eight-hour workday, sometimes on holidays in hazardous and strenuous circumstances. This reflects both their dedication and hard work to their jobs and the need for additional compensation to meet daily necessities. However, under the current income tax system, overtime pay, hazard pay and night-shift differential pay, generally form part of an employee’s gross income and are subject to income taxation, except where the law expressly provides otherwise. Notably, the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC), as amended, already exempts minimum wage earners (MWEs) from income tax and likewise exempts their holiday pay, overtime pay, night shift differential pay, and hazard pay. This measure seeks to extend calibrated tax relief to compensation earners regardless of wage level by excluding from gross income certain overtime pay, night shift differential pay, and hazard pay that are mandated under applicable labor laws and regulations, subject to statutory limitations. To avoid diminishing the benefits already granted by law to MWEs, this measure likewise provides that nothing herein shall be construed to reduce or limit the existing tax exemptions of MWEs under the NIRC. This proposed amendment is intended to increase employees’ take-home pay for additional work rendered and hazardous assignments undertaken, strengthen household purchasing power, and support broader economic activity. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. LAZATIN, JR. label: HB 9951
title: AN ACT CREATING THE POSITION OF BARANGAY NUTRITION WORKER IN EVERY BARANGAY, PROVIDING INCENTIVES THERETO, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize the position of Barangay Nutrition Worker in every barangay nationwide in order to strengthen the delivery of community-based nutrition services and improve the implementation of local nutrition programs. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority and the Expanded National Nutrition Survey of the Department of Science and Technology – Food and Nutrition Research Institute, stunting, undernutrition, and micronutrient deficiencies continue to affect millions of Filipino children. These have long-term consequences on health, learning outcomes, productivity, and economic development1. Despite existing nutrition programs and services, many barangays continue to experience difficulties in delivering essential nutrition interventions due to inadequate manpower and limited institutional support at the local level. As a result, existing health personnel are often compelled to perform multiple functions beyond their designated responsibilities, thereby reducing the effectiveness and reach of community-based nutrition services. This measure creates a mandatory Barangay Nutrition Worker position in every barangay and also provides for standardized qualifications, training, supervision, allowances, and incentives. The creation of Barangay Nutrition Workers is a significant step toward safeguarding public health, reducing malnutrition, and promoting inclusive human development. The urgency of strengthening community-based nutrition interventions cannot be overstated, as the well-being of future generations depends on actions taken today. 1 Food and Nutrition Research Institute (2024). In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9952
title: AN ACT DECLARING A CLIMATE CHANGE EMERGENCY AND ENHANCING RESILIENCY AND ADAPTABILITY TO THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to declare a climate change emergency and establish a comprehensive Climate Change Resiliency and Adaptability Program to strengthen the country’s capacity to mitigate, prepare for, and adapt to the adverse effects of climate change. The measure institutionalizes a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to climate resilience by strengthening climate education, risk assessment, ecosystem protection and ecocentric innovation. The Philippines remains among the countries most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Stronger typhoons, prolonged droughts, rising sea levels, extreme heat, and increasingly unpredictable weather patterns continue to threaten lives, livelihoods, food security, water resources, public health, and critical infrastructure. While existing laws have established important frameworks for climate action and disaster risk reduction, the growing frequency and intensity of climate-related events underscore the need for stronger coordination, greater investment in resilience-building measures, enhanced public awareness, and more robust adaptation strategies. This measure mandates climate risk assessments, promotes open data-sharing systems, integrates climate resilience education across all levels of learning, and prioritizes nature-based solutions and climate-resilient infrastructure as cornerstones of the national response. Climate change is no longer a distant threat but a present reality affecting millions of Filipinos. The costs of inaction continue to rise with every disaster, every displaced family, and every community left vulnerable to environmental degradation. The State must act decisively to strengthen resilience, safeguard future generations, and protect the nation’s development gains. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9953
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A DIGITALIZED OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS (OFW) WELFARE AND MONITORING SYSTEM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a Digitalized Overseas Filipino Workers (OFW) Welfare and Monitoring System (DOWMS) under the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) to ensure the efficient delivery of services to OFWs worldwide through a secure and integrated digital system. According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, personal remittances from OFWs reached a record of more than Thirty eight billion dollars ($38.3 Billion) in 20241, highlighting their significant contribution to national development and their vital role in sustaining the Philippine economy. Despite their economic importance, many OFWs continue to experience illegal recruitment, labor exploitation, contract violations, human trafficking, abandonment, and difficulties in accessing government assistance while abroad. Recent crises, including armed conflicts, natural disasters, and economic disruptions in various host countries, have further demonstrated the need for a more responsive and coordinated system for monitoring the condition of OFWs and facilitating immediate government intervention. The absence of a unified digital platform often results in fragmented records, delayed responses, and difficulties in coordinating assistance among government agencies and foreign service posts. This measure establishes a comprehensive digital platform that will enable real-time monitoring of OFWs, streamline access to welfare services, facilitate emergency assistance and repatriation efforts, strengthen grievance mechanisms, and improve inter-agency coordination. It likewise provides safeguards to ensure compliance with data privacy and cybersecurity standards while generating valuable information that can guide policy formulation and program development for migrant workers. 1 1 BANGKO SENTRAL NG PILIPINAS (2025). Personal Remittances Reach Record High in 2024. Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. Accessed via https://www.bsp.gov.ph/SitePages/MediaAndResearch/MediaDisp.aspx?ItemId=7426 &ref=hackernoon.com. Accessed on 23 June 2026. The welfare of our Overseas Filipino Workers remains a fundamental responsibility of the State. As modern technology continues to transform public service delivery, government institutions must likewise adopt innovative systems that enhance protection, accessibility, and responsiveness for Filipinos working abroad. The establishment of a digitalized welfare and monitoring system shall not only strengthen the government’s capacity to safeguard OFWs but also reaffirms the nation’s commitment to honoring their sacrifices and protecting their rights wherever they may be. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. title: AN ACT EXPANDING HEALTH, WELLNESS, AND DIGITAL INCLUSION PROGRAMS FOR SENIOR CITIZENS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9994, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZENS ACT OF 2010”, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to expand the health benefits and wellness programs available to senior citizens by further amending Republic Act No. 9994, otherwise known as the “Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010”. It also seeks to promote digital literacy and inclusion among senior citizens, and identify sustainable funding mechanisms to support these enhanced services. The Philippines is experiencing a steady increase in its elderly population. The Philippine Statistics Authority reported that the country’s population reached 112.7 million in 2024, while demographic data continue to reflect a growing number and proportion of senior citizens nationwide.¹ As life expectancy increases, so does the demand for accessible healthcare, preventive medical services, mental health support, and programs that promote active and healthy aging. Many senior citizens continue to face barriers in accessing healthcare and social services due to limited mobility, inadequate health resources, and financial constraints. At the same time, the rapid digitalization of government services and everyday transactions has also created challenges for many older Filipinos who lack the necessary skills and confidence to navigate online systems, making them more vulnerable to exclusion, misinformation, and cyber-related risks.² This measure mandates a more comprehensive and integrated health program for senior citizens and establishes nationwide digital literacy and inclusion initiatives. It seeks to ensure that older Filipinos remain healthy, informed, connected, and empowered members of society. label: HB 9955
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION OF THE JUDICIARY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a comprehensive Judiciary Modernization Program, thereby transforming the Philippine court system into a more efficient, technologically adaptive, and accessible institution. It institutionalizes a structured, multi-year approach to modernization anchored on three core components: infrastructure development and facility modernization, equipment upgrading and acquisition, and personnel development and welfare. The judiciary is the cornerstone of a functioning democracy, and the timely and efficient delivery of justice is a fundamental right of every Filipino. Yet decades of underinvestment in court infrastructure, outdated equipment, and chronic understaffing have left many trial courts ill-equipped to meet the demands of modern litigation. Congested dockets, deteriorating court facilities, paper-based processes, and limited technological capacity have slowed the resolution of cases, eroded public trust in the justice system, and imposed disproportionate burdens on litigants who cannot afford prolonged legal proceedings. Under the Program, the national government shall acquire and dedicate land and facilities to eliminate the practice of shared salas and courtrooms among independent court branches. The program further mandates the upgrading of court technology, including modern internet connectivity, computer systems, and secure digital document submission platforms. It likewise prioritizes the welfare and security of judicial personnel, recognizing that the proper administration of justice depends on a qualified, continuously trained, and adequately protected judiciary workforce. The cost of an inefficient judiciary is borne not only in delayed verdicts, but in lives disrupted, businesses unable to enforce contracts, and communities denied equitable access to legal remedies. The modernization of the judiciary is a constitutional imperative and a moral obligation of the State toward its citizens. This measure presents a deliberate, funded, and time-bound path toward a judiciary that truly serves the Filipino people with speed, fairness, and integrity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9956
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SAFE PATHWAYS NETWORK OF BICYCLE LANES, WALKWAYS AND SLOW STREETS TO PROMOTE ACTIVE TRANSPORT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to integrate active transport infrastructure into local and national planning, and establish a nationwide Safe Pathways Network composed of bicycle lanes, walkways, and slow streets. It seeks to strengthen the support for pedestrians and cyclists, and encourages the provision of end-of-trip facilities and other complementary measures that make active mobility a practical transportation option. Traffic congestion, rising fuel costs, air pollution, and the increasing impacts of climate change continue to affect the daily lives of millions of Filipinos. In many urban centers, pedestrians and cyclists are often forced to navigate roads that were primarily designed for motor vehicles, exposing them to safety risks and limiting their mobility. Despite the growing number of Filipinos who walk or cycle for work, school, and essential activities, safe and connected infrastructure remains inadequate in many communities. This measure provides a comprehensive framework for the establishment of protected bicycle lanes, pedestrian-friendly walkways, and people-oriented slow streets. It likewise promotes the conduct of sustained information and education campaigns to foster a culture of safe and sustainable mobility. Building walkable and bikeable communities is an investment in public health, environmental sustainability, road safety, and economic productivity. The creation of safer and more accessible spaces for walking and cycling invites our citizens to a better quality of life and reaffirms the State’s commitment to the development of the overall wellbeing of the commuting public. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9959
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ETHICS ADVISORY BOARD UNDER THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE ETHICAL GOVERNANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is among the world's fastest-growing digital economies and stands to benefit significantly from AI adoption across government, business, agriculture, manufacturing, education, healthcare, and the business process outsourcing sector. However, the country currently lacks a centralized institutional mechanism dedicated to examining the ethical implications of Artificial Intelligence and providing coherent policy guidance across sectors. As AI technologies become more integrated into Philippine society, the absence of a national ethical governance framework risks creating fragmented policies, regulatory uncertainty, and insufficient safeguards for Filipino citizens. Questions surrounding algorithmic fairness, data privacy, synthetic media, automated decision-making, labor transitions, and the use of AI in public services require sustained multidisciplinary expertise that extends beyond the mandates of existing agencies. This measure seeks to establish the Philippine Artificial Intelligence Ethics Advisory Board (PAIEAB) under the Office of the President as the country's principal advisory and coordinating body on AI ethics and governance. By bringing together government agencies, industry leaders, scientists, academics, legal experts, civil society organizations, labor representatives, and the youth sector, the Board shall provide a whole-of-nation approach to addressing the opportunities and risks presented by AI technologies. The proposed Board shall formulate a National AI Ethics Framework, conduct stakeholder consultations, monitor emerging technological developments, recommend policy safeguards, and advise government institutions on issues involving transparency, accountability, fairness, human dignity, and public welfare in the deployment of AI systems. The establishment of the Philippine Artificial Intelligence Ethics Board represents an investment not only in technological governance but also in public trust. Responsible innovation requires institutions capable of ensuring that technological progress remains aligned with democratic values, human rights, and the long-term interests of the Filipino people. In consideration of the foregoing, the prompt approval of this bill is respectfully urged. HON. label: HB 9960
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FREE TERTIARY AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION AND OTHER RELATED COURSES TO THE DEPENDENT CHILDREN OF QUALIFIED INDIGENT FARMERS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide free tertiary agricultural education in State Universities and Colleges (SUCs) to the dependent children of qualified indigent farmers, along with educational support mechanisms to boost participation in agricultural careers and strengthen the country’s food security. Agriculture employs millions of Filipinos yet remains plagued by an aging workforce, youth disinterest, and deep rural poverty. The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), recorded a 27% poverty incidence among farmers in 2023 which goes well above the national average. This reality limits the ability of many farming households to send their children to college. Meanwhile, low enrollment in agriculture-related programs has created a shortage of professionals vital to the sector’s modernization. Although Republic Act No. 10931, otherwise known as the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act, covers free tuition and other school fees in SUCs, many children of indigent farmers continue to encounter financial constraints. These constraints include but are not limited to transportation, books, instructional materials, daily subsistence, and other educational expenses. As a result, many farming families remain trapped in a cycle of poverty and limited economic mobility. This measure seeks to empower farming households by providing targeted educational assistance to the dependent children of qualified indigent farmers who choose to pursue agriculture and related fields. The end goal is to aid harmer households to produce agriculturists, veterinarians, and agribusiness professionals that the country needs. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9961
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PROTECTION OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS AND THEIR DEPENDENTS AGAINST FRAUDULENT PRACTICES, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to strengthen the protection of Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) and their dependents against fraudulent schemes. It defines and penalizes fraud specifically targeting OFWs and establishes stronger enforcement and reporting mechanisms. Government agencies have repeatedly warned that OFWs are among the sectors most vulnerable to fraudulent activities. In 2024, the Department of Migrant Workers issued advisories against investment scams masquerading as legitimate financial platforms and targeting OFWs and their families through misleading advertisements, fabricated testimonials, and promises of extraordinary returns. The agency likewise reported the continuing proliferation of online recruitment scams and other fraudulent schemes that prey on Filipinos seeking economic opportunities abroad. The growing digitalization of financial services has also expanded the avenues through which scammers operate. While existing laws, like Republic Act No. 12010, otherwise known as the anti-Financial Account Scamming Act, address fraud in general, there remains a need for a more focused framework that recognizes the unique vulnerabilities of OFWs and their dependents, who are frequently targeted because of their remittance income, limited access to immediate legal remedies, and geographic separation from their families. This proposed measure establishes a comprehensive framework that specifically protects OFWs and their dependents from fraudulent practices. It imposes stronger penalties against perpetrators, including those who engage in investment fraud, cyber fraud, hidden-fee schemes, and agency collusion. It likewise establishes dedicated reporting and assistance mechanisms through a 24/7 hotline and online portal, as well as provides for a mandatory financial literacy and fraud prevention modules in pre-departure and post-arrival orientation programs. Our OFWs endure separation from their families, uncertainty, and countless personal sacrifices to provide a better future for their loved ones and contribute to the country's development. The money they earn abroad represents years of hard work and dedication that should never be stolen through deception and fraud. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9962
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING EQUAL CRIMINAL LIABILITY AND PENALTIES FOR MARITAL INFIDELITY, PROMOTING GENDER EQUALITY AND UPHOLDING THE SANCTITY OF MARRIAGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE REVISED PENAL CODE”, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to promote gender equality and uphold the sanctity of marriage. It amends Articles 333 and 334 of Republic Act No. 3815, otherwise known as “The Revised Penal Code” and establishes equal standards of criminal liability for marital infidelity regardless of sex. The existing provisions on adultery and concubinage impose different standards of liability on husbands and wives. A married woman may be prosecuted for a single act of sexual intercourse outside marriage, while a married man becomes liable only under more limited circumstances. These distinctions reflect outdated gender norms that no longer accord with the constitutional guarantee of equal protection under the law and the State’s commitment to ensuring the equality of women and men. The 1987 Constitution recognizes marriage as an inviolable social institution and affirms the fundamental equality of all persons before the law. Consistent with these principles, this measure removes discriminatory distinctions in the treatment of marital infidelity while preserving legal protections that safeguard the integrity of marriage and family life. In holding spouses to the same standard of fidelity and accountability, this bill advances fairness, strengthens respect for marriage, and aligns existing penal laws with contemporary constitutional values. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 9967
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING CHILDREN BELOW FIFTEEN (15) YEARS OF AGE FROM CREATING, MAINTAINING, OR USING SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS, REQUIRING SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS TO IMPLEMENT PRIVACY-PRESERVING AGE- ASSURANCE AND CHILD-SAFETY MEASURES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The internet nowadays is swarmed with children accessing and using different social media platforms with contents that are inappropriate for their age. Unsupervised exposure to social media platforms makes them vulnerable to risks of cyberbullying, anxiety, online sexual abuse, online exploitation, depression and sleep disruption during a period when their minds are impressionable. The rate by which online connectivity endangers the youth is already alarming. In fact, in the 2026 Global Safety Survey conducted by Microsoft, it was noted that teen’s exposure to risks rose again, with hate speech (35%), scams (29%), and cyberbullying (23%) among the most commonly experienced harm.1 In 2021 alone, two (2) million children in the Philippines were subjected to online sexual abuse and exploitation.2 They were reported to have experienced grooming, harassment and blackmail. This proposed measure is anchored on the State policy to protect children and to strengthen safeguards against online harms, consistent with existing child protection frameworks and the State’s continuing efforts to address online sexual abuse or exploitation of children and child sexual abuse or exploitation materials. This measure is intended to complement, and not diminish, duties and responsibilities already imposed on internet intermediaries and related entities under 1 “Building a safer digital future, together.” Available at https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2026/02/09/building-a-safer- digital-future-together/ 2 Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children in the Philippines”. Available at https://www.unicef.org/philippines/online- sexual-abuse-and-exploitation-children-philippines Republic Act No. 11930 otherwise known as Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR). The children have reportedly posted photos of themselves holding guns in their social media accounts, something which is rather disturbing considering that such weapons are dangerous when indiscriminately used by children their age. This behavior may also be an indication of the level of maturity of these children and whether they appreciate that such posts may have lasting impact on their personal lives and how others would perceive them later. Hence, this proposed legislation aims to safeguard children from behavioral desensitization and triggering as a result of prolonged exposure to electronic media violence. It intends to promote a clear and responsible usage of digital technology preferably for learning purposes, and aid in the formation of positive values among the youth. This proposed measure prompts parents to take a more active involvement in their children’s growth, to be present to guide them in choosing healthier and more proactive alternatives to learning other than relying on content and information found online. The bill proposes the following policies: a) Prohibit children below fifteen (15) years old from creating, registering, maintaining, accessing, logging into or using social medial accounts, including the use of account-based features such as posting, sharing, reacting, commenting, messaging, live streaming, and joining groups or communities, as these expose them to higher risks of exploitation and abuse; b) Require social media platforms operating in the country to establish age- verification mechanisms and submit annual transparency reports on observed and removed underage accounts; c) Establish accessible reporting and request mechanisms that allow parents or legal guardians or where appropriate, schools through authorized reporting channels) to request the restriction, deactivation, or removal of accounts suspected or verified to belong to children below the allowable age threshold; d) Enable schools and educational institutions to utilize a secure, supervised educational platforms for educational purposes only; While social media platforms offer a wider range of information and allow interaction with different types of individuals, the burden of making these digital systems safer for children still rests on the government, parents, schools and software companies. Let us protect our children’s wellbeing for as long as we could, and until they have developed faculties to safeguard themselves from possible harm and influences that they could ever encounter while interacting online. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. LAZATIN, JR. label: HB 9969
title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE ENTRY-LEVEL SALARY OF GOVERNMENT MIDWIVES FROM SALARY GRADE 9 TO GRADE 11
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The role of midwives is very significant as they provide frontline healthcare services, ensuring the delivery of maternal and neonatal care to mothers and children in the community. During the pandemic, they are among the manpower mobilized to provide medical care and were assigned to administer vaccines. Sadly, despite their contributions, government midwives are among the lowest-compensated health personnel in the public sector. At present, entry-level salary for midwives is at salary grade 9 which does not justify the responsibilities they carry out in reducing maternal and infant mortality. This proposed measure seeks to gain approval for the salary adjustment for entry-level midwives from the current Salary Grad 9 to Salary Grad 11, in recognition of the valuable service they selflessly give. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. LAZATIN, JR. label: HB 9973
title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE MINIMUM SALARY GRADE LEVEL OF SPED TEACHERS FROM SALARY GRADE 14 TO 22
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Special Education (SPED) teachers perform highly specialized functions that go beyond conventional classroom instruction. They are required to address diverse learning needs, manage individualized education plans, and provide targeted interventions for learners with disabilities, all of which demand advanced training, specialized competencies, and sustained emotional and professional commitment. Despite the critical nature of their role in delivering inclusive and equitable education, the current compensation framework for SPED teachers does not adequately reflect the complexity, intensity, and expertise required in their work. This disparity has contributed to challenges in recruitment, retention, and professional development within the SPED sector, ultimately affecting the quality and accessibility of services for learners with special needs. This bill seeks to upgrade the minimum salary grade level of SPED teachers from Salary Grade 14 to Salary Grade 22 in recognition of their specialized qualifications and responsibilities. The proposed adjustment aligns compensation with the level of technical expertise required, while providing a meaningful incentive to attract and retain qualified educators in the field of special education. Moreover, strengthening support for SPED teachers is integral to the State’s commitment to inclusive education and equal access to learning opportunities for all Filipinos. A well-supported SPED workforce ensures that learners with disabilities receive appropriate interventions and are meaningfully integrated into the education system. By providing just and commensurate compensation, this measure aims to enhance the delivery of SPED services, improve educational outcomes for learners with special needs, and uphold the State’s obligation to promote inclusive and quality education. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MA. NINA FRANCESCA P. label: HB 9974
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A NATIONAL LAND USE POLICY, PROVIDING THE IMPLEMENTING MECHANISMS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive National Land Use Policy that will rationalize the allocation, utilization, and management of the country’s finite land resources among competing demands such as agriculture, housing, infrastructure, and environmental protection. At present, the absence of a unified and enforceable land use framework has resulted in conflicting land uses, inefficient allocation of resources, and the gradual displacement of critical public service areas. This is particularly evident in the education sector, where public schools, especially in rapidly urbanizing communities, face congestion, and limited access to suitable and secure sites. By establishing a coherent land use policy, this measure ensures that areas allocated for educational purposes are properly identified, protected, and integrated into local and national development plans. It promotes the accessibility, safety, and long-term sustainability of school sites, thereby supporting the delivery of quality education. Moreover, the bill integrates disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation into land use planning, recognizing the vulnerability of school communities to natural hazards. Through resilient and forward-looking planning, it aims to safeguard lives, infrastructure, and public investments. The proposed policy likewise advances equitable land distribution and balanced development, which will benefit not only students but also teachers and workers through improved housing, better community planning, and enhanced access to essential services. Ultimately, this measure lays the foundation for a more orderly, sustainable, and inclusive pattern of national development. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 9975
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE REGULATORY POWERS OF THE NATIONAL FOOD AUTHORITY TO SUPPORT THE RICE INDUSTRY AND ENSURE CONSUMER PROTECTION THROUGH ADEQUATE SUPPLY AND STABLE PRICE OF RICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8178, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “AGRICULTURAL TARRIFICATION ACT”, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to strengthen the regulatory powers of the National Food Authority (NFA) in order to ensure adequate rice supply, stabilize market prices, and protect both Filipino consumers and rice producers, through amendments to Republic Act No. 8178, otherwise known as the Agricultural Tariffication Act. While the liberalization of rice importation under RA 8178 aimed to increase supply and lower consumer prices, its implementation has exposed structural gaps in market regulation. The removal of the NFA’s direct regulatory and market intervention powers has limited the State’s ability to respond effectively to supply disruptions, price volatility, hoarding, and other anti-competitive practices. Consequently, both consumers and farmers have been adversely affected by unstable rice prices and uneven market conditions. Rice remains a staple commodity and a critical component of national food security. Fluctuations in its price have a direct and immediate impact on household welfare, particularly among low-income families, including public school teachers and other fixed-income earners. At the same time, Filipino farmers continue to face depressed farmgate prices and increased vulnerability to market forces without sufficient government support. This measure addresses these gaps by restoring and enhancing the NFA’s regulatory authority, including the power to monitor supply chains, prevent hoarding and profiteering, enforce compliance through licensing and inspections, and undertake timely market interventions. It also strengthens mechanisms for maintaining buffer stock, regulating storage facilities, and ensuring transparency in rice trade activities. By providing the State with effective regulatory tools, this bill seeks to strike a balance between a liberalized trade environment and the need for strategic government intervention to protect public welfare and agricultural sustainability. Ultimately, the measure aims to promote a stable, accessible, and affordable rice supply, safeguard the livelihood of Filipino farmers, and ensure that the country’s food security framework remains responsive to both domestic and global market pressures. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. MA. NINA FRANCESCA P. label: HB 9976
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A COMPREHENSIVE NATIONAL SUBSIDY AND SUPPORT PROGRAM FOR FAMILIES WITH CHILDREN DIAGNOSED WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a lifelong developmental condition that profoundly impacts a person’s communication, social interaction, and behavior. Raising a child with autism presents extraordinary emotional, psychological, and financial challenges for Filipino families. The cost of managing ASD is prohibitive, with individual therapy sessions costing up to ₱3,500.00. For a child needing weekly interventions, these costs quickly become unaffordable for the average family. As a result, many families cannot afford early treatment, leaving these children without the tools to become independent. While Republic Act No. 7277 (the Magna Carta for Persons with Disabilities), as amended, provides discounts, these reliefs are insufficient to cover the heavy monthly financial burdens on these households. This legislative measure establishes the Autism Support Allowance Program under the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and institutionalizes a direct monthly financial subsidy of Five Thousand Pesos (₱5,000.00) per child diagnosed with ASD. Furthermore, the bill democratizes early intervention by mandating free developmental screenings under PhilHealth and establishing a specialized therapy voucher system. Furthermore, this measure aims to relieve the disproportionate financial burdens on these families, as well as to allow the State to actively fulfill its constitutional mandate to protect vulnerable sectors and ensure that neurodivergent children receive the dignity, care, and tools necessary to achieve their full potential. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9977
title: AN ACT PROVIDING AUTOMATIC AGRICULTURAL INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR QUALIFIED RECIPIENTS OF GOVERNMENT-SUPPORTED AGRICULTURAL CREDIT, ESTABLISHING A ONE-STOP INTEGRATED ENROLLMENT SYSTEM, AND PROVIDING FUNDING MECHANISMS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Agriculture in the Philippines remains highly vulnerable to climate shocks, natural disasters, pests, diseases, and other risks that may result in significant losses for farmers and fisherfolk. Crop insurance serves as an important mechanism for protecting agricultural producers against such losses and promoting the stability of the agricultural sector. Presidential Decree No. 1467 created the Philippine Crop Insurance Corporation (PCIC) to provide insurance protection to agricultural producers. The government likewise extends agricultural credit through various subsidized lending programs administered by government agencies and government financial institutions. While agricultural credit and crop insurance programs presently exist, there is no statutory mechanism that automatically links government-supported agricultural credit with crop insurance coverage. As a result, insurance enrollment remains dependent on separate administrative processes and the timely exchange of information among lending institutions and implementing agencies. Existing laws likewise do not clearly provide that a qualified agricultural borrower shall remain entitled to insurance protection notwithstanding delays, omissions, or failures in enrollment, data transmission, or other administrative requirements beyond the borrower's control. This bill seeks to address this gap by providing automatic agricultural insurance coverage for qualified recipients of government-supported agricultural credit. Under this measure, insurance coverage shall attach by operation of law upon approval of the loan, credit accommodation, or financial assistance. The bill further ensures that a qualified borrower shall not be deprived of such coverage by reason of administrative, technical, or procedural deficiencies attributable to participating institutions. To facilitate implementation, the bill establishes a One-Stop Automated Integration System among participating institutions to streamline enrollment and insurance administration. The bill likewise provides funding mechanisms necessary to sustain the insurance coverage mandated under this Act. By strengthening the linkage between agricultural credit and agricultural insurance, this measure seeks to provide greater protection to farmers and fisherfolk, encourage participation in government agricultural programs, and promote agricultural productivity, food security, and rural development. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9978
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A DEDICATED BARANGAY ANIMAL WELFARE DESK (BAWD) IN ALL BARANGAYS NATIONWIDE TO ENHANCE COMMUNITY-LEVEL MEDIATION, ENFORCEMENT, AND PUBLIC HEALTH COORDINATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE While Republic Act No. 8485 penalizes animal cruelty, the law lacks a localized, community-level enforcement mechanism to handle everyday violations. Consequently, animal welfare concerns, neighborhood pet disputes, and localized abuse cases are left to barangay officials who operate without authority, technical training, or administrative guidelines. This lack of local enforcement leads to neighborhood fights and illegal animal poisonings, while stalling city efforts to control rabies and manage stray populations. This Bill seeks to address this gap by mandating the establishment of a Barangay Animal Welfare Desk (BAWD) in every barangay nationwide under the direct supervision of the Barangay Chairperson. The BAWD will serve as a frontline venue to mediate local pet-ownership disputes, maintain a community-level registry to track and report severe neglect or abuse, and act as a public health coordination hub for targeted rabies vaccinations and humane population control drives in partnership with municipal veterinarians. This measure mandates DILG training for appointed officers to ensure standardized implementation, thereby establishing clear local accountability, protecting public health, and strengthening neighborhood peace and order. Hence, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9979
title: AN ACT PRESCRIBING RIGID STANDARDS FOR CORPORATE RESTRUCTURING RESULTING IN BACKDOOR LISTINGS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE SECURITIES REGULATION CODE, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The integrity of the Philippine capital market is a vital engine for economic growth, anchored by the Initial Public Offering (IPO) process. As a rigorous gatekeeper, the IPO ensures that only financially stable and transparent companies solicit public investment. However, the rise of "Backdoor Listings”, which occurs when private entities bypass these rigors by acquiring dormant shell companies, presents an opportunity to modernize standards and better safeguard small investors from asset stripping and market volatility. The “Capital Market Integrity and Backdoor Listing Prevention Act of 2026” aims to uphold transparency and accountability across the market. This Bill requires backdoor listings to meet the same strict compliance standards and/or undergo the exact same strict vetting process as a standard IPO. It likewise protects small investors by allowing them a veto vote, also called the "majority-of-the-minority" vote, and compels acquiring entities to reveal their true owners. In addition, it implements market safeguards, such as immediate trading suspensions and strict asset-stripping bans, to guarantee that listing on the Exchange remains a merit-based privilege. In light of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9980
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT PROGRAM FOR FAMILIES AND CAREGIVERS OF PERSONS WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER, DOWN SYNDROME, AND OTHER PERMANENT DEVELOPMENTAL AND INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES, PROVIDING FOR LIFETIME SUPPORT AND LONG-TERM CARE PLANNING, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State has long recognized the rights and welfare of persons with disabilities through landmark legislation such as Republic Act No. 7277, otherwise known as the Magna Carta for Disabled Persons, as amended, and Republic Act No. 11650, or the Inclusive Education Act. These laws provide important rights, protections, benefits, and opportunities for persons with disabilities and promote their inclusion in society. These measures have undoubtedly advanced the welfare of persons with disabilities. However, while existing laws focus on the rights, accessibility, education, and inclusion of persons with disabilities, there remains no comprehensive law that specifically recognizes and addresses the unique and continuing burden borne by families and primary caregivers of persons with permanent developmental and intellectual disabilities, such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Down Syndrome, Intellectual Disability, and similar lifelong conditions. For many Filipino families, caring for a person with a developmental or intellectual disability requires significant financial resources, time, and personal sacrifice. Parents and caregivers often shoulder the costs of therapy, developmental interventions, specialized educational support, medical consultations, transportation, assistive devices, and other essential services. In many instances, caregivers are compelled to reduce working hours, forego employment opportunities, or leave the workforce entirely in order to provide the level of care and supervision required by their loved ones. More importantly, there remains no comprehensive statutory framework that addresses the long-term security and continuity of care of persons with permanent developmental and intellectual disabilities when their parents or primary caregivers become elderly, incapacitated, or pass away. For countless Filipino families, the uncertainty surrounding the future care of their loved ones remains a source of profound concern. This measure seeks to fill these gaps by establishing a comprehensive family and caregiver support framework for persons with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Down Syndrome, and other permanent developmental and intellectual disabilities. It recognizes that while disability rights must continue to be protected, the families and caregivers who provide lifelong care likewise deserve meaningful support and protection under the law. By institutionalizing caregiver support measures, strengthening access to developmental services, and establishing mechanisms that promote long-term care planning and security, this bill seeks to complement existing disability laws and provide a more holistic approach to the welfare of persons with permanent developmental and intellectual disabilities and the families who care for them. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9981
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8293, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, TO REGULATE THE COPYRIGHTABILITY OF WORKS CREATED WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, ESTABLISHING STANDARDS FOR HUMAN AUTHORSHIP, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The current Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines (R.A. 8293) was enacted in 1997—decades prior to the emergence of generative artificial intelligence as a mainstream creative tool. Today, technologies like large language models, diffusion models, and automated creators are actively integrated into the workflows of Filipino artists, writers, programmers, and filmmakers. This technological leap has created a severe statutory gap. Our current framework vests copyright exclusively in "authors," which jurisprudence defines as natural persons. However, the law provides no guidance on how to treat works born from a hybrid collaboration between human intellect and machine algorithms. This regulatory vacuum creates profound legal uncertainty. On one hand, over-regulation risks stifling digital innovation and compromising our economic competitiveness. On the other hand, under-regulation threatens to dilute the value of genuine human creativity and clog our registries with automated, non-human outputs. This Bill addresses this gap by amending R.A. 8293 to introduce distinct legal thresholds. It explicitly clarifies that while purely AI-generated materials belong in the public domain, AI-assisted works are protectable only to the extent of the human author's creative control, modification, and arrangement. It also introduces a mandatory disclosure mechanism during registration to maintain transparency and protect the integrity of the intellectual property system. This measure embraces technological progress with foresight and responsibility. By establishing clear legal boundaries for AI-assisted works, it ensures the Philippines remains a competitive digital hub while upholding the core mandate of our intellectual property system—to incentivize and protect the irreplaceable spark of human genius. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9982
title: AN ACT RESTRUCTURING THE PROTOCOLS FOR LABOR DISPUTES IN ESSENTIAL SERVICES, REPLACING ABSOLUTE STRIKE PROHIBITIONS WITH A MINIMUM OPERATIONS STANDARD, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The right to strike is a constitutional guarantee. Section 3, Article XIII of the 1987 Philippine Constitution explicitly mandates that the State shall guarantee the rights of all workers to self-organization, collective bargaining and negotiations, and peaceful concerted activities, including the right to strike in accordance with law. Under Article 278 of the Labor Code, the Secretary of Labor and Employment holds broad powers to assume jurisdiction over disputes in industries deemed "indispensable to the national interest." In practice, this has led to absolute strike bans across entire sectors, such as private hospital personnel and security guards. These blanket prohibitions strip essential workers of their primary leverage to bargain for fair wages and safe conditions, leaving them vulnerable to institutional exploitation. While the State must protect public safety, an outright ban is a blunt instrument that poorly balances public welfare against fundamental constitutional rights. This bill introduces a balanced framework: The Minimum Operations Standard. Instead of enforcing absolute strike bans, this Act allows workers in critical sectors to strike on the condition that they maintain a strictly defined, pre-negotiated level of core operations. This ensures that while public safety risks are mitigated, keeping emergency rooms staffed and critical infrastructure secured, the workforce retains its right to collective action. Lastly, no worker should be forced to surrender their fundamental rights as a condition of serving the public. This Act aims to fix a long-standing statutory imbalance, as well as ensure that essential personnel can legally demand fair treatment without endangering the lives of those they protect. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9983
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING EQUITABLE LABOR STANDARDS FOR GIG ECONOMY WORKERS, REGULATING ALGORITHMIC MANAGEMENT, AND PROTECTING AGAINST UNFAIR DE-PLATFORMING
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates that the State shall afford full protection to labor, promote full employment, and ensure equality of employment opportunities for all. However, a digital loophole has emerged where thousands of TNVS drivers and delivery riders are considered "Independent Contractors" on paper, but are treated like employees in practice. This is the "Gig Economy Gap." Platform providers often use "non-exclusivity" clauses as a legal shield to avoid providing benefits. Yet, through Algorithmic Control, these platforms impose delivery quotas so high that workers have no choice but to remain exclusive to one application. When they fail to meet these quotas, they are "de-platformed" by a faceless algorithm—without a hearing, without a human explanation, and without due process. This Act seeks to align our labor laws with the smartphone age by bridging the gap between technological advancement and worker protection. It defines "Algorithmic Control" to recognize that tracking movements and imposing strict quotas constitute modern employer supervision. Furthemore, this Act seeks to empower platform workers by granting full-time workers legal recognition, providing due process against unfair suspensions, and mandating transparent algorithmic management to ensure that automated decisions are fair and subject to human oversight. In essence, this bill aims to build a sustainable digital economy where technological progress does not sacrifice labor rights. It ensures that amid rapid innovation, every Filipino worker remains protected and included. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9984
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A GSIS SERVICE CREDIT COMPLETION PROGRAM FOR QUALIFIED SEPARATED MEMBERS OF THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM ACT OF 1997” Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 11 of the Constitution declares that the State values the dignity of every human person and guarantees full respect for human rights. This includes the right of workers to social security and a dignified retirement. Under Republic Act No. 8291, otherwise known as the “Government Service Insurance System Act of 1997,” a government employee must complete at least fifteen (15) years of creditable government service to qualify for retirement pension benefits. Consequently, many public servants who have devoted years of their lives to government service but are separated from employment before reaching the minimum service requirement are permanently disqualified from receiving a monthly pension. This situation often affects employees who leave government service due to circumstances beyond their control, such as agency reorganization, abolition of positions, medical incapacity, disability, family emergencies, or other compelling circumstances. While these individuals may have rendered substantial service to the government, the law currently provides no mechanism by which they may complete the remaining service requirement necessary to qualify for retirement pension benefits. The absence of such a mechanism may result in severe financial hardship, particularly among former government employees who spent a significant portion of their working lives in public service and reasonably expected to qualify for retirement protection. This measure seeks to address this gap by establishing a GSIS Service Credit Completion Program. The Program allows qualified separated members to obtain the remaining service credits necessary to satisfy the minimum retirement eligibility requirement through the payment of the full actuarial cost as determined by the Government Service Insurance System. The Program is designed to be fiscally responsible and self-sustaining, ensuring that no additional burden is imposed upon the GSIS Social Insurance Fund or the National Government. The bill likewise recognizes that members who have completed at least fourteen (14) years of creditable service have substantially fulfilled the statutory requirement and should be afforded a reasonable opportunity to complete the remaining service credits. At the same time, the measure extends relief to members with at least ten (10) years of service whose separation resulted from circumstances beyond their control, subject to appropriate safeguards. This measure promotes fairness, strengthens retirement security, and honors the contributions of government employees while preserving the actuarial integrity of the GSIS. In light of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D. label: HB 9985
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE HUMANE TRAP-NEUTER-VACCINATE-RETURN (TNVR) STRATEGY FOR COMMUNITY ANIMALS, RECOGNIZING THE STATUS OF REGISTERED VOLUNTARY CAREGIVERS, AND AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8485 Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE For decades, our approach to stray animals has been trapped in a broken, costly cycle. Local governments constantly round up and euthanize street animals, yet our streets are never cleared, rabies remains a threat, and the stray population never drops. This policy fails because of the "vacuum effect." Removing strays simply clears space for new, unsterilized animals to move in and breed. Taxpayers are essentially funding a costly, endless cycle that does not reduce the stray population. This bill breaks that cycle by institutionalizing the Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Return (TNVR) as the primary national policy for stray management. This Act aims to replace culling with management. By trapping, fixing, and vaccinating street animals before returning them to their territory, we create a stable, rabies-immune population that naturally shrinks over time without a single drop of blood spilled. In addition, this Act also shields Registered Community Caregivers who feed and care for street animals at their own expense. Instead of facing harassment, fines, or unfair legal liabilities under local ordinances, these citizens will now receive statutory protection that validates their role in community safety. We can no longer afford to mistake cruelty for control. It is time to replace an expensive, broken cycle of violence with compassion. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. Rep. Jan “Atty. JP” D.
