label: HB 10038
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PREVENTION OF BULLYING IN EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10627, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI- BULLYING ACT OF 2013,” APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XV, Section 3(2) of the 1987 Constitution requires the State to protect the right of children to assistance and special protection from all forms of neglect, abuse, cruelty, exploitation, and other conditions prejudicial to their development. Furthermore, the Constitution recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building and mandates the State to promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual, and social well-being. Schools must therefore remain safe, inclusive, and supportive spaces where learners can develop free from fear, violence, discrimination, and abuse. More than a decade after the enactment of Republic Act No. 10627, otherwise known as the “Anti-Bullying Act of 2013,” bullying remains a pervasive and alarming problem in Philippine educational institutions. Findings cited by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) reveal that 65% of Filipino students reported experiencing bullying at least a few times a month, among the highest rates recorded internationally.1 More recent data show that 43% of girls and 53% of boys in the Philippines experience bullying at least a few times a month—more than double the average among member countries of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).2 Bullying is not merely a disciplinary issue. It has profound consequences on the mental health, safety, and academic performance of learners. Studies also show that frequent exposure to bullying is associated with significantly lower learning outcomes, with students who are bullied weekly scoring substantially lower in Mathematics and Science than their peers.3 Victims of bullying are likewise more vulnerable to anxiety, depression, social isolation, self-harm, and other adverse outcomes that undermine their ability to learn and thrive.4 Beyond its effects on individual learners, bullying contributes to unsafe school environments and undermines the ability of educational institutions to fulfill their mission of fostering learning, growth, and development. 1 Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2), High Incidence of Bullying in PH Public Schools Alarming (June 13, 2024), https://edcom2.gov.ph/high-incidence-of-bullying-in-ph- public-schools-alarming-edcom-2/ 2 Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2), 10,018 DepEd Schools Without Anti-Bullying Policy (June 19, 2025), https://edcom2.gov.ph/10018-deped-schools-without-anti- bullying-policy/ 3 Keith Clores, School Bullying Affects Students' Test Scores, Says Edcom II, INQUIRER.net (Mar. 16, 2026), https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2196359/school-bullying-affects-students-test- scores-says-edcom-ii 4 United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), What You Need to Know About School Violence and Bullying (Nov. 1, 2019), https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/what-you-need-know-about-school-violence-and-bullying Despite the existence of legal protections, many schools continue to face challenges in preventing, identifying, and responding to bullying. EDCOM 2 also reported that around 10,018 public schools have yet to fully comply with anti-bullying policy requirements, while researchers have emphasized the need for school-wide approaches that address not only incidents of bullying but also the broader school environment in which such behavior occurs.5 Since the enactment of Republic Act No. 10627, the Department of Education has undertaken significant reforms to strengthen the implementation of anti-bullying policies through the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Anti-Bullying Act of 20136 and Department Order No. 6, s. 2026, otherwise known as the Guidelines on Ensuring a Safe and Motivating Learning Environment. These issuances recognize that preventing bullying requires more than disciplinary sanctions. They adopt a whole-of-school approach that emphasizes learners’ rights, prevention, early identification, timely intervention, psychosocial support, restorative practices, and shared accountability among schools, families, learners, and communities. There is an opportunity to build upon these reforms by institutionalizing their fundamental principles in statute, while strengthening accountability mechanisms, expanding coverage to higher education and technical-vocational institutions, and introducing additional safeguards to ensure their sustained implementation. Hence, this bill which seeks to strengthen the prevention of bullying in educational institutions by: (1) expanding the coverage of the Anti- 5 Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2), 10,018 DepEd Schools Without Anti-Bullying Policy (June 19, 2025), https://edcom2.gov.ph/10018-deped-schools-without-anti- bullying-policy/ 6 Department Order No. 90, series of 2025. label: HB 10039
title: AN ACT CONVERTING THE ZAMBOANGA PENINSULA POLYTECHNIC STATE UNIVERSITY-BAYOG EXTERNAL STUDY UNIT LOCATED IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF BAYOG, PROVINCE OF ZAMBOANGA DEL SUR, INTO A REGULAR CAMPUS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to convert the Bayog External Study Unit of the Zamboanga Peninsula Polytechnic State University (ZPPSU), located in Bayog, Zamboanga del Sur, into a regular campus to be known as the ZPPSU–Bayog Campus. It also provides for the necessary funding and plantilla positions for both teaching and non- teaching personnel. Article XIV, Section 1 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates the State to protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education and to make such education accessible at all levels. ZPPSU has long advanced technical, vocational, and higher education in the Zamboanga Peninsula. Its Bayog External Study Unit has provided accessible learning opportunities, but its current status limits its capacity to deliver programs and services equal to those of a regular campus. Granting it full campus status will allow the expansion of academic offerings, the strengthening of research and extension services, and compliance with Commission on Higher Education standards. This will enhance program quality and credibility while directly benefiting Bayog and the wider province by addressing the growing demand for affordable higher education. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JEYZEL VICTORIA C. YU JOSEPH KIM C. YU MARIA KRISTINA JIHAN B. label: HB 10040
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8436, ENTITLED "AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMMISSION ON ELECTIONS TO USE AN AUTOMATED ELECTION SYSTEM IN THE MAY 11, 1998 NATIONAL OR LOCAL ELECTIONS AND IN SUBSEQUENT NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTORAL EXERCISES, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9369, PROVIDING FOR A PARALLEL PRECINCT-LEVEL MANUAL COUNT OF VOTES IN THE AUTOMATED ELECTION SYSTEM AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The integrity of the electoral process is the foundation of a representative democracy. The right of the people to choose their leaders through free, orderly, honest, peaceful, and credible elections must be protected through systems that promote accuracy, transparency, and public confidence. Republic Act No. 8436, as amended by Republic Act No. 9369, authorized the adoption of an Automated Election System (AES) in the Philippines to modernize the conduct of elections and ensure the efficient counting, consolidation, and transmission of election results. Since its implementation, automation has significantly improved the speed by which election results are processed and delivered to the public. However, while technological advancements have enhanced the efficiency of elections, it remains equally important to ensure that transparency and verifiability are preserved at every stage of the electoral process. Public trust in election results depends not only on the speed of the system but also on the ability of stakeholders to verify and observe the accuracy of the results generated. This bill seeks to strengthen the Automated Election System by requiring a parallel precinct-level manual count of votes. This additional safeguard shall serve as a transparency and verification mechanism while maintaining the benefits of automated counting, consolidation, and transmission of election results. By providing an additional layer of accountability, the measure seeks to reinforce public confidence in the electoral process and uphold the fundamental principle that election results must accurately reflect the genuine will of the Filipino people. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. EMIGDIO P. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The barangay is the basic political unit and the primary planning and implementing unit of government programs, projects, and activities in the community.1 Under the 1987 Constitution and the Local Government Code of 1991 (R.A. 7160), the State is committed to decentralization, local autonomy, and the empowerment of local government units to deliver essential services to the Filipino people. In April 2026, the Executive Branch launched the “Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” Program, allocating PhP 200,000 to each of the country’s approximately 42,000 barangays through the Socio-Civic Projects Fund (SCPF) of the Office of the President.2 The SCPF traces its statutory origin to Presidential Decree No. 1869, s. 1983 (PAGCOR Charter), Section 7(a) of which empowers the allocation and distribution of PAGCOR earnings earmarked for infrastructure and socio-civic projects, with the approval of the Office of the President.3 Section 12 of the same decree mandates that the government’s share of PAGCOR’s aggregate gross earnings be set aside for infrastructure and socio-civic projects, with the Office of the President authorized to direct such allocations throughout the Philippines.4 The current administration of the SCPF is governed by Memorandum Order No. 11, s. 2022, which reverted SCPF management to the Office of the Executive Secretary, citing Section 6 of Executive Order No. 1, s. 2022 and Section 7(a) of P.D. No. 1869.5 The program has supported community development projects and educational assistance for graduating college students. However, the SCPF has a statutory origin in P.D. No. 18696 and is supported by an executive issuance chain (E.O. No. 17 and M.O. No. 118), the actual per-barangay 11987 CONST., Art. X, §3; Art. II, §9; Art. XIII, §1. Rep. Act No. 7160, §384 (1991). label: HB 10042
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA OF YOUNG FARMERS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The country’s agriculture sector plays a significant role in the nation’s food security. However, in recent years, the country’s dependence on agricultural exports has been steadily increasing, from $17.91 billion in 2023 and $19.46 billion in 2024, to $20.37 billion in 2025. 1 This increasing rate of imports is brought about by several factors, including the inability of the domestic agricultural market to sufficiently meet the food demands of a growing population. In light of the country’s experiences with global issues, such as the crisis in West Asia, the Ukraine-Russia war, and COVID-19, which have heavily affected global trade restrictions and prices, the country’s dependence on importation is concerning. Thus, there is a need to continue addressing the problems facing the agricultural sector to reduce importation dependence and work towards food self-sufficiency. In 2022, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported a drop from 9.73 million agriculture and forestry workers in July 2022 to 9.22 million in October 2022, marking a loss of over 511,000 workers.2 These declines reflect not just seasonal factors but are largely due to workers leaving the agriculture industry. 3 The Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS) found that population growth, diminishing farm size, and declining incomes in agriculture incentivize the “shift out of agriculture.” 4 1 Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). (26 March 2026). Annual Agricultural Export and Import. Retrieved from https://psa.gov.ph/statistics/agricultural-export-import/annual. 2 Viloan, M.E. (10 June 2025). Aging Farms, Shrinking Fields: The Philippines’ Farming Crisis. Medium. Retrieved from https://medium.com/@b3nt3.lang/aging-farms-shrinking-fields-the- philippines-farming-crisis-91caf8876af7. 3 Ibid. 4 Baclig, C.E. (8 December 2022). PH farms getting empty: Agriculture job loss a worrying trend. Inquirer.net. Retrieved from https://pidswebs.pids.gov.ph/CDN/document/1687311912_64925628d5a2f.pdf. 1 A survey has found that 65% of Filipino farmers believe their kids would not have a bright future if they became farmers.5 Young Filipinos opt out of farming, preferring careers in medicine, IT, or business, because they associate farming with “hard work and poverty.”6 A 2021 science journal study found that the average Filipino farmer is 53 years old, while a Department of Agriculture (DA) report stated 56 years old.7 If these trends persist, the country may face a bigger problem in the agricultural sector and food security in the coming years. This bill seeks to create the Magna Carta of Young Farmers to institutionalize mechanisms and policies that directly address the challenges faced by young farmers and uphold their rights. The bill creates the Council and the National Young Farmers Roadmap to ensure that young farmers are adequately prioritized in the formulation and implementation of national policies and programs that empower them. The bill also guarantees equal access to technology, credit, and capital among young farmers. Furthermore, the bill focuses on the land rights of young farmers by guaranteeing improved access to low-cost farmland. To make young farmers more competitive, the bill also provides them with assistance in farm planning, management, and access to market spaces. Finally, to uphold young farmers’ rights against discrimination and violence, the bill ensures their access to free legal services. In the 20th Congress, similar bills were filed by Representative Nathaniel Oducado in the House of Representatives, and Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan and Senator Risa Hontiveros in the Senate. This bill fully adopts Senator Pangilinan’s Senate Bill No. 719. Early approval of this measure is earnestly sought. LEILA M. DE LIMA 5 Viloan, M.E.(10 June 2025). label: HB 10043
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RIGHTS OF INFORMAL AMBULANT VENDORS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Informal ambulant vendors are among the most visible yet least protected participants in the country’s informal economy. They sell goods or offer non- professional services without a fixed business location, often relying on portable carts, stands, and similar means to earn a living in streets, parks, markets, and other public spaces. For many Filipinos, particularly those with limited access to formal employment, capital, and other livelihood opportunities, ambulant vending remains a primary means of supporting themselves and their families. 1 Notwithstanding their contribution to local commerce and their role in making affordable goods and services accessible to the public, ambulant vendors remain among the most vulnerable workers. 2 Many operate without formal recognition, secure vending areas, social protection, or access to government support. They are frequently exposed to clearing operations, confiscation of goods, removal from vending areas, and the dismantling of their stalls, often without adequate notice, consultation, due process, or alternative spaces where they may continue earning a living.3 Reports from various localities have also revealed instances of 1 Malasig, J. (01 May 2025). ‘Enable People’: Photo of regulated street vendors praised by Pinoys. Retrieved from: https://interaksyon.philstar.com/trends-spotlights/2025/05/01/295672/photo-regulated- street-vendors-praised-pinoys/ 2 Fernandez, C. and Samaniego, L. (12 December 2025). Vetting on vendor visibility. Retrieved from: https://theguidon.com/2025/12/vetting-on-vendor-visibility/ 3 Yap, T. (11 April 2026). Iloilo City gov’t slammed for violent dispersal of ambulant market vendors. Retrieved from: https://mb.com.ph/2026/04/11/iloilo-city-govt-slammed-for-violent-dispersal-of- ambulant-market-vendors 1 unregulated collections, excessive rental charges, and weak government oversight affecting vendors. 4 The lack of a clear and uniform national policy has resulted in differing local approaches to ambulant vending, some of which are focused primarily on removal and enforcement rather than regulation and protection. 5 While local governments have the duty to maintain public order, safety, accessibility, and sanitation, these objectives must be balanced with the constitutional mandate to promote social justice, protect labor, uphold the dignity of every person, and improve the quality of life of all Filipinos. The removal of vendors from public spaces without providing lawful, safe, and sustainable alternatives may further worsen poverty and economic insecurity among affected families. This measure establishes the Magna Carta of Informal Ambulant Vendors to recognize their contribution to the economy and protect their rights while promoting public welfare, consumer protection, and compliance with health and safety standards. It provides for simplified and fee-free registration, security of tenure in designated vending sites, access to social protection programs, and recognition across LGUs. It also creates Local Inter-Agency Councils to identify appropriate vending areas and oversee vendor protection, while requiring consultation, due process, and viable temporary or relocation sites before vendors may be displaced. By institutionalizing a rights-based, orderly, and humane framework for the regulation of informal ambulant vending, this measure seeks to transform the treatment of vendors from one of exclusion and harassment into one of inclusion, protection, and shared local development. This bill adopts HB11337, which was approved by the House of Representatives in the 19th Congress, and SBN 1099 filed by Senator Sherwin T. Gatchalian in the 20th Congress. Similar measures have been filed by Representatives Jernie Jett V. Nisay, Bryan B. Revilla, Lani Mercado-Revilla, Ramon Jolo B. Revilla III, and Senator Camille A. Villar in the 20th Congress. label: HB 10044
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING HALFWAY HOUSES FOR SURVIVORS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE, SEXUAL VIOLENCE, FAMILY VIOLENCE, AND OTHER FORMS OF ABUSE, PROVIDING PROTECTIVE CUSTODY, TEMPORARY SHELTER, RECOVERY, REINTEGRATION, SUPPORT SERVICES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE According to the Philippine Statistics Authority’s 2026 Factsheet on Women and Men, 3,343 cases of violence against girls were recorded in 2025, representing 54.6% of all documented cases of violence against children for that year 1. As of 2022, 19,228 women have been documented as survivors of violence2. These figures, however, capture only what has been reported, and only within particular demographics. Survivors across other gender identities continue to face violent acts and systemic discrimination that perpetuate harm 3, yet remain inadequately recognized under existing law. Compounding this, only approximately 15% of Filipinos live in areas covered by local ordinances that prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, leaving a vast majority without even baseline legal protection4. Ideally, when victims are subjected to abuse or at risk of being abused, they must have a safe place to go to. Having immediate access to a secure environment is 1 Philippine Statistics Authority. (30 April 2026). 2026 Fact Sheet on Women and Men in the Philippines. Philippine Statistics Authority. Retrieved from https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/phdsd/2026-Fact- Sheet-on-Women-and-Men_30Apr2026.pdf. 2 Id. 3 Human Rights Watch. (21 June 2017). Just Let Us Be: Discrimination Against LGBT Students in the Philippines. Human Rights Watch. Retrieved from https://www.hrw.org/report/2017/06/22/just-let-us- be/discrimination-against-lgbt-students-philippines. 4 Id. 1 essential not only to ensure their physical safety and protect them from further harm, but also to provide a stable foundation where they can begin the vital process of healing, rehabilitation, and rebuilding their lives. Currently, the challenge lies not in the lack of designated shelter facilities to cater to these victims, but rather that these facilities are limited in number and geographic distribution, leaving many provinces, municipalities, and remote areas without dedicated shelter infrastructure. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) currently operates shelter facilities like the Haven for Women, which offer temporary shelter and protective custody for women ages 18-59 years old who are victims of involuntary or forced prostitution, illegal recruitment, battered/abused women, victims of sexual abuse, women in detention, women victims of armed conflicts and others 5 and Home for Girls, for girl children aged 7 to below 18 years old 6, but these facilities are still too few to provide sufficient coverage nationwide. At present, DWSD operates and manages about seventy-seven (77) Centers and Residential Care Facilities (CRCF) nationwide7. Of these facilities, eight (8) are dedicated as Havens for Women, eight (8) serve as Homes for Girls, seven (7) function as combined facilities serving both demographics, and none of which particularly cover survivor populations on persons of diverse sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC)8. Thus, this proposed measure. This measure aims to protect survivors of domestic, sexual, and gender-based violence by establishing inclusive halfway houses in every city and province. It ensures immediate, non-discriminatory protective custody and emergency shelter. Furthermore, the initiative mandates trauma-informed, child-sensitive care, strengthens local government capacity to deliver integrated services, and upholds survivors' rights to safety, dignity, and justice. The establishment of a nationwide halfway house system represents a more inclusive and rehabilitative approach to the State’s obligation to protect those who have experienced or remain vulnerable to violence. As both a mechanism and a framework for protection, recovery, and reintegration, it ensures that all survivors, regardless of gender, age, or sexual orientation, receive the protective rehabilitation and sustained support they are owed. 5 Department of Social Work and Development. label: HB 10046
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING COMPREHENSIVE SAFETY PROTOCOLS, SECURITY INFRASTRUCTURE, AND CRISIS INTERVENTION MECHANISMS IN ALL PUBLIC BASIC EDUCATION SCHOOLS NATIONWIDE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution mandates that the State shall protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and shall take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all. Crucial to this mandate is ensuring that our learning institutions remain safe spaces where students, teachers, and school personnel can thrive without fear of violence, environmental hazards, or emotional trauma. Recent tragedies in public school vicinities highlight critical gaps in our current school safety infrastructure and response frameworks. The increasing complexity of both man-made security threats and climate-driven natural disasters demands a comprehensive, modern approach to campus safety. This bill seeks to institutionalize standard safety protocols across all public basic education institutions by establishing three core pillars: 1. Physical and Infrastructure Security: Mandating secured perimeters, controlled access points, and routine safety audits. 2. Crisis and Emergency Response: Implementing uniform emergency response protocols and mandatory training for natural disasters, fires, and active-threat situations. 3. Mental Health and Psycho-social Support: Allocating dedicated personnel to early intervention, peer-mediation, and counseling to address the root causes of behavioral crises before they escalate. By integrating physical infrastructure upgrades with proactive mental health care and rigorous training, this legislative measure shifts our public school systems from a reactive stance to a culture of constant readiness and prevention. In view of the urgent need to protect our nation’s most valuable resource—our children—the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 10047
title: AN ACT GRANTING CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY AND MILITARY RESERVIST STATUS TO QUALIFIED FILIPINO SEAFARERS WITH TWO YEARS OF COMPLETED MARITIME EXPERIENCE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines remains an undisputed global superpower in the maritime labor market, supplying approximately one-quarter of all seafaring professionals worldwide. Our Filipino seafarers endure months of rigorous duty at sea, navigating complex maritime terrains, braving harsh environmental hazards, and managing high-stakes technological and logistical networks. Through their immense economic contributions, which amount to billions of dollars in annual foreign remittances, they serve as a primary pillar of our national economic resilience. They are, without question, modern-day heroes. However, despite their world-class discipline, high technical competence, and proven operational resilience, their professional expertise remains structurally underutilized within our own domestic governance and state defense frameworks. Upon returning to civilian life or choosing to work shoreside, many seafarers face systemic bureaucratic obstacles to entering public service due to a lack of formal civil service eligibility tailored to their specialized experience. Furthermore, our country’s complex geopolitical reality and vulnerability to maritime security challenges and natural disasters necessitate a highly robust, capable, and readily deployable military reserve force. Our seafarers possess invaluable, pre-existing expertise in maritime domain awareness, navigation, marine engineering, communications, and emergency response—skills that would take years and massive state capital to train from scratch. This bill seeks to bridge this gap through a dual-benefit approach. First, it grants automatic Civil Service Eligibility to Filipino seafarers who have successfully completed at least two (2) years of accredited sea service. This integration empowers them to seamlessly transition into crucial civilian administrative, management, and technical positions within the government, particularly in maritime-related regulatory bodies like the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA), the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), and the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW). Second, this measure mandates the automatic incorporation of these qualified seafarers into the Reserve Force of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) as reserve officers or enlisted personnel, subject to standard orientation and background checks. This dramatically fortifies our national defense posture, strategic maritime domain awareness, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) capabilities by integrating an active, disciplined elite corps of ocean-tested mariners. By passing this measure, the state structurally honors the sacrifices of our seafarers, enhances their career trajectories, and strategically harnesses their exceptional talent for national development and territorial defense. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 10048
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING POSTHARVEST FACILITIES IN EVERY RICE, CORN, AND HIGH-VALUE CROP PRODUCING CITY OR MUNICIPALITY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Agriculture remains a vital pillar of the Philippine economy, providing livelihoods for millions of Filipinos and ensuring food security for the entire nation. However, our agricultural sector continues to grapple with a persistent and costly challenge: high post-harvest losses. Due to a severe lack of modern, accessible post-harvest facilities—such as drying systems, cold storage units, milling facilities, and warehouses—Filipino farmers are often forced to dry their grains on public roads or sell their fresh produce immediately at heavily depressed prices to avoid spoilage. According to the Philippine Center for Postharvest Development and Mechanization (PHilMech), post-harvest losses in rice and corn alone can range from 10% to 15%, while losses in high-value crops like fruits and vegetables can skyrocket up to 30% to 40% due to rapid degradation in our tropical climate. These losses translate directly to diminished incomes for our marginalized farmers and higher food prices for consumers. Moreover, it undermines national food self-sufficiency, forcing the country to rely heavily on agricultural imports. This bill seeks to address this systemic bottleneck by mandating the establishment of modern, climate-resilient post-harvest facilities in every rice, corn, and high-value crop-producing city or municipality nationwide. Investing in post-harvest infrastructure is not just an agricultural strategy; it is a direct intervention for poverty alleviation and national food security. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 10049
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SAFE INTERNET EDUCATION PROGRAM IN THE CURRICULUM OF ALL ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The internet has become an indispensable tool for education, communication, and daily life. However, the digital landscape also exposes young learners to severe risks, including cyberbullying, online scams, identity theft, exposure to age-inappropriate content, and online child sexual exploitation and abuse. While students are highly adept at navigating digital interfaces, they often lack the critical thinking skills and psychological readiness to identify digital threats, protect their personal data, and practice responsible digital citizenship. Leaving digital literacy entirely to parental supervision is no longer sufficient, as many parents struggle to keep pace with rapid technological advancements. A structured, proactive approach is necessary. This bill seeks to institutionalize a Safe Internet Education Program within the mandatory curriculum of all public and private elementary and secondary schools. By integrating age-appropriate lessons on digital safety, data privacy, and online ethics into existing subjects, we empower the next generation to navigate the digital world safely, responsibly, and productively. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 10050
title: AN ACT GRANTING DISTINCTIVE HONORS AND PRIVILEGES TO NATIONAL ATHLETES, CREATING A NATIONAL ENDOWMENT FUND FOR SPORTS HEROES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Sports bring Filipinos together, inspire national pride, and showcase the country's talent and determination on the world stage. Every time a Filipino athlete competes internationally, whether in the Olympic Games, World Championships, or regional sporting events, they carry not only our flag but also the hopes and aspirations of the nation. Through their discipline, perseverance, and sacrifices, they become symbols of Filipino excellence and resilience. Yet behind every medal and victory is a story of years of relentless training, physical hardship, and personal sacrifice. While these athletes dedicate the best years of their lives to representing the country, many face uncertainty once their competitive careers come to an end. After retirement, some struggle with financial difficulties, lingering injuries, limited employment opportunities, and inadequate access to healthcare. Despite the recognition they receive during their athletic careers, many are left without sufficient long-term support. Although Republic Act No. 10699, otherwise known as the National Athletes and Coaches Benefits and Incentives Act, provides cash incentives and benefits for outstanding athletic achievements, it does not establish a comprehensive system that ensures the continued welfare, health, and dignity of our national athletes after retirement. By passing this measure, the State affirms that the service and sacrifices of our athletes do not end when they leave the playing field. Those who have devoted their lives to bringing honor and glory to the Philippines deserve more than applause and medals they deserve lasting security, dignity, and the assurance that the nation they proudly represented will continue to stand by them for the rest of their lives. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. ELISA T. label: HB 10052
title: AN ACT ENSURING THE RIGHTS, WELFARE, AND SAFETY OF THE WORKERS IN THE INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING (IT-BPO) INDUSTRY IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Information Technology and Business Process Outsourcing (IT-BPO) industry is a key driver of the Philippine economy, generating approximately US$38 billion in revenues and employing around 1.8 million Filipinos as of 2024. It contributes roughly 8% of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and serves as a major source of foreign exchange, while also supporting jobs in allied sectors such as real estate, transportation, and retail. Despite its economic importance, workers in the IT-BPO sector continue to face unique challenges, including night shift work, high performance demands, job insecurity, and emerging health risks associated with remote and hybrid work arrangements. Studies have shown that prolonged night shift work and high-stress environments can lead to sleep disorders, fatigue, and mental health concerns. Existing labor laws provide general protections but do not fully address the specific conditions of IT-BPO work. There is thus a need for a sector-specific framework that ensures fair treatment, safe working conditions, and adequate health protections for employees. This bill seeks to establish a comprehensive set of rights and welfare mechanisms tailored to IT-BPO workers, including strengthened occupational health and safety standards, protection from unfair labor practices, and promotion of employee well-being. By safeguarding the workforce, this measure aims to sustain the industry’s growth, enhance its global competitiveness, and ensure that its economic benefits remain inclusive and equitable. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 10053
title: AN ACT DECLARING EVERY THIRD WEEK OF NOVEMBER AS “NATIONAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP WEEK”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 14, Article XII of the 1987 Philippine Constitution provides that the State shall promote the sustained development of a reservoir of Filipino entrepreneurs and managers. The Philippines remains a highly entrepreneurial economy, with micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) continuing to serve as the backbone of national development. According to the latest available data from the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), based on the 2023 List of Establishments of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), there are approximately 1.2 million business enterprises operating in the country. Of these, 99.6% are MSMEs, while only about 0.4% are large enterprises. Micro enterprises account for roughly 89% of total MSMEs, followed by small enterprises at around 10%, and medium enterprises at less than 1% (DTI, 2024; PSA, 2023).1 MSMEs play a critical role in employment generation and economic activity, contributing approximately 63% of total employment in the Philippines 1 Department of Trade and Industry (DTI). (2024). MSME Statistics. https://www.dti.gov.ph/resources/msme- statistics/ Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). (2023). 2023 List of Establishments and a significant share in value creation across industries. Despite their dominance, many Filipino entrepreneurs—particularly startups and small business owners—continue to face persistent challenges, including limited access to finance, gaps in digital and financial literacy, and insufficient exposure to modern business practices. One of the most pressing constraints encountered by current and aspiring entrepreneurs is the lack of adequate knowledge in business development, innovation, and financial management, particularly at the early stages of enterprise formation. Strengthening entrepreneurial education and cultivating an entrepreneurial mindset among the youth are therefore crucial to sustaining inclusive economic growth. The institutionalization of a week-long national celebration on entrepreneurship seeks to address these gaps by encouraging the youth to become self-starters, innovators, and job creators. Such a celebration will expose students and aspiring entrepreneurs to the vast opportunities in enterprise development, while providing a platform for successful Filipino entrepreneurs to share their experiences, insights, and best practices through forums, workshops, and other learning activities. It is imperative for the government to take proactive steps in fostering a culture of entrepreneurship by promoting awareness, enhancing skills development, and equipping the youth with fundamental business competencies. In doing so, the State strengthens the foundation for a more resilient, innovative, and inclusive Philippine economy. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 10054
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE COMPLEMENTARITY OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS IN IMPROVING STUDENT CHOICE AND THE DELIVERY OF QUALITY AND ACCESSIBLE EDUCATION ACROSS ALL LEVELS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates and instructs the State to protect and promote the right of all citizens to have access to quality education at all levels and to ensure that all the necessary steps are taken for such to be accessible to all. It further recognizes the complementary role of both public and private educational institutions in attaining that goal thus requiring the need for policies that strengthen both sectors. In spite of this, the mechanisms for ensuring true complementarity remain underdeveloped, resulting in inefficiency, limited options for students, and highly inequitable access to quality education nationwide. The Philippine education system has struggled with congestion, a problem that worsened during the COVID-19 pandemic. There was a significant shift from private to public schools, overwhelming the latter's resources and leading to overcrowded classrooms. This influx also left private schools with unused resources, leading to financial strain and, in some cases, permanent closures. According to DepEd spokesperson Michael Poa, up to 425 private schools have closed permanently since 2020, affecting over 20,000 students. Addressing this issue requires innovative solutions, such as fostering public-private partnerships (PPPs), which can bridge the gap between the undersupply of resources in public schools and the oversupply in private schools. Primarily, this bill seeks to institutionalize and further operationalize the complementarity between both public and private educational institutions by enhancing student choice, improving access, and elevating the quality of education across all levels of education from early childhood to higher education and technical-vocational training. It further aims to establish concrete mechanisms that will enable students to select from a diverse range of educational institutions based on learning outcomes rather than financial constraints. In order to achieve this, financial assistance programs such as student vouchers, grants, and loan schemes are further strengthened and targeted in order to promote cost- effectiveness, institutional diversity, and an increase in public-private partnerships in education. Second, this bill seeks to develop and implement a fair and transparent regulatory framework that upholds the academic freedom of institutions whilst still ensuring a high standard of education delivery. While ensuring that public investments in education are directed toward cost-effective and high-quality providers, this bill encourages public and private institutions to maximize on their strengths while concurrently promoting the use of shared facilities, management partnerships, and regional development programs. Alongside these improvements, the bill mandates the creation of an integrated educational information system across the Department of Education (DepEd), the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), and the Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) Council to facilitate informed decision-making among students, parents, and policymakers. Coordination and oversight to ensure the implementation of these initiatives shall be carried out by an established Partnership Board for Education Complementarity, composed of government agencies, private sector representatives, and education stakeholders. The said Board will be tasked with ensuring proper coordination, policy alignment, and accountability mechanisms that safeguard the quality and accessibility of education. By fostering stronger synergy between the public and private sectors, this bill aims to enhance the overall quality of Philippine education, reduce classroom congestion in public schools by utilizing private sector capacity, encouraging competition and innovation amongst educational institutions, and expanding student mobility through financial assistance programs. More importantly, it 2 ensures that education funding is utilized efficiently and equitably to benefit Filipino learners. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10055
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE DIGITAL READINESS OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS THROUGH THE DIGITAL HIGHER EDUCATION TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 1, Article XIV of the 1987 Philippine Constitution provides that “The State shall protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and shall take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all.” Likewise, Section 10, Article XIV declares that “Science and technology are essential for national development and progress. The State shall give priority to research and development, invention, innovation, and their utilization.” These provisions recognize that education and technology are inseparable drivers of inclusive national progress. In line with these constitutional mandates, the government must take deliberate measures to ensure that higher education institutions (HEIs) are equipped to respond to the realities of a rapidly changing, technology-driven world. The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the vulnerabilities of Philippine higher education, as institutions struggled to transition to online and blended learning due to inadequate infrastructure, uneven faculty training, and persistent digital divides. These challenges revealed that digital transformation is no longer optional, but essential to guarantee access, resilience, and competitiveness in higher education. The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II), created under Republic Act No. 11899, has explicitly identified digital transformation and educational technologies as one of its priority reform areas in higher education. According to its framework, HEIs must become “digitally connected, innovative, and technologically capable, with infrastructure for digital transformation” to meet the needs of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (EDCOM II Priority Areas, 2023). EDCOM II also underscored the urgency of developing digital literacy, strengthening faculty competencies, and building equitable access to technology to ensure that all learners benefit from digital advances (EDCOM II Year 2 Report, 2025). This bill, therefore, seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive framework for the Digital Higher Education Transformation Act, which shall strengthen the digital readiness of higher education institutions by: • Upgrading digital infrastructure and connectivity in SUCs, LUCs, and private HEIs; • Building capacity of faculty, administrators, and students in digital literacy, pedagogy, and research; • Establishing national standards for online and blended learning, micro- credentials, and digital quality assurance; • Ensuring equitable access to digital education for underserved and disadvantaged learners; and • Aligning higher education with the digital economy and the recommendations of EDCOM II to make Philippine graduates globally competitive. By passing this measure will empower HEIs to serve as hubs of innovation, inclusion, and excellence, redefining their role in society and ensuring that no Filipino learner is left behind in the digital era. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. 2 FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10056
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE PROTECTION, PROMOTION, AND ENFORCEMENT OF STUDENT RIGHTS AND WELFARE IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, INSTITUTIONALIZING STUDENT SUPPORT SYSTEMS AND PARTICIPATION IN EDUCATION GOVERNANCE, STRENGTHENING DUE PROCESS IN DISCIPLINARY PROCEEDINGS, ENSURING SAFE AND INCLUSIVE LEARNING ENVIRONMENTS IN PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL SPACES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill, to be known as the Magna Carta of Student Rights and Welfare Act, affirms the State’s constitutional duty to prioritize education and to afford special protection to the youth. It recognizes students not merely as recipients of instruction but as essential partners in the educational process, contributors to social development, and active participants in democratic life. Anchored on the principles that education is a human right, a public good, and a public responsibility, the measure institutionalizes a comprehensive framework for the protection of student rights and welfare across senior high school, higher education, and technical-vocational pathways. It seeks to ensure that student welfare—covering access, participation, retention, completion, and lifelong learning—is not treated as ancillary, but as integral to quality and inclusive education. The proposed Act establishes clear guiding principles rooted in dignity, non-discrimination, transparency, restorative discipline, and responsible use of technology. It safeguards meaningful and non-tokenistic student participation in governance, protects students from harassment, discrimination, red-tagging, retaliation, and privacy-invasive practices, and mandates accessible and impartial grievance redress mechanisms, including the creation of Student Ombud services. In recognition of the growing digitalization of education, it also provides protections against opaque or discriminatory uses of artificial intelligence and technology-assisted decision-making. The measure promotes coordination and policy coherence among the Commission on Higher Education, the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, and the Department of Education to ensure integrated delivery of student welfare services and smooth transitions across learning pathways. Ultimately, this bill establishes minimum, enforceable standards applicable to all public and private educational institutions offering senior high school, higher education, and TVET programs. It clarifies key definitions, ensures that institutional rules and contracts are consistent with constitutionally protected student rights, and declares void any policy inconsistent with the Act, without precluding the adoption of more protective measures. By institutionalizing a coherent and rights-based student welfare framework, this measure strengthens democratic participation in education, enhances accountability and fairness in institutional practices, and affirms the State’s commitment to nurturing empowered, protected, and engaged learners. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. 2 FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10057
title: AN ACT CREATING AN ADVANCED STUDIES DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR EXCEPTIONAL EMPLOYEES FROM THE GOVERNMENT AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Human capital is the foundation of national progress. In an increasingly knowledge-driven and innovation-centered global economy, the Philippines must invest deliberately and strategically in developing a critical mass of highly skilled professionals who can lead in science, technology, research, and other disciplines essential to economic transformation. While the country produces talented graduates and professionals, there remains a pressing need to systematically nurture exceptional individuals who can acquire advanced expertise from leading international institutions and translate such knowledge into tangible national gains. The proposed Pensionado Act institutionalizes a forward-looking and merit-based fellowship program designed to cultivate first-rate specialists who will serve as catalysts of innovation, productivity, and policy excellence. This measure establishes the Pensionado Program under the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), in coordination with key development agencies, to provide fellowships for exceptionally capable and highly motivated Filipinos from government, the private sector, and the self-employed sector. The Program shall support advanced studies and research in priority disciplines identified as vital to national development. It creates a National Secretariat to oversee administration, coordination of foreign and local grants, and reintegration of scholars, as well as a Selection Panel composed of distinguished academic leaders to ensure integrity and merit in the selection process. The fellowship shall provide comprehensive support, including paid study leave, travel, stipends, research allowances, and insurance, through a cost-sharing mechanism between the National Government and the scholar’s employer, with opportunities for international cost-sharing arrangements. Crucially, the bill ensures that public investment yields measurable national returns. Pensionados shall be required to render return service equivalent to twice the period of their fellowship and to share their expertise through seminars, training programs, and research engagement. A National Network of Specialized Institutes for Advanced Studies shall be developed to provide returning scholars with platforms for sustained collaboration, innovation, and policy contribution. By consolidating and strategically managing scholarship grants, the State positions itself to harness global knowledge for domestic advancement. Ultimately, the Pensionado Act strengthens the country’s long- term competitiveness by building a community of elite Filipino professionals committed to national service and transformative leadership. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10058
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING COMPREHENSIVE MEASURES TO ADDRESS CHILD SAFETY AGAINST GUN VIOLENCE, STRENGTHENING SCHOOL SAFETY AND SECURITY, REGULATING ACCESS AND USE OF FIREARMS, ESTABLISHING ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE On 22 June 2026, two students, aged 14 and 15, opened fire inside San Jose National High School in Tacloban City, Leyte, killing three of their classmates and wounding several others. A .38 caliber revolver and a 9mm semi-automatic pistol were used, one of which was registered to a suspect’s aunt, a non-commissioned police officer. The two student-suspects had reportedly planned the attack in advance, discussing the assault online before carrying it out.1 The tragedy of the Tacloban shooting has exposed grave and longstanding gaps in our legal framework governing school safety, firearms regulation, and the welfare of minors.2 It was followed within days by two separate knife-related incidents in schools in Cavite, and by the disruption of a planned attack on another school in Tolosa, Leyte, all forming a pattern that the Department of Education (DepEd) has described as a “high-alert situation” nationwide.3 1 Republic of the Philippines, Department of Education, Statement on the San Jose National High School Incident, Tacloban City (June 22, 2026); Police Regional Office 8, Report on the Tacloban City School Shooting Incident (June 24, 2026). 2 Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring & Jerry Yubal Jr., School shooting in Tacloban: What we know so far, RAPPLER (June 22, 2026). 3 Philippine Daily Inquirer, School shooting kills 3 students in Tacloban (June 23, 2026); Philstar.com, This Act is our nuanced response to this emerging threat. While laws on gun ownership and possession exist, they are not tailored to specifically address the reality of minors gaining access to and learning how to use firearms, especially in and out of households where adults are licensed to own and operate the same. This Bill seeks to address: (1) the unauthorized possession of firearms by minors, (2) the regulation of minors’ access to firearms training and shooting or firing ranges; (3) the civil and administrative liability of parents, guardians, firearm licensees, shooting range and gun club operators, as well as of school officials who fail to act on credible threats of armed violence; (4) the strengthening of school security and emergency preparedness, and (5) the reinforcement of anti-bullying enforcement, guidance counseling, and intervention programs for at-risk youth. No single law can guarantee that what happened in Tacloban will never happen again. But the State owes its children, their parents, and their teachers nothing less than a society that does everything within its power to prevent it. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. PERCIVAL V. CENDAÑA Akbayan Representative JOSE MANUEL TADEO DADAH KIRAM ISMULA “CHEL” I. DIOKNO Akbayan Representative Akbayan Representative KAKA BAG-AO Dinagat Islands Representative Tacloban school shooting leaves 3 dead, 5 injured (June 23, 2026). label: HB 10066
title: AN ACT HONORING AND GRANTING ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO EXEMPLARY CITIZENS OF BARANGAY KALIGAYAHAN, DISTRICT V, QUEZON CITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The barangay, as one’s immediate community, plays a significant role in one’s personal growth and development as one creates ties to peers, the local sports team, and their neighborhood and its residents. As such, it is important that the barangay is a safe setting where correct values are appreciated and positive influences are reinforced. In this era of digital technology, however, people are more susceptible to various forms of influence through multimedia sources, making them more exposed to external influences. The rise of microcelebrities in the form of social media influencers has been widespread, causing millions of followers on the digital platform. Although many influencers have had positive effects on followers, especially in pushing for various social advocacies, studies have shown that exposure and consumption of social media are highly linked with tendencies of depression, anxiety, and antisocial personality disorder, to name a few, which can lead to impairments in vital areas of life. This initiative seeks to promote the beneficial effects of influencers at the barangay level, where people can relate to, engage with, and interact with one another in person rather than online. These community influencers could be leaders and champions in public service, volunteer or civic organizations, or they could be strong advocates for education, climate change impact, reproductive health, and care for the elderly, among others. The purpose of this measure is to honor and celebrate excellent residents of the Barangay, naming them “Pambihirang Mamayan ng Kaligayahan”, who can influence others within the barangay and inspire more leaders and champions in the community who may serve as role models, particularly for the younger generations. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is urgently sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 10068
title: AN ACT HONORING AND GRANTING ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO EXEMPLARY CITIZENS OF BARANGAY SAN AGUSTIN, DISTRICT V, QUEZON CITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The barangay, as one’s immediate community, plays a significant role in one’s personal growth and development as one creates ties to peers, the local sports team, and their neighborhood and its residents. As such, it is important that the barangay is a safe setting where correct values are appreciated and positive influences are reinforced. In this era of digital technology, however, people are more susceptible to various forms of influence through multimedia sources, making them more exposed to external influences. The rise of microcelebrities in the form of social media influencers has been widespread, causing millions of followers on the digital platform. Although many influencers have had positive effects on followers, especially in pushing for various social advocacies, studies have shown that exposure and consumption of social media are highly linked with tendencies of depression, anxiety, and antisocial personality disorder, to name a few, which can lead to impairments in vital areas of life. This initiative seeks to promote the beneficial effects of influencers at the barangay level, where people can relate to, engage with, and interact with one another in person rather than online. These community influencers could be leaders and champions in public service, volunteer or civic organizations, or they could be strong advocates for education, climate change impact, reproductive health, and care for the elderly, among others. The purpose of this measure is to honor and celebrate excellent residents of the Barangay, naming them “Pambihirang Mamayan ng San Agustin”, who can influence others within the barangay and inspire more leaders and champions in the community who may serve as role models, particularly for the younger generations. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is urgently sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 10077
title: AN ACT HONORING AND GRANTING ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO EXEMPLARY CITIZENS OF BARANGAY FAIRVIEW, DISTRICT V, QUEZON CITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The barangay, as one’s immediate community, plays a significant role in one’s personal growth and development as one creates ties to peers, the local sports team, and their neighborhood and its residents. As such, it is important that the barangay is a safe setting where correct values are appreciated and positive influences are reinforced. In this era of digital technology, however, people are more susceptible to various forms of influence through multimedia sources, making them more exposed to external influences. The rise of microcelebrities in the form of social media influencers has been widespread, causing millions of followers on the digital platform. Although many influencers have had positive effects on followers, especially in pushing for various social advocacies, studies have shown that exposure and consumption of social media are highly linked with tendencies of depression, anxiety, and antisocial personality disorder, to name a few, which can lead to impairments in vital areas of life. This initiative seeks to promote the beneficial effects of influencers at the barangay level, where people can relate to, engage with, and interact with one another in person rather than online. These community influencers could be leaders and champions in public service, volunteer or civic organizations, or they could be strong advocates for education, climate change impact, reproductive health, and care for the elderly, among others. The purpose of this measure is to honor and celebrate excellent residents of the Barangay, naming them “Pambihirang Mamayan ng Fairview”, who can influence others within the barangay and inspire more leaders and champions in the community who may serve as role models, particularly for the younger generations. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is urgently sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 10082
title: AN ACT ENHANCING THE STATUTORY BENEFITS AND INCENTIVES OF PUBLIC HEALTH WORKERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7305, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MAGNA CARTA OF PUBLIC HEALTH WORKERS,” AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to expand the statutory benefits and incentives granted to public health workers. It amends Republic Act (RA) No. 7305, otherwise known as the “Magna Carta of Public Health Workers”, to guarantee increased compensation for overtime work, and work performed during rest days and special holidays. Public health workers continuously provide their indispensable services despite long working hours, hazardous working conditions, and public health emergencies. Despite the enactment of RA 7305, the benefits provided fail to adequately match the demands and risks inherent in public health service. This measure requires overtime, rest day, and special holiday work to be compensated exclusively in cash. It also increases the night shift differential, hazard, subsistence, and laundry allowances to accurately reflect the amount needed by our public health workers on the ground. The provision of adequate compensation is essential to protect the welfare of public health workers, improve workforce retention, and sustain an efficient and resilient public healthcare system. Ensuring that those who safeguard the nation’s health receive benefits that reflect their current needs is a necessary investment in the quality and continuity of public health services. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10083
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF AND PROVIDING FOR EXTENDED PATERNITY LEAVE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8187, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PATERNITY LEAVE ACT OF 1996”, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to increase the duration of paternity leaves from seven (7) to thirty (30) working days. It expands Republic Act (RA) No. 8187, otherwise known as the “Paternity Leave Act of 1996” to extend its coverage to all male employees regardless of civil or employment status, and recognizes partners in exclusive cohabiting relationships who have no legal impediment to marry. Paternal involvement during the postnatal period improves family well-being, strengthens child development, supports maternal health, advances gender equality in the home and the workplace, and promotes shared parental responsibility. Despite the enactment of RA No. 8187, the existing seven (7-)-day paternity leave is such an insufficient time for fathers to provide the support that their partners’ needs. This proposed measure also recognizes that many Filipino families are formed outside marriage but deserve equal support during childbirth. Thus, it extends the paternity leave benefits to soon-to-be fathers in exclusive cohabiting relationships. It also includes miscarries and emergency pregnancy termination among the circumstances covered by the paternity leave. Expanding paternity leave affirms the State’s commitment to protect the basic unit of society, promote the welfare of parents and their children, and encourage shared parental responsibility. It ensures that the law keeps pace with evolving family structures while providing fathers with meaningful opportunities to participate in the care and upbringing of their children. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10084
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SELLING AND BUYING OF ADMISSION TICKETS THROUGH UNAUTHORIZED SALES CHANNELS, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to protect consumers from ticket scalping and fraudulent transactions. It prohibits the buying and selling of admission tickets through unauthorized sales channels. Admission tickets are intended to provide the public with fair and equal access to entertainment events. However, the growth of online marketplaces and digital payment platforms has enabled unauthorized sellers to profit from ticket resale at the expense of legitimate consumers. Tickets acquired through unauthorized channels are often sold at steep prices, duplicated, or sometimes rendered invalid. It leaves buyers vulnerable to fraud and denies genuine patrons the opportunity to purchase tickets at their intended price. Ticket scalpers exploit high demand through bulk purchases which distorts the market and creates a picture of fake scarcity. Instead of rewarding genuine patrons, these practices inflate prices and divert sales away from authorized ticket distributors. Aside from prohibiting the unauthorized sale of admission tickets above their face value, this proposed measure also restricts the use of automated software and other schemes to unfairly acquire tickets for resale, and penalizes violations. It further requires event organizers and ticket sellers to adopt stronger safeguards, provide transparent pricing information, and implement measures that discourage ticket scalping to protect the public from fraudulent transactions. Entertainment events should be enjoyed by the public, not exploited for excessive profit. This measure ensures that admission tickets remain accessible through legitimate channels, giving fans fair opportunities to attend events they support while reinforcing public confidence in the ticketing system. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10085
title: AN ACT EXPANDING ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITY AND UPGRADING PENALTIES FOR IMPAIRED DRIVING TO FURTHER STRENGTHEN NATIONWIDE ROAD SAFETY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10586, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI-DRUNK AND DRUGGED DRIVING ACT OF 2013”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to strengthen Republic Act (RA) No. 10586, otherwise known as the “Anti-Drunk and Drugged Driving Act of 2013”. It upgrades penalties for impaired driving, expands enforcement authority, and institutionalizes proactive measures to further prevent alcohol and drug-impaired driving. Driving under the influence of alcohol or dangerous drugs remains a serious threat to public safety. Despite the enactment of RA No. 10586, impaired driving continues to endanger the traveling public and signals a need for stronger deterrence and more effective enforcement. Further, existing penalties no longer adequately reflect the gravity of the offense or its consequences. This measure imposes higher penalties for violations resulting in serious physical injury or homicide, strengthens administrative sanctions on driver’s license, and provides for the periodic review of penalties to ensure that they remain effective and responsive. It likewise requires the continuous acquisition and maintenance of roadside testing equipment and expands its testing in high risk areas. It institutionalizes public awareness campaigns and provides preventive measures that discourage impaired driving before motorists take the wheel. Effective road safety laws require both meaningful penalties and reliable enforcement. This vital piece of legislation shall not only improve compliance with the law, but also deter impaired driving and better protect the lives and welfare of the Filipino people. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10086
title: AN ACT DEFINING AND PROHIBITING OVERCAPACITY OR OVERLOADING IN PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION, PRESCRIBING STIFFER PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to prohibit overcapacity or overloading in public transportation. It establishes clear standards of passenger capacity in public utility vehicles to protect the commuting public. Public transportation serves as the primary means of mobility for millions of Filipinos. Overloading remains a practice in both land and water transport which exposes passengers to preventable risks. Carrying passengers beyond the authorized capacity not only increases the likelihood of accidents resulting in injury or worse, loss of life, but also impairs emergency response and evacuation efforts. The sinking of the MV Trisha Kerstin 3 off of Baluk-Baluk Island in Basilan in January 2026 cost the lives of fifty-eight (58) people and left several others missing. The Department of Transportation identified possible overloading as one of the factors that may have compromised the vessel and contributed to the tragedy1. This has raised serious concerns over passenger safety and demonstrates the need for stronger safeguards to ensure strict compliance with authorized passenger capacities. This measure mandates loading control measures, passenger counting and documentation procedures to further strengthen regulatory enforcement. It establishes accountability among drivers, conductors, operators, owners. Safe public transportation must never be compromised by commercial gain or operational convenience. This measure reaffirms the State’s commitment to protecting the lives and welfare of the commuting public and advances a culture of accountability, discipline, and safety across the transportation sector In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE SALARY GRADE OF DENTISTS EMPLOYED IN THE PUBLIC SECTOR, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to upgrade the salary grades of dentists employed in the public sector. It ensures that their compensation remains commensurate with their qualifications, scope of practice, and specialized competencies. Oral health is an integral component of a person’s overall health. Dentists provide preventive, diagnostic, curative, and rehabilitative dental services that reduce the burden of oral diseases and improve the overall quality of life of individuals and communities. Public dentists likewise serve as frontline providers of oral healthcare in public hospitals, government health facilities, and underserved communities where access to dental services remains limited. Despite their responsibilities, the existing salary structure for public dentists has become less competitive relative to the demands of the profession and opportunities available in the private sector and overseas. This weakens the government’s ability to attract and retain qualified dentists and contributes to workforce shortages in public health facilities. This measure establishes a more equitable salary structure for public dentists across all levels of government service and recognizes their indispensable value in the health sector. Investing in public dentists strengthens the government’s capacity to deliver equitable health services, expands access to quality dental care, and affirms the State’s commitment to promoting the health and well-being of every Filipino. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10088
title: AN ACT DECLARING A CLIMATE CHANGE EMERGENCY AND ENHANCING RESILIENCY AND ADAPTABILITY TO THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a Climate Change Resiliency and Adaptability Program and declare a climate change emergency to strengthen the country’s resilience and adaptive capacity for climate action. According to the 2021 Global Climate Risk Index, the Philippines ranks as the fourth most affected globally by weather-related events. The same report showed that approximately sixty percent (60%) of the country’s land area and seventy-four percent (74%) of its population are exposed to multiple natural hazards. Since 1990, the Philippines has endured five hundred sixty five (565) climate-related disasters which has resulted in the tragic loss of more than seventy thousand (70,000) lives and billions in damages1. Historically, typhoons, floods, and droughts have been responsible for rice losses which has placed the impact among the poorest sectors who depend on climate-sensitive livelihoods and manual labor. The measure institutionalizes climate risk assessments, promotes open climate data systems, integrates climate resilience across education curricula, and supports climate-resilient infrastructures. It likewise reinforces accountability through annual reporting and regular consultations to ensure the continuous evaluation and improvement of climate policies and programs. Climate resilience is essential to safeguarding the nation’s people, economy, environment, and future. Strengthening the country’s capacity to anticipate, withstand, and recover from climate related risks advances sustainable development and reaffirms the State’s commitment to build a safer and more resilient Philippines. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. YAP 1 United Nations Environment Programme. Philippines Climate Change. label: HB 10089
title: AN ACT EXPANDING HEALTH, WELLNESS, AND DIGITAL INCLUSION PROGRAMS FOR SENIOR CITIZENS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9994, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZENS ACT OF 2010”, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to further strengthen Republic Act (RA) No. 9994, otherwise known as the “Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010”. It expands health and wellness programs provided to senior citizens, and provides for the inclusion of digital inclusion programs to promote their digital literacy. The number of senior citizens in the country continue to grow as life expectancy improves and demographic trends point toward an aging population. The Philippine Statistics Authority reported that Filipinos aged sixty (60) and above account for more than nine percent (9.6%) of the country’s one hundred and thirteen million (113.7) million population. While this remains below the ten percent (10%) threshold used by World Bank to define an aging society, the country’s senior citizen population is projected to double by 2035-20401. This highlights the need to strengthen programs that promote healthy, active, and dignified aging. This measure expands the government assistance provided to our senior citizens by requiring annual preventive health check-ups, community-based wellness and rehabilitation services, home and mobile healthcare for vulnerable seniors, and expanded access to telemedicine. It also institutionalizes nationwide digital literacy and inclusion programs to equip our elderly with the knowledge and skills necessary to safely access digital technologies and government services to close the digital divide once and for all. More than strengthening health, wellness, and digital inclusion programs extended to our senior citizens for them to live healthier, safer, and more productive lives in a digital society, this vital piece of legislation reinforces the State’s commitment to safeguard the welfare, dignity, and well-being of our senior citizens. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this bill is immediately sought. HON. ERIC G. YAP 1 MOAJE, Marita (2026). Nat’l discussion on aging timely as senior population hits 11M. label: HB 10090
title: AN ACT CREATING THE POSITION OF BARANGAY NUTRITION WORKER IN EVERY BARANGAY, PROVIDING INCENTIVES THERETO, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a Barangay Nutrition Worker position in every barangay in the country. It institutionalizes a dedicated personnel for nutrition promotion, disease prevention, and child development, and shall strengthen the delivery of community-based nutrition services. The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II) reported that the stunting rate among children under five (5) years old has reached twenty-five percent (25%). This represents one (1) in four (4) children in the country. This is the first increase in a decade and classified malnutrition and stunting as a high public health concern. These conditions impair physical growth, cognitive development, educational attainment while imposing long-term social and economic costs. Despite the enactment of Presidential Decree No. 1569, entitled “Strengthening the Barangay Nutrition Program by Providing for a Barangay Nutrition Scholar in Every Barangay, Providing Funds Therefor, and For Other Purposes”, its reliance on a purely volunteer framework with token incentives has proven insufficient against the current economic landscape and increasing public health challenges of the country. Nearly five (5) decades after its implementation, the evolving gravity of our nutritional crisis demands the transition to a volunteer system into a professional and properly compensated workforce. Although nutrition programs exist at the national and local level, their implementation is often impeded by the absence of personnel exclusively tasked to oversee nutrition interventions in the community. This bill requires every barangay to appoint a qualified Barangay Nutrition Worker and establishes standards for recruitment, training, supervision, benefits and incentives. It also ensures that each community has trained personnel dedicated to nutrition-related services and interventions. Strengthening the nutrition workforce at the barangay level is an investment to public health and human capital. Placing a barangay nutrition worker in every barangay shall improve access to essential nutrition services, support healthier communities, and contribute to the reduction of malnutrition nationwide. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G.
