label: HB 10091
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING EQUAL CRIMINAL LIABILITY AND PENALTIES FOR MARITAL INFIDELITY AND MAINTAINING A PARAMOUR, PROMOTING GENDER EQUALITY AND UPHOLDING THE SANCTITY OF MARRIAGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE REVISED PENAL CODE”, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish equal criminal liability and penalties for marital infidelity. It amends Articles 333, 334, and 344 of Act No. 3815, otherwise known as “The Revised Penal Code”, to remove gender-based distinctions in the treatment of spouses. Marriage is recognized by the Constitution as an inviolable social institution and the foundation of the family. The legal obligation of fidelity is reciprocal and must be enforced without regard to the gender of the offending spouse. The existing provisions on adultery and concubinage impose unequal standards of criminal responsibility. A wife may be held criminally liable for a single act of sexual relations outside the marriage, while a husband incurs liability only under specific circumstances. Criminal laws shall therefore be updated to impose the same standard of conduct and corresponding penalties upon husbands and wives alike, thereby upholding the sanctity of marriage. The proposed measure reinforces the principles of equality before the law, fairness in the administration of justice, and mutual accountability within marriage. It ensures that the State’s protection of the marital institution is carried out through a legal framework that is impartial and consistent to contemporary standards of justice. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10092
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE GRANT OF A ONE-TIME INTERNSHIP ALLOWANCE FOR STUDENTS IN PUBLIC OR PRIVATE HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS AND TECHNICAL-VOCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to grant a one(1)-time internship allowance of Ten thousand pesos (Php 10,000.00) to qualified students in public and private higher education institutions and technical-vocational institutions who successfully complete their required internship, practicum, or on-the-job training (OJT). It provides financial assistance to help students fulfill this requirement and recognizes that experiential learning is an essential component of education. Internship and practicum programs equip students with practical skills, professional discipline, and workplace experience that improve their readiness for employment. However, the costs associated with transportation, meals, uniforms, and other documentary requirements needed for internships place an undue financial burden on students from low-income households. These costs may hinder a student’s ability to complete mandatory training despite meeting academic requirements. The provision of an internship allowance to students who have successfully completed their internships and OJTs helps defray expenses incurred during the training period. It also incentivizes the discipline and hard work these students invest both in themselves and the future of the country, while enabling them to complete their studies without unnecessary financial hardship. The support we extend to our students as they transition from academic instruction to workplace training strengthens the country’s human capital and reaffirms the State’s commitment to accessible and quality education and its investment in a more skilled, productive, and globally competitive workforce. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10093
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION OF THE JUDICIARY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide a long-term framework to upgrade court infrastructure, modernize judicial technology and equipment, and strengthen the development, welfare, and protection of judicial personnel to improve the administration of justice in the country. Article VIII, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution vests judicial power in one Supreme Court and in such lower courts as may be established by law. Article III, Section 16 likewise guarantees every person’s right to the speedy disposition of their cases before all judicial, quasi-judicial, and administrative bodies. The effective discharge of these constitutional mandates requires a Judiciary equipped with adequate facilities, reliable technology, modern equipment, and sufficient human resources. However, realities on the ground paint a different picture otherwise. Many courts continue to operate with outdated infrastructure, fragmented information systems, and inadequate personnel. This proposed measure institutionalizes a Judiciary modernization program that supports the construction and rehabilitation of court facilities, the deployment of secure information technology systems, the acquisition of modern equipment, and the continuous training, welfare, and protection of judicial personnel. A modern and capable Judiciary promotes the timely administration of justice, strengthens public confidence in the rule of law, improves access to judicial services, and enables the courts to exercise the judicial power vested in them by the Constitution. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10094
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR HOSPITAL BENEFITS AND OTHER PRIVILEGES FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS AND THEIR DEPENDENTS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to provide hospital benefits and other healthcare privileges to public school teachers and their qualified dependents. It grants discounts on consultations and other hospital services, and expands their Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) coverage for medical expenses. Public school teachers shoulder responsibilities that extend beyond classroom instruction. Amid the demands of the profession and rising healthcare costs, public school teachers and their families face financial and health-related risks that may affect their capacity to perform their duties and remain in public service. Republic Act (RA) No. 4670, otherwise known as the “Magna Carta for Public School Teachers”, provides annual medical examinations and protects teachers against work related illnesses and injuries. However, it does not provide hospital discounts, priority access to hospital services, expanded health insurance coverage, or healthcare benefits for qualified dependents. This measure augments the benefits provided under RA No. 4670 by providing discounts on consultations and other hospital services, fast lane facilities in government hospitals, and an additional ten percent (10%) PhilHealth coverage for public school teachers and their qualified dependents. The nation’s education system depends on the well-being of those entrusted to teach future generations. Expanding healthcare support for public school teachers affirms the State’s commitment to protecting the welfare of our public school teachers in recognition of their indispensable role in national development. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. label: HB 10095
title: AN ACT MANDATING INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDERS TO IMPLEMENT A ROLL-OVER DATA ALLOCATION SCHEME FOR UNUSED DATA, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to require internet service providers to allow subscribers to retain and use unused mobile and internet data allocations beyond the original subscription period. It establishes standards governing the utilization and conversion of unused data to ensure that consumers receive the full value of the services they have purchased. In 2025, the World Population Review reported that the Philippines has an average broadband cost of Fifteen dollars and Fifty one centavos ($15.51) or approximately Nine hundred sixty pesos (Php 960.00), which ranks fifth (5th) in Southeast Asia1. When adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) to reflect the actual cost of living, the relatively monthly cost triples to Forty three dollars and Thirty four centavos ($43.34) or around Two thousand six hundred and seventy pesos (Php 2,670.00). This shows that relative to local income, internet access takes up a significant portion of a Filipino household’s monthly budget. Despite paying for these fixed data allocations, subscribers often lose unused data once their subscription expires. This results in unconsumed services that internet service providers profit from without delivering. To protect consumers from this systemic loss, this measure mandates internet service providers to implement a roll over data allocation scheme which automatically carries over any unused data at the end of a billing cycle to the succeeding month. This ensures that consumers can fully utilize the services they paid for without expiration dates. This measure affirms the State’s commitment to safeguarding consumer rights while fostering a fair, transparent, and inclusive digital economy. Protecting consumers from the forfeiture of paid internet services supports broader efforts to improve access to affordable and responsive digital services. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. ERIC G. YAP 1 World Population Review (2026). Internet Cost by Country 2026. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Land Transportation Office (LTO) is mandated to register motor vehicles, issue and renew driver's licenses, and enforce land transportation laws throughout the country. The accessibility of these services is a basic expectation of local government units and their constituents, particularly in provinces where distances between municipalities are considerable and public transportation is limited. At present, the entire Province of Nueva Vizcaya, comprising fifteen (15) municipalities, is served by a single LTO District Office located at the Capitol Compound, Municipality of Bayombong. Residents of the southern municipalities of the province — particularly Bambang, Aritao, Kasibu, Kayapa, Dupax Del Norte, Dupax Del Sur, and Sta. Fe — must travel a considerable distance, averaging approximately twenty-nine (29) kilometers from Aritao alone, just to transact with the LTO. This does not yet account for residents from farther upland municipalities such as Kayapa, who must traverse mountainous terrain to reach Bayombong. The Municipality of Aritao is a second-class municipality with twenty-two (22) barangays and a population of forty-five thousand (45,000) as of the 2024 Census, making it one of the most populous municipalities in the southern half of the province. It sits along the Maharlika Highway (AH26) and serves as the eastern terminus of the Benguet–Nueva Vizcaya Road connecting Nueva Vizcaya to Baguio City, making it a natural transport and trade hub for the neighboring municipalities of Kayapa, Santa Fe, Dupax del Sur, and Bambang, as well as the boundary municipality of Carranglan in the neighboring province of Nueva Ecija. The volume of vehicle registration, driver's license applications and renewals, and other LTO transactions in this part of the province has continued to grow alongside the area's population and economic activity, particularly in agriculture and trade along the Maharlika Highway corridor. The absence of a local LTO facility compels residents to shoulder additional transportation costs and lost productive time, and contributes to congestion at the Bayombong District Office. This inconvenience also creates conditions that make residents vulnerable to fixers and unauthorized transaction facilitators. This bill seeks to establish an LTO Extension Office in the Municipality of Aritao, Province of Nueva Vizcaya, to bring vehicle registration, licensing, and related transportation services closer to the residents of Aritao and its neighboring municipalities. This measure is consistent with the State's policy of ensuring accessible, efficient, and citizen-centered delivery of public services, particularly to communities located far from provincial and regional centers. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. TIMOTHY JOSEPH E. CAYTON, PhD. title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE PARENT-TEACHER-COMMUNITY ASSOCIATION SYSTEM IN BASIC EDUCATION, AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 603, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: SECTION 1. Short Title. — This Act shall be known as the “PTCA Institutionalization Act.” SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. — It is hereby declared the policy of the State to: (a) Promote participatory governance in the basic education sector by enabling parents, teachers, and community stakeholders to engage meaningfully in school and local education decision-making; (b) Strengthen the role of families and communities as active partners in ensuring learner welfare and the quality of basic education; (c) Institutionalize a multi-level PTCA structure that provides organizational continuity, accountability, and sustained engagement across the school, city or municipal, and provincial levels; and (d) Integrate the PTCA system into existing local governance mechanisms, particularly Local School Boards and Special Education Fund planning, consistent with Republic Act No. 7160. SEC. 3. Definition of Terms. — As used in this Act: (a) PTCA or School PTCA refers to the Parent-Teacher-Community Association organized at the school level pursuant to this Act and the implementing guidelines of the Department of Education; (b) City or Municipal PTCA Federation refers to the federation of all school PTCAs within a city or municipality, recognized and organized pursuant to
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State recognizes that quality basic education is not the exclusive responsibility of the Department of Education. It is a shared undertaking of families, communities, teachers, and government — one that requires sustained, structured collaboration at every level of the education system. Parent-Teacher-Community Associations (PTCAs) have long served as the principal mechanism for this collaboration. They are present in every public basic education school and are anchored, however thinly, in existing law. Their legal basis was written in 1974 as a narrow organizational mandate at the school level.1 It has never been updated by statute to reflect the governance architecture established by Republic Act No. 9155, the Local Government Code, or the practical needs of a decentralized education system. Studies show that sustained collaboration between parents and teachers can contribute to improved academic performance. On distance learning during the pandemic, researchers from the University of the Philippines Center for Integrative and Development Studies observed that teachers had come to treat parents as partners of their children to ensure that learning happens at home.2 Likewise, the Philippine Institute for Development Studies, found that parental support is consistently positively correlated with test scores,3 with the relationship strongest for low-performing students. The premise that this collaboration deserves stronger institutional footing is not a new one. The Supreme Court has already recognized that official PTA/PTCA recognition establishes the association as a pillar of the 1 Article 77 of Presidential Decree No. 603 , December 10, 1974. Dina S. Ocampo and Junette Fatima D. Gonzales, “Understanding Learners’ Home Contexts and Recommendations for Future School Scenarios,” UP CIDS Policy Brief 2022-04 (University of the Philippines Center for Integrative and Development Studies, 2022). 3Aniceto C. Orbeta Jr., Kris Ann M. Melad, and Maropsil V. Potestad, “Correlates of Test Performance of 15-year-old Students in the Philippines: Evidence from PISA,” PIDS Discussion Paper Series No. 2020-57 (Philippine Institute for Development Studies, Dec. 2020, updated Jan. 2021), Recommendation No. 3. educational system,4 and the Department of Education's own leadership, in issuing the current Omnibus PTA Guidelines, described the effort as one meant to strengthen the role of the PTA in schools.5 Neither the Court's characterization nor the Department's own guidelines, however, can supply what only a statute can: permanence. This Act amends Presidential Decree No. 603 to modernize the school-level PTCA in line with contemporary child welfare and education governance standards. In response to recent incidents of violence involving learners and school personnel, the Department of Education called for closer cooperation among schools, parents, and communities to strengthen school safety and child protection. As Education Secretary Sonny Angara observed, “Schools cannot do this alone. Parents cannot do this alone.” He further described the Parent-Teacher Association as “one of the most important bridges linking the family, school, and community.”6 These statements show that protecting learners and supporting their development require schools, families, and communities to work together. label: HB 10099
title: AN ACT REPEALING ARTICLE 266-C (THE “FORGIVENESS CLAUSE”) AND AMENDING ARTICLES 23, 89, AND 344 OF ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “REVISED PENAL CODE”, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8353, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE ANTI-RAPE LAW OF 1997”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article 266‑C of Act No. 3815, otherwise known as the Revised Penal Code, as amended by Republic Act No. 8353 or the Anti‑Rape Law of 1997, contains what has long been referred to as a “forgiveness clause.” Under this provision, the criminal action or penalty for rape may be extinguished either by the subsequent marriage of the offender and the victim, or, in cases where the offender is the husband, by the wife’s forgiveness. This clause reflects an outdated and harmful notion that marriage or pardon can erase the trauma of rape. In practice, it risks compelling victims to remain tied to their aggressors, thereby perpetuating cycles of abuse and enabling offenders to escape accountability. Such a legal mechanism undermines the seriousness of rape as a crime and diminishes the rights and dignity of women. The proposed measure seeks to repeal Article 266‑C and related provisions of the Revised Penal Code that allow marriage or forgiveness to absolve perpetrators of rape. Its passage affirms the principle that sexual violence is a grave offense that cannot be excused by marital status or personal pardon. This reform is aligned with the State’s constitutional duty to uphold human dignity, guarantee respect for human rights1, and ensure equality between women and men2. It also advances the objectives of Goal No. 5 of the United Nations 1 Article II, Section 11, 1987 Philippine Constitution 2 Article II, Section 14, 1987 Philippine Constitution Sustainable Development Goals, which calls for strengthened legislation to promote gender equality and empower women and girls. The Philippine Commission on Women has consistently included the repeal of the forgiveness clause in its Women’s Priority Legislative Agenda since the 15th Congress. The persistence of this provision in our laws is a glaring gap in the protection of women and survivors of sexual violence. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. DADAH KIRAM ISMULA Akbayan Representative JOSE MANUEL TADEO PERCIVAL V. CENDAÑA “CHEL” I. label: HB 10100
title: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 333 AND 344, AND REPEALING ARTICLE 334 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, TO REMOVE THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN ADULTERY AND CONCUBINAGE AND ESTABLISH A GENDER‑FAIR DEFINITION OF MARITAL INFIDELITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Revised Penal Code provides for a comprehensive legal framework that penalizes unfaithfulness and infidelity to the sanctity of marriage. It classifies adultery and concubinage as crimes against chastity, while the Family Code refers to them as sexual infidelity, or more generally, marital infidelity. Albeit both defined as marital infidelity, the existing legal frameworks penalizes them differently, effectively placing a greater burden on women or wives, than on men or husbands. Without a doubt, marital infidelity of varying degrees knows no gender or sex. A marriage in which a wife sows doubt, infidelity, and deceit is no different from a marriage in which a husband commits the same acts. The harm inflicted upon the marital union, the erosion of trust, and the betrayal of the obligations of marriage remain the same regardless of whether the offending party is the husband or the wife. The 1987 Philippine Constitution expressly provides that all Filipinos are afforded the same and equal protection under the law, regardless of gender or sex. Maintaining different standards for adultery and concubinage is inconsistent with the Constitution's guarantee of equal protection under the law. It therefore seeks to ensure that the law treats marital infidelity with the same measure of accountability, regardless of the gender of the offending spouse. The law must protect the institution of marriage without compromising the constitutional guarantee of equality before the law. This measure likewise gives effect to Section 12 of Republic Act No. 9710, otherwise known as the Magna Carta of Women, which guarantees women equal treatment before the law and mandates the review and amendment of laws that discriminate against women. The existing provisions under the Revised Penal Code that codify concubinage and adultery continue to prescribe different elements, standards of proof, and penalties for the same act of marital infidelity. The promise of equality before the law cannot be fulfilled if marital infidelity continues to be penalized differently based solely on the sex of the offending spouse. This bill therefore seeks to remove these distinctions and establish a single, gender-fair standard of marital infidelity consistent with the Constitution and existing law. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. DADAH KIRAM ISMULA Akbayan Representative JOSE MANUEL TADEO PERCIVAL V. CENDAÑA “CHEL” I. label: HB 10102
title: AN ACT PROMOTING INCLUSIVE AND SUSTAINABLE RURAL DEVELOPMENT AND LIVELIHOOD ENHANCEMENT IN THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to strengthen rural communities through a Rural Development National Framework. This entails fortifying livelihood opportunities, improving access to financial services, and enhancing rural infrastructure. The proposed measure aims to reduce rural poverty, improve economic productivity, and ensure that the benefits of national growth reach communities that have long remained underserved. Despite the country's sustained economic growth, many rural communities continue to experience high poverty incidence, limited employment opportunities, inadequate infrastructure, and restricted access to credit, technology, and markets. Farmers, fisherfolk, rural workers, and micro-entrepreneurs often struggle with low productivity, poor farm-to-market connectivity, limited value-adding opportunities, and increasing vulnerability to climate change and natural disasters. These longstanding challenges continue to widen the development gap between urban and rural areas and constrain inclusive economic growth. This measure adopts a comprehensive approach to rural development by strengthening livelihood generation, expanding access to affordable financial services, and improving rural infrastructure. It also promotes entrepreneurship, value chain development, and the enhancement of technical and digital skills to improve rural productivity and competitiveness. Moreover, it empowers local government units, cooperatives, and community organizations to actively participate in the planning, implementation, and monitoring of development programs. Rural development is fundamental to achieving food security, reducing inequality, generating employment, and promoting balanced national development. Investing in our rural communities goes far beyond an investment in agriculture. This move means our nation’s long-term economic resilience and inclusive growth are being prioritized. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 10103
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT AND WELL-BEING OF CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL NEEDS, PROVIDING FOR COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT SYSTEMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive national framework for the inclusive development, protection, and well-being of children with special needs. This is employed with the end in view of strengthening early intervention services, expanding access to inclusive education and healthcare, enhancing support systems for caregivers, and promoting public awareness. Children with special needs continue to face significant barriers in accessing timely diagnosis, therapy, quality education, and essential health services. Many families shoulder overwhelming financial costs for rehabilitation, specialized learning materials, assistive devices, and continuous medical care, often forcing parents to reduce working hours or leave employment altogether to provide full-time care. Despite existing laws protecting persons with disabilities, access to intervention services remains uneven, particularly in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas where specialized professionals and facilities are scarce.1 The urgency of strengthening support for children with special needs is underscored by both global and local evidence. According to the United Nations Children's Fund, nearly 240 million children worldwide are living with disabilities, many of whom experience poorer educational, health, and social outcomes than their peers.2 In the Philippines, the Department of Social Welfare and Development emphasizes that children with disabilities remain among the country's most vulnerable sectors, requiring strengthened early intervention, inclusive education, rehabilitation services, and community-based support to achieve meaningful inclusion.3 1 World Health Organization. Disability. World Health Organization. Accessed via www.who.int/news-room/fact -sheets/detail/disability-and-health. Accessed on 30 June 2026. 2 United National Children’s Fund (March 2024). The State of the World's Children 2024: The Future of Childhood in a Changing World. UNICEF. Accessed via https://www.unicef.org/reports/state-worlds-children-2024. Accessed on 30 June 2026. 3 Department of Social Welfare and Development. Study: In the Philippines, raising a child with a disability is 80% more expensive. Department of Social Welfare and Development. Accessed via https://fo3.dswd.gov.ph /2022/12/study-in-the-philippines-raising-a-child-with-a-disability-is-80-more-expensive/. Accessed on 13 July 2026. This measure mandates the establishment of accessible early intervention programs. It likewise strengthens inclusive education through teacher training and individualized learning support. In recognition of the medical and financial requirements of children with special needs, this bill covers for the expansion of PhilHealth coverage for therapies and assistive devices and provides vouchers and financial assistance to qualified families. At the community and national levels, the bill develops community-based support centers and caregiver training programs, as well as institutionalizes nationwide awareness campaigns. Every child deserves the opportunity to develop to their fullest potential regardless of disability or circumstance. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 10104
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A NATIONAL MEDICINE SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to institutionalize a comprehensive national telemedicine system, thereby establishing a regulatory and policy framework for the delivery of healthcare services through information and communications technology. Despite significant improvements in the country’s healthcare system, access to medical services remains uneven. Many Filipinos residing in remote, island, and underserved communities continue to face shortages of healthcare professionals, long travel distances to medical facilities, and delays in receiving essential medical care. These challenges become even more pronounced during public health emergencies and natural disasters, when mobility is restricted and health facilities become overwhelmed. Telemedicine has emerged as a practical and effective solution to bridge these gaps. During the COVID-19 pandemic, remote consultations enabled patients to continue receiving medical advice while reducing the risk of disease transmission. Digital health and telemedicine are recognized as key components of achieving Universal Health Care and strengthening the country's health system.1 However, the absence of a comprehensive legal framework has resulted in fragmented implementation, inconsistent standards, and limited interoperability among healthcare providers. This measure establishes telemedicine as an integral complement to conventional healthcare delivery. It establishes uniform standards for the practice of telemedicine, electronic prescriptions, data management, accreditation of providers, and patient protection. It likewise strengthens the country's capacity to deliver essential health services during public health emergencies and disasters through the strategic use of digital technologies. Strengthening access to quality healthcare remains a fundamental responsibility of the State to ensure that essential health services are accessible, 1 Padmanaban, S., Udayasankaran, J.G. (2021). Digital Health Accelerating Progress to Achieve UHC in the Philippines. Transform Health. Accessed via https://transformhealthcoalition.org/insights/digital-health -accelerating-progress-to-achieve-uhc-in-the-philippines-2/. Accessed on 13 July 2026. equitable, and responsive to the needs of all Filipinos. Advancements in information and communications technology present significant opportunities to improve healthcare delivery, particularly for geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, underserved communities, and during emergencies and disasters. Institutionalizing a national telemedicine framework will enable the integration of digital health technologies into the healthcare system, improve access to medical consultations and treatment, promote continuity of care, and enhance the overall efficiency and resilience of the country's health system. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. title: AN ACT REINSTITUTING ABSOLUTE DIVORCE AS AN ALTERNATIVE MODE FOR THE DISSOLUTION OF MARRIAGE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to reinstitute absolute divorce as an additional legal remedy for marriages that are beyond repair. It does not diminish the institution of marriage; rather, it recognizes that in exceptional circumstances, preserving individual dignity, personal safety, and the best interests of children requires a lawful mechanism for the dissolution of marriage. Under existing law, the dissolution of marriage is generally limited to annulment, declaration of nullity, or legal separation. These remedies are often expensive, time-consuming, and available only under limited legal grounds. Legal separation, moreover, does not dissolve the marital bond, leaving spouses unable to remarry despite prolonged separation or the complete breakdown of the marital relationship. As a result, many Filipinos remain trapped in failed marriages, exposing themselves and their children to continued emotional, psychological, and economic hardship. Comparative experience likewise demonstrates that the Philippines remains one of the few jurisdictions that does not generally recognize absolute divorce for its citizens. The absence of this remedy has created legal inequities, particularly for spouses who have long been separated or who are victims of domestic violence, abandonment, or repeated marital misconduct. The availability of divorce in other jurisdictions has shown that legal dissolution, when accompanied by adequate judicial safeguards and child protection measures, provides parties with legal certainty while promoting accountability and orderly settlement of family relations. This proposed measure provides specific and judicially determinable grounds for divorce, ensures due process before the Family Courts, and establishes safeguards against fraud, coercion, and collusion. It likewise preserves the legitimacy of children, protects their custody and support, provides for spousal support where warranted, governs the equitable distribution of property, and imposes penalties for non-compliance with court-ordered obligations. It further institutionalizes counseling, reconciliation mechanisms, legal assistance, and oversight measures to ensure that divorce remains a remedy of last resort while safeguarding vulnerable family members. Rather than the perceived weakening of marriage, this bill establishes a comprehensive legal framework for addressing exceptional cases where the marital relationship has irretrievably failed while ensuring that the rights of spouses, children, and third parties remain fully protected. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. HON. label: HB 10106
title: AN ACT REMOVING THE EXEMPTION FROM CRIMINAL LIABILITY FOR CRIMES OF THEFT, SWINDLING, AND MALICIOUS MISCHIEF INVOLVING PROPERTY OF RELATIVES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 332 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE REVISED PENAL CODE”, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to repeal Article 332 of Republic Act No. 3815, otherwise known as the Revised Penal Code, which exempts certain relatives from criminal liability for the crimes of theft, swindling, and malicious mischief committed against one another, leaving only civil liability. Article 332 was intended to preserve family harmony by treating certain property offenses among relatives as private disputes. However, changing social realities have shown that this exemption has, in some instances, been used to evade criminal accountability for acts involving abuse of trust, fraud, and intentional deprivation of property. Victims are often left without adequate legal protection solely because the offender is a relative. This measure removes the exemption and ensures that persons who commit theft, swindling, or malicious mischief against their relatives are held criminally liable in the same manner as offenders against any other person. In doing so, it strengthens the protection of property rights, upholds the equal application of the law, and reinforces the principle that familial relationships should never serve as a shield against criminal prosecution. The law must protect victims of crime regardless of their relationship with the offender. This measure promotes accountability, deters abuse, and affirms that justice should be applied equally to all. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. label: HB 10107
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES EXECUTIVE PREVENTIVE HEALTH PROGRAM, PROVIDING FREE ANNUAL EXECUTIVE HEALTH CHECKUPS FOR ALL GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Government employees are among the nation's most valuable assets. They are entrusted with delivering essential public services and implementing government programs that directly affect the lives of millions of Filipinos. However, the demands of public service often expose them to long working hours, occupational stress, sedentary lifestyles, and other health risks that contribute to hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, kidney disorders, cancer, mental health conditions, and other chronic illnesses. Unfortunately, many of these diseases remain asymptomatic during their early stages and are diagnosed only after they have significantly progressed, resulting in prolonged treatment, higher healthcare costs, loss of productivity, increased employee absenteeism, disability, and even premature death. While periodic medical examinations are required in certain government agencies, the scope, frequency, and quality of such examinations vary considerably. Many agencies are able to provide only basic pre-employment or annual physical examinations due to limited resources, while others have no structured preventive healthcare program at all. Consequently, government employees do not enjoy equal access to comprehensive preventive healthcare services. This bill seeks to establish the Government Employees Executive Preventive Health Program, a nationwide preventive healthcare initiative that guarantees every government employee one (1) free comprehensive Executive Health Checkup annually. Unlike the traditional Annual Physical Examination (APE), the Executive Health Checkup emphasizes early detection of chronic diseases through evidence-based diagnostic procedures, individualized health risk assessment, mental health screening, age-appropriate cancer screening, and preventive medical counseling. The measure likewise promotes a healthier and more productive bureaucracy by reducing avoidable illnesses, minimizing absenteeism, lowering long-term healthcare expenditures, and enabling early medical intervention before diseases become severe. Investing in preventive healthcare is ultimately an investment in efficient governance and better public service. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 10108
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FINANCIAL LITERACY AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP PROGRAMS FOR WORKERS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XII, Section 14 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution provides that the sustained development of a reservoir of national talents, which includes Filipino entrepreneurs and managers, shall be promoted by the State. The Philippines is an entrepreneurial country. Slowly, entrepreneurship is becoming the backbone of the country’s economy. Micro, small, and medium- sized enterprises (SMEs) comprise around 99% of the establishments in the country and provide 66% of total employment in the private sector. However, a number of problems continue to hold back Filipinos from realizing their entrepreneurial aptitude. Among these challenges include lack of adequate knowledge on financial management, high cost of doing business, lack of access to finance and market information, and low productivity and competitiveness due to the lack of economic capacity. The proposed Financial Literacy for Workers Act aims to address the low level of entrepreneurial and financial skills among young Filipinos through the delivery of highly relevant programs to our students. It seeks to establish a financial literacy and entrepreneurship education program for Filipino workers to empower them to generate more income and ultimately lead a life of economic and financial freedom. This bill mandates the Department of Labor and Employment to provide assistance, in the form of grants or loans, to deserving working entrepreneurs to enable them to launch their own small or medium enterprises. The Department is also directed to offer grants and loans to eligible entities that will provide financial literacy and entrepreneurship programs to workers. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 10109
title: AN ACT MANDATING ALL COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS AND PUBLIC BUILDINGS IN EVERY CITY AND MUNICIPALITY OF THE COUNTRY, WHETHER FOR PROFIT OR NOT AND OPERATING PUBLIC TOILETS TO INSTALL BIDET SPRAYS ON SUCH PUBLIC TOILETS, IMPOSING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREFORE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State recognizes that the right of every establishment to a fair return on investment carries with it a corresponding social responsibility to provide adequate facilities for the comfort of its clientele. As such, Republic Act 11311 was enacted in 2018 to ensure that high foot-traffic areas such as Land Transportation Terminals, Stations, Stops, Rest Areas, and Roll-on/Roll-Off Terminals provide facilities such as internet and clean sanitary facilities. Since most commercial operations are typically located in public spaces with heavy foot traffic, it follows that this is where people would most likely need bathrooms. Basic restrooms ideally include sufficient lighting, ventilation, running water that is safe to use, soap, a mirror, and a hand dryer. As a part of better public service for Filipinos, who traditionally and culturally practice the use of water and soap instead of tissue paper in the restrooms, this measure proposes the installation of bidet sprays in all commercial establishments, especially in restaurants across the country. By having a safe, adequate, and running water supply in every available restroom in public areas, people can be assured that they can be relieved with the same comfort as they would in their own homes. This bill also intends to contribute to the environmental cause of eliminating toilet paper and paper waste over time. While bidet sprays are not the ultimate solution to perfecting restrooms, this bill further hopes to move the nation one step closer to transforming public restrooms into spaces that truly give comfort. In view of the foregoing, immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 10110
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A JOB TRAINING PROGRAM FOR MATURE OR OLDER WORKERS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XIII, Section 3 of the 1087 Philippine Constitution provides: “The State shall afford Jull protection to labor, local and overseas, organized and unorganized, and promote full employment and equality of employment opportunities for all." In recognition of this, the 16th Congress of the Republic of the Philippines pushed for the enactment of Republic Act No. 10911, otherwise known as the "Anti-Age Discrimination Employment Act." This law aims to prohibit arbitrary age limitations in employment and promote the employment of individuals on the basis of competencies rather than their age. Despite this development, many workers who are 18 years old and above still find it difficult to secure employment due to the lack of skills and increased competition in the job market. This bill seeks to provide mature or older workers with the necessary educational and occupational skills to improve their employability and productivity. Under this proposal, the Department of Labor and Employment is directed to develop a job training program designed for employees above 40 years of age and the demands of the job market. It is the hope of this measure to empower mature employees to be able to compete with their young, fresh-out-of-school counterparts, thus giving them an opportunity to contribute to the labor force and better themselves and their families. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 10111
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING TWENTY-FOUR-SEVEN (24/7) AVAILABILITY OF ESSENTIAL FRONTLINE SERVICES THROUGH DIGITAL, VOICE, AND NON- VOICE CHANNELS, AND EXTENDING FACE-TO-FACE FRONTLINE TRANSACTIONS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Technology has changed the way people work, transact, and access public services. Today, many Filipinos rely on the internet, mobile applications, and social media to communicate, request information, and avail of basic services. Government services must therefore keep up with the needs of a digital and fast-moving society. At present, several government agencies have already introduced online services, such as online filing of claims and applications, online requests for civil registry documents, and online clearance applications. This bill requires government offices to identify services that may be offered as “Zero Contact Services” or services that do not require face-to-face interaction and may be made available online. It further institutionalizes the twenty-four-seven (24/7) availability of essential frontline services through digital, voice, non-voice, automated, or other accessible service channels. While not all government transactions may be completed at any hour, essential services such as inquiries, appointment setting, status verification, submission of requirements legally allowed, complaints receipt, referrals that involves life and death situations should remain accessible to the public at all times, including nights, weekends, holidays, and non-working days. The bill also recognizes that the traditional 8:00 A.M. to 5:00 P.M. working schedule may not be convenient for all citizens, especially students, workers, commuters, parents, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and those with urgent needs that requires government action and response. For this reason, we propose a system of extended face-to-face frontline service hours from Monday to Saturday, 7:00 A.M. to 7:00 P.M. 1 By combining 24/7 essential service availability with extended face-to-face operating hours, this measure promotes a more responsive, inclusive, and people- centered government service system. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 10112
title: AN ACT ASSISTING YOUNG ATHLETES BY PROVIDING PROGRAMS AND INCENTIVES FOR THEIR DEVELOPMENT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Sports play a vital role in shaping national identity and unity. It promotes essential personal values including discipline, sportsmanship, teamwork, perseverance, resilience, and leadership and serves as a critical tool for developing young individuals into active, character-driven citizens who contribute meaningfully to the progress and success of the nation. According to the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC), the 2025 Batang Pinoy National Championships gathered 19,000 young athletes from 188 local government units competing in 27 sports disciplines, making it the largest edition of the country's premier grassroots sports competition. Likewise, the Palarong Pambansa annually brings together more than 10,000 to 11,000 learner-athletes from all regions of the Philippines, providing young Filipinos with opportunities to compete at the highest level of school sports. These figures do not yet include thousands of youth athletes participating in local, provincial, regional, university, and private sports competitions nationwide. Collectively, these athletes comprise the Philippines' primary talent pool for future elite competitors. Numerous Filipino Olympians, Southeast Asian Games medalists, and national champions including Hidilyn Diaz, Carlos Yulo, and Nesthy Petecio began their athletic careers in grassroots and school-based sports programs before advancing to international competitions. Their success only underscores the importance of nurturing young athletes and fostering their development in the field of sports. But despite the proven competence of Filipino young athletes, their development is heavily hindered by severe financial constraints. Many athletes face significant challenges covering essential expenses, including specialized training, modern facilities, proper equipment, and other expenses. These systemic inefficiencies 1 directly limit the capacity of promising young athletes to sustain their participation, hone their skills, and reach their full potential. To address these challenges, this bill aims to fulfill the State’s constitutional mandate to promote sports development by establishing a state-funded grassroots sports program for the youth. To encourage athletic participation and develop facilities, the bill mandates the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) to administer three distinct financial initiatives: the "Get Started in Sports Fund" (providing ₱3,000 vouchers to underprivileged youth for sports club fees), the "Get Going Fund" (awarding ₱50,000 grants to local sports organizations to boost youth membership), and the "Get Playing Fund" (allotting up to ₱500,000 for local sports facility development). The entire initiative is backed by a dedicated annual allocation of ₱80,000,000.00 sourced directly from the revenues of the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR). This measure will help in boosting youth sports participation and provide a continuous financial lifeline that dismantles the barriers faced by aspiring youth athletes through an institutionalized government program. The passage of this bill which is a counterpart measure of Senate Bill 2167 is earnestly requested. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 10113
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REVISED GOVERNMENT AUDITING CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution enshrines the principle that public office is a public trust, requiring all public officials and employees to serve with accountability, integrity, and transparency. Consistent with this mandate, the State must ensure that public funds and resources are managed, disbursed, and accounted for prudently. Central to this responsibility is the Commission on Audit (COA), the country's supreme audit institution, which is constitutionally mandated to examine, audit, and settle all accounts pertaining to government revenues, expenditures, and the use of public funds and property. To operationalize this constitutional mandate, Presidential Decree No. 1445, otherwise known as the Government Auditing Code of the Philippines, was enacted in 1978. While it has served as the principal legal framework for government auditing for decades, rapid advances in technology, digital governance, public financial management, and international auditing standards have rendered several of its provisions outdated and inadequate to address the evolving demands of public accountability. Recognizing the need for reform, President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., in his 2023 State of the Nation Address, urged Congress to enact a new Government Auditing Code "to make auditing more attuned to these changing times." In response, this bill seeks to enact the Revised Government Auditing Code of the Philippines. The proposed measure modernizes the country's government auditing framework by recognizing electronic records and digital government transactions as valid subjects of audit and institutionalizing the use of electronic collections, receipts, payments, and other digital audit trails. It likewise strengthens the Commission on Audit's authority to require the production of records and information necessary for the conduct of audits, reinforces compliance with audit recommendations, authorizes the adoption of modern audit methodologies, and enhances internal control systems 1 to safeguard public resources against loss, waste, fraud, and abuse. Ultimately, the measure promotes greater efficiency, transparency, accountability, and public trust in government institutions. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 10114
title: AN ACT GRANTING TAX EXEMPTIONS AND INCENTIVES TO ACCREDITED FILM INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS AND ESTABLISHING THE NORA AUNOR AWARD FOR FILM EXCELLENCE
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE According to Article XIV, Section 14 of the 1987 Constitution, “[t]he State shall foster the preservation, enrichment, and dynamic evolution of a Filipino national culture based on the principle of unity in diversity in a climate of free artistic and intellectual expression.” Therefore, it is crucial to protect Filipino artistic excellence in filmmaking and production while addressing the emerging difficulties faced by the industry. The Philippine film industry, throughout the years, has created countless award-winning productions that have earned local and international recognition. While films have become an essential channel for creative expression, the rising cost of tickets and film production, declining audience attendance, and increasing competition from online streaming services pose pressing issues for the continuation and growth of the film industry. These challenges particularly affect small film outfits and independent filmmakers' capacity to present Filipino creativity and talent and showcase their work on both the local and international stage. This proposed bill, the "Nora Aunor Act", responds to these challenges by providing incentives to the Philippine film industry, including exemptions from income tax, value-added tax, and customs duties, as well as allowing the deduction of film production expenses from gross income for tax purposes. Pursuant to these incentives, the bill also institutionalizes an annual award for exceptional scripts and concepts, the Nora Aunor Award for Film Excellence. This award will empower Filipino filmmakers to thrive and innovate. 1 Through the passage of this bill, the promotion of Filipino talent and the growth of the filmmaking industry will be strengthened, contributing to the preservation, enrichment, and dynamic evolution of a national culture, while also honoring the legacy of the Superstar of Philippine Cinema. Support for this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 10115
title: AN ACT ALLOCATING A FIXED PERCENTAGE OF THE PROCEEDS FROM THE DISPOSITION OF FORFEITED PROPERTIES IN CORRUPTION CASES TO THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 6 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1379, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FORFEITURE LAW
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The constitutional mandate of the Office of the Ombudsman as an independent guardian of public accountability is gravely impaired by persistent fiscal limitations. When measured against the resources provided to comparable anti-corruption institutions in other jurisdictions, the present appropriations for the Office remain manifestly insufficient. To fortify the state's anti-corruption efforts without imposing new burdens on public taxpayers, this measure introduces a self-funding model for accountability. By establishing a statutory claim on state-recovered assets seized under Republic Act No. 1379, the legislation mandates that exactly 30% of all judicially confiscated properties be diverted directly into the operational budget of the Office of the Ombudsman. This dedicated revenue stream provides the fiscal stability necessary to sustain complex, long-term litigations and clear backlogs of public misconduct cases. The passage of this bill therefore is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 10116
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING DETAILED UNIT PRICE ANALYSIS SYSTEM IN THE DETERMINATION OF APPROPRIATIONS FOR ANY AND ALL INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS IN THE NATIONAL EXPENDITURE PROGRAM AND THE GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Public infrastructure accounts for nearly one-fifth of total government expenditure. Under the 2026 General Appropriations Act, ₱1.289 trillion out of the ₱6.793 trillion national budget is allocated for infrastructure. Despite its substantial share, infrastructure spending has long been vulnerable to overpricing, fund leakages, and other procurement irregularities. To strengthen transparency and fiscal accountability, this measure mandates the adoption of a standardized Detailed Unit Price Analysis (DUPA) as the basis for determining appropriations and project costs for all public works. Prepared during the pre-construction and procurement phases, the DUPA establishes the fair and reasonable cost for every work item prior to project implementation and provides line- item specifications for all identifiable and verifiable components including labor, raw materials, heavy equipment operational costs, and other expenses. The DUPA also creates a precise financial baseline. This objective cost structure prevents overpricing, curbs budget inflation, and ensures that unit costs remain strictly within legal and technical standards. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 10117
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE IMPOSITION OF LESSER PENALTIES IN CRIMINAL CASES WHERE THE CORRESPONDING CIVIL ASPECT HAVE BEEN SETTLED THROUGH ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9285, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION ACT OF 2004"
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) has steadily evolved into an invaluable and highly effective legal mechanism within our judicial system, offering an efficient paradigm for the settlement of complex controversies and significantly mitigating the protracted nature of traditional courtroom litigation. In order to incentivize the adoption of ADR mechanisms and systematically strengthen its practice across the country, this measure introduces a restorative and mitigating benefit favorable to the accused through a grant and reduction of the imposable principal penalty in the event of a conviction in criminal proceedings, provided that the civil liability arising from the offense has been conclusively settled with finality through authorized ADR processes. This is also aimed to significantly expedite the disposition of criminal dockets and optimize judicial economy. By accelerating the determination, execution, and full satisfaction of civil liabilities which are legally deemed impliedly instituted alongside the criminal action this measure ensures a more swift, harmonious, and equitable administration of justice for both the aggrieved parties and the state. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 10118
title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE SALARY GRADE OF DENTISTS EMPLOYED IN THE PUBLIC SECTOR, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Oral health is a fundamental component of an individual's overall health and well-being. Despite its critical importance, access to oral healthcare remains inadequate for many Filipinos, as dental care is too often treated as a privilege rather than an essential public health service. This situation reflects longstanding gaps in public health investment and the insufficient integration of dental professionals into the public healthcare system. Data from the Department of Health's National Database of Human Resources for Health indicate that only about 2,400 dentists are employed in the public sector. As of 2026, this leaves one public dentist to serve an average of 53,000 people—far exceeding the World Health Organization's recommended ratio of one dentist for every 7,500 individuals. This significant shortage underscores the urgent need to strengthen the country's public oral healthcare workforce. A primary barrier is the severe wage disparity between government service and private practice. An entry-level public dentist is locked into Salary Grade (SG) 13, which translates to a mere PHP 34,421.00 compensation monthly. In contrast, the private sector offers significantly higher income potential without the rigid bureaucratic restrictions and stringent requirements inherent to the civil service. In alignment with the policy objectives initiated during the 20th Congress, this Act mandates a comprehensive restructuring of the compensation framework for dental health professionals across all public sectors, explicitly encompassing national government agencies, government-owned or controlled corporations, state 1 universities and colleges, and local government units. To fortify the civil service by incentivizing specialized dental education and ensuring the robust recruitment and long-term retention of premier practitioners, the state-employed dental workforce shall be reallocated to upgraded salary grades, specifically designating Salary Grade 17 for Dentist I, Salary Grade 20 for Dentist II, Salary Grade 23 for Dentist III, Salary Grade 25 for Dentist IV, Salary Grade 27 for Dentist V, Salary Grade 29 for Dentist VI, and Salary Grade 30 for Dentist VII. Ultimately, this measure seeks to fulfill the constitutional mandate to protect and promote the right to health of the people, thereby fostering a deeply ingrained health consciousness across the nation. The passage of this bill which is a counterpart measure of Senate Bill 493 is earnestly requested. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 10119
title: AN ACT ENTITLING BARANGAY OFFICIALS TO FIXED SALARIES AND SUCH OTHER BENEFITS BEING ENJOYED BY REGULAR GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Local Government Code of 1991 provides that the barangay, as the basic political unit, serves as the primary planning and implementing unit of government policies, plans, programs, projects, and activities in the community and a forum wherein the collective views of the people may be expressed, crystallized and considered, and where disputes may be amicably settled. In fact, most of the national government’s efforts require intervention and support of the barangays as they are the closest form of government to the people. The barangay is headed by a Punong Barangay with support from the Sangguniang Barangay, who, under the Local Government Code, are receiving compensation in a form of honorarium, and not a fixed salary within a compensation system that will provide just remuneration for the wide range of roles and responsibilities. The barangay serves as the office of first resort of the people, may it be in terms of conflict resolution, medical and burial support, financial assistance, conflict resolution, disaster and risk management, and the like. Simply put, they are expected to address a number of issues apart from their regular duties and responsibilities as Barangay Officials, which are already burdensome to begin with. This bill seeks to provide fixed salary for barangay officials and declare them as regular government employees in order for them to receive just compensation and other benefits that other regular government employees are relishing. It is high time that our barangay officials be given what is due for them and recognize their vital role in carrying out government’s services to the communities. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. PAOLO Z. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The barangay serves as the basic political unit of the country, according to the Local Government Code of 1991. As the basic political unit, it deals with the primary planning and implementation of government policies, plans, programs, projects, and activities in the community and serves as a forum wherein the collective views of the people may be freely expressed, deliberated upon and considered, realized, and where disputes are resolved or may be amicably settled. Most, if not all, of the national government’s efforts requires intervention and support of the barangays as they are the closest form of government to the people. The administration of the barangay, composed of Punong Barangay and the Sangguniang Barangay officials, receive compensation in the form of honorarium, and not a fixed salary within a compensation system under the Local Government Code. Unfortunately, barangay officials are not granted corresponding death, disability and accident insurance during the performance of their duties, despite the number of risks attributed to their positions. The barangay serves as the first recourse of the people, may it be in terms of conflict resolution, medical and burial support, financial assistance, disaster and risk response and management, and the like. Simply put, they serve as the frontliners and are expected to address a number of issues apart from their regular duties and responsibilities as Barangay Officials, which are already challenging to begin with. Hence, it is only right that these officials shall be accorded utmost protection in response to their on-the-ground call of duty. This bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 6942 or “An Act Increasing the Insurance Benefits of Local Government Officials and Providing Funds Therefore” in order to expand the insurance coverage of barangay officials in times of death, total and permanent incapacity or disability, and accident, and increasing the benefits to be received therein, thereby recognizing their vital role in immediately carrying out government’s services to the communities. Henceforth, in view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. PAOLO Z. label: HB 10121
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA OF BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution enunciates the protection and promotion of the right to health of the people and availability of health services to its citizens at an affordable cost. The pursuit towards this constitutional mandate primarily includes the role of health workers in our country in order to swiftly and effectively deliver health services. Similarly, the 1991 Local Government Code introduces devolution of health in the local government units which inaugurates the critical role of healthcare workers in the localities, particularly the barangay health workers (BHWs). The rationale of the said devolution is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of health services management, which starts from the basic political unit in our country. In addition, the main goal of utilizing healthcare workers in the localities is to bring health services to rural areas, most especially the far-flung ones. However, despite the crucial and heroic role of our barangay health workers (BHWs) especially during the proliferation of the COVID-19 pandemic, they still remain to be the sectors to suffer unreasonable compensation and lack of benefits. As a result, most of them and the rest of the Filipino healthcare workers opt to contribute their knowledge and talent abroad, in search of better pay and humane working conditions. This puts our healthcare system in turmoil as there is a significant decline in the patient to healthcare worker ratio. Evidently, in 2019, the doctor to patient ratio in our country is 1:33,000—significantly higher than the global average of 1:6,600. This bill aims to provide free education and training programs for our barangay health workers, in addition to their entitlement to additional compensation and incentives. Apart from granting due recognition to the incomparable services rendered by the BHWs, this proposed measure also seeks to encourage more healthcare workers to render their service in their own country, which would positively result in at par healthcare programs of our government. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. PAOLO Z. Short Title. — This Act shall be known as the “Vehicular Reckless Imprudence Penalty Harmonization Act.” 23 SECTION 2. Declaration of Policy. — It is the policy of the State to ensure consistency, fairness, and proportionality in the imposition of penalties for quasi- offenses under Article 365 of the Revised Penal Code, particularly those involving death or serious physical injuries caused through the operation of motor vehicles. 28 The State likewise recognizes the need to harmonize the provisions of Article 365 with Article 64 of the Revised Penal Code in light of evolving jurisprudence, ensure fair notice to the accused, preserve due process rights, and establish clearer statutory standards governing mitigating and aggravating circumstances in cases of reckless imprudence. 34 SECTION 3. Article 365 of Act No. 3815, as amended, otherwise known as the Revised Penal Code, is hereby further amended to read as follows: 37 “ART. 365. IMPRUDENCE AND NEGLIGENCE. — ANY PERSON WHO, BY RECKLESS IMPRUDENCE, SHALL COMMIT ANY ACT WHICH, HAD IT BEEN INTENTIONAL, WOULD CONSTITUTE A GRAVE FELONY, SHALL SUFFER THE PENALTY OF ARRESTO MAYOR IN ITS MAXIMUM PERIOD TO PRISION CORRECCIONAL IN ITS MEDIUM PERIOD; IF IT WOULD HAVE CONSTITUTED A LESS GRAVE FELONY, THE PENALTY OF ARRESTO MAYOR IN ITS MINIMUM AND MEDIUM PERIODS SHALL BE IMPOSED; IF IT WOULD HAVE CONSTITUTED A LIGHT FELONY, THE PENALTY OF ARRESTO MENOR IN ITS MAXIMUM PERIOD SHALL BE IMPOSED.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 14 Article 365 of the Revised Penal Code governs criminal liability arising from imprudence and negligence. Its present text, however, contains different and potentially conflicting rules on the application of penalties and modifying circumstances. 19 In Noli Z. Ilon v. People of the Philippines, G.R. No. 260538, promulgated on November 11, 2025 and uploaded to the Supreme Court website on May 7, 2026, the Supreme Court held that Article 64 of the Revised Penal Code applies to reckless imprudence resulting in homicide committed through the use of a motor vehicle under paragraph six (6), subparagraph two (2) of Article 365. The Court also ruled that failure to render assistance is a qualifying circumstance which must be specifically alleged in the information and proved beyond reasonable doubt. 27 The Court observed that the present wording of Article 365 produces an inequitable distinction. Cases falling under paragraph six (6) may be mitigated or aggravated pursuant to Article 64, while cases falling under the first four paragraphs may not be mitigated because of paragraph five (5), even though they may still be subjected to the penalty-increasing circumstance of failure to render assistance. The Court emphasized that the determination of penalties is a matter of legislative policy and furnished copies of its Decision to the President, the Senate President, and the Speaker of the House of Representatives pursuant to Article 5 of the Revised Penal Code. 37 This measure addresses the statutory incongruence identified by the Supreme Court. It provides for the uniform appreciation of mitigating and aggravating circumstances in prosecutions under Article 365, in accordance with Articles 64 and 65 of the Revised Penal Code, while preserving judicial discretion in fixing the duration of the penalty within the proper period based on the degree of negligence and the circumstances of each case. 44 1 The bill likewise removes the ambiguous statement that the provisions of Article 365 shall not apply to certain cases. Instead, it specifies that only the general penalties contained in the first two paragraphs shall not govern the exceptional cases enumerated therein. 5 Finally, the measure expressly provides that failure to render assistance is a qualifying circumstance which must be alleged in the information and proved beyond reasonable doubt. It also codifies the rule that contributory negligence does not extinguish criminal liability, although it may be appreciated as an analogous mitigating circumstance and considered in determining civil liability. 11 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 13 14 15 16 17 REP. label: HB 10129
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE COMPLIANCE, MONITORING, AND PENAL PROVISIONS FOR SEWAGE TREATMENT AND DISPOSAL IN PHILIPPINE- REGISTERED VESSELS, STRENGTHENING THE POWERS OF THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Marine pollution caused by untreated sewage discharge from ships and floating facilities poses a serious threat to the Philippines’ coastal waters, fisheries, and public health. The country, being an archipelagic state with one of the largest maritime jurisdictions in the world, is highly vulnerable to the cumulative effects of ship-generated waste. While the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) has issued Memorandum Circulars, including Circular No. 10-14 (2014) and the updated Circular No. 03-25 (2025), compliance remains inconsistent, and enforcement mechanisms require stronger legislative backing. International conventions such as MARPOL Annex IV, together with domestic laws including Republic Act No. 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act), Republic Act No. 9993 (Philippine Coast Guard Law), and Republic Act No. 12064 (Philippine Maritime Zones Act), already provide a framework for sewage management. However, without institutionalized penalties, monitoring systems, and clear authority vested in the PCG, ship operators often evade responsibility, resulting in untreated sewage being discharged into Philippine waters until now. This bill seeks to institutionalize the compliance, monitoring, and penal provisions for sewage treatment and disposal in Philippine-registered vessels. It strengthens the enforcement powers of the PCG by authorizing stop-sail orders, suspension of accreditation, and denial of departure clearance for non-compliant vessels. It also mandates MARINA to integrate sewage compliance into vessel registration, DENR to oversee effluent testing through accredited laboratories, and DOH to certify sewage treatment facilities and personnel training. By imposing stricter fines, requiring regular inspections, and establishing a Marine Sewage Compliance Database, this measure ensures transparency, accountability, and deterrence against violations. It also aligns Philippine maritime practices with international standards, thereby protecting marine biodiversity, sustaining fisheries, and safeguarding the health of our coastal communities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JURDIN JESUS M. title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE AUTOMATIC PENSION ESCALATION MECHANISM FOR RETIREES OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM (SSS), PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

ROMUALDO ___________________________________________________________________ Explanatory Note The Social Security System (SSS) provides retirement, disability, death, and survivor benefits to millions of private sector workers under Republic Act No. 11199. In 2025, the SSS began implementing a multi-year Pension Reform Program (PRP) that grants annual increases to pensions. However, this program is based on administrative approval and is not yet institutionalized by law. Without legislative backing, future pension increases remain uncertain and subject to policy changes. This exposes retirees to the risk of stagnant benefits, especially during periods of high inflation. This bill seeks to institutionalize the automatic pension escalation mechanism for SSS retirees by enshrining it in law. It mandates annual increases of ten percent (10%) for retirement and disability pensions, and five percent (5%) for death and survivor pensions, or the Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rate, whichever is higher. By codifying the pension escalation program, the measure ensures predictability, protects retirees’ purchasing power, and strengthens the long-term social safety net for private sector workers. The GSIS pensions do not have an automatic escalation mechanism. Pension amounts remain fixed unless Congress enacts a new law or the GSIS Board authorizes special adjustments. This situation has created inequity between public and private sector retirees. While SSS retirees now enjoy predictable annual increases under the Pension Reform Program (PRP) beginning in 2025, GSIS retirees are left vulnerable to inflation and rising costs of living. This bill seeks to establish an automatic annual adjustment mechanism for GSIS pensions, either pegged to inflation or set at a minimum of five percent (5%) per year, with safeguards to ensure fund sustainability.
