explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Constitution mandates the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people and to instill health consciousness among them. This guiding principle remains especially urgent today, as lifestyle- related illnesses continue to rise across all age groups in the Philippines. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), ischemic heart disease remained the leading cause of death in the country in 2023, accounting for 18.8% of total deaths. It was followed by neoplasms or cancers (10.7%), cerebrovascular diseases (10.1%), and diabetes mellitus (6.3%). These diseases are heavily linked to poor diet, sedentary behavior, and other preventable lifestyle factors. Alarmingly, cases of such chronic illnesses are no longer confined to older age groups. Increasingly, Filipinos in their 20s and 30s are being diagnosed with hypertension, high cholesterol, obesity, and type 2 diabetes which are conditions that are closely tied to unhealthy food choices and a lack of nutritional awareness. In a society where fast food, sugary beverages, and processed meals are widely accessible and heavily marketed, consumers, especially the youth, often make uninformed dietary decisions that significantly increase their long-term health risks. While packaged food products are required to display nutritional information, this standard of transparency is not consistently applied to food served in restaurants and other food service establishments, where many Filipinos eat on a regular basis. This bill seeks to promote health consciousness and empower consumers to make informed dietary decisions by mandating the clear and visible display of nutritional information, such as calorie count and key nutrient content, for all food items listed on the menus of restaurants, fast food chains, and similar establishments. By increasing transparency in food labeling, this measure aims to encourage healthier consumption habits, reduce the risk of diet-related diseases, and support the broader public health agenda of preventive care. This proposed legislation advances the State’s constitutional duty to protect the people’s health by addressing one of its root causes, which is lack of information. Through informed choices, individuals can take greater control over their health outcomes, leading to a more health-literate, conscious, and resilient Filipino population. A similar bill was previously filed in the 19 th Congress by Representative Joseph Gilbert Violago. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. label: HB 10197
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPLOYMENT OF MOBILE CLINICS TO GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED AND DISADVANTAGED AREAS (GIDAs), STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO PROVIDE REGULAR MEDICAL MISSIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Many rural and geographically isolated communities in the Philippines continue to face serious barriers in accessing basic healthcare services due to inadequate health facilities, limited medical personnel, transportation difficulties, and geographic isolation. These gaps contribute to delayed treatment, preventable illnesses, and poor health outcomes among underserved populations. This bill seeks to establish a Mobile Rural Health Clinic Program under the Department of Health to deliver accessible and community-based healthcare services to Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAs) and other medically underserved communities. Through mobile clinics equipped with diagnostic, emergency, telemedicine, and primary healthcare capabilities, the Program aims to strengthen preventive care, maternal and child health services, immunization, mental health support, and emergency response in remote areas. The measure likewise strengthens coordination among national agencies, local government units, PhilHealth, and local health systems to ensure continuity of care, effective referrals, and integration with the Universal Health Care Act. It further promotes the use of digital health systems, mobile diagnostics, and community health outreach to improve healthcare accessibility and service delivery. By bringing essential healthcare services directly to underserved communities, this measure seeks to reduce health inequities, strengthen rural healthcare systems, and uphold the constitutional right to health of every Filipino. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10198
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AUTISM CENTERS AND EARLY DETECTION PROGRAMS NATIONWIDE, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects many Filipino individuals and families who continue to face significant challenges in accessing timely diagnosis, intervention, therapy, education, healthcare, and community support services. Limited public awareness, shortage of trained specialists, financial barriers, and unequal access to developmental services—particularly in underserved areas—often result in delayed intervention and reduced opportunities for persons on the autism spectrum. This bill seeks to establish a comprehensive and inclusive national framework for autism care and support through the creation of regional Autism Centers, early detection and intervention programs, inclusive education support, professional training, research initiatives, and accessible community-based services. The measure likewise strengthens coordination among healthcare, education, and social welfare institutions to ensure continuity of care and long- term support for individuals with autism and their families. Consistent with the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability, the Mental Health Act, and the Universal Health Care Act, this measure promotes a rights- based, evidence-informed, and family-centered approach to autism care while encouraging inclusion, accessibility, dignity, and equal opportunity for persons on the autism spectrum. By improving access to developmental services, strengthening public awareness, and supporting families and communities, this measure seeks to enhance the quality of life and full participation of persons with autism in society. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10199
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A REAL-TIME NATIONAL DATABASE OF HEALTH WORKERS TO ENHANCE DEPLOYMENT, TRAINING, AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to face persistent challenges in health workforce distribution, with shortages in rural and geographically isolated areas, maldistribution across regions, and limited real-time data for workforce planning. These gaps hinder the effective implementation of Universal Health Care and weaken the country’s capacity to respond to public health emergencies. This bill seeks to establish a National Health Workforce Registry as a centralized, real-time, and interoperable database of all health workers in the country. It aims to strengthen health system governance by providing accurate and updated information on the supply, distribution, and specialization of health professionals and community health workers. The registry will support evidence-based planning, equitable deployment of health personnel, emergency surge mobilization, and health workforce development. It will also be fully integrated with existing government systems, including the Professional Regulation Commission, PhilHealth, and local government health information systems, while ensuring strict compliance with data privacy and cybersecurity standards. By institutionalizing a unified health workforce information system, this measure strengthens health system resilience, improves service delivery in underserved areas, and supports long-term human resource planning for the health sector. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10200
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE OFW FAMILIES ENTERPRISE FUND TO SUPPORT COMMUNITY-BASED LIVELIHOOD AND ENTERPRISE PROJECTS LED BY OFW FAMILIES THROUGH A MATCHING INVESTMENT SCHEME, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) play a vital role in sustaining the Philippine economy through their remittances, which support millions of Filipino families and contribute significantly to national development. However, sustained dependence on overseas employment and remittance inflows has also led to limited opportunities for long-term, sustainable livelihood and local enterprise development among OFW households. This bill seeks to establish the OFW Families Enterprise Fund (OFEF), a special financing mechanism designed to transform remittances into productive investments through matching support for OFW family-led and community- based enterprises. The Fund aims to promote job creation, inclusive local economic development, and long-term financial resilience by enabling OFW families to transition from remittance dependency to sustainable entrepreneurship. To ensure the viability and sustainability of supported enterprises, the measure institutionalizes capacity-building and enterprise development programs in partnership with TESDA, LGUs, and the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), including entrepreneurship training, business mentorship, and market access support. The OFEF shall operate as a blended and development-oriented financing mechanism, complemented by institutional safeguards such as transparency reporting, monitoring, and performance evaluation to ensure accountability and effective use of public resources. This proposal reinforces State policy recognizing the significant contribution of OFWs and their families to national development and builds upon the principles of Republic Act No. 7111 (Overseas Workers Investment Fund Act of 1991) by expanding its framework through a matching fund mechanism integrated with structured enterprise development support. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10201
title: AN ACT RECOGNIZING, PRESERVING, AND PROMOTING PHILIPPINE INDIGENOUS FARMING PRACTICES AND CULTURAL HERITAGE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is home to diverse Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) whose traditional farming systems and agricultural knowledge have long contributed to biodiversity conservation, sustainable land management, food security, and cultural preservation. However, many indigenous farming practices and knowledge systems are increasingly threatened by modernization, environmental degradation, cultural erosion, and unauthorized commercial exploitation. Despite the importance of indigenous agricultural knowledge, there remains a need for stronger institutional mechanisms to protect traditional farming practices, preserve indigenous seed systems and biocultural heritage, and ensure that ICCs/IPs retain ownership and equitable benefits from the use of their knowledge and resources. This bill seeks to protect, preserve, and promote indigenous farming practices and traditional agricultural knowledge systems through documentation with Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC), protection against misappropriation and biopiracy, support for indigenous farming communities, and the integration of sustainable indigenous practices into agricultural, climate resilience, and biodiversity conservation programs. The measure likewise recognizes the collective rights of ICCs/IPs over their traditional knowledge and establishes safeguards against unauthorized commercial or scientific use. By strengthening support for indigenous farming systems and cultural heritage, this measure aims to promote environmental sustainability, cultural integrity, and inclusive rural development. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10202
title: AN ACT REGISTERING LICENSED TRADITIONAL HEALERS AND INTEGRATING SAFE HERBAL REMEDIES INTO THE PRIMARY HEALTHCARE SYSTEM
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Traditional and complementary medicine continues to play an important role in the healthcare practices of many Filipino communities, particularly in rural and indigenous areas where culturally rooted healing systems and herbal remedies remain widely used and trusted. Traditional healers, medicinal plants, and indigenous wellness practices form part of the country’s cultural heritage and community-based health traditions. This bill seeks to strengthen the promotion, regulation, and integration of safe and evidence-informed traditional and complementary medicine into the national healthcare system consistent with Republic Act No. 8423 or the “Traditional and Alternative Medicine Act of 1997” and the Universal Health Care Act. The measure establishes a national accreditation and registry system for traditional healers, promotes research and validation of herbal remedies, strengthens public health safeguards, and supports culturally sensitive and community-based healthcare approaches. It likewise provides mechanisms for training, monitoring, patient safety, and coordination between traditional practitioners and licensed healthcare professionals. By promoting responsible and scientifically guided integration of traditional and complementary medicine, this measure aims to improve healthcare accessibility, preserve indigenous knowledge systems, support preventive wellness, and strengthen holistic public health services for Filipino communities. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. label: HB 10203
title: AN ACT MANDATING ANNUAL HEALTH CHECK-UPS FOR EVERY FAMILY UNIT TO PROMOTE PREVENTIVE HEALTHCARE, WITH FOCUS ON NUTRITION, LIFESTYLE DISEASES, REPRODUCTIVE AND MENTAL HEALTH
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Many Filipino families continue to face preventable health risks due to limited access to regular screening, early diagnosis, and primary healthcare services, particularly in underserved and geographically isolated communities. As a result, illnesses such as hypertension, diabetes, malnutrition, mental health conditions, and other preventable diseases often remain undetected until complications arise. This bill seeks to institutionalize a Whole Family Health Program that provides free annual preventive health check-ups for Filipino households through barangay health stations, rural health units, mobile health teams, and public healthcare facilities. The measure adopts a family-centered and preventive healthcare approach focused on early detection, nutrition, mental health, reproductive health, child development, and disease prevention. The proposed program strengthens the implementation of the Universal Health Care Act by improving access to primary healthcare services, enhancing continuity of care, and promoting coordinated health interventions at the community level. It also provides mechanisms for digital health records, mobile healthcare delivery, referral systems, and local government participation to ensure efficient and inclusive implementation. By prioritizing prevention, early intervention, and community-based healthcare, this measure aims to improve health outcomes, reduce long-term healthcare costs, and strengthen the overall well-being and resilience of Filipino families. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE K. ROMUALDEZ ANDREW JULIAN K. ROMUALDEZ JUDE A. While 60% of those enrolled LWDs do not have access to any of the special needs education resources at their school.2 The establishment of Inclusive Learning Resource Centers in every city and municipality which were intended as support hubs, also remain unfulfilled. While the DepEd strives to address the gaps in school learning resource facilities, training for Special Needs Education teachers, and resource deficits, the government must also ensure that transitional programs for LWDs already at the Grade 12 level are available. Learners with disabilities or special needs can still be functional and can be trained to perform tasks if they are given enough support and with the appropriate facilities to help them cope. At present, TESDA and the National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) are already working together to provide free skills training for persons with disabilities nationwide. The skills training programs are under the Training for Work Scholarship Program (TSWP), so that the Persons with Disabilities could be given the National Certificate (NC) necessary for job application here and abroad. This proposed legislation shall focus on providing transitional skills training programs for Grade 12 learners with disabilities and shall extend the duration of the trainings for up to two (2) years, in consideration of their diverse capacities to learn. Now more than ever is the right time to include persons with special needs in government programs where they could be fully supported, given adequate attention to facilitate and boost the development of their capabilities to be functional and vital part in nation building. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. CARMELO G. LAZATIN,

label: HB 10206
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF ACCESSIBLE, SAFE, CLEAN, GENDER-RESPONSIVE, AND WELL-MAINTAINED PUBLIC TOILETS AND SANITATION FACILITIES IN PUBLIC PLACES, TRANSPORT TERMINALS, TOURIST AREAS, MARKETS, PARKS, AND GOVERNMENT CENTERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to clean, safe, and properly maintained toilets is a basic public health, hygiene, dignity, environmental, and mobility concern. Commuters, market vendors, persons with disabilities, children, pregnant women, senior citizens, and persons with medical conditions are especially affected when public sanitation facilities are absent, unsafe, inaccessible, or poorly maintained. Philippine data and studies show that sanitation and hygiene remain continuing public concerns. The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported that in 2024, while 84.7% of Filipino families had access to basic sanitation service, 10.1% still relied on shared sanitation facilities, 2.7% used unimproved sanitation facilities, and 2.6% practiced open defecation due to lack of toilet facilities. The same report also noted gaps in handwashing access and availability of soap, showing the need to strengthen hygiene infrastructure and practices. In schools, the Department of Education’s WASH in Schools program recognizes that insufficient toilets, inadequate handwashing facilities, and poor hygiene practices contribute to sanitation challenges, illness, absenteeism, and other barriers to learning. A Philippine study on public school toilets further showed that improving toilet usability and cleanliness requires not only infrastructure, but also proper operation, maintenance, monitoring, and hygiene promotion. In public markets, a 2025 study on handwashing nudges in urban public markets in the Philippines found that the introduction of visible handwashing facilities increased handwashing with soap behavior over time, while lack of consistent water and soap supply affected sustained practice. This bill mandates minimum standards for public toilets and sanitation facilities in key public places and requires LGUs and facility operators to plan, maintain, and improve access. It encourages healthy and hygienic practices among the public by ensuring that sanitation facilities are clean, accessible, properly supplied, and suitable for regular use. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. TOBIAS “TOBY” M. label: HB 10212
title: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7305, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE MAGNA CARTA OF PUBLIC HEALTH WORKERS”, BY STRENGTHENING SAFE STAFFING, WORKFORCE REGULARIZATION, MENTAL HEALTH PROTECTION, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, RURAL DEPLOYMENT INCENTIVES, AND RETENTION MECHANISMS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article XIII, Section 12 of the 1987 Constitution provides that “the State shall establish and maintain an effective food and drug regulatory system and undertake appropriate health, manpower development, and research, responsive to the country’s health needs and problems.” Crucial in the efficient delivery of the health needs of the country is also the advancement and protection of the health and welfare of public health workers. Thus, on March 26, 1992, the Magna Carta for Public Health Workers (Republic Act No. 7305) was enacted. Unfortunately, for over 33 years now, the law remains as it is without any amendment to keep abreast to the challenges and needs of the present time. While numerous bills sought to revise or strengthen its provisions from the 16th to the 19th Congress, none have been successfully passed into law. The Magna Carta for Public Health Workers was designed to promote the welfare and well-being of the public health workers by providing various benefits and allowances. However, the monetary values of these benefits have remained unchanged over three decades, failing to keep pace with inflation and evolving economic conditions. Added to these are the growing clamor for more humane conditions of work for health care professionals especially the nurses and doctors. According to the Human Resources for Health by Ateneo de Manila University researchers, the Philippines has a physician-to-population ratio of 7.92 per 10,000 people, which falls below the international minimum standard of 10 per 10,000. In addition, the country is facing a shortage of at least 127,000 nurses. This shortage is further aggravated by the ongoing "brain drain" phenomenon, where many healthcare workers leave the country in search of better pay and working conditions abroad. Almost 4,500 positions in public hospitals across the Philippines remain unfilled, as many licensed Filipino nurses are unwilling to take these jobs due to low salaries, extended working hours, and insufficient benefits as noted by the Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada. Based on the findings of Woo, et.al., burnout symptoms are also widespread among healthcare professionals, leading to serious repercussions such as resignations, career shifts, and eventual migration to other countries in search of better working conditions. The Filipino Nurses United (FNU) consultations with nurse administrators from various healthcare facilities revealed that nurses are burdened by severe understaffing, often managing between 20 to 50 patients per shift while working 12 to 16 hours without receiving overtime pay. In addition, approximately 36,000 government-employed nurses hold contractual positions under schemes such as the Job Order system or the Nurse Deployment Program (NDP), leaving them with limited job security and benefits. In addition, physicians report long working hours, inadequate compensation, delayed allowances, and job insecurity. Many are also tasked with administrative duties due to lack of support staff, further increasing their workload and stress levels. It is the declared policy of the State to safeguard and advance the right to health of every Filipino and to foster greater health awareness among the population. Under Article II, Section 18 of the 1987 Constitution, the State affirms labor as a primary social economic force. It shall protect the rights of workers and promote their welfare. It is thus become imperative to the State to ensure better, fair, and safe working conditions for public health care workers. To effectively address the aforementioned challenges and fulfill the mandate of the Constitution, this bill aims to amend certain provisions in the Magna Carta for Public Health Workers by expanding the benefits and allowances of health care workers, regulate working hours to better support their welfare so they can provide a better quality service to our fellow Filipinos. It also seeks to hold government-owned hospitals, administratively liable for willful non-compliance with, or deliberate evasion of, the provision of benefits due to Public Health Workers. To ensure that the proposed amendments are both responsive and fiscally feasible and sustainable, this bill further incorporates provisions on safe staffing standards, workforce regularization, mental health protection programs, continuing professional development support and rural and geographically isolated area service incentives. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. TOBIAS “TOBY” M. label: HB 10213
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING CONSUMER PROTECTION IN THE PHILIPPINES BY AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7394, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "CONSUMER ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES," TO EXTEND PROTECTION TO ONLINE AND DIGITAL TRANSACTIONS, ESTABLISH ACCESSIBLE REDRESS MECHANISMS, STRENGTHEN ENFORCEMENT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act. No. 7394, or the Consumer Act of the Philippines, has stood as the country’s principal consumer protection statute since 1992. It was designed for a predominantly physical, retail-based economy. In the more than three decades since its enactment, Philippine commerce has been transformed by e-commerce, digital marketplaces, subscription-based services, and cross-border online transactions — developments the Act did not originally contemplate. While Republic Act No. 11967 (the Internet Transactions Act) and Republic Act No. 11765 (the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act) have partially addressed these gaps, consumer protection in the Philippines remains fragmented across statutes and agencies, redress mechanisms remain slow and inaccessible for small-value claims, penalties have not kept pace with inflation or the scale of modern commercial harm, and there is no unified, low-cost venue for consumers to pursue collective or individual complaints. This bill amends RA 7394 to: 1. Clarify the liability of online marketplaces and digital platforms for products and services sold through them; 2. Establish an accessible, low-cost Consumer Redress Mechanism for small- value claims; 3. Provide a clear collective redress (class complaint) procedure for consumer harms affecting multiple persons; 4. Update and index penalties to inflation, and strengthen enforcement powers of the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI); 5. Close the product recall gap by making the sale of recalled products a distinct offense; 6. Regulate subscription traps, forced auto-renewal, and dark patterns in digital transactions, including a "click-to-cancel" requirement; 7. Establish an Inter-Agency Consumer Protection Coordinating Council to harmonize enforcement across DTI, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC), and other sector regulators; and 8. Strengthen enforcement against foreign merchants and platforms targeting Filipino consumers. This measure builds on the consumer protection gains of the Internet Transactions Act and the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act by closing the gaps that remain in the core Consumer Act itself, so that every Filipino consumer — whether transacting in a public market or on a mobile application — has equal access to protection and redress. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ANTONINO B. label: HB 10215
title: AN ACT TO KEEP INCOMES TAX-RELIEVED AND AUGMENTED (KITA) BY AMENDING SECTIONS 24, 32, 33, 34, 53, 57, 109, 123, AND 236 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipino workers are burdened by prices that rise faster than wages, and a tax schedule that has not moved since 2018. The result is “bracket creep,” where salary adjustments push workers to higher statutory tax brackets, increasing their tax burden and eroding their increase in purchasing power. To provide equitable support to Filipino workers, who pay taxes for social assistance programs but rarely qualify for them, this “Keeping Incomes Tax-relieved and Augmented” (KITA) Act proposes several measures to maximize their net take-home pay: 1. Increase the annual income tax exemption from ₱250,000 to ₱650,000 of taxable income and the tax-free ceiling on bonuses to ₱200,000, and expand exemptions to holiday pay, overtime pay, night shift differential, hazard pay, service charges, and compensation for election service, so those with up to ₱57,000 a month in basic pay incur no income tax. 2. Indexes brackets and ceilings to the Consumer Price Index, so relief granted toward is not lost to inflation tomorrow, shifts the taxation of fringe benefits from a flat rate to the progressive schedule, and relieves employer-provided insurance premiums. 3. Raises the VAT-exempt threshold to ₱4 million, simplifying tax obligations for micro- taxpayers, allowing establishments to claim mandated discounts for senior citizens, persons with disabilities, and solo parents as direct tax credits, and providing administrative relief by automating filing extensions during calamities and removing unnecessary requirements. By alleviating these burdens, the KITA Act recognizes workers as essential to our economy, and lives up to the Constitution’s mandate for Congress to “evolve a progressive system of taxation”. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this measure is earnestly sought. label: HB 10216
title: AN ACT FURTHER STRENGTHENING THE INCENTIVES FOR PRIVATE SECTOR PARTICIPATION IN PUBLIC EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8525, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ADOPT-A-SCHOOL ACT OF 1998”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Education is a shared responsibility of the government, the private sector, civil society, and the broader community. While the Constitution primarily mandates the State to establish and maintain a complete, adequate, and integrated system of education, it likewise recognizes the indispensable role of private institutions and encourages their participation in complementing government efforts to improve educational access, quality, and relevance. Strong partnerships between public educational institutions and private stakeholders remain essential in preparing Filipino learners to meet the demands of an increasingly knowledge-driven and globally competitive economy. Republic Act No. 8525, otherwise known as the Adopt-a-School Act of 1998, has encouraged private sector support for public schools through donations and educational assistance. However, after more than two decades of implementation, the scope of the law has become inadequate to address the evolving needs of the Philippine education sector. Existing incentives no longer sufficiently encourage sustained private sector participation, while current administrative processes, limited coverage, and outdated mechanisms constrain the full potential of public-private collaboration across all levels of education. This measure seeks to modernize and strengthen the Adopt-a-School Program by expanding its coverage to include early childhood education, technical-vocational education and training, alternative learning systems, and public higher education institutions. It likewise broadens the forms of assistance that may be provided, including teacher development, scholarships, industry certifications, digital learning resources, laboratory facilities, health and nutrition interventions, assistive technologies for learners with disabilities, and other educational support necessary to improve learning outcomes and institutional capacity. At the same time, the bill establishes an Adopt-a-School One-Stop Shop and an integrated online portal to streamline applications, coordination, and the processing of incentives for participating private individuals and entities. 1 The proposed measure further enhances incentives by increasing allowable tax deductions for educational assistance, granting additional incentives for enterprises that employ graduates of partner public senior high schools, and exempting qualified donations from customs duties, value-added tax, excise tax, and donor's tax, subject to appropriate safeguards. It also strengthens institutional governance through an expanded Adopt-a-School Coordinating Council and requires education agencies to regularly identify priority needs, ensuring that private sector contributions are directed toward communities and institutions where they will produce the greatest public benefit. By fostering stronger collaboration between educational institutions and industry, the measure promotes workforce readiness, expands employment opportunities for graduates, improves educational infrastructure, enhances teacher competency, and encourages innovation throughout the public education system. More importantly, it enables the private sector to become a more active partner in nation-building by investing directly in human capital development, thereby contributing to inclusive economic growth and long-term national competitiveness. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 10217
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE DISABILITY SUPPORT FUND FOR THE EMPOWERMENT, FULL PARTICIPATION, AND INCLUSION OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES IN SOCIETY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE “Carry each other's burdens, and in this way, you will fulfill the law of Christ.” — Galatians 6:2 The Constitution mandates the State to promote social justice, protect the rights and welfare of persons with disabilities (PWDs), and ensure their full participation in society. As a State Party to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), the Philippines has likewise committed to adopting measures that guarantee equal access to healthcare, education, employment, rehabilitation, assistive technologies, community support services, and independent living for persons with disabilities. These commitments recognize that disability often entails additional costs and barriers that require targeted government intervention beyond general social welfare programs. Despite existing laws such as the Magna Carta for Persons with Disabilities and various programs providing discounts, privileges, and social assistance, many Filipinos with disabilities continue to face significant disability-related expenses, including costs for medicines, rehabilitation, mobility aids, assistive devices, transportation, personal assistance, and specialized educational and employment support. These additional financial burdens frequently result in deeper poverty, reduced economic participation, and diminished opportunities for independent living, particularly among indigent persons with disabilities. This bill seeks to establish a Disability Support Fund that will provide sustained financial assistance and strengthen disability-specific services for indigent persons with disabilities. The measure envisions a comprehensive support system that complements existing national and local government programs by funding disability support services, enhancing the capacity of Persons with Disability Affairs Offices (PDAOs), supporting organizations of persons with disabilities, and providing a regular monthly allowance to qualified beneficiaries to help address disability-related extra costs. It likewise institutionalizes a disability and needs assessment system to ensure that assistance is provided using a rights-based and functional approach consistent with international standards. 1 The proposed measure further strengthens inter-agency coordination through the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), establishes an integrated disability data management system linked with existing government databases, and adopts a phased implementation strategy prioritizing children with disabilities, persons facing the highest support needs, and those already enrolled in existing social protection programs. By recognizing disability-related costs as a distinct dimension of poverty, the bill seeks to promote greater independence, improve access to essential services, facilitate employment and community participation, and reduce long-standing barriers to inclusion. Through the establishment of a dedicated Disability Support Fund, the State affirms its commitment to inclusive development by ensuring that persons with disabilities receive not only legal recognition of their rights but also the practical support necessary to exercise those rights fully and equally. Investing in disability inclusion ultimately strengthens communities, expands economic participation, and promotes a more equitable and compassionate society for all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 10218
title: AN ACT GRANTING THE BANGKO SENTRAL NG PILIPINAS EMERGENCY REGULATORY POWERS OVER SUPERVISED INSTITUTIONS DURING A DECLARED NATIONAL EMERGENCY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE “The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.” — Proverbs 22:3 The Philippine financial system serves as a critical pillar of economic stability, public confidence, and national development. During times of crisis—whether caused by natural disasters, public health emergencies, armed conflict, cyber incidents, or other extraordinary events—millions of Filipinos rely on banks, payment systems, and financial institutions to access their savings, receive assistance, pay obligations, and sustain economic activity. The experience of recent crises has demonstrated that disruptions in financial services can significantly aggravate the hardships faced by individuals, families, businesses, and communities. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) implemented various temporary regulatory accommodations and relief measures that helped preserve financial stability, maintain liquidity, support borrowers, and ensure continued access to financial services. However, many of these interventions relied on the BSP’s existing regulatory powers and specific legislative measures enacted during the emergency. The absence of a permanent statutory framework providing clear authority for emergency financial regulatory actions may limit the government’s capacity to respond swiftly and effectively to future crises. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize the authority of the BSP to issue temporary and binding emergency regulatory directives to BSP-Supervised Financial Institutions during periods of officially declared national emergencies. The bill authorizes the BSP, upon determination by the Monetary Board, to impose reasonable and proportionate relief measures, including payment deferments, restructuring accommodations, consumer assistance programs, temporary waivers or reductions of financial transaction fees, and other interventions necessary to preserve financial stability and protect financial consumers. At the same time, the measure incorporates important safeguards to ensure that emergency powers remain temporary, transparent, proportionate, and subject to 1 periodic review. It recognizes the need to balance consumer protection with the operational viability and financial sustainability of banks, payment service providers, and other financial institutions. The bill likewise strengthens accountability through reporting requirements to Congress and establishes clear enforcement mechanisms for compliance with BSP directives. By providing a clear legal framework for emergency financial interventions, this measure strengthens the country's capacity to respond to future crises, protects depositors and financial consumers, preserves public confidence in the financial system, and promotes economic resilience during periods of uncertainty. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 10219
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11310, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps) ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE “He who has pity on the poor lends to the Lord, and He will pay back what he has given.” — Proverbs 19:17 The Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) has become the country's flagship social protection program, providing conditional cash assistance to millions of poor Filipino households and contributing significantly to improvements in education, health, and poverty alleviation. Through Republic Act No. 11310, the State institutionalized 4Ps as a long-term commitment to break the intergenerational cycle of poverty and promote human capital development among the nation's most vulnerable families. Despite its successes, the Philippine social protection system remains highly fragmented. Various forms of government assistance—including emergency aid, livelihood support, food subsidies, and crisis interventions—continue to operate through separate programs administered under differing guidelines and delivery mechanisms. While these interventions address legitimate needs, the absence of an integrated framework often results in duplication, administrative inefficiencies, inconsistent beneficiary targeting, and delays in the delivery of assistance. Moreover, economic shocks, inflation, public health emergencies, natural disasters, and other crises have demonstrated that vulnerability extends beyond traditional poverty classifications, affecting millions of Filipinos who require immediate and responsive government support. This measure seeks to expand the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program by strengthening its social protection mandate and establishing Pantawid Pag-asa as an integrated and rationalized support program for individuals and families experiencing economic distress and crisis situations. The bill consolidates existing social amelioration programs of similar nature under a unified framework to promote more efficient service delivery, improve beneficiary targeting, and ensure timely assistance to those in need. It likewise institutionalizes a centralized social protection database, streamlines documentary requirements through digitalization and integration with the 1 Philippine Identification System, and strengthens transparency, grievance mechanisms, and monitoring systems. The proposed amendments further provide for the periodic adjustment of cash grants based on inflation and poverty thresholds, prioritize food-poor households in program implementation, and strengthen the institutional capacity of the Department of Social Welfare and Development through dedicated crisis intervention offices nationwide. The measure also seeks to depoliticize the delivery of government assistance by expressly prohibiting political endorsement, manipulation, or exploitation of social amelioration programs, thereby ensuring that public funds are distributed solely on the basis of genuine need and not political patronage. By expanding the scope of the 4Ps and integrating social protection interventions under a more coherent, transparent, and responsive framework, this bill aims to build a more resilient and inclusive social protection system capable of addressing both chronic poverty and emerging socioeconomic vulnerabilities. It affirms the State's commitment to ensuring that no Filipino is left behind in times of hardship while promoting long-term pathways toward economic security and self-sufficiency. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 10220
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE IMPLEMENTATION, MANAGEMENT, AND UTILIZATION OF THE COCONUT FARMERS AND INDUSTRY TRUST FUND, ENHANCING GOVERNANCE AND BENEFICIARY ACCESS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11524, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “COCONUT FARMERS AND INDUSTRY TRUST FUND ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The coconut industry remains one of the cornerstones of Philippine agriculture, providing livelihood to millions of Filipino farmers and contributing significantly to rural development, food security, and export earnings. Recognizing the historical injustice suffered by coconut farmers, Congress enacted Republic Act No. 11524, or the Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund Act, to ensure that the recovered coconut levy assets are utilized exclusively for the benefit of coconut farmers and the long-term rehabilitation and modernization of the coconut industry. While the enactment of Republic Act No. 11524 marked a significant milestone, experience in its implementation has revealed operational, administrative, and governance challenges that limit the timely and effective utilization of the Trust Fund. Delays in project implementation, limited absorptive capacity, fragmented coordination among implementing agencies, outdated beneficiary records, and the absence of measurable performance targets have hindered the realization of the law's intended benefits. There likewise remains a need to strengthen transparency, improve accountability mechanisms, and ensure that Trust Fund resources directly translate into higher productivity, increased farmer incomes, and long-term resilience of the coconut sector. This bill seeks to strengthen the implementation of Republic Act No. 11524 by enhancing the governance framework of the Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund. It authorizes the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) to adopt more responsive implementation strategies, establish measurable annual performance targets, periodically update the Coconut Farmers and Industry Development Plan, digitize and continuously validate the Coconut Farmers Registry, and create a dedicated Program Management Office to improve project delivery and monitoring. The measure also expands support programs for coconut farmers, including productivity enhancement, comprehensive insurance, research and innovation, enterprise development, infrastructure, social protection, and disaster assistance. The proposed amendments further strengthen transparency and accountability by requiring the publication of annual implementation reports, beneficiary information 1 consistent with data privacy laws, audit findings, and project accomplishments. It likewise refines the management and disposition of coconut levy assets to ensure that decisions are guided by the long-term interests of coconut farmers and that public assets are utilized in a manner that generates measurable economic benefits for the industry. The bill also enhances farmer participation in governance by extending the tenure of farmer representatives in the PCA Board and institutionalizing regular consultations with stakeholders. By modernizing the governance structure of the Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund and ensuring more efficient, transparent, and accountable implementation, this measure seeks to maximize the developmental impact of recovered coconut levy assets and secure sustainable economic opportunities for present and future generations of coconut farmers. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 10221
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE POLYTECHNIC UNIVERSITY OF THE PHILIPPINES AS THE COUNTRY'S FIRST NATIONAL POLYTECHNIC UNIVERSITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Education remains one of the most powerful instruments for national development, social mobility, technological advancement, and economic transformation. As the country confronts the challenges of industrial modernization, digital transformation, and global competitiveness, there is an urgent need to strengthen institutions that specialize in technical, vocational, applied scientific, and professional education. The Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP), as one of the largest state universities in the country and a leading institution in providing affordable and accessible higher education, is uniquely positioned to fulfill this national role. Since its establishment, PUP has consistently produced graduates who contribute significantly to the nation's workforce, public service, industry, entrepreneurship, research, and innovation. However, the increasing complexity of economic and technological demands requires a stronger institutional framework that will enable the University to exercise greater academic leadership, expand its research and extension functions, strengthen industry linkages, and serve as a model for polytechnic education throughout the country. This measure seeks to formally strengthen the Polytechnic University of the Philippines as the country's First National Polytechnic University. The bill affirms PUP's leadership role in advancing polytechnic education and mandates it to provide guidance and support to other polytechnic state universities and colleges in developing professional, technical, and applied academic programs responsive to national development priorities. The proposed legislation further enhances the University's institutional and fiscal autonomy, strengthens its governance structure, expands its academic and administrative capacities, protects and maximizes the productive use of its assets and landholdings, and grants fiscal incentives necessary to support its educational mission. It likewise provides safeguards to ensure transparency, accountability, and responsible stewardship of university resources while preserving the institution's academic independence and public character. 1 By elevating and strengthening PUP as the National Polytechnic University, the State invests in a strategic institution capable of producing highly skilled professionals, advancing applied research, promoting technological innovation, supporting industrial development, and expanding educational opportunities for millions of Filipinos. This measure is expected to contribute significantly to nation-building by cultivating a globally competitive workforce equipped to meet the demands of the twenty-first century economy. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. EDUARDO “BRO. EDDIE” C. label: HB 10222
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A COMPREHENSIVE ELECTRONIC WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, MANDATING EXTENDED PRODUCER RESPONSIBILITY, PROVIDING INFRASTRUCTURE AND INCENTIVES FOR E-WASTE RECYCLING, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The world is experiencing exponential growth in Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE), commonly referred to as "e-waste." Driven by rapid technological innovation, global e-waste generation is increasing three times faster than the human population growth. In the Philippines, the widespread adoption of digital technologies, remote work paradigms, and online commerce has accelerated domestic electronic consumption. However, our waste management systems have not evolved alongside this digital transformation. Millions of electronic units reach their end- of-life annually, with the vast majority entering a fragmented, unmonitored waste stream. While the Philippines possesses landmark environmental legislation, there is a clear structural gap regarding e-waste management. Republic Act No. 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000) focuses primarily on municipal solid waste (organic, recyclable, residual, and special wastes). It lacks specific directives, standards, or technical mandates for complex electronic assemblies containing toxic elements. Republic Act No. 6969 (Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act of 1990) regulates toxic chemicals and hazardous materials in bulk, but its enforcement mechanisms are largely designed for industrial manufacturing and chemical imports—not for post-consumer retail electronics widely dispersed among millions of households. Republic Act No. 11898 (Extended Producer Responsibility Act of 2022) established a precedent by mandating producer responsibility for plastic packaging. However, its scope excludes electronics, leaving one of the fastest- growing and most toxic waste streams without a clear extended liability mechanism. Consequently, e-waste in the Philippines exists in a regulatory grey area—neither effectively managed by local municipal systems nor adequately captured by industrial hazardous waste frameworks. This bill institutionalizes a national, closed-loop E-Waste Management System built upon four strategic pillars: 1. Mandatory Segregation and Landfill Prohibition: Explicitly bans the dumping, mixing, or incineration of e-waste within general municipal solid waste networks and standard sanitary landfills. 2. Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Framework: Follows international best practices (such as the EU WEEE Directive) by requiring manufacturers, brand owners, and importers ("Obliged Enterprises") to take financial and operational responsibility for the post-consumer phase of their products. This includes establishing convenient consumer take-back points, funding reverse logistics, and meeting progressive annual recovery and recycling targets. 3. Inclusive Formalization of Informal Recyclers: Rather than criminalizing informal waste pickers, the bill mandates a structured transition plan. Led by DOLE, TESDA, and LGUs, informal workers will be provided technical training, safety gear, health monitoring, and formal accreditation—integrating them into certified Treatment, Storage, and Disposal (TSD) collection chains as recognized green workers. Local government units are required to designate specialized E-Waste Collection Hubs within local Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs). To incentivize private sector investment in high-tech urban mining and recycling facilities, accredited TSD operators will be eligible for fiscal and non-fiscal incentives under existing investment priority systems. The "National Electronic Waste Management Act" bridges a critical legislative gap. It protects public health, safeguards fragile ecosystems, secures valuable raw materials, and ensures that the burden of waste management is shared equitably among manufacturers, distributors, consumers, and state regulators. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 10223
title: AN ACT ENHANCING BARANGAY MATERIALS RECOVERY FACILITIES BY SETTING MINIMUM OPERATIONAL AND INFRASTRUCTURE STANDARDS, PROVIDING DEDICATED FUNDING MECHANISMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9003, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Under Republic Act No. 9003, otherwise known as the "Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000," local government units (LGUs)—specifically the barangays—are tasked with primary responsibility for decentralized waste segregation, recycling, and composting. Central to this mandate is Section 32, which requires the establishment of a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) in every barangay or cluster of barangays. However, more than two decades after the passage of RA 9003, full compliance remains elusive. A substantial number of barangay MRFs across the country are non-operational, serve merely as designated "open drop points" without actual processing capabilities, or lack the fundamental infrastructure needed to sort, compost, and store recyclable and organic waste safely. The primary bottlenecks to sustained operational performance are: 1. Vague Standards: Current legislation outlines the requirement for MRFs but lacks clear, enforceable minimum infrastructure, equipment, and occupational safety standards. 2. Lack of Ring-Fenced Funding: Most barangays lack sufficient fiscal resources to cover capital expenditures for standard equipment or recurring operational costs like honoraria for waste handlers and utility bills. This bill addresses these critical gaps by amending Section 32 of RA 9003 to establish explicit Minimum Operational and Technical Standards for all Barangay MRFs (covering structural enclosure, equipment, health/safety safeguards, and recordkeeping). Funding will be guaranteed through a National Barangay MRF Support Fund (NB- MRFSF) alongside a mandatory appropriation of not less than five percent (5%) of each LGU's National Tax Allotment (NTA) local solid waste management allocation dedicated strictly to MRF operations. Professionalizing and incentivizing local waste management personnel through standardized training and safety protocols shall also be effected. By strengthening local resource recovery, this measure will significantly increase national waste diversion rates, reduce pressure on municipal landfills, and foster a localized circular economy. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. EXPLANATORY NOTE Under Republic Act No. 9003, otherwise known as the "Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000," local government units (LGUs)—specifically the barangays—are tasked with primary responsibility for decentralized waste segregation, recycling, and composting. Central to this mandate is Section 32, which requires the establishment of a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) in every barangay or cluster of barangays. However, more than two decades after the passage of RA 9003, full compliance remains elusive. A substantial number of barangay MRFs across the country are non-operational, serve merely as designated "open drop points" without actual processing capabilities, or lack the fundamental infrastructure needed to sort, compost, and store recyclable and organic waste safely. The primary bottlenecks to sustained operational performance are: 1. Vague Standards: Current legislation outlines the requirement for MRFs but lacks clear, enforceable minimum infrastructure, equipment, and occupational safety standards. 2. Lack of Ring-Fenced Funding: Most barangays lack sufficient fiscal resources to cover capital expenditures for standard equipment or recurring operational costs like honoraria for waste handlers and utility bills. This bill addresses these critical gaps

label: HB 10224
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A COMPREHENSIVE HOUSING PROGRAM FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled:
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Public school teachers are the backbone of our nation’s educational system. They are tasked not only with imparting knowledge but also with shaping the character and future of Filipino youth. Despite their invaluable contribution to society, many public school teachers continue to face economic hardships, particularly regarding affordable and decent housing. Due to modest salaries and the rising costs of real estate, a significant number of our teachers are forced to rent substandard housing, live in areas far from their designated schools, or rely on high-interest loans that further deplete their take- home pay. Long commutes and poor living conditions contribute to physical exhaustion and mental stress, which ultimately impact the quality of education delivered to our students. This bill, otherwise known as the "Public School Teachers’ Housing Act," seeks to address this pressing issue by institutionalizing a comprehensive, accessible, and affordable housing program specifically designed for active public school teachers. By providing low-interest housing loans, subsidized amortization, and dedicated on-site housing projects near public schools, this measure aims to uplift the living standards of our educators, ensure their financial security, and motivate them to remain in the noble profession of teaching. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 10225
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A FRAMEWORK FOR THE COMPREHENSIVE DEVELOPMENT, PROMOTION, AND PROTECTION OF THE PHILIPPINE UBE INDUSTRY, DECLARING UBE AS A NATIONAL PRIORITY CROP, CREATING THE PHILIPPINE UBE INDUSTRY COUNCIL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines possesses a rich agricultural heritage and a wide range of crops with the potential to contribute meaningfully to rural development, livelihood generation, food security, and export growth. Among these is Dioscorea alata, more commonly known as ube or purple yam, a crop deeply rooted in Filipino food culture and increasingly recognized in domestic and international markets for its distinctive color, flavor, and versatility. For generations, ube has been a familiar and valued part of Filipino cuisine, used in products such as ube halaya, cakes, breads, pastries, beverages, ice cream, and other traditional and modern food preparations. In recent years, growing interest in authentic Filipino flavors, natural ingredients, and value-added agricultural products has expanded opportunities for ube farmers, processors, entrepreneurs, and exporters. Ube is cultivated in different parts of the country, including Bicol, Bohol, Leyte, Aurora, Quezon, Laguna, Pangasinan, Quirino and other areas with suitable agricultural conditions and farming communities. This broad and expanding production base demonstrates that ube is not merely a local specialty, but a crop with national importance and long-term development potential. Despite this opportunity, the Philippine ube industry remains fragmented and faces continuing constraints in the areas of quality planting materials, research and development, post- harvest handling, processing, financing, market access, quality assurance, and coordinated promotion. Without a clear national framework, the industry may remain vulnerable to inconsistent quality, weak supply coordination, limited farmer participation in value addition, and misuse of names and reputations associated with Philippine ube products. 1 This measure seeks to address these gaps by establishing a comprehensive framework for the development, promotion, and protection of the Philippine ube industry. It declares ube as a National Priority Crop, creates a Philippine Ube Industry Council to coordinate policy and implementation, strengthens support for production, research, processing, quality standards, and market development, and encourages the protection of geographic indications, collective marks, and other intellectual property rights associated with Philippine ube. The bill likewise seeks to ensure that the growth of the industry translates into more stable and meaningful benefits for Filipino farmers, cooperatives, rural enterprises, and local communities. A successful ube industry must not be measured by exports alone, but by the extent to which Filipino producers are able to participate more fully and fairly in the value chain. By providing a clear national policy, strengthening institutional coordination, and promoting quality, innovation, authenticity, and farmer-centered development, this measure aims to position the Philippines as a leading global source of high-quality ube and ube-based products while preserving the crop’s Filipino identity and value. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. RICHARD I. front_matter: Republic of the Philippines House of Representatives July 27, 2026 Quezon City, Metro Manila 10:19 am TWENTIETH CONGRESS Second Regular Session House Bill No. 10226 _______ Act No. 11930), these measures primarily address harms after they occur rather than regulating access, design features, and systemic risks inherent in digital platforms. Globally, governments are shifting toward preventive frameworks. Australia has enacted a minimum age ban on social media access, while European jurisdictions, such as France, have adopted parental consent models. Legislative proposals in the United States also aim to restrict algorithmic targeting of minors and impose heightened duties of care on platforms. These developments signal a growing international consensus that protecting minors in the digital environment requires proactive, design-based regulation and shared responsibility among the State, parents, and digital service providers. The "Responsible Social Media Access for Minors Act" proposes a hybrid regulatory approach, balancing the State's duty to protect minors, the constitutional rights to expression and access to information, and the primary role of parents and guardians. It recognizes evolving capacities of minors while ensuring that digital environments are designed with their safety and well-being in mind. Instead of a total prohibition, the bill introduces a tiered system of access combined with strict platform accountability, ensuring both protection and proportionality

label: HB 10227
title: AN ACT SAFEGUARDING PERSONALITY RIGHTS AGAINST UNAUTHORIZED USE OF FACE, VOICE, AND IDENTITY THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DEEPFAKE TECHNOLOGY, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has brought both opportunities and risks to society. Among the most pressing concerns is the rise of deepfake technology—synthetic media capable of imitating a person’s face, voice, and likeness with alarming realism. While AI can be used for innovation and creativity, deepfakes have increasingly been weaponized for harmful purposes such as identity theft, online scams, sexual exploitation, disinformation, and reputational attacks. Globally, governments and institutions are recognizing the dangers posed by manipulated media. Reports have shown how deepfakes have been used to spread false political propaganda, mislead the public, and exploit individuals without their consent. In the Philippines, the Philippine National Police Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) has already documented thousands of cybercrime cases linked to AI misuse, underscoring the urgent need for a legal framework that directly addresses this emerging threat. Existing laws, such as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 and the Data Privacy Act of 2012 provide general safeguards but do not adequately cover the complexities of AI-generated impersonations. This bill fills that gap by explicitly protecting the personality rights of individuals against unauthorized use of their face, voice, and other identifiable features. It prohibits the malicious creation and distribution of deepfakes, establishes a takedown mechanism for victims, requires labeling of synthetic content, and imposes penalties on violators, including platform providers who fail to act responsibly. By enacting this measure, the State affirms its duty to uphold privacy, dignity, and identity in the digital age. It ensures that citizens retain control over their personal attributes, deters the spread of misinformation, and promotes the ethical use of AI technologies. This bill is a forward-looking safeguard that balances innovation with accountability, protecting both individuals and democratic institutions from the dangers of manipulated media. ATTY. label: HB 10228
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NO CALL, NO TEXT, AND NO EMAIL LISTING SYSTEM TO SAFEGUARD PRIVACY AND PENALIZE VIOLATORS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Unsolicited calls, text messages, and emails have become a persistent nuisance and a growing threat to the privacy and security of Filipino consumers. In recent years, scam- related activities have escalated, with voice phishing (“vishing”), SMS phishing, and AI- generated impersonations being used to deceive subscribers, impersonate trusted institutions, and steal sensitive information. Reports estimate that overall scam-related losses in the Philippines now reach billions of pesos annually, underscoring the urgent need for stronger safeguards. While existing laws such as the Data Privacy Act of 2012 provide general protection, they do not directly address the widespread problem of unsolicited commercial communication and the evolving risks posed by modern technologies. This bill seeks to fill that gap by establishing a No Call, No Text, and No Email Registry under the National Privacy Commission (NPC), allowing subscribers to register their numbers and email addresses to block unwanted solicitations. It also mandates clear consent requirements, opt-out mechanisms, and penalties for violators, ensuring that consumers retain control over their digital communications. By enacting this measure, the State affirms its duty to uphold the fundamental right to privacy, promote responsible business practices, and protect citizens from fraud, harassment, and exploitation. This bill empowers subscribers to choose with whom they transact, reduces exposure to scams, and strengthens trust in digital communication systems. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 10229
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10586, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI-DRUNK AND DRUGGED DRIVING ACT OF 2013”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE More than a decade after the passage of Republic Act No. 10586, or the “Anti-Drunk and Drugged Driving Act of 2013,” incidents of impaired driving continue to claim lives. The issue lies not in the absence of penalties but in weak enforcement and operational gaps. Law enforcers often lack proper equipment, drivers refuse testing without consequence, hospitals fail to conduct timely examinations, and modern evidence, such as CCTV or dashcam footage, is underutilized. Local traffic authorities remain under-empowered, while establishments serving alcohol bear no responsibility in preventing impaired driving. This measure seeks to amend RA 10586 by strengthening enforcement standards, mandating equipment, ensuring admissibility of evidence, requiring post-accident testing, deputizing local traffic enforcers, and assigning preventive duties to establishments. By closing these gaps, the law will move from merely penalizing offenders to being effectively enforced nationwide. Road safety is a shared responsibility, and this amendment aims to protect lives, promote responsible driving, and restore public confidence in traffic enforcement. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 10230
title: AN ACT ENSURING FREE BIRTH REGISTRATION FOR INDIGENT FILIPINO CHILDREN AND PROVIDING FUNDS FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE A birth certificate is the foundation of legal identity. Without it, a child is denied access to education, healthcare, and social services, and remains invisible to the State. Yet millions of Filipinos, especially children from indigent families, continue to live without this essential document due to the costs and penalties imposed for registration. This measure seeks to remove those financial barriers by mandating free birth registration and late registration for children of indigent parents, as well as free registration for foundlings. It also empowers barangays to monitor and assist families, while directing national agencies to ensure proper implementation. By guaranteeing free and universal birth registration, the State fulfills its duty to protect the rights of every Filipino child, uphold their dignity, and secure their access to the privileges of citizenship. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 10232
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR EXPANDED PATERNITY LEAVE BENEFITS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 8187, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PATERNITY LEAVE ACT OF 1996”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The role of fathers in Filipino families continues to evolve beyond the traditional concept of being solely providers for the household. Today, fathers play an increasingly active role in caregiving, child development, and providing emotional and physical support to their spouses and children, particularly during the critical period following childbirth. Republic Act No. 8187, otherwise known as the “Paternity Leave Act of 1993,” recognized the importance of allowing fathers to support their spouses and bond with their newborn children by granting paternity leave benefits. However, the current period provided under the law remains limited and may no longer be sufficient to address the realities and responsibilities of modern parenthood. The early days following childbirth require shared responsibility between parents. Providing fathers with additional time to care for their spouses, assist in childcare, and adjust to their new family responsibilities promotes stronger family relationships, improves the well-being of mothers and children, and encourages a more equitable distribution of caregiving duties within the household. Therefore, this bill seeks to expand the existing paternity leave benefits by increasing the number of leave days granted to fathers and allowing greater support during childbirth, miscarriage, and other pregnancy-related circumstances. By strengthening paternity leave protections, this bill recognizes the essential role of fathers in nurturing their families and promoting a healthier work-life balance. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 10233
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FREE ANNUAL MEDICAL CHECK-UP FOR FILIPINOS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Many Filipinos delay or forego medical consultations and diagnostic examinations due to the cost of healthcare services. This often results in the late detection of illnesses, higher medical expenses, and increased risk of complications that could have been prevented through regular check-ups and timely medical intervention. Preventive healthcare is essential in building a healthier nation. Regular medical check-ups allow early identification of health risks, promote healthier lifestyles, and enable appropriate treatment before illnesses progress into more serious conditions. Strengthening preventive health services will not only improve individual health outcomes but also reduce the long-term burden on families and the country’s healthcare system. More importantly, early detection and proper medical intervention can help save lives by identifying serious health conditions at a stage when treatment is more effective and recovery is more attainable. Therefore, this bill seeks to institutionalize the Libreng Check-Up Program by providing every Filipino with access to a free annual medical check-up through the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth). The program shall cover general physical examinations and basic laboratory and diagnostic tests through accredited healthcare providers and institutions, consistent with existing health programs and subject to expansion based on the health needs of Filipinos. Fundamentally, this bill aims to promote preventive healthcare, encourage early detection of diseases, and ensure equitable access to essential health services so that every Filipino may receive timely care before medical conditions become severe or life-threatening In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR. label: HB 10234
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING LOCAL SPORTS PROGRAMS TO DEVELOP YOUNG ATHLETES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Sports play an important role in promoting the holistic development of the youth by improving physical health, strengthening mental and emotional well-being, fostering discipline, and developing teamwork and leadership. Beyond individual growth, sports also promote unity, camaraderie, and community participation, while serving as an avenue for discovering and developing talented Filipino athletes. The Philippines has continuously produced athletes capable of competing and excelling at the highest levels of competition. However, many promising young athletes, especially those in local communities, continue to face challenges due to limited access to proper training facilities, sports equipment, financial assistance, and organized development programs. These barriers prevent many talented individuals from maximizing their potential and pursuing opportunities in competitive sports. While existing programs support national sports development, there remains a need to further strengthen grassroots initiatives that directly benefit young athletes, local sports clubs, associations, and community-based organizations. Providing adequate resources and support at the local level will help create a stronger foundation for identifying, training, and developing future athletes who can represent the country in national and international competitions. Therefore, this bill seeks to strengthen local sports development programs by providing financial assistance to young athletes, supporting local sports organizations, and improving access to sports facilities and equipment. Through the creation of dedicated support mechanisms, greater youth participation in sports is encouraged and athletic opportunities are made more accessible and inclusive. Ultimately, this bill aims to develop a healthier and more active citizenry, empower young Filipino athletes, and build stronger communities through accessible and sustainable grassroots sports programs. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. MANUEL “WOWO” L. FORTES, JR.
