label: HB 10474
title: AN ACT ENSURING INCLUSIVE AND ACCESSIBLE CIVIL REGISTRATION FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, INTERNALLY DISPLACED PERSONS, FOUNDLINGS, AND OTHER MARGINALIZED GROUPS, STRENGTHENING LOCAL CIVIL REGISTRY OFFICES, PROMOTING DIGITAL AND INTEROPERABLE REGISTRATION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Civil registration is a core function of the State. By recording births, marriages, deaths, and other vital events, government formally recognizes each person’s legal identity and civil status and enables the enjoyment of civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights. Despite previous reforms, the Philippines still faces serious gaps in civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS) coverage.1 The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), as the central authority for official statistics and civil registration under Republic Act No. 10625, or the Philippine Statistical System Act of 2013, has advanced the modernization of civil registration and improved the production of vital statistics. However, several persistent challenges prevent the attainment of a universal, timely, and fully responsive CRVS system. Delayed birth registration remains common, especially in unserved and underserved areas (UUAs) and geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDAs)2. Many children reach school age, or even adulthood, without a birth certificate. Since a birth certificate is frequently required for school enrollment, access to social protection, formal employment, land titling, and other services, these delays directly translate into exclusion. Existing late‑registration procedures can be complex, time‑consuming, and costly, which further disadvantages poor and marginalized families. 1 United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP). 2025 Review of Progress Made on Civil Registration and Vital Statistics in Asia and the Pacific After a Decade of Getting Every One in the Picture. UNESCAP, 2025. https://crvs.unescap.org/2025-review-progress/overview 2 WeSolve Foundation, Inc. Everyone Should Count: Barriers and Opportunities for Birth Registration in the Philippines. WeSolve Foundation, November 2025, citing data from the Philippine Statistics Authority and the Child Rights Network. https://serp-p.pids.gov.ph/publication/public/view?slug=everyone-should-count-barriers-and-opportunities-for-birth-registration-in-the- philippines Registration is also incomplete among Indigenous Peoples (IPs), internally displaced persons (IDPs), foundlings, and children in conflict situations. A 2024 World Bank report, produced jointly with the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples, the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos, and the PSA, found that many IP communities are located in remote areas, rely on customary institutions, and face linguistic and cultural barriers that impede regular engagement with government offices3. IDPs displaced by armed conflict, natural disasters, or development projects often lose their documents or are separated from their place of origin and local civil registry. Foundlings and abandoned infants, as well as children born amid armed conflict, disasters, or displacement, are particularly vulnerable to non‑registration and even statelessness, which may result in lifelong exclusion from formal systems and services. Coordination across institutions is fragmented. The PSA, Local Civil Registry Offices (LCROs), barangay health facilities, the Department of Health (DOH), Department of Education (DepEd), Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), and local government units (LGUs) all play roles in recording or using vital events. Births and deaths frequently occur in health facilities or in communities served by barangay health workers, teachers, and social workers. Yet mechanisms to systematically and consistently transmit information from these front‑line providers to LCROs and PSA remain weak. In practice, many events are either never recorded, or reported late, and data across health, education, and social protection systems are not harmonized. Interoperability among civil registration, health, and social protection databases is limited. At the local level, many LGUs still depend heavily on manual and paper‑based processes. Numerous LCROs use paper logbooks and manual encoding, with insufficient storage, back‑up, and disaster‑proofing of records. Given these legal, institutional, and operational gaps, there is a strong need for a new legislative framework that will transform the Philippine CRVS system into a comprehensive, inclusive, digital, and responsive backbone for governance and social protection. The proposed “Civil Registration Inclusion and Accessibility Act” seeks to: 1) Guarantee universal, inclusive, and timely registration of all vital events, with special attention to Indigenous Peoples, internally displaced persons, foundlings, children in conflict situations, and other marginalized groups. The bill 3 World Bank, in partnership with the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples, the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos, and the Philippine Statistics Authority. No Data, No Story: Indigenous Peoples in the Philippines. World Bank, May 2024. institutionalizes mobile registration, outreach programs, and mechanisms for fee waivers or penalty condonation for indigent applicants and those in exceptional circumstances. 2) Create a robust inter-agency governance mechanism through a National CRVS Inter‑Agency Council chaired by the PSA, with mandatory participation from DILG, DOH, DepEd, DSWD, DFA, DOJ, DICT, LGU leagues, and other relevant bodies. This Council will be responsible for policy harmonization, standard-setting, performance monitoring, and coordinated implementation across national and local levels. 3) Integrate health, education, and social protection systems with CRVS by mandating electronic notification of births, deaths, and other vital events by health facilities and relevant front-line service providers. The bill provides for secure and privacy-compliant interoperability among CRVS, health information systems, and social protection registries to enable more accurate targeting, reduce duplication, and improve service delivery. 4) Accelerate digitalization and modernization of civil registratio

label: HB 10482
title: AN ACT DECLARING JUNE 24 OF EVERY YEAR A SPECIAL NON- WORKING HOLIDAY IN THE CITY OF MANILA, TO BE KNOWN AS "MANILA DAY," AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE June 24, 1571 marks the formal establishment of the City of Manila by Miguel López de Legazpi, laying the foundation for what would become the capital of the Philippines and the center of the country's political, economic, cultural, and historical development. For more than four centuries, Manila has stood at the forefront of the nation's history. It has witnessed the country's struggles, triumphs, and transformation. It serves as the seat of government and the home of countless institutions that have shaped the Filipino identity. Like any great city, Manila's history is full of conflicts, one of both glory and adversity. Yet, through every trial, Manila has remained steadfast, continually rebuilding and moving forward. Celebrating its founding is not only an occasion to honor its past, but also an opportunity to reaffirm hope for its future and recognize the unwavering spirit of the Manileños. Declaring June 24 of every year as a special non-working holiday in the City of Manila will provide residents the opportunity to commemorate the city's founding, participate in civic and cultural activities, and foster greater appreciation of Manila's enduring legacy and invaluable contributions to nation-building. Ultimately, this measure recognizes the importance of preserving local history and strengthening the sense of identity and pride among Manileños, especially the younger generation. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10483
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING ACCESSIBLE AND EFFICIENT NET METERING, AND STRENGTHENING INCENTIVES FOR DISTRIBUTED RENEWABLE ENERGY SYSTEMS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines continues to face rising electricity costs and increasing demand for reliable and sustainable sources of energy. In recent years, the government has intensified efforts to expand renewable energy development and encourage greater consumer participation in the country's energy transition. However, many households, businesses, and institutions seeking to install rooftop solar and other distributed renewable energy systems continue to encounter delays, burdensome procedures, and inadequate incentives in availing of net metering services. Net metering enables consumers to generate electricity for their own use and export excess power to the grid, thereby reducing electricity costs, improving energy security, and supporting the country's renewable energy goals. While existing policies have established a framework for net metering, there remains a need to institutionalize a streamlined, transparent, and consumer-friendly system that will encourage its wider adoption. This measure seeks to simplify and expedite the net metering application process, establish a centralized digital platform for applications and monitoring, strengthen consumer protections, improve compensation for excess electricity supplied to the grid, and expand opportunities for shared and community-based net metering arrangements. By empowering consumers to become active participants in electricity generation, this measure will help accelerate the transition to clean energy, enhance energy resilience, and contribute to a more sustainable and affordable energy future for all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10484
title: AN ACT GRANTING TAX INCENTIVES TO PHYSICIANS AND DENTISTS WHO RENDER QUALIFIED PRO BONO SERVICES TO INDIGENT AND UNDERSERVED FILIPINOS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to healthcare remains a challenge for many Filipinos. While government programs continue to expand healthcare coverage, many patients still rely on the generosity and dedication of physicians and dentists who voluntarily provide their services free of charge. Through medical missions, charity clinics, emergency response efforts, and other pro bono work, these healthcare professionals help bring much-needed care to those who would otherwise go untreated. Their contributions not only improve health outcomes but also strengthen the delivery of healthcare services in communities with limited access to medical and dental care. This bill seeks to encourage and recognize such service by granting reasonable and accountable tax incentives to physicians and dentists who render qualified pro bono services to indigent and underserved Filipinos. By supporting healthcare professionals who volunteer their time and expertise, the State can help expand access to essential healthcare while advancing its constitutional duty to protect and promote the right to health of the people. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10486
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING SAFEGUARDS FOR THE USE OF ONLINE GAMES, SOCIAL MEDIA, AND DIGITAL PLATFORMS BY MINORS THROUGH THE MOVIE AND TELEVISION REVIEW AND CLASSIFICATION BOARD (MTRCB), PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Children today are growing up in a digital environment where social media, online games, and other online platforms have become an integral part of their daily lives. While these technologies offer opportunities for learning, they also expose minors to serious risks. Despite this, there is currently no comprehensive Philippine law requiring digital platforms to implement uniform age verification systems or subjecting them to meaningful accountability for failing to protect minors. Many platforms continue to rely solely on self-declared birth dates, allowing underage users to easily circumvent age restrictions. This measure seeks to fill this gap by empowering the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) to establish age classifications and child safety standards for digital platforms, require reasonable age verification mechanisms, and hold platform operators and developers accountable for violations, while ensuring full respect for the constitutional rights to privacy, due process, freedom of expression, and access to information. It likewise preserves the primary responsibility of parents and legal guardians in guiding and supervising their children's online activities. By requiring digital platforms to exercise greater responsibility in protecting Filipino children, this bill promotes a safer digital environment where innovation and technology can flourish without compromising the welfare and best interests of the youth. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10487
title: AN ACT MANDATING LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS TO USE BODY- WORN CAMERAS IN LAW ENFORCEMENT OPERATIONS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The prime duty of the Government is to serve and protect the people. Article III (Bill of Rights) of the Constitution guarantees every person the rights to due process, security against unreasonable searches and seizures, and equal protection under the law. These constitutional guarantees require that law enforcement operations be conducted with professionalism, transparency, and accountability. Body-worn cameras have become an internationally recognized tool for promoting responsible policing. They provide an objective record of law enforcement operations, protect law enforcement officers against false or malicious complaints, deter abuses of authority, and preserve valuable evidence for criminal prosecutions. Ultimately, it strengthens public confidence in the justice system. Although the Supreme Court has required the use of body-worn cameras in the execution of search warrants through A.M. No. 21-06-08-SC, no comprehensive law presently mandates their use across all law enforcement operations. This measure seeks to institutionalize the mandatory use of body-worn cameras by law enforcement officers during the conduct of law enforcement operations. It likewise establishes standards for their use and custody, protect the privacy of individuals, and impose appropriate penalties for violations. By promoting transparency while safeguarding constitutional rights, this measure strengthens both effective law enforcement and public trust in government institutions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10488
title: AN ACT PROVIDING MAINTENANCE MEDICINE VOUCHERS FOR SENIOR CITIZENS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Every day, thousands of elderly Filipinos rely on medicines to manage hypertension, diabetes, arthritis, and other chronic illnesses. Yet, for many of them, the rising cost of medicines has become a burden too heavy to bear. Too often, our senior citizens are forced to make painful choices. Some skip doses to make their medicines last longer. Others delay buying prescriptions because their limited pensions or savings are barely enough to cover their daily necessities. But this is not right. This is far from what they deserve. Our senior citizens have spent decades working, raising families, building communities, and contributing to our nation's progress. Panahon na upang suklian naman natin ang kanilang mga sakripisyo sa pamamagitan ng tunay at konkretong malasakit. They deserve the assurance that the medicines they depend on will always be within their reach. This measure seeks to establish a Maintenance Medicine Voucher Program that will provide qualified senior citizens with monthly maintenance medicine vouchers worth One Thousand Pesos (₱1,000.00). The vouchers may be redeemed at Department of Health hospitals and accredited hospitals and pharmacies, making assistance simple, accessible, and convenient for elderly beneficiaries. Sa kulturang Pilipino, hindi natin pinababayaan ang ating mga magulang, lolo, at lola. Caring for those who once cared for us is more than an act of gratitude—it is a reflection of who we are as a people. Ultimately, by ensuring that our senior citizens receive the medicines they need, we help them have more meaningful time with the families they love. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10490
title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO DETERMINE, SET, AND APPROVE THE BED CAPACITY AND SERVICE CAPABILITY OF ALL DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH HOSPITALS, ELIMINATING THE REQUIREMENT OF A SEPARATE LAW FOR FUTURE ADJUSTMENTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE At present, increases in the bed capacity and service capability of Department of Health (DOH) hospitals generally require the enactment of a separate law by Congress. While legislative oversight remains important, this process can delay much-needed improvements in government hospitals despite clear and urgent healthcare needs. The Department of Health is in the best position to determine when hospitals need additional beds or upgraded services based on population growth, disease patterns, hospital occupancy, and other public health considerations. Empowering the DOH to make these administrative determinations will enable government hospitals to respond more quickly and efficiently to the healthcare needs of the Filipino people. This measure authorizes the DOH to determine and approve the bed capacity and service capability of all DOH hospitals, subject to appropriate standards and existing budgetary laws. By streamlining the process while preserving Congress' power over appropriations, the bill promotes a more responsive and effective public healthcare system. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10491
title: AN ACT DEFINING AND PENALIZING DIGITAL FORGERY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10175, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "CYBERCRIME PREVENTION ACT OF 2012," AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Artificial intelligence has transformed our lives in many ways. It has opened new opportunities in education, business, healthcare, and countless other fields. However, the same technology has also made it alarmingly easy to fabricate highly realistic images, videos, and audio recordings that falsely portray a person saying or doing things that never happened. These digitally forged or "deepfake" materials have become powerful tools for fraud, identity theft, online scams, sexual exploitation, harassment, political disinformation, and reputational attacks. Because they are often difficult to distinguish from authentic content, they undermine public trust in digital communications and expose individuals to serious harm. While existing laws penalize offenses such as cybercrime, identity theft, defamation, and violations of privacy, they do not directly address the non-consensual creation and dissemination of digitally manipulated content that exploits a person's face, likeness, voice, or other identifying characteristics through artificial intelligence and similar technologies. This bill seeks to fill that gap by defining and penalizing the crime of Digital Forgery. It criminalizes the knowing and unauthorized creation, publication, distribution, and use of digitally manipulated content that falsely represents an identifiable person, while preserving legitimate uses of technology for lawful purposes. As technology continues to advance, our laws must keep pace to ensure that innovation is encouraged without sacrificing the dignity and security of every Filipino. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10494
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING PUBLIC VETERINARY CLINICS AND ANIMAL SHELTERS IN EVERY CITY AND MUNICIPALITY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Every day, we see stray dogs and cats roaming our streets and neighborhoods. Many of these animals have been abandoned or were born on the streets, left without proper food, shelter, and medical care. Their growing numbers have become a concern not only for animal welfare, but also for public health and community safety. Unfortunately, many cities and municipalities still do not have public veterinary clinics or animal shelters that can provide affordable veterinary services, rescue abandoned animals, or implement effective spaying and neutering programs. Without these essential services, local governments are left with limited means to address the increasing stray animal population in a humane and sustainable manner. This bill seeks to establish public veterinary clinics and animal shelters in every city and municipality. By making veterinary care more accessible, local government units will be better equipped to reduce the number of stray animals while improving animal welfare. This measure benefits not only animals, but the entire community. Healthier and vaccinated animals help reduce the risk of diseases such as rabies. Effective population control means fewer stray animals on our streets. Public shelters provide a safe place for rescued animals instead of leaving them to suffer or pose risks to motorists and pedestrians. Most importantly, this bill encourages communities to treat animals with compassion while creating cleaner, safer, and healthier neighborhoods for everyone. A community that cares for its animals is a community that values public health, safety, and compassion. By investing in local veterinary services and humane animal welfare programs, we also invest in the well-being of our communities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10495
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE LOCAL SPORTS DEVELOPMENT FUND FOR CITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES, PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT, DEVELOPMENT, AND MAINTENANCE OF SPORTS AND RECREATIONAL FACILITIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In recent years, Filipino athletes have continued to make the nation proud by excelling on the global stage. From the Olympics and the Asian Games to international competitions across various sports, they have demonstrated that Filipino talent can compete with the best in the world. Their achievements have inspired countless young Filipinos to dream bigger and pursue excellence through sports. These successes, however, must be matched with sustained investment at the grassroots level. Many cities and municipalities still lack adequate sports and recreational facilities where children, aspiring athletes, and ordinary citizens can safely train, exercise, and stay active. Without accessible venues, many promising athletes never get the opportunity to develop their talents. This measure seeks to establish the Local Sports Development Fund to provide every city and municipality with dedicated financial assistance for the construction, rehabilitation, and maintenance of public sports and recreational facilities. Recognizing that every peso of public funds must be properly accounted for, the bill likewise requires the creation of a publicly accessible online transparency portal where citizens can easily monitor the amount of funding received by their city or municipality, the projects undertaken, and how these funds are being utilized. This promotes accountability, strengthens public trust, and ensures that resources intended for sports development truly benefit the communities they are meant to serve. Now is the time to build on the momentum created by the remarkable achievements of our Filipino athletes. By investing in local sports infrastructure, we can discover and nurture future champions while promoting healthier and more active communities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10496
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE MODERNIZATION OF FILIPINO FARMERS BY ESTABLISHING AN AFFORDABLE INSTALLMENT PROGRAM FOR THE ACQUISITION OF MODERN AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Even today, it is common to see Filipino farmers plowing their fields with carabaos, planting and harvesting by hand, and relying on traditional farming methods that have been passed down for generations. While these practices reflect the hard work and resilience of our farmers, they also remind us that many have yet to benefit from the advances in modern agriculture. Modern tractors, harvesters, and other farm machinery are often seen only in large farms. The benefits of modern farming equipment are undeniable. They can help farmers produce more, reduce costs, save time, and lessen the physical burden of farm work. Unfortunately, for many farmers, the challenge is not a lack of willingness to modernize, but a lack of access. This measure seeks to change that by establishing an affordable installment program that will allow small-scale farmers to acquire modern agricultural machinery and equipment through lenient and farmer-friendly payment terms. By making mechanization more accessible, we can help improve farm productivity, increase farmers' incomes, and strengthen our country's food security. The people who work tirelessly to put food on our table should never be left behind. They deserve the same opportunity to benefit from modern technology and build a better future for themselves and their families. Through the Modernong Magsasaka Act, we take a meaningful step toward making agricultural modernization a reality not only for large farms, but for every hardworking Filipino farmer. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10497
title: AN ACT RESTORING THE TAX CREDIT FOR MANDATORY SENIOR CITIZEN DISCOUNTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9994, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZENS ACT OF 2010," AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE For decades, the Filipino people have rightly recognized the invaluable contributions of our senior citizens by granting them discounts and other privileges under the law. These benefits are a reflection of our nation's gratitude and commitment to ensuring that our elderly live with dignity and security. While the objective of these benefits remains unquestioned, the manner in which they are financed has changed over time. When Republic Act No. 7432 was enacted in 1992, private establishments were granted a 100% tax credit for the mandatory discounts extended to senior citizens. This recognized that while businesses served as the mechanism for delivering the benefit, the cost of the government's social welfare policy should ultimately be borne by the State. However, Republic Act No. 9257 replaced the tax credit with a tax deduction, a policy that was later retained under Republic Act No. 9994. As a result, businesses are no longer fully reimbursed for the discounts they are legally required to grant. This has placed a significant financial burden on many establishments, particularly micro, small, and medium enterprises, which continue to comply with the law while absorbing much of its cost. This measure does not seek to diminish or remove the benefits enjoyed by senior citizens. On the contrary, it seeks to preserve these benefits while restoring the original principle that government-funded social welfare programs should ultimately be financed by the government itself. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10498
title: AN ACT GRANTING A TAX CREDIT FOR MANDATORY PWD DISCOUNTS, THEREBY AMENDING SECTION 32 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7277, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MAGNA CARTA FOR DISABLED PERSONS, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Private establishments have long been partners of the government in implementing the mandatory discounts granted to persons with disabilities. While these benefits are essential and must continue to be protected, the financial burden of providing them has largely been borne by businesses. Under the current law, establishments may only claim the mandatory discounts as tax deductions, allowing them to recover only a portion of the amount they are required by law to provide. Today, many businesses—especially micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs)—continue to faithfully honor these discounts despite the growing financial burden of doing so. As partners of the government in advancing social welfare, they should not be expected to finance public welfare programs from their own limited resources. This bill seeks to replace the existing tax deduction with a tax credit equivalent to one hundred percent (100%) of the mandatory discounts granted to qualified persons with disabilities. In doing so, it ensures that private establishments are fully reimbursed for complying with the law, while preserving all the benefits and privileges currently enjoyed by persons with disabilities. This measure does not seek to diminish or remove the benefits. On the contrary, it seeks to preserve these benefits while restoring the original principle that government-funded social welfare programs should ultimately be financed by the government itself. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10499
title: AN ACT FURTHER EXTENDING THE ESTATE TAX AMNESTY UNTIL JUNE 30, 2028, THEREBY AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11213, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Estate Tax Amnesty Act has enabled thousands of Filipino families to settle long-overdue estate tax obligations, transfer ownership of inherited properties, and bring previously unregistered assets into the formal economy. It has likewise encouraged voluntary tax compliance while generating additional revenues for the government. However, many heirs and beneficiaries have yet to avail of the amnesty. Despite the extension granted, many Filipino families continue to face economic challenges brought about by the rising cost of living, inflation, and the lingering financial effects of recent years. For many, settling estate taxes remains a significant financial burden. Extending the Estate Tax Amnesty until June 30, 2028, and expanding its coverage to estates of decedents who died on or before May 31, 2024, will provide qualified taxpayers with a reasonable opportunity to comply with their tax obligations without the burden of accumulated penalties and interest. By giving taxpayers additional time to comply, the government not only assists families in preserving their inherited assets but also promotes a more equitable and effective tax system that ultimately benefits both taxpayers and the State. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10500
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES IN STATE UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES, ESTABLISHING MENTAL HEALTH OFFICES IN ALL CAMPUSES, PROVIDING FOR ADEQUATE MENTAL HEALTH PERSONNEL, PROGRAMS, AND SERVICES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE College should be a time for learning, growth, and pursuing one's dreams. Yet for many students in our State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), it is also a time of overwhelming academic pressure, financial hardship, personal struggles, and uncertainty about the future. These challenges can take a serious toll on their mental health, affecting not only their academic performance but also their overall well-being. While Republic Act No. 11036, or the Mental Health Act, recognizes the right of every Filipino to accessible mental health services, many SUCs still lack adequate mental health personnel, dedicated offices, and comprehensive programs to meet the growing needs of their students. Too often, those who seek help are met with limited resources or have nowhere to turn. This bill seeks to strengthen mental health services in all State Universities and Colleges by establishing Mental Health Offices in every campus, ensuring the availability of qualified mental health professionals, institutionalizing mental health programs and crisis intervention services, and providing adequate funding for their implementation. By investing in the mental well-being of our students, we also invest in the future of our nation. A similar measure was approved on Third Reading by the House of Representatives during the Nineteenth Congress but was not enacted into law before the close of Congress. Considering the continuing mental health challenges faced by our students, the passage of this measure remains both timely and necessary. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10501
title: AN ACT DECLARING THE VERDE ISLAND PASSAGE IN THE PROVINCES OF BATANGAS, MARINDUQUE, OCCIDENTAL MINDORO, ORIENTAL MINDORO, AND ROMBLON, A PROTECTED AREA WITH THE CATEGORY OF PROTECTED SEASCAPE UNDER THE NATIONAL INTEGRATED PROTECTED AREAS SYSTEM (NIPAS), TO BE REFERRED TO AS THE VERDE ISLAND PASSAGE PROTECTED SEASCAPE, PROVIDING FOR ITS MANAGEMENT, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Verde Island Passage (VIP) is internationally recognized as the "center of the center of marine shore fish biodiversity." Spanning the provinces of Batangas, Oriental Mindoro, Occidental Mindoro, Marinduque, and Romblon, it is home to extensive coral reefs, mangrove forests, and seagrass beds that support one of the world's richest marine ecosystems. These waters provide food security, livelihoods for thousands of fisherfolk, and economic opportunities through fisheries, tourism, and other marine industries. Scientific assessment by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources has given the Verde Island Passage a 95.5% suitability rating for protection and recommends its declaration as a Protected Seascape under the National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS). Despite its global ecological importance, the Verde Island Passage faces increasing threats from illegal and destructive fishing, pollution, unsustainable development, and climate change. Existing local conservation efforts, while commendable, remain fragmented across five provinces and numerous municipalities. A resource of such national significance requires a unified legal and management framework. This bill seeks to establish the Verde Island Passage Protected Seascape (VIPPS) under the Expanded NIPAS Act, creating an integrated governance system that strengthens conservation while ensuring the sustainable use of marine resources. It recognizes that environmental protection and economic development are not competing goals. Healthy ecosystems sustain fisheries, tourism, shipping, and coastal livelihoods, while responsible economic activity depends upon the long-term health of the marine environment. Accordingly, the measure adopts a balanced approach. It protects ecologically critical areas while allowing sustainable and properly regulated economic activities consistent with environmental laws. It likewise safeguards the rights and livelihoods of municipal and subsistence fisherfolk by ensuring their continued access to marine resources under science-based management. The Constitution mandates the State to protect the people's right to a balanced and healthful ecology and to conserve the nation's natural resources for the benefit of all Filipinos. This responsibility extends beyond the present generation. We hold the Verde Island Passage in trust for those who will inherit it after us. The Verde Island Passage is more than a marine ecosystem, it is a vital source of food, livelihood, biodiversity, and national heritage. Protecting it is not only a scientific imperative, an economic necessity, and a constitutional duty, it is simply the right thing to do. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 10502
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PHILIPPINE UBE INDUSTRY, CREATING THE PHILIPPINE UBE INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT OFFICE, ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE UBE INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM AND FUND, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines has long been recognized for producing some of the world's finest ube (Dioscorea alata). Once regarded as a traditional backyard crop, ube has evolved into a premium ingredient sought after by global food manufacturers, bakeries, restaurants, and consumers. From ice cream and pastries to beverages and confectioneries, demand for Philippine ube continues to expand in both domestic and international markets. The country has seen the writing on the wall. The global appetite for ube is no passing trend but a sustained opportunity that can generate jobs, raise farm incomes, stimulate investments, and position the Philippines as the undisputed world leader in premium ube products. Yet despite this growing demand, the industry remains fragmented, constrained by inconsistent planting materials, limited research, inadequate processing facilities, weak value chain coordination, and the absence of a dedicated institution to steer its long-term development. This measure recognizes that the Philippine ube industry deserves to be treated as an anchor industry capable of driving rural development and agricultural industrialization. By creating the Philippine Ube Industry Development Office and institutionalizing a comprehensive industry development program, the bill seeks to provide coherent leadership in research, seed systems, production, post-harvest facilities, processing, marketing, export promotion, and investment generation. More importantly, the measure embodies a long-term vision of nurturing the industry from farm to global market. It seeks to empower farmers with quality planting materials, modern technologies, financing, and market access, while encouraging private investment in value-added manufacturing and export-oriented enterprises. Through coordinated planning and sustained government support, the Philippines can build a resilient, competitive, and innovation-driven ube industry. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 10503
title: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 15 AND 18 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9344, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "JUVENILE JUSTICE AND WELFARE ACT OF 2006," AS AMENDED, TO STRENGTHEN LOCAL GOVERNMENT IMPLEMENTATION OF JUVENILE JUSTICE PROGRAMS, ENHANCE ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Twenty years have passed since the enactment of Republic Act No. 9344, otherwise known as the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006. While the law established a comprehensive juvenile justice system centered on rehabilitation and restorative justice, many local government units continue to face significant challenges in its implementation. A recent Senate hearing revealed that only 28 of the country's 117 operational Bahay Pag-asa facilities are accredited by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), meaning that only 24% are fully compliant with national standards. The Bahay Pag-asa, defined by the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Council as a 24- hour child-caring institution established, funded, and managed by local government units, serves as a cornerstone of the country's juvenile justice system. These figures underscore the persistent implementation gaps at the local level and the urgent need to strengthen accountability, funding, and oversight. The success of the juvenile justice system depends not only on sound national policies but also on the commitment and capacity of local governments to implement them. Without functional Local Councils for the Protection of Children (LCPCs), adequate local funding, effective monitoring, and properly maintained rehabilitation facilities, children in conflict with the law are deprived of meaningful opportunities for intervention, rehabilitation, and reintegration. This measure strengthens the implementation of Republic Act No. 9344 by requiring the establishment and functionality of Local Councils for the Protection of Children, ensuring adequate local funding, enhancing monitoring and reporting mechanisms, providing incentives for compliant local government units, and holding local officials accountable for the faithful implementation of the law. No child should be denied the opportunity to reform, rebuild, and become a productive member of society simply because the programs intended to protect them were not fully implemented. By strengthening accountability and ensuring that every local government fulfills its responsibilities under the law, we reaffirm our commitment to giving every child the care, guidance, and second chance they deserve. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10504
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS (OFW) REMITTANCES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) have long been hailed as the country's modern-day heroes. Through their unwavering dedication and countless sacrifices, they endure prolonged separation from their families and loved ones to provide them with a better future. Beyond supporting their own households, their hard-earned remittances have become a vital pillar of the Philippine economy. According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), cash remittances from OFWs reached a record US$35.63 billion in 2025, reflecting the indispensable contribution of millions of Filipinos working overseas to the country's economic growth, foreign exchange reserves, and financial stability. Every remittance sent by an OFW is the product of hard work, sacrifice, and perseverance. It is therefore imperative that these hard-earned earnings are protected from excessive fees, hidden charges, fraudulent practices, and other forms of financial exploitation that unnecessarily reduce the amount ultimately received by their families. This bill seeks to uphold the constitutional mandate under Article II, Section 18 and Article XIII, Section 3 of the 1987 Constitution by protecting the rights and promoting the welfare of OFWs. It establishes safeguards to ensure fair, transparent, and reasonably priced remittance services, penalizes abusive and fraudulent remittance practices, and promotes financial literacy and responsible financial management among OFWs and their families to help secure their long-term financial well-being. A similar bill was approved by the House of Representatives during the Seventeenth Congress, and a counterpart measure has likewise been recently approved by the Senate. However, the measure has yet to be passed by the House of Representatives in the present Congress. The continued growth of OFW remittances and the enduring sacrifices of our overseas workers underscore the urgency of finally enacting this long-overdue measure into law. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. title: AN ACT INCREASING THE INCOME TAX EXEMPTION THRESHOLD FOR INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS TO FIVE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (₱500,000.00), AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 24(A)(2)(a) AND SECTION 24(A)(2)(b) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The present income tax schedule under Section 24(A)(2)(a) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, imposes a zero percent (0%) income tax rate only on the irst Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (₱250,000.00) of taxable income. The irst ₱250,000.00 of taxable income is treated as exempt from income tax under the tax reforms introduced by Republic Act No. 10963, otherwise known as the “Tax Reform for Acceleration and Inclusion (TRAIN) Act.” The cost of basic goods and services, housing, transportation, education, health care, and other necessities has substantially increased since the current threshold was established. Increasing the exemption threshold to Five Hundred Thousand Pesos (₱500,000.00) will provide individual taxpayers with greater disposable income and help ensure that income needed for basic living expenses is not subject to income tax. The Supreme Court has recognized that income tax exemptions and adjustments may be intended to limit the amount of income subject to tax, thereby enabling individuals to meet basic necessities and retain more disposable income. This measure therefore proposes that the irst ₱500,000.00 of the taxable income of individual taxpayers be subject to a zero percent (0%) income tax rate. It likewise 1|Page adjusts the succeeding tax brackets to maintain a clear and administrable graduated income tax schedule. label: HB 10506
title: AN ACT PROHIBITING PRIVATE ELECTRIC UTILITIES FROM RECOVERING SYSTEM LOSSES FROM CONSUMERS, LIMITING THE RECOVERABLE SYSTEM LOSSES OF RURAL ELECTRIC COOPERATIVES TO FIVE PERCENT (5%), PROVIDING FOR THE VERIFICATION AND USE OF SYSTEM-LOSS CHARGES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7832, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Electricity is not a luxury but a basic necessity that powers our homes, schools, hospitals, farms, and businesses. Every Filipino family depends on electricity for their daily lives, yet many continue to struggle with high and rising power bills. Consumers should only pay for the electricity they actually use and for costs that are fair, reasonable, and necessary. They should not be made to shoulder expenses caused by theft, poor maintenance, inef icient operations, or management failures that are beyond their control. Under existing laws, distribution utilities are allowed to recover certain system losses through electricity rates, subject to rules set by the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC). While some technical losses are unavoidable in delivering electricity, many losses result from illegal connections, electricity theft, defective equipment, billing errors, and operational inef iciencies. These are problems that should be addressed by the utility itself, not passed on to hardworking consumers who faithfully pay their bills every month. This bill seeks to put consumers irst by prohibiting private electric utilities from charging consumers for any system loss. For rural electric cooperatives, which often 1|Page serve remote and dif icult-to-reach communities, the bill allows only veri ied and unavoidable technical losses to be recovered, subject to a strict maximum cap of ive percent (5%) and prior approval by the ERC. The measure also requires full transparency by ensuring that any approved system-loss charge is clearly shown in electricity bills and used only for projects that improve the distribution system and reduce future losses. Non-technical and administrative losses, including electricity theft, meter tampering, billing mistakes, collection inef iciencies, and poor management, can never be charged to consumers. This measure promotes fairness, accountability, and transparency in the power sector. It encourages distribution utilities to improve their systems instead of passing the cost of their inef iciencies to the public. More importantly, it protects Filipino families from paying for electricity they never consumed and expenses they never caused. At a time when every peso counts, this bill will help make electricity rates more just, affordable, and responsive to the needs of the Filipino people. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10507
title: AN ACT FURTHER EXTENDING THE PERIOD OF AVAILMENT OF THE ESTATE TAX AMNESTY UNTIL JUNE 30, 2028, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 4, 6, AND 8 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11213, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 11213, otherwise known as the “Tax Amnesty Act,” established an Estate Tax Amnesty to enable quali ied estates to settle estate tax obligations under simpli ied procedures and subject to the immunities and privileges provided by law. The period for availing of the Estate Tax Amnesty was subsequently extended by Republic Act No. 11569 and Republic Act No. 11956. The most recent statutory extension allowed availment until June 14, 2025, covering the estates of decedents who died on or before May 31, 2022. The continued existence of unsettled estates demonstrates the need for a further extension. Heirs, executors, administrators, transferees, and bene iciaries continue to encounter dif iculties in obtaining civil registry records, titles, tax declarations, certi ications, and other documents required for estate settlement and transfer. A further extension will encourage voluntary compliance, facilitate the transfer and registration of inherited properties, reduce administrative backlogs, and generate government revenue from estates that may otherwise remain unsettled. It will likewise provide taxpayers additional time to comply with the documentary and procedural requirements of the Estate Tax Amnesty. 1|Page This measure proposes to extend the period of availment of the Estate Tax Amnesty until June 30, 2028, while retaining the existing statutory coverage, quali ications, documentary requirements, tax rate, and immunities and privileges under Republic Act No. 11213, as amended. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10508
title: AN ACT EXEMPTING MICRO AND SMALL BUSINESSES FROM THE MINIMUM CORPORATE INCOME TAX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 27 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Micro and small businesses are the backbone of the Philippine economy. They create jobs, provide livelihoods, support local communities, and encourage entrepreneurship. However, many of these businesses operate with limited capital and small pro it margins, making them more vulnerable to economic downturns, rising costs, and unexpected business losses. During dif icult times, every peso matters, and unnecessary tax burdens can make it even harder for them to survive and grow. Under existing tax laws, corporations may be required to pay the Minimum Corporate Income Tax (MCIT) beginning on their fourth year of operations if it is higher than their regular income tax. Unlike the regular corporate income tax, which is based on taxable income or actual pro it, the MCIT is based on gross income. As a result, even businesses that earn very little or are struggling inancially may still be required to pay the MCIT, placing additional pressure on their cash low and limiting their ability to recover and continue operating. This bill seeks to exempt quali ied micro and small businesses from paying the MCIT. The exemption is limited only to businesses that fall within the classi ications set by law and recognized by the Bureau of Internal Revenue. It does not remove their obligation to register with the BIR, ile tax returns, keep proper books of accounts, or 1|Page pay the regular corporate income tax and all other applicable national and local taxes. Instead, it simply ensures that small businesses are not required to pay a minimum tax despite having little or no taxable income. By allowing micro and small businesses to retain more of their working capital, this measure will help them sustain operations, protect jobs, and invest in future growth. It promotes a fairer tax system by recognizing the inancial realities faced by smaller enterprises while maintaining their responsibility to comply with tax laws. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10509
title: AN ACT POSTPONING THE NOVEMBER 2, 2026 BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECTIONS, SETTING THE SAME ON THE LAST MONDAY OF NOVEMBER 2028, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9164, AS AMENDED, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Barangays constitute the basic political units of the country and serve as the primary planning and implementing units of government policies, programs, projects, and activities in communities. The Sangguniang Kabataan, meanwhile, provides an institutional mechanism for meaningful youth participation in local governance. As the country continues to undertake reforms aimed at strengthening local governance and improving the administration of elections, there is a need to ensure that the conduct of the next Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections is properly aligned with these reforms. The additional period will provide the government, particularly the Commission on Elections and concerned national and local government agencies, sufficient time to institute and operationalize measures intended to improve election administration, strengthen electoral processes, update and rationalize election-related systems, and ensure the orderly and effective implementation of reforms affecting barangay and youth governance. The postponement will likewise provide an opportunity to harmonize the electoral calendar with ongoing institutional reforms while ensuring adequate preparation for the conduct of credible, orderly, and efficient Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections. This measure therefore seeks to postpone the next regular Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections scheduled in November 2026 and set the same on the last Monday of November 2028. Incumbent barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials shall remain in office in a temporary holdover capacity until their successors have been duly elected and qualified. Such holdover shall operate solely by virtue of law and shall not be construed as creating a new mandate or extending their term of office. The postponement contemplated under this measure is limited to the November 2026 elections and is not intended to establish a precedent for future postponements. Rather, it seeks to provide sufficient time for the necessary preparations and reforms while safeguarding the people's constitutional right of suffrage and ensuring that the next Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections are conducted in a free, orderly, honest, peaceful, credible, and accessible manner. In view of the foregoing, ug sa ngalan sa SERBISYONG TINUORAY, the undersigned respectfully requests the immediate passage of this measure. CHRISTOPHERSON “COCO” M. label: HB 10510
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE INCOME TAX EXEMPTION CEILING FOR INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS TO THREE HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND PESOS (PHP 350,000) ANNUALLY, THEREBY AMENDING SECTION 24(A)(2)(a) AND (b) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution declares that the State shall promote a just and dynamic social order that improves the quality of life, raises the standard of living, and frees the people from poverty through sound economic and social policies. It likewise mandates that the rule of taxation shall be uniform and equitable, and that Congress shall evolve a progressive system of taxation. These constitutional principles recognize that the tax system must not only generate revenues for the government but must also be fair, responsive, and sensitive to the economic realities faced by Filipino taxpayers. In 2017, Congress enacted Republic Act No. 10963, otherwise known as the Tax Reform for Acceleration and Inclusion (TRAIN) Law, which increased the income tax exemption threshold from ₱10,000 to ₱250,000 annually. The reform was intended to provide meaningful tax relief to Filipino workers by allowing them to keep more of their earnings. At the time, the increase reflected prevailing wage levels and the cost of living, and significantly improved the disposable income of millions of taxpayers. Nearly a decade has passed since the enactment of the TRAIN Law. During this period, the country has experienced unprecedented economic challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic and sustained increases in the prices of basic necessities. Although nominal wages have gradually increased, the purchasing power of Filipino families has been steadily eroded by rising living costs. Consequently, many workers whose annual incomes now exceed ₱250,000 are not necessarily better off than those who benefited from the original exemption under the TRAIN Law. The existing income tax exemption ceiling no longer reflects present-day economic conditions. Taxpayers with modest incomes are increasingly brought into the taxable bracket despite continuing financial pressures brought about by inflation and the higher cost of everyday living. Updating the exemption threshold is therefore necessary to preserve the intent of the TRAIN Law. This measure proposes to increase the income tax exemption ceiling from ₱250,000 to ₱350,000 annually and to correspondingly adjust the graduated income tax brackets. It likewise increases the exemption threshold for self-employed individuals and professionals who avail of the eight percent (8%) income tax option. These adjustments provide much-needed tax relief while ensuring that the tax system remains progressive, equitable, and responsive to current economic realities. At a time when many Filipinos continue to grapple with the rising cost of living, providing reasonable tax relief is both a matter of fairness and sound economic policy. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JOEL R. label: HB 10511
title: AN ACT POSTPONING THE NOVEMBER 2, 2026 BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECTIONS TO NOVEMBER 1, 2027, EXTENDING THE TERMS OF INCUMBENT BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN OFFICIALS IN A HOLDOVER CAPACITY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (BSK) are the fundamental institutions of local governance, serving as the government's primary link to communities and the youth. Through the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE), citizens are afforded the opportunity to choose leaders who will promote grassroots development, maintain peace and order, and advance meaningful youth participation in governance. However, the conduct of nationwide synchronized elections demands substantial financial, administrative, and logistical resources. As government continues to address competing national priorities, including the implementation of critical infrastructure projects, education and health programs, disaster preparedness initiatives, and fiscal consolidation measures, it has become imperative to reassess the timing of the 2026 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections. Postponing the BSKE to 2027 will enable the government to redirect public funds toward more urgent and immediate national concerns while allowing the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) sufficient time to complete procurement activities, enhance election preparations, improve voter education campaigns, and ensure the orderly, efficient, and credible conduct of the elections. The proposed measure likewise seeks to prevent disruptions in the delivery of essential public services at the barangay level by allowing incumbent barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials to continue serving in a holdover capacity until their duly elected successors shall have qualified. Such holdover authority is intended solely to preserve continuity in governance and maintain uninterrupted delivery of basic public services during the postponement period. This measure does not diminish the people's right to suffrage nor alter the democratic process. Rather, it merely adjusts the schedule of the elections in furtherance of the State's compelling interest in ensuring fiscal prudence, administrative efficiency, and the orderly conduct of elections, while preserving stability in local governance. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PASSING ON OF NET SYSTEM LOSS CHARGES TO RESIDENTIAL ELECTRICITY CONSUMERS, REQUIRING DISTRIBUTION UTILITIES TO ABSORB SUCH LOSSES AS PART OF THEIR COST OF DOING BUSINESS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Electricity is an essential public service indispensable to every Filipino household. However, millions of residential consumers continue to bear the burden of Net System Loss Charges, a component of electricity bills that represents the cost of electricity lost during transmission and distribution due to technical inefficiencies and non-technical losses such as pilferage, theft, meter tampering, and other unauthorized use. While some technical losses are unavoidable, requiring ordinary consumers to shoulder the financial consequences of inefficiencies and illegal activities beyond their control undermines the principles of fairness and consumer protection. Distribution utilities possess the authority, technical capability, and regulatory responsibility to reduce system losses through infrastructure modernization, anti-electricity theft programs, improved monitoring systems, and efficient network management. This measure recognizes that consumers should only pay for the electricity they actually consume and should not be made financially responsible for losses arising from the operation or management of the power distribution system. Accordingly, this bill prohibits the imposition of Net System Loss Charges on residential electricity consumers while encouraging distribution utilities to improve operational efficiency and reduce wastage. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. GERVILLE “JINKY BITRICS” R. label: HB 10513
title: AN ACT TO PROMOTE FURTHER PROTECTION TO LABOR, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 284 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ. - Galatians 6:2 In many Filipino homes, one worker’s salary helps carry the weight of an entire family. It pays for the food on the table, rent, electricity, children’s school needs, medicines for aging parents, and the small daily expenses that keep a household going. For many workers, especially those who serve as the primary support of their families, every day of work is not merely a means of earning, but an act of love and responsibility for the people who depend on them. When a worker dies, the loss is therefore more than the passing of a loved one. It may also mean the sudden loss of the family’s main source of support. In the middle of grief, those left behind must confront funeral expenses, unpaid bills, continuing household needs, and the uncertainty of how to move forward without the income that once sustained them. As part of a humane system of labor protection, the law should recognize the worker’s years of service through a clear minimum benefit for the family left behind. While no amount can answer for the loss of a loved one, such benefit gives practical recognition to the dignity of work and the sacrifices made in the course of employment. For this reason, this bill amends Article 284 of the Labor Code to provide separation pay in case of death of an employee. Under the measure, when an employee who has rendered at least one (1) year of service dies, the employer shall be liable for separation pay equivalent to one-half (1/2) month salary for every year of service. The bill also provides reasonable exemptions, taking into account existing employer- provided death benefits, the capacity of small establishments, and circumstances directly attributable to the employee’s own acts or gross negligence. The separation pay may be claimed by the family of the deceased in the following order: the surviving spouse; the legitimate, legitimated, legally adopted, or illegitimate children; the parents of the deceased employee; and the brothers and sisters of the deceased employee. This proposal rests on the truth that a worker’s service is never rendered in isolation. It is tied to the family sustained by the worker’s daily labor. While no benefit can answer for the loss of a loved one, this measure provides practical help to the family left behind and eases the immediate burdens that follow. For every Filipino worker, and for the loved ones who depend on them, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. JORGE DANIEL S. label: HB 10514
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR TAX INCENTIVES ON DEVELOPMENT OF ECONOMIC AND MEDIUM-COST HOUSING
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The housing sector is a cornerstone of national development, yet millions of Filipino families continue to struggle with inadequate or unaffordable housing. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), the country’s housing need for 2023–2028 is estimated at 3.7 million units, reflecting both existing shortages and projected household formation. Despite government efforts under the Pambansang Pabahay para sa Pilipino (4PH) Program, only about 575,693 units were produced or financed between July 2022 and June 2026, representing just over half of the administration’s recalibrated target of 1.13 million units. The affordability crisis is most acute in Metro Manila, where the median condominium price is 19.8 times the median annual household income of $8,957 (approx. ₱500,000). Townhouses are even further out of reach at 33.4 times annual income, while median monthly rent exceeds the typical household’s monthly earnings by 41 percent. Independent studies estimate that the private sector produces only 128,000 housing units annually, against demand of 478,000 units, leaving a shortfall of about 350,000 units per year. This bill seeks to provide tax incentives to developers of economic and medium-cost housing projects, thereby reducing fiscal barriers and encouraging greater private sector participation. By lowering development costs, these incentives will enable developers to offer more affordable housing units, directly benefiting low- and middle-income families who are often excluded from high-end developments and underserved by socialized housing programs. The measure aligns with the government’s agenda of inclusive growth and poverty reduction, while also addressing the structural imbalance between housing demand and supply. Beyond meeting shelter needs, expanded housing development will generate employment, stimulate allied industries such as construction and materials supply, and contribute to sustainable urbanization. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought to ensure that economic and medium-cost housing becomes a viable and attainable option for millions of Filipino families, thereby strengthening the nation’s social and economic foundations. HON. MA. NINA FRANCESCA P. label: HB 10515
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE INTEGRATION OF BASIC FIRST AID AND SURVIVAL SKILLS TRAINING IN THE CURRICULA OF ALL INSTITUTIONS OF LEARNING AND PROVIDING THE APPROPRIATE FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Across the Philippines, accidents, natural disasters, and emergencies are recurring realities. Data from the Philippine Red Cross and the Department of Health show that thousands of Filipinos suffer injuries annually from road accidents, workplace hazards, and calamities such as typhoons and earthquakes. Yet, many victims could have been stabilized or saved if bystanders had basic knowledge of first aid and survival techniques. For example, the World Health Organization estimates that timely first aid can reduce preventable deaths by up to 15% in trauma cases. In disaster-prone countries like the Philippines, where an average of 20 typhoons strike yearly, survival skills such as evacuation readiness, CPR, bleeding control, and safe sheltering are not optional but essential. Integrating these competencies into the educational system ensures that every student, from elementary to tertiary level, acquires life-saving knowledge early on. This measure also aligns with the Department of Education’s thrust to promote holistic learning and disaster risk reduction education. By institutionalizing first aid and survival training, schools become not only centers of academic learning but also hubs of resilience and preparedness. The provision of funds guarantees that institutions can procure training materials, partner with accredited organizations like the Red Cross, and capacitate teachers to deliver standardized modules. Ultimately, this Act seeks to cultivate a generation of citizens who are not only academically competent but also equipped to respond effectively in emergencies, thereby reducing fatalities, strengthening community resilience, and supporting national disaster preparedness goals. HON. MA. NINA FRANCESCA P. label: HB 10516
title: AN ACT DEFINING ATM PAWNING SCHEME AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The practice known as ATM pawning or “sangla-ATM” has become a widespread informal lending scheme in the Philippines, wherein borrowers surrender their Automated Teller Machine (ATM) cards together with their Personal Identification Numbers (PINs) to lenders as collateral for loans. In this arrangement, lenders directly withdraw the wages, pensions, or remittances of borrowers once funds are credited, often charging exorbitant interest rates ranging from five to twenty percent monthly. While this scheme provides immediate cash to borrowers, it exposes them to serious risks such as loss of control over their income, vulnerability to fraud, and long-term indebtedness. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), through advisories such as Circular No. 902, has repeatedly warned against ATM pawning, citing its predatory nature and the grave security risks it poses to the banking system. Existing laws, including the Access Devices Regulation Act (Republic Act No. 8484), the Truth in Lending Act (Republic Act No. 3765), and the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act (Republic Act No. 11765), already provide mechanisms to penalize fraudulent use of access devices and abusive lending practices. However, there remains no explicit statutory prohibition that directly addresses ATM pawning as a distinct scheme. This bill seeks to fill that gap by formally defining ATM pawning, declaring it unlawful, and prescribing clear penalties for lenders and entities that engage in or facilitate the practice. By doing so, this measure aims to protect vulnerable borrowers, uphold labor rights by ensuring workers retain control over their wages, and strengthen financial integrity by discouraging practices that compromise banking security. The enactment of this law will harmonize fragmented regulations, provide clarity to enforcement agencies, and safeguard the public from exploitative lending schemes. It is high time that we put a stop to this form of unfair business practice by imposing penalties against those who engage in the same and protect the public from these unscrupulous practices. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this house bill is earnestly sought. HON. MA. NINA FRANCESCA P. label: HB 10517
title: AN ACT RAISING THE TAX-EXEMPT INCOME THRESHOLD FOR INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS AND INSTITUTING A MECHANISM FOR PERIODIC INFLATION INDEXATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 24 AND 32 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: SECTION 1. Short Title. — This Act shall be known as the "Income Tax Exemption Adjustment and Indexation Act.." SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. — Pursuant to Section 28(1), Article VI of the Constitution, which mandates that the rule of taxation shall be uniform and equitable and that Congress shall evolve a progressive system of taxation, it is hereby declared the policy of the State to protect the purchasing power of Filipino workers and their families, as guaranteed under Section 3, Article XIII and Section 1, Article XII of the Constitution. Toward this end, the State shall increase the tax-exempt income threshold of individual taxpayers, periodically and automatically adjust income tax thresholds and ceilings to reflect changes in the consumer price index without eroding real income through bracket creep, and strengthen tax administration, compliance, and enforcement so that tax relief is balanced with fiscal stability and revenue integrity. SEC. 3. Amendment of Section 24(A)(2)(a). — Section 24(A)(2)(a) of Republic Act No. 8424, otherwise known as the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, is hereby further amended to read as follows: “SEC. 24. Income Tax Rates. — “(A) Rates of Income Tax on Individual Citizen and Individual Resident Alien of the Philippines. —
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 10963, the Tax Reform for Acceleration and Inclusion (TRAIN) Act, exempted the first Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (PhP 250,000.00) of annual taxable income of individual taxpayers beginning 1 January 2018.1 That threshold has not been adjusted since and inflation has not stopped. Based on the Consumer Price Index of the Philippine Statistics Authority (2018=100), which stood at 135.4 in June 2026,2 the goods and services that cost PhP 250,000.00 in 2018 now cost approximately PhP 338,500.00. Stated inversely, the present exemption retains only about PhP 184,600.00 of its original purchasing power, an erosion of roughly twenty-six percent (26%). Inflation quietly increases their tax burden through automatic withholding while their actual purchasing power stays the same. In line with national policy priorities to grant individual tax relief, this bill raises the annual tax-exempt income threshold to Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (PhP 350,000.00). Estimates from the Department of Finance project that the measure will benefit at least 3.13 million workers, lifting approximately 1.2 million earners out of the income tax net entirely and increasing the total tax-exempt workforce to roughly 6.3 million.3 This bill fully adopts the Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Peso (PhP 350,000.00) tax-exempt threshold. By recomputing every bracket base from this new starting point, the schedule delivers a uniform Fifteen Thousand Peso (PhP 15,000.00) tax reduction to all taxpayers above the exempt limit. This design intentionally prevents a notch discontinuity at the threshold, ensuring marginal income is not penalized and tax relief is extended across all income bands. 1 Republic Act No. 10963 (2017), amending Chapter III, Section 24(A)(2)(a) of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, effective 1 January 2018. 2 Philippine Statistics Authority, Summary Inflation Report, Consumer Price Index (2018=100): June 2026. 3 Department of Finance, statement of Secretary Frederick D. Go, 29 July 2026, reported in “Tax relief plan to benefit 3M workers, but cost P66B in foregone revenues — DoF,” BusinessWorld, 30 July 2026. To prevent inflation from eroding these gains over time, Section 5 introduces a mandatory indexation mechanism beginning in the taxable year 2030. Every three (3) years, the Secretary of Finance shall adjust all income thresholds, fixed bracket tax amounts, and the tax-exempt benefit ceiling upward using official Philippine Statistics Authority inflation data, with downward adjustments expressly prohibited. Anchoring each cycle to the three (3) calendar years immediately preceding publication ensures the adjustments rely on final, auditable data without leaving gaps in inflation coverage. This mechanism satisfies the completeness and sufficient-standard tests governing the valid delegation of legislative authority under Abakada Guro Party List v. Ermita 4 because it leaves the Executive with the purely ministerial function of factual ascertainment and arithmetical computation. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is respectfully and urgently sought. ATTY. TIMOTHY JOSEPH E. CAYTON, PhD. Representative Lone District of Nueva Vizcaya 4Abakada Guro Party List v. Ermita, G.R. No. 168056, September 1, 2005 [Per J. Austria-Martinez, En Banc].
