label: HB 11339
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A MAGINHAWANG BUHAY SUPPORT FRAMEWORK FOR LOW- INCOME AND MIDDLE-CLASS HOUSEHOLDS, PROVIDING A TWENTY PERCENT (20%) DISCOUNT ON ESSENTIAL NEEDS INCLUDING BASIC UTILITIES, HEALTHCARE, EDUCATION, AND HOUSING, ESTABLISHING AN INFLATION-RESPONSIVE AND INTEGRATED DELIVERY MECHANISM, PROVIDING FOR BENEFIT CEILINGS, TARGETING, FISCAL SAFEGUARDS, INTER-AGENCY COORDINATION, TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND CONGRESSIONAL OVERSIGHT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In every economy, there is a quiet line that separates stability from vulnerability. It is the line where income, though earned honestly and steadily, is no longer enough to keep pace with the cost of living. For millions of Filipino families, particularly those in the low-income and middle-class sectors, that line has been crossed not because of idleness or failure, but because prices have risen faster than wages, and essential needs have become increasingly unaffordable. Electricity, water, healthcare, education, and housing are not discretionary expenses. They are the fixed costs of dignity. When these become too expensive, households are forced into painful trade-offs—between food and medicine, tuition and rent, work and care. Over time, these trade-offs accumulate into deeper inequality, poorer health outcomes, educational attrition, and economic fragility. This proposed measure seeks to correct that imbalance by institutionalizing a Maginhawang Buhay Support Framework, grounded on the principle that every Filipino household is entitled to a basic social floor of economic security, regardless of income level, so long as they remain within the broad low-income and middle- class spectrum. In this sense, the measure draws from a universal income perspective—not by distributing cash, but by protecting real income at the point where it matters most: the price of essentials. Persistent inflation in recent years has eroded household purchasing power, disproportionately affecting families whose incomes are fixed or slow-moving. While emergency subsidies and conditional assistance programs have provided temporary relief, these measures are often reactive, fragmented, and dependent on discretionary political action. Moreover, existing social protection mechanisms are largely targeted at the poorest households, leaving a growing segment of the middle class exposed—too “rich” to qualify for aid, yet too financially constrained to absorb rising costs. This condition has created a silent crisis. Middle-income households increasingly rely on debt, reduce preventive healthcare, delay education, or accept substandard housing conditions. The long-term cost of these decisions is borne not only by families, but by the State itself, through higher healthcare expenditures, lower educational attainment, reduced productivity, and social instability. 2 There is therefore a clear need for a permanent, automatic, and inflation- responsive mechanism that stabilizes household welfare before economic stress turns into economic damage. This bill establishes a Maginhawang Buhay Support Framework that grants qualified low-income and middle-class households a twenty percent (20%) discount on essential needs, specifically basic utilities, healthcare, education, and housing expenses. The discount is designed as a baseline social protection measure that operates continuously, rather than episodically. The measure is carefully integrated with existing lifeline rates, PhilHealth benefits, free tuition and scholarship programs, and housing subsidies, ensuring that it supplements rather than replaces current entitlements. It introduces a national beneficiary registry, anchored on official statistics and interoperable government databases, to ensure accurate targeting, transparency, and protection against leakage. Recognizing the cyclical nature of inflation, the bill further provides for an automatic, time-bound expansion of benefits when inflation breaches defined thresholds, thereby avoiding the delays and uncertainty of ad hoc emergency legislation. To ensure fiscal sustainability, the measure adopts a cost-sharing mechanism with the private sector, requiring covered service providers to grant discounts upfront, while allowing reimbursement solely through tax credits and incentives, subject to fiscal ceilings, audit, and verification. No direct cash reimbursement is allowed, and no new or special appropriation is mandated. 3 Oversight is institutionalized through an inter-agency council attached to the Office of the President, supported by a permanent secretariat, and complemented by congressional oversight and sunset review provisions. The immediate impact of this measure is the protection of real household income. By reducing the price of essentials, the bill functions as a form of universal income stabilization, ensuring that earned income retains its purchasing power even during inflationary periods. Unlike cash transfers, which may be inflationary, this approach directly lowers effective prices and moderates second- round inflation effects. Economically, the measure is expected to stabilize consumption, particularly among low- and middle-income households with high marginal propensity to spend. This sustains local demand, supports small and medium enterprises, and mitigates economic contraction during periods of price volatility. Socially, the bill reduces the risk of preventable health crises, educational dropouts, housing insecurity, and debt accumulation. Over time, these effects translate into lower public health costs, higher educational completion rates, a more resilient workforce, and a broader tax base. From a governance perspective, the measure shifts social protection from discretion to design—from reactive relief to automatic response—thereby strengthening public trust and policy credibility. At its core, this measure affirms a simple but powerful idea: income is only meaningful if it can meet the cost of living. By institutionalizing a Maginhawang Buhay Support Framework, the State acknowledges that protecting dignity in times of economic stress is not charity, but responsibility. 4 This bill does not promise abundance. It promises stability. And in an economy shaped by uncertainty, stability is the foundation upon which opportunity, growth, and shared prosperity are built. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly requested. FERDINAND MARTIN G. ROMUALDEZ YEDDA MARIE

label: HB 11340
title: AN ACT PRESERVING AND PROMOTING THE INDIGENOUS GAMES OF THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Culture shapes values. In this digital era, Filipino children spend most of their time with game consoles or mobile gadgets either at home or in internet cafés, in contrast with the children of the past who spent their leisure time interacting with other children and playing traditional street games. These games include patintero, tumbang preso, siato, and taguan, to name a few. These indigenous games have shaped generations of Filipinos and have imparted values of teamwork, resilience, and sportsmanship. They have been part of our childhood and our cultural heritage. This proposed measure seeks to preserve indigenous games to ensure that future generations of Filipinos can still enjoy them. This bill has been approved on third and final reading in the House of Representatives for three consecutive Congresses (17th, 18th, and 19th) but failed to be passed into law due to time constraints. We seek to revive efforts to make this worthwhile advocacy a law. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11341
title: AN ACT REQUIRING LAND, AIR, AND SEA TRANSPORT PROVIDERS TO PROVIDE PRIORITY SEATING FOR THE ELDERLY, FURTHER AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7432, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9257 AND 9994, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “EXPANDED SENIOR CITIZEN’S ACT OF 2010”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE It is the duty of the State to ensure that public utilities and transportation services are accessible to all people, especially those in vulnerable groups such as senior citizens and persons with disabilities. In furtherance of this mandate, Batas Pambansa Bilang 344, or the Accessibility Law, and Republic Act No. 9994, or the Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010, were enacted to improve access to public transportation for persons with disabilities and senior citizens. Under these laws, public transport providers are required to designate seats for persons with disabilities, and the Department of Transportation is directed “to develop a program to assist senior citizens to fully gain access to public transport facilities.” Administrative issuances, including Department of Transportation Department Order No. 2014-013, likewise provide for reserved or priority seating for persons with disabilities, senior citizens, and pregnant women in certain public transportation facilities. However, existing law and regulations do not establish a comprehensive statutory requirement expressly prescribing priority seating for senior citizens across all modes of public transportation— land, rail, air, and sea—along with uniform standards on seat designation, labeling, reservation, enforcement, and penalties. As a result, senior citizens continue to experience difficulties in accessing priority seats. They often find themselves standing in cramped, moving vehicles while non-eligible passengers occupy seats that should be available to them. The lack of clear statutory rules and consistent enforcement undermines the intent of existing accessibility and senior-citizen laws. In recognition of the invaluable contributions of senior citizens to nation-building, it is only right and just to provide them with additional privileges, particularly in public transportation. By ensuring priority seating for the elderly, this measure promotes their mobility and access, enabling them to continue participating actively in the life of their communities. This bill seeks to strengthen the Expanded Senior Citizens Act by expressly requiring priority seating for senior citizens in land, air, and sea transport, including rail services. It further provides for appropriate penalties for public transport operators who fail to comply with this requirement. It is the hope of this measure to mainstream mobility and access for senior citizens in public transportation, so that we may continue to support them in their daily lives and in their ongoing efforts to contribute to nation-building. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11342
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE DISPLAY OF NUTRITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE MENU OF FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Good nutrition has been attributed to healthier food choices and, generally, a healthier diet. The presence of nutritional information on the food labels helps people maintain their healthy diet and nutrition because of informed choices. This, in turn, helps prevent the rise of various diseases attributed to an unhealthy diet. The World Health Organization indicates that 80 percent of premature heart disease, stroke, and Type II Diabetes and 40 percent of cancers can be prevented through a healthy diet. Thus, consumers have now become more discerning in their choice of food, always checking the nutritional information and calorie count on food labels. Filipinos, however, are not as informed when dining in restaurants. They are often unaware of the calorie and nutritional content of a meal, leading them or misleading them into an unhealthy eating pattern. This bill aims to mandate the disclosure and display of the nutrition content information on each standard menu in all types of restaurants, including fast food chains, in order to enable and empower consumers with the right to choose the food they want to eat without compromising their health. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11343
title: AN ACT ALLOWING AND REGULATING THE USE OF MOTORCYCLES AS PUBLIC UTILITY VEHICLES, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LAND TRANSPORTATION AND TRAFFIC CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State provides that it shall protect and promote the rights and obligations of commuters, drivers, and operators through an efficient and fair transport system for the commuting public. As such, Republic Act 4136, otherwise known as the “Land Transportation and Traffic Code,” was enacted, providing for the control, registration, and operation of motor vehicles and the licensing of owners, dealers, conductors, drivers, and similar matters. While the law covers relevant provisions for privately owned and for-hire motor vehicles, the law lacks coverage for motorcycles-for-hire which have become a growing mode of public transportation in recent years. In 2022, there were at least 682,000 registered motorcycles and tricycles for hire in the country. For many commuters, these motorcycle taxis are sometimes the better option of transportation because of their accessibility, efficiency, and reliability. The growing demand for motorcycles as public utility vehicles also led to the operation of non-registered motorcycles-for-hire, which in turn have posed risks for many commuters since riders do not necessarily have the proper training or insurance coverage to protect themselves and even their passengers. The proposed amendments to RA 4136 shall ensure that the law includes motorcycles-for-hire among the defined public transportation, and as such guarantee their roadworthiness while assuring the safety of the riding public. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of the bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11344
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A BILL OF RIGHTS FOR AIR PASSENGERS, PENALIZING VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State has established that it shall protect the interest of all consumers, promote their general welfare, and establish standards of conduct for business and industry. With the vital role of the air transport industry in fostering inclusive economic growth, it is imperative to guarantee that the air transport sector operates effectively. The industry is experiencing phenomenal growth and has not only regained but, in some indicators, surpassed its pre-pandemic levels, as shown by the sustained rise in business and leisure travel since mobility limitations were relaxed. According to the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP), total passenger movements reached about 27.3 million in 2023, 25.2 million in 2024, and 24.5 million in 2025, reflecting robust recovery in domestic and international air travel.1 As the industry offers services to travelers from all socioeconomic backgrounds, issues looming in air travel have continuously affected many air passengers, including but not limited to flight delays, airline overbooking, baggage loss, the disappearance of bookings, and trouble with refunds, among many others. These concerns persist despite the existence of the DOTC-DTI Joint Administrative Order No. 1, series of 2012 (the Air Passenger Bill of Rights), which was further updated by the Civil Aeronautics Board through Economic Regulation No. 9 in January 2024 to strengthen carrier obligations and passenger entitlements for delays, cancellations, denied boarding, and baggage issues.2 1 Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP), “Aircraft, Passenger, and Cargo Movements” annual reports: 27,305,261 passenger movements in 2023; 25,194,580 in 2024; 24,450,723 in 2025, https://www.caap.gov.ph/aircraft-passenger-and-cargo-movements/; 2 DOTC-DTI Joint Administrative Order No. 1, series of 2012 (Air Passenger Bill of Rights), issued December 10, 2012; Civil Aeronautics Board, Economic Regulation No. 9 (updated Air Passenger Bill of Rights), effective January This proposed measure aims to focus on the right of air passengers to receive the full value of the service they have purchased and the convenience it offers. Consequently, it protects air passengers, especially during events when their flights are canceled or delayed, and their baggage is lost or damaged, to name a few. It establishes a mechanism to address the grievances of affected air passengers and maintains their right to full and truthful information regarding the contract of carriage. This bill institutionalizes and updates the Joint DOTC-DTI Administrative Order No. 1 issued on 10 December 2012, incorporating developments such as the CAB’s 2024 amendments, with the intent of ensuring the rights of air passengers in the country and promoting efficient air transport service. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11345
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE BILL OF RIGHTS OF COMMUTERS, PROMOTING EFFICIENT, SAFE, CONVENIENT, ACCESSIBLE AND INCLUSIVE PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Greater Manila Area is home to millions of commuters daily who need to move from their homes to their workplaces or schools by taking buses, jeepneys, taxis, trains, tricycles, and pedicabs. With the existing road-based public transport system, a regular commuter in Metro Manila will have spent about 15 to 59 minutes 1 on a regular day or worse, 3 hours for a 13-kilometer distance2 , and will have transferred from at least two modes of Public Utility vehicles before he or she gets to work. For those taking trains or buses, an additional of at least 30 to 40 minutes on average will be allotted for waiting time alone. A study on commuting in Metro Manila finds that Filipinos spend about 16 days a year stuck in traffic, costing them about 100,000 Philippine pesos ($2,000) a year in lost income 3 or an estimated economic loss of 4.6% of the GDP4. With the evident economic losses and the commuter’s daily ordeal, it is the State’s obligation to remedy the public’s outcry for better, efficient, and dignified transport system. 1 “Duration of daily Commute in the Philippines as of June 2022” https://www.statista.com/forecasts/1274764/philippines- duration-of-daily-commute Accessed on September 20, 2022 2 Metro Manila Development Authority 2019 3 Ana P. Santos, 2019. “Carmageddon: The indignity of commuting in Metro Manila” https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2019/10/24/carmageddon-the-indignity-of-commuting-in-metro-manila Accessed on September 21, 2022 4 Asian Development Bank, 2012 “ Transport Sector Assessment, Strategy and Roadmap” https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/institutional-document/33700/files/philippines-transport-assessment.pdf Accessed on September 21, 2022 This bill seeks to promulgate and implement policies and programs that will ensure the welfare and dignity of the commuting public, address challenges of mobility amidst rapid urbanization, promote road safety, reduce road congestion and air pollution, mitigate transport-related health hazards, and improve access to services and markets, thereby fostering social equity, economic development, and ecological balance. When the system for mass transportation is efficient and effective, fewer people will take private cars, leading to less cost, less pollution, and a more dignified overall commute experience. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this measure is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA OF TRICYCLE DRIVERS AND OPERATORS, INSTITUTIONALIZING MECHANISMS FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Tricycles are considered the “vehicle of the masses”. It is often the transportation option of many low-income households to reach major thoroughfares, and a significant income source of many Filipinos displaced in the formal working sector due to a lack of employable skills. Oftentimes, driving a tricycle will be the only mode of livelihood until retirement. According to the 2023 Annual Report of the Land Transportation Office, there are more than 7 million registered private motorcycles and tricycles in the country. It is high time that we give value to our tricycles in the country. It is high time that we give value to our tricycle drivers and operators for their contribution to the daily life of the ordinary Filipinos and to economic development. This measure ensures the welfare of the tricycle drivers and operators for a more organized sector by defining the requirements for proper operation of tricycles and simplifying the registration system imposed in the application and issuance of motorized tricycle operator permit (MTOP). It also mandates the establishment of a one-stop shop in every local government unit to cater to all the transactions of tricycle drivers and operators. It advances the welfare of the tricycle sector by mandating the Social Security System and the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation to assure their provision of health care and social benefits. The measure outlines the significant role of the Local Government Units and other government agencies in supporting the sector. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11347
title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE PREVENTION OF ADOLESCENT PREGNANCY, STRENGTHENING THE FAMILY AND COMMUNITY SUPPORT FOR ADOLESCENTS, AND PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL ADOLESCENT PREGNANCY PREVENTION AND EDUCATION PROGRAM
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Adolescent pregnancy remains a significant public health, education, and social protection concern in the Philippines. While recent data show encouraging improvements1, the persistence of pregnancies among adolescents, particularly among younger girls and those from disadvantaged households, demonstrates the need for a comprehensive and sustained national response. The figures reveal that teenage pregnancy is closely linked to socioeconomic disadvantage. The PSA's 2022 National Demographic and Health Survey reported that 10.3 percent of women aged 15 to 19 in the poorest wealth quintile had experienced pregnancy, compared with only 1.8 percent among those in the wealthiest quintile.2 These disparities demonstrate that adolescent pregnancy cannot be addressed solely as a matter of individual choice. It is also a question of unequal access to information, health services, education, protection, and opportunities. Of even greater concern are pregnancies involving very young adolescents. PSA data showed that registered births to mothers aged 10 to 14 increased from 1,903 in 2016 to 2,113 in 2020, an increase of 11 percent. During this period, an average of five to seven births each day were registered to mothers aged 10 to 14.3 Pregnancies at such young ages require particular attention from the State because they may be associated with abuse, exploitation, coercion, or other circumstances that compromise a child's safety and rights. 1 Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), 2025 National Demographic and Health Survey: Teenage Pregnancy. The 2025 NDHS reports that 4.9 percent of women aged 15–19 had ever been pregnant, compared with 5.4 percent in 2022. 2 Philippine Statistics Authority, 2022 National Demographic and Health Survey: Teenage Pregnancy. The PSA defines teenage pregnancy as the percentage of women aged 15–19 who have ever been pregnant. The survey reported a prevalence of 10.3 percent among women in the lowest wealth quintile and 1.8 percent among those in the highest wealth quintile. 3 Philippine Statistics Authority, Adolescent Pregnancy in the Philippines: 2016–2020, PSA Reference No. 2022-477, 8 December 2022. The report states that registered births to mothers aged 10–14 increased from 1,903 in 2016 to 2,113 in 2020, equivalent to an 11.0 percent increase. Page 1 The consequences of adolescent pregnancy can extend beyond pregnancy and childbirth. A young mother may face difficulty continuing her education, increased economic vulnerability, diminished employment opportunities, and greater dependence on her family or social protection programs. These consequences can, in turn, reinforce an intergenerational cycle of poverty. The response of government must never be to stigmatize adolescent parents. A young person who becomes pregnant remains entitled to education, health care, protection, and opportunities to build a productive and dignified life. Prevention and support must therefore go hand in hand. The proposed Adolescent Pregnancy Prevention Act seeks to adopt a prevention-centered, family-supported, values-based, and age- and development- appropriate approach to adolescent pregnancy. It recognizes that no single government agency, program, or intervention can adequately address the problem. The measure therefore establishes the Adolescent Pregnancy Prevention Inter-Agency Council which shall serve as the policy-making body responsible for the development of a national framework that shall be called the National Adolescent Pregnancy Prevention and Education Program. The measure shall strengthen, at the community level age, culturally-sensitive and responsive, and age- and development-appropriate education on responsible decision-making, healthy relationships, self-respect, self-discipline, personal boundaries, and the consequences of early and unplanned pregnancy and childbearing for all adolescents through the development and delivery of the Adolescent Pregnancy and Reproductive Health Education. The measure further recognizes the importance of parents, families, schools, communities, and local governments. Government programs will have limited impact if young people lack supportive environments in which they can ask questions, obtain reliable information, seek help, and make responsible decisions without fear of stigma. The bill therefore promotes stronger family and community engagement and clearer coordination among service providers. Education continuity shall be an important component of the national strategy through School-Based Programs to be implemented by the Department of Education which includes interventions such as educational, career, and life-planning support, and continuing educational support and reintegration of adolescent parents. The proposed Act shall likewise strengthen mechanisms for the early identification and referral of adolescents who may be at heightened risk of pregnancy, school disengagement, abuse, exploitation, or other forms of vulnerability. Particular attention shall be given to children and adolescents in communities with persistently high rates of adolescent pregnancy or other identified risk factors. label: HB 11350
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Sierra Madre Mountain Range is one of the Philippines’ most important natural ecosystems and a vital environmental and disaster-resilience asset. Stretching across eastern Luzon, it serves as a natural barrier that helps lessen the impacts of typhoons, heavy rainfall, flooding, landslides, and other natural calamities. In line with this, this measure seeks to strengthen the protection, conservation, restoration, and sustainable management of the Sierra Madre Mountain Range by establishing a dedicated Sierra Madre Mountain Range Authority and providing a comprehensive framework for its long-term management. Among its salient features are: (1) the creation of a dedicated authority to coordinate conservation, enforcement, restoration, climate adaptation, and disaster- risk reduction efforts; (2) the formulation of a 25-year Sierra Madre Master Plan integrating biodiversity conservation, watershed management, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, sustainable livelihoods, land-use planning, and the rights and traditional knowledge of Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples; and (3) the establishment of landscape zoning, ecological corridors, restoration measures, and stronger enforcement against activities that degrade the mountain range. The measure is firmly anchored in Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution which declares the State’s duty to protect and advance the people’s right to a balanced and healthful ecology. It also advances the State’s responsibility to protect the nation’s natural resources for present and future generations. By treating the Sierra Madre as a critical natural foundation for disaster risk reduction, climate resilience, and public safety, the bill gives concrete effect to the constitutional mandate of environmental protection. The protection of the Sierra Madre is therefore not merely an environmental concern. It is a matter of public safety, national resilience, food and water security, and national survival. The mountain range functions as one of Luzon’s principal natural defenses against typhoons and extreme weather, while healthy forests and watersheds help reduce flooding and landslide risks. The bill accordingly recognizes the Sierra Madre as a critical natural foundation for national security, disaster risk reduction, and climate resilience, and directs government agencies to integrate ecosystem-based approaches into disaster and national security planning. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. PERCIVAL V. CENDAÑA Akbayan Representative JOSE MANUEL TADEO DADAH KIRAM ISMULA “CHEL” I. label: HB 11352
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FAIR TREATMENT OF CERTAIN SENIOR CITIZEN PENSIONERS BY GRANTING ANNUAL CHRISTMAS CASH GIFT, THIRTEENTH-MONTH PENSION, AND PENSION INCREASES TO PENSIONERS OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM AND GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM WHO ARE BENEFICIARIES OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7699, “AN ACT INSTITUTING LIMITED PORTABILITY SCHEME IN THE SOCIAL SECURITY INSURANCE SYSTEMS BY TOTALIZING THE WORKERS’ CREDITABLE SERVICES OR CONTRIBUTIONS IN EACH OF THE SYSTEMS”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 7699, otherwise known as the “Limited Portability Law,” allows workers who have rendered service or made contributions under both the Social Security System (SSS) and the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) to totalize their creditable periods for purposes of qualifying for benefits. This recognizes the contributions and years of service of workers who have moved between the private and public sectors. Despite this recognition, pensioners who qualify under the portability scheme have not always received benefits on the same basis as similarly situated old-age pensioners of the respective systems, particularly with respect to supplemental pension benefits and pension increases. This measure seeks to ensure fair and equal treatment by granting qualified pensioners under Republic Act No. 7699 the same annual Christmas cash gift, thirteenth-month pension, and pension increases granted to similarly situated pensioners of the SSS and GSIS. A pensioner receiving pensions from both systems shall be entitled to the applicable benefits from both systems, based on the pension payable by each. The measure further seeks to protect existing benefits and ensure that the implementation of the law shall not result in the diminution or reduction of benefits already enjoyed by portability pensioners. The passage of this measure will uphold the principle that workers who have contributed to both social insurance systems should not be placed at a disadvantage merely because their pension entitlement was established through the portability scheme. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11353
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AUTISM CENTERS AND EARLY DETECTION PROGRAMS NATIONWIDE, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) affects many Filipino individuals and families who continue to face significant challenges in accessing timely developmental screening, diagnosis, intervention, therapy, healthcare, education, and community support services. These challenges are compounded by the limited availability of specialized facilities and trained professionals, financial barriers, and unequal access to developmental services, particularly in underserved and geographically disadvantaged areas. This proposed measure seeks to establish a nationwide network of accessible and affordable Autism Centers that will serve as regional hubs for developmental screening, diagnostic assessment, intervention, rehabilitation, family support, educational coordination, and referral services. It likewise seeks to strengthen early detection and intervention by integrating developmental screening into existing health and community-based programs and by training frontline healthcare, education, and community personnel to recognize developmental concerns and facilitate timely referrals. The measure further promotes inclusive education and community support, strengthens the capacity of healthcare professionals, therapists, educators, and other service providers, and encourages research and data-driven policymaking to improve the availability, quality, accessibility, and affordability of autism-related services. Recognizing that timely and continuous support is essential to improving outcomes, the bill provides for coordinated referral mechanisms among Autism Centers and relevant healthcare, education, social welfare, skills training, and employment institutions. It also encourages the expansion of appropriate health coverage and financial assistance for indigent and financially vulnerable families. Consistent with Republic Act No. 7277, otherwise known as the “Magna Carta for Persons with Disability,” as amended, Republic Act No. 11036, otherwise known as the “Mental Health Act,” Republic Act No. 11223, otherwise known as the “Universal Health Care Act,” Republic Act No. 11650, otherwise known as the “Instituting a Policy of Inclusion and Services for Learners with Disabilities in Support of Inclusive Education Act,” and other relevant laws, this measure adopts a rights-based, inclusive, family-centered, community-based, and evidence-informed approach to autism care and support. By establishing accessible Autism Centers and strengthening early detection, referral, intervention, and support systems nationwide, this measure seeks to reduce disparities in access to services and enable persons with ASD and their families to receive timely, appropriate, and continuing support regardless of their place of residence or economic circumstances. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11354
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE RECRUITMENT, TRAINING, AND EDUCATION QUOTA FOR WOMEN IN THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 58 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8551, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE REFORM AND REORGANIZATION ACT OF 1998,” AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Women play an indispensable role in modern law enforcement. Their presence in the police service strengthens the capacity of law enforcement institutions to respond effectively and sensitively to cases involving women and children, sexual and gender-based violence, domestic abuse, and other crimes and situations requiring gender-responsive policing. Recognizing this need, Republic Act No. 8551, otherwise known as the “Philippine National Police Reform and Reorganization Act of 1998,” established women's desks in police stations and provided for the prioritization of women for recruitment and training. Section 58 of the law currently requires the Philippine National Police (PNP) to reserve ten percent (10%) of its annual recruitment, training, and education quota for women. The statutory quota was established more than two decades ago. The evolving demands of policing and the continuing need for a more representative and gender-responsive police organization warrant a progressive increase in the participation of women in the PNP. This measure therefore seeks to increase the existing quota from ten percent (10%) to fifteen percent (15%) during the first five (5) years from the effectivity of the proposed law, and to twenty percent (20%) beginning on the sixth (6th) year and every year thereafter. The measure does not dispense with the qualifications, merit, fitness, eligibility, and other requirements prescribed by law for appointment to the PNP. Rather, it seeks to ensure that qualified women are given meaningful and increased opportunities to enter the police service within the reserved quota. The measure likewise requires the PNP to incorporate the women's quota in its recruitment and manpower planning and to undertake reasonable and sustained efforts to attract, recruit, and qualify women applicants. This will help ensure that the statutory quota is treated as an integral component of PNP recruitment policy and not merely as an after-the-fact numerical target. To promote accountability, the measure establishes a monitoring and reporting mechanism requiring the PNP to submit an annual report to the NAPOLCOM and Congress on its compliance with the women's quota, including the number of women who applied, qualified, were appointed, and underwent training, as well as any unfilled portion of the reserved quota and the reasons therefor. The measure further recognizes that increasing the number of women in the PNP should not confine them to women's desks. Women recruited and trained under the program should be afforded equal opportunities for assignment, promotion, professional development, and career advancement throughout the police organization. This is consistent with the existing statutory policy that the women's-desk provisions should not restrict the assignment of policewomen to other positions or be used to prevent their promotion. By progressively increasing the representation of women in the PNP, this measure seeks to build a more representative, professional, responsive, gender- sensitive, and effective police force capable of providing accessible and appropriate police services to all sectors of Philippine society. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11355
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPLOYMENT OF MOBILE HEALTH CLINICS TO GEOGRAPHICALLY ISOLATED AND DISADVANTAGED AREAS (GIDAs) AND OTHER UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO PROVIDE REGULAR MOBILE HEALTH SERVICES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to basic healthcare remains a significant challenge for Filipinos living in Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAs) and other underserved communities, where distance, inadequate health facilities, and shortages of healthcare personnel can prevent timely access to essential medical services. This measure seeks to establish a Mobile Rural Health Clinic Program under the Department of Health (DOH) to provide regular, accessible, and community-based healthcare services in areas where permanent health facilities are limited or difficult to reach. The Program shall provide primary and preventive care, diagnostics, medicines, maternal and child health services, mental health services, emergency care, health education, and referral assistance, as appropriate to the needs of the communities served. The measure likewise strengthens coordination among the DOH, local government units, PhilHealth, and other concerned agencies to ensure continuity of care and integration with existing health systems, while providing appropriate standards for mobile clinic operations, personnel, equipment, and digital health systems. By bringing essential healthcare services closer to underserved Filipinos, this measure seeks to advance equitable access to healthcare and strengthen the delivery of primary health services in communities that need them most. label: HB 11356
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF ACCESSIBLE, SAFE, CLEAN, GENDER-RESPONSIVE, AND WELL- MAINTAINED PUBLIC TOILETS AND SANITATION FACILITIES IN PUBLIC PLACES, TRANSPORT TERMINALS, TOURIST AREAS, MARKETS, PARKS, AND GOVERNMENT CENTERS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to clean, safe, accessible, and well-maintained toilet and sanitation facilities is a basic public-health and public-dignity concern. Yet in many public places, including markets, parks, transport areas, tourist destinations, and government centers, adequate sanitation facilities remain insufficient, inaccessible, poorly maintained, or unavailable to the public. The absence of reliable public sanitation facilities can contribute to poor hygiene, environmental contamination, open defecation, and preventable health and safety risks. It disproportionately affects children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, pregnant person, persons with mobility limitations, workers, commuters, and other vulnerable members of the public. While existing laws provide sanitation and accessibility requirements for particular establishments and facilities, there remains a need for a coordinated framework that specifically addresses public access to sanitation facilities across high-use public places. This measure therefore mandates the provision, maintenance, or designation of compliant public toilets and sanitation facilities; establishes minimum standards for cleanliness, water, handwashing, safety, privacy, accessibility, and gender responsiveness; and requires local government units to prepare Public Sanitation Access Plans identifying existing facilities, access gaps, priority areas, maintenance responsibilities, and financing options. The measure also promotes the use and upgrading of existing facilities before new construction, provides for phased implementation, and establishes coordination among the Department of Health, local government units, and other concerned agencies. It further harmonizes the measure with existing sanitation and accessibility laws, including Republic Act No. 11311, to avoid duplication and double penalties. The enactment of this measure will strengthen the country's sanitation system by ensuring that the public can reasonably access facilities that are not only available, but also safe, clean, accessible, functional, and worthy of human dignity. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11361
title: AN ACT DECLARING EVERY 10TH OF FEBRUARY OF EACH YEAR AS NATIONAL SAFER INTERNET DAY IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines ranks as the top country in the Asia-Pacific with the highest daily online usage. About 76.7 million Filipino internet users spend an average of more than 10 hours every day scouring the World Wide Web. With the forecasted improvements in the internet infrastructure, about 15.5 million households are predicted to be connected to the internet by 2025. The availability of the internet throughout the nation has facilitated people's connectivity and daily activities, including those related to education, commerce, and entertainment. Digital operations have increased the efficiency of daily transactions by reducing the time required for otherwise in- person, human transactions and making collaboration doable even for colleagues who are miles apart. While the potential of internet efficiency has improved our daily lives, it has also presented a number of safety and security challenges to its users both children and adults. In 2021 alone, there were more than 98,000 cyberattacks recorded and around 2.8 million cybercrimes listed, including fraud, sexual abuse and exploitation, bullying and identity theft. It is our belief that appropriate steps towards lowering the risks of internet users against cybercrimes can be achieved by first raising awareness among the people. In the pursuit of making the online world a safer space for its users, this bill seeks to declare one day every year as National Safer Internet Day. By making Filipino internet users conscious of their online activities and the potential threats of their digital interactions, their vulnerabilities to scammers, hackers, and online syndicates can be dramatically reduced and prevented. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11362
title: AN ACT ENSURING THE AVAILABILITY, ADEQUACY, ACCESSIBILITY, AND SAFETY OF FOOD TO EVERY FILIPINO
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is a country that is regularly hit by natural and human- induced disasters, and the need for early warning systems is paramount. Access to such information ensures that vulnerable communities have the capacity for evidence-based and timely decision-making even before a crisis arises. The huge and fast-growing population in the Philippines is often cited as the main factor driving the country’s global competitiveness and improve attractiveness to investment. While reports indicate that there is enough food to feed the entire country, many Filipinos, especially children below the age of five, continue to suffer from malnutrition due to inadequate intake of food and nutrients. In the 2022 Global Food Security Index (GFSI) by Economist Impact, the Philippines ranked 67th out of 113 countries, with an overall score of 59.3 out of 100.1This represents an improvement from its 70th place in 2018, but the country’s performance has been uneven: it rose to 64th in 2019, slipped to 73rd in 2020, recovered to 64th in 2021, and then settled at 67th in 2022.2 Among sub-categories, the country again ranked first in only one—nutritional standards—underscoring a recurring pattern: strong performance in policy 1 Economist Impact and Corteva Agriscience. 2022. Global Food Security Index 2022: Global Report. September 2022 2 Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS). 2022. “Is Food Supply Accessible, Affordable, and Stable? The State of Food Security in the Philippines.” and standard-setting, but persistent gaps in implementation and systemic resilience. Among its many provisions, the foregoing measure explicitly lists governmental obligations of the State to respect, protect, and fulfill every Filipino’s right to adequate food. It also lays out specific percentage targets for the reduction of hunger, ultimately aiming for zero incidences of forced hunger within ten years. This measure seeks to address the following concerns: 1) food availability, stability, and adequacy; 2) food quality and safety; 3) the determination of standards on the minimum amount of food to be given to any person suffering from hunger or undernutrition; 4) physical and economic access to food; and 5) well-functioning distribution, processing, and market systems. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11365
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL FORENSIC DNA DATABASE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine justice system continuously faces the challenge of solving crimes efficiently, accurately, and fairly. Modern forensic science, particularly Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) technology, provides law enforcement agencies and courts with a powerful scientific tool for identifying individuals, linking biological evidence to persons, excluding innocent individuals, and assisting in the resolution of otherwise difficult or unsolved cases. DNA evidence may be recovered from biological materials found at crime scenes and from other sources relevant to criminal investigations. When properly collected, analyzed, stored, and compared, DNA profiles can establish associations between crime-scene evidence and individuals with a high degree of scientific reliability. A national forensic DNA database can therefore complement existing investigative techniques and strengthen the evidentiary foundation of criminal investigations and prosecutions. Several legislative measures have previously recognized the need for a Philippine forensic DNA database. Among these are House Bill No. 94 of the 19th Congress, which sought to institutionalize a national forensic DNA database for criminal investigations, identification of missing persons and unidentified human remains, and related purposes, as well as House Bill No. 1179 filed during the 20th Congress, which similarly proposed the establishment of a forensic DNA database in the Philippines. Despite these legislative initiatives, there remains a need for a comprehensive statutory framework that will establish, maintain, regulate, and ensure the proper use of a Philippine National Forensic DNA Database. The proposed measure seeks to provide such a framework while ensuring that the collection and processing of DNA information are conducted in accordance with law, scientific standards, due process, privacy rights, and other constitutional safeguards. The proposed Philippine National Forensic DNA Database shall serve as a centralized forensic resource for authorized government agencies. It shall facilitate the comparison of DNA profiles obtained from crime-scene evidence with legally obtained reference profiles, subject to the requirements and safeguards provided under the proposed Act. At the same time, the use of DNA information presents legitimate concerns involving privacy, confidentiality, data security, consent, unlawful collection, unauthorized access, and misuse of genetic information. The proposed legislation therefore intends to establish clear rules governing the collection, submission, storage, retention, access, disclosure, use, and destruction of DNA samples and profiles. Appropriate safeguards should be incorporated to ensure that the database is utilized strictly for legitimate forensic and law-enforcement purposes and is not used for unauthorized discrimination, surveillance, or other purposes inconsistent with law. The establishment of a national forensic DNA database will also promote greater coordination among the Philippine National Police, National Bureau of Investigation, Department of Justice, courts, forensic laboratories, and other authorized government agencies. A unified system can help minimize duplication of forensic records, facilitate lawful information-sharing, and improve the country's capacity to investigate and resolve crimes through scientifically supported evidence. Importantly, DNA evidence should complement—not replace—the constitutional rights of persons accused of crimes. A DNA match must be evaluated together with other evidence and the applicable rules of evidence and procedure. The proposed Act therefore seeks to balance the legitimate needs of law enforcement with the fundamental rights to due process, privacy, and protection against unreasonable searches and seizures. The experience of previous legislative proposals demonstrates the continuing recognition of the importance of establishing a forensic DNA database in the Philippines. Senate Bill No. 1456 of the 19th Congress and Senate Bill No. 357 of the 20th Congress, for example, both proposed legislations establishing a forensic DNA database, with the latter specifically proposing a Philippine National Police forensic DNA database. This measure is therefore intended to provide the Philippines with a modern, scientifically grounded, secure, and accountable forensic DNA infrastructure capable of supporting criminal investigations, improving the identification of offenders and exoneration of innocent persons, assisting in the identification of missing persons and unidentified remains, and strengthening the administration of justice. For these reasons, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. REP. ANTONIO T. KHO REP. ELISA “OLGA” T. label: HB 11366
title: AN ACT REGULATING THE POSSESSION AND OPERATION OF UNMANNED SYSTEMS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The rapid development and widespread availability of unmanned systems have brought significant technological, economic, and social benefits to the Philippines. Unmanned aircraft and other unmanned systems are increasingly being used in agriculture, infrastructure inspection, mapping and surveying, disaster response, environmental monitoring, photography, logistics, research, public safety, and other legitimate activities. At the same time, the increasing accessibility of unmanned systems presents emerging challenges to public safety, national security, privacy, property, and the orderly use of public spaces and airspace. Improper or unauthorized operation may endanger persons and property, interfere with aircraft operations, compromise restricted or sensitive areas, or facilitate other unlawful activities. The Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP) has already established regulatory requirements for remotely piloted aircraft systems, including registration, personnel or controller certification, operator requirements, operational limitations, and sanctions for violations. CAAP likewise recognizes the need to ensure that unmanned aircraft operations do not compromise aviation and public safety. However, the continuing development of unmanned technology calls for a comprehensive legislative framework that will complement existing aviation regulations and provide clear rules concerning the possession, registration, operation, use, and accountability of unmanned systems. This measure therefore seeks to establish a national policy governing unmanned systems while respecting the existing mandate of CAAP and other government agencies with jurisdiction over particular applications of unmanned technology. The proposed Act seeks to ensure that persons who possess and operate unmanned systems do so responsibly, safely, and in accordance with established standards. It shall provide appropriate requirements for registration, identification, licensing or certification, and operation, as may be applicable to the type, weight, capability, and intended use of the unmanned system. The measure likewise seeks to establish reasonable restrictions on the operation of unmanned systems in areas where their operation may pose a substantial risk to public safety or security, including airports, aerodromes, restricted or prohibited airspace, government and military installations, correctional facilities, emergency response areas, and other areas designated by competent government authorities. CAAP's existing regulations, for example, recognize different categories of remotely piloted aircraft and impose additional requirements depending on the type of operation. Certain operations may require controller certification, operator certification, or special flight permits, particularly for operations involving controlled or prohibited airspace, nighttime operations, operations beyond visual line of sight, operations near airports, or operations above prescribed altitude limits. The proposed legislation also recognizes that unmanned systems should not be regulated solely from the perspective of aviation. Their operation may affect public order and safety, privacy, national security, telecommunications, environmental protection, and the protection of critical infrastructure. Accordingly, the bill provides for appropriate coordination among CAAP, the Philippine National Police, the Armed Forces of the Philippines, the National Telecommunications Commission, local government units, and other concerned government agencies, within their respective mandates. The measure further seeks to promote responsible use of unmanned systems by establishing clear obligations on owners and operators, including compliance with applicable registration and operational requirements, observance of designated no-fly or restricted areas, maintenance of the unmanned system in safe operating condition, and compliance with lawful instructions issued by competent authorities. The proposed Act shall likewise provide penalties for unauthorized possession or operation, operation in prohibited or restricted areas, reckless or dangerous operation, interference with aircraft or other critical operations, failure to comply with registration or identification requirements, and other acts that may endanger persons, property, public safety, or national security. At the same time, the bill recognizes that regulation must be reasonable, proportionate, and consistent with constitutional rights. Legitimate recreational, educational, scientific, commercial, agricultural, humanitarian, and other lawful uses of unmanned systems should not be unnecessarily restricted. The regulatory framework should therefore distinguish between activities that present different levels of risk and impose requirements proportionate to the nature and circumstances of the operation. The bill also recognizes the increasing use of unmanned systems for disaster response and public service. Government agencies and authorized responders may use unmanned systems for search and rescue, disaster assessment, emergency response, environmental monitoring, and other public- interest purposes, subject to appropriate safety and operational protocols. Furthermore, the proposed legislation shall be implemented in coordination with existing laws and regulations, including Republic Act No. 9497, otherwise known as the “Civil Aviation Authority Act of 2008,” and applicable Philippine Civil Aviation Regulations. CAAP is already mandated to establish and prescribe rules and regulations concerning aircraft registration and operations and to enforce laws governing air transportation. The bill therefore does not intend to diminish the authority of CAAP over civil aviation. Rather, it seeks to provide a broader statutory framework for the responsible possession and operation of unmanned systems while preserving the respective mandates of government agencies under existing laws. label: HB 11370
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE CYBERSECURITY COUNCIL AND ENHANCING THE NATIONAL CYBERSECURITY FRAMEWORK
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 24 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution recognizes the vital role of communication and information in nation-building. Communication services, such as the internet, serve as major tools in driving economic and social development by connecting people and industry linkages which contribute toward a cohesive and progressive nation. title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE JONI VILLANUEVA GENERAL HOSPITAL IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF BOCAUE, PROVINCE OF BULACAN, INTO A LEVEL III GENERAL HOSPITAL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Access to appropriate hospital care depends not only on the presence of a health facility, but also on whether that facility has the capacity, services, equipment, and personnel required to respond to the needs of the population it serves. The 1987 Constitution directs the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people. Consistent with this mandate, the Universal Health Care Act seeks to ensure that all Filipinos have equitable access to quality and affordable health care services through an integrated and responsive health system. Enacted in 2022, Republic Act No. 11720 established the Joni Villanueva General Hospital (JVGH) in the Municipality of Bocaue, Province of Bulacan, as a Level II general hospital under the direct control and supervision of the Department of Health (DOH). In the years since its establishment under R.A. No. 11720, JVGH has experienced substantial growth in the utilization of its services. Its bed occupancy rate increased from 34.05% in 2023 to 125.97% in 2024 and 119.71% in 2025, and further reached 145.15% as of June 2026. Admissions rose from 656 in 2023 to 10,494 in 2025, while emergency room visits increased from 10,638 to 36,352 and outpatient visits from 26,551 to 60,144 during the same period. This increasing utilization has placed corresponding pressure on the hospital's existing capacity. JVGH currently has a licensed capacity of 100 beds, while its implementing bed capacity as of 2026 already ranges from 120 to 150 beds. The sustained rise in admissions, emergency cases, and outpatient consultations supports the continued expansion not only of bed capacity, but also of hospital facilities, service capability, and human resources. The hospital has already begun developing the institutional capacity required for a higher level of care. Its Hospital Development Plan identifies the progressive strengthening of critical care, specialty services, advanced diagnostics, health human resources, infrastructure, and referral networks as part of its strategic direction toward Level III capability. The plan likewise envisions JVGH as a stronger frontline referral facility for critical cases and expressly includes the pursuit of legislation upgrading the hospital to Level III. The need to upgrade JVGH must likewise be considered in relation to the size and continuing development of the population it serves. Based on the 2024 Census of Population of the Philippine Statistics Authority, Bulacan had a population of 3,876,806 as of 1 July 2024, while Central Luzon had a total population of 12,989,074. Bulacan was the most populous province in the region, accounting for about 29.8% of Central Luzon’s population. Central Luzon’s population increased from 12,422,172 in 2020 to 12,989,074 in 2024, equivalent to an average annual population growth rate of 1.08%. The province’s substantial population, together with continuing urbanization and economic and industrial development, reinforces the need for accessible and adequately distributed hospital facilities capable of providing specialized and subspecialized care. This need is reflected in the Philippine Health Facility Development Plan (PHFDP) 2020–2040, which provides the national strategic framework for health-facility development based on population need, equitable access, and the coordinated expansion of infrastructure, equipment, and human resources for health. For Central Luzon, the PHFDP reported a supply of only 2,094 Level III hospital beds in 2019, against a projected requirement of 8,468 beds by 2025, indicating a gap of 6,374 beds between the reported baseline supply and projected 2025 need. The PHFDP further projects additional requirements of 1,417 Level III or apex beds by 2030, 1,596 by 2035, and 1,793 by 2040, bringing the cumulative Level III bed requirement for Central Luzon for 2025–2040 to 13,274 beds. The regional shortfall is particularly relevant to Bulacan. JVGH is the province’s DOH-retained hospital and presently provides Level II public hospital capability. At the tertiary level, the province has only one Level III hospital, with an authorized bed capacity of 300 beds. Based on the current provincial hospital inventory, Bulacan has 3,008 authorized hospital beds, of which 2,031 are in private facilities and 977 are in public hospitals. Public-sector capacity consists of 577 Level I beds, 100 Level II beds, and 300 Level III beds. The province has 141 intensive care unit beds, only 39 of which are in public hospitals, including 35 in the public Level III hospital. These figures illustrate the limited public tertiary and critical care capacity available to a province of nearly 3.9 million people. The proposed upgrade of JVGH would therefore address more than the needs of a single institution. It would strengthen Bulacan’s public referral network, expand access to higher-level care, and contribute to addressing the broader deficiency in Level III hospital capacity identified for Central Luzon. It is likewise consistent with the development trajectory already set out in the JVGH Hospital Development Plan, which calls for the progressive expansion of infrastructure, equipment, specialty and critical-care services, personnel, and teaching and training capability necessary for Level III operations. This bill therefore seeks to upgrade the Joni Villanueva General Hospital from a Level II to a Level III general hospital, provide for the corresponding upgrading of its professional health care services and facilities, authorize the necessary increase in its workforce, and allow future increases in bed capacity to be guided by its Hospital Development Plan, the Philippine Health Facility Development Plan, and applicable DOH standards. label: HB 11373
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE LATERAL ENTRY PROGRAM OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 33 OF REPUBLIC ACT 6975, AS AMENDED
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine National Police (PNP) plays a vital role in maintaining peace and order, protecting lives and property, preventing and investigating crimes, and ensuring public safety. The effectiveness of the police organization depends not only on adequate resources and modern equipment, but also on having a competent, professional, and well- qualified corps of officers and personnel. Republic Act No. 6975, otherwise known as the Department of the Interior and Local Government Act of 1990, provides for the organization and administration of the Philippine National Police. Section 33 thereof provides for the lateral entry of officers into the PNP, particularly for line and technical positions, in recognition of the need to bring into the organization individuals who possess specialized knowledge, skills, training, and professional qualifications that may not be sufficiently available through the regular recruitment and promotion system. However, the existing qualification framework for lateral entry may unduly limit the pool of qualified applicants by recognizing only certain baccalaureate degrees or professional qualifications for particular positions. With the increasingly complex nature of law enforcement, modern policing requires expertise in a broad range of disciplines, including information technology, cybersecurity, forensic science, criminology, psychology, guidance and counselling, medicine, engineering, and other fields relevant to police operations and administration. There is likewise a need to provide greater career mobility and professional advancement opportunities to police non-commissioned officers and non-uniformed personnel who are already in government service. Many of these personnel have acquired relevant baccalaureate degrees, professional licenses, specialized training, and substantial experience in the performance of police and police-support functions. Their institutional knowledge, practical experience, and familiarity with the operations of the PNP constitute valuable assets that should be recognized and utilized in filling appropriate vacancies. The proposed measure therefore seeks to amend Section 33 of Republic Act 6975 to broaden the qualifications for lateral entry into PNP by allowing other appropriate baccalaureate degrees. This will enable the organization to recruit and appoint individuals possessing diverse educational and professional backgrounds necessary for modern and specialized policing. More importantly, the bill seeks to ensure that qualified police non- commissioned officers and non-uniformed personnel already in the service are given meaningful opportunities to qualify for lateral entry into appropriate line and technical officer positions. Such a policy recognizes the principle that career advancement should not be limited by one’s initial mode of entry into the organization, particularly when an incumbent personnel has subsequently obtained the education, qualifications, training, and experience required for a higher position. This measure will also promote merit, competence, professionalism, and equal opportunity within the PNP. By opening lateral entry opportunities to qualified personnel already serving the organization, the PNP can retain experienced and capable individuals while encouraging its personnel to pursue higher education, professional development, and specialized training. The proposed legislation is therefore intended to strengthen the PNP by expanding its pool of qualified officers, maximizing the talents and experience of its existing personnel, and providing equitable opportunities for career advancement. It seeks to ensure that the qualifications for police leadership and technical positions remain responsive to the evolving demands of law enforcement and public safety. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. MAURICIO G. label: HB 11374
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Sierra Madre Mountain Range is one of the Philippines’ most vital ecological assets. Extending from Cagayan to Quezon, it encompasses forests, watersheds, rivers, biodiversity areas, and coastal ecosystems that provide essential services for water security, agriculture, livelihoods, infrastructure, and local economies. It also serves as a natural defense against typhoons, flooding, landslides, drought, and other climate-related hazards. Despite its importance, the Sierra Madre continues to face degradation from illegal logging, destructive extraction, incompatible land conversion, habitat fragmentation, and biodiversity loss. Its management is likewise dispersed among various agencies, jurisdictions, and regulatory systems, making integrated, range-wide governance difficult. This proposed measure seeks to address these gaps by establishing the Sierra Madre Mountain Range Authority (SMMRA) as a government-owned or -controlled corporation with an original charter, attached to the Office of the President for policy coordination and administrative supervision. The Authority shall lead the policy, planning, coordination, and regulation of the integrated management of the Sierra Madre, without diminishing the mandates of the DENR, local government units, NCIP, Protected Area Management Boards, and other competent institutions. The bill establishes a 25-year Sierra Madre Ecological Integrity and Sustainable Development Master Plan to provide a unified, science-based framework for ecological limits, management zones, restoration priorities, permitted and prohibited uses, and measurable outcomes. It adopts a landscape-scale, ridge-to-reef approach and a Nature-Based Solutions-First policy for addressing climate, disaster, watershed, and coastal risks. The proposed framework strengthens environmental standards, monitoring, enforcement, restoration obligations, and accountability, while protecting the constitutional and statutory rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities, including ancestral-domain rights, participation, benefit-sharing, and Free and Prior Informed Consent where applicable. This landmark legislation seeks to establish a permanent, integrated, and accountable framework for the protection and sustainable management of the Sierra Madre Mountain Range. More than an environmental measure, it is an investment in the country’s water and food security, disaster resilience, biodiversity, livelihoods, and long-term national development. By safeguarding the Sierra Madre today, the State protects an ecological foundation upon which present and future generations of Filipinos depend. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 11375
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A PHILIPPINE MEDICAL ACT, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 2382, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MEDICAL ACT OF 1959
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 2382, otherwise known as the “Medical Act of 1959,” has governed the practice of medicine in the Philippines for more than six decades. The rapid development of medical science and technology, the changing needs of the health-care system, and the emergence of new modes of medical education and practice necessitate the updating and modernization of the law. This bill seeks to establish a comprehensive Philippine Medical Act that will strengthen the regulation of medical education, internship, licensure, postgraduate training, and the practice of medicine. It creates appropriate institutional mechanisms, including the Medical Education Council, the Professional Regulatory Board of Medicine, and the Postgraduate Medical Education Council, while integrating the medical profession under a national professional organization. The measure also promotes innovative medical education, recognizes telemedicine as part of the practice of medicine, strengthens standards for physician licensure and specialization, and provides safeguards for the welfare, working conditions, and grievance mechanisms of resident and fellow trainees. These reforms are intended to develop competent, ethical, and globally competitive physicians while ensuring that patient welfare, safety, and access to quality health care remain paramount. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. label: HB 11376
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PERPETUAL EXISTENCE OF THE PHILIPPINE INTERNATIONAL TRADING CORPORATION (PITC), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 2 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1071, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE REVISED CHARTER OF THE PHILIPPINE INTERNATIONAL TRADING CORPORATION”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine International Trading Corporation (PITC) was created under Presidential Decree No. 252, with its charter subsequently revised by Presidential Decree No. 1071, otherwise known as the “Revised Charter of the Philippine International Trading Corporation.” Under Section 2 of P.D. No. 1071, PITC is authorized to exist for fifty (50) years, with its present corporate term set to expire on 25 January 2027. For decades, PITC has served as a government corporate vehicle in advancing the State’s objectives in international trade, including facilitating trade, promoting Philippine products and enterprises, and supporting government procurement and marketing activities within the scope of its charter. With the impending expiration of its corporate term, there is a need to ensure the continuity of PITC’s juridical personality, operations, contracts, obligations, assets, liabilities, and other lawful commitments. The proposed measure therefore seeks to provide PITC with a perpetual corporate term, unless otherwise provided by law. Perpetual existence, however, shall not exempt PITC from government oversight and accountability. The Corporation shall remain subject to the evaluation, monitoring, and other appropriate actions of the Governance Commission for Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations (GCG) pursuant to Republic Act No. 10149, or the “GOCC Governance Act of 2011,” and other applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Such evaluation may consider PITC’s relevance, financial viability, operational efficiency, governance, performance, and contribution to Philippine international trade. The proposed measure does not expand PITC’s substantive powers and functions under P.D. No. 1071. Rather, it seeks to provide institutional continuity while preserving the authority of Congress and the appropriate government agencies to evaluate, amend, or otherwise take lawful action concerning the Corporation when warranted. The immediate enactment of this measure will prevent disruption arising from the expiration of PITC’s corporate term and enable the Corporation to continue performing its existing mandate in support of Philippine international trade, subject to continuing government oversight and accountability. In view of the foregoing, the immediate enactment of this measure is earnestly sought. KING GEORGE LEANDRO ANTONIO V. title: AN ACT GRANTING HAZARD PAY TO BARANGAY TANOD MEMBERS 22 Be it enacted by the Senate and the House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 25 SECTION 1. Short Title. — This Act shall be known as the “Barangay Tanod Hazard Pay Act”. 28 SECTION 2. Declaration of Policy. — The State recognizes the role of the Barangay Tanod, which was duly created under the Local Government Code, as an indispensable instrument in maintaining the peace, safety, and protection of their barangay, even during times of calamity and crisis.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 In February 2025, a barangay tanod in Binondo, Manila, Peton Biazon, was fatally stabbed while responding to an alleged e-bike theft. His death is a tragic reminder that barangay tanods can face serious and life-threatening risks while carrying out their duties to protect their communities. 26 Barangay tanods serve as the eyes and ears of their communities, often the first to respond when help is needed most. While the Local Government Code allows them to receive honoraria, allowances, and other benefits, there is no specific statutory hazard pay recognizing the risks they assume in the performance of their duties. 31 Hence, this proposed measure seeks to provide hazard pay of not less than Five Hundred Pesos (₱500.00) per day to qualified barangay tanods who render service under conditions that expose them to substantial risks to their health, safety, or lives. 35 When they are called upon to respond to emergencies, confront dangerous situations, or remain on duty during calamities, they place their own safety at risk for the safety of others. Their service deserves not only appreciation, but meaningful compensation that recognizes the dangers they willingly face. 40 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 42 43 44 REP.
