title: AN ACT PROTECTING SENIOR CITIZENS FROM VIOLENCE, DEFINING ELDER ABUSE, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The State, under Article II, Section 11 of the 1987 Constitution, proclaims the “value[ of] the dignity of every human person,” thereby “guarantee[ing] full respect for human rights.” In connection, under Article XIII, Section 11, the sector of the elderly is one that is entitled to prioritization when it comes to receiving government aid and protection, for their access and enjoyment of “essential goods, health and other social services.” Hence, under Article XV, Section 4, though the family, as a social unit, is entrusted with “the duty to care for its elderly members,” the State is likewise given this responsibility, to be acted upon “through just programs of social security.” As early as March 2020, it was confirmed that we have gotten “closer to having an aging population,” where “at least 7[%] are over 65 years old”:1 More than 8 million, or 8.2 percent, of the Philippines’ population of 108.9 million are aged 60 and above, per a report of the Commission on Population and Development (PopCom). Of this group, 5 million (or 4.7 percent) are aged 65 and older. With the rise in the aged population came an increase in the cases of senior citizens who have been subjected to abuse and/or been abandoned outrightly by their families:2 The Coalition of Services of the Elderly Inc., which advocates better care for senior citizens, warned recently that a crisis looms in elderly care. 1Ador Vincent Mayol, “Number of abandoned elderly rising,” Inquirer, March 9, 2020, available at https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1238586/number-of-abandoned-elderly-rising#ixzz6VxqjnkLU. 2“Crisis in elderly case,” Philippine Star, July 13, 2003, available at https://www.philstar.com/opinion/2003/07/13/213451/crisis-elderly-care. COSE said the elderly has become the fastest growing sector of the Philippine population. COSE, citing figures from the National Statistics Office, reported that the country has 155,200 people aged 65 to 80 who are listed as living alone. Some are widowed; others live alone by choice while others have been listed as abandoned. About 31,500 who are at least 80 years old have been abandoned or are living alone, COSE reported. Elderly abuse has unfortunately become a full-blown social cancer in the Philippines:3 Physical abuse are acts that are committed with intention of causing physical pain and injury. It can be in the form of being hit, sexually assaulted or burned. Any act leading to physical or bodily pain (i.e. bruises, sprains, welts, abrasions and fractures) and injury is classified under this. Psychological or emotional abuse involves verbal assaults, threats, humiliation, and ridicule. Such abuse is usually accompanied by physical abuse but may happen separately. Material or financial abuse includes misuse of property or money, theft, or forced signing of legal documents. Neglect may be referred to as passive or unintentional and active or intentional. Passive or unintentional neglect would mean isolation of the elderly or the elderly are left alone. The family, because of other duties, may not be able to meet the needs of the elderly or the caregiver is incompetent to provide care for the elderly. Active or intentional neglect involves the deliberate withholding of items needed for daily living (food, medicine, companionship and care) especially from those who are physically dependent. xxx A. Domestic Abuse There has been no major local study of this incident. DSWD admitted receiving reports of such circumstances but no record or action has been made. Unlike child abuse, to be able to protect abused elderly, the elderly themselves should report such incident before any action could be taken. Many abuses occur in different forms in their own homes but only few would admit such circumstances. The victims are often silent or in denial. They are afraid to seek help and guidance from people who can help them. Thus, elderly abuse is still unrecognized in our country. 3Clarita R. Carlos, “Concerns of the Elderly in the Philippines,” Philippine Social Sciences Review 56(1-4): 18-22, available at https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/8a6b/2d097fc02065e561553ba2231b04f3a9450d.pdf. Being physically vulnerable, the elderly is one of the most usual preys and victims of abuse. Because of the frailty, such condition is taken advantage of. Moreover being single and widowed is another factor adding to their susceptible condition. Being dependent on the family, unfortunately, in a way has become a disadvantage as well. For some families, they see the state of the elderly as an opportunity to take over whatever wealth the elderly has and deliberately neglecting or ignoring the elderly. A radio program called the Senior Citizen hour receives several calls and letters asking for advice regarding elderly abuse. Most of the abusers are the children themselves. Financial abuse is one of the frequent complaints accompanied by physical abuse. The children who still live with their parents, either employed or unemployed are oftentimes the perpetrators or abusers. The abusers extort money from them to support their needs or expenses, failure of the elderly to give money usually leads to physical abuse. There are also cases wherein the working parents would force their elderly parents to take care of their grandchildren even though the elderly have expressed their refusal. There are several cases being reported but do not really fall into any category of elderly abuse but still can be considered to be abusive. For instance, an elderly couple live together with their four children. The house belongs to the elderly couple, their children ages 27 to 45 are earning for themselves but have never contributed to the household expenses such as food, water and electricity bills. label: HB 11498
title: AN ACT INCREASING THE MONTHLY SALARY AND OTHER BENEFITS OF HEALTH WORKERS IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The experiences of the COVID-19 Pandemic in the Philippines left a lasting mark and a vital lesson. The country, as well as the globe entire, were caught lacking and unready to deal with a health emergency of such size. Although not unprecedented in recent human history, the pandemic was unique in its scale and disruption in living memory. It is a grim reality, warned by medical experts, scientists, and historians alike, that such a global pandemic will not be the last. It most assuredly will happen again. As such, the COVID-19 pandemic serves as a wake-up call. For our government, its instruments, and our precarious health care system, capacities must be expanded, processes must be streamlined, and bureaucracy must be made more efficient. A strong healthcare system likewise relies on its greatest resource: human resources, or the health workers that are on the frontline of such health emergencies. Without competent members of the healthcare profession comprising our public health system, we cannot expect that our public healthcare will be able to sustain and provide quality healthcare for all Filipinos. As such, it is of utmost importance that they be given the appreciation and benefits they deserve, in light of their significance in Philippine society. It is then incumbent for us to increase their salary and benefits considering the risks that their employment poses. It is for these reasons that the passage of this bill is earnestly sought In view of the foregoing, the passage of this measure is urgently sought. ALFRED C. label: HB 11499
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A BRIDGE OR UNDERSEA TUNNEL LINKING THE PROVINCE OF CEBU AND THE PROVINCE OF NEGROS ORIENTAL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Cebu and Negros Island are linked by sea, but travel and the movement of goods between them remain dependent on maritime crossings. A permanent link would improve connectivity within Central Visayas, facilitate the movement of people and goods, and create new opportunities for trade, tourism, investment, and regional development. It would also provide an additional transport option when sea crossings are unavailable or disrupted. This bill provides for the construction of a bridge or undersea tunnel connecting the Municipality of Santander, Cebu, and the Municipality of Sibulan, Negros Oriental. The proposed project would establish a direct and continuous land transport connection between Cebu Island and Negros Island, subject to the results of comprehensive feasibility, engineering, environmental, and other necessary technical studies. The project must consider not only the bridge or tunnel crossing itself, but also the necessary approach roads, interchanges, and connections to the existing road networks of Cebu and Negros Oriental. These components must be planned and developed as an integrated transport corridor to ensure that the completed link provides safe, efficient, and convenient movement between the two islands. The proposed link would make travel between Cebu and Negros Oriental easier and more efficient, provide a more direct route for the movement of goods, and improve access to essential services, employment centers, and economic opportunities. It could also strengthen disaster response and emergency mobility by providing another route for personnel, equipment, relief supplies, and other essential resources between the two islands. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MARCELINO C. label: HB 11501
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A BRIDGE OR UNDERSEA TUNNEL LINKING THE PROVINCE OF SOUTHERN LEYTE AND THE PROVINCE OF BOHOL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Southern Leyte and Bohol are linked by sea, but travel and the movement of goods between them remain dependent on maritime crossings. A permanent link would improve access between Eastern and Central Visayas and create new opportunities for trade, tourism, and investment. It would also provide another transport option when sea crossings are unavailable. This bill provides for the construction of a bridge or undersea tunnel following a proposed alignment from Maasin City, Southern Leyte, through Lapinig Island, Bohol to Ubay, Bohol. It would establish a continuous land route across the two water crossings, subject to the results of feasibility and engineering studies. Lapinig Island serves as an intermediate point in the proposed route. Accordingly, the project must consider the connections between Maasin City and Lapinig Island, between Lapinig Island and Ubay, and across the island itself. Examining these sections together is necessary to ensure that the completed link functions as one practical transport corridor. The proposed link would make travel between Southern Leyte and Bohol easier, provide a more direct route for the movement of goods, and improve access to essential services. It could also strengthen disaster response by giving emergency personnel, equipment, and relief supplies another route between the two provinces when conditions permit. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MARCELINO C. front_matter: ===== [page 1] ===== Republic of the Philippines HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES Quezon City, Metro Manila TWENTIETH CONGRESS Second Regular Session 4 House Bill No.11502 Introduced by Representative Rebecca Maria A. Ynares EXPLANATORY NOTE The conversion from Extension office to District office of the Land Transportation Office in the Municipality of Taytay, Rizal, represents a significant step towards enhancing accessibility and efficiency in providing essential services in the Ist District of Rizal. This strategic move will bridge the gap between the government’s services and the underserved communities. label: HB 11505
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (DOH) TO ENSURE THE AVAILABILITY OF MEDICINES AND PROCUREMENT OF MEDICAL EQUIPMENT IN ALL PUBLIC HOSPITALS THROUGH THE UTILIZATION OF THE MEDICAL ASSISTANCE TO INDIGENT AND FINANCIALLY INCAPACITATED PATIENTS (MAIFIP) FUND.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates the State to protect aud promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. Despite this constitutional guarantee, many public hospitals across the country continue to grapple with chronic shortages of essential medicines and a lack of basic diagnostic equipment. This reality places a heavy burden on indigent and financially incapacitated Filipinos who rely entirely on government healthcare facilities for their survival and well-being. This proposed measure seeks to address this critical gap by institutionalizing a proactive and sustainable procurement mechanism. It mandates the Department of Health (DOH) to ensure a continuous, adequate supply of essential medicines and guarantees that all public hospitals are equipped with baseline diagnostic tools like functional X-ray, ultrasound, and ECG machines. To ensure the viability of this mandate, the bill introduces a strategic funding approach. It maximizes the existing Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) Fund by explicitly earmarking at least twenty-five percent (25%) of its annual allocation exclusively for the procurement of essential medicines and medical equipment. By converting a portion of direct financial assistance into tangible, readily available healthcare resources at the point of care, the government can prevent stockouts, lower overall healthcare costs through bulk procurement, and provide immediate diagnostic and medical relief to marginalized patients. Furthermore, the bill institutes safeguards for transparency, efficient inventory management, and regular congressional reporting to ensure that the funds are utilized effectively and reach the Filipinos who need them most. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHILIY CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. label: HB 11506
title: AN ACT MANDATING TO PROFESSIONALIZE AND ELEVATE STERILE PROCESSING AS A CRITICAL COMPONENT OF HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND PATIENT SAFETY, AND DEVELOP THE INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS, RESOURCES AND BEST PRACTICES IN STERILIZATION SCIENCES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution declares that “The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them.” Central to this mandate is the guarantee of patient safety and the delivery of high-quality healthcare services in all medical facilities across the country. Despite advancements in medical technology, Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs) remain a persistent and life-threatening risk to patients. A critical vulnerability in infection control is the improper cleaning, decontamination, and sterilization of reusable medical devices and hospital workspaces. The emergence of highly resilient pathogens, such as prions, and the increasing complexity of surgical instruments necessitate a rigorous, scientifically backed approach to infection control that leaves no room for error. Currently, there is a need to professionalize and standardize stcrile processing as a distinct, highly regulated discipline within the Philippine healthcare system. The Central Sterile Services Department (CSSD) is the beating heart of hospital infection control, yet standardizing its operations to meet rigorous international benchmarks requires dedicated legislative backing. This bill seeks to elevate sterilization sciences by requiring all health care facilities, whether government or private, hospital or office-based clinic, to secure a specialized “Sterile Permit” prior to operation. To achieve this, the proposed measure: 1. Establishes Strict Regulatory Standards: Mandates health care facilities to submit detailed operational plans for decontamination, disinfection, and sterilization based on international best practices, including the Spaulding Classification System. 2. Empowers the Department of Health: Designates the Health Facilities and Services Regulatory Bureau (HFSRB) as the licensing agency tasked with inspecting facilities, issuing permits, monitoring HAI rates, and enforcing compliance. 3. Professionalizes the Workspace and Workforce: Requires dedicated architectural spaces for decontamination and _ sterile storage, specialized equipment like medical washers, strict use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and concrete protocols for process failures and occupational exposure. 4. Protects Healthcare Workers: Integrates occupational satety measures and transmission-based precautions to shield the personnel handling bioburden and hazardous materials daily. By treating sterile processing not merely as a hospital support service, but as a critical, highly specialized component of patient survival, we can drastically reduce preventable infections, protect our frontline healthcare workers, and align Philippine medical facilities with global health standards. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHI CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. label: HB 11507
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL HEALTHCARE SAFETY AND RELIABILITY SYSTEM, THEREBY CREATING THE NATIONAL HEALTHCARE SAFETY AUTHORITY (NHSA), AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates that “The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them.” While significant strides have been made to expand healthcare access across the country, access alone is insufficient if the care provided is unsafe. Preventable medical harm, adverse events, and systemic errors remain a significant but often underreported threat to public health and national development. Currently, the approach to medical errors in the healthcare sector is heavily punitive. This environment discourages healthcare workers from reporting near-misses and adverse events out of fear of administrative, civil, or criminal retaliation. Without transparent reporting, the healthcare system loses critical opportunities to analyze root causes, correct systemic flaws, and prevent future harm. The proposed bill mandates the creation of the National Healthcare Safety Authority (NHSA), an independent body attached to the Department of Health (DOH). The NHSA will be tasked with developing mandatory national patient safety standards, conducting safety audits, and establishing a confidential, non-punitive national incident reporting system. By legally protecting good-faith reporters, the State empowers healthcare professionals to become active partners in identifying systemic risks without the fear of unjust reprisal. Furthermore, this bill introduces a public Healthcare Safety Rating System to empower patients with transparent data regarding facility compliance and safety outcomes. It also mandates the integration of these safety metrics into PhilHealth’s accreditation and reimbursement systems, ensuring that public funds are directed toward institutions that prioritize high-quality, reliable care. Healthcare must be designed to heal, not harm. By establishing a dedicated authority and a proactive, evidence-based framework for patient safety, this legislation will strengthen public trust in our medical institutions and ensure that every Filipino receives the safe, high-quality healthcare they deserve. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHI CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. label: HB 11508
title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE TEACHING OF BASIC ROAD SAFETY AND COMPREHENSIVE DRIVERS' EDUCATION AS PART OF THE CURRICULUM OF THE K-12 PROGRAM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Road safety is a pressing public health and education concern. The World Health Organization’s Global Status Report on Road Safety (2023) highlights that road traffic injuries remain the leading cause of death among people aged 5 to 29 worldwide. In the Philippines, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported over 11,000 road crash fatalities in 2022, while Metro Manila alone recorded more than 65,000 road accidents in the same year. These alarming figures underscore the need for a preventive approach through early education. By integrating Basic Road Safety and Comprehensive Drivers’ Education into the K-12 curriculum, students will gain practical knowledge on traffic rules, pedestrian rights, commuter etiquette, and defensive driving principles. The inclusion of a Monitoring and Evaluation mechanism ensures accountability and continuous improvement, allowing policymakers to track outcomes such as reduced youth-related road incidents and improved safety awareness. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11509
title: AN ACT INCREASING CAMPUS SECURITY AND CRIME AWARENESS BY INSTALLING CLOSED-CIRCUIT TELEVISION (CCTV) CAMERAS AND WALK- THROUGH METAL DETECTORS IN ALL SCHOOLS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Schools are meant to be sanctuaries of learning where students, teachers, and school personnel can thrive without fear of violence or disruption. However, educational institutions remain vulnerable to various threats that may compromise safety, disrupt learning, and undermine the right of every learner to a secure educational environment. This bill seeks to strengthen and institutionalize school security nationwide by mandating the installation of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras and walk-through metal detectors in all schools. CCTV cameras will enhance monitoring, incident documentation, and crime prevention, while metal detectors will serve as a preventive measure against the entry of firearms, bladed weapons, and other dangerous objects into school premises. The measure also requires coordination among the Department of Education (DepEd), Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), Philippine National Police (PNP), and Local Government Units (LGUs) to ensure the proper deployment, maintenance, and operation of these security measures. Schools may likewise be prioritized based on risk assessment and other relevant security considerations. By institutionalizing these measures, the State affirms its responsibility to protect the lives and welfare of students, teachers, and school personnel. Ensuring a safe and secure school environment is essential to sustaining quality education and allowing learners to study, grow, and develop without fear. This legislation is a proactive and long-term measure to strengthen school safety and prevent violence and other security threats within educational institutions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11510
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SAFETY INTERNET EDUCATION PROGRAM IN THE CURRICULUM OF ALL ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In today’s hyperconnected world, the internet has become both a gateway to opportunity and a source of risk. The Philippines, with 90.8 million social media users as of January 2025—representing 78% of the population and averaging 3 hours and 32 minutes daily online use (DataReportal, We Are Social, Meltwater – Digital 2025 Report), ranks among the most active nations globally. This level of engagement underscores the urgent need for structured education on internet safety and media literacy. While young Filipinos are often described as “digital natives,” technical proficiency alone does not equate to digital literacy. Exposure to cyberbullying, misinformation, predatory grooming, and privacy breaches continues to rise, threatening both individual well-being and national resilience. This measure seeks to institutionalize an Internet Safety Education Program (ISEP) in all elementary and secondary schools. The program will equip teachers with professional training, empower students through peer-driven initiatives, and engage parents and communities in building a “360-degree” safety net. By embedding internet safety and media literacy into the curriculum, the bill ensures that the next generation is not only connected, but protected, informed, and responsible. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11511
title: AN ACT PROTECTING SENIOR CITIZENS FROM VARIOUS FORMS OF FRAUD THROUGH INFORMATION DISSEMINATION AND PROVIDING MECHANISMS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Senior citizens are increasingly vulnerable to fraud schemes that exploit mail, telecommunication, and online platforms. Common tactics such as phishing, text scams, and investment fraud not only cause financial losses but also bring emotional distress to the elderly. According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (2021 Financial Inclusion Survey), only 2% of respondents correctly answered all six basic financial literacy questions, showing limited awareness that makes seniors more prone to scams. The Anti-Money Laundering Council (2015 Strategic Analysis Report) further reported that cross-border investment fraud involving the Philippines amounted to ₱4.66 billion over five years, underscoring the scale of financial crimes that can affect vulnerable populations. This measure mandates the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), through local government units, to regularly disseminate information on mail, telemarketing, and internet fraud targeting senior citizens. It also requires coordination with agencies such as the BSP, SEC, NTC, DICT, and NBI to provide updated fraud prevention materials and reporting mechanisms. By institutionalizing education, awareness, and reporting systems, this bill ensures that senior citizens, their families, and caregivers are better equipped to recognize and avoid fraudulent schemes. It strengthens government accountability and affirms Congress’ commitment to safeguarding the welfare of the elderly in the digital age. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11512
title: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR CHILD DEVELOPMENT WORKERS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The early years of a child's life are critical to their physical, emotional, social, and cognitive development. During this period, Child Development Workers (CDWs) play a vital role in providing care, early education, protection, and developmental support to young children, particularly those in vulnerable and underserved communities. Despite the importance of their work, many CDWs continue to face challenges related to employment security, compensation, benefits, professional development, and access to adequate support and resources. These conditions may affect not only their welfare but also the quality and continuity of early childhood development services provided to children. CDWs perform responsibilities that require patience, dedication, specialized knowledge, and a deep commitment to the welfare of children. It is therefore necessary for the State to recognize their indispensable contribution to nation-building and ensure that they are provided with appropriate employment protection, fair compensation, benefits, training opportunities, and other forms of support. This measure seeks to establish a comprehensive framework for the protection and promotion of the rights and welfare of CDWs. It aims to strengthen their employment security, provide appropriate plantilla positions and compensation, promote continuing education and skills development, and ensure access to benefits and other privileges commensurate with the importance of their duties. By investing in the welfare and professional development of CDWs, the State likewise invests in the future of Filipino children. A well-supported and adequately protected workforce is essential to ensuring that every child receives quality care, early learning, and developmental support during the most formative years of life. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE OF MOBILE DEVICES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC GADGETS DURING CLASS HOURS FROM KINDERGARTEN TO SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL IN ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The widespread use of mobile devices and electronic gadgets among students has created both opportunities and challenges in the classroom. While these tools can support learning, their unregulated use during class hours has led to distractions, reduced academic performance, and even health concerns such as poor posture, sleep disorders, and vision problems. According to the 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), 41% of Filipino students are distracted by their own device use and 37% by other students using devices during math classes. Globally, countries such as France, Spain, China, and Australia have already adopted restrictions on smartphone use in schools, balancing technology with structured learning environments. Locally, the Department of Education (DepEd) has issued guidelines discouraging cellphone use in classrooms, but enforcement has been inconsistent. This bill institutionalizes a clear and enforceable policy across all public and private schools from Kindergarten to Senior High School, ensuring that classrooms remain focused and conducive to holistic development. The measure also provides for monitoring and compliance to ensure that schools adhere to the prohibition and that enforcement is consistent nationwide. By passing this Act, Congress affirms its duty to protect the physical, intellectual, and social well-being of Filipino learners. Limiting gadget use during class hours will foster discipline, improve focus, and promote healthier learning environments for the youth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11515
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING SPECIAL EDUCATION (SPED) CENTERS IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS, PROVIDING FUNDS FOR SPED TEACHER TRAINING, SPECIALIZATION, AND SUPPORT, AND EXPANDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11223 (UNIVERSAL HEALTH CARE ACT) AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11959 (REGIONAL SPECIALTY CENTERS ACT) TO INCLUDE COMPREHENSIVE DEVELOPMENTAL AND SPECIALIZED EDUCATIONAL SERVICES FOR CHILDREN WITH DISABILITIES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 11223, or the Universal Health Care (UHC) Act, and Republic Act No. 11959, or the Regional Specialty Centers Act, laid the foundation for an integrated and people-centered health system. However, gaps remain in addressing the developmental and educational needs of children with disabilities, particularly during early childhood and school age when timely intervention is most critical. Public schools are the most accessible institutions for Filipino families, yet the establishment of Special Education (SPED) Centers remains uneven and discretionary. The absence of a nationwide mandate and sustainable funding mechanism continues to limit access to properly resourced SPED services. Challenges such as the shortage of trained SPED teachers, limited specialization programs, inadequate compensation, and weak coordination between health and education systems persist. This measure seeks to institutionalize the establishment of SPED Centers in public elementary and secondary schools nationwide, prioritizing underserved and marginalized areas. It provides sustained funding for SPED teacher training, specialization, scholarships, and professional development, alongside additional compensation and incentives for SPED personnel and allied professionals. Further, the bill strengthens collaboration among the Department of Education, Department of Health, local government units, and barangays to integrate developmental and therapeutic services into the mandates of the UHC Act and the Regional Specialty Centers Act. Importantly, it also emphasizes parental involvement through consultations and school-based activities, ensuring that families are active partners in the education and holistic development of children with disabilities. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING GOVERNMENT SUPPORT FOR GIFTED AND TALENTED STUDENTS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Every Filipino learner possesses unique talents and abilities that, when properly nurtured, can contribute to the country's progress and development. Gifted and talented students require learning opportunities that go beyond the regular curriculum to fully develop their potential and prepare them to become future leaders, innovators, researchers, artists, and professionals. While existing programs provide support to some gifted learners, access to specialized education and development opportunities remains limited. There is a need to institutionalize a comprehensive support system that promotes academic excellence, creativity, innovation, and talent development while ensuring that deserving learners receive the guidance and opportunities they need to succeed. This measure seeks to establish a sustainable framework for identifying, developing, and supporting gifted and talented Filipino students through specialized educational programs, scholarships, mentorship, and research and innovation opportunities. By investing in their potential, the State strengthens the country's human capital and promotes long-term national development. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. label: HB 11517
title: AN ACT DECLARING JANUARY 9 OF EVERY YEAR A SPECIAL NONWORKING HOLIDAY IN THE ENTIRE COUNTRY TO COMMEMORATE THE FEAST OF THE BLACK NAZARENE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is the third-largest Catholic country in the world, with about 90 million Catholics, or more than 86 percent of the whole population1. Thus, the prominence of Catholic traditions and occasions in our nation. For more than 400 years, the historical statue of a dark-skinned Jesus Christ kneeling and carrying his cross has been a symbol of devotion, struggle, faith, and resilience for Filipino Catholics. The iconic statue, which is currently enshrined in the Minor Basilica of the Black Nazarene, more famously known as the Quiapo Church, has survived raging fires, earthquakes, floods due to numerous typhoons, and even bombings during the Second World War. On January 9 of every year, an estimated 18 million Filipinos from all around the country take part in the celebration of the Feast of the Black Nazarene. Devotees take part in an extraordinary procession popularly known as Traslación where they carry a replica of the iconic statue in a display of extreme religious devotion. This iconic religious procession does not happen in Manila alone but is also conducted in different locations nationwide, such as in Cagayan de Oro, Samar, and other provinces which feature their own version of the kneeling mulatto Nazarene. 1 Asia Society. “Religion in the Philippines.” https://asiasociety.org/education/religion-philippines (Accessed Online 9 September 2022) As a widely practiced religious event by many of our countrymen, it is imperative that January 9 of every year be declared as a special nonworking holiday to commemorate the Feast of the Black Nazarene. Furthermore, given the immense number of people involved in the celebration of this feast, and in order to ensure peace and order and the security and safety of participants and the general public, it is necessary to institutionalize the coordination of different government agencies and instrumentalities for smooth coordination between the public and private sectors, and the extension of necessary assistance in connection with the celebration of the Feast of the Black Nazarene. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11518
title: AN ACT DECLARING JULY 2 AS A SPECIAL NONWORKING HOLIDAY IN THE FIFTH DISTRICT OF QUEZON CITY TO BE KNOWN AS THE “ARAW NG NOVALICHES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Fifth District of Quezon City, or the Novaliches District, is one of the fastest developing areas in Quezon City. It has a size of 5,246.72 hectares, comprises 14 barangays, and its population has already reached the half- million mark. Located at the northernmost part of the city, Novaliches serves as the gateway to the metropolis of the big province of Bulacan and is also the geographical center of Quezon City, San Jose, and Caloocan City. The District also houses the La Mesa Dam Watershed, which supplies water to over 20 million residents of Metro Manila, and the La Mesa Eco-Park, an ecological nature reserve site that has become a favorite destination of city dwellers. Apart from its development potential, the Novaliches District has also been a witness to the Philippines’ rich history. The District is the home of the Katipunan Tree, which was a staging area of the Katipuneros during the Philippine Revolution. Under this old duhat tree, the Katipuneros held meetings and treated their wounded1. Additionally, it is in one of the barangays in Novaliches where Melchora Aquino, more popularly known as Tandang Sora, last stood her ground and was eventually arrested by the Guardia Civil on August 29, 1896, prior to her 1 Philippine News Agency. 2018. “Significance of the Katipunan Tree in Novaliches cited.” https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1038015 (Accessed Online 9 September 2022) exile to Guam. On July 2, 2012, a separate legislative district of Novaliches was reapportioned and created in Quezon City by virtue of Republic Act No. 10170. It is on this day that the newly established Fifth District of Quezon City was founded and continued to flourish and thrive with Hon. Alfred Vargas as its first-ever district representative in the Philippine Congress. This bill seeks to commemorate this historic event and declare July 2 of every year as “Araw ng Novaliches”, a special nonworking holiday in the Fifth District of Quezon City. It is the hope of this measure to instill a sense of pride and consciousness in all Novaleños. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. label: HB 11519
title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE PROVISION OF INFANT-FRIENDLY FACILITIES IN GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND MAJOR ESTABLISHMENTS IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Under Article XV of the 1987 Constitution, “the State recognizes the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation,” and shall defend “the right of children to assistance, including proper care and nutrition.” Consistent with this mandate, the State is duty-bound to create an enabling environment that supports parents and guardians in fulfilling their caregiving responsibilities. Recent national data underscore the urgency of this measure. The 2023 National Nutrition Survey (NNS) on Infant and Young Child Feeding shows that only about 50.4% of infants under six months are exclusively breastfed, while more than one-third (36%) of infants under six months are fed infant formula. Although the Philippines has made gains—exclusive breastfeeding rose from 35.9% in 2008 to 60.1% in 2021, and the 2023 NNS reports 50.4%— significant gaps remain in ensuring that caregivers can feed, change, and attend to infants safely and comfortably in public spaces. Existing laws already recognize the need for infant- and mother-friendly facilities. Republic Act No. 10028 (the “Expanded Breastfeeding Promotion Act of 2009”) mandates lactation stations in workplaces and public places, and Republic Act No. 11311 (the “Safe Mobility Act of 2019”) requires, among others, exclusive spaces for diaper-changing in land transport terminals. However, compliance remains uneven, and many government offices, commercial establishments, and food service venues still lack basic infant- friendly amenities—particularly diaper-changing stations accessible to both mothers and fathers, and child-friendly seating in dining areas. This bill, titled the “Infant-Friendly Facilities Act,” seeks to close these gaps by: • Requiring all government agencies and major establishments to provide at least one safe, sanitary, and convenient diaper-changing station on each floor, located in restrooms or in a common area accessible to both men and women; and • Mandating all food service establishments to provide child-friendly seats for their customers. The measure explicitly recognizes the growing role of Filipino fathers in childcare. Observations on the ground indicate that where diaper-changing tables exist, they are often installed only in women’s restrooms, effectively excluding fathers and other male caregivers. By ensuring gender-inclusive access, this bill promotes shared parental responsibility and removes practical barriers to family participation in public life. Through this simple but high-impact initiative, the State affirms the value of family quality time, supports optimal infant feeding and hygiene practices, and helps parents and guardians rear children in conditions conducive to health, dignity, and civic efficiency. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM’ D. label: HB 11520
title: AN ACT PRESCRIBING SCHOOL BUS SAFETY STANDARDS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The World Health Organization published those deaths due to traffic accidents in the Philippines has reached more than 13,000 in 2020. In Metro Manila alone, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) reported that there are 227 accidents per day that have put the lives of Filipino citizens in danger. Among the highly susceptible age groups to road accidents are children, who, with full-time face-to-face classes, now travel from their homes to their schools and back daily. As the State seeks to improve road safety and to protect pedestrians and motorists alike, this bill empowers the Department of Transportation to prescribe safety standards for school buses, set proficiency measures for school bus drivers, require the installation and use of seatbelts in school buses, and determine the practicability and feasibility of certain safety and access requirements for school buses. In ensuring that our students are safe from vehicular accidents, we are safeguarding the future development of our nation. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11521
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NURSING HOME FOR THE ABANDONED AND NEGLECTED SENIOR CITIZENS IN THE FIFTH DISTRICT OF QUEZON CITY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE As enshrined in the 1987 Constitution, “[t]he State shall adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development which shall endeavor to make essential goods, health and other social services available to all the people at affordable costs. There shall be priority for the needs of the underprivileged, sick, elderly, disabled, women and children.”1 “The family has the duty to care for its elderly members, but the State may also do so through just programs of social security.”2 The issues concerning rising incidents of abandonment of the elderly have been raised during this Representation’s consultation with the senior citizen sector. The problem is often attributed to the migration of young family workers, as well as the costs for elderly care being unaffordable and inaccessible to low-income households. Recognizing the rights of the elderly to life and protection, this bill seeks to establish a nursing home for the abandoned and neglected senior citizens in the Fifth District of Quezon City. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11522
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF CULTURE, ARTS, TOURISM AND HERITAGE COUNCILS IN EVERY PROVINCE OF THE COUNTRY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Nations that fail to learn from the past are bound to repeat their mistakes. For this reason, civilizations have long valued their art, heritage, and traditions. Our culture—expressed through our languages, cuisines, music, handicrafts, museums, and literature—shapes the shared identity of Filipinos today. When we enrich and celebrate our nation’s culture, we do more than honor those who came before us; we also equip and inspire the next generations of Filipinos to build a stronger future. The National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA) was created primarily for the purpose of developing, enhancing, and institutionalizing arts and culture programs in the country. However, it remains limited by its organizational nature – an agency based in the country’s capital with no bureaucratic network to expand its programs, projects, and activities up to the grassroots level. At best, it could only enter into memoranda of agreement with local government units to fund particular programs or projects with an arts and culture component. Animating the citizenry with the love and passion for their culture, arts, tourism, and heritage should be a shared responsibility of both the national and the local government units. Cultural programs at the provincial and city level must be complemented with the support of national agencies like the NCCA, the National Museum, the National Historic Commission of the Philippines, and stakeholders from the private sector. While a number of local government units have taken the initiative of organizing their own arts, culture, tourism, and heritage councils, a vast number of our provinces, which have rich untapped potential, remain in need of such support. In order to strengthen and institutionalize this necessary collaboration, this bill seeks to establish Culture, Arts, Tourism, and Heritage Councils in every province of the country. These opportunities to preserve, enhance, and develop local arts, culture, tourism, and heritage shall be a fitting gift for the next generation to appreciate and enjoy. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11523
title: AN ACT GRANTING A SPECIAL LEAVE OF ABSENCE OF FIFTEEN (15) DAYS A YEAR WITH FULL PAY TO ALL LEGITIMATE SPOUSES OF OVERSEAS WORKERS IN THE PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTORS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines ranks as one of the major labor-sending countries worldwide.1 With most Filipino migrants being parents, many children need to live away from their OFW parents for an extended period. With the proliferation of transnational families, studies have shown impacts on the mental and emotional health of children due to prolonged parent-child separations and the overall transnational living arrangements. 2 As the State recognizes the sanctity of family life, it strives to protect and strengthen the family as a basic autonomous social institution. In this endeavor, it shall also protect the well-being of left-behind families, especially children who are significant predictors of the development of a nation. With the limited number of days of leave for employees in the country, many OFWS whose spouses are employed in the Philippines do not get to spend a hundred percent of their vacation time with their family. 1 “Number of OWFs nearly fell nearly a fifth to 1.8M in 2020”. 2020 https://www.bworldonline.com/top-stories/2022/03/09/434745/number-of-ofws-fell-nearly-a-fifth- to-1-8m-in-2020/ Accessed Online on September 6, 2022 2 Graham, E and LP Jordan, 2011” Migrant Parents and the Psychological Well-being of Left-behind Children in Southeast Asia”. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3229683/ Accessed Online on 19, 2022 To ensure that OFWs’ rare vacations are well spent with their loved ones and to reinforce their familial ties, this bill aims to give every legitimate spouse of an OFW in the private and public sectors an additional special leave credit of fifteen (15) days a year with full pay, subject to certain qualifications. While the bill recognizes that mere additional days in the OFWs’ vacations would not compensate for the number of days that they are away from the family, the bill hopes that by providing the left-behind spouses additional days of leave, every transnational family will choose to strengthen the bond of their families, and be as involved as possible in their homes, as basic structures of the institution. It further hopes that the bill can help address the rising number of marriage dissolutions among transnational couples. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11524
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITY AFFAIRS OFFICES (PDAOs) IN ALL LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10070, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS AN ACT ESTABLISHING INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISM TO ENSURE THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROGRAMS AND SERVICES FOR PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES IN EVERY PROVINCE, CITY, AND MUNICIPALITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The objective of Republic Act No. 10070, which establishes an institutional mechanism to ensure the implementation of programs and services for Persons with Disabilities in every province, city, and municipality, is to ensure that relevant and sustainable programs for Persons with Disabilities are implemented at the local level. Under this law, specific roles ascribed to Local Government Units (LGUs) are initially delineated and coordinated within the operational framework of the Persons with Disability Affairs Office (PDAO). For provinces, cities, and 1st to 3rd class municipalities, PDAO shall be established through a Local Ordinance. In 4th to 6th class municipalities, a Focal Person (FP) performs the functions of PDAO, which is mandated through an Executive Order. However, thirteen years after RA No. 10070 was passed, over 50% of LGUs still have yet to establish their respective PDAO. Based on the recent record of the National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA), there are 739 PDAOs, or 43% compliance, as of February 2022. One of the primary reasons for non-compliance is funding constraints. Since the establishment of an office is subject to the availability of funds, it leaves discretion to LGUs to create their respective PDAO. Not to mention that the success of data gathering, a comprehensive database, further capacity building, information dissemination, and public awareness campaigns all remain to be seen. In addition, there is still a lack of updated and reliable official data on the actual number of people in the disability sector, which has a strong correlation to delays in policy implementation. Due to a lack of capacity and funding sources, many LGUs do not have a properly maintained database. This highlights the pressing need to capacitate and establish PDAOs in all LGUs tasked with having a uniform and standardized local database linked to a national Philippine Registry for Persons with Disability (PRPWD) system. In light of the implementation of the Mandanas ruling and in the continuous and overdue quest for improving local service delivery for the disability sector, the need to insist on the mandatory nature of the creation of PDAOs and appropriate funding source for the establishment and operations of PDAOs is timely and imperative. This measure proposes to amend RA No. 10070 specifically to: (1) ensure the mandatory creation and operation of PDAOs in all Local Government Units (LGUs); (2) provide a clear budget allocation for their establishment; (3) further strengthen their functions; (4) include a uniform and standardized local database linked to a national PRPWD system; (5) ensure mechanisms for data management, capacity building, and information dissemination about PDAOs; and (6) refine its fragmented institutional framework. After more than a decade since the enactment of RA No. 10070, policy interventions should be made to fully strengthen the implementation of RA No. 7277 and to ensure relevant and sustainable programs as well as active participation and empowerment of the disability sector in various undertakings and projects of LGUs. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “Family Tree Planting Act.” 29 SECTION. 2. Declaration of Policy. – It is the declared policy of the State to protect and advance the right of the Filipino people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature. Towards this end, the State shall promote and pursue reforestation programs and encourage tree planting as part of the family’s responsibility and legacy to protect the environment and conserve our natural resources for the future generation. 36 SECTION 3. Mandatory Tree Planting. – All parents residing in the Philippines whether legally married or not, shall be required to plant two (2) trees for every child to them. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 There are moments in a young person's life that mark the beginning of something new. Graduation is one of them. It is the day a student closes one chapter of life and begins to build a future of his or her own. 25 But while graduation marks the beginning of a new chapter for the student, it should also mark the beginning of something new for the country. 28 This proposed Graduation Legacy for Reforestation Act seeks to make tree planting a meaningful part of a student’s life. By requiring every graduating senior high school and college student to plant two trees, graduation becomes not only the beginning of a new chapter in a student's life, but also the beginning of a new life in the form of a tree. Years from now, the graduate may no longer remember the exact details of the ceremony, but the tree can remain as a living reminder of the day he or she began a new journey. 35 More than a graduation requirement, this measure seeks to give every graduating Filipino an opportunity to leave a living legacy. 38 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 40 41 42 REP. title: AN ACT PROVIDING STRONGER MEASURES FOR THE CONSERVATION AND PROTECTION OF WILDLIFE RESOURCES AND THEIR HABITATS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9147 OR THE “WILDLIFE RESOURCES CONSERVATION AND PROTECTION ACT” 26 27 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 30 SECTION 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “Revised Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act”. 33 SECTION. 2. Declaration of Policy. – It shall be the policy of the State to conserve and protect the country's wildlife resources and their habitats for sustainability and to promote ecological balance, enhance biological diversity, and ensure the provision of ecosystem services. In the pursuit of this policy, this Act shall have the following objectives: 39 (a) Regulate the collection, possession, use, and trade of wildlife, wildlife by- products and derivatives; 42 (b) Pursue, with due regard to the national interest, Philippine commitments to international conventions, treaties, and agreements on the protection of wildlife and their habitats, and on the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits from the lawful utilization of wildlife genetic resources; 47 (c) Initiate or support scientific studies on the conservation of biological diversity and sustainable utilization of wildlife resources. 50 (d) Promote full awareness and widest dissemination of policies on wildlife conservation and protection; and
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 The Philippines is a home to many unique and threatened wildlife species. However, wildlife continues to be threatened by illegal hunting, collection, transport, trade, and destruction of their habitats. While Republic Act No. 9147, or the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act, already provides the current basic law for the protection and conservation of wildlife, the changing nature and increasing scale of wildlife crimes require stronger penalties and better enforcement measures. 28 Hence, this proposed measure now seeks to strengthen and update the existing wildlife protection law, particularly by providing clearer and heavier penalties for serious violations. The bill also adds important enforcement measures, including presumptions in certain wildlife cases, stronger administrative powers to confiscate and forfeit wildlife and equipment used in violations, Wildlife Enforcement Agents, Wildlife Traffic Monitoring Units, and a wildlife law enforcement information system. 35 Through these measures, the bill seeks to provide stronger penalties, better enforcement, and greater government support for the protection and conservation of Philippine wildlife. 39 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 41 42 43 REP. title: AN ACT PROVIDING THE REGULATORY FRAMEWORK TO CONSERVE, PROTECT, RESTORE, AND SUSTAINABLY MANAGE PEATLANDS AND THEIR RESOURCES TO ENHANCE THE COUNTRY’S RESILIENCE TO CLIMATE CHANGE 25 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 28 SECTION 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “Peatland Conservation Act”. 31 SECTION 2. Declaration of Policy. - It is the policy of the State to promote the conservation, restoration, and sustainable development of the country’s peatland and peatland resources; enhance the resilience of the Filipino people towards climate change adaptation and mitigation, disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM) consistent with the principles of sustainable and inclusive economic development, poverty reduction, and biodiversity conservation, while advancing the right to a balanced and healthful ecology in harmony and rhythm of nature. 39 SEC. 3. Scope and Coverage. — This Act shall apply to all peatland and peatland resources nationwide within public and private lands. 42 SEC. 4. Definition of Terms. — As used in this Act: 44 (a) Adaptation refers to the adjustment in natural or human systems in response to actual or expected climatic stimuli or their effects, which moderates harm or exploits beneficial opportunities. 48 (b) Climate change refers to a change of climate which is attributed directly or indirectly to human activity that alters the composition of the global atmosphere and which is in addition to natural climate variability observed over comparable time periods. (c) Carbon sink refers to carbon reservoirs and conditions that take in and store more carbon than they release.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 The country’s peatlands are more than ecosystems to be protected. In July 2025, a peatland fire in the Agusan Marsh affected approximately 152 hectares. In 2026, another peatland fire burned for nearly two weeks, although the exact area affected had yet to be determined. These incidents show the continuing vulnerability of peatlands to fire, drainage, land conversion, and other human activities. 27 Despite their importance, peatlands have received less attention in environmental and climate policies compared with other ecosystems. Their value as carbon sinks, water regulators, and habitats for biodiversity is often overlooked. This measure aims to address this gap by providing specific rules for the protection, restoration, and proper management of peatlands. It provides for the mapping and monitoring of peatlands, the prevention and control of peatland fires, the restoration of damaged areas, and the regulation of activities such as drainage, conversion, reclamation, and peat extraction. 35 By protecting our peatlands, we protect one of nature’s most important stores of carbon. 37 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 39 40 41 REP. label: HB 11529
title: AN ACT ADOPTING INTEGRATED COASTAL MANAGEMENT AS A NATIONAL STRATEGY FOR THE HOLISTIC AND SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF COASTAL AND RELATED ECOSYSTEMS AND THE RESOURCES THEREIN FROM RIDGE-TO-REEF, ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL COASTAL GREENBELT ACTION PLAN, OTHER SUPPORTING MECHANISMS FOR IMPLEMENTATION, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR 28 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 31 CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS 34 35 SECTION 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “Integrated Coastal Management Act.” 38 SEC. 2. Policy Statement. – It shall be the policy of the State to ensure the sustainable management of the country’s coastal and marine environment and resources by looking at the interconnectivity of ecosystems from the watersheds to the coastal and marine areas. Towards this end, it shall adopt Integrated Coastal Management as a framework in regulating different human activities, restoring or rehabilitating ecosystems, and ensuring a multi-stakeholder participation and ridge-to- reef approach to ecosystem management, with due consideration to ecological connectivity and their impact on social and ecological systems. The framework shall support the country’s achievement of sustainable development, promotion of blue economy, food security, just transition to sustainable livelihood, poverty alleviation and its resilience and risk reduction, from sea-level rise and other coastal stresses, while respecting the traditional resource rights of indigenous peoples and gender equality. 52
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 The Philippines is, by geography and by livelihood, a nation deeply connected to the sea. With a coastline stretching approximately 36,289 kilometers, and more than 70 million Filipinos living in coastal areas, the health of our seas and coastlines is inseparable from the welfare of our people. 26 Our coastal ecosystems are likewise among the country's most valuable natural assets. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), as of 2025, the Philippines had approximately 2.15 million hectares of coastal resources, consisting of 1.34 million hectares of coral reefs (or at least 62.3%) 496,560 hectares of seagrass (or at least 23%) and seaweed areas, and 318,160 hectares of mangrove forests (or at least 14.8%) 33 Likewise, the PSA, in 2024, reported that the country's ocean-based industries generated ₱943.05 billion in 2023, contributing 3.9% to the country's Gross Domestic Product, with the ocean economy growing by 9.9% from the previous year. Ocean fishing alone accounted for 28.6% of the total ocean economy. 38 However, undeniably, these resources and industries face increasing, if not constant, pressures from development, pollution, climate change, habitat degradation, and poorly coordinated activities across political boundaries. 42 Hence, this proposed measure establishes Integrated Coastal Management (ICM) as a national strategy to coordinate national agencies, LGUs, communities, and other stakeholders in protecting and managing coastal resources. Aside from the creation of a National Coordinating Committee on ICM to lead this initiative, it also creates a National Coastal Greenbelt Action Plan to identify and restore vulnerable coastal areas, revert abandoned, undeveloped, and underutilized fishponds to mangroves, and remove illegal structures in protected areas. 3 In short, the proposed measure combines coordinated governance, science-based planning, and ecosystem restoration—including penalties for unauthorized structures and other violations within designated coastal greenbelts. By institutionalizing integrated coastal management, the measure aims to ensure that the Philippines' coastal resources remain productive and capable of sustaining communities and the economy for generations to come. 10 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 12 13 14 REP. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The absence of a cybersecurity law leaves a big gap in our legal framework, considering its importance in terms of national security and economic stability. Without a robust cybersecurity law, the country’s digital infrastructure remains highly vulnerable to increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. Earlier in 2024, the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) reported 282 cyberattacks against government organizations, 90% of which were resolved. In other cases, only about 76% of the early-stage hacking attempts were detected and neutralized by the agency’s National Security Operations Center.’ The absence of legislation on the identification, management, and regulation of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) creates a discernible blind spot. We cannot protect what we have not formally identified. This lack of a clear framework, combined with the poor coordination among CII and government agencies, means our most essential digital assets are at a high risk from uncoordinated and fragmented defense strategies. label: HB 11532
title: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 4 AND 12 OF THE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9514, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "FIRE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES OF 2008”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 9514, also known as the Fire Code of the Philippines of 2008, stands as a cornerstone of the nation's commitment to public safety, economic development, and the professionalization of the fire service. Since its enactment, the Code has provided a comprehensive framework for fire prevention, suppression, and the enforcement of safety standards across the country. However, with the rapid pace of urbanization, came the emergence of new economic and industrial zones, technological advancements, and the increasing complexity of fire hazards that have exposed regulatory gaps and operational challenges within the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) that must be inevitably addressed. This proposed measure seeks to update and strengthen the Fire Code to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness in safeguarding lives, property, and critical infrastructure. The bill expands the applicability of the law to encompass all persons, buildings, facilities, and structures-including those situated within economic zones, information technology parks, tourism zones, and other special entities, as well as vehicles, ships, petroleum installations, airports, and other high-risk areas. By closing existing regulatory gaps, the measure ensures that all sectors, particularly those with heightened fire risks, are subject to uniform and robust fire safety standards. Recognizing the need for adequate fiscal resources to fulfill its mandate, the bill likewise modernizes the funding mechanisms of the BFP by introducing new sources of income, including fees for the issuance of clearances assessed based on floor area and hazard level. These mechanisms are intended to support the continuous upgrading of the BFP's manpower, infrastructure, and equipment, enabling it to respond effectively to the evolving landscape of fire risks that BFP are currently facing. Given the wider scope that this measure seeks to achieve, this measure will invariably address the concerns on regulatory gaps in jurisdiction as well as to give the BFP sufficient autonomy to carry out its mandate independently and effectively. label: HB 11534
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SEGREGATED SHARP AH-COMPLIANT PROVIDENT SAVINGS AND HOUSING FINANCE WINDOW WITHIN THE HOME DEVELOPMENT MUTUAL FUND, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9679, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “HOME DEVELOPMENT MUTUAL FUND LAW OF 2009”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to establish a segregated Shari’ah-compliant provident savings and housing finance window under the Pag-IBIG Fund, amending for the purpose Republic Act (RA) No. 9679, otherwise known as the “Home Development Mutual Fund Law of 2009.” While the 1987 Constitution guarantees access to decent, affordable housing and promotes broad-based economic participation, structural gaps in the existing financial framework continue to limit access to provident savings and housing finance for members who adhere to non-interest-based financial principles. Under RA No. 9679, Pag-IBIG’s existing savings and financing mechanisms are principally structured around conventional, interest- bearing arrangements. Providing an alternative mechanism within the country’s principal public provident savings and housing finance institution can help address this gap and broaden financial inclusion. Republic Act No. 11439, or the “Islamic Banking Act,” recognizes Islamic banking and establishes a policy of tax neutrality between Islamic banking transactions and _ their conventional equivalents. However, RA No. 11439 principally governs banks and Islamic banking units, while Pag-IBIG is a government provident fund and housing finance institution. Express authority under RA No. 9679 is therefore necessary for the Fund to establish and sustainably operate a Shari ‘ah-compliant window suited to its mandate. To bridge this gap, this measure establishes a segregated operational and accounting window within Pag-IBIG. It authorizes the use of recognized, non-interest-based and asset- backed structures such as Mudarabah (profit-sharing), Murabahah (cost-plus sale), [jarah Muntahiyah bi al-Tamlik (lease-to-own), Musharakah Mutanagqisah (diminishing partnership), and Istisna (construction financing). The Window will be available to all qualified Pag-IBIG members on a voluntary basis, regardless of religion, while existing conventional savings and housing programs remain available and unaffected. Because certain Shari’ah-compliant structures may require the Fund to acquire, hold, lease, co-own, sell, or transfer property, the measure provides the incidental authority necessary to implement such transactions. It likewise requires appropriate segregation of assets, liabilities, income, and expenses, prudent standards for investment, liquidity, reserves, risk management, valuation, accounting, and internal controls, and policies that facilitate access by lower-income members while preserving the actuarial soundness and solvency of the Fund. To ensure Shari’ah compliance and protect members, the bill establishes a Shari’ah Advisory Committee to certify products, contracts, operational policies, and investments and to conduct compliance reviews. It also provides for appropriate disclosures, transparent pricing, fair treatment in matters such as default and early settlement, and accessible complaints mechanisms. The implementing rules will provide the detailed procedures for enrollment, participation, fund management, accounting, standard contracts. disclosures, compliance, and other operational matters. The measure likewise adopts the principle of tax neutrality so that additional transfers or documents required solely by an approved Shari ’ah-compliant financing structure do not result in more burdensome tax treatment than a functionally equivalent conventional transaction. This is intended to prevent structural double taxation while preserving existing tax laws and exemptions applicable to the Fund. By modernizing Pag-IBIG’s framework to accommodate voluntary, inclusive financing options, this bill expands member choice, strengthens financial inclusion and savings mobilization, and makes state-backed housing programs more accessible while safeguarding the provident character, financial stability, and public accountability of the Fund. For these reasons, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. o~ USTADZ YUSOP T. label: HB 11538
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE FULL ACCOUNTING OF ALL DISASTER-RELIEF AID OR DONATIONS RECEIVED BY THE PHILIPPINE GOVERNMENT FOR NATURAL AND HUMAN-INDUCED CALAMITIES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is among the countries with the highest number of calamities annually due to its geographic location along the Pacific Ring of Fire and the typhoon belt. The country is highly vulnerable to earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, typhoons, and severe flooding, which result in significant economic and humanitarian challenges each year. The Department of Science and Technology (DOST) reports that an average of 20 storms and typhoons enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility annually, while the country also experiences between 100 and 150 earthquakes of varying magnitudes. These recurring disasters necessitate robust mechanisms, including immediate relief efforts and long-term recovery programs. Over the years, the resilience of the Filipinos in facing these disasters has been strengthened by both local and international humanitarian aid. Donations in the form of cash and in-kind assistance from foreign governments, multilateral organizations, private institutions, and individuals have played a crucial role in the disaster relief and recovery efforts. However, concerns regarding the transparency, accountability, and proper utilization of these donations have persisted, raising questions about their efficient deployment to affected communities. The proposed Donation Transparency Act seeks to establish a legal framework for the full disclosure and accounting of all disaster-related aid received by the Philippine government. The measure aims to ensure that every donation- whether from foreign entities or domestic sources-is properly documented, tracked, and utilized strictly for its intended purposes. The bill is designed to enhance public trust in disaster-relief efforts by eliminating opportunities for mismanagement and corruption in the handling of donations. By ensuring that all aid is appropriately accounted for and disclosed, the measure promotes good governance, transparency, and efficient disaster response and recovery. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D. label: HB 11539
title: AN ACT ENSURING CHILD SUPPORT AND PENALIZING PARENTAL REFUSAL OR NEGLECT THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE As indicated in the 1987 Philippine Constitution, it is the duty of the State to defend a child’s right to assistance, including proper care and nutrition, and special protection from all forms of neglect, abuse, cruelty, exploitation, and other conditions prejudicial to their development. This is further enshrined in several laws, including the Presidential Decree No.603 or the Child and Youth Welfare Code, the Republic Act No. 7610 or the Special Protection of Children against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act, and the Republic Act No.9262 or the Anti-Violence against Women and Children Act. Every child, whether legitimate or illegitimate, has the right to receive support from their parents. Support, as defined in Section 194 of the Family Code of the Philippines, comprises everything indispensable for sustenance, dwelling, clothing, medical attendance, education, and transportation, in keeping with the financial capacity of the family. On February 18, 2022, the Philippines signed the Convention on the International Recovery of Child Support and Other Forms of Family Maintenance (known as the Child Support Convention), which was negotiated under the authority of the Hague Conference on Private International Law. This convention is but one of the affirmations of the country’s commitment to protecting children’s rights by ensuring child support. While the State has enacted and implemented several laws that protect a child’s right to support, these laws do not penalize parents who willfully fail to provide child support. This bill seeks to penalize any person who willfully fails to pay child support for at least one year or has an outstanding amount due of Fifty Thousand Pesos (Php 50,000.00) or more. It is the hope of this measure to protect children’s rights and ensure child support as they grow up by penalizing parental refusal or neglect of child support. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PATRICK MICHAEL “PM” D.
