label: HB 11596
title: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6552, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “REALTY INSTALLMENT BUYER ACT”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act (R.A) No. 6552, otherwise known as the “Realty Installment Buyer Act”, was enacted to protect buyers of real property on installment from onerous and oppressive conditions. Through the years, as real estate transactions and modes of payment have evolved, there is a need to further strengthen these safeguards and ensure that buyers are adequately protected from inequitable contractual practices. This bill seeks to strengthen the rights of buyers availing installment schemes by providing clearer rules on grace periods and cancellation of contracts, allowing restructuring or renegotiation in cases of financial difficulty, regulating penalties and additional interest on delayed payments, and ensuring the timely transfer and registration of ownership upon full payment. It likewise recognizes modern means of communication to ensure that buyers are properly informed before cancellation may take effect. These amendments seek to provide greater fairness, transparency, and certainty in real estate installment transactions, while maintaining reasonable protections for both buyers and sellers. In view of the foregoing, which is a counterpart measure of Senate Bill 2504, is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. label: HB 11598
title: AN ACT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill proposes the creation of an additional Regional Trial Court (RTC) branch to be stationed in the City of Carmona, with jurisdiction over the City of Carmona and the Municipality of General Mariano Alvarez (GMA). The historic progress of Carmona, following its cityhood, together with the continued development of GMA, has led to an anticipated rise in civil, criminal, and commercial litigation. To meet these growing demands and to ensure that justice remains accessible and efficient for the people of these rapidly advancing communities, the establishment of a new Regional Trial Court in Carmona is both timely and relevant. The creation of a new RTC branch is a necessary measure to strengthen the administration of justice in the area. By establishing a court dedicated to these communities, this measure will ease the load of existing dockets and help maintain the prompt disposition of cases. This is not merely an administrative adjustment but a substantive fulfillment of the constitutional mandate for the speedy disposition of cases under Article III, Section 16 of the Constitution. It gives life to the judiciary's core duty to resolve legal controversies promptly and ensures that the right to speedy justice becomes an accessible reality for every Carmonense and resident of GMA. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. ROY M. label: HB 11599
title: AN ACT PROMOTING EMPLOYMENT IN THE PROVINCES BY GRANTING A TAX CREDIT TO DOMESTIC AND FOREIGN ENTERPRISES THAT HIRE RESIDENTS OUTSIDE THE NATIONAL CAPITAL REGION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution affirms that the state shall promote full employment, afford full protection to labor and to promote equality of employment opportunities for all, and ordains that all regions of the country shall be given optimum opportunity to develop. Notwithstanding these constitutional mandates, economic activity remains heavily concentrated in the capital. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority, the NCR accounted for 31.2 percent of the national economy in 2024. This is despite of the fact that based on the 2020 Census of Population and Housing conducted by the same agency, the NCR is home to only 12.37 percent of the Philippine population. As a consequence, workers from the provinces are constrained to leave their homes and families in order to secure gainful employment. Existing fiscal incentives do not sufficiently address this disparity. According to the Fiscal Incentives Review Board, the incentives under the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended by Republic Act No. 11534 or the CREATE Act and Republic Act No. 12066 or the CREATE MORE Act, including the additional deduction of fifty percent (50%) on labor expense, are available only to registered business enterprises. No corresponding incentive is extended to the ordinary employer that establishes operations in the provinces and employs the residents thereof. The present measure seeks to fill this gap by attaching the incentive to the employment itself. The proposed measure is patterned after two (2) foreign models. The first is the Work Opportunity Tax Credit or WOTC under Section 51 of the United States Internal Revenue Code. According to the United States Internal Revenue Service, the WOTC, enacted in 1996, allows an employer to claim, as a credit against federal income tax, forty percent (40%) of up to US$6,000 of the first- year wages paid to a newly hired individual belonging to a targeted group, among them the residents of designated empowerment zones and rural renewal counties. From the WOTC, this bill adopts the form of the incentive, namely, a tax credit computed on the wages of a newly hired employee and granted by reason of the place of residence of such employee. The second is the Jobs Growth Incentive or JGI of Singapore. According to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, which administered the program, the government co-funded up to twenty- 1 five percent (25%) of the first S$5,000 of the gross monthly wages of every new local hire for twelve (12) months, and up to fifty percent (50%) in the case of mature workers, persons with disabilities and ex-offenders, on the condition that the local workforce of the employer had increased over its baseline. From the JGI, this bill adopts its safeguards, to wit: that the incentive be granted only for employment that is genuinely new, and that a higher rate be accorded to workers who face greater difficulty in securing employment. Accordingly, the proposed measure grants the employer a credit against income tax equivalent to twenty-five percent (25%) of the first-year wages of every resident of the provinces hired for work in the provinces, and forty percent (40%) in the case of priority hires, such as workers aged forty (40) years and above, persons with disabilities, and members of households covered by the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program. In order to protect government revenues, the credit shall be allowed only for employment in excess of the existing workforce of the employer, and only after the employee has rendered at least six (6) months of service. It bears stressing that both models were instituted as temporary measures. As stated by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, the JGI covered new hires from September 2020 to March 2023 only. According to the United States Department of Labor, the WOTC is authorized until 31 December 2025, and as reported by CPA Practice Advisor in January 2026, a measure for its further extension has been filed in both chambers of the United States Congress. Consistent therewith, the credit herein proposed shall apply only to hiring made within five (5) years from the effectivity of the Act, after which Congress shall review its results. The creation of employment in the provinces will keep Filipino families together and retain wages within the local economy. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Human Settlements Adjudication Commission (HSAC) plays a vital role in protecting the rights and interests of homebuyers, homeowners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders in the housing and real estate sector. As the principal adjudicatory body for disputes involving subdivision and condominium developments, homeowners associations, and related housing matters, the effective and timely exercise of its jurisdiction is essential to ensuring accessible and meaningful remedies for the public. Republic Act No. 11201, otherwise known as the "Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development Act," established the HSAC and defined its powers, jurisdiction, and organizational structure. However, the increasing complexity and volume of housing and real estate disputes necessitate further strengthening of the Commission's institutional and adjudicatory framework. This measure seeks to enhance the HSAC's organizational structure, personnel complement, jurisdiction, adjudicatory mechanisms, and enforcement powers to enable it to discharge its mandate more efficiently and effectively. It likewise strengthens the Commission's legal, administrative, technical, and operational support through additional personnel and appropriate organizational units. label: HB 11603
title: AN ACT PROVIDING A HEALTH CARE PROGRAM FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE A public school cannot deliver quality education without teachers who are physically and mentally capable of performing their duties. Teachers do more than teach in the classroom. They also monitor student progress, provide feedback, prepare reports, participate in school activities, and respond to the different needs of their learners. Public school teachers therefore require a dependable health-care arrangement that complements existing government benefits. Access to a Healthcare Maintenance Organization can help teachers obtain preventive, rehabilitative, and other necessary medical services while reducing delays and personal expenses. Moreover, an HMO incentive has higher benefit limits, consultations, hospital coverage for pre-existing conditions, and more access to accredited hospitals nationwide. This bill seeks to establish a health-care program for all public school teachers under the Department of Education. It directs the Department to procure, through competitive bidding, a contract with a duly recognized Healthcare Maintenance Organization accepted by hospitals throughout the country. The bill further provides that the amount necessary for its implementation shall be included in the General Appropriations Act for the year following its approval. By protecting the health of teachers, the State also protects the continuity and quality of public education. ATTY. MIRO S. label: HB 11604
title: AN ACT PENALIZING ACTS OF ROAD RAGE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE There has been an alarming surge in road rage incidents across the country in recent years. Reports of motorists engaging in hostile behavior, including shouting, cursing, using foul or degrading language, issuing threats or engaging in intimidation, have become all too common. In many instances, road rage has escalated into physical assaults or attempts to inflict harm. Some cases have even resulted in serious injuries or fatalities due to the use of firearms and other weapons. The increasing frequency and severity of road rage incidents demand decisive government intervention. At present, there is a glaring lack of specific legislation that categorically defines and penalizes road rage as a distinct and punishable offense. This legislative gap leaves road users vulnerable to the hostile and often violent actions of aggressive drivers. This proposed bill seeks to define and penalize acts of road rage to safeguard all road users from harassment, intimidation, physical harm, or loss of life. Beyond punitive measures, this bill also emphasizes the importance of prevention and education. It mandates the implementation of programs that promote responsible road behavior and foster a culture of respect and accountability among motorists. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11605
title: AN ACT DEFINING DEFENSIVE DRIVING AND PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF MOTOR VEHICLE DRIVERS INVOLVED IN A ROAD CRASH
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In the Philippines, there is a recurring and problematic practice where drivers involved in vehicular incidents—even those who are clearly not at fault—are subjected to automatic arrest and detention. This often happens because law enforcement perceives any involvement in an accident, particularly one resulting in injury or death, as presumptive proof of criminal negligence. This "automatic detention" culture places an unfair burden on individuals who were merely reacting to sudden and unavoidable hazards. This bill seeks to address this by: 1. Institutionalizing "Defensive Driving": Recognizing that a driver’s attempt to avoid harm through reasonable maneuvers (such as braking, swerving, or stopping) is a crucial factual consideration. 2. Protecting Due Process: Mandating that law enforcement and prosecutors evaluate the full circumstances of an incident—including dashcam footage, witness accounts, and environmental factors—before deciding to detain a driver or proceed with criminal charges. 3. Ending Automatic Detention: Ensuring that if the evidence suggests the driver acted defensively and reasonably, the driver is not subject to unnecessary detention while the case is being investigated. It encourages the use of regular preliminary investigations for complex cases rather than immediate inquests that keep drivers in custody. This measure does not provide immunity. If further investigation proves that the driver was, in fact, negligent, they will remain liable under the law. However, it ensures that the Philippine justice system distinguishes between those who cause accidents through true recklessness and those who are victims of unfortunate circumstances. By requiring an objective, evidence-based approach to vehicular incidents, this bill upholds the constitutional right to due process and prevents the waste of public resources on the detention of innocent citizens. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11606
title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE PERIOD OF VALIDITY OF REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES OF MOTOR VEHICLES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 14 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “LAND TRANSPORTATION AND TRAFFIC CODE”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Motor vehicle drivers and riders are essential to Philippine society. They transport people, goods, and services, helping support the country’s economy and everyday life. This includes jeepney and bus drivers, delivery riders, and private vehicle owners. However, they face many challenges, such as rising fuel prices, expensive vehicle maintenance, and the costs and inconvenience of complying with government requirements. One major burden is the yearly renewal of motor vehicle registration. For those who depend on their vehicles for their livelihood, this process takes time, money, and effort. This bill proposes extending the validity of motor vehicle registrations. The measure would provide financial and practical relief to millions of Filipino drivers and riders by reducing the need for annual renewal. It recognizes their important contribution and seeks to lessen the difficulties they face. Furthermore, recognizing that technological advances have made newer vehicles more reliable, consequently, extended registration periods may be warranted beyond the three-year exemption. The extension would also benefit the government. It would reduce the workload of the Land Transportation Office (LTO) and allow its personnel to focus on other important services and improvements. It could also help reduce long lines and overcrowding in LTO offices and make the registration process more efficient. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ASSISTANCE TO INDIVIDUALS IN CRISIS SITUATION (AICS) PROGRAM UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT (DSWD), PROVIDING FUNDING, ESTABLISHING OVERSIGHT AND IMPLEMENTING RULES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Many individuals and families affected by sudden, severe, or unforeseen events—medical emergencies, accidents, displacement, death in the family, trafficking, and other crisis situations—often require immediate financial, material, medical, psychological, and transport support to stabilize their circumstances. While AICS interventions have been provided on an ad hoc basis, the absence of a statutory mandate limits predictable funding, standardization of eligibility and benefits, and coordinated delivery across national and local levels. Institutionalizing AICS will ensure timely, standardized, and accountable assistance to those in urgent need, with priority given to the poor, vulnerable, marginalized, and disadvantaged The AICS program is hereby institutionalized to provide immediate and timely assistance to individuals and families assessed to be experiencing crises or extreme difficult situations needing financial or material support. The AICS programs serves as a stop-gap measure to support the recovery of individuals and families suffering from unexpected life events or crises. In addition to the usual assistance under the program, there is a need to expand the scope of assistance to include Fuel Subsidy allowance. A targeted fuel subsidy for motorists facing crisis situations is warranted to ensure immediate mobility and access to essential services during emergencies. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11608
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA OF MOTORCYCLE TAXI RIDERS AND DELIVERY RIDERS, PROMOTING THEIR RIGHTS AND WELFARE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Motorcycle delivery riders and drivers play a vital role in the Philippines’ transportation, delivery, and digital-economy sectors. Through their daily work, they transport passengers and deliver food, medicine, documents, and other essential goods to individuals, households, and businesses throughout the country. Their services help sustain commerce, support local businesses, improve access to essential products, and provide convenience to the public. Despite their important contribution, many riders and drivers continue to face difficult and uncertain working conditions. They may also be exposed to road accidents, harassment, discrimination, and other forms of abuse. Many also lack sufficient access to social protection, health and accident insurance, emergency assistance, and other employment-related benefits. These conditions demonstrate the need for a clear legal framework that recognizes the essential role of motorcycle delivery riders and drivers and protects them from exploitation and unfair treatment. This bill seeks to establish their rights in fulfillment of the State’s constitutional duty to protect labor, promote social justice, and ensure decent and humane working conditions. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11609
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY ALLOCATION OF PARKING SPACES FOR MOTORCYCLES AND A GRACE PERIOD FOR DELIVERY SERVICE VEHICLES IN ALL PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ESTABLISHMENTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Motorcycle use in the Philippines has increased because it provides affordable and convenient transportation. At the same time, delivery riders have become essential in bringing goods, food, and services to the public. However, many motorcycle riders and delivery personnel have difficulty finding proper parking. Some establishments do not have designated motorcycle parking, while others charge fees even when delivery riders stay only briefly to pick up or deliver orders. This proposed law requires commercial, office, and public establishments to provide designated parking spaces for motorcycles. It also grants delivery riders a reasonable grace period during which they may wait or complete their transactions without being charged parking fees or penalties. This measure promotes fair access to parking facilities and recognizes the important role of delivery riders in the Philippine economy. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11610
title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11235, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “MOTORCYCLE CRIME PREVENTION ACT”, AS AMENDED, TO INCLUDE ALL MOTOR VEHICLES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Republic Act No. 11235, or the Motorcycle Crime Prevention Act, has been an important tool in addressing crimes involving motorcycles. The original law, enacted in 2019, sought to reduce the occurrence of crimes like robbery, drive-by shootings, and other violent acts committed by individuals using motorcycles as a means of escape or a weapon. On May 2025, Republic Act No. 12209 was enacted which seeks to rationalize the safety features and penalties relative to the operation of motorcycles. However, while the law successfully targets crimes committed by motorcycle riders, there has been a noticeable gap in the law's application to other types of motor vehicles which have also been increasingly used for criminal activities, such as cars, vans, and other forms of transport. In light of this, it is imperative that the law be expanded to cover not only motorcycles but also other types of motor vehicles, thereby ensuring a more comprehensive approach to crime prevention and improving public safety across all forms of transportation. The Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Act aims to amend Republic Act No. 11235 by expanding its coverage to include all motor vehicles, not just motorcycles. This bill seeks to strengthen the existing legal framework to ensure that law enforcement agencies have the tools necessary to track and prevent the use of motor vehicles in the commission of crimes. The inclusion of motor vehicles within the law’s coverage will provide a more comprehensive solution to crimes that pose significant threats to the safety and security of all Filipinos. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11611
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PUBLIC TRANSPORT SAFETY MONITORING SYSTEM AND PROVIDING FOR THE USE OF SAFETY MONITORING AND EMERGENCY RESPONSNE TECHNOLOGY IN PUBLIC TRANSPORT VEHICLES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Millions of Filipinos depend on public transportation each day. Accordingly, passengers should be assured of safe travel and have timely access to assistance in the event of accidents, crimes, harassment, or other emergencies. Technology such as GPS, CCTV, dashcams and emergency alert systems can help government agencies and transport operators respond quickly to incidents and investigate complaints. However, these technologies must be part of a coordinated system rather than being installed merely as standalone devices. This bill therefore seeks to establish a Public Transport Safety Monitoring System that will allow government to monitor public transport vehicles, receive emergency alerts, preserve relevant recordings, and coordinate with law enforcement and emergency responders. The measure also protects the privacy of passengers, drivers and operators by requiring compliance with existing data privacy laws. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11612
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE INSTALLATION OF TIMERS IN TRAFFIC LIGHTS AND PEDESTRIAN LIGHTS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Traffic congestion and road accidents remain significant concerns in both urban and rural areas. Motorists and pedestrians often experience uncertainty when approaching intersections because they cannot determine how much time remains before a traffic or pedestrian signal changes. This may result in sudden stops, rushed crossings, traffic violations, and avoidable accidents. The installation of countdown timers on traffic lights and pedestrian lights will provide motorists and pedestrians with clear and timely information regarding the remaining duration of each signal. By displaying the time left before a signal changes, timers can promote safer decision-making, improve compliance with traffic rules, reduce sudden movements at intersections, and contribute to the smoother flow of traffic. Through this measure, the State can promote safer roads, improve traffic management, protect pedestrians and motorists, and reduce congestion through the use of simple and effective technology. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. RAMON RODRIGO L. label: HB 11613
title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AT LEAST ONE (1) LEVEL II HOSPITAL IN EVERY PROVINCE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 15, Article II of the Constitution states that "The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them." Furthermore, it provides that the State shall adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development which shall endeavor to make essential goods, health and other social services available to all the people at affordable cost. The Philippines is composed of 82 provinces, each serving as an important geographic and administrative unit in the delivery of basic services. Among these essential services is healthcare, making it vital to ensure that adequate and appropriate health services are available within these geographic areas and accessible to communities across the country. However, access to hospital care remains uneven to date. While several provinces already have hospitals capable of providing Level II services, such facilities are not uniformly available throughout the country. The Department of Health has recognized this disparity, with former Health Secretary Teodoro J. Herbosa reporting that 40 of the country’s 82 provinces did not have a DOH hospital, with residents in some areas having to travel three to four hours to another city or province to access a DOH facility and government-supported medical services'. Such barrier can make it more difficult for patients to benefit from government programs such as the Zero Balance Billing policy, particularly when access to govermment hospitals require considerable travel. ! Villanueva, G. (2025, September 10). DOH says lack of hospitals, beds hinder access to zero balance billing. Philippine Daily Inquirer. This challenge is particularly significant and visible for communities outside highly urbanized cities. Patients requiring healthcare services beyond those available at primary or Level I facilities may have to travel to another province or highly urbanized city, or seek treatment from private hospitals, resulting in additional costs that can be particularly burdensome for those with limited financial means. Strengthening hospital capacity at the provincial level is therefore necessary to bring more comprehensive medical care closer to communities and reduce the geographic and financial barriers to accessing appropriate hospital services. This proposed measure seeks to institutionalize the establishment of at least one (1) Level II government hospital in every province of the Philippines. Its objective is to establish a uniform national framework that ensures every province has access to enhanced and comprehensive hospital care. It likewise seeks to advance the policy of the Department of Health pursuant to the Republic Act No. 11223, or the Universal Health Care (UHC) Act, whereby all provinces should have at least one Level II hospital, with the vision of establishing an equitable health system where every Filipino can access appropriate and quality healthcare where they reside. The measure further aims to upgrade, expand, modernize, or, where feasible, convert existing provincial DOH primary care facilities and Level I hospitals into Level II hospitals. By ensuring that every province has access to at least one (1) Level II government hospital, the State can strengthen the country’s healthcare system, facilitate patients’ access to government health programs such as the Zero Balance Billing policy, and advanee its constitutional mandate to make essential health services accessible and affordable to all. label: HB 11614
title: AN ACT PENALIZING SELECTIVE, DISCRETIONARY, AND DISCRIMINATORY ACTS IN THE DELIVERY OF SOCIAL PROTECTION PROGRAMS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Section 1, Article XI of the 1987 Constitution states that “[p]ublic office is a public trust. Every government worker is expected to serve the Filipino people with utmost integrity, efficiency, and fairness. However, the persistent gap between this ideal situation and the reality on the ground is apparent. Across the country, access to social assistance, from emergency relief and medical subsidies to educational aid and cash transfers, is too often derailed by favoritism, politics, and local bias. During times of crisis, the local distribution of aid frequently devolves into a system of "palakasan." Some barangays are selective in their distribution of relief goods, requiring the presentation of voter’s IDs or prioritizing their friends and relatives.’ Deserving, low-income families get left off the master lists simply because they lack the right connections or fall on the wrong side of local political lines. Meanwhile, those with close ties to officials skip the line, turning basic public services into political favors. This bill seeks to tackle the issue of discrepancy head-on by creating clear, enforceable penalties for any government worker who uses discretion to favor, exclude, or discriminate against beneficiaries. By removing personal bias from the distribution process and enforcing strict accountability, this measure ensures that government aid finally reaches every qualified Filipino fairly, impartially, and without condition. label: HB 11615
title: AN ACT PROMOTING INCLUSIVE AND SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTIVITY GROWTH, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6971, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PRODUCTIVITY INCENTIVES ACT OF 1990
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This bill seeks to promote gainful employment, improve working conditions, maintain industrial peace and harmony, and promote the principle of partnership and shared responsibility between labor and management, Mandatory wage increase without corresponding increases in the productivity of the workers will only result in higher inflation rate as firms and businesses would pass on the cost of the wage increments to the cost of the product or the service being produced or provided, thus wiping out the value of wage increases almost as soon as they are mandated. The continuing oil crisis triggers a domino effect that excessively impacts the poor and low-income households that spend most of their income on immediate survival needs and live without savings to absorb sudden price hikes. By recognizing the right of labor to its just share in the fruits of production, and the right of business enterprises to reasonable returns on investments and for growth and expansion, this proposed measure aims to provide incentives to both labor and management for undertaking productivity improvement programs, as it also grants tax incentives to business enterprises that adopt the program with a special deduction from gross income equivalent to 50% of the total productivity incentives given to employees, and to business enterprises that provide training and special studies to employees. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ~~ Keith Micah “Atty. Mike” D.L. title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM TO ACHIEVE EFFICIENCY AND EQUITY, AND TO IMPROVE PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11223, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "UNIVERSAL HEALTH CARE ACT” 26 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 29 SECTION 1. Section 4 of Republic Act No. 11223, otherwise known as the “Universal Health Care Act” is hereby amended to read as follows: 32 “SEC. 4. Definition of Terms. – As used in this Act: 34 (a) Abuse of authority - xxx; 36 (b) Amenities - xxx; 38 (c) Basic or ward accommodation - xxx; 40 (d) Co-insurance - xxx; 42 (e) Co-payment - xxx; 44 (F) DEPENDENTS OF A MEMBER REFER TO: 46 1) THE LEGITIMATE SPOUSE WHO IS NOT A MEMBER; 48 2) THE TWENTY-THREE (23) YEARS OF AGE AND BELOW WHO ARE UNMARRIED AND UNEMPLOYED, LEGITIMATE, LEGITIMATED, ILLEGITIMATE, ACKNOWLEDGED CHILDREN AS APPEARING IN THE BIRTH CERTIFICATE, LEGALLY ADOPTED, OR STEPCHILDREN, OR CHILDREN OF SOLO AND FOSTER PARENTS.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 There are moments when the promise of universal healthcare becomes most meaningful. 24 It is when a Filipino can seek medical care without having to choose between treatment and the family’s daily needs, when contributions to the health system translate into substantial benefits that address not only the most serious illnesses but also the broader healthcare needs, and when public health resources are managed with the highest degree of efficiency that actually translates to concrete benefits that will bring smiles to families. 31 Republic Act No. 11223, or the Universal Health Care Act, established the framework for providing every Filipino with comprehensive and affordable healthcare. However, aside from the debatable claim that healthcare under the law is truly “affordable,”, recent developments have shown that the implementation of this framework still requires clearer safeguards and stronger mechanisms. The Supreme Court's 2025 ruling on the transfer of PhilHealth funds underscored the need to protect the Corporation's reserves and ensure that excess funds are used consistently with the purposes expressly provided under the UHC Act. Concerns raised during the 2026 budget deliberations likewise highlighted questions surrounding the adequacy, release, and proper use of government funds intended for PhilHealth and universal healthcare. 42 Hence, this proposed measure seeks to translate these reforms into concrete benefits for Filipino patients and PhilHealth members. Excess PhilHealth reserves would be directed toward expanding benefits and reducing premium contribution rates, while future contribution rates would be based on updated actuarial assessments and subjected to legislative review. For migrant workers, the bill provides a clearer and more equitable arrangement for premium contributions and protects them from having unpaid contributions become a barrier upon their return to the country. 3 This proposed measure likewise seeks to make every peso contributed to PhilHealth work harder by allowing cost-effective public, private, and public-private arrangements for benefit delivery, while strengthening the Special Health Fund so that PhilHealth reimbursements can be used to improve local health facilities. 8 Moreover, this measure strengthens the systems that support universal healthcare. A national UHC Coordinating Council would bring together the agencies responsible for health, finance, labor, social welfare, education, technology, and local governance; independent external audits would supplement existing government oversight; and specific penalties would apply to the misuse of funds intended for healthcare. 14 In practical terms, these reforms seek to ensure that the money contributed by Filipinos and the resources appropriated for healthcare do not merely remain as funds on paper, but are ultimately converted into better coverage, more responsive health services, stronger local facilities, and greater financial protection for patients and their families. 19 With this, the promise of universal healthcare can become more tangible in the everyday lives of Filipinos. Under the current system, ordinary Filipinos like Juan and Maria may still find themselves forced to choose between paying a hospital bill and keeping the savings they need for their children’s education, daily necessities, and their family’s future, despite paying high contributions. 25 However, under this stronger healthcare system envisioned by this measure, Juan and Maria can face that moment differently. Their PhilHealth contributions can be kept at a level that is actuarially justified and corresponds to the realities of increasing costs of living, while ensuring that those contributions translate into more substantial benefits when illness strikes. Moreover, PhilHealth can now cover a greater share of their hospital expenses, leaving them with a smaller balance to pay and reducing the need to exhaust the savings they had set aside for their children’s education, a better home, or simply a more secure and comfortable life. 34 For families like Juan and Maria’s, this is what universal healthcare should ultimately feel like, that is, contributing fairly and receiving meaningful protection in return, knowing that when illness comes, they can receive the care they need without having to sacrifice the future they have worked so hard to build. 39 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 41 42 43 REP. title: AN ACT CREATING A SYSTEM OF PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A PEOPLE'S COUNCIL IN EVERY LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT, PRESCRIBING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND PROVIDING FOR ITS PARTICIPATION IN THE LOCAL SANGGUNIAN AND LOCAL BOARDS, COUNCILS, COMMITTEES, TASK FORCES OR SIMILAR WORK GROUPS 28 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 31 SECTION 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the "People Empowerment Act.” 34 SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. – It is hereby declared a policy of the State to ensure participation of citizens in all avenues of local governance. Likewise, the State acknowledges the value of creating a mechanism where its citizens' views and opinions in different areas of governance may be heard and considered. Furthermore, pursuant to Article II, Section 23 of the Constitution, the State recognizes the value of non- government, community-based, or sectoral organizations in nation building and in creating an avenue to ensure their growth and development. The State also recognizes that the partnership with people's organizations (POs) and civil society organizations (CSOs) will spur development in local communities as envisioned by the Local Government Code of 1991. 45 SEC. 3. Definition of Terms. – As used in this Act: 47 (a) Civil society organization refers to any organized citizens' group including POs and non-government organizations such as community groups, labor unions, indigenous groups, charitable organizations, faith-based organizations, professional associations, and foundations; 52 (b) Local sanggunian refers to the local legislative body specifically the
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 Meaningful participation of citizens and civil society organizations in local governance is essential to responsive, transparent, and accountable government. While existing laws recognize the role of civil society in local development, there remains a need for a clearer and more consistent mechanism through which organized citizens can participate in local decision-making and work with local governments. 27 Hence, this bill seeks to address this need by establishing a People’s Council in every local government unit and providing a clear framework for the accreditation, organization, recognition, and participation of civil society organizations in local governance. 32 The measure provides People’s Councils with a formal role in local planning, policy- making, program implementation and evaluation, as well as representation in local boards, councils, committees, task forces, and other similar bodies. The objective of this measure is clear – that is, to ensure that local policies and programs reflect the lived experiences of the communities they serve. 38 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 40 41 42 REP. title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PROCEDURE FOR REGISTRATION OF VOTERS AND ADOPTING A SYSTEM OF ONLINE REGISTRATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 2, 3, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 22, 23, 24, 29, 32, 33 AND 45 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8189, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “VOTER’S REGISTRATION ACT OF 1996” 26 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 29 SECTION 1. Short Title. – Section 2 of Republic Act No. 8189, otherwise known as “The Voter’s Registration Act of 1996”, is hereby amended to read as follows: 32 “SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. - It is the policy of the State to [systematize the present method of registration in order to establish a clean, complete, permanent, and updated list of voters] ESTABLISH A SYSTEM OF REGISTRATION THAT ENSURES AND GUARANTEES A CLEAN, COMPLETE, PERMANENT, AND UPDATED LIST OF VOTERS. TO ENCOURAGE AND ENSURE A CONTINUING SYSTEM OF VOTER REGISTRATION, THE STATE SHALL ADOPT AND MAKE USE OF TECHNOLOGIES THAT SHALL FACILITATE AND ALLOW THE AUTOMATED AND ONLINE REGISTRATION OF VOTERS AS AN OPTION, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE INTEGRITY, COMPLETENESS, AND ACCURACY OF THE LIST OF VOTERS.” 44 SECTION 2. Section 3 of the same Act is hereby amended to read as follows: 46 “SEC. 3. Definition of Terms. – As used in is Act: 48 (a) Registration refers to the act of accomplishing and filing of a sworn application for registration by a qualified voter ONLINE OR before the election officer of the city or municipality wherein [he] THE APPLICANT resides and including the same in the book of registered voters upon approval by the
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 Voter registration remains largely a manual and paper-based process, despite the availability of technology that could make registration more accessible, efficient, and convenient for the public. 25 During the voter registration period that ran from October 20, 2025 to May 18, 2026, the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) processed 5,470,889 applications nationwide, including applications for new registration, transfer of registration, reactivation, and correction of entries. 30 This figure alone represents an overwhelming burden not only on our hardworking COMELEC personnel, but also raises a more important concern. Behind these millions of applications may be qualified Filipinos who remain unregistered because the existing manual process is difficult, time-consuming, or otherwise inaccessible to them. 35 The existing framework under Republic Act No. 8189, otherwise known as the “Voter’s Registration Act of 1996,” was established at a time when electronic registration, digital records, and secure online transactions were not yet part of ordinary government services. The law therefore needs to be updated to respond to the realities of modern voter registration. 41 Hence, this proposed measure seeks to modernize the voter registration system without compromising the integrity and accuracy of the voters’ list. 44 First, the bill allows online voter registration through the official website of the COMELEC as another option based the manual one. Second, the bill addresses a practical difficulty faced by voters who may be qualified to register but lack conventional documents proving their residence. It now allows alternative forms of proof of residence, including utility bills, certifications from landlords or lessors, and affidavits of qualified disinterested witnesses. These are more practical, yet the bill also proposes safeguards against fraudulent registration. 4 Further, the bill strengthens coordination between the COMELEC and the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) for the identification and cancellation of the registration records of deceased voters. This is intended to help prevent outdated records from remaining in the voters’ list. 9 This proposed bill recognizes that voter registration should not be made unnecessarily difficult by outdated procedures, nor should modernization come at the expense of electoral integrity. The objective is to modernize the voter registration system and make the exercise of the right to vote a little less burdensome to qualified Filipinos, so that more citizens are encouraged and able to register and participate in elections. 15 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 17 18 19 REP. title: AN ACT RENAMING THE LITERACY COORDINATING COUNCIL TO NATIONAL LITERACY COUNCIL, STRENGTHENING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, EXPANDING ITS MEMBERSHIP STRUCTURE AND SUPPORT MECHANISMS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7165, AS AMENDED 26 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 29 SECTION 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “National Literacy Council Act”. 32 SECTION 2. Declaration of Policy. – Pursuant to Article II, Section 17 of the Constitution, it is the declared policy of the State to give priority to education to foster patriotism and nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development. 37 Article XIV, Section 2(4) of the Constitution likewise mandates the State to encourage non-formal, informal, and indigenous learning systems, as well as self- learning, independent, and out-of-school study programs particularly those that respond to community needs. To this end, the State shall give priority to the adoption of measures for the universalization of literacy. 43 SECTION 3. Renaming of the Literacy Coordinating Council. – The nomenclature of the Literacy Coordinating Council, established pursuant to Republic Act No. 7165, as amended, entitled “An Act Creating the Literacy Coordinating Council, Defining Its Powers and Functions, Appropriating Funds Therefor, and for Other Purposes”, is hereby changed to National Literacy Council, hereinafter referred to in this Act as the “Council”. 50 The Council shall serve as the lead inter-agency coordinating and advisory body to the various agencies of the national government, the local government units (LGUs), and the private sector, on matters pertaining to the formulation of policies
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 While the Philippines has a high basic literacy rate, functional literacy remains an area of worry. Functional literacy refers to the ability to read, write, compute, and understand and apply information in everyday life. The 2024 FLEMMS reported that 93.1% of Filipinos aged 10 to 64 had basic literacy, but only 70.8% had functional literacy. In other words, many Filipinos who can read, write, and compute still have difficulty understanding and applying information. 27 This concern is even more relevant today, when people are constantly exposed to fake news, misleading information, and other unreliable content. In today’s world, literacy must therefore go beyond the ability to read and write. 31 Hence, the proposed measure therefore seeks to strengthen the Literacy Coordinating Council as the country’s lead coordinating and advisory body on literacy. The Council will be given more specific functions to identify literacy needs, support marginalized and vulnerable groups, promote research and evidence-based policies, engage the private sector and other stakeholders, and strengthen coordination with the Bureau of Alternative Education (BAE) and the LGUs. It also establishes Local Literacy Councils to bring literacy efforts closer to communities and provides support for effective literacy programs and outstanding literacy workers and ALS mobile teachers. 40 Through these provisions and updates, the measure aims to ensure that literacy programs do not merely teach people to read and write, but help them understand, evaluate, and use information effectively in everyday life. 44 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 46 47 48 REP. title: AN ACT REGULATING THE OPERATION OF MOTORCYCLES-FOR-HIRE AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF 23 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the Philippines in Congress assembled: 26 SECTION 1. Short Title. – This Act shall be known as the “Motorcycles- for-Hire Act”. 29 SECTION 2. Declaration of Policy. – The State recognizes the importance of transportation in economic development. The recent innovations in technology have opened an opportunity for other modes of public conveyance, such as motorcycles-for-hire, to thrive as a reliable and accessible mode of transportation. However, despite its promise of convenience and fast service, it must be regulated to ensure that the interest of the general public is protected. Thus, the State shall allow the regulated operation of motorcycles-for-hire to provide the public with an additional mode of public transportation, which is sufficient, safe, secure and economical. To this end, the State shall establish mechanisms and guidelines in regulating all the operational aspects of motorcycles-for-hire. 41 SECTION 3. Definition of Terms. – As used in this Act: 43 a) Digital platform refers to information and communications technology-enabled mechanism that connects and integrate producers and users in online environments where goods and services are requested, developed, and sold, and data is generated and exchanged; 48 b) Motorcycle refers to any two (2)-wheeled motor vehicle without appendages; 51 c) Motorcycle-for-hire refers to a motorcycle, duly registered as such under this Act, and used to carry passengers or goods on a for hire basis, offering
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 At 7:30 in the morning, Juan books a motorcycle ride through an app to get to work. The trip is quick and convenient…until the motorcycle is involved in a road crash. Juan is injured and rushed to the hospital, but questions now arise: Who will shoulder his medical expenses? Who is responsible for the accident? And who will provide immediate assistance? 27 The proposed Motorcycles-for-Hire Act seeks to address these gaps by establishing clear mechanisms and guidelines for the entire operation of motorcycles-for-hire, from registration, licensing, and safety standards to franchising, fares, platform accreditation, insurance, emergency response, enforcement, and penalties. It seeks to ensure that as motorcycle-based transport continues to grow, convenience is matched by safety, accountability, and proper government regulation. 34 Because behind every motorcycle-for-hire is not just a rider or a passenger, but a person trying to get to work, get home, or make a living. The measure seeks to ensure that the convenience of this service never comes at the expense of the safety of the people who depend on it. 39 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 41 42 43 REP. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 21 The Philippines has a substantial and growing demand for motor vehicles, but this demand does not automatically translate into a strong domestic manufacturing base. The country needs to further develop its capacity to manufacture vehicles and automotive components, create skilled jobs, attract investments, and participate more meaningfully in global automotive value chains. 27 The proposed Philippine Motor Vehicle Manufacturing Industry Act establishes a national framework to strengthen this industry. It creates a six-year National Motor Vehicle Manufacturing Development Plan with specific manufacturing and export targets, identifies priority products for development, and provides for incentives for vehicle and component manufacturers. 33 It also requires the national government, GOCCs, and LGUs to prioritize domestically manufactured vehicles for at least 50% of their existing fleets, when locally produced vehicles meet the required specifications and quality. 37 Ultimately, the measure seeks to make the country’s growing vehicle demand a driver of Philippine manufacturing, jobs, and industrial growth. 40 In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 42 43 44 REP. label: HB 11625
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL HEALTH SERVICE OUTREACH PROGRAM FOR SENIOR CITIZENS AND INDIGENT PERSONS WITH FUNCTIONAL DISABILITIES, PROVIDING FOR INTER-AGENCY AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT COORDINATION, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE For many senior citizens and indigent Filipinos with disabilities, access to health care remains difficult even when government health services are available. Age, illness, disability, limited mobility, transportation costs, and financial hardship can prevent a person from regularly visiting a health center or hospital. This is particularly difficult for senior citizens who live alone, persons who are bedridden or have difficulty walking, and families who cannot afford repeated transportation and other expenses associated with seeking medical attention. In these situations, government health services should not always require the patient to come to government. Where circumstances require, government must also be capable of bringing basic health services closer to the patient. This bill seeks to establish a Health Outreach for Seniors and Indigents Program that will provide appropriate health services to qualified senior citizens and indigent persons with functional disabilities through coordinated national and local health outreach. The Program shall strengthen home and community-based health services, including basic health assessment, monitoring, appropriate medical consultation, access to medicines and basic diagnostic services, referral to hospitals and specialists when necessary, and health education for patients and their families. It shall likewise provide qualified beneficiaries with appropriate assistive devices and basic hygiene and oral-care supplies according to their individual needs. 1 The measure also recognizes the important role of local government units, barangay health workers, public health facilities, and other frontline health workers. By strengthening coordination among these existing institutions, government can identify persons who have difficulty accessing health facilities and connect them with the services they need without unnecessarily creating another layer of bureaucracy. A person's age, disability, inability to travel, or lack of financial resources should not become a barrier to receiving basic health care. Bringing appropriate health services closer to those who need them most is a practical way of making our health care system more accessible, responsive, and humane. label: HB 11626
title: AN ACT PROTECTING THE REMITTANCES OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS, PROMOTING FAIR, TRANSPARENT, SECURE, AND AFFORDABLE REMITTANCE SERVICES, STRENGTHENING CONSUMER PROTECTION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Millions of Filipino families depend on money sent home by overseas Filipino workers for their daily needs, education, medical expenses, housing, and other essential expenses. Every peso deducted from these remittances through excessive charges, unfavorable exchange rates, or undisclosed fees reduces the amount that ultimately reaches an OF W's family. OFWs already make significant sacrifices to earn their income abroad. Sending their hard- earned money home should therefore be safe, transparent, affordable, and convenient. This bill seeks to strengthen the protection of OF W remittances by promoting reasonable remittance costs and requiring greater transparency in fees, charges, and foreign exchange rates. Before completing a transaction, an OFW should be clearly informed of how much the transaction will cost and, as far as practicable, the actual amount that the intended beneficiary will receive. The measure likewise recognizes that remittances are increasingly being sent through digital platforms and electronic financial services. Consumer protection must therefore apply regardless of whether money is sent through a traditional bank or remittance center or through an authorized digital or electronic remittance service. The bill also strengthens mechanisms for addressing unauthorized transactions, fraud, erroneous transfers, unreasonable delays, and other problems encountered by OF Ws and their beneficiaries. Financial institutions and remittance service providers must maintain accessible channels through which complaints can be promptly addressed. At the same time, OF Ws and their families should be provided with clear information that allows them to compare remittance costs and make informed financial decisions. The money sent home by an OFW represents hours of work and years of sacrifice away from family. Government must ensure that this money reaches its intended beneficiaries through a financial system that is fair, transparent, secure, and accountable. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. 24 District, Caloocan City WN num 10 11 12 13 14 Republic of the Philippines House of Representatives Quezon City, Metro Manila TWENTIETH CONGRESS Second Regular Session HOUSE BILL No. 11626 Introduced by Representative EDGAR R. label: HB 11627
title: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO DETERMINE AND APPROVE THE BED CAPACITY AND SERVICE CAPABILITY OF HOSPITALS UNDER ITS DIRECT SUPERVISION AND CONTROL, PROVIDING STANDARDS AND SAFEGUARDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Government hospitals must be able to respond to the actual health needs of the communities they serve. As populations grow and demand for medical services increases, some Department of Health hospitals find themselves operating beyond their authorized bed capacity or requiring additional services, personnel, and facilities. At present, increasing the authorized bed capacity of a government hospital generally requires legislation. While congressional oversight remains important, requiring a separate law every time a DOH hospital needs to adjust its bed capacity can delay improvements that are already justified by actual patient demand. Hospital capacity should be able to respond more efficiently to changing conditions. This bill seeks to authorize the Department of Health to determine and approve the bed capacity and service capability of hospitals under its direct supervision and control. Such decisions shall be based on objective considerations, including actual hospital utilization, population and health needs of the area served, availability of other health facilities, demand for specialized services, and the capacity of the hospital to safely provide additional services. The measure also recognizes that increasing the number of authorized beds alone does not necessarily improve health care. Additional beds must be supported by sufficient doctors, nurses and other health personnel, as well as the necessary equipment, facilities, medicines, and operating resources. Any expansion in hospital capacity must therefore be accompanied by corresponding improvements in staffing and service capability. 1 By allowing the DOH to make evidence-based adjustments while retaining appropriate safeguards and congressional oversight, government hospitals can respond more quickly to increasing patient demand without sacrificing the quality and safety of health services. Ultimately, hospital capacity should reflect the number of Filipinos who actually need care rather than remain limited by figures that may no longer reflect present conditions. label: HB 11629
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL VEHICLE HISTORY AND SAFETY REGISTRY, INSTITUTIONALIZING ROADWORTHINESS INSPECTION AS A REQUIREMENT FOR THE REGISTRATION OF MOTOR VEHICLES, REQUIRING THE REPORTING OF MAINTENANCE, REPAIR, INSPECTION, AND ACCIDENT RECORDS OF MOTOR VEHICLES, MANDATING DISCLOSURE IN THE SALE OF USED MOTOR VEHICLES, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution provides that the State shall protect life and property, promote the general welfare and the right to health, protect consumers from substandard or hazardous products, and recognize the right of the people to information on matters of public concern. Congress has already exercised this power over motor vehicles through multiple statutory enactments which allow the LTO to inspect motor vehicles and to refuse registration to those found unsafe, set forth conditions for registration in an emission test, and prohibits deceptive sales acts and practices. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), 13,125 persons died in land transport accidents in the Philippines in 2023. This was the highest number in more than a decade and 7.2 percent more than the 12,240 deaths recorded in 2022. Many of these deaths involved a defective vehicle which is unknown because the condition of vehicles is barely recorded. According to the Metro Manila Accident Reporting and Analysis System Annual Report 2020 of the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), 63,741 of the 65,032 road crashes reported in Metro Manila in 2020, or 98 percent, were logged without any cause. Only six were attributed to brake malfunction and nine to mechanical defect. The registration process does not fill this gap. Republic Act No. 8749, or the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999, makes an emission test a condition for registration, but the law does not expressly require a test of the brakes, tires, steering, or lights. According to the Land Transportation Office (LTO), as reported by the Philippine Daily Inquirer on October 21, 2021, mandatory roadworthiness inspection has been suspended since August 2021. An owner may instead renew registration through a private emission testing center, which tests emissions only, together with a visual inspection by LTO personnel. According to the same 1 LTO statement, 80 percent of renewals take this route. A vehicle can thus be registered year after year without its brakes ever being tested. The same gap harms buyers of used vehicles. No official record shows whether a vehicle was regularly serviced, was flooded or wrecked, or has had its odometer altered. Republic Act No. 10642, or the Philippine Lemon Law, covers only brand-new vehicles. The proposed measure therefore seeks to establish a National Vehicle History and Safety Registry under the LTO that records the maintenance, repairs, inspections, odometer readings, accidents, and safety recalls of every motor vehicle; require a roadworthiness inspection, in addition to the emission test, before a motor vehicle is registered or its registration is renewed; and penalize odometer tampering, false entries, and the concealment of a vehicle's history. In view of the foregoing, approval of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. OMAR VINCENT S. DUTERTE HON. PAOLO Z. label: HB 11630
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A STANDARD ONE-STOP SERVICE CENTER IN EVERY BARANGAY IN THE PHILIPPINES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The barangay is the basic political unit in the Philippines. It is the primary planning and implementing unit of government policies, plans, programs, andprojects in the community. As the most immediate and accessible political unit, it is often the very first point of contact for citizens seeking public services, redress, or clarity about government programs. Despite this critical role, millions of Filipinos still face significant friction when processing government transactions. Residents often endure the financial and temporal burden of traveling to municipal or city halls—or even regional national agency offices—to secure basic documents, process registrations, or seek employment assistance. While Republic Act No. 11032, otherwise known as the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018," successfully mandated the creation of one-stop business facilitation services at the city and municipal levels, the grassroots barangay level has largely been left to rely on fragmented, manual, and localized administrative systems. This bill seeks to bridge that gap by establishing a standard Barangay One-Stop Service Center (BOSSC) in every barangay nationwide. The BOSSC will serve as a unified, digitized frontline desk within the barangay hall. It will consolidate the issuance of all barangay-level documents (clearances, certificates of residency and indigency) and act as a digital conduit for national and municipal services. Furthermore, it will streamline the implementation of special mandates, such as the free issuance of pre-employment records under the First Time Jobseekers Assistance Act. By equipping these centers with standardized technology in partnership with the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), we empower barangays to serve not just as political boundaries, but as highly efficient service hubs. To ensure that no Filipino is left behind by bureaucratic red tape, and to bring the government directly to the doorsteps of the people, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. label: HB 11631
title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE LOCAL FLOOD AND DRAINAGE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, MANDATING THE FORMULATION OF LOCAL FLOOD MASTER PLANS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines is geographically situated in the Pacific Ring of Fire and the Pacific Typhoon Belt, making it one of the most vulnerable countries in the world to natural disasters, particularly typhoons and torrential monsoon rains. An average of twenty (20) tropical cyclones enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) annually, bringing massive rainfall that frequently results in devastating floods. While the national government, through the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) and the Metro Manila Development Authority (MMDA), implements macro-level flood control projects, these efforts are often undermined by inadequate, poorly maintained, or entirely absent drainage networks at the local and barangay levels. Rapid urbanization, improper solid waste disposal, informal settlements along waterways, and the effects of climate change have further exacerbated urban and rural flooding. Currently, flood management is highly fragmented. Local Government Units (LGUs) often lack the technical expertise, dedicated personnel, and financial resources to develop and maintain a scientifically sound local drainage master plan. This bill seeks to address this critical gap by institutionalizing a Comprehensive Local Flood and Drainage Management System. It mandates the creation of a Local Flood and Drainage Management Office (LFDMO) within every city and municipality, tasked specifically with the formulation, implementation, and maintenance of a 10-year Local Flood and Drainage Master Plan. Furthermore, it establishes a funding mechanism and ensures strict coordination with the DPWH, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), and the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) to ensure that local drainage systems seamlessly connect to national flood control infrastructures. By empowering LGUs and institutionalizing accountability in local drainage management, we can mitigate the devastating impacts of flooding on lives, properties, and the local economy. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 11632
title: AN ACT MANDATING THE HIRING OF SCHOOL-BASED LICENSED GUIDANCE COUNSELORS, PSYCHOLOGISTS, AND OTHER MENTAL HEALTH PERSONNEL IN ALL PUBLIC BASIC EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS, UPGRADING THEIR SALARY GRADES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The psychological well-being and mental health of our youth are foundational to their overall development and academic success. In recent years, educational institutions have witnessed an alarming surge in mental health issues among students, including anxiety, depression, and self-harm. These challenges have been exacerbated by the long-term impacts of the pandemic, cyberbullying, and academic pressure. While the State has enacted milestone legislations such as Republic Act No. 11036 (The Mental Health Act) and Republic Act No. 11206 (Secondary School Career Guidance and Counseling Act), the effective delivery of mental health services in schools remains severely crippled by a critical shortage of licensed professionals. Currently, the public school system suffers from a disproportionate counselor-to-student ratio, sometimes reaching one counselor for every tens of thousands of students. A primary driver of this shortage is the uncompetitive compensation framework. Under the current system, highly qualified professionals with master’s degrees and board licenses are often offered entry-level positions at Salary Grade 11. Consequently, many licensed guidance counselors and psychologists opt for private practice or corporate roles, leaving our schools understaffed and our students vulnerable. This proposed measure seeks to address this crisis by mandating the Department of Education (DepEd) to hire and deploy school-based licensed guidance counselors, psychologists, and allied mental health personnel (such as psychometricians and clinical social workers) in all public basic education institutions. Furthermore, to attract and retain these vital professionals, this bill proposes the upgrading of their entry-level salary grades to match the rigorous educational and licensure requirements of their professions. By institutionalizing a standard student-to-mental-health-personnel ratio and providing competitive remuneration, we can ensure that every school becomes a safe, nurturing, and psychologically supportive environment for the Filipino youth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. SALVADOR A. PLEYTO, SR. label: HB 11633
title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM IN CULTURAL AND INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES BY INSTITUTIONALIZING THE TRAINING AND ENGAGEMENT OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE This measure seeks to institutionalize the training, recognition, and engagement of Indigenous Community Health Workers (ICHWs) who are members of the communities they serve. They will serve as a vital link between Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) communities and the formal health system by promoting health education, disease prevention, sanitation, nutrition, maternal and child health, immunization, basic health monitoring, first aid within the limits of their training, referral, and assistance in accessing appropriate health facilities. The measure likewise recognizes the value of traditional health practices of ICCs/IPs while ensuring that their use and promotion remain consistent with applicable laws, public health standards, and regulations governing traditional and herbal medicines. Community herbal gardens may also be supported as appropriate, subject to relevant health, environmental, biodiversity, and traditional knowledge protection requirements. The selection of ICHWs shall respect the customs, traditions, and customary decision-making processes of the concerned ICC/IP community, while their training and recognition shall be subject to standards established by the Department of Health. The measure also provides for continuing training, health insurance and hospitalization assistance, educational assistance, legal assistance, and appropriate honoraria and other incentives, subject to existing laws and the availability of funds. The proposed program shall complement, and not diminish, existing programs for Barangay Health Workers under Republic Act No. 7883. It shall likewise be implemented in coordination with the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples, local government units, and other concerned government agencies. Through this measure, the State can strengthen community-based primary health care, improve access to essential health services, and promote a more responsive and culturally appropriate healthcare system for Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11634
title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MODERNIZATION AND CAPABILITY ENHANCEMENT OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine National Police (PNP), as the country’s primary law enforcement agency, must be equipped with the infrastructure, technology, mobility assets, communications systems, investigative capabilities, and other resources necessary to effectively perform its mandate and respond to evolving public safety and security challenges. While the PNP has undertaken various capability enhancement initiatives, modernization efforts remain dependent on periodic appropriations and individual procurement programs. A comprehensive and sustained framework is therefore necessary to ensure that capability development is systematic, responsive to operational needs, and supported by appropriate procurement and institutional mechanisms. This measure seeks to institutionalize a PNP Modernization and Capability Enhancement Program covering infrastructure and facilities development, equipment acquisition and upgrading, information and communications technology, investigative and forensic capabilities, and institutional and professional development. It likewise provides for appropriate procurement strategies, supply-chain security, technology transfer, coordination with relevant government agencies, and a defined implementation period and funding framework. Through this measure, the PNP shall be better positioned to strengthen its operational capabilities, uphold human rights and professional standards, adopt modern technologies, and deliver more effective and responsive police services to the Filipino people. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ERIC L. label: HB 11635
title: AN ACT PROVIDING MEASURES TO PREVENT MINORS FROM PURCHASING PRODUCTS THAT ARE HARMFUL OR MAY INCITE VIOLENCE, INCLUDING REALISTIC TOY WEAPONS, MANDATING SCHOOL AWARENESS PROGRAMS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The alarming rise of violence in schools involving minors calls for strengthened measures to protect children and promote safe learning environments. Recent incidents involving violence in schools, including shootings, knife attacks, and the confiscation of weapons from minors, underscore the need to address children's access to dangerous products and realistic toy weapons that may create safety risks in schools and communities. The 1987 Constitution provides the foundation for this measure. Article II, Section 13 declares that the State recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation- building and shall promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual, and social well-being. Article XV, Section 3(2) further mandates the State to defend the right of children to assistance, including proper care and protection from all forms of neglect, abuse, cruelty, exploitation, and other conditions prejudicial to their development. This bill builds upon existing laws and policies, including: 1) Republic Act No. 7610, otherwise known as the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act, which provides special protection to children from abuse, exploitation, and discrimination; 2) Republic Act No. 10627, otherwise known as the Anti-Bullying Act of 2013, which provides measures to prevent and address bullying and violence in schools; 3) Republic Act No. 11934, otherwise known as the SIM Card Registration Act, insofar as applicable to measures promoting accountability in digital transactions; and 4) Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, which provides the framework for local government action and community-based programs. Research on children's exposure to weapon-related toys and violent stimuli has identified potential short-term associations with aggressive cognition or behavior, although such exposure alone has not been established as a predictor of later criminality. These findings underscore the importance of age-appropriate safeguards, responsible supervision, and preventive education in school and community environments. This bill therefore seeks to: a) Prohibit the sale, distribution, or provision of specified harmful products and realistic toy weapons to minors; b) Establish reasonable age-verification requirements for transactions involving restricted products, including online transactions, while respecting applicable data privacy laws; c) Mandate school awareness and prevention programs to promote peace, conflict resolution, responsible behavior, and child safety; d) Strengthen coordination among national government agencies, local government units, schools, parents, and community organizations; and e) Provide appropriate mechanisms for monitoring, reporting, and enforcement while ensuring that children who may come into possession of prohibited products are treated primarily as children requiring protection and appropriate intervention. This measure is not merely about restricting toy guns, knives, or other products. It seeks to strengthen the State's preventive approach to child protection by addressing children's access to products that may endanger their safety, while promoting education, responsible behavior, and a culture of peace in schools and communities. The immediate passage of this bill is, therefore, earnestly sought. ERIC L.
